title: Fine Two-Pack of Cables
review_text:
If you own an iPhone, iPad or one of the newer iPods you are familiar with the need for lightning cables. These are basically special USB cables that are reversible and are specific to Apple electronics. The problem with these cables is that they can be expensive, especially if you go with Apple-branded cables. There are some good third-party cables available, and they represent a good value when compared to Apple cables. I get offered a LOT of lightning cables for review and I have noticed an unpleasant trend: most vendors hawking their cables to not mention MFI certification at all, anywhere, and this is important. This particular cable is clearly marked in the description as certified, so it is worth some consideration on that basis alone when compared to many of the others available.

These come in a two-pack, and they are a little more than 3’ in length. These have hard plastic plugs on the end and the length is insulated with a vinyl sheath for protection. So far these have shown no signs of fatigue at the plugs and they work very well. I have been able to charge my phone as well as connect it to iTunes. I attempted to pull the shielding away from the plug and was unable to do so, so I see no risk of exposing the wires inside the casing.

I mentioned the certification above, and I will restate that this is a very important feature. Because these cables are certified, they are guaranteed compatible and will work. If you use a cable that is not certified you might get messages on your phone or tablet that the cable is unrecognized and it might not work as desired. I have worked with non-certified cables and sometimes they work while others do not work at all. I have never had a certified cable fail me.

If you are looking for a less expensive alternative to Apple-branded cables, make sure you select a product that has been certified to work. This two pack of cables is a good choice; so far, they have given me no trouble at all and they have worked well for me. They are definitely compatible and are made well too. And, getting two of them instead of just one in the package means you can have one in the office and one at home.

title: Three Good Mounts in One Package
review_text:
I have been looking for the right phone holder for the car after the one I had been using for a good while finally broke on me. The one I had was great; it had a strong suction cup and a large-opening clip that held my phone securely and could also be used as a holder for my TomTom. Since it broke I have been looking for a suitable replacement and I had the opportunity to work with this car mount. Rather, this is a set of car mounts. So far it has performed well for me and it has kept my phone secure while I am driving.

There are three separate mounts in this package. The one I use most is the short dashboard mount. I have it mounted on a weighted movable base that I can slide to either end of the dash while I am driving. It holds fairly well and it has not come loose while I am driving. I did discover that the suction cup released after several hours though, which is a problem I have seen with other mounts when using this same base. The second one is a windshield mount with a flexible mounting arm. This is the most flexible and versatile of the mounts, though I am not a fan of this type of mount as the phone tends to jiggle and bounce when the car is in motion. The third one is an air vent mount and I do not use this one as my air vents do not cooperate with it, though it seems to be ok with most vent systems.

The mounting brackets are spring-loaded sliders and they provide a good bit of tension when holding the phone in place. The brackets seem to be tight enough to survive the “shake test” for most typical situations though the phone can be shaken loose if you shake the mount hard enough (though this becomes an unrealistic test). It requires two hands to open the brackets which is a good sign that they will hold.

The brackets attach to the different mounts via ball joints which give solid flexibility and allow for angling the phone properly. One of the problems I had with another mount was that the ball got chewed up by the bracket assembly so I look for this when I see these types of mounts, and so far the brackets have mounted properly and have proven to be well designed.

Most car mounts are of a single type. This is a set, though, so you get not just one type of mount but three that you can use simultaneously, for the price of a single mount. These are made well and they work well, so at the price point this is really hard to beat.

title: Well-Made Messenger Bag
review_text:
I prefer a good messenger bag to a backpack most of the time. I prefer the way a messenger bag looks, how it is organized and how it provides protection to the contents of the bag most of the time, the trade-off being reduced space when compared to a regular-sized backpack. This is a nice bag and I am pleased with it. It recently came in very handy when we were traveling.

This is a large, canvas messenger bag. The canvas used is not the heaviest grade canvas I have seen but it is not the lightest or softest either. It seems to be the right balance of durability and softness as the bag is durable and holds up to abuse but is still soft and pliable enough to be workable in most spaces (like crammed behind a car seat).

Most messenger bags I have seen of late have used magnets as the closing mechanism and this one does so too. There are two leather straps on the flap that have buckles, but these buckles are strictly decorative. Attached to the main body of the bag and to the buckles are magnets and plates that work to close the back with little effort. They hold as well as metal snaps in most cases, the exception being if you overstuff the bag. There is a zipper to supplement the flap, so if you can zip the bag then you can snap it shut too.

The bag has a large main compartment that has a padded divider in the middle. This compartment is large enough to handle a smaller laptop (and I have a 10” tablet and keyboard that fits it very well) and it also is large enough to handle a couple of books. title: Excellent Sound
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:99ec24b728fa83828f854618bef8cc0]] Most of the Bluetooth speakers I have used have been smaller and more portable, designed to be on-the-go and useful when traveling or outdoors. This speaker by GGMM is also wireless and can go with you, but I personally prefer to keep it in my room above my desk where I can use it to listen to music. This is a much better speaker than most of the speakers I have used and I am very pleased with it.

This is a large speaker, bigger than most I have used and as a result it weighs more. It is encased in a leather cover and looks very upscale when compared to plastic or rubber. The controls are straightforward and easy – power on/off, set the mode between Bluetooth, WiFi and Line-in, volume up and down and finally a bass booster. On the back there is a barrel port of plugging in the speaker, a reset button that you likely will never need to use and the port for plugging in a 3.5mm plug.

The sound profile is about as close to perfect as I have seen in any speaker. The bass is on target – strong but not overdriven unless you use the bass booster. The midrange is excellent and the music sounds rich and full, not lifeless, hollow or like it’s coming from a tunnel. The highs are bright and clean but not piercing. The sound is balanced very well and I am happy.

The bass booster does exactly what you think it does – it gives the bass a kick. Even with the boost, the bass is not overpowering but it comes forward quite a bit on bass-heavy tracks. I do not use the bass boost often as I prefer the highs.

So far I have had no connection issues and the speaker connects very quickly when put in Bluetooth mode.

This is an excellent speaker – far and away better than most smaller speakers I have seen and used. It is much more expensive, but it brings to the table great sound and fine connectivity. I use this in my home office where it sits just above eye level on my desk shelf, and I use it every night for listening to music.

It does work and it is a big step up from my inexpensive scope but it does have a couple of minor issues that merit attention.

To summarize, much of which I discuss in the video attached to this review:

PROS:
- Very sturdy tripod that is easy to adjust
- Three eye pieces of varying strength to make it easier to see that which you are viewing
- Heavy and durable construction
- Includes a Barlow lens as well as a view finder
- Tray is good for holding lenses and it also locks the tripod so that it can’t collapse

- Sensitive to slight wind and soft bumps
- Expensive

This is a decent scope and is a good starting place for the beginner or casual sky watcher. It is not a high-end scope, but it is suited for someone who is more casual or is just starting out.

title: Good Replacement Pads - Inexpensive but Slightly Different than Bose Pads
review_text:
I have a set of Bose QC-15 headphones and I damaged the pads some time ago. I was able to find replacements, though the original Bose pads are quite expensive. I have been looking for good replacement pads that are less expensive and I have tried some off-brand pads in an effort to save money. So far I have found none that are an exact match though I have seen some that are quite close. These are a reasonable match though they are definitely different than the original pads, but at a fraction of the cost.

In appearance these are close to the originals though they are smaller and they do not fit exactly the same. When I put on the headphones with these pads in place, I have to fiddle with the phones a little bit to get them to fit right, more so than when these had the original pads. It’s a noticeable difference but it is not a real problem unless you have to have an exact match.

The pads are soft, but not as subtle and buttery as the original pads. They will soften over time with use, but brand new they are slightly more stiff.

The main difference I have found with these pads is that they do not do as good a job with passive noise canceling as the original pads. I replaced one pad with one of these new pads and put them on my head. With a fan on in the background I listened closely. The new pad allowed more ambient noise to reach my ear than did the original pad. As it softens I think it will fit a little better and will help with the noise isolation, but even new the Bose original pads did more for sound isolation. They still do a good job, just not as good.

So, why would you consider these? There are two good reasons to buy these. First, these are a LOT less expensive than the Bose replacements. At under $10 these represent a very significant savings over the manufacturer’s own replacement pads. Second, although these are different than Bose replacements, they do a good job of making the phones look new and they do the job well enough for most people. The phones are plenty comfortable with the new pads on and unless you are looking for difference you probably would not notice.

These are good pads to consider if you need replacement pads for your headphones and you don’t mind the small differences. If you have to have 100% identical pads, these aren’t what you’re looking for. If you are content with approximately 85% the same, these are a very inexpensive alternative to Bose replacement pads.

title: Simply Works. Linux & Windows Compatible
review_text:
An air mouse is not something you would normally use with a PC-based system unless you are trying to save space or are giving a presentation in which case it is a convenient accessory. Such a mouse is a lot more useful for things like Smart TVs, though it is also useful for embedded systems like a Raspberry Pi. I have used several air mice and I was curious to see how well this one would compare to others I have used. So far it has worked well, under both Linux as well as Windows. I will state up front that I have not used it with a Smart TV.

At a glance, this little device looks like a TV remote and little more, but it is quite a bit more than that. It does work as a remote, of course, but it also works as a mouse with a full-up keyboard. On one side of this device there are all of the controls you would expect to find on a remote for a Smart TV remote – volume control, channel settings, mode buttons, play, search and more. Flip the unit over and there is a keyboard, with 38 keys and most regular keyboard functions accessible through function key settings.

The unit requires two AAA batteries, not included.

I decided to try it with my Linux workstation, running CentOS 7 with a 64-bit 3.10.0-series kernel. I did not have to load special drivers and I did not need to do any special configuration at all, it was just plug and play. I was able to move the mouse just by waving the device in front of the screen and several of the buttons on the remote side worked as I would have hoped – Home took me to the browser home page, volume controls worked, Search worked, the menu button brought up the menu for the current application with focus and more. The keyboard portion worked as it should and I was able to type, though I found it a little awkward after being used to a full-sized keyboard for so long.

I also tried it with my Windows 10 system and I got nearly identical results. It required no drivers, no special configuration, no extra set-up – it just works as expected. The buttons works the same under Windows as they did under Linux for me and I was able to navigate as desired.

This is a good air mouse that works well under Linux and Windows. It should work fine with smaller systems like the Raspberry Pi (which uses a derivative of the Linux kernel). As an added bonus, it is relatively inexpensive. If you need an air mouse, this one is worth some consideration.

title: Good Phones at the Price Point
review_text:
I have a number of headphones and I have gotten quite fussy about them and how they sound and how they fit. I was interested in this set, as they resemble a set of Philips headphones I used many years ago and my experience with them was positive. The difference was that the Philips set I used was quite expensive and had active noise cancelling functions. These are a lot less expensive. While these are not the best headphones I have used they are well worth their asking price and I think they are a good set.

These are very striking-looking headphones and they really stand out. I have the blue set and they are by far the most eye-catching phones I have used. The paint is electric blue and the pads and headband are black. I like the overall design, The cord is long enough to make them useful for using at a workstation or desk without having to sit still, a problem I have seen with a number of headsets with very short cords.

There are two primary considerations I have when looking at headphones – comfort and sound profile.

The comfort is good. The pads are long and oval and they appear at first like they would pinch or otherwise not fit well enough to make a seal. I was mistaken. They are quite comfortable and they feel good when wearing them. I will say I personally prefer headphones that really fit tightly, and these are a lot softer than I prefer, but many people prefer lighter headphones so I cannot consider this a fault. They do get a little warm after wearing them for a while, though. Keep in mind that because these do not clamp down tightly, they are not the very best for noise isolation.

The sound profile is another matter entirely. The bass is strong and there is no problem there. The midrange is sorely lacking and as a result the music sounds like it is in a tunnel – this is a problem with many headphones and I specifically look for it. It can be corrected with an equalizer which is fine if you have access to such. I will say that it’s noticeable to me but I have worked with more expensive phones that sound a lot worse. The highs are fine and are clear. I have also noticed that as the volume gets boosted higher, the sound distorts.

Now, if these were expensive headphones I would be a lot more critical, but these are under $20. For a $20 set of headphones, these are just fine and they are very much competitive with others in their price range. They sound all right through they could be better, they are quie comfortable and I really like the price point. If you need an inexpensive pair of headphones, these are not a bad choice at all.

title: Fine Camera Strap
review_text:
I have a camera, a Samsung NX300, that I bought a couple of years ago that I use for everything. I prefer it to my camera phone and I like it better than my older point-and-shoot camera. It is not high-end by any means, but it is better than the average camera and I am pleased with it. It came with a neck strap, but the strap is the weak point of my camera – too short and not well made. I have been looking for a good strap for my camera and I was afforded the opportunity to review this one. So far it has proven to be a nice one and it works well for my purposes.

I have the “Color10” camera strap which is a blue background with a floral pattern. It is a cloth cover sewn to a thin leather backing – not the most heavy construction but just fine for a camera. The ends of the strap are sealed with large leather connectors that attach to the thinner nylon straps that fasten to the camera itself. Looking over the strap, there are no loose threads and the seams seem to be straight and tight. There’s no problem with the workmanship.

I was a little surprised when I looked in the package and there was a little envelope, with two rings and leather cut-outs so that one can attach the strap to a camera that otherwise has no suitable place to attach it. My camera has two small metal eyes that are not anywhere big enough to feel through the nylon ends of the straps but they can handle the rings without issue so there is no problem using this strap with my camera. This is a thoughtful inclusion – other straps I have seen do not come with these, so this one is better suited for more cameras.

The strap seems to be about the right length and it is very comfortable when I wear it around my neck. There’s really not much more I could ask of it – it is well made and it is comfortable.

I really like this camera strap. The manufacturer showed some thought in the design and made this strap workable without requiring additional hardware, and it is made well too. It is slightly more expensive than some other camera straps I have seen but I think the design and the inclusion of the rings and leather cut-outs justify the price. If you have a camera and you need a better strap than what came with it, this one is very much worth some consideration.

title: Simple Plug and Play for Me, Has Been Stable and Reliable
review_text:
With the Bluetooth receiver in my Windows laptop dying a slow death I started looking for a USB solution. I tried a different TrendNet receiver and was disappointed so I hoped this one would work better for me. It has proven to be a lot better and works more reliably.

This is a micro receiver that plugs into a USB port. On my Windows 10 system it was immediately recognized and the system was able to install it and start using it without installing any drivers or third-party software. It immediately allowed me to see all devices that were in range and broadcasting, I was able to pair and connect and it works as well as the internal BT receiver in my laptop did when it was brand new.

One of the things that has proven tricky with other receivers is that when I close my laptop lid, all devices disconnect and when I open the lid again they may or may not reconnect. This is a real hassle when using a BT-based mouse and/or keyboard. With this receiver, the large majority of devices reconnect automatically when I open the lid to my laptop again, which is all I really can ask.

Other reviewers have complained about included software and weird errors. Fortunately for me, I have encountered none of these issues. I am not sure if TrendNet had a bad lot go out, but mine works just great and I am very pleased with it.

This is a good receiver that has worked out well for me. My system recognized it right away, it works stably and it seems to recover properly after the system comes back from sleep mode.

title: Excellent Filter for SNAP! Case Users
review_text:
A Circular Polarizer Lens (CPL) filter is a useful tool for the photographer that generally is used to reduce light during long exposure times. The idea is that it can be used to take a longer exposure of something in motion without washing out, and in the case of moving water it can make the water seem almost misty and magical. I have a CPL lens for my dedicated camera, but this one goes with the Bitplay SNAP! series of cases. In this context it is a great lens for deepening colors and reducing glare.

This lens is small, designed to attach to the SNAP! case threads. If you do not have the case, this lens is very unlikely to work for you.

It works by having two glass lenses, one that is fixed in place and one that rotates. As the lens is rotated, the light coming through the pair fades due to the polarization. It is easily tested by looking through this lens at a flat-screen monitor like a laptop screen.

One of the issues with a CPL filter is that often there is an uneven fade; this lens does not seem to suffer from this problem as much as with other CPL filters I have used and I have gotten consistently even shots with minimal bright spots.

While I haven't yet messed with my phone enough to know how to increase the shutter speed, I still have been able to take shots with reduced glare. Much like polarized sunglasses, this lens is suitable for dealing with glare and reflections, and it works well.

I am pleased with this CPL filter. It works well with my phone and it is does exactly what it is supposed to do. If you have a SNAP! case for your iPhone 6 and you are looking to “up your game” when it comes to taking pictures with your phone, this is a lens that will serve you well once you learn to use it and get the hang of how it works.

title: Turn Your iPhone Into a Natural Point-and-Shoot Camera
review_text:
The cameras built into smart phones are getting more and more capable and they have impacted sales of point-and-shoot cameras significantly. I still prefer using a dedicated camera instead of using my phone, and part of the reason is that using my phone doesn't feel the least bit like using a camera. This case changes that and converts your iPhone 6/6s into a camera that actually looks and feels like a dedicated camera in your hands. This is not just a cheap plastic shell with a lens port on it; it actually provides some good protection for the phone.

I will start with the shell case itself. The case is a hard plastic shell, providing back and bumper protection for the phone. It snaps over the phone and holds well. It is not so tight that it is near impossible to remove, nor is it so loose that it runs a risk of letting the phone slip. Overall, it is snug and holds well. The shell itself is a hard, semi-rigid plastic that has a small amount of flex but very little. The bumper guard is a softer material though still quite stiff and it has added material at the corners to give it some extra shock absorption. This is better than the majority of shell cases I have seen and used, and on the shell itself this is a good case.

In the package is everything you need to turn your phone into a point-and-shoot camera: the shell case itself, two grip bases (one hard plastic, one wood), a carry strap, a lanyard, a lens kit and a thumb rest for when you are holding the phone. There is even a small screwdriver so you can change the grips. It requires no other equipment or tools.

I did not understand the purpose of the grips right away, until I removed the base plate from the shell and attached one. It made sense then – the case actually looks and feels like a camera, with a natural groove for your middle finger when holding the phone like a dedicated camera. I of course prefer the wood one, but the black plastic one better matches the shell.

I also was puzzled by the thumb rest (wasn't even sure what it was) until I attached it to the case and held it up. My thumb rested on it naturally and it was actually a little more comfortable than my regular camera.

The case comes with a small lens kit which is made up of a wide angle lens and a macro lens for close-up shots. I experimented with the lenses and took a picture of the field behind my house after a recent snowstorm and it definitely captured a wider view than without the lens in place. I then removed the wide angle lens and used the macro lens to take a picture of a fiber on a blanket, and it did a better job than my dedicated camera with a close-up lens. I have attached both of these pictures with my review.

The one thing this kit does not include is a screen protector. A lot of cases do not have screen protectors and you have to buy them separately anymore. I would suggest using a tempered glass screen protector to get the best possible protection to go along with this case.

This case is enough to make me seriously think about using my phone's camera a lot more. It makes the phone feel like a dedicated camera, it has some thoughtful features and it provides very good bumper, corner and back protection for the phone. Also available for this case are separate add-on lenses like telephoto and fisheye lenses so you can expand the capabilities even more. If you have an iPhone 6/6s, consider getting this case before you buy a separate camera.

title: No Wasted Outlets!!
review_text:
I have a workbench where I frequently have little projects underway, and the issue I have had is a shortage of power outlets so I am frequently changing the configuration on my desk to account for this. I decided to use this surge suppressor/power strip on my workbench to resolve this issue and so far it has worked out well for me.

There are eight full-sized, grounded power outlets on this tower, and each one is spaced properly to handle a full-sized power adapter like what comes with many electronics. As such, there is no need to compromise when plugging in devices that have larger adapters, because there is enough room for all on this tower. Every outlet includes a ground plug too, which is great for devices that require one (in my house, it's about 50/50). With almost every other surge suppressor, I have had issues with oversized adapters crowding other outlets – this is not a problem with this one.

There are also four USB charging ports on this tower which is a really nice bonus. These are all 2.1A ports so they can output a full-speed charge to devices that can handle it, but most of my devices take a 1A charge so the 2.1A is lost on me. I have not yet put a meter on these ports to check the actual power output but so far these seem to output about the same as most other USB charging blocks I have used. Power output aside, having USB and AC ports together allows choice if you have a device that uses a USB adapter to plug into an AC outlet.

The circuit breaker button is on the bottom.

One thing I particularly like about this tower is that the outlets are one two circuits and there are buttons (on the top) that control each circuit. This may require a little logic when planning your power usage – if you want only/all lights on one circuit, place them so that they are controlled by a single button and you can then power them all on and off together.

This tower have allowed me to clean up my work area and it has enough outlets on it to cover my devices without issue. It is very easy to use and understand, it has plenty of outlets that are spaced apart nicely so there is no waste, and it includes USB outlets too. I have had no trouble with it at all and have no problem recommending it it if you are looking for a good power strip/surge suppressor.

title: Small and Very Portable AM/FM/Shortwave Receiver
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:90e56caf53bb9127a941c450bd417db8]] A battery-powered radio receiver is a good piece of equipment to have on hand when there is an emergency. It can be used to receive important information when there is no power otherwise available. This particular receiver works well and it has the distinction of being one of the smallest receivers I have ever used. It is about the size of a cell phone and it is able to receive shortwave signals as well as AM & FM stations.

This unit is small enough to fit in a pocket and is comparable in size to my iPhone 6 in its case. This makes it ideal for packing along on a trip or keeping someplace where it can be out of the way but ready in an emergency. In my opinion, the size is one of the strongest selling points.

Turning it on by the switch does not turn on receiving. This turns on only the power to the LCD and from there the radio can be turned on by holding down the on/off button on the front. This is an interesting way to make sure the radio is not accidentally powered on, though it is slightly inconvenient. This feature suggests the ideal behind this radio is primarily emergency readiness.

There are a number of ranges set for AM, FM and shortwave on this radio that correspond to different locales. Operable range in one country may be very different than in another, and by separating these out into preset ranges enables changing the suitability for a locale a matter of pressing a button rather than tracking down a new device. This makes traveling with this radio very workable.

After turning it on I have had no issue with finding stations on each appropriate frequency range, though it was easiest finding FM stations due to the prevalence of such in the area where I live.

This is an interesting little radio. It works well, and it is able to pick up stations in different regions by simply changing the available range to scan. The size makes it easy to take with you. Though it is most clearly useful as an emergency radio it works well as a general purpose radio too. The price is nice too, making this an easy radio to recommend.

title: Polished and Feature Packed Smartwatch
review_text:
Smart watches have gotten more popular with the release of the Apple watch. They tend to have a standard set of functions, such as access to instant messaging, email, time, alarms and a lot more, typically tied to your phone. Not all smart watches are alike, though, and offer different sets of functions, better connectivity and other various differences from one another. This particular smart watch offers the mainline set of functions, setting itself apart through the user interface which is more polished and clean than most others with which I have worked. That said, I have a couple of quibbles with it, leaving room for a little improvement.

This is a standard-sized watch with a rubber wristband that can actually fit a larger wrist like mine. I have trouble finding watches and watch bands that fit me, so the fact that this one fits me is a pleasant surprise.

Powering it on, the user is immediately greeted with a complex and fairly complete visual menu system with tiles for every function available to the user. This is a standard presentation for a smartwatch, but this one looks a bit more polished and clean than the others I have seen. Switching to other menu screens just requires a swipe gesture, as to be expected. I have big hands, and this means that, for me, using a stylus makes working with this watch a lot easier. This is not the fault of the watch but a reality of working with a small device.

My first issue with this watch came when I paired it to my phone. The date and time on the watch were off, so I expected that it would grab the time from my iPhone when I paired it. It did not. Instead, I had to dig for the clock application and manually set the time. I dislike this and think that having it set itself when it is paired is much more accurate and cuts effort on the part of the user. For Android users, there is an application to allow for syncing up the time, date and more, but iOS users are out of luck for now. To the manufacturer's credit this is made clear on the product listing so this is not a surprise. Regardless, I am of the opinion that the watch should fetch the time, not rely on being sent the time. In the grand scheme of things, though, this is an annoyance, not a deal breaker.

There is a fairly comprehensive list of functions provided by this watch in addition to time/date and phone answer. Through the menus the user has access to call logs and function, Bluetooth functions, a remote finder function, a pedometer, a sleep monitor, a reminder function to get up and move on occasion, calendar and clock functions, audio functions, video functions and a few more.

One of the interesting functions that this watch offers is a camera. So, I tried to use it and it complained that there was no memory card available. Reading through the limited documentation included, I was unable to find anything about a memory card. I finally noticed that the back of the watch has a small groove where it can be popped off, and when I removed the back I found the battery which is removable (replaceable - another pleasant surprise). Under the battery is a slot for a micro SD card.

Adding a memory card comes with a big catch. It requires removing the battery to get at the holder which in turn clears the clock and resets it to midnight 01-01-2015. So, adding the memory card requires me to set the time again. And again if I remove the card.

Although I think the time sync functions of this watch are lacking, it is otherwise a good smartwatch. The interface is professional and polished and the whole provides access to a large number of useful functions. It's priced well too. Overall, this is a solid offering worth a look if you are wanting a smartwatch.

title: Good Speedlight for Someone Trying to Learn
review_text:
If you are seriously into photography a speedlight is a valuable asset that can help you get the lighting just right, which I have found to be particularly helpful when dealing with portrait shots. I have worked with other K&F Concept products and have had consistently good experiences with them so I expected the same from this speedlight. I have not been disappointed. I encountered a couple of minor speed bumps along the way, based largely on learning curve.

This is a sizeable device, and it has a bit of heft to it when the batteries are installed. Please make sure you have proper support for the camera when you are using this light as it can unbalance the camera and make it awkward to use. This is not specific to this particular speedlight but to speedlights in general.

First things first – this thing takes 4 AA batteries and that adds weight. The battery compartment is easily accessible and it is easy enough to install the batteries.

The controls on this light are very straightforward though knowing what the settings do is a different matter. If you do not know what slave mode is or how the settings relate to the zoom, you are going to find yourself frustrated. It took a little bit of research and some experimentation to get the hang of this light and I have found the best use for me is to use it in slave mode to supplement the lighting my the flash that came with my camera, though through the hot shoe I can install it on my camera.

Read the manual that comes with it. It will help a lot in learning how to use this light properly.

The light comes with a small stand so it can be set up independently from the camera and in that manner it can be used as a standalone flash. Turning on slave mode allows for positioning it so that it can add the right balance of light in reaction to the flash on the camera and as a result you can get very good backlighting.

The mode button on the back of this light allows for switching between modal settings and making adjustments, There are also 4 directional buttons that are used for making individual setting adjustments such as zoom. There is the on/off switch which toggles power but also toggles the backlight on the LCD display. Finally, there is a flash button that allows for activating the flash manually. The flash can be fired repeatedly in manual mode but seems to be on a 3-second recharge when not so.

The light has 90 degrees of freedom of movement so that it can be positioned as desired. I like the fact that the neck has angular measures on it for 45, 60 and 75 degrees,

Be aware that this speedlight is not universal and does not work on all cameras. It works fine with a Canon camera; my Samsung camera does not register the presence of this flash at all so to use it with my Samsung camera I have no choice but to use it in manual or slave mode.

This is a nice speedlight and it works well, It is not the fanciest or most expensive but it gets the basics down very well and it has not let me down. This is an affordable speedlight and it is good for the photographer who wants to learn how to improve their lighting techniques.

title: Small displays like this one serve in areas where larger displays may ...
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:ee00283940adc73cdd08d66738c2c471]] Small displays like this one serve in areas where larger displays may be inappropriate. One example is in automotive displays, another being embedded processing such as with a Raspberry Pi or similar small platform. This is a nice display with some good features.

This display accepts several display types, including A/V, HDMI as well as VGA. I have tested it with the VGA and HDMI inputs and it has worked very well. Though it is very small it is clear, bright and quite readable.

It comes with a decent stand that will keep it stable and secure, and if you are so inclined you can install this display on the dashboard of your car using the included double-sided tape that fits the base. You would do this if you choose to set it up as a display for a backup camera in your vehicle.

Included is a small remote for navigating through the options available to you. You can do the same things with the buttons on the face of the screen but I have found the remote to be a little more convenient. In using the remote I discovered an FM tuner – I can change the settings but I have not yet successfully made it work.

I go into more detail in the video I have attached.

This is a nice monitor. It's small and compact and in an emergency it will work as a primary display for a computer. It is much better suited for embedded systems where it is very good. If you are working on small systems like a Raspberry Pi this is a fine choice.

title: Very Easy to Use
review_text:
As a child one of my favorite things to do was to look at things under a microscope. I vividly remember gathering a water sample from a swamp near the house and looking at a sample and finding my first paramecium. It has been years since I have owned a microscope, but with this microscope I can see how things have advanced and changed. This one does not have the same magnification as that microscope I had as a child but it is a lot easier to use and I can still see things with it that I cannot see even with a good magnifying glass.

This unit looks more like a drill press than a microscope, in terms of the design. The scope itself fits on a metal shaft and two turning knobs make it easy to raise and lower the scope in relation to the base. The base has two clips for holding down your slides or paper or whatever else you want to look at through the scope. There is no eye-piece on the scope – the image is viewed on a computer screen instead and the connection is made via USB.

Included with the scope is a software CD and this must be installed to use the scope. Installation is quick and painless. I installed under Windows 10 64-bit and had no issues. After installation I launched the software immediately.

The software consists of a view/capture application and a supplemental application for saving your work. The main part of the view & capture app is a live window that shows what is visible through the scope. As the object or slide on the scope base is moved, the image updates in real time. I found it a little awkward to line things up just right at first but I finally did manage to get things in the viewer just as I wanted them.

I started with a gray piece of paper that I thought was solid gray, but I found that the gray is actually a micro dot pattern like magazine print. More interesting was the corner of a $5 bill showing not just the print pattern detail but the fine fibers in the paper. A penny, cat hair and a very close-up view of a microfiber cleaning cloth all proved to be interesting subjects. Attached to this review are some of those detailed images, my favorite being the penny. I have not yet gone to the culvert near the house to gather water samples.

The software allows for two different capture types – photo or video. I have only played with the photo capture so far but it it very straightforward – click the photo button, either on the application interface or on the USB cable where the light level can be adjusted and the image appears in a list on the right side of the application window. If you double click the image you can save the image to the hard drive, zoom in on it and do a few other operations.

Linked to a tablet instead of a computer, this is a great travel scope to take with you. It is well-suited for classroom use as well as for use in the office.

I like this microscope. It is very easy to use, it does a good job of magnification and images are nice and clear. It is very different than the microscope I used growing up, in ways that I like. It's so much easier viewing on a screen than looking through a viewer, making this more fun to use too.

title: Fine Small Projector
review_text:
Projectors for home use are typically set up for home theater systems. I have seen a number of systems set up with projectors suspended from the ceiling, and I have seen a few that rely on being mounted on a table top. This is a table top model and it is a very good and easy-to-use projector.

This is a 300-lumen projector which is fine for home theater systems, though it would be a little underpowered to use in a larger room or something like a small church. It is good for small presentations too and is a good option if you want to take it with you for meetings instead of keeping it permanently placed somewhere.

There are several input sources for which the projector is configured. For testing and experimentation I found it easiest to work with HDMI though I was able to use some of the other sources as well. It accepts VGA (which is great for older computer systems and other hardware), it can read files from an SD card or even a USB drive. Using a USB drive or SD card, this projector becomes very compact and portable and doesn't even need an external source of input.

This projector even has a pair of speakers inside so you can use this projector for the entire A/V experience, though you will get better sound from a dedicated sound system. This projector is capable of receiving sound as well as outputting it.

I used the HDMI input to feed the image from my computer to the projector and it did a fine job of displaying my desktop on the wall for me. I was also able to configure Windows to use it as an extended display so I could then look at PowerPoint on the computer screen and use the projector to output the slide show. This is very, very convenient and makes this configuration ideal for presentations. I was able to adjust the focus manually and get the image as sharp as I wanted too.

The remote with this unit is great. It provides full access to the projector's functions, so if the projector is on a shelf out of reach the remote is sufficient for any adjustments you may want to make. If you prefer not to use the remote or have some reason you would rather directly interact with the projector there are several buttons on the top of the projector that give access to the different functions. You can change the input source, power on and off and get into the menu system which allows you to tweak all manner of settings: brightness, change the resolution, update the firmware from USB, set the date and time and more.

This projector does output a lot of heat – to be expected from a projector with a bright light in it. Make sure that you have decent ventilation in the room when using this projector unless you want the room to warm up. I did notice that when the projector is shut off, the fan stops too which is a minor disappointment – I would rather have had the fan continue for a few minutes afterward to cool down the LED.

This is a nice projector. It accepts a lot of different input types, it works well for small rooms and home theaters and it is easy to take with you due to the small size. It is especially useful if you want to run your video or presentation from either USB or from the SD card. If you're looking for a small-scale projector, this is a good choice.

title: Very Nice Messenger Bag
review_text:
I use messenger bags as book bags to take books and tools to and from work every day. I favor canvas bags because they are tougher than nylon and they are a bit more masculine-looking. This particular messenger bag is a little more stylish than some of the others I have seen and so far I am happy with it.

A messenger bag is characterized by the fold-over flap that snaps closed over the main compartment. This particular bag has a very colorful and decorative weave that makes up the entire flap and the result is a softer and more supple flap than if it had been made of the same canvas material as the rest of the bag. That is not a fault or imperfection by any means but needs to be mentioned as a difference. Compared to the flap, the rest of the bag is more coarse and rigid.

Everything about this bag suggests quality. The stitching is very tight and the materials are even and there are no imperfections (nicks and cuts) that I can find on this bag. The stitching used to attach the shoulder strap to the metal loops on the bag, as well as to attach the leather trim to the canvas, is visibly thicker and stronger than what was used to hold the canvas portions of material together. I like the fact that there is some manner of reinforcement on the bottom of the bag (stitched inside so it is hard to know exactly what kind of reinforcement was used).

Instead of actual snaps, the flap is attached to the front of the bag using magnets. These make it a lot easier to open and close the bag.

In the main compartment of this bag are three pockets, one zippered and two smaller pockets that are open on the top. The smaller pockets are ideal for cell phones, small note pads, a calculator and the like while the larger pocket is big enough to accommodate a checkbook or a small book; it is not quite wide enough to handle a DVD case. There is a front pocket that is just barely wide enough to handle a 10” tablet (though I would put a tablet in the main compartment instead). Finally, there is a zippered pocket on the back that is slightly more narrow than the front pocket because of the zipper and is good for papers and maps.

This is a nice messenger bag and I like it. It is made very well, it is spacious enough to handle a couple of technical books and it looks nice.

title: Excellent Results
review_text:
I have worked with several K&F Concept lenses and filters in the past and I have had excellent results with them. I am still very much a beginning photographer and I am still learning as I go but I have learned a lot in the process. One of the things I have especially come to appreciate is the fisheye effect. Up to this point I have only had the ability to work this out via software, so I was pleased to have the opportunity to work with this fisheye lens. So far I have had a lot of fun with it and I love how it works, though I have again learned a few things along the way.

A fisheye lens is somewhat similar to a magnifying glass with a great deal of distortion. The center comes out clear and the edges are distorted and warped, giving the effect of looking through a lens that is very thick in the middle and thins out towards the edges. Straight edge objects like sidewalks become warped and bent.

This particular lens is a chunky and hefty fellow, actually comprised of two lenses instead of just one. There is a large macro lens that can work independently of the fisheye lens and it is very good for taking very close-up shots. The fisheye lens attaches to this macro lens and relies on it.

I took several shots with the fisheye lens and I discovered something I did not realize though it is fairly obvious now. When using the minimum amount of zoom, the distortion is maximized and you get the most effect. The more you zoom in the more dampened the effect though it is still noticeable. I used the lens to take two pictures of the case in which the fisheye lens packs, one zoomed in all the way and one zoomed out all the way. For the one zoomed out, you can see the warping effect on the blinds over the windows and you even can see the entire image framed in a black circle. The image zoomed in has minimal distortion.

I should state that this particular lens is designed for 58mm threads. Make sure your camera can use it before you buy it. If you have a different thread size for your lens, buy the right sized fisheye for that lens.

This is one of the most fun lenses I have. It works great and it does a good job of giving the distortion you want with a fisheye lens, and it is not particularly expensive. I am very pleased with it and am looking forward to working with it for many years.

title: Spacious and Well-Designed Backpack Camera Bag
review_text:
I have a growing interest in photography and I have been learning as I go. One of the things I have discovered is that a good camera bag – sufficiently large to hold the camera, lenses you need and any accessories – is absolutely essential. I have a messenger-style camera bag that works well enough but I have run out of room in it and it does not have the capacity to hold all of my extra lenses and filters. I looked to this camera bag as a solution. It definitely holds more than my old bag, it seems to be made well and there are some nice features to this bag.

This is a backpack style bag and it is about the same size as a small travel backpack, though it is an order of magnitude thicker. There are zippers and pockets everywhere. There's a lot of padding to protect the camera and multiple movable partitions.

The main compartment is large enough to hold a small laptop if all of the partitions are pulled out. There are three small partitions and two large ones and these can be arranged in any configuration to accommodate a wide array of accessories. As shipped, the partitions are arranged to allow for the camera lens and camera to sit through the middle of the pack which maximizes the padding and protection for the most valuable parts of your setup, and the smaller partitions are about right for 2-3 lens kits. I have a smaller camera – a Samsung NX300 with the 18-55mm lens – so I need less room for my camera and rearranged the configuration to permit room for several filter kits, a telephoto lens, a fisheye lens and a few smaller accessories, all in the main compartment. I have not yet purchased additional lenses but will rearrange when I do.

The main compartment also has a pocket that is suitable for either a thin book or a tablet. So, even with all of my other gear in the main compartment, I still have room for my tablet. I really can't ask for much more than that.

There is a smaller zippered compartment on the front that has room for even more accessories. In this I have loaded up a spare set of macro lenses that would not fit in the main compartment. Inside this compartment there is yet another pocket suitable for holding a tablet as well as a mesh pocket for loose items, my choice being a couple of pens. However, the most interesting item in there, attached by a tether, is a waterproof nylon cover for the whole bag. So, if you need to go out in the rain with this backpack, you can do so without fear of getting your equipment wet.

On the sides there are two small pockets, sufficient for holding a couple of small items like a filter or two or even a very small flashlight.

On the front there is one more zippered pocket that is well suited for thin items, like a map, magazine or papers.

The shoulder straps are adjustable and padded so getting the pack to fit just right is not an issue. However, there is a carrying handle loop on the top of this bag and I prefer carrying this bag using that instead (I have always preferred carrying backpacks this way).

This is a very nice camera bag. A lot of thought went into the design and it can hold a lot of equipment for its size. It has replaced my other camera bag outright.

title: Excellent Alternative to Wacom Intuos
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:9c7f474d82697dfd8035b3c7cf95ccc5]] I am a longtime graphics tablet user, having started with a Bamboo small. Since then I have had several tablets including a Bamboo Fun Pen & Touch, am Intuos4 and finally an Intuos5 Medium. All of the tablets I have used have been Wacom tablets; this is my first experience with another brand, and it is the first time I have even heard of Huion as a brand. To me it makes sense to compare this tablet with my Intuos5, with which it actually compares quite well for about 20% of the cost.

My test system for testing this graphics tablet is a Dell laptop, with an Intel i7 processor and 16G RAM, running Windows 10 and Corel Painter X3.

Comparing this tablet to the Intuos5 it is approximately the same size (both are medium tablets). They both look very similar at a glance and there are some distinct similarities in the pen and pen holder as well. In operation they are both similar but there are some very distinct differences, and each one has advantages over the other.

One of the differences between these two tablets is that the Huion tablet has a numbered gauge across the top of the writing surface and includes a replacement surface in the box; the Wacom does not. The gauge is not a big deal but it does make a nice measure if you are looking for consistency in length of lines. The replacement surface is another matter – it is easy to damage the surface and over time it does get scuffed, so being able to apply a new surface is a huge plus to me.

The pens are different and there is give and take with them. The Wacom pen is sealed and does not need batteries or recharging. It is also reversible and both ends can be configured for drawing. Typically one end it set up as an eraser. The Huion pen is rechargeable and is not reversible. I prefer the Wacom pen, but I like the feel of the Huion pen and it works well.

The pens both come with a stand, extra nibs and a nib extractor. The Wacom stand is slightly heavier, but otherwise they are functionally equivalent.

The software is obviously different, and I have been experimenting with the Huion software to learn how to configure the buttons. The Wacom software is a little more intuitive, btu I have found the Huion software to be a bit more versatile and it provides better control. Speaking of buttons, the buttons are a little different between these two tablets with the Wacom providing fewer buttons but providing a scroll wheel.

Both tablets have 2048 pressure levels, and the only real way to test the pressure levels and drawing capabilities of each is to use a drawing application and start experimenting. I loaded up Painter and selected some acrylic brushes and started playing. I was able to get very similar results using the same brushes and the application had no issues with recognizing the pen or the position on the writing surface.

Operationally, these two tablets are very similar. However, the Wacom is more expensive – a lot more expensive. The Huion tablet costs roughly 20% of the cost of the Wacom and to be honest when I compare these two it is hard to justify the cost of the Wacom when the Huion tablet works as well for so much less.

Working with the Huion graphics tablet has been an eye-opening experience. It compared beautifully against a Wacon tablet of similar size and capability. I am very pleased with this tablet and can heartily recommend it as an excellent alternative to more well-known brands.

title: Good, Inexpensive Magnification Lenses
review_text:
The primary lens I have on my camera is a good 18mm-55mm lens and it does great for capturing images that are a foot or more away. When I get much closer than that my camera is unable to focus properly and I end up with a crummy shot and I either have to give up or back up so that it can focus – not what I want most of the time. These magnifying lenses are a good solution, but there are somethings you have to keep in mind when using them.

I will start with a statement that should be obvious: make sure you have the correct lens size when you are purchasing add-on lenses like this set. This particular set can be used only with a lens where the thread size is 55mm. If you have a lens that has a different sized thread, you should consider looking for this kit in a different thread size. You can use a ring adapter, but getting the right size at the start is better.

There are four lenses in this kit, a 1x, 2x, 4x and 10x lens, each increasing in power as the numbers suggest. You can somewhat view these as magnifying glasses for your camera, but that metaphor is not completely accurate. They do magnify the image for you, but they allow a closer shot as well and you can get very close to your subject when you have one of these attached to your lens. Perhaps a better way to describe them is to realize that they make your camera very nearsighted and your camera can see close-up well and distance not at all when using these lenses.

The main thing to remember about them is that as they go up the scale in strength they introduce a lot more edge distortion. This is most obvious with the 10x lens. If you take this lens and hold it so that you can see things through it clearly in the center, you cannot help but notice a large area around the edge of the lens that is distorted. The effect is less then you get it close to something on which you wish to focus but it is something to keep in mind. If there is too much distortion, use a less powerful magnification lens.

These particular lenses have a little bit of heft to them but they are not what I would consider heavy. Because they are glass they are a bit more substantial than resin or plastic lenses.

Overall, these are nice lenses. I have been able to use them for taking very close shots that I otherwise would not be able to take with my camera, such as ridge detail on a penny or dot patterns on magazine print. These are not real-world examples but they definitely show off the capabilities of such lenses. If you are looking for good magnification lenses for your camera, this is a good set that works well. Just make sure you have the right thread size before you buy.

title: Fine Travel Keyboard
review_text:
I have been looking for a good Bluetooth keyboard for some time, to pair with my tablet and use when I want to work on documents. This would get me closer to using my tablet for most general tasks for which I need a computer and allow me to repurpose my laptop. This folding keyboard is a decent one and though it is a little on the small side for me to use full-time with my tablet it works great for when I am traveling.

This is a very small and compact little keyboard, folding up to easily fit in a pocket. When unfolded it is still small but it opens to reveal a full keyboard with smart use of function keys. The keyboard has all of the key functions of a normal keyboard less the keypad. Some keyboards that lack a keypad simulate a pad through the function keys, but this one does not and that's ok.

As soon as it is opened the keyboard powers on and it flashes an LED on the top to indicate that it has power. However, to connect it you have to tell it to connect via a function key combination which is printed right on the keys so there is not really any mystery on how to get it to connect. When broadcasting it identifies itself simply as “Keyboard” or “Bluetooth 3.0 Keyboard” (depending on the platform) and it pairs and connects without any issue.

I first paired this to my laptop as a sanity check and it connected and started working immediately. I was able to type and interact with the computer with no issues and it worked exactly as expected. I then paired it with my tablet which is an Android-based Sony. Again, it paired and connected without issue and I was able to use it in the word processing application I have loaded on there. This is really all I can ask.

Included in the package is a set of instructions and a USB cable for charging. The instructions include a lot of good information which include the specifications and care for the keyboard as well as a chart that shows how the function keys are defined in each of the supported operating systems.

One thing I noticed in the product description is that the Windows 8 Mobile OS is not supported. Having a Windows phone available to me I decided to try it, just as an experiment. The keyboard does connect very quickly to the phone, but it disconnects very shortly thereafter. So, the claim is accurate - not for use with Windows phone. I am not sure if this would also mean it will not work with the Surface?

This is a straightforward keyboard. It is a no-nonsense product that is easy to understand and easy to use. It is on the small side so do not expect a full-sized keyboard when you use this, but it works well and it is a good option particularly when you are mobile and need a keyboard with you.

title: Solid Construction Makes It an Excellent Toolbag
review_text:
I use a messenger bag to carry tools and supplies with me to and from work. I typically have a flashlight, a power bank, batteries and any tools I need for the day in my bag. I had a different bag that I used prior to receiving this bag and I have chosen to use this bag as it is better made and is larger.

I have the gray version of this bag and it is an attractive bag, to say the least. Like a typical messenger bag it has a large pouch pocket over which there is a flap that snaps down and keeps everything in place. There is more to this bag than just the basics, though. It is made of heavy canvas and it is very rugged; after carrying it with me for a month it still looks new and unused though it has been packed and repacked daily for weeks. The shoulder strap is heavy canvas too and it is of course adjustable so it is easy to find the right fit for your shoulder. The flap does not actually snap down but instead is held in place with two strong fastening magnets.

On the front of this bag are two loose pockets that are perfect for carrying a flashlight, a utility blade or other tools. I have even been able to fit a power bank in there for charging my phone when I have needed to make room in the main compartment. I like these because they do not share space with the main compartment and are separated from it by a layer of canvas. On the back is a zippered pocket that shares space with the main pocket. It’s ok for very small things. The main compartment is large enough to handle a set of screwdrivers, some wrenches, a pack of batteries and more (though adding all that stuff makes the bag understandably heavy). There is a small zippered pocket inside the main compartment that is great for things like AA batteries or other small items. There are also two small open pockets inside that work well for holding smaller items, though by being open they can handle larger things that the zippered pockets.

I have been using this bag as a tool bag and it is working out very well for me. I have been pleased with all of the pockets and compartments and I like the fact that this is a heavy-duty bag meant to last a long time. I had another messenger bag that I used for this, but now it’s used just for carrying a tablet and a few minor accessories. This is a high-quality bag at a good price.

title: Supports Multiple Input Sources; Compact and Lightweight
review_text:
I use a full-sized projector every week to give presentations to a fairly large group of people. This projector is configured to connect via a VGA cable across the room and is suspended from the ceiling so that it can be hung in front of a projection screen. A full setup like this is not always the best configuration for every situation and a smaller projector is a better fit for certain situations. This is one such projector and it works very well.

I have the ST-038 model. This is a very small projector, measuring approximately 6"x5"x2". Because of the size it also is very light and is ideal for putting on most shelves or light desks. Because of the size it is ideal for taking along for events such as business presentations, church functions and family fun nights.

This projector has a 1,000-lumen light source and it is bright enough to handle projections in an entertainment room. It is not really strong enough to work in a large auditorium though it will do in an emergency if brought closer to the screen. Overall, I would say this is a good unit for using in the home or with small businesses.

There are several input sources that can be used and the projector has no problem allowing you to select from them. I worked primarily with the HDMI input during testing. If you have an older computer you can use the VGA port to project as well. It is also able to accept video files from USB as well as an SD card so in that way it can be used as a stand-alone projector, either for slides or video. There is even an audio input and a headphone jack on there so you can make it more personal.

There are two ways to control this projector. There is a series of buttons on the top that allow you to change input sources, change picture settings, modify sound settings, set the clock and make other settings adjustments including updating the firmware. The other method of interacting with this projector is to use the remote that is included in the package which allows access to the same settings, using an IR signal between the remote and the projector (the IR sensor is a large red square on the back of the projector).

Using an HDMI cable I was able to use my laptop to project my desktop and subsequently my videos. Done correctly, this projector is a fine second screen and makes an excellent presentation screen for PowerPoint (this requires setting up the desktop to extend the display on the second detected monitor - this projector - and then tell Powerpoint to use the second display for playing the slide show). It works very well and I am pleased with it.

There are two manual controls on the side of this projector. One controls the focus and the other slightly adjusts the tilt of the image on the surface where it is being projected. The focus is unable to get a clear image if you set the projector less than 6'-10' from the projection surface - not too bad of a distance.

On thing you have to remember, though - this unit puts out heat and lots of it, though less than larger projectors. It can quickly warm up a 10'x10' room so consider ventilation when using this or any other small projection device. I was a little surprised too that when the projector is shut off the fan stops instead of running a little longer to cool down the light - not a big deal but noticeable.

I like this projector. It travels well, it has a lot of options for inputs, the controls are intuitive and the picture is bright enough for smaller audiences.

title: Interesting Feature Set; Highs are a Little Muted
review_text:
I listen to music all day at work and I also enjoy listening to music at home and as such I spend a lot of time with headphones on my head. This is one of the more unusual headsets I have used, more in terms of their appearance than for their features or quality. These are decent headphones with some very interesting features though the sound profile is a little off, particularly in the highs.

I received the blue and yellow headset and these definitely look like headphones for kids. They almost look like toys, though in use they have revealed themselves to be a bit better than toys. The main features they offer are Bluetooth connectivity, FM tuning, direct audio connection via 3.5mm cable and hands-free connectivity.

When I received these, they were completely dead and needed to be charged up. It took me a little time to realize they were not broken, but once I plugged them in to charge the problem became very clear. I was then able to work with them. So, if you receive these and cannot get them to work, try plugging them in first.

I was able to pair these to my computer and they connected without trouble. The headphones identify themselves as “KB-2600”. When I had them connected to my computer they worked fine and they did not stutter or skip which is all you really can ask for. I did not try testing the range.

I discovered, quite by accident, that this headset has a full-blown FM tuner and it can scan for channels and make channel presets. It actually works surprisingly well and I found myself listening to a station coming from 50 miles north and it was surprisingly clear. Most headsets I have used to not have an FM tuner so finding these to have a tuner was a pleasant surprise.

I loaded up some music and listened very closely to the sound, and unfortunately I found an issue with the sound profile. The bass is good; it is about right, not overdriven and not soft. The midrange is slightly strong but still quite good. The problem is in the highs which sound muddled and flat. When listening to vocals the sound is not particularly sharp, instead sounding far away. It is fixable with an equalizer, but with small music player or phone an equalizer may not be available.

Comfort-wise, these are actually more comfortable than their looks would suggest. I personally like a headphone that clamps a little tighter on my ears but these are better than some of the other sets I have used. The pads on each phone is a mildly firm leatherette material that is comfortable and does not heat up as much as one might expect. The headband itself has a very soft pad on it that provides a very nice cushion between itself and the head.

These are very interesting headphones and they have some cool features. Except for having a deficiency in the high range, these work well and they are quite comfortable. If you get a two-color unit it is a very good choice for younger listeners.

title: Good Clarity
review_text:
I have a hands-free package with my car so I don’t have to use a headset when I am driving to go hands-free. However, that does not help me when I am outside of the car. I looked to this Bluetooth headset to fill that need. Other single-piece ear pieces I have used in the past have either not been clear, have had poor microphones or both. With this set I was able to hear well enough and the person on the other end of the call said I was quite clear as well - a big improvement over most single-ear headsets I have used.

This is a single ear unit and it can be placed in either ear. The actual unit itself is separate from the insert which is a silicone plug with a look to hold it in place. Also in the box and separate from the actual unit is the over-the-ear hook that snaps onto the unit, and it is reversible so it can go on either ear. Because of the silicone insert this unit is actually comfortable to wear.

I had no trouble pairing and connecting it to my phone. It seems to work just fine with my phone which happens to be a Windows phone.

I tested this headset by making a call. Call clarity and volume is good, and I had no issue with hearing the person on the other end. The person on the other end said I sounded slightly muted but clear. This is better than most other single-ear headsets I have tried, where the person I called would complain about not being able to understand me.

This is a decent headset and is better than other single-ear headsets I have used. I personally prefer a two-ear headset though it is more comfortable than others like it I have tried. If you like single-ear headset, this is a very good option.

title: Better than the Strap that Came with my Camera
review_text:
I have come to understand the value of a good camera strap. It is more than just a designer item and more than just a simple strap to keep the camera hanging around your neck. It needs to be strong enough to keep the camera secure and it needs to be long enough to allow for grabbing the camera and taking a quick shot instead of having to struggle with getting the camera from around your neck and risk missing the shot by a second or two. The strap that came with my camera is functional but much too short and I expect it to rip eventually. This strap by Orota is a much better strap than that provided with my camera.

This is a well-made strap. One side is a heavy weave not unlike a car’s seat belt but not as smooth and shiny. It is also quite a bit thicker than a seat belt and will have no issue with supporting the camera. Sewn to it is a decorative layer that is also a heavy weave, similar to but not exactly like canvas. These are stitched together with heavy thread and I see little risk of them separating.

Each end is clamped with a leather reinforcement that is held in place with four metal rivets. The leather ends each hold a metal buckle with the thinner nylon straps that actually connect to the camera. Looking closely at each component I found no loose threads, no uneven seams, no flaws in fabric or materials. There is nothing about this strap that suggests it will fail under daily use.

This is a much longer strap than what came with my camera, measuring a little less than 3' long. I like the fact that with this trap attached to my camera I can lift my camera and quickly get the shot I want and I don’t have to take it from my neck in order to focus on it. I can hold it far enough from my face to actually focus on the camera. This is a very big improvement over my old strap which was short enough that I could not get the camera in front of my face at a comfortable distance.

This is a very well-made strap and I am very pleased with it. It is stylish, well constructed and it is long enough to make it much more useful to me than my old strap.

title: Good IP Camera with a Couple of Minor Quirks
review_text:
An IP camera is an inexpensive and straightforward way to add a little extra security to your property, whether it is watching a door, monitoring a hallway or even just keeping an eye on the dog while you’re at work for the day. This is one such camera by Foscam, and it seems to work fairly well in my testing. There are a couple of minor issues I have seen, though nothing that I would consider a showstopper.

This is a small and lightweight camera, about the side of a baseball, and it is hinged such that it can be angled in a range of about 300 degrees of coverage if it is placed properly though in practical use (meaning, when it is placed on a wall and anchored to it) it is likely to be positioned more like 70-90 degrees. It also rotates on the base, so it can be configured to point to just about any target from where it is anchored.

The base itself is detachable and the whole camera can be popped off the base with no tools. To me this represents a concern. It means that someone can simply take the camera from the mounting place if it is low enough, using no tools. I like being able to rotate the camera on the base but I also like knowing the camera is not going to get taken easily.

Setup of this camera is very easy and I was able to get it connected to my network without too much effort. That said, I struggled a little bit with the Foscam software and it took me a little while to get the software talking to the camera. I have had this trouble with another Foscam camera, and the problem seems to be the software - very specifically the IP Camera Search Tool utility - and not the hardware or the network. I was able to find the camera in the monitoring client.

Once the camera is connected and available it can be logged into directly. There, the user has some control over a multitude of settings including firmware updates, login credentials and more. I like the interface even though it is somewhat basic as it is easy to navigate and is completely accessible from a web browser.

The monitoring client software allows for more control, which includes concentrating on a single camera if there are more than one connected, scheduling, playback and more. In addition to the software that runs on a computer, users can connect to it via smartphone if they have an iPhone or an Android. Windows phone users are unfortunately out of luck.

The camera resolution is very good and is detailed with fairly accurate colors. This certainly is not the same as a camcorder, of course, but it is sufficient to recognize faces even at a fair distance. The night vision (infrared) is excellent and is sufficient that I was able to read a sheet of instructions that was held in front of the camera.

I do not like the LEDs on the camera, though... It is very hard to place the camera inconspicuously and have it remain unseen in the dark when it lights up with a ring of LED lights. This is the one major issue I have with this camera that I think needs improvement. It’s not a complete deal-breaker, but consider the possibilities when an intruder sees the camera and knows he or she is being recorded. These can be turned off in the settings and I highly encourage doing so.

The camera has a micro SD slot near the hinge where storage can be inserted. It is unfortunate that there are no cards in the box though this is a minor gripe. I used an 8GB card for testing and the camera was able to record to it without trouble and I was able to control this from the monitoring client.

This is a decent little IR-capable security camera. So far I am pleased with it, though there are some minor quirks. It’s a relatively inexpensive camera and is an easy way to monitor areas of your house and record what is going on when you can’t be there.
