title: Good Eye Protection and Good Video Quality Too
review_text:
I have always been intrigued by discrete video cameras and I really like the concept of having the camera embedded in a pair of sunglasses. I was interested in giving these glasses a try and so far they have been great. They video quality is better than I expected.

At a glance these appear to be basic sunglasses with really wide arms. They are not especially stylish but they do not look bad either. The surprising part for me was that they fit very well and completely cover my eyes and form a wind barrier for me. Most sunglasses I have tried leave some gap around my eyes so that I do get a little wind when wearing them - no so with these.

These serve as a Bluetooth receiver and they seem to work well in that regard. When set to pair they identify themselves as “MS2 Bluetooth” and when I paired them to my Windows phone they paired and connected without issue, both for audio and voice. The product description says these work with Android and iOS phones but do not mention Windows phone. So, for the record: they work with Windows phones.

The sound quality for music is not great but it’s not bad, either. The highs are great and are very detailed. The midrange is somewhat flat and as a result the music sounds a little hollow but not unacceptable. The bass is weak. Now, all of this said, these are not designed to be a constant-wear set of headphones so the emphasis was not poured into the sound quality. If you listen a lot to music and plan to use these all the time for that, these just won’t do the job. But, for the day on the ski slopes or occasional use outdoors they are just fine.

The main feature of this set of sunglasses is of course the embedded video camera. The quality is actually better than I expected and it produces a decent video, though certainly not as nice as a hand-held dedicated camera with anti-shake. The sound is not bad either, though if you are moving or are outside when it is windy you will pick up some wind noise, but it is not terrible most of the time (all bets are off if you choose to wear these on a rollercoaster or on a speed boat). Color is bright and vivid, and the detail is there.

These come with 8GB of storage. Installed in one arm of these glasses is a Class 6 8GB card. According to the product description these can support cards up to 32 GB, but I have not attempted to put a different card in there at this time.

These come in a hard, crush-resistant case and are in a small microfiber bag in the case. The case is lined in a velvety material that will prevent scratches if you scrap the bag. Also included are the detachable ear buds and silicone inserts of different sizes so they can be fitted better.

The sunglasses themselves are polarized and are UV-coated so they provide very good eye protection when in the sun. These are a great choice if you are a fisherman and you want to capture highlights from a day on the lake - the UV coating protects your eyes and the polarization cuts down reflections on the water. These will also serve well if you are looking to spend a day at an amusement park, but be aware that there is no anti-shake so if you want to use these on a rollercoaster expect a very jumpy video.

I like these sunglasses. They do a good job of protecting my eyes and they fit very well, they record video very nicely and they have acceptable sound quality. Overall, I am happy with them.

title: Bass Boost Done Right
review_text:
I have worked with and used a large number of headphones and headsets. There are some significant differences between various models and brands which include comfort, sound quality and noise isolation (or active noise cancellation for some of the more expensive headsets). I was eager to see how well these Panasonic earbuds would work out, especially since the last Panasonic headset I had was a dud. These have proven to be much, much better than my last Panasonic headset and are better in a lot of ways to most of the other earbuds I have tried. They are not perfect, but they come close.

Right up front I will state that these are strictly earbuds, not a hands-free headset. If you are looking for a headset for talking, this isn’t it.

Style-wise these are very attractive earbuds, with a dark gray housing and red trim. The cabling is round wire with thick insulation. The round wire is more prone to tangling than the flat ribbon-style cables that have become more popular, but for me I prefer the round wire.

When it comes to comfort these are more comfortable than many I have tried. They fit my ears reasonably well and I have not had problems with them jabbing me or slipping out. I can pull them out by the wire which is good from my perspective as it means if I catch them on something they will pop out of my ear instead of pulling. I have been able to wear these for a couple of hours without any discomfort which is a good thing.

The most important aspect of any set of headphones or earbuds is the sound, and this one gets it really close to perfect. The highs are very clear and bright and I am very happy with how well vocals sound when listening. The midrange is balanced nicely and the music has some depth as a result without sounding hollow or like it is coming from a tunnel. The bass is strong - very strong - and while it is a touch heavier than I like, Panasonic did a good job of not wiping out the whole sound profile with just the bass. If you like earbuds that boost the bass, this pair does it right.

These also have very good noise isolation, or passive noise cancellation. I have worn these for a couple of weeks while at my desk with an air purifier running less than two feet from me and they do a good job of blotting out the sound of that purifier. I do have active noise cancelling headphones too and those do a better job of killing the sound from that air purifier but at a much higher cost and for the difference in sound reduction it’s not an appreciable difference to justify the cost.

Included in the package is a carry pouch and more silicone ear inserts.

I am very pleased with this set of earbuds. They are a bit pricier than the typical set of earbuds I have seen and used of late but they do a great job of blocking ambient sound and they sound great. I am not a huge fan of the bass boost but I seem to be in the minority, and to Panasonic’s credit these buds boost the bass correctly - meaning, the rest of the sound profile is very solid. If you want a set of really good-sounding earbuds with a bass boost, this set is among the better ones I have used.

title: Works Well with Canon 50D
review_text:
I have been shooting a Canon 50D DSLR for several years, mostly outside or with stage lighting. Occasionally, I also have been using a small camera-mounted flash, but it is weak and very limited. To improve my flash photography, I decided to try the Mago Speedlight by Pixel. This is an excellent, mid-priced flash with loads of features.

The Mago Speedlight comes with a nice soft case and a fold-out manual which guides you through the setup of the flash and includes screenshots of the back LCD. It also includes a small stand which is great for use in slave mode, and a clip-on flash defuser. The flash uses 4 AA batteries or an external power supply (not provided). It is even upgradable via a USB port hidden in the battery compartment (not tested).

The controls are easy to use after some experimenting. The manual really helps as there are so many features. The buttons are solid and the display is easy to read, with an optional green backlight.

The flash head can be tilted up and down, or rotated left or right. It also includes a built-in defuser and a white card reflector. These are very useful if you are not bouncing the flash off of a ceiling or reflector.

One interesting feature is an LED model light that can be turned on/off easily via a dedicated button. This light is quite bright and very useful for setting up your shots.

I tested the flash on a Canon 50D with 20mm and 50mm lenses and somewhat cooperative subjects (my kids). After learning the controls, I took several excellent pictures.

The flash supports E-TTL mode, manual mode, and multi-flash mode. I tested all three.

To test the multi-flash mode, I set the flash to 5 bursts at 500 HZ and took a picture of fan blades, resulting in a very interesting effect.

As a final test, I put the flash in slave move (S1) and put my old flash on the camera. This flash worked great as a slave flash and I took some interesting pictures using both flashes. I also used S1 mode to slave the this flash to the camera's on-board flash. Note, I did not test the wireless flash mode (a smart slave mode) as I do not have another flash that supports that feature.

title: Absolutely Outstanding
review_text:
I work with a lot of headphones, headsets and earbuds. I am very partial to one very special set of headphones that I own, a pair of Monster Inspiration phones that includes active noise cancelling (ANC) and this is the pair of headphones against which I compare all others. Although I have worked with many sets of very excellent headphones it takes a lot for me to really rave about a specific set. To be that awesome, the headphones have to be very, very comfortable, have brilliant sound, be made well and have at least good passive noise cancelling if not ANC. These phones by Geega are nothing short of outstanding and actually complete very well with my Monster phones.

These are some of the more comfortable phones I have used. They are completely over the ear phones and cover my entire ears so there is no pinch. The earphones themselves are padded with a soft leatherette that is almost buttery soft and the headband is covered in the same material. These are very easy to adjust to get the fit just right. I can wear them for long periods of time and they do not pinch or get uncomfortable though they do get warm after about an hour. Because they are over-the-ear they provide some measure of passive noise cancelling.

The sound profile is excellent. The bass is at about the right level - not weak and not too forward so the bass response is very good. When the bass drops, you know it but not because it causes a headache. The midrange is very rich and full and the music has amazing depth, better than many others I have used. The highs are absolutely brilliant, bright and crisp. I would stop short of calling these audiophile headphones, but the sound profile is every bit as good as a pair of $350 Sennheiser headphones I own - better, actually, and it makes me sad to know I spent that much on those phones when I could have spent a lot less for these. I intend to connect these to a Bluetooth transmitter and connect them to a professional sound mixing board to see how detailed the sound is - I will update this review when I have done so.

I have these paired to my tablet from which I stream Pandora to them. They paired and connected without issue on all of the devices I have tried - my laptop, my phone and finally my tablet. They identify themselves as “GEEGA S204” and on all three devices I tried to connect I had no issues at all maintaining the connection.

These phones come in a nice, hard protective case that provides good protection from crush damage. There is a mesh pocket inside for keeping the included USB cable for charging and the AUX cable for alternate input.

The range on these phones is 20' - 30' which is very much in line with most phones I have used. Interestingly, they did not stutter and cut out, they just completely cut off when I passed that threshold. I am not sure if this is just a function of my environment or if they really are that sensitive at the threshold.

Overall, these are simply outstanding. I have not found any other set of Bluetooth headphones with the same level of comfort or sound quality. These are the best wireless phones, of any type, that I have ever used. These are my new reference point for wireless/Bluetooth headphones and are the standard by which I will judge any others. I will still use the Monster phones, for the ANC function and for comparison against other wired phones, but these phones by Geega will be used for listening in my home office where I enjoy listening to music most.

title: Fantastic Camera for a Very Reasonable Price
review_text:
I have always liked the video footage taken by bikers as they barrel down a mountain trail or through a wooded area on their bikes (or the crazy base jumpers wanting to capture the drop). It gives a really good sense of what the rider was seeing when riding and you catch every bump in the road, every acceleration and deceleration. I have never used on of these little cameras before now so I was very excited to have a chance to evaluate one of these cameras. So far I am very happy with it and it works well, though I have learned that those with big hands and fingers will struggle a little bit with it.

This is not just a camera, it is a complete kit with the camera, a waterproof housing, cables, mounting brackets, double-sided adhesive pads - everything you need to use this little camera in just about any outdoor activity you might want to capture. I will write mostly about the camera but will touch on a couple of the accessories as well.

Except for cameras designed to be hidden and concealed this is the smallest and lightest camera I have ever seen or used. This is of course required for a device like this that is intended to be used on the go. It very easily can be slipped in a pocket or a bag or purse. It comes packaged in the hard plastic frame that is the waterproof case but even this case is small enough to fit in a purse or smaller bag.

I will say this - read the included manual! The manual is not perfect but it is better than what comes with most electronics and it gives a very good rundown on how to use this little camera. I had no clue at all what to do with this camera until I looked through the manual. I suspected it was touch-screen and I was right. Even though the screen is touch screen and easy to navigate the interface is only semi-intuitive. It is also complicated by the fact that there is an anti-scratch cover on the screen for shipping and if you do not peel this off the screen is a lot less responsive. This is where I had the most trouble - trying to work around the plastic sheet over the screen when I didn’t really even notice it before.

This camera has a lot of the same capabilities of a good phone camera. You can take still pictures, video and also play back that which you have recorded. The camera can snap stills up to 12MP resolution and the video recording can go all the way up to 1080P. These equate to very good image quality when used properly. There are a million little settings for these modes too, from white balance, ISO, anti-shake, motion detection and a lot more. Many of these will be familiar to anyone who uses their digital camera for anything more than just casual shots.

In testing my images and videos came out ok. I am still learning how to balance all of the settings on my big camera so I am no expert, but what I was able to produce was acceptable, particularly the video. I did manage to get the date set correctly and displayed in the corner of the video, I got the lighting right and color straight. I spent too much time playing with the zoom and I learned I am very adept at shooting videos of my hands.

This is a rechargeable device and a standard micro USB cable is provided for charging.

I ran into one issue with the camera and it related to the fact that I have huge hands and the camera is so small. I found that the only way I personally can work the touch screen is to use a stylus. Using my fingers I am unable to pinpoint the spot on the screen I want to touch and I got very frustrated trying to get certain things done on the screen. If you have really big hands, consider using a stylus on the screen.

There is no storage included in the package. The camera takes a microSD card so you will need one to save any pictures or recordings.

The waterproof case is a perfect fit for this camera and it seals wonderfully. It snaps closed without effort and it keeps the water out. It is supposedly good for submersion up to 30m (according to the description). I have not had an opportunity to test this.

There are a number of mounting solutions in the kit, including mounting screws for attaching to a selfie stick, bicycle frame/handlebars and helmets. In the case of the bike mount, it holds very tightly and a good series of bumps is not enough to rattle it loose.

Having never had a sport camera like this I have no basis of comparison but so far I am happy with this little camera. It is very compact and lightweight and it does a great job of taking pictures and video (though it is obviously not a full replacement for a dedicated point-and-shoot or a dedicated video camera). It’s inexpensive too (a LOT less expensive than GoPro) so I think it’s a great option for someone wanting to capture their adventures.

review_text:
I have a sleeve for my tablet that works out very well for me. It provides some protection for the screen and provides some limited protection against drops and bumps. This is the first sleeve I have used for a laptop and so far I like it. It is appreciably cheaper than a laptop bag or backpack, but it also has less room for accessories.

Overall I am pleased with the materials and assembly.

title: Awesome - Quiet and Moves a Lot of Air
review_text:
Heat is the main killer of computers and computer equipment so keeping a system cool and ventilated is a big deal, especially when involving systems that see heavy use. Laptops are just as vulnerable as larger servers and require the same precautions. One of the main solutions for heat dissipation and ventilation for laptops is a chill pad (a fan-based platform that moves air under the system) and this one by AMNIE has been outstanding. I have been using it for about two weeks on my personal system and likely will swap it over to the system in the house that sees the heaviest use.

This is a good-sized pad, able to comfortably handle laptops up to 17”. It has a total of 4 larger fans that move some serious amounts of air, and fans are paired two and two between a pair of switches. The frame is painted metal mesh and offers good support to the laptop it holds.

The switches that control the fans are dial controls and they provide variable fan speeds for each pair of fans they control. There are no graduations so you can set the speed anywhere within the range to suit you, though having that much control is probably not all that necessary. The fans run very quiet but on the highest speed setting really move the air. When maxed out and all four fans running at top speed the fans blew cooler air from between the frame and the laptop, telling me I had the speed up much higher than needed. For my particular system under my typical use load, it seems I only need to turn them on about half way.

I have worked with some chill pads that have flaws in either the fans or the bearings and they make awful amounts of noise. So far, the only noise this pad makes is a low-frequency hum. It is quiet enough that even with lower-end noise canceling headphones I can cancel out the noise completely. This pad is not silent even on the low end of fan speed but it is very quiet all the way through the range of speeds. I have been able to leave the fans on full speed all night and sleep through the sound.

I have not measured the temperature difference between when the fans are on vs. when they are not, but I have noticed that the internal fan does not kick in as frequently when doing video rendering as when the fans are off. It does turn on and it still hits high speed on occasion but it is noticeably less frequently.

This is an excellent chill pad for laptops and so far it has worked out exceptionally well for me. It is quiet, it moves a lot of air and my laptop’s internal fan does not kick in as high as often. Because there is a system in the house that is much more frequently used for gaming, I will be moving this pad to that laptop instead and will use the other pad for myself.

title: Useful Tool for Photographing Small Objects
review_text:
Sometimes it is necessary to take a picture of something on a solid background, often white for contrast but also sometimes black for lighter-colored objects. This is especially true when you are creating promotional materials and you want the item in question to stand out in the picture. It’s not always easy to get that kind of background. A light box is a good way to accomplish this. The Purebox is one such light box and I have had the pleasure of working with it for the past week. This is my very first light box so I have been learning as I go.

The whole thing comes in a gray padded fiber sleeve that is about the size of a padded envelope. I was a little surprised at first when I opened the package and this flat cloth envelope was all that I found. Once I opened everything up and started assembling the Purebox it made sense. The sleeve does provide some protection and it is also compact enough that it can travel fairly easily, though I would discourage packing it in luggage. The box itself is made of white vinyl.

When unfolding the box it is fairly straightforward to see how the box assembles. There are lengths of Velcro along the edges of the tabs that hold the box together and retain its shape. Itf you line these up wrong it results in a box that is very unstable and does not stand up right. When finished, the whole box is approximately 12"x”12"x12".

The top of the box has a very bright ring of LED lights, so bright that I was able to illuminate my basement just with the box alone. They cast an almost clinical light that borders on harsh and it makes the entire box (which is opaque) glow.

Included with the box are two long, wide strips of plastic, one white and the other black. By placing these against the back of the box, it is possible to get the solid-colored background desired. It occurred to me that there is no reason that a different color plastic sheet couldn’t be used to make even more color backgrounds, like light blue, pale yellow and more. It would be easy enough to make such a background from construction paper in a pinch.

This is a box suitable for very small items, such as a pair of glasses, a toy car or a small computer peripheral such as a mouse. In testing I photographed several small items such as batteries, my trackball, a small rock and the like. I used the white insert and I noticed that there is very little shadow at all, though if you look hard enough for it you can see shadows on taller items.

I found one thing about this box that gave me a little concern until I spoke to the vendor about it. I had trouble with the sides of the box staying open properly, and as a result I was constantly fiddling with the sides to keep them open. I finally tried a small paperclip on the sides in the upper corners and that seemed to resolve the issue. A better solution will be to add a little more Velcro, a suggestion I offered to the vendor. This is not a huge problem as I think I could resolve it by opening the box and forcing the crease in the sides to open more so they would press against the sides a little more tightly, and it is easy enough to correct if it appears.

This is a nice photo white box for someone who needs a pure, clean background for capturing images of small items. The light is very bright and with changeable backgrounds one can capture the image just as it’s envisioned. I am pleased with this box and I will be working with it often if not daily.

title: Long Cables, Work Well
review_text:
Most of the USB cables I have are either 3' cables or are really short ones that come with electronic devices. Sometimes a longer cable is really handy, especially when the immediate area surrounding a work space is cramped. I looked to these 10' cables to help alleviate one such issue and I learned a few things. One of those things is that a cable can be too long in some cases, though this is a failure in organization, not in the cable.

These are flat USB cables. Flat cables are less likely to tangle than their round counterparts, but I will confess to preferring round cables anyway (it’s a personal preference, not a technical preference). These are shielded in woven nylon which is great; the nylon is stronger than soft plastic shielding and gives the cable a little more stiffness but does not make the cable so stiff that it’s awkward to run. The connectors are interesting - two-tone plastic that is different than anything else on my desk which makes it a lot easier to determine where both ends of the cable are plugged in. I tried stressing the cable ends at the connectors by trying to pull out the shielding from the plugs and they held firm.

I tried one of these with my phone and it worked just fine, I was able to charge the phone and move data between it and my laptop. I did not attempt a speed test.

There is a big difference between 3' cables, 6' cables and 10' cables. If you need a 6' cable, a 10' cable will leave you trying to figure out what to do with the extra 4' of cable. In my case this meant having to use a twist tie to bunch the cable up in the middle. This is not a criticism but rather a suggestion - get a cable that’s the right length for the job. If you need a 10' cable, these have worked great for me.

These are nice USB cables. They seem to be made well and they work as expected. If you need a really long cable, this is a good choice.

title: Good Looking Speaker, Innovative Design
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:9452f3f4fe85561cedb2616d98f18348]] I have worked with many different Bluetooth speakers, and most of them are very similar in design and sound profile. The iDea Taco is a bit different and is the most innovative of the speakers I have used, not so much in the shape but more in the way it projects sound.

This is a pill-shaped speaker that is angled off at the sides and styled to look like a taco, though it is deceptive to that end. The sound does not come out of the ends but rather it comes out of the bottom. When the speaker is powered on and playing, the sound is reflected off the shelf or desk where it sits and this somehow enhances the sound (I am no expert in acoustics so I can't really explain).

I had no troubles with pairing or connecting. It advertises itself as "iDea Taco" and I was able to pair it to my phone and also to my computer (at different times). I had no trouble streaming to it and it was very responsive.

The sound profile is good, though not perfect. The bass is very good though it is not artificially boosted like with so many other speakers (overdriving bass is the current trend and it drives me crazy as it drowns out the rest of the sound profile). The midrange is full and as a result the music sounds warm, not like it is hollow or in a tunnel. The highs are the soft spot, with very slightly muddied sharps but still mostly clear and warm. The sweet spot for the sound is when the speaker is sitting at approximately a 45 degree angle from vertical, with the actual speaker facing down. It's at this point that the sound is best. This design decision is a bit more innovative than with most speakers I have used which project either straight up or straight out.

This is a solid little device and seems to be assembled well. It has a slight heft to it and it feels very solid - no give in the housing and no noise when shaken.

Overall this is a nice little speaker. It's designed a bit different than other speakers I have used and so far I am very pleased with it.

title: All Metal and Very Quiet
review_text:
Sometimes I like to have a little air moving across my desk when I am working at the computer. Even when it is hot, a little bit of a draft can make it seem cooler. Large desk fans and box fans can create too much air flow, but a small desk fan like a USB fan is often just the ticket for getting the air flow without blowing papers everywhere. I have worked with other BTOOP products and they have all been very good, so I had high expectations for this fan. The only real issue I have had with this fan is that my son has absconded with it and claimed it for himself.

The most obvious advantage of this fan is that it does not require batteries or direct AC power. It plugs into a USB port on a computer, power bank or even a charging block and that is all it needs to run for hours.

What has struck me as most interesting about this fan is that it is all metal, not cheap plastic anywhere. Even the blades of the fan are metal. It’s a refreshing change from all of the plastic junk that is prevalent everywhere. I have a huge air mover in my bedroom and even that fan is mostly plastic.

Considering that this is a metal fan and not a plastic one, the current asking price (under $15, subject to change) is surprising. I would have expected it to cost a lot more.

This fan operates quietly but still is able to move substantial air, enough to cool down a work space.

There are a couple of small improvements in design that would make this fan even better, in my opinion. It is not the easiest to adjust the tilt and having a wing nut to loosen/tighten the screws for tilt would be a big help to that end. That is an easy modification that can be made at home without really any effort. The other improvement would be a variable fan speed setting but this is not a deal-breaker. The price of the fan is compensation enough for these two minor quibbles.

Overall, this is a nice little fan and I like it. I especially appreciate the fact that is it all metal and it works so quietly.

title: Premium Lightning Cable
review_text:
I have only recently started using UGREEN cables and so far every one of their cables I have used has been a top-notch product. I was interested to see how well their lightning cable would work out for me and, based on my experiences with their other cables I expected this cable to be excellent. I have not been disappointed.

First things first – this is an Apple-certified cable which is not insignificant. Because it is certified it will work right with your Apple device and the device will not complain about it being an unrecognized cable. If you have used cheaper cables that do not come with a certification you have seen the warning messages that appear when you connect it. This one will not cause that problem which is good right out of the box.

This cable seems to be well made and so far I have found no issues with build quality or assembly. The insulation is nice and thick and it securely attached on both ends so it will not pull away from the plugs. Each plug is shielded in an aluminum sheath which protects the plug and makes it a little easier to grip. I have the 5’ version of this cable which is nice; I like that I have a little more leeway with the extra length of the cable.

There’s something I want to emphasize about this cable which many might not consider or may think is insignificant. UGREEN has put their name right on the plug ends, where it is easy to see and read. This says that they believe in this product enough to brand it, which is actually uncommon. Most of the cables on my desk are not branded so it is very nice being able to identify a cable by manufacturer. When one goes bad, if it is not branded it is difficult to know where that cable came from. The very best micro USB cable I own is by UGREEN and because it is branded it is very easy for me to identify in the tangle on my desk. Now I can tell which lightning cable is theirs too.

I have not had this cable long enough to see how well it will hold up over time but in the time I have had it, it has been reliable and compatible. I like the extra length too which gives me some flexibility when figuring out where to put it and the device I connect to it.

title: Good Add-On Kit
review_text:
This is a 3-piece accessory kit for a camera with a threaded lens (in my case, a 58mm thread). I use this kit with a Samsung NX-300 with the 18-55mm zoom lens and it fits that lens well. My experience with this kit has been mostly positive.

Included in the kit are two lens hoods and one lens cap. I will discuss each separately.

The lens cap is, to me, the best component in the kit. It does not look like a particularly exciting item, but in this case this lens cap actually fits my lens better than the original cap from the manufacturer. It is tight and is seated evenly on the lens assembly. As an added bonus is has a lanyard that allows it to hang on the lens barrel so it does not need to be specifically tracked when it is not in place covering the lens.

The second item in the kit is a tulip hood for the lens and it is neither better nor worse than the one that came with the camera. It does an acceptable job of keeping the lens in the shade instead of allowing sunlight to hit it directly. Note that when the tulip cover is in place the lens cap will not fit.

The last item in this kit is a rubber hood that works similarly to the tulip hood and it helps prevents direct light from angling in to hit the lens. This one component is the only one in the kit about which I have anything critical to say, and it’s this: when the lens is zoomed all the way in the edges of the hood can be seen in the picture. It does not take much to zoom out past it but it still merits some mention.

I am satisfied with this kit. It includes two hoods and a lens cap that in my case is better than the original that came with my lens. This is a decent kit at a good price.

title: Very Nice ND Filter for 58mm Thread-Size Lenses
review_text:
I have been learning more about photography and as time has permitted I have been improving my skill as an amateur photographer. I have worked with other types of filters, in particular CPL and FL-D filters, but before now I have never worked with ND filters. I have been able to achieve good results with it and so far I am pleased with this filter though I know I have more to learn about it.

A neutral-density filter is used to reduce light reaching the aperture without fiddling too much with the colors. This allows one to get creative with shutter speeds. This particular filter is adjustable and turns on the lens body face, allowing the photographer to increase or decrease the amount of filtering done. At the lowest setting the filter does very little filtering; when turned up to the maximum filtering level very little light gets through and a moire pattern appears so I do not recommend turning up the filter to this level.

To get a feel for how well this filter works I took my camera outside as a big thunderstorm approached and took some pictures of one of the cloud formations. I selected two pictures from that set, one where I did not use the filter and one where I did use it on about 1/4 strength. Although the filter evenly reduced light levels, the color contrast in the filtered image is much more pronounced and obvious.

The most common use for this kind of filter is to reduce the light levels, then take an extended exposure for a scene with motion, such as a waterfall.

This is a very nice filter and I could not be happier with it. It is very easy to use and it really works well.

title: Solid Sound Profile
review_text:
The current trend with ear buds is to boost the bass to the point of overpowering the rest of the sound profile. I don’t particularly like bass that is too heavy because it can give me awful headaches. These buds have the bass boosted but it is not over the top.

These ear buds are very lightweight and low profile. Smaller than many ear buds I have used they fit in my ears very comfortably. The silicone inserts are soft and do not cause any discomfort, but just as important they create a good seal in the ear canal and as a result they have good passive noise canceling (sound isolation). This is a good sign right out of the package - many ear buds I have tried do not seal properly.

The sound profile is the most important aspect of any earphones or ear buds. There are really three areas in the sound profile that merit mention - the highs, the mids and the bass. This set of buds is marketed as heavy bass and that is not completely true. Yes, they do have good bass, but it is not heavily overdriven like most. The bass is a little more front-and-center, not in-your-face, if that makes some sense. The mids are good and the music sounds full as a result, not hollow and depthless. The highs are very bright and clear which is a slight surprise - most ear buds that enhance the bass do so at the expense of the highs, so having a set that had strong bass and highs together is a very nice change of pace.

These buds come with a very small carrying case. It is a pinch case and has enough room for just the buds and the replacement silicone inserts. It is a soft plastic case and provides protection only from dirt and moisture (though by no means waterproof) so this is not a case that will help when the buds are crammed in a pocket or backpack.

This is a very nice set of ear buds at a very nice asking price. They have a very good sound profile and they are comfortable to wear. Keep these in mind when looking for inexpensive buds and good sound.

title: Works Well with Linux
review_text:
I needed a simple dock station to copy some hard disks. The All in 1 HDD Docking System fitted my needs nicely. I was able to insert an old Maxtor IDE drive in the first slot and a brand new SATA SSD in the second slot.

I had hoped to test the one-button copy feature so I powered it up and tried to follow the directions. Both drives were recognized, however I could not get the docking system to perform a drive copy. This could be due to either a brand new, unformatted SSD or due to the use of the Linux EXT2 file system (not FAT or NTFS). If I have a chance I will test copying between two FAT file systems.

With both the Maxtor and SSD plugged in, I added an SD card. I could mount the card and read the files from it, or copy files from it to either of the hard disks or to my system disk!

I tried using both a CF card and an SD card at the same time. However, I was not able to successfully access both at the same time. When I removed the SD card, I could read the CF card.

title: This Hands-Free Kit Gets it Right
review_text:
I have worked with quite a few car kits and some work better than others. Most of them are rechargeable Bluetooth receivers that allow you to turn your car’s stereo system into a hands-free system for talking on the phone while driving, though some plug into the 12V power outlet for power. All of the others I have used have connected to the car stereo by way of the AUX jack. But, not all systems have an AUX input which makes those solutions useless in those situations. I had an FM transmitter solution years ago that allowed me to connect a CD player to my basic AM/FM radio and it worked but I had forgotten about that type of solution until now. This kit works with Bluetooth and FM to connect phones to cars and it works very well. It also has some nice features I wish other kits had.

This is a basic kit that works by allowing the phone to pair with it via Bluetooth and then uses a small, low-power FM transmitter to connect to the car’s audio system on any FM channel desired (I suggest using an unused frequency). Music can be streamed from the phone to the transmitter and from there it goes to the radio frequency in the car. It’s simple in concept and it works. No more AUX jack.

For power the transmitter plugs into a USB port, and the kit includes a 2-port 12V plug. This allows for powering the transmitter and still having enough power for another device like the phone or a GPS navigator. One port on the adapter is a 1.0A and the other is a 2.1A so if you have a high-speed cable and your device can accept a high-speed charge it will work with the adapter. Because the adapter has two ports and it allows for completely disconnecting the transmitter it can be used for charging two devices at once.

Regardless of where in the vehicle the 12V adapter lives, the kit comes with a magnetic pad for attaching the receiver so that the receiver can be mounted almost anywhere. This is important - it means that it can be put in an optimal spot so that when speaking it has the best chance for picking up the voice clearly which is a very good thing. In my car, the 12V outlet lives under the center console so other kits sometimes do not get the best reception for my voice.

Sound quality is clear for both caller and receiver, particularly because the transmitter can be placed anywhere. When there is no competition for the channel the sound is as good as an AUX-connected sound source.

This hands-free kit for the car is better than most others I have used as it is easier to place the transmitter to get clear voice transmission and it does not require an AUX port on the care stereo system to work. I am pleased with it and am happy to recommend it.

title: Excellent Cables at a Great Price
review_text:
I have a good tangle of cables in my home office for a variety of devices that require a micro-USB cable. Most of these cables are very nondescript and I have no idea who made them, though there are a couple of them that have manufacturer names printed on the plugs on the end. Most are plain black and are mostly indistinguishable from one another. These cables from Magic-T are absolutely the most easily identifiable cables on the desk and it has made it very easy to assign cables to every device on the desk. But, there is more to these cables than just pretty colors.

The most obvious advantage of this cable set is the colors. Each of these cables is a different color and none of them are black or gray - there’s blue, pink, orange and green. And, even more important than the color is the fact that they are insulated in nylon weave, not plastic coating, which in my experience holds up a bit better under stress and the result is a more reliable cable.

The plugs on both ends are metal shielding with a plastic base, sufficient to give these strength for the connections. The cables have been inserted in the bases and attached within, not attached to the plug base, but those connections are very tight and seem to be solid so I am not concerned about them pulling loose.

Each cable is about six and a half feet in length which is much more convenient for me than the regular 3' cables.

These cables are capable of high-speed charging so if you have a device and a charger that are both capable of high-speed charging then these cables will work well for you. I used one for my tablet and a high-speed USB charger and the tablet did charge faster than when using a lower-grade cable.

I want to mention the pricing. As I write this, the price on this set of four cables is about $9. That’s about $2.25 per cable, and the cables are of good quality. The price can change of course, but at the current price this is an absolute bargain.

There’s something else I need to mention. The manufacturer offers a 12-month warranty on these cables, and to me that’s just amazing. For a cable that costs less than $2.50 per individual cable the manufacturer thinks enough of their product to back it with a 12-month warranty. I doubt I would ever need to use the warranty for one of these, but it’s reassuring to know the manufacturer believes in their products.

It is hard to find fault with these cables. They are made well, they are easily identifiable and they are very inexpensive. This is a fine set at a great price.

title: Works Great with Raspberry Pi
review_text:
I selected this keyboard/touchpad with the idea of using it with my tablet. Admittedly I mistakenly thought it was a Bluetooth keyboard which would have made it suitable for my tablet but this turned out to be a misunderstanding on my part. That said, it has proven to be a very handy keyboard in more ways than I had originally planned. In particular, in addition to working with Windows and Linux it works with Raspberry Pi which opens a whole world of possibilities for this keyboard.

This keyboard is very small, barely bigger than a Hershey bar, and it has a full set of keys as well a touchpad and mouse buttons on the right side. This is sufficient for doing pretty much everything you’d want to do, including surfing the web, text editing and software development. Granted, the size makes it less than ideal for some of these functions but it does work as a full keyboard/mouse combination if you want to use it that way.

Right out of the box, the switch was on and the keyboard had completely drained its battery so it had to be plugged in and charged overnight. This was a surprise but was not a big deal, just unusual.

When connected to a Windows 8 system the OS recognized it and immediately it was usable. It required no special drivers, no configuration changes or anything else – just plug it in and turn it on. It worked the same under Linux as well.

The real test for this keyboard/mouse was on a Raspberry Pi system. The keyboard connected and worked without a glitch – expected since it worked fine with Ubuntu Linux but not guaranteed as the kernel was known to work but the hardware was not yet tested. With a second external keyboard connected it was possible to type on both at the same time and also to use the other keyboard as a regular keyboard and the other just as a mouse.

There are a number of other SBC types and designs out there, and there is no reason that this device should not work with any of them that have a Linux-based kernel. Embedded Windows system should also support it as well.

Though I have not really tested the full range it is good to at least 10 feet. At that range the system still recognized input from the keyboard and touchpad without any issues.

So far I have found only one issue with this keyboard and that’s the space bar. I habitually press the space bar in the middle, and on this keyboard the press sensors are on the ends. The spacebar is not quite stiff enough and when pressed in the middle it bows instead of pressing down on the sensors, thereby not registering the press. To get it to recognize the press I have to press on the ends specifically. This is a minor irritant and is a very small price to pay for what this device offers.

This is a very small but fully functional keyboard/touchpad combination that works with multiple configurations. It connects easily and so far has given no real operational issues. Keep in mind that this thing is extremely small, though, which is great for portability, mobility and economy of space but less pleasant for systems that aren’t being transported anywhere.

title: Very Quiet and Moves a Lot of Air
review_text:
A good laptop chiller pad becomes important when you run a lot of graphics-intensive games or if you are doing anything requiring the CPU to run a heavy load. Heat is the enemy of a computer system and the fastest way to a dead laptop is to not deal with heat issues when there’s a problem. I had a chill pad some time ago and it was sub-par. This one by LotFancy is much better and it does a good job.

First off, this is a big chill pad, the same basic dimensions as my laptop but much thicker. I have a 15.6" laptop and this pad is almost a perfect and exact fit, with only a narrow area in the back that extends past the end of the laptop. If you want a small and petite chill pad, this is not the one you want. It does incline too with a metal bar and slots in the case so that the laptop can be angled up. This actually is good for exposing it to even more air.

This chill pad connects to a USB port so it can either be plugged into a port on the computer or into a hub. There are two ports on it and both seem to be the same in terms of how the pad operates. That is, the pad operates at the same speed regardless of which port is used. There are also two buttons on the pad for turning it on. One turns on the larger fan in the middle, and the other turns on all the other fans. Two green LEDs next to those buttons indicate that the pad is powered on and working.

This pad moves a lot of air and it does a good job of cooling the laptop. But, it does so very quietly which is a huge plus. I have it set up in my home office and the pad makes about as much noise as a desktop computer, maybe a little less. The sound it makes is a gentle hum.

When powered on each fan has a bright blue LED in it. While they look cool when there’s no laptop on the pad, they’re all but invisible when the laptop is sitting on top. There isn’t even much of a glow coming from the pad. I turned on the pad, turned out all of the lights and the glow from the laptop screen was enough to overpower any light that might have come from the pad. Except for the low hum I wouldn’t know it was even turned on.

This is a good chill pad. It works quietly and it moves a lot of air. Compared to other chill pads I have used this one is very good and I am happy to recommend it.

title: Solid Lightning Cable
review_text:
It’s good to have a solid, workable cable when charging and transferring data, and lightning cables are what works for Apple products. After the original cable that came with an iPhone failed I looked to this cable as a replacement. It has filled the need very nicely.

First and foremost, this cable comes with Apple certification and that’s important. It means that Apple endorses this cable to work with their iPhone and iPad products, which in turn means that compatibility is not an issue (and neither are those compatibility messages).

This cable seems to be a bit better than the manufacturer-supplied cable. It is well made and I believe it will hold up longer than the cable before it which died through stress bends at the end points. It is a little thicker and a little heavier which should hold up well. And, although it has a little heavier insulation the Apple-side plug is narrow enough to fit and connect even through more bulky cases which is a problem with some cables.

So far I have had no issues with this cable. It works well, is fully compatible and it appears to be better made than the OEM cable.

title: Suitable for Bird Watching and Amateur Astronomy in the Field
review_text:
My wife loves birdwatching and our teenage son enjoys stargazing so we have an assortment of binoculars and inexpensive telescopes. Before this monocular I had never used one and even though I have not had it very long at all I am already very pleased with it. Though it is ideal for bird watching and field work, it also will work as an amateur telescope.

At roughly 7" long, this monocular is large enough to be usable but small enough to fit in a coat pocket or even in a briefcase. It comes in a nice, nylon-weave carrying pouch that even has a belt loop so carrying it into the field is easy and does not take up extra room. It also has a holding strap much like a camcorder does so it can be held more securely. It has a small metal tripod suitable for setting up on a desk or table. It’s not a big tripod - the legs extend to 7.5" - but is works well if you are recording or are seated and need a steady hand. Finally, it includes a microfiber cleaning cloth in the box for wiping the lenses safely without scratching them.

This is a waterproof monocular and everything about it showcases that. There are two rubberized caps for either end that cover the lenses and keep out moisture and dust when not in use. These are physically attached to the barrel (one by a rubber flap and one by a nylon cord) so there is no issue with losing the caps. Most of the barrel is rubberized as well except for the focus knob assembly and where it attaches.

I used it to focus on the tree line behind the house (roughly 30 yards away) and was very pleased with how sharp and clear I was able to get the image. From the front of the house I was able to focus on the stop sign at the end of the street and had no issue with getting fine edge detail even at a distance of roughly a football field. The focus is very smooth and easy to adjust and getting the image in perfect focus is not the least bit difficult.

Though I enjoy cameras and optical equipment and I have learned a good bit about optical equipment I am a far cry from being an expert, so I took this monocular to work and approached two teammates who are very well-versed in optics, photography and astronomy and I asked them to look it over and give me their honest opinion. Both of them examined it and expressed their approval. They both said similar things about it: the image through this monocular is very bright and clear, the focus is very smooth and it seems to be very well made. They both made a comment about the lens and that it was very good due to not having a darkened coating.

One of my teammates told me to try looking at the stars with it. I had not really considered this but knew this would be an excellent test for it so I went outside after dark and pointed it skyward. Though I can definitely see more detail through a dedicated telescope, I was able to make out some of the larger surface detail on the moon including the high point in the middle of a crater. I was hindered by the fact that it is a full moon right now so I will have to try again this weekend during the eclipse. I then picked out a planet and looked at it through the monocular. Though it is a little tough to make out, I know I found Jupiter as I could see three of the moons as bright spots not visible to the naked eye (I have looked at it through a telescope so I recognize it from seeing it already). Finally I discovered a cluster of stars I could not see without magnification. This monocular is certainly not as good as a dedicated telescope but it is sufficient when camping and it eliminates the need to pack a big, bulky telescope unless you want to see more detail.

This is a great tool for use in the field. It has very good range, the image is bright and clear and it even is sufficient for stargazing should you choose to use it for everything on the road. Great product!

title: Amazing Sound, Especially for the Price
review_text:
I spend a good deal of time with headphones on or earbuds in my ears and I have formulated some very strong ideas of what makes a pair of headphones or earbuds worth consideration. I was anxious to try the Sound Intone i66 earbuds and they have far exceeded my expectations, especially considering the cost (as I write this, they are going for about $11, but price may change). For such low-cost earbuds these are among some of the best I have used.

Ok, right out of the package - I received a pink pair of earbuds. Bright, bubblegum pink! That does not bother me in the least as color is irrelevant but being pink these are just perfect for a teenage girl. These also come in brown so there is a choice if pink is not desired.

In the package are the earbuds and three sets of ear inserts so that getting the right fit is easy. The inserts are a little more stiff than some of the others I have used but they are not uncomfortable. The slight stiffness might be slightly less comfortable than more supple inserts but they’re much less likely to tear. To me that is a very worthwhile tradeoff. When inserted these buds create a very good seal and they do a fine job of sound isolation.

Like most headphones available today these have a talk feature that allows them to be used with a cell phone for two-way conversation. I admit that I have not tried these for conversation but will try these and come back to update this review when I have done so. I do like the fact that the microphone hangs about 6" from the ear piece which positions it almost perfectly by the mouth.

The most important aspect of any set of earphones or earbuds is the sound profile. For a very inexpensive set of earbuds, these get the sound awfully close to perfect. The highs are right on target and they are clear and crisp without being oversharp. The midrange is solid and full. The bass is strong - very slightly overdriven but not to the point of extreme. I compared these to headphones costing over $100 and these compete very well.

I am very hard-pressed to find much to fault with these earbuds. These fit well and they seem to be well-made, but their strength is their sound quality which is tough to beat in the under-$20 price range. And, if you really want a pair of pink earbuds, these will definitely fill the need. Regardless of the color, these are surprisingly good earbuds, better than most, but definitely one of the best values available.

title: Very Deep Bass
review_text:
Sound Intone makes good, inexpensive headphones and the HD-680 headphones is one of their newest offerings. I will admit to initially disliking this particular set of headphones, but a conversation with the manufacturer and persistence with a 16-channel equalizer has brought my opinion of these headphones up substantially. I can’t say these are my favorite headphones as I am not into heavy bass, but I am pleased enough with them to use them when working on my computer.

Right out of the box, these are striking phones that are quite attractive. I have the blue and white edition and my teenage son’s first words upon seeing them was, “those look great!” These are very lightweight and as a result they have a light fit. I personally prefer a headphone that fits more tightly but that’s a personal preference, not a criticism. The padding is firm but not hard and I did notice that these phones get a little warm on the ears over time - again not a big deal but worth mentioning.

When it comes to the build quality, the strongest feature of these phones is the cord - I am exceptionally partial to woven tangle-free cords versus plastic coated wire.

The difficulty I had with these phones initially was the sound profile. The bass is exceptionally heavy, so heavy that it drowns out the highs quite a bit and the result is a sound that is muddy and unclear. It took some time to realize that this is very reminiscent of the sound you get at an outdoor concert - the bass carries forever and the highs get lost. The midrange is absolutely solid. I don’t care for bass that’s so heavy (it gives me a headache) so I fed everything through a 16-channel equalizer. It took a good bit of experimentation and persistence but I finally was able to find the balance to get the sound right and now these phones sound great. The issue is overdriven bass; once I squelched some of the bass and boosted the treble channels just right the profile is solid. They still sound a little like being in a concert hall but that’s more than acceptable.

Oddly enough, these sound good when listening to straight speech, even without an equalizer.

These headphones are different than most other phones I have used. The typical headphone I use does not boost the bass to an extreme. If you really, really like bass, then these phones are for you and will not disappoint. If you prefer something a little more balanced, feed the sound through an equalizer and the sound can be made near-perfect. Although I did not initially like these phones I have come to appreciate them and can recommend them.

title: Good Rear-View Video System; Poor Documentation
review_text:
Many cars on the market come with a rear-view camera that allows for seeing where the vehicle is moving when in reverse. Often the view appears on a dashboard screen. This is handy when parking and maneuvering while the vehicle is backing up. For vehicles that do not have a rear-view camera the alternative is to add on a kit that provides the same functionality. This is my first experience with such a kit and so far I am pleased with it. It does require doing a little work on the vehicle to set it up but the effort is worth it.

The package contains everything needed to set up this camera system. In addition to the camera and the screen, the kit includes the mounting screws for the actual camera as well as all of the wiring to connect everything together and to the power (reverse lights). There is also a mini-remote for interacting with the video screen though this is slightly inconvenient.

I spent a good deal of time reading and rereading the directions and concluded that the instructions could have been better. There are three pieces of documentation in the box; one shows a generalized set of four different configurations for connecting everything together (the fourth diagram on this sheet matches the configuration you want), one is a photocopied image of a wired system and the third is a “User’s Manual” which is one half-sheet of paper with a brief summarization of the product. There really needs to be a better documentation set than this.

If you are not skilled in working with electrical systems, either plan on this taking a good while or have someone you trust install the system. It’s not especially hard to set one of these up, but it does take some patience and a little bit of knowledge of the layout of the car’s wiring. I have worked on car electrical systems in the distant past so I had a vague familiarity, but it still took me a while to have everything set up and working.

Once wired the system is fairly straightforward to use. If it is wired up properly (meaning everything is connected to power on both ends and the two main components can see one another) it works nicely. The image when the camera is feeding to the monitor is bright and reasonably clear; the brightness can be adjusted as needed which helps when using this system at night. Another reviewer commented that he used a different camera connected to this system - while I am personally satisfied with the image quality, it’s reassuring to know that you can use another video camera if desired or necessary.

The addition of the remote will appeal to some, but for me it’s a component that can easily be lost. The menu system on the monitor provides the same functionality as the remote and this is good enough for me.

This is my first experience with rear-view video systems and though it gave me a little trouble setting up it was from lack of good documentation and inexperience, not from being a bad product. Once installed this is a nice and easy-to-use video system. Time will tell how long it works.

title: Excellent Camera but Troublesome Install
review_text:
FOSCAM is a well-known name when it comes to security cameras and security equipment and they make a good variety of security solutions for home and business use. The F19803P camera is a wireless IP camera that is weatherproof, has night vision and can be accessed via smartphone. One configured and set up on the network it works great but the setup process can be a very painful one.

In the box is the actual camera, the antenna, power adapter, mounting kit, installation software and an Ethernet cable. The camera housing is roughly the size of a new roll of bathroom tissue - very small, compact and lightweight. The mounting kit is a small but solid painted aluminum bracket plus the screws needed to secure it. When mounted properly, this camera can be very inconspicuous.

Following the included directions, I installed the software first and then hooked up the camera to the router. According to the included documentation the IPCamera application should immediately see the camera and from there one can select the camera, log into it and manipulate it as needed. This did not work for me and the camera never did appear. I tried downing my firewall, I tried connecting to a different router and even tried directly connecting to the camera and still was unable to see it. I finally managed to reach the camera by opening the FOSCAM client software and telling it to search for cameras. When I did this, the camera finally appeared, and the IPCamera application showed it too. This works but runs contrary to the documentation.

I did get into the camera finally and was able to change the username and password. I also set up the wireless network settings and found other settings to adjust like IR timer, time source and more.

I found that the camera’s administration settings can be accessed as needed through the IP address and specifying port 88 (unless the port is deliberately changed). I strongly encourage assigning a fixed IP address to the camera via DHCP through the router; otherwise, the IP address can change and accessing the camera gets more difficult. I learned this the hard way, when I had the Ethernet MAC defined but not the WiFi MAC in my router’s DHCP table. My fault, but this was made more difficult by the IPCamera application still not seeing the camera and I had to let the client software scan again.

I made one more mistake and reset the camera via the reset button and it cleared everything I had set already: user name, password, everything. I was concerned that I would lose everything again with a power failure so as a test I unplugged the camera for a few hours and plugged it in again, and fortunately it retained its configuration.

The camera cannot see my 5G network, only my 2.4G network. However, even though my computer is on the 5G network it still can access the camera. title: Solid, Well Made and Very Smooth
review_text:
Fishing is one of the activities I have loved ever since I was very young and able to hold a fishing rod. Though I have used several types of fishing reels my personal preference is spinning reels. There are a number of reputable brands available and I have tried several - Lew’s, Quantum, Daiwa, Mitchell’s, Shakespeare and more. Until recently I was unfamiliar with KastKing as a brand and had no experience with their fishing tackle, and in a short time I have come to realize I have been missing something important. I received a Triton 3000 spinning reel for test and evaluation and have been thoroughly pleased with it.

This reel has some heft to it, very solid and tight. It’s more substantial than many reels I have used but it’s also not the largest or heaviest either. In terms of size and weight, it falls in the middle of the pack of reels I have used for freshwater fishing and it’s a bit on the small size compared to many saltwater reels I have used. I have larger hands and the size it about right, but someone with smaller hands might find a smaller size (like the Triton 2000 or 2500) a better match. In terms of assembly, there is nothing loose or flimsy on this reel at all and there is nothing that required tightening or adjustment right out of the box (which has been a problem with some others I have used in the past). Overall, this is a solid and well-assembled reel.

Appearance-wise, this reel is absolutely gorgeous. It is a deep shade of purple, almost black, with chrome and nickel colors on the spool, bail and handle. Appearance is not really all that important but it certainly does add to the package, and this is a reel that you won’t be embarrassed to break out in front of others. It relies on simple elegance, not bright flashy colors to make its statement.

This reel has a good-sized spindle on it and it can hold a good amount of line. I put at least 150 yards of 8-lb test on this reel and there’s a lot of room for more. The spindle is tall, not deep.

Ok, on to the really important stuff - how does this reel perform?

This reel has 10 ball-bearings for forward reeling and the reel is about as smooth and quiet when retrieving as could be. Cheaper reels (cheaper meaning lower quality) tend to grind a little bit when retrieving or they make substantial amounts of noise, and some reels even have a clicker in them to mask the sound when retrieving. Some also feel hollow when retrieving, but the Triton feels solid and smooth without a hint of inferior build quality. As nice as the reeling forward is, one of the most important features in a good reel to me is a zero-reverse clutch and this reel has it down. When engaged, the reel will not reverse even a little and to me this is worth its weight in gold.

One very real issue I have seen with some spinning reels is a poorly shaped bail that interferes with the distance when casting. If the bail is too shallow and does not allow enough clearance to allow the line to fly freely off the spindle, it can seriously impact casting distance. Fortunately, this reel has a very wide bail that has plenty of clearance around the spindle and it does not impact the cast at all. I get very good distance when casting as a result. Instead of concentrating on distance, the angler can instead concentrate on accuracy (and after years of practice I am still working on improving my accuracy).

I tested the drag and am pleased with it as well. When tightening the drag the dial does not get more difficult to turn like on some other reels and the drag gradually makes the spindle harder and harder to turn. It is not a graduated turn, meaning it does not increase in steps so there is essentially a limitless variance in how tight the drag can be adjusted. The dial remains easy to turn all the way through the turning range until it is tightened completely, at which point it just stops.

When reeling, either forward or backward, this reel remains balanced and does not wobble much at all. It is hard to notice wobble when the reel is attached to a rod so I tried something when I had not yet attached the reel to a rod. Holding the reel in one hand by the assembly and giving the handle a good spin, I was able to feel the reel gyrating very slightly but not appreciably. I tried the same with another high-quality reel and it was similar. This is not the case with cheaper reels which may or may not balance.

I love the fact that the reel is mounted on an arm long enough to prevent the bail from whacking me on the knuckles when I retrieve. A reel mounted too close to the rod due to a short arm can have this unpleasant effect and I look for this problem specifically so I can avoid it. I also appreciate that the handle is far enough from the reel body to avoid hitting my hand.

In the box with the reel is a velvety microfiber cloth bag for storage and transport when the reel is not in use. This is the only reel I have ever had that has come with such and it’s a nice touch. The bag is useful for keeping the reel clean and also for keeping supplies with it, like a small container of lubricating oil, an extra spool of line or even an extra lure or two (though this is no substitute for a tackle box).

I am very hard-pressed to find anything to criticize about this reel. It is a solid and well-made, looks great and works like a dream. I believe I have found my new primary reel.

title: Superb 12' Audio Extension Cable
review_text:
I work with a sound mixing board that is used to connect multiple instruments and sound inputs to an amplification system. The limitation of the system is the cabling which prevents relocating certain pieces of equipment. One of the biggest trouble spots in the system happens to be audio cabling between the mixing board and the computer used to process the data. This audio cable has helped remedy that situation.

This is one of the better-made cables I have used. Instead of a cheap, plastic-coated cable made of low-gauge wire, it is instead a heavy-gauge wire insulated in a thick nylon braid. I have had bad fortune with cheaper cables as they have a bad tendency to degrade when twisted or pulled tight. Another point of failure is the connection between the plug and the cable which is usually molded plastic that is much too flexible and allows the cable to break. This cable has a metal cap that screws down over the plug and adds a lot of stiffness to the connector. This is probably one of the heaviest audio cables I have used.

This particular cable is 12' and using it as an extension in the sound system it has added a lot of flexibility to the configuration.

This is a very good audio cable. It works as it is supposed to work and it is designed to last much longer than the average cable. This is an excellent choice if you need an audio cable that will not wear out or break quickly, and at 12' there is plenty of cable for almost any use.

title: Excellent Audio Extension Cable
review_text:
One of the frequent frustrations with headphones is the limited cord length of the phones - typically about 3'. Bluetooth is one way around this - an inexpensive receiver can turn a good set of wired phones into a wireless pair - but this is not always practical. An extension cable is a much more practical solution in many situations and is a lot less expensive in most cases. This extender cable is one of the better ones I have used.

This is not a cheap, basic audio cable. It is a heavier-gauge wire encased in braided nylon insulation. Though braided nylon is becoming more common, plastic coating is still the standard and in my experience the nylon braid holds up under heavy use much better. More interesting are the plugs on the end of the cable, though - instead of just a molded plastic grip on the end, this cable has a substantial metal cap that screws down and gives the whole cap much more sturdiness. This won’t help with constant sharp tugging at a tight angle but it does all but eliminate most stresses on the plug.

I should mention that this cable is for stereo audio only and does not work for replacing a cable used for talk (never mind that there’s no microphone). It will work with other cables that are set up for talk, but once this cable is in the mix the ability to talk goes away. That’s not a defect but a design decision. So, if you plan to use this to extend the reach of a two-way headset it will not work.

This particular cable is 6' and I have it connected to my headphones and that gives me much more range to move around my work area.

This is a very good audio cable. It works as it is supposed to work and it is designed to last much longer than the average cable. This is an excellent choice if you need an audio-only cable that will not wear out or break quickly.

title: Superb Tablet Stand, Suitable for Industrial Use
review_text:
I have a 10" tablet and it primarily gets used as an e-reader and as a music streaming device. It's a great device and I love it, but I do get frustrated with figuring out where to put it when I am streaming music through it. Although it is a relatively small device it does take up some room on the desk when in a stand case. I have tried suction mounts to attach it to a window and that works fine but the window cannot move and when the window is cold the suction mount lets go. This flexible mount for tablets is a very good solution for my needs and is far better constructed than suggested by the product description.

This is a simple mount in concept and design. It is flexible coil tube with a screw-on vice clamp attached on one end and an adjustable frame-style bracket attached via a ball joint to the other. In the box the unit comes unassembled and requires less than two minutes to put together. When finished, the whole thing is approximately 3' long.

Everything about this mounting stand suggests that it is built to last and is designed to hold up under heavy use. The coil tube is about the heaviest I have ever seen: it is roughly a half inch in diameter and is exceptionally stiff which makes it well suited for supporting the weight of the tablet. The item description here says it will support 2.2 pounds but it will support a little more than that (though I would not try to put much extra on there, particularly if the coil is horizontal).

The coil attaches to the vice clamp via a threaded machine screw assembly and it has enough threading to allow the coil to turn 360 degrees without becoming detached. This allows the tablet to be swung around a work area in an arch without having to really do anything that requires any effort. While this is great, what really caught my attention is that the clamp itself can be screwed to the coil in two ways at 90-degree angles (top or side) so that the clamp can be attached to an anchored surface that is either horizontal or vertical. This is one of those design decisions that just makes sense but I have seen very few manufacturers make this kind of effort.

The coil is covered by a very heavy plastic sleeve which protects the tube and makes flexing the tube easier on the hands.

The mounting bracket is connected to the top of the flexible tube by a ball joint, similar to the kind of joints many GPS navigators use in cars to attach to the suction base. When I first attached the bracket to the coil I put it on upside down, which is not a big deal except that the weight of the tablet worked against the joint and it tilted downward slightly. The bracket itself is a standard slider with a lever that presses against the slider which then catches on teeth on the frame to lock it in place. There's a fair bit of padding on the bracket to protect the tablet when it's being clamped in and when the position is being adjusted.

This mounting stand is of such heavy construction that it suggests the stand was designed for industrial use. While it is just fine for home use and is not out of place in a professional office, it is a good for a manufacturing assembly line or even a busy retail location.

This is a great mounting stand for tablets in 7"-11" range. The whole stand is very sturdy and solid and is build to last. Based on my experience with it I can heartily recommend it to any one who needs a mounting solution for a tablet.
