title: First impressions and background
review_text:
Just got this and started playing with it, but first a little background.

I also have two 5 Blacks and a 7 Black. I drive a truck (truck, not peekup) and use these to record my trips and the traffic around me. I record several hours of video every day. With a minor amount of effort, these work much better than typical dashcams. I use them without batteries inside the cab, with USB-C cables powering them. They tend to overheat with the batteries installed when mounted inside the windshield. The 5s still overheat sometimes without the battery. The 7 seldom does. They're often in the sun for hours at a time, so this isn't really a fault. It's not what they're designed to do. The 7 stays connected to the app much better than the 5s do. It's just a much more capable camera all around.

The Hero 7 Black TimeWarp and stabilization are first rate. The first video I took using it on my Jeep, a friend thought I'd bought a gyro-stabilized mount. It's that good. I assume the 8 is at least as good. I expect it to be better.

I've also owned a cheaper "Action Camera". It actually handled the heat better, until the battery swelled up and destroyed the camera. If you're looking for a toy, those are fine. If you want something that lasts, GoPro, with all its faults, is just about all there is. Nothing else does what they do while taking a substantial amount of abuse.

title: Cheap fun, Great as a dash cam
review_text:
Akaso Brave 4 (Updated) Review

Note: WiFi apps tested using a Google LG Nexus 5x without a sim card, which is a spare phone I use to control my GoPro Hero4. I haven't tested it with my Galaxy S9, because I don't plan to use them together. You may have different results with a different phone, and there may be a better app than the recommended one. LD Cam, for instance, almost works better, but not quite.

Note2: Manufacturer claims "Since 4K resolution is too big, APP does not support." Well, the GoPro app does. I think it's the software library used in many of the other apps that limit the size to 1080p. USB transfers work extremely well. It identifies as a USB drive on the PC and other devices.

Pros:
-Inexpensive compared to GoPro (less than a used Hero 4 Black)
-4K/24fps is higher frame rate than GoPro Hero 4
-Simple to use (other than the WiFi app)
-Plenty of useful settings and features
-Can be used with a PC as a webcam
-Windows 10 recognizes it and loads a driver for it
-Connects via USB-OTG to Galaxy S9 flawlessly for transferring files
-Doesn't overheat like both my GoPro Hero 4 and Hero 7 Black.
-Very lightweight.
-Works great when set up as a dash cam.
-Doesn't overheat and shut down like a GoPro.

Cons:
-Recommended WiFi apps don't support 4K (yet?)
-Recommended WiFi apps require mobile data be turned off (even without a sim card)
-Recommended WiFi apps don't stay connected with my Nexus 5x
-WiFi apps reset camera settings to arbitrary values
-WiFi has to be turned off and back on and app restarted if it disconnects
-Battery cover could be easier to remove
-Not a rugged camera (though not that heat sensitive)
-Klemme 1, an open tripod mount, doesn't hold the camera firmly so wouldn't work as an action mount (used a heat gun to tighten it up and it's tolerable now.

Other:
Though this looks like a GoPro Hero 4, and is very similar in size and layout, it's only similar. They're different enough to prevent using a Hero 4 case. Not much. Just a little. But enough. That's unfortunate, because the Suptig case I have works with an external battery that allows me to record for several hours (5+) with the Hero 4. I was hoping this would work with that case, but it won't. That's what happens when I have unreasonable expectations.

It abruptly adjusts to changing light conditions but lags slightly behind during rapidly changing conditions, particularly when using time-lapse, so that going from the darkness under a bridge to bright sunlight while driving often results in a total whiteout. I haven't notice the same effect with the GoPro Hero 4, and I suspect that it ramps a bit more slowly from darkness to light to avoid this effect.

If the recommended WiFi app, or the alternative worked better, I'd give it one more star (gave it that one more star after using it as a dash cam). Even with all the cons relating to WiFi, I actually like the camera, and think it's worth the ~$80 I paid for it.

review_text:
My rating is my first impression of the entire package, without knowing how well the battery itself will hold up. The battery was a higher capacity than the original, and physically larger. There was space in the DEZL 770 for the larger battery, that had been filled by a plastic card the original battery was stuck to.

The original was an 1100 mAH single-cell Lithium, while the replacement was a 1500 mAH of the same voltage. The Torx driver included appears to be a T6, while the 770 required a T9, which I already had. The pry tool included is something I'll probably use again. It does the job and seems to be made of quality materials. The disc included was for a DEZL 760, which is very similar, and possibly explains the incorrect driver.

The Garmin powered up and is currently charging fine. The original battery would only last about 5 minutes, which wasn't critical, but the device was occasionally resetting while plugged in and tracking, which I'm hoping was due to the battery being at the end of its life. Considering the price of this battery, compared to buying a new GPS, this is really a bargain if it solves the issue. If not, it'll still be a good spare if I buy a new device, with a good battery.

I can't comment on the video disc included, because I didn't use it. Replacing the battery isn't difficult, but does require some care. For someone who's never done something like this before, it might be a good idea to get a 10-year-old to help. I've been taking things apart for at least 55 years, and most of the time can put them back together. My philosophy relies on the fact that if it's not working now, I can't either fix it, or screw it up bad enough that it'll need to be replaced.

title: Good deal for the money
review_text:
I'm pretty picky about how good speakers perform. I'm not a hard nose audiophile, but I know good speakers when I hear them. I have used the same song for decades to truly test the quality of the bass. That song is Alan Parson's "The Raven" and the bass test is the very last note in the song. Most speaker systems cannot handle this deep bass guitar note at any volume. This set did. So as far as the bass, this speaker set passed the toughest test I could throw at it.

The high end was strong and clean, the midrange was the only level I saw a little lacking. This was playing music of the classic rock genre. I play my music pretty exclusively through Windows Media Player which offers a built-in equalizer. Just a little adjusting on the equalizer and I had all levels well balanced, sound was very good.

Some reviewers had mentioned hearing a hum or the like from the right speaker (the one which contains the power and volume controls). When I first hooked everything up out of the box I heard it too. It was noticeable and given time I could see it becoming irritating. I know what causes this hum and how to fix the problem. The problem is caused by poor shielding on the speaker wiring. I added 3 ft. extensions that were double shielded and lo and behold...no more hum, dead silence. I have since put 10 ft. double shielded extensions on both speakers and they are working flawlessly with zero degradation in performance. If you check the answered questions you will find the exact extensions you need. Be careful, not any VGA extension will work for the right speaker! Keep the original speaker wires away from any power cords or power sources and you should get the same result in the end.

I haven't had these speakers for very long so I can't comment on longevity yet. If they unexpectedly have problems I will definitely update this review. But in my honest opinion they seem like a good deal for the money.

I would honestly expect to pay hundreds more for a camera of this quality and though it is not Wi-Fi compatible, transference from camera to computer was not difficult at all. title: Doesn't focus on what you want
review_text:
I have a hard time with this camera. Maybe I'm just not camera savvy enough, but I seriously just wanted a simple point and shoot that would produce good quality photos. This camera comes with a ridiculous amount of fancy settings which I'm sure a lot of people enjoy.

A big reason we got it was to replace our DSLR which I never really learned how to use and I wanted something simpler. I try to take photos of birds in the back yard and this camera is completely hopeless with that. It will not focus on anything you want it to focus on, especially if there's any movement. It'll focus right next to the bird or behind the bird or under the bird or wherever. So you have to try to zoom in to the bird so the camera focuses on it, then zoom out again and hope that it stays focused on your bird (or whatever).

If you're looking to take photos of wildlife or anything of that sort, I'd find something else. We've switched back to the DSLR for wildlife photos so this camera will sit around to be used once a year with family or something. Hopefully it takes good landscape photos but I haven't seen a setting for that yet.

This is exactly what I wanted for my new Paperwhite, which I got for a Prime Day Deal in July 2019. A 10th generation/2018 Paperwhite.
I had two wishes for my case: that it had a kickstand and that it was yellow. Perfect.
The strap in the cover to help hold it is a little small and tight, so if you have big hands it might not work for you. I don't really use it much. The strap clipped to the corner to carry it isn't bad though, if you need that sort of thing.
I use the kickstand all the time though. I was always looking for things to lean my old kindle against to read while eating lunch, and now I can do it easily. Love it.
And I love the yellow--it's nice and bright! Not quite eye-watering, not quite mustard. A wonderful shade.

title: PROBLEMS
review_text:
I've only had this laptop for a year and a half. It's given me problems before, but recently I had to take it in to get professionally fixed. Apparently windows had a bad update or something, and I spent $125 fixing it. A week later the same problems I was having previously showed back up again. Now my trackpad isn't working. In fact, when I go into devices and drivers, it doesn't say there's a trackpad at all. There's nothing for me to try to update. Why would my laptop get rid of my trackpad? All I did was put it to sleep overnight! The only way to use it now is to plug in a mouse. I tried downloading the trackpad drivers-- no luck. I tried a system restore and it won't do the restore. So now I'll have to take it in to get fixed again for another couple hundred dollars. I spent almost $1000 on this piece of junk and I do NOTHING that would cause problems on a basic laptop. I use Word, upload photos, and surf the internet and social media. I do not game and I do not go on porn sites or anything sketchy. I don't download random files from the internet. I have virus protection and malware. Never again, HP!
Update: When I updated the BIOS driver, I would get my trackpad mouse back. This happened multiple times--and every time nothing worked except updating that already updated BIOS driver. Even the guys at the repair shop didn't know that something like that would "fix" it.
Update 6/5/2019: It's been less than two years since I bought this laptop. I have never mistreated it--never slammed the lid, never dropped it, nothing. But last weekend when I opened the lid I heard a "pop" and found a shard of plastic on my desk. One of the hinges became misaligned somehow, and then I could neither close it nor open it further without the outside backing of the lid forcefully separating from the screen. I shut it down real quick, and then was able to maneuver the lid and the hinge enough to get it closed. I was on a work trip when this happened, and luckily I was able to get by without using my laptop again until I came home. I was able to carefully open again and it seems to be working, but I will not attempt to close it again. I'll do an extra backup and I will probably use it (if it lasts) until August when my MS Office and Bitdefender subscriptions run out, then I'll have to shell out for a new laptop. You can bet it won't be another HP!

Overall, great buy!

title: Good quality, not likely to use often
review_text:
I read a few reviews before purchasing this mouse (the Logitech Lift Vertical Ergonomic Mouse, Wireless). The reviews seemed to suggest this mouse made a big difference for people who were having aches/pains with using a traditional mouse.
I wanted to try this mouse for everyday use, and maybe even for gaming.
Unfortunately, the novelty of the vertical grip wears off quickly and what you are left with is learning how to use a new mouse efficiently all over again.
If you have wrist/arm/grip issues, this mouse might be a great solution for you. If you are just looking for a more efficient and accurate mouse, I would not recommend this product.
I used the mouse for a few weeks and found that every time I would switch back to my regular mouse it was like a handicap had been lifted.
To be clear, the mouse is very well made. The buttons are nearly silent, the wheel seems to track well, the surface that contacts your desk or mousepad seems to be smooth enough. I would even estimate the batteries are probably good for quite some time.
Logitech makes quality products, and I will be keeping this mouse just in case I ever have the need to switch it up a bit.
Overall, this might be a great solution for people with pain associated with traditional mouse posture, but not likely to be much fun for the average person who is just looking for a new or modern mouse.

review_text:

point where you last stopped playing...when

- you disconnect the USB device.
- you play other content.
- you turn off the player.
That means you have to start from scratch and get thruough ALL the warnings and previews EVERY time you can't finish a movie in one sitting. and the button placement makes it very easy to do so accidentally.

So I'm not buying sony products anymore.

PS. The machine is not malfunctioning (still very new), just badly designed, so one might say that it deserves more stars, but i always read the "1-star reviews" before buying anything, and i want to warn people.

I initially ordered this product because I wanted to be able to see what my dogs were doing, particularly our new puppy, when we weren't home. We have quickly grown to love this camera/treat dispenser/laser pointer. And the dogs love it too.

The pros: you can take pictures or short videos of your dogs, dispense treats, talk to them AND hear them, and use a laser pointer to entertain them. No monthly fees.

The cons: the treat dispenser only holds eight small treats, so if you have more than one animal or are going to be gone for a longer period of time, you may run out of treats before you return. Also, the laser sometimes gets stuck.

However, the customer service on this product is excellent. Outstanding, even. When our laser got stuck about three weeks after we purchased this product, we contacted the company and they attempted to walk us through a troubleshooting process to unstick the laser. When that didn't work, they sent us a brand new product no questions asked, no hassle, no fuss. We are extremely pleased with their customer service.

Also, unlike some other similar products on the market, this product does not require you to pay a monthly service for storage of photos or videos. You use an app on your mobile phone or tablet and can store photos and videos on your device or on your own cloud. I would highly recommend this product.

title: Works well, if you don't want to pan
review_text:
This is a great deal on outdoor cameras. They are easy to set up and work well with the software you can download. They are sturdy and compact. I got them to replace some cameras that are around our barn so we can see the horses, and the only surprise was that they didn't pan. The other cameras were able to move up and down, right and left so that I could see where the horses are.
I was going to give them 4 stars, but then I realized it was my issue. The description never said they would pan and I just missed that.
So, if you want remote cameras and don't mind that they are stationary, this is a great deal. You get three cameras for $160. However, if you look at the current description, one camera is $49.99, so you can buy three individual cameras for slightly less than the 3 pack. Goofy, but that's sometimes the case.
UPDATE: I also noticed that the speaker on the camera, so I can talk to whoever is there, has such a low volume it cannot be heard over 1 foot away. Not very helpful for a remore camera. I sent in a request to their support team asking if there is a volume control on the camera or the mobile app. They responded with a request for the model number, which is fine, and then didn't reply to my response for over a month. Their next reply was to ask a bunch of questions about firmware and app permissions, which was not helpful. This indicates to me there is a problem with support and also possibly a problem with the deveopment group. Any retail product should have a features list somewhere, maybe not available to the public, but certainly available to the support team. That feature list should indicate if there is a way to control the volume. Rather than taking a month to ask additional, irrelevant questions, the support people should have either looked at the feature list or asked the developers if there is a way to increase the volume.
That did not happen, and so I'm reducing the rating to 3 stars. All products can have problems and the test of a good product is having a support group that can quickly and accurately respond to the problem (or question), and that is not the case with Merkury.
Since I planed to install this about 6 feet off the ground, the camera is of limited value. It doesn't pan, which was my issue, and no one can hear what is said through the app, which is their issue. Support is not helpful so I don't know if this is a problem with the camera or a feature they left our or a feature they intend to include later. I can no longer recommend this product, unless you are going to install it very close to whoever you are wanting to speak with.

title: Nice USB-C hub
review_text:
I got this because my laptop has only 3 USB C ports and no standard USB ports. One of them is for power, and I've got a wireless mouse and keyboard, which leaves one port for everything else.
Needless to say, I need a few more ports and also an ethernet connection (RJ45).
The unit comes nicely boxed and for some reason has a bunch of stickers for the flags of various countries. Not sure why, but it's an interesting approach.
It has a lot of ports, an HDMI, RJ45,SD Card and micro SD, 1 USB C, 1 PD, which looks like a USB C, but is a power port, 2 USB 2.0 and 2 USB 3.0.
There is a warning label that says it might get hot (up to 130" F) and thatdevices with power higher than 7.5W are not supported, so check on the things you will be plugging into the hub before you buy it. It also says the PD adapter is under 40W and may not be able to charge all devices through the hub.
So, if you are going to use this to power a bunch of USB devices or charge your phones, it might not work. But if you are just plugging things in like cameras, microphones or drives then it will work fine.
For having all those ports, it's not as large as some others I've used and all in all is a nice hub. If you need more ports, then this is definitely worth considering.

title: Nice hub that allows you to have multiple monitors
review_text:
I recently got a 15" portable monitor to use with my laptop when I'm traveling and because I don't have a lot of USB C ports on my laptop, I was looking for a hub. This one seemed to be just what I needed and it had the ability to plug in 2 HDMI monitors and also card readers for SD cards.
When I first tried it, I was disappointed in how it worked. It didn't light up the two additional monitors and the ethernet connection seemed slow. I took it off and went back to my old hub. Then a couple of days later I decided to try it again, and this time it worked great. I guess the monitors need some time to figure out what they are doing and I did a speed test with this ethernet connection and my old one and the speed was the same.
So, now instead of just having a portable monitor, I have three monitors and it works great. One thing I don't like about it is that you have to use the HDMI ports to make it recognize multiple monitors. That's fine for my desktop monitor, but the portable one has the ability to do USB-C to USB-C connection of the monitor. When I'm traveling, I can just use that connection and the cables are much easier to deal with. So that's one downside but it may be just my personal preference so I'm giving it 5 stars because it works and does what it's supposed to do. If you are looking to set up multiple monitors for a laptop, this is the hub you want to get.

title: Great watch, much better than my old "smart" watch
review_text:
I got Moto 360 several years ago when smart watches first came out and it was nice, but annoying. It was tied into everything and kept giving me alerts and so eventually I got tired of it. My wife also had a first generation Samsung Gear watch and that was about the same as the Moto.
Well, fast forward a few years and now my wife, daughter, son and daughter-in-law all have newer smart watches (Apple Watches and Fitbit) and they all love them. It was time to get a new phone, so I got a Samsung S20 FE and then decided to get the Samsung watch. I saw on the reviews that it really works well with Samsung phones and so I decided to get the Watch 3. I was looking at the Watch 2, which had a few less features and then I found the Watch 3 in the 41mm size and then found a refurbished one so I ended up paying about the same for the Watch 3 as I would have for the Watch 2.
I'm very impressed with the watch and really love it. I didn't get the one with a cell phone, it just connects to my phone with bluetooth and/or wifi, but it's really amazing. I get my messages, and can turn off the ones that I don't want and then I also get all the health apps. So, now it tells me to get off my chair and walk around and does EKG and stress tesing and Oxygen levels..
I was concerned that the 41 mm might be too small, but it is a great size for me as you can see from the pic. I have had a Citizen Echo Drive for more than 10 years and it is a little larger, but I like the size of the Watch 3 better.
If you are thinking about getting a watch, this one is a good deal right now and I believe it does work best if you use it with a Samsung phone.

title: Didn't work for me, but Seller is Great
review_text:
A friend of mine recommended this product and so I got it before taking a trip out west. The installation went well and it seemed to work at first, but after about 5-15 minutes things started going wrong. The music would just go out for no reason while I was riding. If I clicked the buttons it might come back on and it might not. I didn't want to fiddle with it since I was on my bike, but when I stopped I could get it to work and then it might work for half an hour. In some cases, it didn't even last as long as one song until it went out. After the first day I thought I had it working, and the second day was not too bad, but the third day it was a total bust. I couldn't get it to work at all.
That's the bad news, and from some of the reviews I've read it is a crap shoot whether you get a good one or not. And by the way, the price of this was $69 when I bought it and now it's almost double.
The good news is that I got in touch with IBD Electronics and they were great. They gave me the options of replacing it (but it was back ordered), refunding my money or getting another product. I had a couple of questions and acutally ended up calling them. The people there were fantastic. I eventually decided to get an LG Tone and they sent it out and credited me with the difference in the same day. Great customer service.
By the way, the Tone is great. I have not tried to use it to make or receive calls, but really don't want to do that while riding my motorcycle, so playing the music and listening to the GPS is all I need it for. When I'm not on my bike, the thing works great at not only the music, but also at making and receiving calls. The parrot device may be good for when you are on the bike,but that's it. The Tone is great for sitting at your desk and listening to music. Give it a look, and it's only about $40.

title: Player is great, software is garbage
review_text:
I had an iPod 2GB Nano and wanted to get something with larger capacity. I did some research and finally bought the Walkman. I was around for the very first Sony Walkman casette tape player, so the idea of getting a Sony MP3 player was appealing.
After using it for over a month, I find it a great little device. The battery life is amazing. I charged it over two weeks ago and have used it on multiple three hour car rides. I also had it hooked up to a speaker in my office and left it on for several hours and it stil has battery life.
It took me some time to get used to the navigation, but now I am fine with the difference between the Walkman and the iPod. The sound quality is good and although the volume could be better, it is acceptable for my use.
The major problem I have with the unit is the software. Sony included one of those mini disc's which loaded a couple of software programs on my computer. The main program is one which allows you to drag and drop files from your computer to the player; however, it doesn't work. I dragged a few tunes to see how it worked and then started dragging all the music. The software kept accepting the tunes, but after it "loaded" for about 2 hours, I discovered it had only loaded the first set of tunes. The rest, and the two hour wait, was for nothing. The software also has a "delete" function, which also doesn't work. It tells you that it delets items from the player, but they are still there.
So, I junked that software and decided to use the Windows Media Player. This is ok, except that the Media Player has a very odd way to create playlists. There are some round about ways to create the play list and I have finaly learned how to do it, but it took way too long compared to iTunes. The other odd thing is that when you create a play list it has to be from tunes on your computer, not on the device. Then when you sync the device to load the playlist, it may or may not put duplicate versions of the music on the device. Sometimes it finds the songs on the device and sometimes it does not. So, I ended up with multiple copies of some songs. The device software is also pathetic. It doesn't allow you to create playlists on the device, and as others have noted, there is no way to delete items from the device without using the software.
I finally just had the computer recognize the device as an external drive and was able to load songs and delete them with no probme.
Despite the isues, I still like the device better than my Nano. For one thing it has an FM receiver, which works great. Now that I have come to terms with the crappy software, it works great. So, if you are looking for an alternative to the iPod, this is a good option. Just stay away from the software provided by Sony and you will be fine.

title: Fantastic functionality; limited lifespan
review_text:
I should start by saying that purchasing this iPad case dramatically changed how and how much I use my iPad. How wonderful to have the laptop - style hinge, but one that rotates 360°. In any position, at a desk, sitting up in bed, lying on my side, or in my lap, it is incredibly easy to set the screen at the perfect angle. The Bluetooth connection is great, and the size of the keyboard is exactly right for my medium sized hands.

So why only four stars? The sad fact is that after six months of daily hard use, the plastic surrounding one of the hinges began to crack, with the crack growing progressively bigger. Finally, before the unit was seven months old, the two halves of the clam case began to separate completely, and the keyboard was no longer operational. That was very disappointing, obviously.

So why rate it so highly? Because I have tried a significant number of other cases, and none even came close to the functionality of this clam case. Given my heavy use, I would actually rather replace a clam case every six months than struggle with the fixed angle and other limitations of every other model I have used. My upshot: if you have the money to spend, you will love this item. Just don't expect the hinges, or the plastic surrounding them, to last for more than six months of heavy daily use.

title: Great for the most part
review_text:
I received this Kindle for Christmas and actually wanted it over the IPAD Mini based on reviews. I have to say that I am for the most part very happy with this product. It is very easy to use and has a lot of the apps (games, Netflix, Hulu Plus, Email, Facebook)that I want. The format for displaying books that I have in the past purchased (on my original Kindle) appeared automatically. With all of the positives, however, there are a couple of short comings. The most significant is the fact that reading the Kindle 8.9 in bright sunlight is just not possible. The touch screen has a shiny surface that reflects causing reading, watching films or playing games virtually an impossibility. On the otherhand, reading in a dark room has been corrected with its own lighted background. Another issue is that many of the android apps that are available on other devices are just not available here (not a major problem but a disappointment). Using the Web has its limitations as well since it loads extremely slow and if opening something from an email closing the site will not take you back to the original email (again not a major problem). Recommend the optional quick charge plug since this Kindle requires a charge quite frequently (daily typically) and this provides a charge very quickly. Overall, I have really enjoyed my Kindle 8.9 and use it daily.

Edit (8/25/13). Additional comments. Certain videos require Flash Drive which is not available with the Kindle which is disappointing. While not the fault of Kindle potentially Amazon does not partner with Directv for their Directv Everywhere function or certain programing like ESPN 360 although HBO GO, Showtime Anywhere, Starz and Encore movies and programing are available if subscribed though Directv or a recognized provider.

title: Minor complaints, but generally a decent buy
review_text: I’m not a DIY kind of guy, so I went with the cheapest, simplest mount I could find. It’s okay, but be prepared for some minor adjustments. The Pros: price. It’s much less expensive than most of the others. It’s also quite minimalist - no thick bezels. It’s made of a flexible silicone material - that’s both a pro and a con - the pro - it’s soft on your tablet - no scratches. It’s also somewhat flexible - I installed mine vertically in a tight space and there’s no room to slide the tablet in from the side. Instead, I have to seat it in the bottom mount and sort of snap it into place in the top. Given the flexibility of the material, this works fine. The cons: included with the mount are 6 each screws and wall anchors - no spares and no washers. The anchors don’t have any lip on the end so a couple of mine dropped into the wall cavity, making it necessary to go buy some spares. Also, the screw heads easily pull through the holes in the mounts when tightened. I fixed that with a handful of small washers which should be included with the mount kit. Also, my tablet (an old iPad Air 2) Is quite slim and doesn’t fit snugly in the mount so I put a short strip of thin silicone insulation behind it to better hold it in place. There is a slot in the center of one mount to allow access For a charging cable. Thoughtfully, it appears to be even wide enough for the old style wide Apple connector. Included is also a paper template for various size devices and a stick on cable retainer. Aside from the minor complaints about washers and wall mounts, I’m satisfied with the kit.

review_text: I bought these to use with Brain.fm. I would have preferred wireless but Bluetooth enabled models don’t seem to be able to run all night (8 hours) on a charge. These are actually better than I expected in a couple ways - first, they sound surprisingly good for the price. The headband is a light fleece type material - it tends to be warm, but that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather. That’s really my only complaint - there’s nothing to really keep them firmly positioned. They tend to shift around easily when putting on or removing the headband. Initially, the headband was a little tight on me but I was able to stretch it out a bit for better comfort - still snug enough to stay in position, but not enough to be uncomfortable.

title: I’m a satisfied customer
review_text: After reading the many critical of Blink’s customer service I wanted to add my two cents. I don’t have a LOT of experience with support, but did just have one of my cameras (indoor) fail on me after several months of trouble-free use. I tried an assortment of things before emailing Blink (reset, replace batteries, uninstall/reinstall) and had pretty much determined it was a hardware issue. Blink support had me go through the same troubleshooting steps and came to the same conclusion. The entire process from my initial contact to their resolution took less than a day. I’m satisfied with my system and Blink’s support. My only criticism is minor - the iOS app doesn’t support iPad in native landscape mode and I live on my iPad. Battery life has been great - I’ve had most of my cameras for almost a year and haven’t had any batteries die yet. Blink’s servers have been down (maybe?) three times since I’ve been using their gear (that I’ve noticed) and one of those times was a widespread outage which couldn’t be blamed on them. Acceptable service, especially considering it’s provided at no cost. I’m sure you can buy better security cameras, but I don’t know of anything better, easier to setup or more flexible for the price.

title: the ear of the beholder
review_text: Everybody has an opinion and they're all different. I finally settled on a pair of MDR-EX51LP buds for my iPod. The buds that come with the iPod are poor sounding and uncomfortable, no matter how trendy it may be to have a white wires dangling from your ears. I tried several different types and brands and settled on these. They have a more balanced sound than the other headphones in the sub $50 bracket that I tested - good bass, clean highs and mids. Do they compare with premium studio cans? No, but neither do the price tag, size or weight. They block office noise at a reasonable SPL and allow me to concentrate on my work without distraction. I can still hear some outside sound if I keep the music volume low enough - as has been mentioned before, that can be a good thing. They're very comfortable - I wear them for hours at a time on a daily basis. I don't get the uneven cord length, but it really isn't a big deal. Headphones are like operating systems - there is no such thing as one size fits all. Get the ones that work for you (and your audio device!) and don't start a holy war with someone who prefers something different.

title: UPDATED REVIEW!
review_text:
Update 2/9/23: My (cognitively) young son, who has that very expensive iPad mini I mentioned below in the original review, now pushes his iPad to the side at least 50% of the time and 'steals' my FirePad. There are apps and games on the FirePad that aren't on Apple's AppStore - granted, they're usually pretty basic, or else I imagine they'd be available across multiple OS platforms - but he's very young, cognitively, and he doesn't care. I am 100% certain that whenever this iPad he's got needs replacing (because Apple does that way more than is right, IMO) we will be going the 'FirePad' route.

Our family has had so many iPads, iPad Airs, iPad minis... and I can say that - when bought brand spanking new, at the time of release, we were in love. Honeymoons don't last forever, unfortunately, and neither do the tablets. NOT ONCE did we break them beyond being fixable; every single time they've 'updated out' and none of the apps worked. They're not even good for internet after awhile, because even Safari and Chrome have to be updated for use... and the updates will not work with the outdated IOS. Yknow, because $600+ for 2-4 years is acceptable. NOT. But dumb sheeple me, kept on buying them. 🤦🏼‍♀️

I bought my son a 6th Gen iPad mini last November. It was newish and on backorder til about early-mid December. I gave it to him as a gift IN A CHILDPROOF CASE. So it has been protected since I got it. Since before he got it. And two weeks ago it quit charging. Now, he uses his iPad for everything: Communication. Education. Entertainment. Besides the $600 I paid, and even with the $3.49/month AppleCare, it's just totally unacceptable. After taking it to two localish Apple Premium partners, neither of which wanted to fix it and both of which wanted to just sell me a new one, and because all our other iPads (4 that I haven't tossed yet) won't allow him to access his communication apps anymore, I cried and then ordered the Fire Mini on my 23% interest credit card because he needs accessS to something he can communicate on.

I'm, erm, a girl of a certain age. Getting more and more stubborn about learning new technology stuff. So getting used to this has been a mite frustrating for me. My son, 25 with the cognitivity and resilience of a 2 year old, hasn't skipped a beat. It's early days - and I did buy the 2 year Amazon Protection with the 'FirePad' as we call it - but for $200 plus tax, tag & title 😉 this little Fire Tablet is at least the quality equivalent of the $600 iPad Mini.

The only cons... the display IS just as good as the iPad, though the colors aren't quite as vibrant/vivid and the brightness isn't as bright. Is that worth $400 more... not for anyone I know. It just takes a little getting used to (I'm talking maybe 2 days with minimal usage by a stubborn adult) and then it's not an issue anymore. The biggest con, though, is that Google won't hop in bed with Amazon - apparently - as willingly as they do Apple. No Google app, no Chrome app, no YouTube app. I just use the Silk browser (Bing... YUCK!) type in Google for Google searches or YouTube to watch videos. Maybe 3 seconds of frustration but it does remember my YT log in after the first time, so there's that to help lessen the annoyance for when I use it. (My son watches YouTube on his TV anyway.)

CLIFF NOTES: 🔩🍎. 💸🔥
(Screw Apple. Buy Fire.)

review_text:
My 'kid' is 24 (cognitively he's about 2) and takes his iPad with him to bed. Doesn't use it, just that's where he puts it when he goes to sleep. Between his pillow and the wall. (If you knew all the off the wall sh** that can and does go wrong with seizures, you'd get why all the one-in-a-billions go through my head!)

Anyway, this was the best $ I've spent in a long time. It holds the iPad without any sliding or moving (the device or the pillow) and it came in his favorite color. He loved it. I love it.

title: It's pretty good -
review_text:
3.5 STARS. I rounded up because it is more good then bad:
Bought as a Christmas gift for the boyfriend. We are long distance and we FaceTime a lot. Well, actually, I FaceTime with the underside of his kitchen cabinets, the blanket on his bed, the ceilings in all his rooms, or the top of his nightstand. He talks away, oblivious until I say something. It's funny mostly but sometimes in a relationship you need all the connection you can get, even if it's their face on your device while they smile or laugh or talk you through a bad moment. So, I got him this for Christmas so that he could hands-free me and I could still see his pretty face. He finally put it together and started using it the other day... with an asterisk. *THE INCLUDED SCREW/BOLT IS GARBAGE. It was machined badly. Really badly. So it only screws maybe halfway into the arm/neck or whatever it is called, which sits in the weighted base. Thankfully he really doesn't need the screw/bolt because the arm/neck (like a metal dowel, I suppose, that inserts into the base maybe half an inch. The screw/bolt is inserted from under the base and - if it fits correctly) recesses into the base when it's tightened. As this one had threads that weren't smooth about halfway down on the screw/bolt, it left the screw/bolt jutted out. The base won't sit on the nightstand or other flat surface with this issue unless he just doesn't use the screw/bolt. I'd post a photo for clarification but the stand isn't available and getting him to send photos isn't always something I remember when we do talk.

The screw/bolt is I'm sure metric and it does use an Allen wrench (included) to screw in; the threading is very tight, so finding a true replacement screw/bolt is probably gonna require going to a specialty nuts/bolts/hardware store. That's annoying enough to take off 1.5 stars for me.

title: Im ordering a replacement. Will stick with Momentum
review_text:
Ive had a momentum camera for 4years and have really liked everything about it. I am not tech savvy, but the picture quality-day and night is great, notifications, use on app easy, sd card, everything has been great. I have even reviewed footage to see where I set something down lol.
I have been looking for a few days to see if theres anything better or cheaper since I dropped my camera last week.
I am floored and appalled by what is out there.
Yes some cameras say they have clearer video. But no night vision. And some record only when motion detected, but only 6-12 seconds, what use is that? And many have a privacy policy that you absolutely have to agree to, or camera doesnt work. And those policies state that the company can access your personal information, files and data. As in social media, contacts, pictures, passwords, etc. and is authorized to use any of that and video clips to use how they want.
Some cameras dont turn off no matter what, and people found out they were being recorded without permission.
I don't like the idea of a surveillance camera in my home, but, I have been robbed too many times. So I would rather do passwords, get dressed etc in a different room.
And I have ordered another momentum camera. I did have trouble setting up the 1st camera, but I thought it was me. After reading a few reviews, I hope the 2nd one is as good as my other one has been for years.
I will do an update if anything changes.

title: Great Cable Modem - BUT...
review_text:
I have nothing but high praise for this Netgear CMD31T Cable Modem. The instructions were clear and no-nonsense; the physical installation took less than two minutes.

I would however, like to give NEGATIVE 5 stars to Comcast's ridiculous telephone service. I called the toll-free number that is provided on my bill and with the modem's paperwork. After wading through endless automated prompts, I was told that my waiting time would be 39-50 minutes. I sat and waited... After about 15 minutes, my call was disconnected. I went through the same ordeal again. After a total of close to an hour, I finally got to talk to someone - just to be told that they couldn't help me there; I needed to call a different number.

I called the new number. When I finally talked to someone there, she told me that she couldn't help me; I needed to call a different number. She read the "different" number to me - yes, the same number that I just called her on! I finally talked her into transferring me.

The person that I was transferred to didn't speak English very well. After repeating the Serial Number and the Mac ID many, many times to him, he finally got it. But it ends up that he couldn't actually help me either - he said that he would put me on hold to contact the correct person to do the switch over. When he put me on hold, he disconnected me...

I called again. 'Got someone else that barely spoke English. He said that my new modem was now in their system and that he would send a test signal. The signal did not make it to my modem for some reason. He asked me to unplug the modem from the power strip that it's on and plug it directly into the wall. I told him that I wasn't going to do that; it was obviously getting power. He then asked me to hold, so he could transfer me to tech support. When he put me on hold, I was disconnected again.

I decided that if the modem was showing up in their system now, maybe I could getting it working myself. I unplugged and replugged the power, and waited about 10 minutes. Then I unplugged and replugged my router's power. Success! It's working fine now.

title: It works, but not so well...
review_text:
I'm keeping this unit only because it fits the space that I wanted it in very well - I'm not at all happy with the performance of it.

I purchased this TV to mount on a very large desk that I have. The mounting is pretty straight-forward (they supply a cardboard drilling template and a few different spacer options). One thing to keep in mind on the mounting - make sure to allow for extra space for the speakers when drilling your mounting holes (the template does not have this space added).

Electronically, this is just a very average to below-average unit. I'm using cable as my video source. The TV that was in this location previously had an excellent picture. This unit has a snowy picture, and very poor color balance (I have tried adjusting it many times - it never does get a "good" picture).

The sound is awful. You have to create a balance between two different volume sources - one on the front of the main unit, the other on the TV itself (controlled by buttons on the TV, or by the remote). Between the two, if you turn it up to the point of what I would consider normal volume, you hear a faint but noticeable high-pitched whine (my Jack Russell Terrier hears it too...). The quality of the sound is pretty bad too - very thin and tinny. They should have added an Audio Out Jack, so that you could hook up a decent set of amplified speakers to it.

The Power button on the front of the unit is a cheap, spring-loaded design; I can tell that it will create problems in the long run (it has already stuck a few times).

The clock display is a bit annoying also - most digital displays will display the single-digit time without a zero in front nowadays - 3:00, for example. This clock displays it as 03:00.

The remote must use very unique frequencies - I was not able to program my regular Tivo remote to it (not even when cycling through the hundreds of preset codes that the Tivo remote has). I then purchased a "learning" Tivo remote - even that remote wouldn't accept the "power" or "volume down" functions ("volume up" was the only button that would accept the programming).

I did not purchase this keyboard for gaming, I purchased it to use mostly as a higher-end computer keyboard. I'm using it in conjunction with [[ASIN:B003BIFI6E the Razer DeathAdder Left-handed Gaming Mouse]].

~ The smooth finish of the area around the keys shows fingerprints horribly. This surface should be matte.

All in all, I like the keyboard (and will keep it), I just wish that a few things about it were designed differently...

Fast forward to October 2014. The lens now has lost the ability to focus in either manual mode or AF. Until now, it had never shown any indication of any kind of problem.

Its warranty was for one year, so I'm now checking with Canon and other repair shops to get an estimate for fixing this problem.

I am very disappointed that a Canon lens had such a short useful life. The lens was used moderately, and stored properly. There's no discernible reason why it had a lens failure. If my lens cannot be repaired at a reasonable price, I'm not sure that I trust Canon's quality control enough to buy a replacement.

title: Had to return it due to connectivity issues
review_text:
I got this internet radio and tried it for a few weeks. At first I was happy with it - the sound quality is quite good, it seemed pretty easy to set up, and I was able to find my favorite NPR station streams as well as connect to my Pandora stations. But after the first two weeks or so, I started having problems with connectivity.

- I'd come home from work and the thing would be on, not playing, with "error connecting to network" or some similar message flashing on the screen. The best way to solve this seemed to be to turn it off, then turn it back on, and then it would work (for a while).

- While listening, it frequently stops playing in the middle of a song. Then the display says either "Buffering" for a few minutes, or more frequently, will actually say "Connecting" for up to five minutes at a time! This happens, on average, every 4-6 minutes. The thing is, I have a wireless router upstairs on the same floor as the radio (Apple Time Capsule) and the wireless signal is quite strong. The other devices that connect to this router never have a problem with connectivity - devices that include a Roku box, a Chumby, my iPhone, my HP netbook, my Macbook, etc.

The problem with losing connectivity started infrequently but got worse and worse over the past two weeks or so, to the point where I can't really listen to music on it at all anymore. So I'm returning it. Too bad, because in terms of looks, sound, and basic functionality, it had everything I wanted.

title: An upgrade from my previous Nuvi!
review_text:
I previously owned a Garmin Nuvi 360 which I loved. I specifically need a GPS that includes Bluetooth, since I use it both for directions and for hands-free phone use (which is rare, but important when I need it). I loved my 360 and used it daily until just a few months ago, when the Bluetooth suddenly stopped working. After troubleshooting with Garmin's tech support, it was determined the unit would need to be sent in for service, and since it was out of warranty, the flat charge for service was $79, which didn't include insured shipping costs.

Well, do the math. Obviously, one can acquire a brand-new GPS for not much more than $79, so I started shopping. That's how I ended up with my new Garmin Nuvi 265T. And I LOVE IT! I'm almost glad that my old unit went on the fritz, because it gave me an excuse to upgrade to this newer, fantastic unit.

The 360 was great for accurate directions, easy to see and read display, and consistent Bluetooth (until it broke). Here's how the 265T is even better:

- Smaller, lighter, and thinner, but with a slightly wider screen.
- No "antenna" on the back to flip up and fiddle with - it just works.
- Uses my existing mount (from ProClips), so no change to that was necessary.
- Includes FREE traffic notifications, which so far seem to work pretty well.
- When you power it on, it seems to bypass the warning screen that you need to "Agree" to quicker, and then shows a simple display: Where To, and View Map. On the 360, if you didn't do anything else, it would sit on the menu indefinitely, but the 265T automatically switches to map display after a few minutes if you don't select anything else. Basically, you can start your car and just forget about it, until you need it!

The traffic feature is ad-supported, so occasionally very small banner-type ads appear on the display, usually offering coupons for local restaurants etc. They are quite small and not intrusive in any way, so I don't mind them. I guess there's also an option to upgrade to a paid traffic service that would not include ads, but I don't see a need for that for my own use.

In general I am thrilled with Garmin products, and this Nuvi 265T is no exception. What a great deal, and a nice early Christmas present for myself!

title: I May Not Know Much, But I Know I Love These!
review_text:
I'm not an audio expert by any means, but I know what I like and I have owned many, many pairs of headphones in the past. Noise-cancelling, non-noise-cancelling, earbuds, headphones, in-ear, out-of-ear, surround-ear, you name it. It seems like headphones and headsets are kind of an obsession of mine.

I use larger headhpones such as these Sennheisers primarily for playing video games on my computer after my toddler has gone to bed, and occasionally for listening to music (also on one of my computers). (When it comes to my iPod, I generally use something smaller and more portable, such as earbuds.)

When I took the HD201 headphones out of the box, I was first amazed at light they are. They seem to weigh almost nothing, though they don't feel flimsy by any means. I tried them on, and they were immediately very comfortable. They surrounded my ears comfortably, and the adjustable length on each side allowed for a perfect fit. I also noticed that the cord on these is nice and long, which is a plus. So far, so good. So I plugged them in for the real test.

WOW.

These sound GREAT! It's really kind of amazing to me that Amazon can offer these for under $20. I read the other reviews and paid attention when some reviewers said that they weren't loud enough, or sounded funny on "s" sounds. I did not find that to be the case for me. They sound just fine on all types of sounds and music, at various levels, and the volume is not a problem.

Pros: light-weight, comfortable, great sound, amazing price
Cons: too big for my taste to travel with, since they don't fold

I kind of wish they had an attached microphone, because then I'd never need another headset for gaming! However, for listening only, these are top-notch and I was very pleasantly surprised by the terrific quality at such a low price.

title: Cable too short!
review_text:
These are really, really high quality earbuds, especially for the price. The sound quality is actually pretty amazing. I had a middling-quality pair of those "Inked" earbuds attached to my laptop at work. The sound quality was always disappointing, but I had sort of assumed that it was probably due to the laptop sound card, etc. Then today I attached my new Sony Fontopias and wow...what a difference! Yes, they have bass boost, but not so much that it overwhelms the music.

These headphones are also surprisingly comfortable. They aren't the typical in-ear shape that gets jammed all the way into your ear, but there's a little more to them than the default "sort of hang in the outer part of your ear" that you get with the default iPod earbuds, for example. I like the hybrid, in-between quality and they fit me pretty well. They're not noise-cancelling, but the sound is so good that I really don't notice other office sounds (not even my disgusting cubicle neighbor who eats cookies like the Cookie Monster and sounds completely disgusting - now you know why I need to listen to music at work!). I'm so happy with the sound quality and comfort of these headphones, I'm willing to give then four stars in spite of one very major drawback:

THE CORD IS RIDICULOUSLY SHORT.

I have NEVER seen such a short cord on any pair of headphones, earbuds, headset, etc. that I have owned. I measured the cord from the jack to the point where the "Y" that goes to each individual bud starts, and it is barely 2 feet. TWO FEET! People, that is SHORT. So I'm going to go to Radio Shack at lunch today and buy an extension cord/adapter. So unless you're going to sit right next to the source you are connecting the headphones to, whether it's a computer or MP3 player or stereo, you'll need to add the cost of an extension cable to the price. Trust me - it's way too short as sold, like it wouldn't even stretch from my iPod in a backpack to my ears if I was walking around.

Otherwise, awesome headphones.

title: Portable, Quality Means for Listening to Music
review_text:
I like listening to music when I spend time in my backyard. I used to rely on my alexa for this purpose, but more often than not, the volume and clarity were not that good. A portable Bluetooth speaker was the answer and I found just what I needed with this Bluetooth, from Tpone.

What you get with this Bluetooth is a portable, chargeable speaker with that offers up to 18 hours of playback on a single charge. Getting it fully charged will take time, but after that, it’s a matter of pairing it with the Bluetooth on your phone. In about two minutes, it will be ready for use.

The sound quality you get with this Bluetooth speaker is quite good. I like the bass, and for my needs, the volume is sufficient. It’s not powerful enough to blast you away, but for what I need, the volume level works. I use it mostly when I sit on my back patio and/or jump in the pool. I don’t need extreme volume, so this works. There is a plus and minus button on the unit that at first seem like volume controls, but they are not. If you push these, the music will either advance forward or backward to the next song on the list. The volume is controlled by your phone or whatever device you have paired.

There are different colored lights on this speaker that react to the music, adding to the visuals. Again, for my needs, I really don’t care about the lights. But I can see how this could certainly add to the coolness factor for some people. The added colors and the way they react to the intensity of the music is a nice addition. Oh, and I like that I can use this to charge my phone. If a phone is paired, it could drain the phone’s power quickly while you play music. You can easily counter this by plugging your phone directly into the unit, helping to keep your phone charged.

Having the means to listen to music is an ongoing need for me. Whether I am listening to music in my backyard or taking a trip to a nearby beach, I need to be able to play my tunes and the easiest way is to use a portable Bluetooth speaker. This Bluetooth from Tpone delivers on most all counts. The easy pairing, the bass, and the overall sound quality make this an easy winner and an excellent Bluetooth choice.

title: Secure Connection and Made to Last
review_text:
In the information age in which we live, electronics are part of our daily routine. Sometimes, it is necessary to connect electronics and a HDMI cable like this one from SIREG is ready to help.

Heavy duty in construction, this cable is designed to connect devices like laptops, monitors, projectors, etc. You simply plug in one end to the device you’re sending data from, and the other end to the device you want to send to. Be sure you are connecting the in and out the right way, and you should be set to go. The connection is secure and the cords don’t pop out easily, so you shouldn’t have any trouble in that regard.

One end is HDMI, the other end is DP interface. Be sure your devices will match this, otherwise this cord will not work.

We often need to connect electronic devices. I often connect my laptop with my television and this HDMI cord from SIREG is a useful tool for the task. It securely connects and the images look sharp and clear. It’s a little more expensive than others, but the quality makes it worth it.

title: No Batteries Needed and Cool Lights
review_text:
Navigating on a pc screen requires a mouse of some sort. They have come a long way over the years, with more features and more comfort. One that is great for those who like to add a little color to their navigation is this wireless mouse from PEIOUS.

Shaped for your hands, this mouse is comfortable to hold and click. It’s easy enough to use and you can’t feel any strain on your hands, so it earns good marks there. But the feature that is most appealing is the lights. You can change the lights to different modes and even shut them off completely, if you prefer. I like that the lights are soft- you notice them, but they are not so bright that they distract from what you are doing.

The bluetooth works okay on this mouse and one of the more unusual features is that you have to plug it in to charge. With most others I have used, you need to supply batteries, but this one charges by plugging it into a usb outlet. It’s nice not to have to buy batteries, but it also means you need to have a usb nearby for charging purposes. I consider this feature a plus, as I hate having to search for batteries when the need arises.

To conserve power with this mouse, there is a switch to shut it off. Plus, it will automatically shut off, to preserve power, if there is no movement for several minutes. This is good because, with regular use, you will need to recharge this more than you realize and saving power makes a difference.

Computers need a means for navigation and that requires a mouse of one type or another. You could go for the boring, ordinary mouse with buttons to click and nothing more, or you could have a little fun and get this wireless mouse from PEIOUS. I vote for the latter. It might only be a mouse, but the lights and the elimination of batteries make this a standout mouse and one I recommend.

title: It Works, but There are Some Issues
review_text:
Living with a teacher means there is a constant need for supplies. Teachers almost always have to supply their own things for the classroom and one item that my teacher wife needed was tablet. I fulfilled the need with this UGEE Digital Drawing Tablet.

This tablet earns good marks in certain areas. It features a large drawing area and it is easy to set up. The 12 buttons can be customized and used as shortcut buttons, making your tasks easier than before.

The issues with this tablet, however, are a few. One small issue is that it isn’t wireless. This isn’t a huge deal, but wireless would be better. The positioning is a little more challenging than expected, too. But the greatest problem I have is with the stylus and its tendency to scratch. Peeling off the plastic was easy enough, but already, I could see scratches from my fingernails! Just the slightest scrape leaves a permanent mark behind.

Drawing tablets are useful to have and for the price point, this UGEE Digital Drawing Tablet is a decent option overall. It gets the job done, but the issues stated above convince me to rate it average overall.

title: HP Knocks it Out of the Park
review_text:
I have been in dire need of a new computer for a LONG time. My laptop is about five years old and takes about 10 to 15 minutes just to power up completely. I already have the use of a laptop from my workplace, so I don’t really need a replacement for it. What I need is a desktop computer to use when my laptop is still at work and this need was enough to convince me to get the HP Pavilion 24-inch All-in-One Computer, Intel Core i5-9400T, 12 GB RAM, 512 GB Solid State Drive with Windows 10.

Taken out of the box, consumers will of course need to set this computer up and get it ready. I am happy to say that the set up is about as simple as it could possibly be- much simpler than the set up of other pc’s I have owned, which shows just how long it has been since I have gotten a new computer. In under 10 minutes, it was ready to use. It was so easy, I started to worry that I had forgotten something, but everything was good to go.

This computer comes with a nice size screen- about 24 inches- which is the largest I have ever had in my house. It does make it easier to see things and I like watching videos and movies- something I didn’t like as much on my laptop, which had a screen about half as wide. The resolution and colors are good, too. I watched a few online videos and was impressed by how vibrant the different colors looked and how life- like people and faces appeared.

Having a touch screen is cool and this is something new for me. I have never owned a touch screen computer before and while I like and support new technology, I admit that this is taking time to get used to. I still prefer to use my mouse out of habit, but this will likely change in due time. It really is much easier to simply touch a screen and it makes navigation faster.

About the only issue I have with this computer is the fees charged for Microsoft Office. You get a free trial period, but after that, you will have to pay for the service. Considering the price of this computer, Microsoft Office should be part of the deal. I get that these companies need a regular revenue stream and charging for services was bound to happen but I still think it should have been an exception with this computer, given its higher than average cost.

Getting rid of my laptop is a great relief. With my HP Pavilion 24-inch All-in-One Computer, Intel Core i5-9400T, 12 GB RAM, 512 GB Solid State Drive with Windows 10 computer, my power up time has been reduced to under one minute and I have a viewable screen that is much more vibrant than before. I’m still a little irritated with the whole Microsoft Office thing, but it’s not enough to lower my rating, which is an easy five stars for this excellent HP product.

title: Good for Securing Your Home
review_text:
Most of the places I have lived have been reasonably safe, so I have never felt any pressing need to add a camera security system to my home. I already have an alarm system, which is useful, but no camera system. I decided that it would be good to be able to see people at the main entrances to my home/property and this convinced me to add the Arlo Ultra - 4K UHD Wire-Free Security 2 Camera System to my house.

Setting this security system up is simple enough. You have to mount the included 2 cameras and it doesn’t take much time to complete this step. I placed one of them by my front door and the other one just outside my garage, facing the driveway. The gated entrance to my backyard is right there, and I usually leave my car in the driveway and not the garage, so this seemed like a good place.

There are many things to like about this security camera system, like the wide angle of view that is good for seeing from my backyard gate to the end of my driveway. You can even speak back and forth with someone at your front door and this can prove useful when you want to avoid talking directly, face to face, with solicitors.

With the image quality, although it isn’t as sharp as I expected, it seems sufficient to me. I haven’t experienced any intruders thus far- knock on wood- so I haven’t necessarily needed to get crystal clear details. One limitation I have is that I haven’t owned a camera security system before. This is a first for me, so I don’t have any point of comparison. Still, the picture quality seems good. And I like the notification system. Any motion detection is set up to record, so you can see what is going on and you know quickly.

The app itself is user- friendly enough but one thing to keep in mind is that the Arlo Smart Servive and cloud recording are free for only the first year. After that, you have to pay for a subscription. I will wait to see if the system is worth my while, then decide whether to subscribe. A year of free usage time should be sufficient to make the call.

Security is important and the Arlo Ultra - 4K UHD Wire-Free Security 2 Camera System is a good way to keep safe. Two cameras are definitely better than one because I am able to secure the two areas of my property where an unwanted individual is most likely to show up. I find the app and picture quality good and the system as a whole has enough positive points to recommend.

title: Good Sound Quality and Lightweight
review_text:
I’m never been a huge fan of headphones. I recognize their value and necessity when you want to listen to something but no one around you does. The reason I don’t like headphones is the bulkiness and wires but Soundcore Anker Liberty Air True Wireless Earphones with Charging Case have eliminated these issues.

These earphones come in a small case and they are extremely lightweight. You simply remove them from the package, connect via Bluetooth, insert in the ears, and start listening to your favorite tunes. There are no wires so you can move around as you please and because they are so small, you don’t have the bulkiness. Many people, unless they take a close look at you, will not even know that you are using earphones.

Of course, what matters most with something like this is the sound quality and these earphones score above average marks for sound. They claim to last up to 20 hours on a charge, but I haven’t come even close to using them for that much time, so I cannot verify the claim.

title: Very Good Starter Camcorder
review_text:
My two girls love their electronics. Mom and dad love them too, so we can’t really fault the two pre- teens from using and enjoying their electronics to the fullest. We like it best when they are at least devoting some of their electronic time to doing things more constructive and/or creative, and this is what convinced me to get my hands on this SOSUN Camcorder.

I had not heard of SOSUN until I got this camcorder, but I had read good things about the brand and decided that such a large percentage of customers must be right about something. One of my girls wanted a camcorder and this one seemed to have what she needed and seemed good for a beginner. The camera is lightweight and easy to hold. It can be used for regular picture taking and for video. The quality of video produced is good, too. There are better camcorders out there that create better videos and have more features, but this one is still good for a beginner like my 13 year old.

The battery life on this camcorder is about 2 hours. Given my kid’s short attention span, this is more than enough to keep her happy. In fact, she typically creates videos that are only two to five minutes in length. Unless her habits change, the 2 hour battery life is more than sufficient.

Camcorders can get expensive , especially if your needs and demands are high. But if you’re looking for a good starter camcorder for a very low price, this SOSUN is going to be difficult to match. The low price and above average quality make it worth the purchase and my increasingly more creative middle school age kid can vouch for its worthiness.

title: Good for Google Users Like Me
review_text:
Electronics are a fact of life and most families have multiple electronic devices to get through their day. My family of four has four cell phones, about six different pcs, laptops, and tablets, and three printers. Now, we also have our first ever Chromebook thanks to this Amazon product.

Chromebooks, I quickly learned, differ from the usual windows or apple laptop in several important ways and chief among them is the limit on the number of things you can download. If you have specific games and other things you want to download, they may not work. I already knew this going in but I can tell from reading other reviews that some people were not aware that it worked this way and they now have a device with limited usefulness.

Once you accept the Acer Chromebook for what it is, you will find that it does serve as a handy device. It’s excellent for browsing the internet, creating google docs, using google apps, and pretty much doing all things google. I am already a google chrome user when I go online and I already use many apps from the google play, so what this Chromebook offers is compatible with my needs.

Looking at other specifics of this Acer Chromebook, it is about the same size as my old laptop, at least in terms of the screen size. The image is good, although I have seen other laptops/tablets with more pixels and sharper images. Still, it should be sufficient for most needs, and it has a good deal to offer for the price. I have noticed that the charge doesn’t hold as long as the manufacturer claims and the bottom of the Chromebook does feel hot a little sooner than with others. But the Acer Chromebook is still functional and it performs well enough for my needs.

Electronics are a fact of life and as much as we try to limit their use, they are here to stay. Since we have to have them and use them, it makes sense to get the electronics that best suit our needs for a fair price and this Acer Chromebook does exactly that. It does have its limits and it cannot do everything that a windows or apple laptop can do, but as long as you know the limitations before you purchase, you should be fine.

title: Good for Your Bedroom Nightstand
review_text:
In the age of electronics, we all need more ways to plug ourselves in and manufacturers know this. They have responded by added usb ports and regular outlets to everyday appliances and this added convenience was enough to convince me to get the Seealle Bedside Desk Lamp with USB Fast Charging Port and Outlets Power Strip.

This lamp requires a small amount of assembly out of the box. The assembly is simple, but it takes longer than it should due to the way they pack everything into the box. I know they do this to require as little space and as small of a box as possible, but the way the shade is inverted with the base stuck inside it takes effort to get loose. I was extra careful and avoided damage, but many people will not be so lucky.

Once assembled, you just need to screw in a light bulb, screw the shade in place, and set the lamp on your desired table. My wife needed a night light for evening book reading, so I placed the lamp on her night stand. She likes having two places to plug in her phone, and the added light is nice for reading. There is a master switch on the cord and this provides another way to turn everything on and off, including the outlets. Another switch on the side of the base also controls the outlet. This is why, when you plug something in, you need to check to make sure it is charging. If it isn’t, then there is a good chance that one of the switches is in the off position. The light can be turned on/off using either the switch on the cord or by pulling the vertical, hanging metal cord underneath the light bulb.

This small light looks good on a night stand, but it is slightly smaller than expected. It also seems rather delicate and due to the darkness of the shade, it may not produce the level of light you need. I find it fine as a bedroom nightlight because we don’t want it to be bright in this type of setting anyway, but other people might find that the shade makes everything too dark.

It’s always good to have extra outlets and lamps with added outlets are commonplace nowadays as manufacturers answer customer needs. I like that this light has two added outlets, but the lamp is small and I still cannot get over the effort it took to dislodge the inverted shade from the base when I pulled the lamp out of the box for the first time. So, when all factors are taken into account, this lamp rates as average overall.

title: Much More than Your Standard Power Strip
review_text:
Electronics have become a regular part of life. There is really no sense in resisting- electronics are here to stay and most would agree, even if they have slight reservations, that electronics have improved our lives overall. These electronic devices need to be continuously recharged and an excellent tool for the job is this Kasa Smart Wifi Power Strip.

This power strip is intended to charge lots of electronics at once. It has six standard outlets and three USB outlets. That means you can charge up to nine devices at once, making this a very useful and popular item to take with you at your next conference. You will find that people around you will ask to plug themselves in and you will have no trouble obliging. It has surge protection, too, so that your electronics stay safe.

What sets this power strip apart, however, is its high tech personality. It can be controlled remotely using the Kasa app and you can see exactly how much power each item is using, then shut off individual outlets if you like, all from the app! And if you have Google Assistant, Alexa, or Microsoft Cortana, you can use voice commands to control the outlets. That means being able to turn on and off, say, a light that is plugged into the strip with a simple utterance. It’s a geek’s power strip dream come true. I plan to use it on my holiday lights when the season comes around- it will be much easier then climbing behind the tree to manually turn the lights on and off.

Kasa Smart Wifi Power Strip is a heavy- duty power strip that seems like it was made to last. The plug on the strip does require a three prong outlet to plug it in, so make sure you can accommodate before you buy. It has all of the things you would want in an app controlled, voice activated power strip and it receives my highest recommendation.

title: Useful for Business, School, and Travel
review_text:
As much as we travel in my household, we need an assortment of luggage, backpacks, and other user- friendly containers. We have several different pieces and that’s great because it means there is always an appropriate bag for the trip at hand. But one area my household lacks a little is with smaller bags and that is what convinced me to add the Solo Gramercy Rolling Case Laptop Bag to my collection.

First and probably foremost, this bag is made to hold a laptop computer and it has a separate compartment for it. I like that the laptop compartment is quickly accessible because it means that, if you take this to an airport, you can quickly remove the laptop, as you are required to do. But this is much more than a place to store your laptop computer. It is also good for carrying books, brochures, and other paper items, with large and small compartments to keep everything organized.

I sometimes take very short trips that don’t require much clothing or grooming items and I was concerned at first that this bag wasn’t designed correctly to hold such items. But in fact, it is, provided that you don’t have much. As a man, I normally don’t need to take much with me anyway and I have found that I can fit what I need for a day’s change in clothing, plus my personal grooming items, plus my laptop, all within the confines of this bag. It won’t hold much more than that, so don’t think of using this as your sole piece of luggage for a multi- day trip. There isn’t sufficient storage space in that instance, but you can get away with using it for a one or two day trip.

This makes it ideal to drag along when you’re at an airport, but I should also point out that this bag is useful even if you have no need or limited need to use it during air travel. It’s also very useful when you need to carry your laptop and school or business books and documents from place to place. It’s better than a traditional briefcase because it has more ways to organize your items.

We like and need an assortment of bags in my household because we never know where we will travel next and what we will need.
