title: Acer Aspire: Everything We Want in a Computer
review_text:
Computers are an important part of life. I know, I know- we need to get away from electronics and try to return to the days when more personal interactions were the norm. But regardless of how you feel about the proliferation of electronics in everyday living, there is no denying that most of us need them to one degree or another. We are writers/bloggers in my home and need good machines to carry us through the day. And the Acer Aspire Touch Desktop is one excellent machine for everyday use.

Let’s start with the physical attributes. This Acer computer features a very large flat screen with excellent clarity, making it ideal for watching videos, television shows, etc. The keyboard and mouse are wireless, so there is no issue over wires getting tangled as you work. Best of all, the CPU is part of the monitor. There is no separate tower or other computing unit, and that means this computer is space efficient. All you need is a place wide enough to handle the width of the monitor. The keyboard is certainly different from the one I was using previously and it took some adjusting to get used to. But this is the case with any new keyboard and you know what?- the adjustment period for this keyboard was less than a day. In almost no time at all, my wife and I took to the change and had no further issues.

As for the set up, well, it doesn’t get much better than this. I can remember when it would take several hours and much frustration to set up a new computer. But with Acer Aspire, the set up was complete and the computer was ready to use in less than 10 minutes after removing it from the box! We actually scheduled some time in our day, thinking it was going to require a fair amount of time to complete everything. It was so fast I started to worry that I did something wrong. But that wasn’t the case- everything is pretty much ready to go, straight from the package.

Because of our writing and blogging, we often need to have multiple windows open at any given time. This was an issue with my wife’s laptop and it would often slow her computer to a crawl. With this Acer computer, there is no such problem. She can have ten separate windows open, along with Microsoft Word and Excel, and the speed is still as good as ever. Again, this is a definite plus, as computer speed is a top concern for us and many other computer users.

I always try to find something that needs improvement when I write a product review but with the Acer Aspire, I can think of only one thing, and it relates to the Office Suite. They give you Office Suite for a free trial but once the trial is up, you will have to purchase it yourself. Acer could easily make this improvement and while this type of criticism has really nothing to do with the functionality of the product itself, it is about the only issue I can find. Everything else about this computer is well above average.

Computers are essential to my household. We need our computers for writing, for the classes I teach, and other uses. With the Acer Aspire Touch Desktop, we have found a cutting- edge computing machine that fits our needs perfectly and has everything we desire. It’s an excellent computer that would look really good on your desktop and I recommend it when it comes time for your next pc upgrade.

title: Great for My Kid's Tech Table
review_text:
More electronics in the home means a need for more outlets. An ordinary extension cord will do the trick, but if you want something that looks nicer, has more functionality, and protects against power surges than one good option is the APC P11U2 APC Surge Arrest.

This surge protection device is great for those who need extra outlets for plugging in electronics and other things. It has eleven sockets plus 2 USB ports for a total of 13 places to plug things in and keep them running. An indicator light will tell you if there is an overload, which is highly possible when there are so any plugs. We don’t have this problem because we use this on our kid’s tech table. It allows them to plug in their cell phones, tablets, kindles, and other items- all which use minimal power- and get everything charged all at once without them fighting over limited outlet availability.

Each of the outlets on this surge protector has a safety closure, which is good for keeping out unwanted items. This can be useful if you have young children- wouldn’t want junior sticking a paper clip or other item inside one of the sockets. And a light glows to indicate that the surge protection is working as it should.

If I could change one thing about this, it would be the length of the cord. It would be better if it was just a little longer because it would be capable of reaching further. But other than that, this surge protector has worked just fine for my needs. It has ample space to plug in and charge all of our household electronics, keeping them ready for use and protecting against power spikes in the process.

title: Dell Inspiron 13 7000 Series: Updated Technology has Won Me Over
review_text:
Looking for a quality laptop at a fair price? Then one you might want to consider is the Dell Inspiron 7000 Series. This laptop computer offers the latest in technological improvements for an all- around user- friendly experience.

I have owned many Dell products over the years and have generally had good success with them. This Dell laptop impresses from the start, first with its attractive, modern design. It looks and feels the way a top- of- the- line computer should look and feel, with a lightweight composition and sleek appearance. Second, this Dell product is extremely easy to set up. A person needs no computer skill whatsoever to prepare this laptop for use. You just answer a few simple questions, link and e-mail account if you like, set up a user name, etc., and presto- you are logged in and ready to connect your wifi for home usage.

As for its usefulness, this Dell computer scores well in most areas. One of my kids likes to use it and she was immediately impressed by the fact that the hinges allow the screen to be folded backward, flush with the base, for a tablet- like arrangement. She likes to use the computer to play games, so she liked this capability. The images are very clear, too, better than those I have on my previous laptop, which was an HP model a couple of years old.

One of the key features of this laptop is its touchscreen capabilities. I must admit, I was a little skeptical about this feature for a few reasons. First, I was concerned that it wouldn’t work the way it should and second, I didn’t know if I would take to the new technology. I normally adapt to change quickly, but touching a computer screen when I could easily use the built in mouse control? I just wasn’t sure this would work for me. But now that I have used it, I like the touch screen feature. I use it more than expected and have now abandoned the use of the mouse, in most circumstances. The only slight issue I have had is with the tendency of the touch screen to not always react immediately. Sometimes, it requires a second touch for the command to accept. Other than that, it seems to work well.

Dell Inspiron 7000 Series has a 13 inch screen which is just slightly smaller than that of my previous laptop. The speed of this laptop is better, however, and it quickly moves from one web site to the next without much trouble. It’s a very good laptop for the price and it’s one I recommend.

title: Monitor Your Home or Office with Ease but try to Ignore the Wires
review_text:
Q- see 12 camera security system is a nice way to protect a home or business from threats. Install the cameras in different sections of the home or company and then access from home, online, etc. for top level security.

This security system seems much more complicated than it really is and the reason, I think, is due to the number of cameras. Looking at all of those cameras, out of the box, is a little bit intimidating and it leads one to believe that setup will take days and even weeks to complete. But it is actually much simpler than it looks and there is no need to install all 12. Just use the number of cameras you feel is necessary and store the rest for later use.

With this security system in place, you can access the live feed through the internet and even on your mobile phone via the Q- See applications. This is great for convenience and its one of the security systems best features. Other security systems have this feature as well, so it’s nothing unique. But it is very easy to use and it lets you monitor specific places on a property, for maximum security. Wherever you might be, home or away, you can take a look at what’s going on by pulling the mobile phone from your pocket. It doesn’t get much easier than that.

The one issue I have with this system is the same one others have complained about, and that is the wires. In the modern world in which we live, we expect wireless technology more and more. This system is wired and it could present some problems as you try to tape wires and otherwise conceal them from view. If this was a wireless system and I could place the cameras anyplace I like, then I would be hard pressed to find much wrong with this product. But I know many people who would likely reject this product immediately for this reason alone.

Security is important, especially for those who live in less safe areas or who operate a small business in a vulnerable area. With Q- See watching the home or business, you can feel a little more at ease. The cameras detect motion and can quickly help you catch a person in the act of theft, trespassing, or vandalism, providing proof positive of what happened and where. Like I said, the lack of wireless technology is a problem but if you can get past that issue, you will find that this is a very good security system for home or business needs.

title: A Good DVD Player for Those With Limited Needs
review_text:
Portable DVD players have their use and the Verezano Portable DVD Player is a decent one for general needs. With a nine inch screen area, stereo speakers, and a swivel screen, it’s a good DVD player for children and others and it’s nice to have when on vacation or in other situations when the kids need some electronic entertainment.

We use portable DVD players in my household mostly for child entertainment so I often base buying decisions and reviews from that perspective. This portable DVD player does seem to have the minimum requirements to keep the kids happy and occupied. It is made mostly from plastic and is lightweight. And kids love the swivel screen. I have had to step in a few times and calm them down, as they love grabbing the screen and twisting it back and forth.

I find the functions on this portable DVD player simple to use and my kids had no trouble picking up on the operations. I did notice, however, that the remote control does not always make the unit respond. I often have to grab it and point more directly at the unit to get it to accept my command and even then, it takes a couple of pushes before anything happens. It isn’t a battery issue, as it does this even when the batteries are fresh.

Speaking of batteries, probably my greatest problem with this Verezano DVD player is the battery life in the unit itself. A charge is good for only about 2 hours, and that means it will die out after a one full movie is watched and sometimes even sooner. This means a long road trip in the car or flight on a plane will be too much. The unit will die out and have to be recharged long before your destination is reached.

So, judging this product from different angles, it seems to have the adequate properties to make it a worthwhile purchase for those with limited needs. My kids really like the swivel screen and they quickly figured out how to make it the player operate. But the battery life and issues with the remote control convince me to lower my rating to 3 stars. You basically get what you pay for, and that means a very average product.

title: Is This Really Necessary?
review_text:
Notebook computers can overheat. It isn't a worry when you use your computer sparingly, but it can become a problem with extended usage. This cooling pad was designed to solve the problem by circulating air via two small fans with the power supplied by your notebook's USB. The movement of air is, supposedly, enough to keep your notebook from overheating or at least lessen the chances.

A product like this certainly sounds like a good idea and a practical solution to a problem, but does it really work as promised? Well, it does cause some extra flow of air, as expected, but the cooling effects are minimal. The main reason is because the flow of air is so light. Turn on the fans and place your hand next to them. You will barely feel anything and this is reason enough to suspect that it makes little difference.

Another thing to keep in mind with this cooling pad is that it will not work if you do not set it up properly. It has to be standing on a flat surface so that the air can flow underneath. If you're the type who holds your notebook on your lap, then a product like this will not work for you. There has to be space underneath so that the fans can operate and get the air moving.

The Mac Cooling Pad does fit securely on Mac's of different sizes and can be used for non- Mac pc's as well. I suppose it could make some difference in temperature, but it seems like a novelty product to me. Unless you are already experiencing an overheated notebook, a product like this is a waste of money.

title: A Simple Means for Security
review_text:
Bell & Howell's Wireless Video Door Intercom System is a simple system that can be used to communicate directly with someone outside your front door. The device is not just an intercom system- it also presents a video image of the person at the door, for better security.

This device pretty much works as it promises to work and it is basically a walkie- talkie with a video screen. One has to press the button to talk and, likewise, the person at the front door has to press the button to respond. The two- way communication has to be initiated on both ends for the device to work the way it should. You can still view the person at the door regardless, but for them to respond to your questions, they have to press the button. Don't be surprised if you have to instruct the person at the door to press the button before they speak. Most will not know this and will start to answer questions that cannot be heard on the other end until the button is pressed.

Besides the manual operation mentioned above, another issue I have with this system is the video quality. Now, I realize that the product is a simple one, but for the price, I expect a little clearer and more accurate image. It appears I am not alone with this complaint- many other consumers have said the same thing. You can easily tell who is at the door, but the video quality does not display the colors very well.

Security is nice and this Bell & Howell intercom system does provide some security and ability to tell who is standing at the front door before you turn the knob. It is overpriced for what you get, but it is easy enough to use and it does offer wireless operation, making it a decent choice for some consumers.

title: Good Protective Cover and Stand for your Apple iPad2
review_text:
The Targus VuScape Protective cover and stand is a pretty good, helpful aid for those who own an Apple Ipad2. It features a thin, lightweight design that is meant to hold the iPad2 snugly in place while you work.

title: Philips GoGear Vibe: Nothing Special, but Good for the Price
review_text:
Philips GoGear Vibe 8 GB MP3 Player is a reasonably priced MP3 player from Philips Electronics. Small and with a good deal of memory, this MP3 player offers enough of the basic features to satisfy casual MP3 users' needs.

Let's talk about the good points first. This MP3 player is a good value and it has a long battery life. A full charge can last the better part of a day so it is ready when you need it. The compact size and durable construction are also plusses with this MP3 player. It takes up very little space and the metal construction is made to last. I like the menu navigation as well and found it very intuitive.

Most important to an MP3 player is sound quality and in this area, my feelings are mixed. My MP3 player experience is limited, so I have little to which I can compare. title: Simple Intercom Unit for Basic Needs
review_text:
The Defender GK300- 7M2 Hands Free 2- wire color video intercom system is a relatively inexpensive intercom system designed to provide peace of mind with minimum hassle. This device is simple enough to install and is instantly ready to use with the flick of a switch.

Besides the simple setup, this monitor has some other interesting features that make it useful. I really like the night vision option because it makes visible what would otherwise be difficult to make out. I like the sound- it is easy to tell exactly what is being said- and I like the loud, easily noticeable chime when someone rings the doorbell. The fifty- foot cable is also nice because it is long enough that I was able to place the viewing monitor in my bedroom with no problem.

As for the cons, I can find a few. The video quality isn't the greatest- it is a little fuzzy, even though I can still tell who is on the screen. Then, there is the duration of the video- it displays for only about thirty to thirty- five seconds. After that, the screen goes blank and you have to keep pressing the video button to get it back. This latter feature is one I wish was different. Often, you will want to watch and listen to the person at the door, but because you have to remember to keep pressing the video button, you could easily miss something important.

This is a basic intercom unit, hence the average quality overall. I know there are more sophisticated products on the market, but they all cost several times more than this, the Defender GK300- 7M2 intercom. I suppose for the price, it is an acceptable option but don't buy this expecting a fancy, high tech intercom unit. All you get with this are the basics, making it good enough for only for those with minimal security needs.

title: Cool Digital Camera for Beginners
review_text:
Nikon Coolpix S220 Digital Camera is a compact digital camera that makes a good camera choice for the first- time digital camera owner who is ready to get started in the world of digital photography but wants something that isn't priced too high or requires too much tech savvy. It is one of the smaller cameras available and it is offered at a price level that makes it ideal for the budget- minded consumer.

Digital cameras are offered in many sizes and with many features and the Nikon Coolpix S220 Digital Camera is easily the smallest digital camera I have ever used. There are some cameras that are even smaller, but most are inadequate for my needs, due to their often tiny LCD viewing screen. This camera offers an LCD screen that is large enough to easily see what you need to see so that picture taking is optimized. The size is sufficient enough that it doesn't hinder the taking of quality pictures.

Picture quality is the most important feature of any digital camera and the Nikon Coolpix S220 Digital Camera does, indeed, take good pictures for a simpler camera. It also includes helpful features that produce better photographs, such as its image stabilization system. I also like the color options. Standard color is the option most photographers will use, but there is also a setting called Vivid Color. This option brightens the colors and in many ways, it reminds me of the colors common to a videotaped television program. However, one needs to be careful with this feature because I have found that it sometimes distorts the colors in certain situations. For example, outdoor pictures should not be taken using the Vivid Color option because it can result in a level of color that is a little unrealistic.

Another picture taking aid with this camera is its Smart Portrait system. This includes features such as Smile Mode, which automatically snaps the picture when the subject is smiling; Built- in blink proofing, which snaps two pictures and deletes one of them if eyes are blinking; Face- Priority technology, which focuses quickly on faces and adjusts brightness so that faces look more natural; etc. These features are nice, but not always reliable. I have found, for example, that the blink- prevention feature doesn't always work. Sometimes, pictures get snapped anyway with the eyes of the subject shut. Of course, one can easily delete the picture and try again, but it would be nice if this technology was more predictable.

The Nikon Coolpix S220 Digital Camera is a small digital camera, so it fits easily into one's shirt pocket or other small space. This is generally good, but it can also prove to be a problem. Because it is so small, it is easy to lose this camera. A camera this small and thin can fit into many places where other cameras will not fit, so you need to be careful where you leave it.

Nikon makes some very good digital cameras and they also make a few average cameras. Nikon Coolpix S220 Digital Camera fits into the latter category. It is a good point and shoot digital camera, but it lacks the sophistication of other cameras and some of its features are inconsistent. Still, it's a decent beginner's camera and its small size and 10 megapixels make it a good choice for those new to the world of digital .

title: HP937 Offers Large LCD Screen and Many Great Pictures
review_text:
The Hewlett- Packard Photosmart R937 Digital Camera is a slightly more advanced digital camera than the average with a few extra features that make some of the simpler digital cameras pale in comparison. I have owned a few different digital cameras in my day and with each purchase, I tend to look for more features in a more user- friendly package. This HP camera combines the features I had on my last Hewlett- Packard camera with a larger viewing screen and more photo effects for more advanced and more convenient photography.

Hewlett- Packard Photosmart R937 Digital Camera offers many good reasons to rate it highly but among them, the one that caught my attention first was the huge LCD screen. Small viewing screens are a great annoyance with many digital cameras, but the LCD screen on the Hewlett- Packard Photosmart R937 Digital Camera measures a whopping 3.6 inches. In fact, it encompasses almost the entire back side of the camera and it provided exactly the extra viewing area I wanted. Not only does the large screen make it easy to capture images and clearly see the image you are about to take, it is also perfect for the playback of the video feature. With a screen this large, one can preview a video with ease. There is no need to strain the eyes when the LCD screen on your camera is 3.6 inches.

This camera offers many different shooting modes to create just the right picture. Beach, landscape, snow, sunset, etc., are among the many choices and you need to just try each one out to find out which one works best for different situations. I also like the auto- shooting mode. Using this, the Hewlett- Packard Photosmart R937 Digital Camera becomes idiot proof. It will do its best to conform the image electronically, saving the user the time or hassle of seeking out just the right mode. Picture cleanup is also very fast with the Hewlett- Packard Photosmart R937 Digital Camera. The large LCD screen makes it easy to find problems and makes it easy to delete the problems with a touch of the screen.

Is everything perfect with the Hewlett- Packard Photosmart R937 Digital Camera? No, there are a few problem areas. One is the lack of available memory. There is enough space on this camera to handle about 20 to 25 pictures. This isn't much at all, and it won't suffice for even the casual picture taker. This is why memory cards are a must with this camera. Another problem is with the zoom function. It doesn't zoom very wide, and it is also one of the few features of the Hewlett- Packard Photosmart R937 Digital Camera that is not activated by using the touch screen. Another small complaint is the time it takes to transfer pictures from the camera to your pc. The 1.1 USB connection isn't very fast, so you have to be patient as you wait for the pictures to flow from one device to the next.

Perfect or near- perfect digital cameras may exist, but they will likely cost a week's wages or more and are not practical for the casual photographer. The Hewlett- Packard Photosmart R937 Digital Camera isn't perfect, but it does take plenty of great pictures, offers great editing, has a long battery life, and offers a gigantic LCD viewing area of 3.6 inches, all for a relatively low price. It's a winning digital camera in my book, giving you the minimum features you want plus a little bit more without the excessively high price tag common with the more sophisticated cameras.

title: Stores Your Laptop and Dozens of Related Accessories
review_text:
Case Logic 16-Inch Full Size Security Friendly Laptop Case is a storage and organizational device that is very useful for storage of both laptops and related accessories. I use this case when going on vacation and making other short trips. My laptop almost always accompanies me, and having a safe place to keep my computer is important.

This laptop computer bag looks much like other computer bags from the outside. Its black color and Case Logic metal badge with logo make it look like a briefcase when viewed from a distance. This gives the bag a more professional, serious look that makes it a good choice for businessmen and businesswomen. At the same time, the bag looks casual enough that others can use it as well. It could even double as a storage bag for other items and many students could use this case for hauling around a few books, folders, notebooks, and papers.

Opening up the Case Logic 16-Inch Full Size Security Friendly Laptop Case reveals an obvious fact: This is no ordinary briefcase/laptop carrying bag. There are separate sections and zippers galore. There are four main sections and these are subdivided into other storage sections with variations in each section that help users find the perfect place to store their notebooks, cell phones, calculators, pens, etc. One of the end sections is designed exclusively for your laptop and includes pillow- like walls to keep your laptop computer safe from damage. The other sections have a combination of pockets without zippers, pockets with zippers, deep pockets, shallow pockets, and even a nylon mesh pocket. With so many pockets and storage areas, one can quickly find the perfect place to store everything from cell phones, to calculators, to CD's, and more.

Carrying the Case Logic 16-Inch Full Size Security Friendly Laptop Case is made easy through the two available options: The briefcase- like handles and the optional shoulder strap. I usually use the handles, but if my bag is overloaded, I have found that the shoulder strap is the best way to go. Not only can this strap be used to carry the bag hands- free, it can also be used to strap the bag to a piece of rolling luggage, for even more freedom of movement. The strap is long enough to fit around most any piece of luggage, making a quick run through the airport fast and simple.

One other nice feature of the Case Logic 16-Inch Full Size Security Friendly Laptop Case is that it is designed with airport security in mind. This is one of the main appeals of this laptop bag because more often than not, when I am packing my laptop into a bag, it is for taking it on a trip and more than half of my trips involve flights. Case Logic designed this laptop case in compliance with TSA government guidelines so that you don't have to remove the laptop from the case in order to pass it through airport security. This is great for those who don't have time to waste and need to get to their gate as quickly as possible.

Case Logic 16-Inch Full Size Security Friendly Laptop Case has many great things to offer, so are there any cons? I can think of only a few. One is the lack of padding in the majority of the compartments. The laptop compartment is protected by padding, but the rest of the case is not. Thus, you have to be careful not to place anything delicate in one of these non- padded sections- particularly the one on the outside. These more delicate items will have to be placed toward the center of the bag instead of at the ends. Another possible con is that this bag is not expandable. Granted, it has enough storage space and is large enough that most anyone can find a place to store what they have. But the lack of expansion means you cannot place a large object inside this storage bag and it also means that some of the larger laptop computers may not fit.

Still, in spite of these minor inconveniences, the Case Logic 16-Inch Full Size Security Friendly Laptop Case is a very nice computer case with many great things to offer. It can be used to store your laptop computer and related accessories in many different ways, with a design that is both practical and imaginative.

title: Logitech Eliminates Strain and Improves Precision
review_text:
Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is one of the better computer accessories I have used and it offers a noticeable improvement compared to traditional computer mice. Its unique shape makes it much more comfortable and a no- sliding- necessary design eliminates the need to drag your mouse across a flat surface to move the computer pointer on your screen. To move the pointer, all you do is move the large, red marble trackball. There is less strain on the fingers and wrist, making for a more comfortable experience.

Besides the added comfort, another advantage of the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is that it requires less space than a traditional mouse. Because this mouse is stationary and doesn't need to be dragged across a desk or other surface, it can fit into many small spaces. You don't need to make room to drag it, so it can be placed in tight quarters. This is great for those who work in offices with limited desk space.

The Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse offers four buttons to use for clicking. The large tabs on each side of the mouse are used for the usual right and left click functions and then there are two smaller tabs right above each of the larger tabs that are used for various functions. These two small tabs can be programmed to perform several things, and many will likely program them to scroll since this Logitech mouse doesn't have a scroll wheel. But the tabs can be programmed for other things, too. Since I don't necessarily need to scroll, my small tabs have been programmed as browser back and forward buttons. This makes life a little easier because I no longer need to move my mouse to the top of my screen and click the forward and backward arrows in the upper left corner. I just click my small left tab to go back and my small right tab to go forward.

The Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is a marked improvement compared to the standard mouse, but I admit that it does take some getting used to. Having used a traditional mouse for most of my computer- using years, I had grown accustomed to sliding my mouse across the desk surface. Thus, when I started to use the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse, I kept sliding it around on my desk also, even though I knew this mouse didn't need to be dragged. It took some time to break this habit. It also took time to get used to the sensitivity of the trackball. The slightest movement sends your pointer flying and when I first started to use this mouse, I would continually underestimate the precision of the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse. My movements of the trackball were far too extreme. The pointer would soar across my computer screen, even though I would swear I wasn't moving the trackball very much. It is a very sensitive device that almost seems too loose at first because it moves so freely and with such little effort.

Compared to a traditional mouse, the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse has many great things to offer and it is a mouse I am happy I took the time to try. It is superior to the traditional model in most areas, reducing pain and strain and offering greater accuracy and an easy grip. It does take time to get used to, but it is worth it in the long run and even those who initially resist the change will be happy, in due time, that they made the switch to Logitech.

title: Like Technological Progress? Then You Won't Like This Television
review_text:
Philips Magnavox PR1903C is a simple television set designed for the technologically apathetic. It has very few features and very few of the mechanical and technological updates one would expect in a modern television.

This television set offers the usual minimum features a consumer expects to find in any television- like adjustments for color, brightness, etc.- along with a few extras, like a language control that allows the consumer to switch from English to Spanish to French, sleep timer, and close captioning. Most all features have to be accessed from the remote control- the front of the television offers no such options- not even to access the menu. Also, there is only one input jack on the back of the television, placing severe limits on accessory compatibility.

If there is one redeeming factor for this television set, it is the quality of the picture.

This surprised me at first, because the overall quality of most everything else is below average, leading me to believe that the picture quality would follow suit. But the picture is actually quite good on Philips Magnavox PR1903C. The sharpness is very good and I cannot detect any small lines or other problems with the viewing. In this regard, the television set deserves commendation. I can't really find anything wrong with the picture quality for this type of set.

Going back to the negative points, I have noticed that this television set is prone to wear out a little faster than others. One sign of wear that is easily noticeable is the button on the front of the screen, to access the power. This button is a large, round button that is plastic in construction and is enclosed inside a round space. When pressing the button in, it is supposed to snap solidly in place but instead it rattles back and forth a little, making me worry that it is going to pop off. Of course, the way it is situated inside the round space, it cannot come out (as far as I know). But the looseness is obvious and it is a little surprising. With the limited amount of times the power button on the front of the television set is used (it is usually powered on/off with the remote control), I wouldn't expect it to wear out so quickly.

Overall, Philips Magnavox PR1903C is an unacceptable television set for the many reasons listed above. I like the sleep timer and the picture quality is certainly very good, but the strikes against this television are numerous. There are too many bad points to make it worthy of a recommendation.

title: Acceptable Television, but Seriously Outdated
review_text:
Sanyo DS25390 is a simple, no- frills television that offers enough features to get by but is lacking in some of the basics that we now take for granted in television sets, making it a questionable choice of sets for many consumers. Starting with the remote control, this television is very limited and quite out of date. Besides the usual keys (the ten numbered buttons, power button, etc.), you get a set- up key, CC key (closed captioning), Enter, and a Previous Channel selector. The various settings for the television can be accessed from the remote using the menu button, and they include the usual options (changing brightness, color, etc.). There isn't much more to it than that and the control itself has an old- fashioned look to it.

Picture quality on Sanyo DS25390 is okay, but nothing exceptional. The sharpness is the greatest weakness of this Sanyo television. Depending on your distance from the screen, the images seem a little fuzzy on the edges. At a good distance, this problem is minimized well enough that most people will not notice but it is definitely not as sharp as the picture on most newer models.

Picture quality is most important, but one other important consideration when choosing any television is its features and friendliness to accessories. Sanyo DS25390 has limited abilities and limited features. Chief among these is the limits on input. There are only a few input and output jacks and, because of this, there is no way to directly hook up a DVD player or video camera. This fact alone would probably discourage most people from considering this television. You could probably connect a DVD player or other device by going through a VCR first, but how many among is still own a VCR? I realize this television set was considered acceptable during its day, but it is difficult to overlook things like this.

One other problem I have with this television is the sound quality. There is only one small speaker, so the sound delivered is in mono. This certainly reduces the sound quality when watching certain movies or music video. The sound is acceptable for most television shows because the need for stereo quality isn't important. But it isn't very good for certain films and other programs that are greatly enhanced with stereo sound.

Overall, Sanyo Model DS25390 is a difficult television set to evaluate. It seems adequate in some ways and it was probably considered a good television set when it was first introduced. But compared to modern televisions, I cannot imagine anyone buying this set. The fact that a DVD player cannot be directly hooked up to this television is reason enough to reject it. Add to that the picture quality and its lack of sharpness and you have a television set that is too flawed to recommend. It's inexpensive, yes. But you most certainly get what you pay for.

title: Taking Digital Pictures with Hewlett Packard
review_text:
Hewlett Packard Photosmart M407 is a nice little digital camera that is small enough to fit inside your pants pocket. This camera is one of the best buys around among cameras with greater than 4 megepixels and while there are better cameras on the market, this is a very nice one for the money.

My favorite qualities of this camera are its size, its ease of use, and its sharp resolution. Pictures can be taken in VGA (lowest quality) or in 2 MP or 4MP resolution. These higher resolutions are going to eat up more memory but they produce sharp, clear photos. For everyday picture taking, I have found the VGA to be just fine, but for someone who is more experienced as a photographer, the 4 MP setting is needed to produce the sharpest images. The ones you get with this camera at that resolution level are very good, but you need to keep in mind that the memory (without buying a memory card) is capable of storing only about 10 images at this level. Lower the quality to VGA, and you can store about 160 images.

Some of the disadvantages of this camera include its video capabilities and the placement of certain buttons and controls. The video is offered with an MPEG format and it produces images at 30 frames per second. Its quality isn't very good and I recommend it only to people who really need/want to take a video and have no other alternative. I don't like the placement of the video and picture shutters on the top of the camera either. The picture button is larger than the video shutter, like it should be since it is used more frequently. But the picture shutter is placed to the left of the video shutter on the top of the camera. The picture shutter is used more and it should be on the right side because, to most people, your instinct is to press the button furthest to the right. I cannot count the number of times I have accidentally pressed the video button by mistake.

This camera comes with batteries, two USB cables, a strap, a user manual, and HP image software. This software is nice because it helps new photographers organize pictures and upload them into a pc. The other additions are expected with a digital camera but they help aid in the usability of this electronic device.

Overall, HP Photosmart is a good digital camera for the money and it is one of the few that offers more than 4 megapixels at such a low price. It was the first digital camera I ever purchased and I haven't regretted making the buying decision.

Also, turn off the motion sensor while driving unless you want the camera restarting often. I found to let it just run is the best solution. Maybe use the motion sensor if you are using the camera as a security feature or something.

title: Port Replicator not a true docking station
review_text:
I'm rating this 4 stars since there is a bit of a gap in what Dell is calling a Docking Station versus what this unit really is. This is essentially a port replicator meaning that you have to have a separate power source to charge the laptop. If it were a true docking station you would be charging your laptop simply by being plugged into it. For this device you plug via USB and having an extra power plug in.

Now the good stuff. It works really well and I run triple monitors. Please keep in mind that if your monitors are a bit older and have the pin style plugs you will need adapters to convert to DVI /new style HDMI. Would I buy this again? Yes. Am I happy with my purchase? Overall yes but disappointed about having extra cabling for charging the laptop.

title: Pay the extra and get rid of ads but find out if it gets rid of ads in games too.
review_text: I have NEVER hated an electronic device more than this one.  I don't know why it doesn't show that I purchased this in 2022 (and also in 2010 - before Version 1 died).  I hate it, I really hate it.  I detest Alexa  and all the things she doesn't do but get in the way of letting you do what you want.  I hate her.  I LOVED my previous FIRE the ads were just a few seconds long and I could live with that.  But to play my favorite Spider Solitaire game I've had ads go on as long as 10 minutes,  I've had it forget to navigate back to the game and I end up having to go home and locate the correct version of Spider I was playing.  EVERYTIME I open the thing It is pure HELL trying to get to what I want.  For example, today all I kept getting was movies.  I'd go back to home, and it would still show me movies, I turned it off and back on - more movies.  When I did a search for either the book I'm currently reading (Spare) of course OR my favorite Spider Solitaire, Alexa kept displaying some kids Blue's Clues music that didn't have any of my search words in its name. After a number of tries Alexa finally found my game.  If I pay the extra to get rid of ads will that include all the ads every 10 seconds on any game, you play so you can get your points and move on with the game?  All I do is play this ONE game and read books and now I go through hell to be allowed to do it - between Alexa and Ads the device is barely usable.  Oh and get this - I was eating in the dining room (I live in Senior Independent living but I'm VERY competent on computers}  I was in the dining room reading Spare when suddenly Alexa decided she should show me how it sounded with audio and Harry started reading it to me at full volume until I figured out how to turn the volume off. It startled me and a number of others in the room - I was seriously pissed off.  I could do this on my computer, but I always use my kindle when I'm doing 4 different breathing treatments that takes over an hour or when I just want to curl up in a chair and read or every time, I get hospitalized due to lung issues.  How can I get rid of both Alexa and the ads?  I'll pay whatever it takes.  I really only have a few years left to live assuming I don't get a bad case of COVID or Influenza  (I have a weak immune system) and I don't want to waste it on Alexa getting lost or screwing around with ads and games.

title: Disgusted - no USB cable was included in my purchase, and neither were there any instructions.
review_text: Perhaps I shouldn't write reviews when I'm so angry and frustrated.  They say they include a USB cable (without a plug) and the seller DID NOT include a USB cable of any size.  Standard USB doesn't fit, the Kindle trapezoid charger doesn't work as the seller suggested.  I have no idea WHAT size each end of the USB cable is assuming had I actually received one with my purchase, which I didn't, - so I can't even try it out.  I have a dozen or more different cables we've collected over the years and NONE of them work.  No worries on the electrical connector assuming it really is USB - I guess I will never know what It is because it is NOT USB as it says on side of the player, and I have no idea what size the other end of that cable is because it's not included and there are no instructions included in the box.  I finally need to charge it and looked again for the supposed cable or instructions and realize there is no cable or instructions, I suspect this may be one that has been used before and they just stuck it in a box without adding all the cables.  As far as sound - it sounds like a cd being played in a tin can.  I'm not one bit particular and I think it sucks - my son-in-law bought me a speaker block that does work and now it sounds like a high-end stereo.  The writing on the device is back on black. I had to use my glasses, a magnifier and a small flashlight to read what it said just to turn it on.  I guess it now goes in the trash because the original charge wore out and I have no idea what size each end of the non-existent charger should be.  I only wanted this for when I am in the shower or doing my nails - to avoid needing to use my hands again so it doesn't get hours and hours of use.  I just wanted a simple USB (identified size) and the correct size plug for the other end.  I'm using this in the bathroom and there is no place to put my computer in there for additional usb ports.  I'm perhaps a little old-fashioned but I don't care for laptops- screen size is way too small and I need two screens , a regular mouse and a standard size keyboard so  I use a regular but top of the line, Alien computer.  Laptops are difficult to work on while almost anybody can build (or repair) a PC

Unfortunately none of our color Kindles work any more or I'd just use one of those (I did until it stopped working - and it was a bit of a pain to navigate but nothing like this new model).

title: What is the purpose of this device?
review_text: My AT&T/Direct TV salesman talked me into buying this worthless overpriced junk to somehow enable voice commands for my DirectTV remote (they are about the only tv service that has a remote without it).  Didn't work.  3 IT people in the family worked on it for over 2 hours just to get it connected to the Internet.  The only instructions I found on the Internet about using it to voice control my remote basically required "hacking" and reprogramming the Echo.  So gave up on that and cancelled by Direct TV service to go back to my old service that had voice commands and a wonderful search engine built right into the remote.  We did get it to stream music - and it sounded like a scratchy LP. So I have to buy expensive speakers for that? I'm out of table space for all of this and hate ugly cords running everywhere.  I'll just stick a CD in my DVD player or computer and listen to the music I want to listen to.  Siri on my iPhone has a better search engine.  It seems like every device you want to connect to (and I really don't want to connect it to anything - I simply don't care) costs more money for special equipment that will work with the Echo.  Spent HOURS of research on the internet trying figure out it's vague instructions.  The only time I need a smart anything is when I'm in my car and need directions - Siri does that quite well most of the time and I don't need to buy anything else.  In my home I have two computers, my iPhone and television.  All are pretty smart and keep me well informed on news and weather.  I have enough noise in my life - I don't need a device that just adds scratchy noise.  As far as music streaming Sirius is a huge waste of money so I stopped that service and decided my hundreds of CD's and/or an MP3 player can play all the music I want to hear.  I don't need any more complications in my life and I'm sick of trying to get devices to talk to each other - and the echo is the worst example of this.

title: Good Picture, Poor Camera and Support
review_text:
Hi!

I was very excited about this camera, having used the GoPro exclusively until now.

However, I have to say that I was extremely disappointed with the camera, the website support, the smartphone apps, and the PC software.

I found the camera manual extremely short on important info, such as what I could and could not do while the camera was attached to my computer via the USB cable. There are no instructions anywhere (that I could find) for using the Connect app. I guess they figure people will just touch the screen in various places to see what happens. I was surprised to find that I could record from the Connect app, as info online said that all I could to was "frame" camera shots.

In addition, the camera itself did not work well. The Storyteller software did download and install the latest firmware. Here are some of the things I encountered:

1. The camera would "hang" regularly, as in every time I used it. The only way to "reset" was to remove and replace the battery.

2. Bluetooth communication only worked about 50% of the time, using iPad, iPhone, and iPod.

3. I often had to "reset" the camera (battery re-install) for it to be recognized using the USB connection.

4. Record OFTEN didn't work!! I tried to demo the camera to several people and it would not record unless I re-installed the battery.

5. The camera often would not STOP recording! I would slide back the record switch and the RECORD light would remain on under it and on the bottom of the camera. Again, the only resolution was a battery re-install.

I could find no help for ANY of these issues on the website. I am VERY frustrated by the fact that they do not offer telephone support.

The Storyteller software is terrible, and very lacking in support. It is necessary to eject the camera every time its configuration is reset! This is very frustrating when the camera was only recognized by my computer on a seemingly random basis (I tried all my USB ports and even a different cable!).

I like many things about the Contour much better than the GoPro. However, GoPro has the industry momentum, and if Contour wants to slow that down and gain some traction of its own, their product will need to work better and be much better supported. I think the Contour is a better camera, but the few problems I had with the GoPro were resolved quickly and easily with the information they provided.

I hope this product gets better. Until it - and the support - improves, I can't use it or recommend it to anyone else! :)

hb

UPDATE: Received a call from Contour Tech Support. They "schooled" me on the fact that everything taking place in this camera requires the SD card. There isn't even a little on-board memory. Thus, if the SD card doesn't work exactly right, neither will the camera. Without an SD card working perfectly, all you have is a piece of hardware! They suggested that I format the SD card with the utility at [...] (SD Formatter), and then re-format in the camera. I have already sent back the camera, though!

title: OK, but you get what you pay for.
review_text:
Horrible customer service. Not quite ready software app.
Ordered two direct from Wyze. One was defective, with a purple tint to the video. Followed advice on their support forum to clear it (night vision on/off/on/off), move the case away from the magnet, update the firmware. Nothing worked. Tried calling "we are experiencing high call volume...unable to take your call...try email". Filled out the web form, attached the photo, 5 days later, no response. I guess I may have received a defective unit, but now I can't even get any support.
Software app OK, but one key feature not quite developed. These are indoor cameras with motion detect alerts. I can't disable alerts based on my schedule. There is only one daily on/off allowed. No accommodation for morning evening routine, no accommodation for weekday/weekend schedule. So, with my alerts off for the afternoons only, I'm forced to have alerts on in the morning with contact beeping most of the day on weekends.
So, yes, these work, are inexpensive, include some cloud storage. But they don't work well enough for me to pay to replace the defective one. I'll have to keep looking for a better solution.

title: A pleased long-time user
review_text:
Although this review may seem to be "a little late", I do think that my experience with the earlier model of this Sony is appropriate. I bought a KDS-60A2000 in January of 2007 so I've had it for a few months over a year. As most of you will recognize, my unit is a 60" SXRT from the previous model year.

Like many of you, I did a lot of Internet research before settling on the Sony - it was very highly rated by a number of sites. The final straw was live viewing many sets side-by-side on the same program from the same source - it was a no-brainer - the Sony had at least as good a picture as any Plasma in the store and the price couldn't be beat.

I use Verizon's FIOS fiber optic service and have the unit hooked up through my home theater audio. The picture - indeed the HD experience - is simply awesome - especially live sports - like ice hockey.

I did "tune" the picture using the DVE (Digital Video Essentials) HD optimization DVD and it remains the sharpest, most accurate picture that I have personally seen (including the high-bucks plasma sets). I've had absolutely no problems of any kind and there have been no regrets on purchasing this set.

Another tidbit: I also purchased a Logitech Harmony 880 remote control and am able to control the Sony, the Verizon HD receiver, a Yamaha home theater receiver and a Sony upscaling DVD with a single click. It's programmed via the Logitech Internet site (using a USB connection) and can handle about any peripheral you might have. I've got a bowlful of unused remotes now. It's a little pricey at $150 but it has contributed to my HD enjoyment by simplifying the mechanics.

title: You really need this remote
review_text:
Like so many others with multiple remotes, I view this unit as a very attractive alternative to a sixpack of remotes. A single button turns on (in sequence) my Sony HDTV, Yamaha receiver, and FIOS DVR/receiver. Or, alternatively, the Sony, receiver, and Sony DVD - depending on the selection. It even switches the input on the receiver appropriately. A single button turns off whatever units are "on". And one of the best features is the ability to re-program the remote via the Logitech website if/when something is upgraded or replaced.

The only downside is that (obviously) a "universal" remote can't select EVERY option that may be available with the manufacturer's OEM unit. But those options tend to be little used ones. Another peeve is that sometimes I must shake the unit to get the display to light up. Otherwise, I don't see how most folks can get along without one. I really like mine.

UPDATE (4/3/2013) I don't know if anyone will be interested due to the original date of this review, BUT just to show the utility of this remote, I thought I'd post this update. I recently replaced the previously mentioned Yamaha receiver with a new Denon unit and the Sony DVD was replaced by a Sony Blu-ray AND I added a Roku streaming box. I went to the Logitech site and created new profiles using the new equipment and now I control all of the new units just as well as it had controlled the original units. So, the point is - the remote can grow with your system when you change or add new equipment. Pretty great, huh?

title: A great little  - BIG speaker
review_text:
I was really amazed at the sound! A tiny speaker the size of a soda can that creates a wonderful sound environment. I have it hooked to my Echo dot and the sound clarity is really good! And the bass coming out of the top is pretty precise. It's not the thundering bass but the correct one (to my ears). Takes up really a very small space.

Set up was very easy. Pressed a button to pair it with Echo using Bluetooth. My phone and Echo both picked it up really quick. Can't really tell if it's going to work in long distance but I have no reason to doubt what the manufacturer is claiming.

The only issue I had was figuring out how to use the volume buttons. I assume it's a quick press to lower or increase the volume but it's actually a long press. And then I am not sure how long to hold down the button to increase and decrease since there's no visual cue. But once I found the right volume it's OK. I can control the actual volume from the source as well.

I got the black one so it sits very nicely behind a few Knick Knacks and not really visible. The sound is "surround" so it's not directional. I have not paired it up with a twin to test out the stereo effect. But that's not how I intend to use this speaker anyways.

Very happy with this purchase. Kudos to the engineers for putting together such a nice speaker!

title: This is the best e-reader I've ever seen
review_text:
It's just plain spectacular how good the Kindle Voyage is.

I'm kind of a gadget junkie. Whenever a new Kindle reader comes out, I pass on the old one and buy the new. So I'm coming from a place that has used everything from the old Kindle Keyboard through to this, my newest Kindle, the Kindle Voyage 3G.

First, screen quality. I knew it had 300 v. 221 PPI I had on my PW2, but until I saw it, couldn't believe how much of a difference it made. Now, the PW2 screen is great, but this beats it soundly. For regular reading, I don't see any reason to switch from a PW2 to a Voyage, but I'd imagine that with illustrations and such, it would make a really big difference. I can actually read at one size smaller font than I could on the PW2.

The light: Nice light, no weird shadings. My device is smoothly lit from bottom to top.

Size/Weight: It's smaller, definitely (not the screen though). Couldn't really see any difference in weight between this and the PW2, but honestly, what's an ounce either way, especially once you start sticking covers on it? It's not something I particularly care about.

Storage/Memory: I wish it were a bit bigger. Not that I have any desire to have 2,000 on my Kindle at any given time, but once you get into using about half the memory, these devices always slow down and get ornery.

Wishes/Dreams for the next e-reader: That they'd include text to voice. I doubt this will happen, but I wish it would.

title: Needed to wait a day before writing a review
review_text:
I've been using the Kindle since it first went on sale, buying every generation as it became available. My 3G KT arrived yesterday, and let me tell you, I was not impressed. Nothing worked in a way that seemed at all intuitively. It seemed awfully clunky. But I know me and knew I just get used to this version. It's a really good reader. Once you figure out how it works, it does become fairly intuitive and works well. I'm used to buttons, where they are, how hard to push, etc., so this was new for me, at least on a reader. It took very little time for it to become an extension of my hand.

If you already have the KK, you don't need this. You may like it a great deal, and think it's cool and all, but you don't need it. If you're coming from a K2, yeah, you kinda do.

Regarding not being able to use 3G to surf the web on this device. I don't care. The web on the Kindle has always been pretty awful, so less accessibility is meaningless to me. However, if it does to you and you have the KK, don't switch.

The one thing I really don't like is the fact you can no longer rotate your books to landscape or flip it upside down. When I'm in the middle of a book and running out of juice I flip it upside down with the plug on top and that's not doable with this. I'm sure that's something that will be addressed in one of their updates.

All in all, it's a really decent device, and super great looking, but lacks the spectacular awesomeness I'd decided it had without ever having actually seen it.

I like the fact that you can re-charge it easily with AAA batteries (not included). I have found that re-charging with a hand-crank is too slow. Solar re-charging works well on most devices if you keep the device stored on a windowsill for the year so that it is fully charged during a weather event. Having the option to use three AAA batteries is great because the radio can be ready to use immediately. Another feature that I like is that no screwdriver is needed in order to open the compartment in order to change-out the batteries. This is important when evacuating and also when the power goes out.

During Hurricane Ike, I evacuated to a friend's home. The storm made landfall around midnight or so. In the dark, it is hard to find anything, so it's good to be ready before the lights go out. I can remember lying in bed alone listening to my friend's radio (not this radio) in the dark as the NOAA forecaster reported the progress of the surge up through Galveston Bay and into the bayous, lakes, and streams inland. It was so helpful to know exactly what was happening to the area in which I lived.

My friend's radio was a very expensive radio, and the main difference between her radio and this radio seems to be the reception.

Hers ran all night with no interruption with reception. With this radio, I do have to turn the radio off and then back on if I lose reception to the channel. A really expensive weather radio would probably have better reception if you want to listen non-stop.

For my needs, however, this radio is excellent and is the best that I have owned in its price range.

title: Excellent desktop computer
review_text:
I have typically bought and loved Dell Inspiron desktop computers for use with school and business purposes and have been very satisfied over the years.

When we were told that we needed Windows 10, I tried to download it to my old Inspiron but was not successful because my Dell equipment was really too old for a successful install; I really love the Inspiron and Windows 7.

In February 2020, I bought a new desktop and had a really stressful experience. There was something wrong with the configuration, and the tech support people could not get the computer to perform properly. After many hours online with tech support, the situation started to seem hopeless. The pandemic began to become worrisome both here and in India (tech support), and I returned the desktop for a fully refund.

Last week I started again trying to find a desktop with Windows 10. I didn't want to spend a small fortune for a computer that I use primarily for shopping, email, browsing, and, rarely, online banking transactions. I found this Acer after reading good reviews. Since my current desktop is an I3 and has basically the same specs, I chose this computer rather than the I5.

One of my siblings told me that Acer has a long history of excellent quality and that I would be pleased. He was right! This desktop is great.

PROS:
Comes with Windows 10 pre-installed. Plug it in. It's ready to go.
Norton Security is pre-loaded with a 30-day trial period.
The computer is extremely user friendly. I had no struggles with glitches with any of the programs.
Bloatware is easy to recognize and easy to remove (a Windows 10 feature).

CONS:
There really are no cons except that the "feel" of the plastic components is not as hefty as some of the desktops that I have used in the past (other companies). The plastic casing of the tower, the keyboard, and the mouse are beautifully designed but not quite as heavy as prior desktops that I have owned. That isn't necessarily a "con," and I like the keyboard, mouse, and computer case. Very attractively designed.

MY RATING:
5 STARS

title: EDITED:  Not a good buy
review_text:
I have owned two LG "budget" smartphones through Verizon, the second of which was bought during H Harvey when the first LG ceased working in the high humidity. Last week I lost the LG smartphone, and the only "budget" phone available was the Galaxy J7.

It has been hard to use. For one thing, malware with ads almost immediately downloaded with eithr a Verizon or a Google Play app; Google Play Services are partnered with the phone. I called Samsung, which remotely took control of the phone but was not able to delete the malware.

Second, and more importantly, the phone freezes A LOT. Despite the fact that the Samsung agent set all of the APPS and controls to optimum performance, the phone does permit many system overrides.

Compared to the LG phones that I owned, this phone, while beautiful to look at, is not operating well. It is "buggy" and, consequently, time-consuming to operate easily.

EDIT: I have been able to improve the performance of the cell phone by working to uninstall or disable the many, many apps that are pre-installed on the phone. Many are system apps but seem to serve no purpose. I also discovered that the Messages app is not quite the same as the Messages+ app and that some of the problems that I thought were "freezing problems" were user-error problems associated with the fact that the two apps delete messages differently.

So I have upgraded my rating from ONE star to THREE stars because I have learned how to speed-up the response time of the phone. The popup ads are still a problem. As noted before, a Samsung agent took-over the phone remotely but could not remove the popup ads. The suggestions made by the Verizon agent did not remove the ads. I have been using FORCE STOP with the Game Launcher and Game Tools apps and hope this will correct the problem. Have cleared cache of the browsers and apps numerous times already.

title: Easy Move from Analog to Digital Over-the-Air Broadcast
review_text:
I have been using a converter box and analog TV ever since we were required to make the change to digital TV. My 29" SANYO analog TV was a gift and has been a great TV. However, I have wanted to make the change to a digital TV, as well.

Today I received the Samsung UN40H5003 TV and am very pleased. I also purchased the byone HDTV window antenna with a stand. Byone offers black, white, and clear antennas in a paper thin plastic. I bought the clear and mounted it on a byone stand, purchased separately. I liked the fact that this antenna offered a 20 ft cable since I needed to place the antenna in another room, and most of the antennas do not have cables longer than 10 ft. The TV and antenna arrived on time from Amazon and were packaged beautifully.

The delivery service brought the large shipping carton into my home. If you live alone, you will want to proceed very carefully so that you do not damage any of the items in the shippng carton or the Samsung TV box, but you should be able to gently move the Samsung box out of the shipping carton.

The instructions suggest that you assemble the stand first. Basically, a shell-shaped post slips onto the shiny black base and is secured using 4 screws.

Once that step has been finished, the other end of the shell-shaped post screws onto the back of the TV. This step is the most delicate step of the entire process since the TV has be to placed gently, face down, on a table or flat surface that is covered by a cloth. The post will be attached to the back of the TV. Instead of using a table, I used the Samsung TV box, lying flat on the carpet, as the table so that the TV was never at risk of falling more than a few inches.

The instructions are pretty simple as you begin to program the TV. Batteries are included with the remote, which you will use to turn-on the TV and scan for channels. The instructions suggest that all components (such as a DVD player) be added before the TV is turned-on.

The single most important step is to be sure to select AIR as the source if you are not planning to use cable or satellite, etc. To do this, you press the button labeled Source on the remove. Then you will follow the prompts as they appear. Many of the prompts are pre-selected (highlighted), so you simply press the Enter button, which is positioned at the center of the up/down/left/right arrows section on the remote.

There is a bit of a lag sometimes with the TV's loading of some channels. For that reason, it's best to re-scan often until you are sure that your TV has captured all channels within your viewing range. I don't know whether or not this lag is due to the antenna or the TV set.

If you get an antenna stand, as I did, you may find it hard to get the posts that support the antenna into the base of the stand. Just keep working with them. Eventually they pop into place.

The shipping carton was heavy, but the TV box inside the shipping carton was not heavy. I took the carton and box to the carpet and worked on the soft carpet, taking care to keep the TV set upright as instructed.

Everything looks great, and I'm delighted that I am able to get a few extra channels that I had not received before. I live about 35 miles south of metro Houston.

I want to add that Amazon shipped everything beautifully, as mentioned above. This TV is available at other stores, but I knew that Amazon would ship the item beautifully and would help me if there were any glitches with the shipping or delivery or return, if needed.

title: So far, so good
review_text:
My neighbor Mariam and I are in our mid-sixties. Her husband recommended this device so that we could get help during long walks just in case Mariam, who has a heart condition, begins to feel bad. We have great Verizon coverage in our area, and she has been very pleased with her tests of the device.

I didn't have any problems during the activation of my device: I thought that the steps were explained clearly by the Customer Service representative, who talked with me clearly and politely during our approximately 20-minute telephone call.

I have not yet retired and like the fact that this device can travel with me to work and back.

The only problem that I encountered was that initially I could not get the device to turn off. Consequently, I really couldn't figure-out whether or not it was "on" because I didn't know how to tell the difference between off and on. After several days, the "off/on" button worked properly, and I've learned that a voice speaks when it powers off and on in a way that is similar to the procedure that a cell phone uses when it powers on and off.

Because of the problem above, the cell phone was actually "on" for several days. I didn't recharge it during that time. The unit has a small "ready" light that blinks to show that the device is operating properly. The device continued blinking all week, and I am re-charging the device now and hoping to restore the full battery charge, indicated by a steady green light on the battery indicator.

It couldn't be simpler. I understand that a cell phone can be used to call 911, as well; however, it takes awhile for my cell phone to power up. It's not always easy to use. This device is simple and, hopefully, works as well as promised.

I am pleased with the battery life and so far am pleased with everything. Hope it isn't needed but am glad to have it.

title: Beautiful smartphone and tablet / Good for first-time smartphone users
review_text:
First, let me say that I purchased the Lucid 2 through Verizon, a fact that may be important to readers here who want to read reviews only of products purchased through Amazon. I am a very active Amazon customer but have a Verizon landline account; it was easy to move forward using my existing account.

The Lucid 2 looks like a beautiful tablet. It offers two modes: a mode for the first-time smartphone user and a standard mode for the experienced user. I chose the starter mode since I had not previously owned a smartphone.

The hardest part of the learning process was inserting the SIM card. You have to pop-open the back cover (also called the battery cover) using the same opening as the charger port. A new user does not want to damage the charger port, and it takes a little patience to be sure that you are handling the delicate SIM card and the removal of the back cover with proper care.

After inserting the SIM card and battery, one is instructed to charge the battery. A blue light shows that the battery is charged. At a later time, you can add a battery charging screen (three are available and are stored within the smartphone) so that you can view the progress of the charge.

There are video tutorials stored within the smartphone and a very fine series of help screens located at Verizon.com under Support.

The smartphone feels very much like a tablet. I was able to watch movie previews by accessing the App (icon) to an online movie site.

One of the main reasons that I wanted a smartphone was for weather-watching during hurricane season. There are various ways to use Apps (icons) that are basically shortcuts to features that you wish to use. The weather App also functons like a pop-up screen to give you instantaneous viewing of local time and temperature. My primary interest is the tropics, however, and I am able to access [...] easily. I will download the App from that site at a future time.

By the way, you can use Voice to access sites on Google. You can also use Voice to display the name of a person or a telephone number (that you had previously entered); you can then touch the name or number and then send the call. Voice can be used for text-messaging as well. As a young senior (age 63), I really like these Voice features.

I own a Canon digital camera and did not buy the Lucid 2 for photography. Those people who do use a smartphone for photography may wish to read reviews about this feature on Lucid 2; my understanding is that three or four other smartphones might be a better choice if photography is one of your priorities when buying a smartphone.

I have read some online, professional reviews that criticize the Lucid 2 as being plain from a design perspective. I disagree. One reviewer -- whose opinion matches mine -- said that the Lucid 2 is gorgeous. It is. It is elegant and fun to use.

UPDATE: I am having a lot of problems with freezing and lack of responsiveness. A LOT of problems.

title: Delighted with the Kindle Touch 3G
review_text:
Before buying the Kindle Touch 3G, I visited a Target store to see and handle the different Kindle e-readers. I immediately loved the simplicity, elegance, and convenience of the Kindle Touch 3G.

My sole desire is to read books easily without any distraction by the device that I am using. The Kindle Touch 3G is simple to use: "intuitive" is the word that ideally describes the operating features of this e-reader.

You can swipe the page to turn (as with any paper page) or tap.

Two toolbars disappear while you are reading, but both are accessed simultaneously with a simple tap at the top of the screen. A functional toolbar (allowing you to shop at Amazon, see battery status, etc.) appears at the top; a reading toolbar (allowing you to change font, etc.) appears at the bottom. Both are easy-to-use: just tap the choice you wish to make.

You have only two buttons to click on a regular basis: the on/off button at the bottom edge of the device and the Home button (looks like a tiny speaker) located just beneath the viewing screen.

You must hold the on/off button for approximately 7 seconds in order to power-off completely; otherwise, the screensaver will appear indefinitely.

Other features are available and are easy-to-master; however, you can begin reading out-of-the-box if you have a Kindle on your PC. The system automatically duplicates your archived items.

If you do not have a Kindle on your PC, you can begin reading once you register by entering the email and password that you use at Amazon.com. It is VERY, VERY easy to register: very user friendly. The screen and enclosed guide "walk you through" the simple process.

The Kindle Touch 3G is elegant. I also bought the case ($39.99). Together, the two items are almost as slim as a DVD and case rented from a Red Box. The design is sleek, slim, and pleasing to use.

Convenient? I found myself yesterday racing to an emergency room at my doctor's request. While waiting to be seen, I pulled-out my Kindle Touch 3G, began reaading a Sherlock Holmes short story, and had "no worries" about battery life or connectivity.

I heartily recommend the Kindle Touch 3G to anyone with an older relative who loves to read and may not have WiFi access OR who needs larger type in order to better enjoy the reading experience.
