title: Very happy with the Canon ELPH 100 HS (Grey)!
review_text:
The Canon ELPH 100 HS is beautiful, and the Smart Auto feature takes great, no-stress photos for the user who has little or no experience with camera equipment.

Before buying the Canon ELPH 100, I read reviews and did a lot of research online to find a point-and-shoot camera that I would enjoy within the under-$200 price range. There are a lot of good products from which to choose.

I next went to Best Buy, Office Depot, and Sears to hold different point-and-shoot cameras made by the major producers: Canon, Nikon, Sony, Olympus, etc. For me, these visits to different retailers is an important part of the process of buying a point-and-shoot digital camera for the first time.

Another important step is to learn whether or not the camera's software is compatible with your desktop computer. Because my computer is old (2006), I had to research compatibility with the different cameras that I liked. You can find the information at the product websites.

Canon has a very user-friendly website that influenced my purchase considerably.

I had XP Service Pack 2 on an older Dell Dimension E310. For the Canon, I had to download XP Service Pack 3.

I ordered the camera from Amazon.com. From the moment I opened the box of the Canon ELPH 100 HS, I liked everything that I saw. The instructions are clear and organized well.

Finally, I love the pictures that I am taking. No, they are not the same quality as those taken by friends and family members who own thousands of dollars worth of camera equipment. However, these photos are beautiful and fun to take.

I am practicing now so that I will be ready to take photos at baby showers and graduations in the next couple of weeks.

Is it easy to learn how to use the Canon ELPH 100 HS? It is VERY easy to learn how to use Smart AUTO. The sliding Smart AUTO button is on the top of the camera: you slide the latch to Smart AUTO, and you are finished. The camera "decides" whether or not to activate flash and also determines other settings.

To learn to use all of the optional features (P mode) is fun but not essential to photographing great photos right away.

Another reason that I bought the Canon ELPH 100 is that it is considered to be among the best in its price range -- and possibly THE BEST -- in low-light conditions. The only time the colors seemed to be distorted somewhat was when I took photos of pets sitting in a semi-darkened room while they were directly under the strong light of a table lamp. I found that the bright light from the lamp washed over all objects close to the lamp; the objects outside of the lamplight were fainter in color. Since then, I've taken the precaution of composing photos more carefully so that I am not creating a spotlight effect.

I read that the ELPH 300 could be a better choice if you plan to use the video features a lot. For me, the video features on the ELPH 100 are fine.

While in Playback (viewing photos that I have taken), I am learning how to use the displayed menus to select options such as Slideshow and Erase -- so far, so good. While not as easy as Smart Auto, the menus are fairly intuitive.

I have been very pleased. The sheen of the dog's coat, the warm expression in her eyes, and the mysterious, bold gaze of the cat -- all captured beautifully.

title: Good Little DVD Player
review_text:
Well, I've had this for a week or so now. It's honestly cute just because of its size. I've had books that were bigger than this is. The power cord is just a bit over three feet, that's a hindrance. I was lucky enough there was a plug just in range but an extra foot of power cord would be better. The unit comes with a set of thin but serviceable RCA cables. I have some pro level RCA cables I obtained when I worked for a TV station, springs protecting the cables at the connectors, super heavy cable and insulation. . . and when I tried them with this DVD player the weight of the cables literally pulled the player off the antique dresser I use as a TV stand but the picture using the included cables is fine, playback is sharp & crisp. The unit has a functional set of controls on the front of the player which are sometimes missing in this modern era. The remote is a little small for my hands and the layout is a bit cramped and wonky but it works as long as you're in the fairly narrow field that the remote and device can see one another.
I've binged a few of my older DVD sets so far. The unit has a resume feature that picks up wherever you left off. Actually there's quite a decent set-up menu for the unit. Enough to get you going but not so much you need a degree in sound and electrical engineering to figure things out.
My only complaints so far have been;
1 - the device when loading or searching for tracks can be a bit loud but while watching content its whisper quiet.
2 - occasionally it reverts to turning the closed captioning on. There's a control on the remote, 2-3 clicks and its fixed.
3 - the already mentioned too short power cord.
Pluses are many. The player is supposed to be region free, I have no foreign DVDs to test this with. The small form factor means you can (within the limits of the cabling) put it almost anywhere. It easily fits under the corner of my large screen TV with room to spare. The display is orange, I don't know why. It's not attractive but it is easy to read from across the room (maybe that's why it's orange). It does have a voice reading function for people with impaired sight. It will read every control or function as you select them.
Not a complaint and not a plus. Most devices have a single LED that stays on to let you know it's in standby mode and ready to go. This unit steps things up a notch. When it's off it literally displays "OFF" on the screen for all to see.
I've been quite happy with the functionality of this unit. I have a decent DVD collection I haven't been able to watch for a while so I'm pleased to be able to watch these old favorites, Serial Experiment Lain, Robot Chicken, Wonderfalls and many others.
Edit - I received the instructions from the manufacturer and another user on setting this unit up as Region Free. I followed them, several times, reverting back to Region 1 each time. When set to Test - Region 0 (supposedly the region free setting) Region 1 discs become unplayable! See the image I posted. The menus load but try to play any content and the message screen I shared "This Disc Not Formatted to Play In This Region." is all you get.
Manufacturer was unable to offer a solution.

title: Beautiful Screen, Does Not Have a Qualcomm Processor {Edited 05-17-2021}
review_text:
Edit - I'm leaving the original review below but. . .
Rating dropped to two stars, not sure it even deserves that. Don't buy this tablet. It's truly horrible. I can't go a day without Lenovo's own built in software; screen assistant, dolby, etc. crashing. This won't run casual games like Angry Birds 2, even trying to browse the web is a painful chore. Chrome lags horribly with only a couple tabs open. The display might be nice but when you can't even reply to a YouTube video without the keyboard disappearing and taking forever to reappear, often I have to clear the memory just so the keyboard will stay on the screen. Less than a year old and I hate it. I don't even want to try a warranty claim because I just don't want another slow, kludgy, poor quality tablet.
I would not recommend this tablet.

I was on my third replacement Fire 10" tablet and the same issue started happening again. I wanted no part of a 4th replacement so I decided to get this Lenovo M10 Plus. It was a recent release, had good specs and the price was comparable with the latest Fire 10" (that I had NO intention of even considering). One big selling point was in the Amazon description which stated "Throw in seamless Qualcomm Snapdragon octa-core processing. . ." Imagine my surprise on getting the tablet running CPU-Z and discovering it does not have a Qualcomm processor. CPU-Z reports a Cortex A-53, Lenovo's website says (as does the system information) that it has a Media Tek Helio P22T. This didn't make me happy. Trying to contact Lenovo made me even less happy.
But. . . I needed a tablet, I have a tablet, I'm going to keep it. Simple as that.
It does have a really sharp and clear screen. Color reproduction matches my laptop pretty well. I like the side firing stereo speakers. The remind me of my old Samsung 10" tablet that had speakers in the bezel that were aimed at your face. These are a close second. The Dolby Atmos controls take a while to tweak but sound reproduction is above average. I'm a little disappointed at how restrictive Lenovo is with Android 9. My settings menu, even with developer options turned on, I look like a strict business product that the corporation doesn't want the employees messing around in.
Performance is ok, this isn't a gaming rig and it shows. I tried Castle Wreck which I play on my Galaxy S9 phone and it ran, horribly, but it didn't crash. But again, I needed a tablet because I'm disabled and spend a lot of time flat on my back. I watch videos from several sources, surf the web and my casual games, cribbage, backgammon, etc. run fine.
I had to get a case for it. The tablet screen is slightly bigger 10.3" vs my old Fire's 10.1" but the tablet itself is significantly smaller than the Fire. It's thinner, lighter and the bezels are almost non-existent. That, plus the incredibly slick aluminum back made holding the tablet while laying down difficult to say the least. Found an affordable 3rd party cover that does what I needed.
All in all? The screen is stunning. It runs everything I need it to though not all I wish it would. Price was right and it had a full year warranty. It'll do.

title: Drastically Increases Size of Tablet, Poor Magnets {Updated}
review_text:
I tried my M10+ tablet for a day without a case, I only use it in my bedroom and it's stored in a pocket on my bed rail. I just couldn't hold the slick sides of the tablet and the small bezels just screamed I needed a case. The one from my defunct Fire 10" tablet wouldn't work and let's face it, this was the cheapest option I could find. I didn't care about the magnetic on/off function. I just wanted a case to make it easier for me to hold the tablet and something to protect the screen was needed as well.
The magnets are weak, seriously cheap and weak. They don't hold the cover closed unless it's laying flat on its back and then it's gravity and the weight of the entire cover. I put the tablet vertically in my bed rail pouch and in either orientation (cover in or facing out) it doesn't really sty closed. Maybe after it breaks in after a few months but the magnets themselves are not going to get stronger. They barely hold now. I don't plan on traveling with this. . . I don't plan on traveling period, so this case does enough. It's easier to grip though it takes an extremely thin and sexy modern tablet and bulks it up to look like something from years ago. Small price to pay. I don't like that the slightest movement causes the magnets to disengage and I can see the tablet come on while closed and in my bed rail. I've adjusted the self-timer on the screen to shut off sooner than I normally have my tablets set just to save battery life. The inner lining is a soft either felt like or microfiber material so the screen won't get scratched. The case has enough texture to make gripping it while laying in bed (adjustable bed) much easier than the aluminum table alone. That's what I needed, that's what I got. Better magnets would really have helped. I really haven't used the foldable cover to make a stand, I don't sit or use a tablet where that would be useful. Again, I bought this because:
1 - It is held by tension on all four corners and nothing else. Some cases for this actually cover the bezel area which I tried years ago on a Samsung tablet and absolutely hated the design.
2 - It literally was the most affordably priced cover. The same seller has several different colors and designs, a couple I'd have preferred but the plain black of their own products saved me a couple bucks over a colorful design.
3 - Access to all the ports, speakers, microphones and controls is well done.

Not 100% happy. . . maybe 75% pleased. It'll do. It was way cheaper than the Amazon brand cover I had to buy for my Amazon brand tablet.
If all you want is a cover to add grip to a slippery tablet and something to protect the screen from scratches this will do.
I think that covers a perfect TL:DR "This will do."

Update - Review dropped to 2-stars, the magnets in the cover were almost never turning the device on or off. The cover would never stay closed. The cuts/thin places that allowed the cover to be bent into a stand after a week became so bendable the cover would flop open leaving the screen vulnerable. I have returned the cover. The TL:DR is now "This just won't do."

title: Better Than the One I Bought In 2014
review_text:
I bought the original Fire TV Stick in 2014 when they first announced it. I used it on and off but we had cable and a DVR so I put it in a drawer. Recently I had some financial setbacks and canceled all the cable services. At about that time Amazon sent me an email offering a major discount on the new Fire TV Stick with Alexa integration. I bought it, delivery took a while and was even delayed beyond the promised delivery date. Installation was cake. Plug the wall wart into an outlet, plug the HDMI extender (recommended for better streaming) and USB power cable into the Stick. Mine oddly wasn't preregistered to my account but that took only a few minutes time to resolve. The longest time drain was downloading and applying the numerous firmware updates that were available. That took the better part of an hour, hour and a half or so.
Once done and running everything's been fine. Any streaming quality issues I attribute to my cable company constantly needing to work on the equipment in the area. I often had problems with the cable TV quality dropping or cutting out entirely. The new Stick is a bit snappier than the old, it's got a bit faster CPU though, sadly in five years the storage hasn't been updated. It still has the same 8gb the original came with. Alexa integration is nice, though mostly good for asking for specific shows to be played or asking for the next episode to be played before waiting for the onscreen prompt. Getting the weather displayed as on a Show is a bonus.
I think the best part of the whole purchase is the Stick's remote controlling the power and volume of my television keeping me from needing two remotes to watch TV. With the bargain price I'm glad of the purchase. I don't think I'd have bought it at full price but I'm glad I did when it was for sale.

title: Stylish Speaker
review_text:
This speaker seems more designed for more modern music somehow. Maybe it's how current music is mixed. I'm not sure but newer music like Billie Eilish has much more bass than music from the 70s, Led Zeppelin, etc. and even heavy metal from the 80s such as Iron Maiden. The older music, streamed from the same source, comes across flatter with a duller sound. It doesn't sound bad just newer stuff is clearer, has sharper highs and clearer bass.
The speaker is stylish with a nice modern design. There are rubber feet to isolate the unit and keep it from moving. Controls are. . . difficult to use. They're on the back, out of the way. They're dark although somewhat intuitive. Wireless connectivity was easy although the connection drops and reestablishes a few times a week at random times.
Issues with the speaker. I use this in my bedroom. The power/Wireless light is on the front and is a brilliant bright blue. With no other lights in the room this is almost bright enough to read by. I've had to resort to putting a piece of black duct tape over the light so I can sleep at night. The speaker has a narrow band where it sounds good; with the volume low the tone is flat and dull. Crank the volume and something, I think the passive bass radiator, buzzes horribly. Inside that volume window where the sound is good it's pretty darn good but it has it's limits. Not sure if it's my app or the speaker but every, single, time it loses wireless connection for more than a few seconds my volume, bass and treble settings reset back to flat defaults. It's only a mild annoyance but it's there.

title: Not Really Impressed
review_text:
I have had several water resistant shower speakers and none, not one, my $600 Samsung Galaxy phone isn't. . . nothing is waterPROOF. It's a lie. Many advertisers and sellers like to claim waterproof status but what they mean is water RESISTANT. IPX7 means a device can survive immersion, up to 1 meter (3 ft 3 in) depth for up to 30 minutes. Let's also be clear here; those tests were with pure, likely purified, filtered water not highly chlorinated pool water. Not salty sea water. Not brackish lake/pond/river water. And also not water containing soaps, shampoos and conditioners. All that. . . stuff in every day water is going to reduce the effectiveness of the water resistance of any device.
So, I unbox this and it's light. Lighter than just about any speaker I've used. I look at the specs. . . 3 watts. THREE watts of power? Okay it's supposed to be primarily used in a small enclosed indoor space but it also says it's great for camping, hiking and general outdoors stuff (please, don't blast music when you're hiking, wear headphones, show some respect and restraint). I've never seen a non-novelty speaker that was less than 5 watts. It feels light and cheap and thin. The suction cups; they send two likely expecting one to fail. Neither worked. The best I could get with the cup wet with soapy water, alone, no speaker, stuck to a mirror for maybe five minutes. I can't get these suction cups to stick to my desk. No worries, my shower has a shelf. I turned off my oontz Angle 3 and connected this to my phone using Samsung Music as a player to take advantage of the Dolby Atmos and excellent sound (only PowerAmp sounded better of the half dozen players I tested and PowerAmp is a paid app only) quality it offers. I guess if you wanted noise in the shower this would work. Sound quality was about as bad as you'd expect. Distorted bass, harsh highs, muddy midrange. No EQ settings I tried made this sound good. It's just not worth it. You can for just a little more money get far better sounding water resistant speakers. You should enjoy the music in your shower or bath not suffer with it.

title: Loving My New Phone
review_text:
I had a Galaxy S4 for several years. It was suitable and did the job. . . mostly. I was having some battery issues and my phone wouldn't update past Android 4.4. I was running into apps that needed a newer version of Android. I could have bought something cheap but I decided to treat myself and found the blue Galaxy S9 on sale for a decent price. I have to say I'm loving this phone.
The 5.8" Quad HD+ Super AMOLED screen is GLORIOUS! I run this is high performance mode with the brightness cranked up. Games, movies, even YouTube and TikTok videos look amazing. The curved edge I worried might be distracting but honestly I only notice in a couple games.
Sound is really good for a cell phone it has stereo speakers. Volume is more than enough.
Performance from the Octa-Core processor and 4GB of ram have not struggled to run anything I've thrown at it.
The camera is great. Maybe struggling a little in very bright light with a light colored subject. Otherwise, night mode gives great low light results. Video shooting is very nice with great slow motion results and a nearly unique super slow-motion recording mode at a mind boggling 960 frames per second is a lot of fun to mess around with.
Battery life is good, I got most of a day is high performance mode and could easily extend it by cutting things back to save battery.
The fingerprint sensor is quick to unlock and easy to use. A trick I found online to improve performance of the fingerprint sensor is to register the same finger more than once. It really works like a charm.
The look is sleek and sophisticated though I'm protecting that glass body with a nice Otterbox Symmetry case. The only real minor negative to the whole thing is this weighs more and is larger than my S4, a little hard on my hands and pocket but really, it's worth it.
I can't express how happy I am with this phone. I'm even buying props and things to use in creative videos and photo shoots.

review_text:
I have two desks in my den. One has my 3D printer and other electronics. I have a similar (though more expensive) power tower on that desk. My other desk is for my laptop and random crafting. I had been using an old extension cord that lacked three prong plugs. When this tower became available I was happy to be able to replace the old extension cord and be able to charge my numerous USB devices. Then it arrived. . .

Tips over too easily. It doesn't instill confidence in the product. I like the idea of a desktop power tower and have one I rely on. I don't recommend this one.

title: Nice Dash Camera
review_text:
I like the size. It's small enough that I was able to put it on the far side of the mirror and I really have to crane my neck to see the body. That being said I didn't pull the trim and conceal the cable so that runs down almost in the center of the car. But after a few weeks I completely stopped noticing it. The screen shuts down to be less of a distraction and the status indicator lights aren't bright enough to be annoying, even at night. Installation was fairly easy. Hardest part for me was getting the static disc that goes on the windshield and is what the mount glues to (this is done so you're not putting super strong glue directly on the glass) off its backing paper. I ended up needing an Xacto knife to get it free. Clean the glass then the clear plastic disk applies to the glass with static cling. The mount sticks to this and the camera easily attaches to the ball socket and can be swiveled into optimal position before being tightened down.
There are many settings you can use to configure your camera, I suggest going over them carefully and making the changes you want before mounting the camera. It's small and the buttons are fiddly. Some options include recording audio or not (I've got a foul mouth and tend to sing horribly off key so I turned my audio off), video resolution I set it to highest for best possible details, clip recording length; the camera will film for X number of minutes before saving a clip and starting the next (once the memory card is full the oldest video is deleted to make room for new video) I have mine set to 3 minute intervals. There's a G force sensitivity setting that once triggered (by impact or even extreme braking) it locks the current recording so it can't be deleted, recommended is medium to avoid over sensitivity. Night recording can be set to color or black and white. It does a good job with color in most situations. There's a ton of other options so make sure you explore and see what there is you may want to change. I'm quite happy with this unit and feel safer knowing it has my back. . . by watching out the front.

title: A Strong Entry Level Router
review_text:
This is a review of the Archer AC900:
It's a good router. In many ways it's a very good router. Might not be the choice for a large family with a lot of bandwidth consumption but it does do a good job for our small family usage. I've had multiple devices online at the same time the living room T.V. was streaming an HD movie. That and good coverage is all I really need. With our previous router the Echo Dot at literally the other end of the house had problems maintaining a streaming signal. Since installing the AC900 it's streamed music all night, every night for the two plus weeks it's been up and running. Signal strength was dramatically increased everywhere in the house. Speeds are a little better but not by too much. I had more of a consistency issue than a speed problem with the old router. The router sits low and doesn't seem to have great cooling so I have it sitting on a brace that I made so it's now couple inches off the shelf it's on. Better and more efficient cooling and less chance for dust build up.
I was happy to see that using a web browser you weren't required to install any software to get into the router's management although there is an Android app to manage the router. I've found the web browser access have be as easy if not easier to use though rarely I have to reload the main page a time or two but I think that's my choice of browser and not a problem with the device itself.
The router is great, for the novice, intermediate or even expert user. Unpack it follow the easy set up guide (pick a decent password) then connect your devices and you're done if you want to be or you can dig deeper and have fine control over the router's many features. It may not be the perfect choice for every installation but if you don't need a lot there's no reason to spend a lot.
In the end the AC900 delivers a lot of bang for the buck.

title: A Not So Good Anker Product (Updated: 01/23/2018)(Updated: 02/08/2018)
review_text:
I have a six foot PowerLine cable that's just about a year old. That's twice as long as any other cable, braided, cloth, heavy duty, whatever, has lasted. Where I keep my tablet in the pocket of the grab bar on my bed puts a fairly sharp bend in cables. I've had them cracking and splitting at the plug as soon as a week and never more than two or three months. I'm replacing the six foot cable for two reasons. The six foot cable just isn't long enough, it's really close and the ten foot cable is going to be more than I need but I think it's better to have the extra length. The cable has developed a permanent bend at the small end but still shows no signs of cracking or splitting. The other reason is the connector has loosened up a little which I've noticed in both my tablet and Kindle but it still works so it's a good backup cable to have around. The new cable end are very tight fitting which I'm happy with, the old one was getting a little too easy to pop loose but it got a LOT of usage so I really can't complain seeing as how much longer the six foot cable lasted. If this ten footer lasts that long I'll be quite happy.

title: Another Great Kindle
review_text:
I've been a Kindle fan since I pre-ordered the K3. I have owned that, the PaperWhite (IMO for the money the best Kindle available), the Voyage and now, celebrating ten years of quitting smoking I scrimped and saved enough to buy the new 7", 8gb, Oasis.
The extra inch of screen greatly increases the reading pleasure the twelve LEDs create a perfectly even lighting environment even with the light set low to eleven or twelve. Contrary to some claims I've seen the screen is not square, it appears that way because of the different size bezels. I miss my page turn buttons from the K3 and now I have something similar, on a wider bezel my finger doesn't slip off of and hit the screen.
The edges are a little rough, I'll agree with that. In ways it feels like the device was rushed into production. That being said this is by far the most comfortable Kindle to read for long periods of time on. The fact that you can flip it over and switch hands with all the settings remaining intact was a great idea. I HIGHLY recommend reversing the page Forward/Back buttons so the lower button is the page forward and closer to where you'd grip the device to read.
I bought the 8gb version which leaves just over 6gb for the user, I have over 200 books on my Oasis and Windows still shows over 5.5gb free, I can't see needing any more storage than that, ever. My one real complaint, I'll mention here but deal with in another review is the cover (I chose the Blue cloth cover). If it's dark or late or I'm tired I find the magnetic only cover rather easy to come off with a little torque. I in the past put a finger between back and front cover of my PaperWhite and Voyage for easier one handed holding. That's not a good idea with this new configuration. I did hold the Oasis in it's cover over a pillow and had a friend ready just in case and the device DID stay securely in place during some fairly violent shaking it's just a twisting action that easily pops the magnetic connection loose. I'm hoping a 3rd party or Amazon for that matter does something to resolve the issue and hold the device securely in the cover like the PaperWhite and Voyage covers do.
I've only had it just short of two week but I'm very happy with the purchase and am truly enjoying reading on this new device.

review_text:
Some people have claimed the screen is square, it's not. Like all previous Kindles this is measured diagonally. It only appears square because the one side of the bezel with the buttons (also not loud as has been claimed and the touch screen works fine if the nearly inaudible click might keep a partner awake).

title: As Basic As It Gets
review_text:
AmazonBasics at its very basic. . .
Where to start? This does not have magnetic closure or magnetic auto on/off. There's an elastic strap you pull around that holds the cover closed. There's also four elastic straps inside with foam & faux leather pads that I found very hard to get in place that hold the Fire tablet in place. That's not a bad thing. It does provide a secure hold on the device. Unless these stretch out easily they appear to be a good system for a low cost cast to hold the device in place. The cover itself provides some protection against drops and strikes it would be good if you wanted to toss the tablet in a backpack or purse.
Complaints, I have a couple. They show this being used as a standing cover. The front folds back and fits into a slot built into the back. Good luck with that! Maybe if you broke it in for a few weeks but right out of the box all it does, no matter how I try, is tip over. The stand is useless. Next, which actually should have been first. No matter how you twist, push, pull or move the tablet one of the elastic straps meant to hold the device in place partially covers the charging port. I was able to use the plug to push the band out of the way and plug in the device. My 86 year old mother struggled for fifteen minutes and gave up passing the job to me. It'll work, that's about the best I can say for it. There's no frills, unless you count a stylus loop as a frill. It's as basic a basic cover can get. The blue which we received is much darker than the blue of the Fire tablet we own. It's not ugly but a better color match would been nice.
Personally I prefer the covers with the plastic bezel that the device snaps into place with and the magnetic closure that secures the cover and automatically turns it on and off.

title: Good Sounding, Poor Fitting (on me)
review_text:
I debated between three and four stars these do sound quite good; fairly good highs and the bass isn't bad with a large 50mm driver. My problem is the fit. the headband is somewhat narrow which makes the bottom of the ear cups (these are on not over the ear) feel looser at the bottom as if they're rocking from a point just above the top of your ear. You can adjust the length of both ear cups but not the width of the of the band. They're a bit narrow for my head. At first I thought these hadn't come with the cable mentioned on the box but eventually I did. These come with a somewhat short 4.2 foot braided nylon cable that's not supposed to tangle. There's a one button controller that sits on me at about the top of the shoulder, the controls supposedly only operate with the iOS operating system (Apple iPhones) and not with Android or Windows operating systems.
So in the end, they sound good but fit poorly on me. I do have a fairly large head so there's a majority of people whom these would fit just fine.

title: Attractive But Cheaply Made
review_text:
Cheaply made feels like it will easily break. I do like the grey and blue color. Cable is proprietary, would using a micro-USB plug to charge instead of an old style round plug-jack add that much to the cost? With a universal cable for power I could use my 10' cable and put the fan nearly anywhere without worrying about wasting batteries. I'd only use batteries during a power outage. I can still use one of my large battery packs but I honestly find it ridiculous not to use a standardized cable.
The fan had two speeds, I guess we didn't need the option of three. On low it moves a fair amount of air and is nearly silent. On high, with no batteries inside, it tends to creep across the desk. Use care or it will end up on the floor. It's somewhat noisier on high but surprisingly more quiet than similar portable desk fans. It moves quite a bit of air on high.
Pros: USB powerable. Quiet. Can be run off battery packs. Moves air well.
Cons: Cheap, thin plastic, proprietary cord. 'Walks' across desk on high.
I honestly don't have much faith in the hinge for adjusting air direction. The high/low/off switch. Or the very thin power cable lasting a year but we're heading into hurricane season so an extra battery powered fan isn't a bad thing to have around. I'll update the review should durability become an issue.

title: Perfect Replacement For Previous PaperWhite Version
review_text: We have two PaperWhites with the lower resolution screen. Viewing just text there honestly isn't a LOT of difference until you look closely at the edges. I replaced my PaperWhite with a Voyage (an almost regretful purchase) back in October and while there is a huge difference the added sharpness of an extra 88 PPI and the two extra LEDs make a difference. Since I tend to read in dim light the sharpness mattered more than the number of lights. when my mother's refurbished PaperWhite started acting up (reboots, updates, nothing helped) jumping forward or backward two, five, a dozen pages at a single click and often when turned on would be on the wrong page we decided to upgrade her to the latest PaperWhite. She's used to using the touch screen for changing pages and the lighting in the PaperWhite was more than adequate. In fact if I was asked to choose, right now, which Kindle to buy as a replacement I'd stare lovingly at the Oasis, look closely at its price, and honestly buy the PaperWhite. Two extra LED and the page turn 'buttons' just aren't worth the extra cost of the Voyage. They lured me in last year but after having had them since October I realize I could easily make due with the PaperWhite and the price difference would buy quite a few books. Now that this has the same 300 PPI screen, the adaptive lighting I turned off the first day and never turned back on. The PaperWhite has all the features you truly need and often goes on sale for a great price. In fact we were discussing replacing my mother's somewhat malfunctioning refurbished model she said to buy one when it went on sale and I swear the very next day Amazon had the Kindles all on sale (except the Oasis, grr). He unit had done three years of hard labor, that lady can READ so I didn't feel bad about replacing it. She's quite happy with it since it looks and functions exactly like her old one though slightly sharper. It even fit her customized case. Quite happy with the purchase.

title: So Far, So Good (**Updated 08/11/2017**)
review_text:
I've bought expensive USB cable. I've bought cheap USB cables. I've had braided nylon USB cables that felt like they were taking your skin off you hand when they rubbed against you. Other than the braided cable every single cable I use to keep my bedroom tablet plugged in with has split, torn or ripped at the point just above the micro-USB plug end where the cable meets the plug (no, I don't, as I've been accused in the past, yank on the cord. I always use a firm grip on the plug.) Some last a month or two. My old white Kindle charging cable started flaking apart the same day I put it in use. I'd probably still be using the braided cable which hasn't failed but won't stay plugged in.
They advertise that this cable lasts 10x longer and has a 5,000 bend lifespan. I've only had it a short while. There just under seventeen months left on the warranty. I'd honestly be ecstatic if it lasts that long. I'm tired of worrying about shorts or what might happen to the tablet if it goes from plugged to unplugged over and over. So, here's to hoping that this cable lasts as advertised.

Update May 2nd 2017 - Well, here we are a little over three months since I purchased this cable and although it has developed a permanent bend just past where it plugs into the tablet it show no cracking, no lightening of the covering which would show stressing. This has literally at just three months has doubled the average lifespan of my USB cables. This device which is plugged in 24/7 (unless I need to charge my eReader) gets used numerous times a day, it just doesn't sit there. I'm extremely happy with the durability of this cable.

Update August 10th 2017 - I am amazed. No other cable has ever lasted as long as this Anker. I've had cables fail the same day, the same week and as I've mentioned it has developed a distinct bend from the way it hangs from my tablet, kept in the pocket of the grab bar on my bed, the cable shows almost imperceptible whitening just above the connector from strain but no cracks, splits or crumbling. It also stays firmly plugged into my Fire tablet and on occasion it's fine with my PaperWhite as well. Will certainly buy this brand again. Very impressive quality.

title: Affordable Coverage for Your Dot
review_text:
Here we have another case of purchasing an extended warranty being asked to provide a review but never having made use of (and hoping never to have to) the purchased coverage. The price was right but lower on SquareTrade's site (I'm signed up for the specials and such mailings so I should have been made aware of. But it's only a few dollars so its no big loss).

The plan covers up to three replacements of the covered item or the term of the warranty you purchased (two years in this case). After trying to troubleshoot your device over the phone they will make the decision to either repair or replace your item. If they decided to replace the item it's wholly their choice to either provide a new or newest model of your device or provide a refurbished model of what you have. They promise quick turn-around and cover shipping in both directions. If you do not return the defective model within in a certain time frame (I believe it's 30 days) of receiving your replacement your credit card (which you MUST have on file to file a claim) will be charged the full cost of the device when new.

I've heard nothing but good things about SquareTrade for years and almost all of the low-star reviews seem to be user's not understanding the plan or not making sure they would be covered for their purchases rather than anything to do with SquareTrade itself. While I hope I never need to use the plan it was affordable enough to make up for Amazon's fairly deplorable ninety day warranty (our refurbished PaperWhite came with a full year's coverage. A brand new Dot, like their seven and eight inch tablets (unlike their six or ten inch tablets, the Echo or Tap and their entire eReader line which all have one-year warranties) only has ninety days I don't know why. I've always trusted Amazon's electronics, I wonder at their apparent lack of faith.

But anyway. I've rambled on enough. The two years of coverage is comforting and was quite affordable. I'm happy with the purchase and honestly hope I never need to use it.

title: Truly Couldn't Be Happier {Updated 04-04-2017}
review_text:
I knew, due to my disability, that I was going to need to find a professional installer to install this Boss Audio Systems B9351WRC head unit and wireless reverse camera along with two replacement door speakers I decided needed replacement (and wow, they really needed replacing). The installation took approximately three hours or so. The only problem which may not be a problem but I'm a worrier. The bracket for the wireless reverse camera somewhat, but not entirely, covers the plate expiration stickers somewhat. Other than that the head unit fit as good if not better than the stock radio fit. in the dashboard.
This radio plays AM/FM stations though there's very few decent radio stations around here. The unit also plays from USB thumb drives which plugs into a port under a panel under the volume/pause/power button. I put 600+ songs on a USB 2.0 16 GB driver and it played everything as far as I could tell. There might be a couple VBR or odd format MP3 files it may not play but I haven't gotten to them yes. Nothing's refused to play and even a couple that had imbedded album artwork actually showed up but so small it was almost impossible to see and I had no idea how to make it better. The instructions in the manual were basically "Play with things and see what happens!" more than specific directions how different functions work.
What I went with, is a 32 gig micro-SD card that had the same 600+ songs the thumb drive has. But with the micro-SD card you can close the hatch under the volume and control knob which you couldn't with the thumb drive. There's also an AUX input jack for old style MP3 players and phones.
The six inch screen is sharp and crisp. The backup camera, even with a streetlight thirty feet away had more than enough light to back out of my garage. I even backed down the street a ways in almost complete darkness and could see just fine with just the reverse lights on the car. Now as long as no cops have a problem with it I'm golden.
I tried home burned CDs and while it took a few seconds longer to recognize it played them fine. I tried store bought CDs and they played right off the bat. OH! and it plays DVD discs jut fine in case my passenger wants to watch a movie as we drive. I promise I'm no dumb enough to watch a movie while I drive.
According to the installer I can leave the micro SD card in the unit all the time. So, 600+ songs anytime I want which I can shuffle or randomly pick and play songs anytime I want. I couldn't be happier. With the stock deck I'd sometimes get to my destination just as the deck decided to recognize the CD so this deck is a godsend when I really needed a new one. Now with as many songs as I can cram into a 32 gig drive. Right now I've got 687 songs and tons of free space. I may have to start buying more music and ripping some more albums from my collection to add to my micro-SD card.
So I can play hundreds, thousands of MP3 songs on a micro-SD card. I can play CDs both homemade and store bought. I can watch DVDs on a pretty sharp (all settings can be changed in the system) the dimmer is a bit bright until it goes off completely but it's not too bad or too bright. There's a user setting EQ option as well as several other preset settings to choose from. There are options to add sound effects such as large hall, church, cavern, etc. I avoided them entirely and set my own EQ settings with the loudness off. The new speakers sound great for high end and midrange. The stock back speakers add some needed bass.
All in all? This is an affordable head unit with all the features and functions one could ask for. It comes with a remote that I'm not sure I'm even going to keep anywhere in the car. Anything you need to do can be done on the deck and no one's sitting in the back seat of a '07 Hyundai Accent, seriously. So the remote is useless but amusing.
I love this unit, the backup cam is awesome, The many ways to play music. The fit and finish, it's close to perfect.
This a little long and meandering review but I really like this radio and I'm glad I replaced the door speakers and went with a professional installer who's basically given me a lifetime warranty on his labor. I couldn't be happier.

Update 04-04-2017: It's been nearly six months since I had this head unit and backup camera installed. Radio reception is still bad, I still despise listening to radio so that's no big deal. Have kept a micro SD card loaded with hundreds of songs installed. Turn the unit on it automatically defaults to that. Everything is still working fine. Professional installation was worth the money.

title: So Far So Good. Decent Tablet For the Money.
review_text:
This tablet was purchased to replace my 85 year old mother's Big Lots special that she used for years and which was starting to have more problems than it was worth. The biggest problem my mother had was adjusting to the wide-screen 16:9 format of the Fire tablet compared to the old fashioned 4:3 format of her old tablet. This also had a faster processor with two more cores and four more megs of ram augmented by an 8gb memory card to expand storage. The blue color is quite attractive. The tablet so far runs everything she wants and I've even taught her to use the appstore to download her favorite games. The colors are sharp and clear. Video is smooth and while we watched only one half hour show so far there was no pausing or buffering.
I think the only thing I honestly dislike and it's my fault for not seeing it when this was a Prime Day special. I can forgive the tablet going out of stock and not being alerted to that fact when we placed the order. What I find somewhat insulting is this is the ONLY Fire tabled that comes with a limited 90 day warranty while every other Fire tablet has a minimum of one year warranty. I think there's something wrong with that. I probably would have bought this anyhow. My mom can't stand the weight of my 10" tablet (an ounce heavier than the 10" Fire) and the 8" was (and still is) available in one configuration (color, memory, special offers, etc.) which wasn't attractive and appeared to be fairly heavy.
So far so good. The tablet is functioning properly with a couple glitches here and there but every touch screen tablet and computer has similar issues. Other than what should have been a year warranty like every other Fire, Kindle, TV stick/device and Echo/tap has. That's just wrong and unfair to people buying a specific size of tablet.

title: Speedy, Lightweight SSD External Drive
review_text:
I like tech. I've had a computer since the commodore Vic-20 came out. That being said I'm not into competing with or against other computers and computer users. I don't run testing or speed diagnostics on my hardware. If it works and feels or seems to be working as advertised and expected I'm completely happy. I just don't care to sit here are see how many micro-seconds faster my new drive is than my older ones.
All that being said I use external drives exclusively for maintaining backups of my personal files, photos, documents, music, eBooks, Etc. Everything else I can simply reinstall in a couple hours. I don't have that many things installed. My computing needs are simple. But I have lost files due to a drive crash so I meticulously make weekly backups of my important files. Currently I've been using two USB 3.0 Seagate Backup Plus drives to make my backups every Monday.
This new Samsung solid state drive is remarkably faster at copying files to than my mechanical drives and easily a quarter the size and weight of the Seagate drives. I had a couple hiccups when I first formatted the drive to NTFS (I had no need of proprietary encryption) and started copying my files over to the drive but after one or two false starts I got tens of thousands of files copied over with no more problems and have for several weeks just copied new files to the existing collections in their directories and once again this SSD drive flies through the process much faster than the Seagate drives. Now I have three complete backups of my files and feel that much safer and secure with three copies of my files and I love that there's no moving parts. The cable's long enough, about eighteen inches, to work fine with my laptop though someone with a desktop may want to invest in a longer cable.
I'm knocking one star off for a device this expensive not coming with even a cheap hard shell case or even a rubber plug to protect the USB port from dust. It's the one point of possible entry of foreign matter into the drive and causing damage or failure. For the price they're currently charging it wouldn't have been any real hardship to include a case or plug to protect this device.

title: Incredibly Tall & Useful USB Light
review_text:
I love this light, absolutely love it. I purchased a laptop without backlit keys thinking I wouldn't be using it all that often but a disability has led me to require the touch-pad on the laptop as using a mouse on my desktop had become a near impossibility. I had come across another flexible USB lighting system that was less than half the height of this light and also lacked the on/off function as well as the dimmer capability which I find extremely useful.
When plugged into my rear most USB port this light reaches just above the top of the screen on my 15.6" laptop and with the light dimmed somewhat it doesn't glare even where it's just an inch or so from the screen itself but sheds enough light that I can see the entire keyboard easily.
The neck is strong enough to hold its position while standing there as well as once it's unplugged and put on the table when the laptop is not in use. It does wiggle a bit at the USB port but I think all USB ports seem to have a little wiggle room built into them.
Control couldn't be easier though controls would have, to me, been more convenient. You quickly press/tap the end of the USB light bar very, very lightly to turn or off the light. Dimming the light requires holding the end as the light dims or releasing it and holding it again as the light brightens. Personally I think separate switches would be more convenient but the single switch works well enough.
I love this light. It's absolutely perfect for my needs and puts so much more light on the keyboard than the smaller light I previously used (shown in one of the photos I'll attach) plus the fact that I can turn it on and off as well as dim or brighten the light just adds to the usefulness of the light. This also works great with a USB power pack.
I received this light in exchange for my review.

title: Add Three Usable USB 3.0 Ports to Almost Any Computer
review_text:
This is a decent multi-port 3.0 adapter. My laptop, like many other older models had just one USB 3.0 port and I have several USB 3.0 devices. At first I had a little problem getting the computer to recognize the devices were plugged in but a little wiggling of the cable that came with the adapter and things started working just fine. When plugged in both of the the ends and the port slots glow a rather attractive royal blue. I was able to connect both of my USB 3.0 portable hard drives and there didn't seem to be any speed problems or differences than when I had a single drive connected to the USB 3 port on the laptop.
I have one quandary about this device and one slight problem. On the back of the unit next to USB plug is what appears to be a power connector of some type. The only reference I could find was in the product description where it says "configurable with power switch; and USB LED indicator(Without power included)" so I'm guessing maybe you can use this with a power connector as a stand alone USB 3 port. As to my slight problem this unit could be a little heavier. With two drives plugged in as well as the unit plugged into the computer the unit tends to easily slid around on the desktop. A little more weight would help keep the device more stable and in one position. Other than that though this is a cool looking adapter that takes up little desk space but adds three more usable USB 3.0 ports to your computer. This is a very handy and attractive device.
I received this item in exchange for my review.

title: Two Laptop Cooling Pad Reviews *Updated*
review_text:
I have been considering a laptop cooling station for quite a while now. I had really hoped to review the smaller N5 mode which appears much lower than the N3 I was asked to review.
The first thing I noticed is the unit expects your laptop to have a USB port on the left hand side. Okay, the cable IS long enough to reach one of the two USB ports on the left side of my laptop but just barely. The on/off button and the extra USB port that's part of the base which is powered by the laptop's port that powers the cooling pad are rather out of the way and hard to reach. The port is also USB-2 only so if your machine is like mine make sure you leave the USB-3 open for things that require USB-3 connectivity.
The single fan is very quiet, I wouldn't call it 100% silent but it doesn't make that much noise. When it runs it gives an attractive blue glow. . . which you really don't get to see because the laptop's on top of the cooling pad. There are two removable clips on the base end which can be used if you want to use any of the five higher positions to stand the laptop at and they'll hold your laptop safely in place.
I was a bit disappointed in the height of this unit. My laptop is ¾ of an inch from front to back to front sitting on the table. With the addition of this N3 laptop cooling pad the height increases to two inches at the wrist rest and two and three quarters of an inch at the monitor end. That makes using the laptop somewhat uncomfortable. In the instructions it mentions that if you want to use this stand you should consider using an external keyboard and mouse. . . Sorry, but if I wanted to use an external keyboard and mouse I'd have bought a desktop computer. I have a desktop computer I was just hoping for a small lift to the laptop and a bit of extra cooling.
This unit left me disappointed. It's too high, too hard to reach the additional USB port and on/off button. The adjustability is quite impressive you can raise the screen quite high, eye level or even higher, but I just don't want to buy and use an external keyboard and mouse. To me, that defeats the purpose of having a laptop in the first place. Being disabled I bought a laptop because I have such a hard time using a mouse and the touchpad on the laptop was a blessing. Some users may find this useful or handy but I honestly did not enjoy using this at all.
I received this in exchange for my review.

*Update*
I also received the N5 cooler to review (all items listed on the same product page share the same review pool) the N5 does not light up like the larger N3 reviewed above. The N5 has its power switch and USB ports far more conveniently located on the center of the back of the Unit. The N5 does not have the ability to adjust the height or angle of your laptop. It raises the front one and a half to one and a quarter inches in height in the front depending on how you position the laptop. In the back the laptop is raised between two and two and a quarter inches. My fifteen inch Asus laptop overhangs each side by about a half inch but that doesn't seem to affect cooling. Although the N5 lacks the light up fans and height adjustability I think it's a superior cooling unit that could even comfortably fit in your lap. The N5 is a solid four-star item while the N3 remains subpar.
I received this unit in exchange for my review as well.

title: Pack It Along in Style

There is a large zipper compartment with a soft nylon lining which is quite big enough for any 15" laptop. My Asus X533M fit with room to spare. Zipping the bag closed with my laptop which is no lightweight by any means was not a problem. I ,carefully of course, held and shook the bag by the carry handle, the shoulder straps and the even side pockets with my laptop onboard and all the seams held nicely.
Other pockets for accessories, gear, cables, etc. on the pack a small zipper pocket inside the main laptop compartment as well as another half compartment pocket in the laptop area. Make sure these are taunt when you use the shoulder straps. This isn't anything against the pack. I was actually pleased to see them stay with the retro styling all around.

title: Terrific Little USB Lights
review_text:
This is a review of the 2 Pack Mini Book Light LED Task Desk Lamp. I received these lights in exchange for this review.

These things are great! They're impressively bright and easy to adjust. My chair's in a darker corner of the living room and my laptop doesn't have backlit keys. I plug one of these into a USB port on the laptop and after a little adjusting to keep the glare off the screen and out of my eyes there's plenty of light to type and see even the small print on the function keys.

On top of being a good task light on the laptop you can plug these into a portable battery charging pack and instant flashlight! I have a charging pack with dual USB ports plugging both in creates a blinding amount of light. At only 1.2w draw per lamp a good battery pack would last quite a while.

Another use these would be handy for is if the dome/interior lighting in your car was inoperable. You could plug one or both of these lamps into a car's USB charging port for quick and you've got quick and easy interior lighting.

Two features I would love to see added to these lights are a dimmer control the lights are very bright and sometimes you don't need the full output of the lamp. An on/off switch would be a useful if not entirely necessary feature. I wouldn't mind the option to leave the lamp plugged into the laptop when I didn't need light.

One thing of note is on the opposite side from the lights there is a metal heat sink that does get quite warm. I tested the sink for a bit over an hour and while it didn't cause any burns it was warm enough that I wanted to stop touching it so give it a few minutes to cool down before handling or throwing it in your bag or pocket.

title: Can't Trust This. . .
review_text:
When I saw this I thought it would be a great addition to my camera gear. The description says it's good for DSLRs and up to six pounds. After opening and inspecting this monopod system I reluctantly tried my ultra-compact Sony WX9 camera on this mounting system. My conclusion is I can't and won't trust this rig with my WX9 let alone my much heavier mirrorless Fuji gear.

The padded extendable main monopod shaft consists of three sections that are secured with a twist. It's easy to not torque the sections hard enough for them to unexpectedly collapse while you're trying to take a picture.

The ball-head mounts, this system comes with two, are fairly smooth metal on metal construction. Alarmingly these have no secure locking system. You simply use your thumb to engage a friction locking system. All it takes is a tap to cause the ball-head to be completely free moving. I would never trust a camera I liked on these mounts.

There are two feet that come with this set. A rubber edged magnetic mount and a suction cup -
The magnet is too small for a secure mount. With the monopod vertical and not extended it was reasonably stable. Horizontally it felt unsafe set up in any configuration. Extending the monopod drastically increases the ease with which this tips over. The magnet is just not wide enough to be stable.
The suction cup mount was surprisingly strong but like every other securing point in this rig the slide to release the mount does not lock in place. It's just too easy to hit the release while trying to set things up. I had thought I could mount this low on the car to get some interesting video but after trying this out I'd be worried road vibration would cause this to release and drop the camera.

In conclusion: While the materials are of decent quality this system lacks security. I won't risk my cameras on it.

First and foremost let's get to the issue of PU leather, check Google or Wikipedia, it's not leather. It looks like leather. It feels somewhat like leather and it's supposed to be easier to clean than real leather. To me there's not really a lot of difference. I usually put my name, phone and email contacts under my Kindles. I couldn't get this OFF of my Kindle! I have bruises on several finger tips from trying. I may have to use a screw driver to carefully pry this off or I may need to cut this off if I decide to go back to my custom air-brushed Amazon cover. I'm going to leave it on for now. I've had black Kindle covers for years. This does everything the Amazon case does. There's decent protection for the Kindle. It has a magnetic clasp that automatically turns the Kindle on and off. It certainly holds the Kindle well enough. The cover folds back all the way for easy one handed reading. I'd have given it five stars but for one thing, the company thought it was a good idea to emboss their company name on the front cover. I just don't care for that. It's small so no one's going to see it. The only person who will see the embossed name is me and I've already got the product. I don't need to be constantly reminded who made it.

{Edit - 06/13/16}
Just slightly more than a year since I obtained this case. I've left it on all this time because I really do like the brown color and the lack of the metal plate the Amazon case comes with. Fit's been perfect only had a couple issues where opening didn't turn the Paperwhite on but even the Amazon brand has that issue from time to time. My biggest problem is all the brown on the edges and corners either is or has already fallen off. The bulge where the magnet sits is beginning to split open. It's gotten some hard use and been with me in my walker bag for this past year but it hasn't worn well and while I still like the color I'm not sure I want to replace this with the same brand if, even at this price, it only lasts a year before falling apart. Makes me sad. Dropped from four to three stars.

I'm very impressed by their customer service which got the new cover to me very quickly even though I could find no warranty information for the product anywhere. They even allowed me to make a color change and select the red instead of the brown I had originally had. I hope this cover lasts longer than a year. Thank you for standing behind your product.

title: Really Nice Zoom Lens
review_text:
My family got together and picked this up for me during Fuji's sale/promotion in March. This is going to cover Christmas and birthdays for the next few years :)

Build quality is top notch. The zoom, focus and aperture rings are all nicely sized and very... grippy. The zoom itself is almost, but not quite, too stiff. I noticed no creep whatsoever. Autofocus is, expectedly, a bit slower than the kit lens but still decent. Image stabilization is impressive enough for hand-held shooting in low light at full zoom. Image quality is impressive. The included hood is huge, seriously huge. It's actually a little hard to get the lens cap on with the hood on. Speaking of the lens hood; my one gripe with this rig is when fully 'on' the lens the hood tends to rattle a little bit. I've found that backing off the connection a 1/4 inch or so keeps the hood from rattling and still keeps it firmly in place.

It does make my X-E2 a little front heavy but it's not that horrible. I'm contemplating buying one of the extension grips from Fuji for the camera. A nicely padded neck strap is a definite plus when carrying a camera with this lens mounted on it. One thing I've had to pay attention to is when switching back to my 18-55mm lens I need to be careful of how hard I twist the barrel to zoom in and out this lens is MUCH stiffer to use than the kit 18-55mm that came with my X-E2. I worry I may break the smaller lens after using this lens for an extended period.

Highly recommended.

title: Not as Impressive as I'd Hoped...
review_text:
Beyond bells. More important than whistles. When it comes to a camera, no amount of features are as important as one simple question. And that question is "How well does it take pictures?"

And in the case of the Fuji Finepix S1 the answer is "It depends..." It depends on what you're going to do with your pictures. Are you going to look at them on the camera's 3" screen? Are you going to share them with friends who use cell phones? Are you going to post them to Facebook and Twitter and maybe Flickr? Then you will probably be happy with this camera.

I have to admit I'm what people, sometimes insultingly, call a pixel peeper. I honestly believe that if the sensor of my camera produces a 4608 x 3456 pixel image that one which is properly composed and shot should look good at its original, 100% magnification, size. The Finepix S1, not so much. I've shot several hundred pictures with the S1 and I believe I've come up with two pictures that look okay (not outstanding, okay) at 100%. That's not saying this won't take a decent picture. Reduce the size to 1920 x 1080 or smaller and the images look much better. Out of the hundreds I've shot I've saved more than a few 'good' pictures.

A few drawbacks I'd like to point out about the Finepix S1:

This is supposed to be their new 'flagship' big zoom camera but it has a smaller sensor than their HS30EXR and HS50EXR cameras. Why not put the bigger sensor in the (currently) more expensive 'flagship' camera?

No external battery charger is included. Charging is done in camera via a USB cable and AC adapter.

The camera is not threaded for filters. Seriously? To mount a filter on the camera you need to purchase a relatively expensive adapter. Plus you'll need a lens cap that fits the filter dimensions since the camera's cap cannot be used with the filter adapter.

No lens hood is included. An optional and somewhat expensive lens hood is available. The optional lens hood and filter adapter ring cannot be used together.

The screen for the EVF is somewhat far inside the camera housing. There is white light coming from the bottom of the EVF enclosure and the EVF screen is significantly smaller than the space it is in. This makes it feel like you're looking around a tiny movie theater.

The battery can be inserted wrong way around. I don't see this as doing damage to the camera but I've never seen a battery system that didn't have some kind of notch or tab to keep you from inserting the battery in the wrong way. You can fully latch the battery down and not have power to the camera.

When I first read the user's manual I was psyched to find out the camera had the capability to shoot high speed video. This was always something I wanted to play around with. Then I tried it...

The fastest the camera will record is 480 fps (frames per second) which is fairly impressive except it only records that fast at a resolution of 240 x 180 pixels. The video quality was good and the slow motion was fairly impressive but even on a 5" cell phone screen that size video is small. It's an unviewable postage stamp on a 23" monitor. Switching to 120 fps results in a 640 x 480 resolution video. This size was viewable and could even been watched (the quality suffered) full screen but the video speed wasn't as exciting as the much faster recording rate. It did make birds in flight an interesting sight but that was about it.

Some good things about the Finepix S1:

The camera body is weather sealed. It is dust and water resistant (I would not submerge it). If there's a hurricane or thunderstorm and I want to take pictures (and I will) this is the camera I'll be reaching for.

The 3" LCD screen is fully articulated which combined with the weather sealing opens lots of opportunities for interesting photography.

Super macro mode with ~1cm focal distance.

Smooth and quick zooming within the full 50x (24-1200mm) range. The zoom control on the shutter button has two speeds and there is a separate zoom control on the lens barrel which can be set to fast or slow zooming.

The camera has a nicely rubberized grip and body. It felt quite secure in my hands.

All in all? I like the features and function of this camera but I'm not ecstatic about the image quality. There's significant noise and grain in low light, shots where the ISO is above 400 and at the long end of the zoom. Reducing the size of the images and some post processing work can produce decent pictures. It is an interesting mix of technology and the weather sealing is a plus but the image quality isn't much better than my several years old Kodak Z990 which though not weather sealed has made hundreds of trips to the beach without incident or damage.

title: A Disappointing Camera From Samsung {Edited}
review_text:
My first impression upon unboxing this camera was "Wow, that feels cheap." Everything's made from unattractive plastic. The single dial on the top rear of the camera (oddly blank) feels light, spins too easily and clicking it feels mushy. The other buttons on the camera, power, movie and flash all have the same, cheap, mushy feel. The shutter button has poor tactile feel.

The camera is surprisingly heavy; for me uncomfortably, painfully, so.The back is so taken up by the huge 4.8" LCD screen that the thumb rest is too short, more of an afterthought that cause me quite a bit of discomfort during extended use. The DSLR style handgrip is quite large (perhaps too large for small hands) to accommodate the massive 4360 mAh battery.

On paper the idea of an Android OS with a 4.8" LCD screen and a big APS-C sensor sounds great but I was sadly less than impressed.

Because of the Android OS startup time from fully off to ready to shoot is a very long 23 seconds. In standby mode the camera was ready to shoot in approx. 4 seconds. The camera runs warm, very warm, even just sitting idle on a cool 50 degree day. I would worry about overheating in the summer months.

Image quality was unimpressive especially in low light. Early morning, post sunrise, images with sky and clouds were extremely grainy and noisy. Performance in full light was better but not spectacular. Auto focus was run of the mill, often seeking excessively in low light situations. High ISO performance was exceedingly poor. Past ISO 800 images were rather noisier and grainy. In auto mode the camera seemed to make poor choices for ISO and shutter speeds.

Controls. Almost every setting is accessed via the large LCD screen.

There are over twenty pre-configured shooting modes. I used several of them while checking out this camera. These selections are made from a top to bottom scrolling 'carousel' where you scroll through until you find the option you want. I found it annoying to find and stop on the mode I wanted. You're going to miss shots trying to find the mode you want.

Continuous Shooting: burst mode. Surprisingly fast.
Kids Shot: the camera plays one of three sounds to attract a child's attention and then bursts five photos.
Macro: The Galaxy NX has a surprisingly short minimum focal distance with the kit lens and the macro photos I took were among the best results I was able to get from the camera.
Rich Tone: Samsung's HDR mode. Processing time was excessive.
Panorama: This is a sweep mode, smoothly move the camera (a tripod helps) to capture up to 180°'s of view. Disappointingly the camera reduces the image size significantly in Panorama mode.
Multi Exposure: combines two or more images into one.
Drama: combines several images of a moving subject into a single image. The camera was very picky about detecting moving objects. I encountered at least a 50% fail rate trying this mode. Additionally, as with the Panorama mode the image size is greatly reduced.

The camera can also be used in manual mode. Samsung calls it 'Expert Mode'. This gives you access to the standard PASM controls. The settings are controlled by three half-circle on screen dials that I found frustratingly hard to use. Try to change one and my thick fingers would spin the wrong dial. Using Shutter Priority mode I found the processing time of 30 second exposures was a disappointing additional 30 seconds.

There are some things I did like about this camera. It's not all bad. It can produce decent images and I honestly think the majority of the limitations I experienced were due to the cheap kit lens. The 4.8" LCD is gorgeous, in the right light, I recently went back to a camera with a beautiful 3" screen and it felt small. Some of the included shooting modes are fun to play with. Connectivity via WiFi was rock solid (I wasn't able to test the 3G/4G connectivity) even in parking lots of places that offered free WiFi. There were eleven gigs of free space in internal memory. That was plenty of room for a day's shooting and testing. I never did get around to installing an SD card.

In conclusion...
I'm not really sure who this camera is aimed at. They seem to be trying to attract smart phone users with the ability to access the internet almost anywhere and instantly share you photos. But do you really need an expensive, heavy and complex large-sensor camera to post photos to Facebook and Twitter?
On the flip side I just can't see this camera being attractive to professional photographers or high end photography enthusiasts. While the inclusion of the electronic viewfinder is nice I found the all on-screen controls to be distracting and bothersome and the image quality was for the most part lackluster.

title: A decent USB 3.0 Cable
review_text:
I do frequent, manual, backups of my important personal files to a pair of Seagate portable hard drives. This six foot cable gives me a bit more freedom on where I can put my portables, lets me use a rear USB port and keeps my drives away from the edge of the desk where I had to put them when I used the short cables that came with the drives.

I was surprised at how heavy duty this cable actually was. It's almost too heavy. I've found it hard to flex and keep in place and while my portable hard drives are weighty enough to stay in place I could see this cable dragging a lighter phone or other device off a desk.

I had no problems with fit or connections and while it may be my imagination (I've run my backups hundreds of times over the last couple years so I know how long it normally takes) it seems like data transfer might be just a bit faster with this cable than with the ones Seagate sent out with their drives.

This is a well made, possibly too heavy for light devices, cable from AmazonBasics. I have used AmazonBasics cables for quite a while now and never had a problem with any of them.

title: A Rather Decent Monopod
review_text:
The Amazon Basics 67-Inch Monopod is basically (pardon the pun) everything you need in a monopod. It extends to a nice height and even at full extension it feels reasonably sturdy. Collapsing the thinnest section and using just the two thicker sections increases the stability greatly and still gives you a little over 51 inches to work with.

Build quality is decent. The locking cams are hard plastic but don't feel cheap and give a positive, tight lock when engaged. The foam grip isn't glued into place. It is just held in place by friction and the three screw heads that hold the camera mount to the monopod.

The monopod also includes a wrist strap held in place on the head of the mount by a split ring.

A carry bag is supplied. It's enough to protect the monopod though it's not padded and the shoulder strap is short enough to be more of a carry strap.

The rubber foot of this monopod can be retracted on its threaded mount to expose a metal spike foot for use in outdoor.

The only negatives I've found with this monopod are:
The wrist strap is rather small and I cannot fit it over my hand. For reference I wear a size large glove. For me this is more of a palm strap.

The soft foot has very little rubber extending past the end of the metal spike. I measured this at just slightly over 1mm. Moderate wear will surely leave the metal foot expose and potentially damage flooring.

All in all though this is an affordable and well built monopod and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.

title: One Heck of a Camera (Updated}
review_text:
I've only had the Fujifilm X-E2 camera and 18-55mm lens for a short while and I've barely scratched the surface of it's capabilities. This is a camera anyone can use right out of the box but also one that you can spend years learning to master.

The retro look and styling are very attractive but they made it, for me at least who was used to an extended grip on the camera body, a little hard to handle. I found myself hitting the AE-L and AF-L buttons often and frequently by accident spun the exposure compensation dial without even realizing I had. I resolved this with the LensMate Thumb Grip designed for the X-E1/E2. It made a good camera great. I also added LensMate's brass soft release button to the shutter release. It does aid in smoother pressing of the shutter button but it also looks great on the camera.

The 18-55mm lens that comes with the X-E2 is a real pleasure to use. The zoom is stiff enough to let you feel in control but easy enough that you don't need brute force to use it.

Image quality, even at 100%, is outstanding. I've been getting so many 'keepers' that I've had to reevaluate my shooting style. I feel like I'm overshooting. In the past I was shooting three or four hundred images in an outing and getting maybe four or six shots I really want to keep and share. Now, with the X-E2 I'm finding two, three even four times that many shots that are worth keeping. I'm going to need a bigger hard drive!

Battery life has been pretty good for me. Even shooting in temperatures down in the 30's and 40's I had no problem taking well over three hundred images and still having battery bars left. In the times I've gone out all day wandering around the county I've yet to have to swap out the battery though I did purchase an extra just to have around.

Functionality, configurability and controls are extensive and a bit quirky but easy enough to get used to. As an example the Q button gives you 'Q'uick access to many of the more necessary and often used controls. You navigate around the Q menu with the 5-way controller but you make setting changes with the command dial. One of the features I found most interesting was the ability to constrain the ISO in Auto mode and set a minimum shutter speed. I also liked the ability to configure the four letter prefix for file names. All the 'extra' settings like special effects, double exposure, movie mode and panorama are accessed through the Drive button.

I did find a couple small negatives. Nothing to cause me not to want to use it but made me wonder. The odd menu systems. The pop-up flash is a bit anemic and is somewhat blocked by the 18-55mm lens. It's even worse when the hood is attached. The shoulder strap that comes with the camera... I know they're usually bad but this is cheap camera bad not quality camera bad. I put it around my neck, gave a tug, and then threw it away without putting it on the camera. I expected a little more quality there. The tulip lens hood that comes with the 18-55mm feels hard and brittle. It too could have been a bit better quality. I already mentioned the LensMate thumb grip that I think is an absolute must add item (it's really worth the cost). My big clumsy hands desperately needed it to aid in stability and control.

Where to start with a conclusion? This is an interesting mix of old school retro styling and modern camera technology. I think Fuji have really blended them together well. I can see myself enjoying this camera for years to come. Very highly recommended.

{Update}
Not wanting to pile on the negatives but I had intended to and completely forgot to mention the battery door. It's really kind of flimsy and feels like it could easily break. Also, with the way it's hinged I find it rather hard to get the memory card out of the camera because it's so close and parallel to the battery door's hinge.
