title: A great value, love the SFF chassis, needs better packaging
review_text:
*UPDATED*

Update after living with this PC for half a year: Zero problems, fast, and works perfectly for my application (business use). And excellent value. VERY pleased with this purchase.
---

The PC itself seems to be a great value, and is working fine thus far. The system is plenty fast. The HDD is a bit busy/noisy, and spins a bit more than it should, as though the system is caching to disk constantly. I'm not doing anything demanding with it at all--just light MS Office use and surfing. That's it. No gaming, no video editing, nothing heavy. Note this system is intended for business use, and could not handle much in the way of gaming or video editing, as it has no video card. The on-board graphics use the system's RAM, so anything asking a lot from the system's limited graphics capabilities will slow the entire system down immensely. Luckily, I outgrew DOOM years ago.

The SFF case is heavy, but oddly a bit flimsy, with more flex than I had expected for the weight--especially the back panel--mine was oddly bent outward. I pushed it back in/straightened it (I had to in order to plug things in--the plugs were deeply recessed due to the bent real panel--very odd). The chassis itself is a joy to work with though, as the case pops open on hinges without turning a single screw--not even a thumbscrew, and everything is very accessible. The HDD's working vibrations and sounds are amplified by the plastic subframe the drive is mounted in, which acts like an amplifier for the vibrations. I worry a bit that the system's small case will have cooling issues. There just isn't much room in there, and there is only one small 3" system ventilation fan (+ the power supply's fan, and a fan over the CPU). There are vents on the front and rear of the system, but I would like a lot more ventilation--I would have appreciated a perforated lid. Heat is the enemy of all electronics, and my other systems all have more ventilation than this box. Of course, this is an off-lease corporate desktop workstation, and is not designed to have the long life of other systems. The components in the box are the cheapest possible variants thereof, and I do not expect this system to last more than 3-4 years at the most. That said, $269 for a branded Lenovo PC with a 3.2GHz Intel Core i5, 12GB of RAM and a 2TB HDD is a fantastic value. If it dies in 3 years, I will have gotten my money's worth.

Important note about the packaging: it simply was not enough protection. I guarantee the system took some hard knocks on its way to me. The UPS driver actually dropped it at my feet from a height of 1'--not kidding! The system is not packaged in an inner box within the shipping carton--the carton IS the box. The small Styrofoam corner blocks used to float the system inside the box are unusually rigid, so much so that they provide little in the way of cushioning, and one of them had cracked in half--meaning the PC wobbled around in the box during shipping. Also, the carton was sealed with "Microsoft Certified Refurbisher" packing tape, making it clear to all it contained a PC. They need to change the packaging--a desktop system simply needs more/better protection than this. I half expected it to be DOA due to the abuse it took on the way here from Arizona.

title: Serious (and odd) design flaw makes it uncomfortable to hold in your hand - not a good case for reading
review_text:
I looked at a lot of cases before selecting this one, and I am sad to say I am very disappointed in this purchase. I have an Omoton case for my Kindle PaperWhite. I really like the design of the shell--the way Kindle fits into on it, so I was trying to find something similar, where the entire unit is enclosed all the way around. This was the only case I found which appeared to fit this way, so I ordered it. Build quality is fine, and the Kindle does fit snugly in the case, providing the fit I was looking for. Unfortunately, there is a serious (and odd) design flaw in this case: a small lip that protrudes outwards and runs all the way around the edge of the unit.

This lip serves no purpose, and I do not understand why it was built into the design. I don't know why the lip did not register as a potential problem when I was making the decision to buy the unit--I suppose I thought it would be too small to matter. I was wrong. It matters. It is not an issue when you are not holding it: for example, using the tablet to watch movies and it is supported by the folded case on a flat surface (although this feels somewhat precarious/barely balanced). The issue is when you are holding the case in your hand and trying to read with your Kindle: the lip digs into your palm or fingers and after a few minutes becomes uncomfortable. You end up shifting the kindle to your other hand every couple of minutes. This is uncool, and makes what would otherwise be a great case almost unusable as a hand-held device. I thought about returning it, but given the hassle involved, I decided not to bother for a $12 unit.

I cannot recommend this case. If you plan on reading with this case (i,.e. holding it in your hand for any length of time), it will be uncomfortable (sure is for me anyway).

title: *UPDATED REVIEW* Will not automatically pair, on-board microphone disables the mics in my phone, and charges phone VERY slowly
review_text:
*UPDATED REVIEW*

A seller replaced a different defective FM transmitter unit with this one for me (mine has the Kollea brand name on it, but this is the identical unit, private-labeled). This is a better product than what it replaced, but is not without it's flaws. I have three (*UPDATE: now four, and the fourth one is a deal-breaker--see below) complaints with this unit:

1) It will not automatically reconnect to my phone about 75% of the time. I have to manually shut Bluetooth off and turn it back on on the phone, sometimes a few times before it pairs successfully. This is a hassle--a PITA. Every time I get in the car, I have to go through this process--every time power is cut from the transmitter, actually, so if your passenger knocks it and it pops out of the 12V socket, it will have to be re-paired, which is supposed to happen automatically, but does not, and you then have to go through the process. Frustrating.

2) Charge output is only 1.0A. this is why I returned the first one--phone gives a "slow charging" warning when charging from this unit, regardless of what USB cable I use (I tried four different cables, all of which I know for certain can carry 2.1A).

3) Callers have occasionally complained they cannot hear me well when using this unit, and I occasionally (but not often) encounter FM interference. I believe Bluetooth itself is part of the problem, and anyone who has used a few Bluetooth headsets or units like this knows audio quality is terrible. Period. We just deal with it. Add to that the burden of having to transmit your signal via FM to a car stereo and the user-side audio (what you will hear in your car) is always going to be craptastic.

4) (*UPDATE) When paired, voice recognition on my phone, which is usually quite good, becomes severely impaired. This is also likely the culprit for complaint #3, above. I suspect this is because when paired, it tries to use the built-in microphone for voice recognition instead of the microphones on my phone (of which there are 4). It is disabling the extremely good microphones in my phone (Nokia lumia Icon which is well known for having incredible audio input) and using the unit's crappy microphone instead. This microphone is located in the unit, which is attached to the center console of my car near the shifter, and thus picks up all the vibrations and related road and engine noise transmitted through the structure of the car as I drive. This approach is terrible. I have stopped using the unit for anything requiring voice input, including telephone calls. In other words, this is just a big awkward charger now, and one that charges painfully slowly (see complaint #2). If it were possible to disable the onboard mic, and use the mics in my phone instead for calls and voice recognition, this would be a much more serviceable unit As it is now, it is just a piece of junk.

Cannot recommend this item. There are definitely worse products out there. I have not tried them all, but of those I have used, this is the best one so far. I will likely keep using it until the lack of automatic pairing pushes me over the edge with it one day and I get something else. (*UPDATE: this thing just does not work well, and I am now looking for something else.)

title: Love this case - exactly what I wanted.
review_text:
This case is exactly what I wanted: extremely durable shock-absorbing (read: drop-proof) protection without screen protection. Let me qualify that statement: I did *not* want screen protection. I love the pearl eink display on my graphite Kindle Keyboard, and it now has a big brother. I do not want a screen cover, as this would greatly reduce the screen's otherwise remarkable clarity, adding unwanted elements such as bubbles, surface scratches, and glare to the mix--no thank you. There is a reason I disliked reading on the iPad so much I gave it back (very reflective!). In fact, this OtterBox defender case came with a stick-on screen protector--no way. It would ruin that big, glorious pearl eink display.

A screen cover serves no purpose once you remove the device from your backpack/messenger/tote/briefcase for use. Assuming you transport your Kindle device safely in an appropriate sleeve (you put your other expensive electronic equipment--your laptop/tablet in one; your Kindle deserves the same amount of respect), the screen protector is completely unnecessary--the sleeve protects the screen during travel. THAT is when the screen needs protecting--when you are not using it, from the other goodies in your messenger bag/backpack (keys, pens, earbuds, and anything else rattling around in there). Yes, that's right--I'm talking about a Kindle in an Otterbox Inside a sleeve inside your briefcase. ...Inception-level protection. You got it. Better safe than sorry, right? What if they once again stop producing our beloved Kindle DX and something happens to yours? I do not want to have to replace my DX--especially if it has to be with a Fire device (5% the battery life, reflective, heavy, expensive--no thanks!). When you are holding your Kindle in your hand, reading, a screen cover only detracts from the experience.

What you see in my pictures is exactly what you get: a beefy, black rubber (not silicone--too easily torn; rubber is much stronger) form-fitting sleeve with an equally form-fitting outer plastic shell. Science geeks like me understand how this works, and just in case you are not one, here is the idea: if you drop your device onto the floor, the outer shell absorbs some of the impact energy generated by the device hitting the floor. It then disburses the remaining energy of the impact broadly into the rubber inner lining. The rubber lining then in turn disburses the now greatly-reduced impact energy into the device. In other words, by the time the force of the impact is filtered through two layers of protection, the second of which is very absorbent and resilient (rubber) the device inside absorbs little if anything of the original impact.

I feel very good about having my Kindle DX in an Otterbox Commuter. If I ever had one of those incredibly poorly-designed (read: seriously fragile) apple devices, such as an iPad or iPhone (which I do not, and am not ever likely to), it too would live in an OtterBox Commuter case. OtterBox = the best protection a device can get. I paid $18 including shipping for this. A great price, and worth much more in terms of peace of mind.

title: Exactly what I expected--maybe a little better, even.
review_text:
I spent a long time hmmming and hawing over this purchase. I really wanted the OEM Panasonic case for my LX7, but at $65 here on Amazon, it was just too expensive. I compared the aftermarket cases for this camera and examined photographs closely. This was the winner for apparent quality and design. And it lived up to expectations.

I was worried that it would block some of the screen or controls in the back, but this is not an issue at all. This case fits almost perfectly (screw mount is slightly out of alignment with the hole on the bottom of the camera--but it works), and is of as high-quality materials as one can imagine, given that this is *not* a leather case. The prospective purchaser should be aware that the vast majority of the cases on Amazon for the LX7 are not real leather. You can tell a case is real leather on here if it costs a fortune. The real leather cases on Amazon are all >$50, and some are $100+.

For $15, this case represents an excellent value, as it fits pretty well, is well-made (sturdier than I expected!), and looks very nice. (I have the white LX7 and I bought the light brown case--the color of a well-worn baseball glove). One thing: as expected, the strap is made of vinyl, and looks it. I will likely be upgrading to a proper, padded camera strap though, so this is of little import, at least to me.

If you are on the fence, take my advice and go for it. This is a good value, and a decent case--especially for this price. I did, and I have no regrets.

Note: you will have to remove the case to access the battery/SD card compartment and the ports, as is the norm with all cases of this type for this camera (I was unable to find one that did not require this).

---

UPDATE: After several months of hard use, this case has held up remarkably well. No evidence of wear. I get compliments on it, as well. Note: Do not attach the camera to a tripod with the bottom of the case on. The knob on the case is threaded to allow you to do this, but getting it off the tripod mount afterwards is a nightmare. Just take it out of the case--trust me.

title: My world is forever changed; or how I learned to relax and love the box.
review_text:
This is ridiculous. Never before have I ever gotten so much joy from an electronic gadget (and I'm a gadget NUT). After renting from Netflix for YEARS, I finally got a Roku box for Xmakkah from my girlfriend, who shall henceforth be worshiped as a god. I LOVE it (and yes, her too!). I have only two complaints, neither of which has anything to do with the Roku box itself, but rather the service I receive from Netflix.

1) Netflix desperately needs to step up the selection of available streaming content. The vast majority of the 20K titles currently available are old, unloved, and largely undesirable. Sure there is some decent content, but nowhere near enough of it. A good example of this is TV: I can Watch Dexter, LOST, and Heroes, but not Survivor, X-Files, or The Sopranos. I can watch the Old Battlestar Galactica, but not the new one. I can watch Masters of Horror, but not The Twilight Zone. You get the idea.

2) Video quality degrades when other devices are used that eat up bandwidth. I use my broadband cable connection for everything except my microwave oven. Seriously: telephony (Vonage), Internet access, online backup, and Roku. If I am watching something on the Roku box and I answer the phone, the resolution on the screen drops dramatically and the audio quality on the call is terrible. You get the picture (pun intended)...

Oh, and I have one more issue, although this is not really an issue--more of a request: Roku needs to greatly expand the channel store!!! YES PLEASE!!

Setup was a breeze and I was watching a movie in less then 10 minutes (and 9 of those minutes were the Roku box connecting to Roku itself and registering/updating firmware). :o)

Get one of these.
Trust me.
Best thing I got for Christmas by a mile.

title: Buyer beware--lens mechanism problems
review_text:
This camera was highly recommended from a very trusted source, and the reviews were mostly positive. I expected a lot from it, and for a brief period, (maybe 4 months) it worked well. Then the problems began. Lens errors. Yes, despite Canon's insistence that this sort of thing "never" happens, the mechanical lens error you will read about in other people's reviews (known issue with this camera) of this camera happened to me. I bought it hoping they wouldn't, but alas, I am apparently a sucker. Next time, I shall heed the warnings of my fellow Amazonites. No more Canon products for me....

As time wore on, the lens error became more and more of a problem. After another three months, I called Canon. The (arrogant) tech support guy just said, "Oh, this happens when the batteries are weak."

"Oh really?" I said, unwrapping a new set of Energizer AA's. "Let me just stick these puppies in here and see what happens... Huh. Well, would you look at that. So much for your battery theory pal."

After embarrassing him thusly, his only "solution" was to send the camera in for Canon to look at it (at my expense). This would take a minimum of six weeks, after which there was no guarantee I would not continue to have the same problem with the camera. I mean, come on--a design defect is a design defect, after all. I was certainly not the first person to have this problem with this camera. Not only that, but no camera for SIX WEEKS?? I would not have survived.

Sadly, before I could pack the thing up and send it in, I dropped it from the staggering height of three feet. You guessed it, end of camera. Canon makes cheap crap with poor durability and cheap lens mechanisms.

So guess what I did? Yup, I bought myself a Nikon. I've had three of them with ZERO problems over the years. This is number four. My replacement is working beautifully, and is smaller to boot. Excellent image quality too. I will not buy a Canon again. Fool me once, it's your fault. Fool me twice, it's mine.

Buyer beware.

title: Quick & dirty
review_text:
This is going to be quick--I only have a minute. However, as an avid point & shoot hobbyist, I wanted to contribute my $0.02 worth in on this magnificent little gem. Small, simple, and almost goof-proof, this is an ideal inexpensive camera for anyone just getting started. No optical viewfinder, managable file sizes, and the typical unbeatable Nikon lens mean you get serious bang for your buck with this camera. Full auto works well, and easy access to simple manual control over the basic parameters of the capture process mean it is easy for anyone to make minor adjustments. Also, there are (I think) 16 or 20 custom auto modes, including fireworks, black & white, etc.

HUGE plus: this camera runs on AA batteries. Spend about $25 once on a charger and two sets of high-capacity rechargables (2600miAh), and you will be all set. Regular Energizers are good for 100+ shots with the flash. The rechargables I bought are good for easily 250+ on a charge. MOney VERY well spent.

For your dollar, this is a hard camera to beat--and what makes it great is that it's a Nikon--these people know lenses... and TRUST ME, it's all about the optics. Nikon simply rules in that dept, IMHO.

title: Nice but very fragile
review_text:
I got one of these for the holidays last year (12/06) and I was totally stoked. This was my first iPod--what a shame that it turned out to be such a fragile, poorly engineered device. I mean, this thing got dropped once from about 2.5 feet (it was only 2 months old) and it was TOAST (and it was in a plastic hardshell case!). I have had Laptops that survived worse. Come to think of it, I've had a lot of (far cheaper) devices that are better able to take abuse than this $400 item--including TV remotes, cell phones, Nintendo Game Boys (designed to be nearly indestructible), OTHER MP3 PLAYERS, etc. It seems that a physically appealing design does not necessarily equate to superior engineering--quite the opposite in this case. I do like it, and the replacement I got from Apple works very well. It's great looking and it does the job well. Too bad I'm so terrified of dropping it that I had to buy a big, bulky silicone case to improve its chances of survival. Let me tell ya, in its crash-test-dummy outfit, it no longer looks even the slightest bit sleek.

Have you ever dropped your keys when getting out of the car? Your cell phone? If you answered yes to either of the above, then you can probably expect to drop your iPod one day. I hope you have a (thickly) carpeted garage--or that it lands on your foot. Bottom line: If I were thinking of getting an MP3 player, iPod or another brand, it would have zero moving parts; on other words, I would buy a flash-based device instead of one with a hard drive.

I also cannot help but wonder why Nintendo does not take what they have learned about building child-proof, nearly indestructible portable gaming devices and apply this to a worthy competitor to the iPod. I would be the first in line...

I gave this product 3 stars because it does a good job of what it is touted to do: play MP3s & video/images. In fact, the user interface, including the GUI and the click wheel is one of the nicest, most intuitive designs I have ever seen on a piece of consumer electronics equipment. Too bad it's put together so cheaply. Grossly overpriced? Most definitely. I hope the iPhone turns out to be a higher quality piece.

---

title: My 4x4 iPod
review_text:
This thing is genuinely neat. I got the black one for my black 80GB video iPod. I had to laugh when I (finally) got my iPod into this thing (no easy feat, let me tell you!): it looks like an iPod wearing a piece of an offroad 4x4 tire--which is just fine with me. It also makes me think of something you might see in Doom3 or Halo... totally rugged and "futuristic". This is a sci-fi fan's iPod case. I have not dropped it (yet), so I cannot attest to any protective qualities it may have, but the silicone is very thick and (reassuringly) strong. Do not try this at home, but I am reasonably sure it would bounce around if I dropped it. I removed the beltclip anchor as I would never use it (I cannot imagine myslf hanging a $[...] piece of hardware on my hip attached by a flimsy piece of plastic that reportedly breaks anyway. Nope, my ipod's travel plans will consist strictly of into and out of the briefcase (or jeans pocket).

Incidentally, you may be interested to know that I bought this case to replace one of those clear acrylic hinged ones that did nothing for my last iPod when I dropped it (may it rest in pieces). No kidding--my friends, you do NOT want to drop an unprotected iPod, and the form-fitting clear case I had for my last iPod may have protected it from scratches, but it offered zero crash protection. I learned my lesson, and this one should do a nice job of both.

title: Excellent headphones for those who know what they're looking for
review_text:

They've been available now for 10 or so years. You can't get this high end quality audio anywhere else for this price point. I got an excellent deal. The headphone purchase also included 3 high quality extra items for just about the same price as the headphones alone. My package included an extra cable, a solid hard plastic carrying case, and a FiiO A1 headphone amplifier.
The headphones live up to all the positive reviews, and the extras included made for a very good total price.
I would definitely recommend this product.
Updated 2/4/2021, 4 months later.
I still love these headphones. I have to laugh when I occasionally check the customer reviews and find that most of the criticisms are based on how these headphones were purposely engineered. Let me be more specific. Some of the negative comments include:
-others around you can hear what you're listening to. Oh well. Too bad. They should probably put on their own noise cancelling headphones. Which brings me to my next point:
-they're not noise cancelling. Yup, that's right. When I did my search for headphones, I specifically did NOT want noise cancelling OR Bluetooth. Much prefer putting the money saved when not buying these options and putting it toward better cans.
-there is no microphone on the cables. Correct again. These headphones were not necessarily intended for those who want a set of cans primarily to support their cell phone addiction.
-they must be used with the company's proprietary cables to attach to the headphones. I'll take that and love it. Why? Because they twist and lock into the bottom of the can. How many times, with other headphones, have I moved too far, or stood up or whatever, and the cord would be ripped out of the cans!!
-too much bass, not enough base. Midrange too pronounced, or not enough. And they go on and on and on.
-the "best" (tongue in cheek) criticism stated that none of the included cables, nor the included adapters fit his computer. I don't know what kind of a computer this person has, but, if Bill Cosby appears in TV commercials for your computer, headphones should not be your #1 focus right now
-and finally, and I quote, "I needed to add an EQ to make them sound like I wanted them to". Precisely! These cans were designed and manufactured specifically for those who are looking for an accurate, unadulterated representation of the original recording. The way the musicians and the recording engineers intended it to sound. If one doesn't find that acceptable, and that's fine, include an EQ somewhere in the mix. As a matter of fact, I have more than my share of sound shaping hardware and software all over my system in order to tailor the music to my liking.
You need to like the sound quality reproduced through headphones and speaker systems alike. And this is very subjective. One person's likes are another person's hates, especially when it comes from those who love to sound like they "might" know what they are talking about.. I bought and returned a number of headphones because I didn't care for how they sounded. I kept these.
I do agree with one common complaint. The earpads do get uncomfortable after a while. I checked for aftermarket replacements, but many included their own negative reviews that they changed the sound quality from the originals. That's the last thing I want.

title: A very nice keyboard with many connection options.
review_text:
Typically I stick to higher end gaming keyboards. Mechanical and optical switches are generally my go to. I had never used a keyboard from this brand before so when I was given the chance to grab one, I figured I would see how it stacks up.

So far I'm fairly impressed. I've used some tournament edition keyboards with the smaller form factor from other brands so I knew what I was getting into when it came to the size of the keyboard. All in all, sizing is fine. They key placement and distance between keys works fine. I do run into issues at times where my fingers get lost on the right side of the keyboard. Getting used to that will come in time though. The key response is quick. They are mechanical switches but they do manage to deaden the sound a bit which is nice. The RGB features are basic at best. You have a few settings you can select from and all of it is done directly on the keyboard itself. It has your normal basic modes. It illuminates well though and you can increase/decrease the brightness. The build quality is nice. For being a 75% keyboard, it has some weight to it. I like the fact the keys are labeled for both Mac and PC. I primarily use it on my PC though. The place where it seems to shine is in the connectivity department. I can connect it by bluetooth to numerous devices or I can have it wired. I generally run wired to my main PC and if I need to use it on my MacBook or other devices, I just unplug it from the PC and connect by BT to the other device. It works out nicely.

From a gaming standpoint (which I do a lot of), I'm not certain that I like it as much yet. Emphasis on the "yet". I know it takes some time to become accustomed to a new keyboard. The response and feel. I'm going to continue gaming on it for a while to see if I become more adapted to it. It just feels different than what I'm used to. It most likely has to do with the key spacing more so than anything else.

This is definitely a nice keyboard and I recommend it. I will most likely continue to use it as my daily keyboard for a while longer to see how it holds up over time.

title: Nice band but could be better
review_text:
I've always leaned more towards this style band and this one is decent. It's definitely worth the price point, however there are some minor issues compared to other bands of this style that I have. The cuts in the metal, particularly on the sides, are not rounded off or smoothed. On my wrist, this makes it feel a little rough at times. It's not something I pay much mind to, but I do notice it occasionally. Other bands of this style, that I have, seem a little more rounded or smoothed out. They feel a bit more comfortable in that regard. The band does fit the watch face perfectly. Installation was a breeze. I did not have to adjust the length of my band so I can't speak to how easy/hard that is. The locking clasp works fine. Again, you can see/feel the difference between this clasp and pricier versions of these bands, but it gets the job done.

All in all, this is a decent band that's well worth what it costs. I'd definitely recommend it to someone looking for a replacement band for this watch if they were trying to stay more budget conscious.

title: Great little watch...but...
review_text:
I love this watch but I do have some issues which usually sway me from wearing it all the time. When I first got it and saw the band style, I knew right off the bat I was probably going to have a couple issues. I was right. These bands (silicone maybe) typically cause my skin to get a rash. I'll wear it all the time, including in the shower, until the rash starts. Then I have to take it off for a few days. The bands do look replaceable but they don't say what other bands they're compatible with.

The other gripe I have with it is the accelerometer (I assume) being used to determine when you raise the watch to look at it. It's spotty at best. Often times I'll raise my wrist to look at the screen and it will not turn on. I will have to turn it on by the button. Other times it will be overly sensitive and turn on whenever it feels like it. Maybe it's just my device but I was really hoping that feature would work better. I like the idea of raising my wrist and the watch face turning on.

The app connectivity is nice and the tracking of all your stats is nice. The ability to customize what shows on the main screen as well as changing your watch faces is great as well. It really is a nice watch. If I can find a band that is better, I would wear this thing all the time but I get so irritated by the rash that develops. If you don't have that issue with silicone bands, then by all means, this is a great little watch.

title: Definitely not worth the price in my opinion...
review_text:
Maybe it's just the set I received, but on a few levels I can advise against these. For starters, the price.
I do not feel these are worth what they're charging. Although the filters look nice with the colorful trim, etc, that's about as far as I'd go with them. The case is okay. It's plastic and has a snap style latch to keep it closed. However, the filters just sit in foam. When I received mine and pulled them out of the box, all of the filters were out of their foam slots and just floating around in the case. After pushing them back into their foam spots, they seemed to hold in place. There's a lot more case than needed for the 6 filters so if you're trying to consolidate space, you may want to put them in something else.

The huge issue I have with all of them is how loose they fit the Mini 3 camera. Each one of mine can practically fall off. I'd understand if maybe one of them was super loose, but for all of them to behave the same it seems like a design flaw to me. I've used other brand filters that hold in place equal to that of the stock attachment but I'm afraid these are going to fall off too easily. Maybe not necessarily in flight since it's on a gimbal that accounts for turbulent air but I almost guarantee they'll fall off when fiddling around with the drone in your hands. A suggestion to the manufacturer would be to create a little more tension where they lock onto the camera like DJI and other brand filters do to prevent them from spinning back the very slight distance it takes for them to come off.

title: Works just fine for my E422VA Visio TV
review_text:
The keyboard on the back of this remote makes searching on Amazon, Netflix and Hulu so much easier - no more having to navigate that onscreen "keyboard".

I was hesitant to purchase this item since it was not clear from the product description or from the Vizio website that this remote would even work with my model TV, which came with the VR17 remote. But I decided I would take a chance, and return if it it did not work.

The front of the remote contains three quick-access buttons for Amazon, Netflix and Vudu, and then all of the same keys found on the VR17 in the same positions, with one minor exception. The XRV1TV 3D is designed for use with a 3D TV, which mine is not. Where the VR17 remote has the "WIDE" key in the lower left corner position, this remote has a "3D" key. But that is not an issue for me, since I rarely use that function, and it is available through an on-screen menu anyway.

The one thing that keeps me from giving this remote a 5-star rating is that I find the remote a little awkward to hold and use without accidentally pressing a key on the reverse side. It takes some getting used to having to hold this carefully to prevent that happening.

title: These are great
review_text:
I wanted a dual set because we have two backseat drivers that need distraction. Well, maybe they just need a better driver but in any case I needed a DVD player set. I decided on these based on the reviews and am thoroughly impressed.

There is a built in battery which has served us well given I didn’t realize that at first and while driving the DVD player stopped. I thought it was broke and then realized it had just not been plugged in properly. After reading through I was pleasantly surprised by this feature.

My kids like the ease of access and to be able to use the remote. I really like the lack of skipping that occurs while driving as a previously set we had would skip and then restart the disc. No issues in that regard here.

The audio is great though we have the kids wear headphones as usually we have a few different sounds happening (radio, wifes phone, older sons phone, and DVD player would just add to that). I did listen to it at first as I didn’t want to have the headphones given it’ll only be a few years before he wears them all the time (teen years are fun).

If there were a downside to these, it is something that happens to all DVD players in that when cold, the laser reader has to warm before it can read the disc. That happens with all players though so it’s more of a tip than anything.

Highly recommend

title: Great camera, cloud isn’t
review_text:
I liked the camera so much I bought the outdoor one as well.

This camera has motion detection that will follow the motion. It actually made my son nervous and thought someone was controlling it. I explained that it detects motion and follows that which is ideal should someone get inside the house.

The camera does have two way Audio that works well and only has a slight lag but is fairly clear.

I am able to monitor the cameras from the app but this is where the problem starts. The app is adjustable to some degree, the problem that I’ve explained to the manufacturer is they require each camera to have separate cloud storage at a separate fee per month. The cloud storage should be based on the account and total account cloud usage. This helps with better networking as well as retaining cloud activity in one central location. If the motion detection were capturing someone who did eventually make it inside, that sequence from camera to camera would be great if it all linked in one cloud account. The problem is that LongPlus has not done this and you pay separate fees per camera.

Not pleased but it is the only company I’ve seen that has an indoor camera and an outdoor camera (where the outdoor camera is battery powered).

title: Poor camera, poor cloud
review_text:
Update: arrived 4/16, installed after charging on 4/17. Died today on 5/3. Roughly 2.5 weeks of battery life.

I really enjoy the camera overall. It was easy to install the app using the QR code in the manual. Then following the manual to register the camera and have it read the QR code to register the camera to the account.

I wanted a camera brand that had both Indoor and Outdoor cameras but needed the outdoor camera to have a battery and found that in LongPlus.

There is a slight lag in the camera but the quality is solid.
The motion detection can be adjusted which is nice as it is fairly sensitive.

The big downside is regarding the future of the online world which is their cloud service. There is only a 7 day free trial, not 30 days (and nowhere to add a code to get the 30 days that is promised in the description). Outside of that, rather than having one cloud service payment per month, you pay for each camera. The cost saved appears to be made up with their cloud services costing money if you want a full network of cameras. Very disappointed by something so simple. There is no easy customer service portal for questions in the app, only app feedback (which I submitted but there should be an easy line of communication).

There are also many misspelled words within the app itself adding to the confusion and overall trust. I rarely have one star for my reviews but this is just really a simple fix on the LongPlus side.

title: So far so great
review_text:
We picked up this camera because we were getting a new puppy and needed to keep an eye on him during the day.

The clarity is pretty solid overall given the cost and can be seen in the photo above (which includes our little pup).

The camera can take snapshots which I am not able to save to my phone (or haven’t quite figured out how to save to my iPhone but they do save in the app).

I don’t really need this for motion detection but have tested that feature out as a just in case measure if we used in the future. The sensitivity can be adjusted but overall a very nice feature.

The camera does have a micro sd slot that would allow storage of footage (like movements) but we use the live footage as our means of checking the feed.

The connection to the device was fairly smooth but we did have to refresh our router when completing the process. It could’ve been a bandwidth issue given we have more Smart items than ever.

The app is fairly user friendly and my wife and I can both view the live feed at the same time. The feed itself is about .5 -1 second slow which we haven’t found as a problem.

The audio in/out is also quite clear which was fantastic. We try not to talk to our pup too much but it definitely was a nice feature for the first 2-3 days of him being in the crate (and being able to hear him as well as talk to him if he got frustrated).

Highly recommend this one!

title: Perfect!
review_text:
I am very pleased with this purchase and I wanted to write a review on things start to finish.
Packaging
-Fantastic overall look and also care in terms of making sure the watch face was protected and sitting in its' own section of the box. The bands were not attached but were easy to slip on (there's a small little nub on the band end that attaches to the watch, color side will face down). There is also a screen protector to peel off the watch face. The charger is magnetic and the charging process may have taken an hour (I just plugged into my computer).

Directions
-These were really fantastic. They lay things out in detail but also keep it brief for the many different options available. Turn on the bluetooth mode on your phone. I found the app "Da Fit App" from the product description, though the directions only show a QR code. From there it was opening the app and doing a quick profile setup (Sex, Height, Weight, Birth Year). It automatically scanned for the phone and the letters displayed on the screen and it was the only one shown so that was quick. I do wish it would pop up a notification that the pairing was successful but there is a watch icon in the app at the bottom. If you click that it displays "Connected" right at the top and shows your exact watch. It also let's you customize the "face" of the watch from within the app. I like Dial 3.

The App
-Very well laid out and some details were provided earlier but you can adjust the notifications you receive and it all pairs through Bluetooth so as long as they are on (and you accept push notifications on the phone) you'll receive the notifications on the phone. You can make a lot of the adjustments you want through the watch, but the app can allow for a faster level to set all at once.

The Modes

The mic comes with a pop filter screen as well as a wind screen filter which are nice additions for recording audio in any condition.

The mic can be sensitive with some light wind so if there is a breeze do not forget the wind screen filter.

I would definitely recommend this as a low cost alternative to the similar Rode mic.

title: Not disappointed
review_text:
I am not going to cover every feature in detail since other reviews have some an excellent job of that. My points of comparison are a Galaxy Tab S6 Lite 10.4-inch Android Tablet 128GB that I purchased in June 2021, and my first large format Galaxy, the Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro SM-T9000ZWAXAR 12.2-Inch Tablet that I purchased in June 2015.

This one is a major performance improvement over the most recent (June 2021) Galaxy, and better in all respects than the much older 12.2 Galaxy I purchased in June 2015.

I was totally pleased with the Tab S6, but missed the larger screen of the Tab Pro 12.2. This screen is significantly more vivid than the 12.2 Tab Pro, and the 256gb memory in this one pretty much assures that the performance is significantly better than either the 32GB Tab Pro or the 128GB Tab S6. But that is expected.

What I truly love about this tablet over the older large format one is the body is sturdy and not prone to bending. That is why my Tab Pro ultimately failed: the body was so thin that it flexed and at some point it started acting crazy. It would have cost more to repair it than to purchase the Tab S6. Prior to purchasing this one I made sure that that issue had been resolved. Yes, it's not as light, but it more than makes up for it in sheer speed, superior display, and even sound quality.

If you want or need a large format tablet that is reasonably priced and provides excellent battery life and performance this is worth considering.

title: Use it more than I thought I would
review_text:
I purchased a pair of these in September 2020 - one for me, and one for my wife - and am surprised by how much I have become dependent upon it. It reads from my google calendar two hours from a scheduled event, so that is one useful feature. If I cannot remember a fact or quickly need to look up something, all I have to do is ask. I also use it as a clock.

Except for the visual display of time and date, I could have accomplished everything I mentioned with my old hockey puck, A.K.A. "Dot." However, for some reason I did not use that one as much, so, perhaps the visual display catches my eye and reminds me that I have a fairly useful appliance that will do things for me. At any rate I use this a LOT more than I did the Dot.

The real user in the house if my wife. She is constantly interacting with her Echo, but she was the household power user when she was using a Dot as well. While I feel as though I have gotten my money's worth from mine, the truth is my wife's daily (hourly?) use of hers makes the pair we have in our own home work spaces a bargain.

Bottom line: cool device that has numerous uses - many of which I don't personally use. For some reason the screen inspires me to use mine a lot more than the screenless Dot, and honestly I rarely use the Echo visually.

title: Nice workhorse tablet
review_text:
I finally upgraded my circa 2018 Galaxy Tab A to this. The Tab A and this one represent lower tier Galaxy tablets, meaning that they were not the flagship models. This one does everything I want. That said, my needs are relatively simple: mostly web browsing, and streaming movies from Netflix and Prime. Things that I absolutely love:

- the old Tab A had 16GB and this has 128, a major increase in storage.
- screen quality is amazing. Streaming videos is noticeably better from a visual standpoint.
- in the same price range as the old Tab A, so when I upgraded I felt as though I was getting a much better tablet for about the same price as I paid for the old one in 2018.

While the battery life on this new tablet is much better, it longer than I thought it would to charge it. And, yes, I am using the included fast charger and cable. When I was transferring my data and apps from the old tablet the power consumption of WiFi, CPU and whatnot resulted in the charging rate crawling to a snail pace. It was as though it was consuming power at close to the same rate as it was being charged. In normal use, the charging is faster, but still not as fast as I guessed it would be using a fast charger. Not a real issue, but I thought I would mention it to set expectations.

As for the S-Pen, I am not currently using it. I am using an old fashion stylus in lieu of fingers to navigate (old habits die hard), and have not found a use for the S-Pen that requires its power and capabilities. It is certainly more than just a stylus, and is designed to integrate with some specific apps. I did watch a Youtube video explaining and demonstrating it, and it is impressive. But that is for a later time when I feel like experimenting and exploring.

Overall I love this tablet and am not only pleased with its features and capabilities, but am very happy with its modest price tag.

title: Cloning? This is probably not your best option
review_text:
I thought that I'd save a few bucks and grab this instead of the Crucial SSD in approximately the same size that was about ten bucks more. Unfortunately I did not read the full description and discovered that this does not come with cloning software or any software. The Crucial drive comes with cloning software that is easy to use and effective.

All is not lost, however. Although this is listed as an internal drive, the case is sturdy enough to use as an external drive without purchasing a separate enclosure. All you need is a SATA to USB cable and a spare USB port on your device, and you are good to go. I am using a StarTech cable that supports USB 3.0 and everything works like a charm.

For the price and the capacity this is a decent deal if you are looking for extra storage. If you are thinking about cloning, though, look elsewhere. Make sure that whichever brand that you get comes with bundled software. A number of other brands, including that one that I ultimately purchased for the cloned drive, come with OEM versions of an app called Acronis True Image. The bundled version will only work with the brand of SSD that it comes with, but for replicating a drive for safety, upgrading, etc. it works well.

Despite my dislikes I intend to purchase one more of these as both a spare and as a second light source for some shots that will benefit from the added illumination.

title: Needs some improvement, but is truly useful (especially for the price)
review_text:
I ordered a three pack because I wanted one for my music room, living room and one for my girlfriend. Set up was super simple for the basics - connecting to a bluetooth speaker, your calendar (I use google's calendar), and a music source. For the latter I use Pandora and that, too, was simple.

The subtracted star is because while I own a few thousand dollars worth of MP3 albums that I purchased from Amazon, I cannot access them. Apparently you can only stream music from Amazon's cloud if you have Prime, and even then I am not sure that you can access any of your own music that resides in their cloud. To me that is a fail, and an indication that the business and requirements analysts who assisted in the development of this device do not fully understand customer requirements at a very basic level. Another nit is the iHeart Radio music source that is plain confusing to use.

Some other areas where this would be a LOT more useful is to have the ability to set up more than one route for traffic (currently I can only identify a single route, home-to-work or back, whereas I am frequently traveling from one place to the other and traffic conditions for those trips would be very helpful. title: Easy to use in receiver mode - a little tricky in transmitter mode, but still solid
review_text:
I received mine as a free review sample. This is physically smaller than the photos lead you to believe (about 2.5x1 3/8 inches), but the switch and button, and charging port are easy to access and use. If I have a single wish it would be that the short 3.5mm cable were removable instead of fixed. That would allow you to not only use longer cables if you wanted, but also make it easy to replace that cable if it were to become damaged.

This is easy to use - there is a quick reference card in addition to an instruction sheet. I was able to have this up and running in receiver mode within minutes. Placing it in transmit mode took two tried, but that still took less than five minutes.

Mine will auto-reconnect as long as I do not connect to any other bluetooth receivers between uses with this one. Since I usually connect to a different receiver at home I need to manually reconnect to this one after using the other. However, if this is the last receiver to which I have connected, it will reconnect to my Note 4 phone when I power this on.

My main use is as a receiver going into the 3.5mm AUX port of a Fender Mustang Amp. In that capacity it works perfectly, especially when I stream a backing track into the amp via this receiver. I did test the transmitter mode to make sure it worked, but honestly do not use it.

Overall, this is as reliable as any of a half dozen bluetooth receivers that I own. It does not drop out or flutter even if I am separated by a wall, although it is sensitive to distances further than twenty meters AND a wall. The nice bonus is it can be placed in transmitter mode for enabling remote speakers, but for me it's the receiver mode that is going to be the primary use. In that respect it's rock solid.

title: Inexpensive solution for upgrading some older vehicles
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. Since Vince McLaren's exceptionally helpful review of August 21, 2016 covers what I also discovered, take the time to read his (and mark it helpful because he did an excellent job.)

It took me a few weeks to get around to writing this review because I needed to order an adapter for the 1998 Ford Explorer it was destined for, and also to have it professionally installed. The adapter I purchased is [[ASIN:B01ES32D7C Fits Ford Explorer 1998-2001 Double DIN Stereo Harness Radio Install Dash Kit]]. There are other kits by different brands for most vehicles. One of those will allow you to install (or have professionally installed) in older vehicles where this system will add some modern touches.

The reasons why I subtracted a star are the touchscreen is not as sensitive as I had hoped (not unusable, but frustrating sometimes), and the instructions are not that great. A professional will have no problem installing this unit, and there is a comprehensive wiring diagram in the product photos on this page. If you are planning to do the install yourself, refer to that photo to get an idea of the complexity of the job.

For me, the bluetooth capability and radio make this is great bargain in my opinion. I have a back-up camera that attaches to a license plate holder that adds that feature (you will need to provide your own camera, but they are inexpensive.) While this will display videos, you will need to load them via the TF card slot because this has no DVD (or CD) slot for that kind of media. Frankly, streaming music via bluetooth obviates the need for a CD (in my opinion), and I do not foresee myself ever needing to use any video player in the driver/front passenger compartment of a vehicle. If those are important to you, this is not the in-dash solution for you.

My overall impression is this is a good - and very inexpensive - solution for upgrading in-dash entertainment and hands free solutions in older vehicles. Before you plunk down your money, though, make sure that this will fit your vehicle, and that there is an adapter kit available for installing it in your vehicle's make, model and year.

title: Excellent use of storage space, great construction and innovative features (but one shortcoming)
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I docked it a star is the active tablet window needs improvement (and that could have been one of the stand-out features if properly designed.) Here is the problem: it's the perfect size for an iPad Air 2, but could not accommodate my Tab 2 10.1 inch tablet. It did hold my Samsung Tab Pro 8.4 (even in an Otterbox Defender case). The vinyl window wrinkles and also reduces sensitivity when you interact with your tablet.

If the active tablet window is unimportant to you, then the rest of this backpack is a winner. Pairing my phone to the bluetooth speakers was as simple as flipping a switch and scanning for it on my phone's settings. And the speakers are loud with better than expected sound quality. I was pleased with that - some thought went into the speakers.

The padding is more than ample for protecting electronics, and there are sufficient pockets for the geekiest geek. What I like, though, is the storage areas are not overly complex. I own a Booq bag that is a storage dream come true, but almost requires a photographic memory to remember were all of the pockets are. This one is designed much simpler, but still efficient and effective.

Construction (except for the active tablet window) is first rate. The tablet window is marred by a difficult zipper, whereas all of the other zippers on this bag are sturdier and smooth. The outer fabric seems tough (I have not had it long enough to make any claims beyond that), and all of the seams are reinforced, straight and tight.

It's very comfortable and can be adjusted to evenly distribute the weight of a fully loaded pack. Considering that the bag itself is somewhat heavy this is a major plus for me.

I do want to note one thing about the backup battery: it is rated at (and stores) the full 4000mAh. However, like all batteries using this one's technology it's only 70% efficient, so expect about 2800mAh of usable capacity. That is not a flaw in this bag, but a reality that I wanted to point out so your expectations are properly set.

Overall, this is a well made bag with some innovative features (battery back-up and bluetooth speakers). If the active tablet window is not an important feature it's definitely worth considering. This one will be replacing my Booq because the storage is there without the complexity.

title: Beautifully made from quality materials (and NO split leather or other shortcuts)
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. Frankly, this is probably the best crafted bag I have owned in the past twenty years (and I have one from Booq.) The reason for the high rating is the leather parts are the real thing. Too often these days you get split leather, which is a thin veneer of leather over polyurethane. Not the case here - the leather is not only the real thing, but is generously cut.

The construction is excellent in every respect. The canvas is high quality, all of the stitching and seams are straight and tight, and reinforcement points are heavy-duty. Moreover, the zippers are as heavy-duty as the other parts.

Unlike many bags (even high end ones) that have a chemical odor when you unpack them for the first time, this one does not. The lining is synthetic, which resists water (but I would not claim this to be waterproof.) The snaps, reinforcing rivets and other metal are designed to look like brass, but are probably steel since a magnet will stick to them.

The pockets and compartments make this an excellent work bag that can accommodate smaller laptops. I use mine for my [[ASIN:B00HWMPTI2 Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro SM-T9000ZWAXAR 12.2-Inch Tablet]], which is an easy fit. That leaves me room to spare for other odds and ends, as well as music charts. The main interior pocket is about 13 7/8 inches wide by 10 inches tall. If you are purchasing this for a laptop use those dimensions to determine if this bag will work for you.

Overall, I am not only pleased, but surprised by how well this is made and the quality of the materials. I want to emphasize that this may not fit many of the larger laptops on the market, but is still a great bag for books, tablets and assorted other gear. I hate gushing, but in this case I think the bag warrants it.

title: Inexpensive DAC that is easy to install and performs nicely
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. I actually had a need for one of these because I wanted to run an audio signal out of my Yamaha receiver to an older analog reel-to-reel recorder. The receiver had a toslink out, and the recorder had RCA in. This box was the perfect DAC.

title: A little noisy and not exactly a micro-sized projector, but versatile and a cheap way to get a big screen
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. I subtracted a star because in small quarters the fan can get irritating, and also the picture area is a little skewed. The latter is not enough to ruin a video, but combined with the fan noise I felt that this falls into the four star category. To be fair, this is about on par with other portable projectors in this price range and sharing the general form factor.

On the plus side, this is an inexpensive way to get a large screen TV (assuming that your wall is the screen), that does a credible job of projecting movies, TV and presentations. I tested it using a Chromecast and streaming video from YouTube to my phone, then casting from my phone to the Chromecast dongle connected to one of the HDMI ports in the rear. No issues and it was actually a treat. I also tested it with an old Roku in an HDMI port streaming a movie from Netflix. To be sure, neither experience compares to my HD TV screen and surround sound system, but this does not come close to the price tags of those. Bang for the buck this is excellent if you are in a budget.

Frankly, I did not test the other ports, but do want to point out that the 'SD' card port is really USB A that will take a flash drive or an SD card using an adapter. Actually, I think that is a plus as well because flash drives are cheap and a 32GB one can hold a respectable amount of movies, home videos or presentations.

Sound quality is not spectacular, but is definitely adequate. Overall, this is as good as any projector among the four that I have either owned or tested, and is better than some. It would easily be a five star projector if it had a quieter fan. If you can live with that you will probably love it.

title: Especially useful if you use 18650 batteries; fast charging and auto-detect works very well
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. I subtracted a star because it does not center AA batteries very well in the left slot for some reason, and I got a spark at the plug the first time I plugged this into an outlet. That did not recur after a few more tests, but once was enough to give me pause.

Up front, note that this WILL NOT work with alkaline rechargeable batteries and the instructions clearly state that. It definitely works with the batteries listed, and I am thrilled to have this charger for the growing pile of 18650 batteries that I have accumulated.

My testing was confined to Ni-MH AA and AAA, 18650, and a few battery backups I use for phones and tablets. I let this device auto-detect instead of attempting to manually set voltage and current, and it was spot on in every case. It is relatively fast charging (especially for the Ni-MH AA and AAA batteries), and aside from the spark mentioned above has proven to be reliable. My only direct comparison for recharging speed is for the AA and AAA batteries that charged up 25% faster with this unit than with the Knox charger I had been using for those. I have no baseline for the 18650 and backup batteries that I tested.

I did not test the protection features cited in the specs other than polarity because I did not have depleted or non-rechargeable batteries. I also did not receive the optional car charger adapter, so cannot discuss that. I will say that for the batteries that I did test this performed flawlessly.

A final note: the display is a bit confusing, and the instructions will put you to sleep. However, I highly recommend that you carefully go through the instructions because there are some important caveats and safety precautions of which you need to be aware. Overall, I am pleased with this charging solution and highly recommend it if you use any if the IMR type batteries and especially the 18650 size.

title: Surprisingly good phones at an entry level price - not  optimum for all styles of music though
review_text:
I received these as a free review sample. They are one of three different models of Spider phone that I have tested, and these are the loudest and deepest from a low frequency perspective (to my ears) among the three.

Like another reviewer, I noticed that the right and left channels are inverted, but that is not a problem for me. The sound quality is very good across the high, medium and low frequency bands. These are compressed at the high end, with a definite bias in the mid and low frequency ranges. The mids are very realistic, while the low end is a bit on the processed side if you are listening to acoustic jazz, or similar styles of music. For modern music they are perfect. Factor that into your purchase decision.

I do need to mention that these can get a little on the loud side, especially if you are listening from a device that automatically attenuates SPL levels on phones and you opt to override that setting. For example, my Note 4 phone will attenuate direct AUX connections, but I can override that and listen full volume. These phones can actually damage hearing if you do that and listen at max for prolonged periods of time. For me the attenuated setting is still plenty loud.

Overall sound quality and level is perfect for modern music, especially genres that are bass and drum centric. For acoustic music (jazz, Americana, older country and the such), these are a little too processed. For those styles I recommend that you consider the [[ASIN:B01BY0262O Spider USA SPEB112-BK Jade Series Metal Earbuds]].

title: Decent, but not the best - there are some caveats
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I subtracted a star is the grabbing arms are not spring loaded. Indeed, they are a friction, pinion design that makes it a little more difficult to insert and remove your phone while the assembly is attached to your windshield or dash.

Also, before you make a final decision, make sure your phone will fit. The maximum width is 3.5 inches, and that measurement is absolute. My Note 4 would fit when I removed it from its case, but with two of the cases that I swap it between, it would not fit. Take that into account.

This will definitely stay where you attach it! It even adhered to the pebble grain covering on my vehicle's dash, but it was a but too awkward there for me. It is perfect on the windshield, though and that is its final resting place for me.

It's also rock steady, so if you are on bumpy roads the display is not apt to jiggle, which is a nice thing of you are glancing at your phone's GPS map (something I do often.) Basically, this is a decent mount, but not the best (in my opinion.) On the other hand, it's definitely not the worst either!

title: Entry level price; upper intermediate level performance - worth checking out
review_text:
I received these as a free review sample. Note: these are NOT bluetooth. They are wired ear buds that should fit any device with a 3.5mm output jack.

My rating is based on both sound quality and price. The list on these are in the twenty buck range, but the sound quality, in a blindfold test, would fool you into thinking that these are a tier above other buds in this price range.

The mid range and lower end of the frequency spectrum seem to be emphasized, with highs a bit compressed. These are perfect for casual (and even some critical) listening. An audiophile would probably not like the bias and compression, but most other folks will appreciate it. I mentioned the 'lower' end of the frequency spectrum. At the lowest end it is deep, but not thumping (although it will reproduce 20Hz, which you can feel if not hear.) For anyone listening to acoustic or lightly amplified music, and especially music that uses a big chunk of the audio frequency spectrum (for consumer phones), these are surprisingly good.

There is a disparity between the product description's claim that there have flat, tangle-free cable and the actual cable, which is tangle-free, but round. I want to point that out because one of the things I check when reviewing is any differences between product specs and claims, and what you actually receive.

Basically, these are priced at the upper end of entry level phones, but are good enough to pass for high end intermediate level phones.

title: Convenient and perfect for up to 60 Watt devices
review_text:
I purchased one of these from a different source to power a 12V portable fridge that was designed to operate from a lighter socket. This converter puts out a full five Amps, which is 60 Watts (5 Amps x 12 volts.)

In addition, this will easily charge tablets and phones if you use a multi-port USB vehicle charger with it. In fact, any 12V DC device like an air pump, etc., that is designed to operate from a vehicle lighter socket is fair game as long as it does not require more than 5 Amps or is rated at 60 Watts or less (and to be on the safe side I would probably lower that to 50 Watts.)

This runs fairly cool as long as you are not operating it at the edge of its capacity or for sustained periods, and mine has never gotten so hot that it alarmed me.

title: Light duty, and good for hanging banners indoors - not for outside use
review_text:
I purchased this to hand a band banner behind us on stage. In that respect this is perfect because the dimensions are totally as described in the product description, the product photo is accurate, and I knew up front that this was going to be a lightweight support.

There are some limitations. The first is although you can extend the tripod legs to provide decent stability, this is not for environments where passers by can bump into it. Also, with a banner or backdrop clipped to it, it is not going to work well outdoors unless there is zero breeze. It would not take much to catch a light breeze in the 'sail' area of a backdrop or banner and topple this. However, for me this is a major plus because it's light and easy to carry. If you are a musician you already know the advantage.

The cross-member sections are about an inch in diameter, so you will need large clips. The bag was a surprise. I was expecting some cheap, vinyl bag that was an afterthought. While the bag is lightweight, it is designed specifically with pockets for the two stands and the four cross-member sections.

Assembly and disassembly are fast and easy. I marked the posts with small pieces of tape so I could quickly level it after I initially got it to the correct height and leveled it. I recommend that you do the same because the first time it takes patience and a bubble level (or tape measure) to get it set up correctly.

title: Truly useful and if you are a musician who uses pedal boards, this is very handy
review_text:
If you are a musician who deals with pedals and pedal boards, or has other gear that uses DC power within the range of this power supply, this can be a life saver. Since I own pedal boards that use both 9V DC (Boss and a few other guitar effects pedals), and 12V DC (TC Helicon), this is a spare that sits in my gig bag in case I misplace or damage one of the wall warts that powers those pedals.

Also, because this can put out up to 1.2 Amps, it can power three of my TC Helicon pedals off of a power cable chain. I usually employ a TC Helicon power supply for that, but since I use this one as a spare, it is always ready if needed. I have tested it with the pedals and verified that it will power all of the ones I use simultaneously.

If you do get this and find that the adapters that come with it are not the sizes you need, you may want to consider this add on set by another brand: [[ASIN:B00CMMO6AE Generic Universal 28 DC Power 5.5x2.1mm Jack to 28 Plug Power Adapter for Notebook]]. For my needs, though, this is all I require and I am very pleased with it.

title: Excellent cable at a bargain price, but read on if you are using it on a crowded pedal board
review_text:
I purchased this cable based on my very positive experience with some other cables that I ordered from this brand ([[ASIN:B003L18XKE Monoprice 104749 1.5-Feet Premier Series XLR Male to XLR Female 16AWG Cable]].)

Like the XLR cables, this one is slightly different in size that what is described. Overall length is 18.5 inches and the cable that is approximately 17 7/8 inches when measured from the housing of the connectors. For me that is not a real issue, but what may be an issue of you are planning to use these with pedals mounted on a pedal board, the length from the strain reliefs to the top of the connector housings is 2 inches. Also, the TRS end's tip to the top of the housing is 2.25 inches, with 5/8" of the housing protruding when the TRS end is fully inserted. Those numbers should help you to determine if this will work in your particular pedal board.

The cable is noise free in my application, which is interconnecting a [[ASIN:B00HMQ1G9O TC Helicon VoiceTone Correct XT Vocal Effects Processor]] to a [[ASIN:B00HMQ1SHO TC Helicon VoiceTone H1 Vocal Effects Processor]]. I did notice that the housing ends are split, two piece design that are held together by the strain reliefs. Also, at the end of the strain relief, the bend radius of the 16AWG cable is very tight, which was a pleasant surprise.

Bottom line: the only potential issue I see with this cable the it may not work well on a pedal board with tightly spaced pedals. In all other respects it has proven to be mechanically and electrically sound, and I intend to order more.

title: One of the easiest-to-use and install dashcams I have come across
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. M.Erb's extremely detailed and helpful video review of May 14, 2016 covers this in a great deal of depth. I'll add my thoughts and reasons why I also rated this five solid stars.

First, I have tested and used at least a dozen dashcams, many of which were excellent in their own right. However, the shortfall in each was the screen and a complicated array of controls. With this one your screen is your smartphone or tablet, and your controls are those that are provided with the app you need to download (for free) to control the camera and settings. There is a separate remote control, which is really just a clicker that does one thing: triggers a short video and a snapshot.

Another thing I personally love is the mounting kit. This one, properly used, will run your power cable in an unobtrisive manner (well, as unobtrusive as possible), and the cable is sufficiently long to run the cable from close to my rear view mirror to my dashboard lighter socket in my 2016 Outlander. Other dashcams either forced you to put up with dangling cable or - in one case - have the power and video feed cables professionally installed. Plus this uses a standard USB cable with USB A on one end and micro USB on the other. Some dashcams require a proprietary cable with a barrel connector that makes it difficult to replace if necessary.

Video quality is not award winning (indeed, the camera lens is a fisheye), but is still more than sufficient to capture accidents and even scenic drives. You can also use this for other than a dashcam. I discovered that will fit in a standard microphone clip that fits a Shure SM58 (i.e., a very common size.)

You can use up to a 64GB micro SD card, which will store almost eleven hours of video. Most dashcams are limited to 32GB. The instruction manual is adequate, but not comprehensive, and it also does not cover the software and its capabilities. I hope the company rectifies that, which will make this dashcam even more user friendly, especially for novices. However, most folks do not want to wade through a manual anyway, and the one that comes with this will get you going.

Bottom line: as far as dashcams go, this one is probably the easiest one to use that I have come across. My FAVORITE feature is simplicity that allows my phone or tablet to be the screen and controls.

title: Decent construction and great for my Tab 3 10.1 tablet
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. It nicely accommodates my Tab 3 10.1 tablet, but is just a bit too small for my Tab Pro 12.2.

Up front, there is a chemical odor that lingers for about a day, but it dissipates afterwards. You can hasten the removal of the odor by wrapping a teaspoon of baking soda in a washcloth, securing it with a rubber band and leaving it in the case (opened) for an hour.

This is somewhat spongy feeling, and affords a little protection against falls. Frankly, it is not going to protect a tablet against a waist high fall on an irregular, hard surface unless the tablet is in a ruggedized case. On the other hand, it was not designed for that, so I am not docking it any stars. It's as good as any other case that I own.

Other things I like are the sturdy, dual zippers, and the bottom reinforcement. I would have loved a handle, but this is a portfolio style case, so I am still very pleased.

title: Decent as an external USB storage device, but read critical reviews carefully if you plan to use it as a boot drive
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. Since there are reviews that cite premature failures I waited a full month before writing a review. In the ensuing time I have been using this as backup storage on two laptops - one running Win7 and the other running XP. I have had zero failures, although this is not the speediest SSD I own (which accounts for the subtracted star).

Over the course of any given day this drive is used about thirty minutes to backup Outlook files and any new documents that I may have created or edited. When I first initialized it the usable storage was around 111GB, so be aware that there is some overhead if you are expecting the full 120GB. This is NOT uncommon so I did not ding it another star for that.

Mine is housed in a [[ASIN:B00K6I9NL8 Patriot Gauntlet 3 SATA III 6 Gb/s USB 3.0 Compatible Hard Disk Drive Enclosure]], which is suitable for my uses and not a bad enclosure if you are planning to use this drive the same way I am. If you are planning to make this a primary boot drive I recommend that you carefully read some of the critical reviews and take them into consideration because there are reported latency issues that make make it untenable in that role. For an external USB storage device, however, this one has been performing for me reliably and I would not hesitate to get another if I need more space.

title: Easy to use, but some caveats
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. I'll get the reason for subtracting a star out of the way first: (1) once you place a drive in the case bed removing it is difficult. (2) It runs a little hot. I had the circuit board exposed while initializing a 120GB SATA drive and by the time it was done the printed circuit board was hot. Not enough to cause blistering, but still hot to the touch.

If you plan to install a drive permanently this is not a bad case. It easily slides together (after a little finagling to get the drive in and lined up), and the USB 3 connector is a big plus. The drive that I installed was not the fastest on the market, but this enclosure and associated electronics got good results when I transferred a 5 GB set of MP3 files from my laptop to the external drive it housed.

This comes complete with screws (too many, in fact and the only ones that work are the black ones), and a screw driver. The cover precisely lines up with the bed that houses the drive, and the USB 3 cable that is included is decent.

I've been using this for a month with no issues, and have to admit that despite my complaints above it is an easy way to transform a SATA drive into an external USB storage device.

title: Functional hands-free solution for vehicles with 3.5mm ports in their stereo, but some limitations
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I subtracted a star is the cables (both the one from the charger to the control module, and the 3.5mm connection) are hardwired. This means that if either cable becomes damaged it can cost more to repair than to replace, unless you have the skills to repair them. Had the charger been configured with a micro USB port and the control module with a 3.5mm port for separate cables that can be easily purchased just about anywhere (including pharmacies and supermarkets these days), a damaged cable would be an easy swap and the value and utility of this solution been a lot more.

Operationally, this kit functions as promised. The mic will pass through commands if your phone has voice recognition, and the overall quality of sound is more a function of your vehicle's stereo system than this unit. Since my vehicle is already bluetooth-enabled I used a small, powered speaker with a 3.5mm input to test this. Since the cable, as mentioned, is fixed I had to still perform the test in my vehicle. The sound quality was overall good, and making and receiving test calls were easy and the connections clear enough to be heard without 'can you hear me now?'

Surprisingly the extra USB port in the charger was relatively fast, and proved to be as good as any high-speed (but non QC) charger on both my Note 4 and a friend's iPhone 5S. In fact, that is why I only subtracted one star because while the cable issue does detract, the charging capability of the extra port is better than I expected.

Bottom line: this is an OK hand's free solution for older vehicles that have an AUX port, but no bluetooth (and you NEED an AUX port to make this work.) Since the control module is hardwired into a lighter-style charger you cannot use this with a home stereo that does not have bluetooth, but does have 3.5mm input. There are similar solutions that use basically the same design, but replaceable cables that do allow this, so this one is restricted to vehicle-only use. If that is all you need, this one does perform as claimed.
