title: For folks with USB C devices. Reliable file system and decent performance
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. The reason for five stars is the design, which is convenient for folks who own USB Type C devices.

My acid test is to overfill a drive. On a poorly made thumb drive once the file is at capacity the files will become corrupted and are impossible to remove. In essence, the drive is useless. This one passed that test with no problems. I did not test the transfer rate because the only port I had open on my Thinkpad T61 was an ancient USB 1.1. It was slow (as expected), but the transfer was steady and error-free.

If there is a flaw, it's the loop for attaching this to a key ring is too small for one. Not a show stopper for me since I normally do not keep a thumb drive on my key ring, but if you do, this is NOT going to fit (and that I know of.)

This is definitely for folks who are now using USB C. I would have loved it even more had it come with a piggy back adapter on the C side for a USB micro adapter as well. Perhaps the next version will, but since USB C seems to be the coming thing, perhaps my personal wish is not practical in the long term.

title: Good entry-level speaker - OK sound quality and very LOUD
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. I subtracted a star because the sound quality of calls using the hands-free function is a little tinny, That is curious because when streaming music the sound quality if more than adequate.

What distinguishes this speaker - for me - are two things: (1) it's loud, and (2) the controls contain separate volume and skip buttons. Especially the latter because on speakers that combine those buttons I am forever skipping a track when I really wanted to increase or decrease volume. Not so on this speaker.

Some reviewers complained about hiss; I did not experience that at any volume level, even when the speaker was on, but not connected to my phone. Other complained about a loud announcement letting you know power on, pairing and the such. Yes, that is true. And you cannot change it or turn it off (that I know of). For me it is not a problem, but if stuff like that irritates you then you should be looking at different speakers instead of this one.

Sound quality is decent for a small speaker. The high frequency is stable and does not break up or get tinny at max volume. There may be a little compression, which most people like. I prefer truer reproduction. The mids are rich and I suspect that they are purposely biased to emphasize that frequency band. It definitely enhances casual listening, but if you are accustomed to true fidelity it may drive you nuts. The bass is not especially boomy. It's more than adequate if you listen to acoustic music and other genres, but for bass-centric music it's a little weak.

Volume is a surprise. This is a small speaker, but puts out a lot of sound. You can easily hear it from five to eight meters away when you have the volume cranked. Do be aware that you will more than cut play time in half if you max out the volume while on batteries. Still, you will get close to eight hours of play. The volume will cut through ambient noise, though, so this is ideal at the beach.

Bottom line: I view this as an entry-level speaker that is priced accordingly, but has some nice features compared to others in its range. Can you find a better speaker for the price? Possibly, although you will have to dig through a lot of product pages. Is this a safe choice? In my opinion, yes, as long as you can live with some of the issues that I mentioned.

review_text:

That means I have to eat some recent words along the lines of there is no bluetooth speaker that is truly audiophile quality. This speaker disproves that.

Out of the box this quickly pairs and connects to bluetooth devices. I tested mine with a Note 4 phone and it took literally seconds to have it up and running. I was so blown away by the fact that this speaker reproduces music in a neutral manner by default that I was ready to sit down and give it a glowing review. Then I downloaded and installed the app.

Some how, some way it finally found the speaker, then was totally confusing when it came to setting up my personal profile (speaker location, bias and other features.) title: Almost perfect (and works as a music stand light)
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. It is close to being perfect, but there is one thing that prevented me from awarding it five stars: the power cable is hardwired into the lamp. It's basically a standard USB cable that should have been a standard USB micro or USB C style, but is instead unremovable from the lamp. That means that if you damage the cable instead of replacing it with a readily available USB cable the repair cost is probably greater than replacing the entire lamp - unless you are handy at such things.

Aside from the cable, I love this lamp. For one thing the clamp will firmly hold the entire lamp in place on a music stand's thin, metal shelf. Plus the gooseneck, while flexible,holds the lamp where you place it. I have similar lamp that will move position if you bump it, so for me this one is vastly better than most.

I do love the fact that I can power this from a wall using the included charging adapter or from a battery such as a [[ASIN:B014O2AXB0 Kikicom Power Bank]] (or similar model). Also you can actually power it from a laptop's USB port, which makes it perfect for small study desks. The included charger has a 1 Amp port for powering the lamp and a port marked 2.1 Amps for charging phones and tablets. To be honest, the 2.1 port is not especially fast and I suspect outputs less than the labeled capacity, but it still can keep up with my tablet.

Bottom line: if you area musician this is possibly the best music stand lamp in its price range (and it is not described as a music stand lamp!) For reading and even small room lighting it is also excellent. It would be an easy five stars had the cable been standard.

title: Excellent entry level tablet with Samsung's features and performance
review_text:
I purchased this specifically because I needed a knock around tablet that was more compact than my Tab Pro 12.2. I was looking more for basic web access, calendar and email on the go, so power and storage were not principal considerations. Also, as an FYI, mine was refurbished and provided by Direct Distributor, and since sellers vary I want to cite my experience with the specific one from which I purchased this.

As a basic tablet this is excellent. It has the Samsung user interface to which I have grown accustomed, and even though this is an older tablet with little storage it was still pretty snappy for browsing the web and other common tasks. I also love the display. Despite the lower resolution than most tablets in 2016, it's still vivid and easy on the eyes. I thought 7 inches would be hard to read (after using a 12.2 inch tablet), but it isn't. I did increase the memory with a 32GB SD card I had laying around (a [[ASIN:B010Q57T02 SanDisk Ultra 32GB microSDHC UHS-I Card]].)

This arrived at 90% battery charge, so I was able to use it immediately. The initial set up screens take about ten minutes. An original Samsung charger and charging cable was bundled with it. Aside from the SD card the only other accessory I bought was a [[ASIN:B013XZXIXE Tab 4 Case, Galaxy Tab 4 7.0-inch case, OMIU(TM)3-Piece In 1 (Black+Purple) Durable Silicone Plastic Combo Shockproof Case]], which was less than fifteen bucks and almost as good as a more expensive OtterBox Defender. So total cost of this tablet, extra memory and a decent case was less than 150 bucks! Bottom line: I am thrilled with this tablet - for what it is and what I paid - and have recommended it to friends who are considering a tablet, but are not sure. The performance and features, combined with the low price of a refurbished unit make it a relatively safe, entry level purchase.

title: Not for road warriors, but is one of the few projectors I have tried that works in a range of lighting conditions
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. Since there are ample specs and two very detailed reviews before this one I am going to stick to some observations and why I rated it so highly. First, though, if you are looking for a portable projector for a road warrior who needs to travel light this is NOT it. It's light enough, but bulky. As a home or office projector, though, this one has a lot going for it.

The main reason why I rated this so highly is it works in rooms with some ambient light. I tested it in normal lighting conditions in my living room with typical morning light with open drapes and sunlight behind partially closed blinds. I could read a newspaper in that light, so was surprised and pleased that the picture quality of a video I was displaying through it was adequate. What I mean is I could see all of the details in the video, but, of course it would have been sharper and more vivid in lower light or even a dark room. I also own a high end business projector that would not display any discernible picture in the same lighting conditions.

What I did not care for is the fact that I needed to included remote controller to access all of the features. Since this is a home and office projector I can live with that. On the other hand, unlike another reviewer's experience that this did not default back to the last input setting, mine did. Consistently.

Another reason why I rated this so highly is the array of inputs - you have two HDMI ports, two USB, a VGA and AV connectors (the latter employ RCA jacks). I tested this from an old Lenovo T61 laptop via its VGA connector as well as using a Samsung Tab Pro 8.4 using an [[ASIN:B00K76A732 Addao® 5 in 1 Multifunction MHL Micro USB MHL To HDMI HDTV Adapter Connection Kit]].

Bottom line: this is an inexpensive way to get a wide screen TV for streaming movies from the web. It's also perfect as a fixed projected in corporate settings. It comes with all of the cables you need, a terse - but useful - user guide and a lens cover.

title: Outstanding protection, although bulky and heavy
review_text:
I purchased this solely because of how happy I am with the [[ASIN:B00NF4SXSO OtterBox Samsung Galaxy Note 4 Case Defender Series]] that I have been using for the past five months. That case has saved my Note 4 twice from falls, so I did not hesitate to purchase this along with my Tab Pro 8.4.

This case WILL add a lot of bulk and weight to your tablet, so if you are looking for sleek, this is NOT the case you want. For me I wanted the assurance that my tablet would be protected and this is the only case that I have found that will do that. The way the rim around the screen is beveled and how it recesses the screen is a nice level of protection. I am guessing that the included screen protector is effective, since I did not use the included one with my Note 4 case (I opted for the Zagg for that phone, but I am using the protector that came with this case and it does allow complete sensitivity. Time will tell.

Installation is straightforward and easy. I had mine completely installed in about five minutes. Of course I had prior experience with the Note 4 case, and there was a learning curve because the instructions are a little terse. All of the cutouts are also precise. The case does not hamper access to any feature or interfere with the camera. Ports have tabs that seal them against water and dust. Frankly I do not need that level or protection and actually cut off the tab protecting the charging port. However, if you work in harsh environments those are nice features. Also, I do not use the back cover that has the kickstand for propping the tablet up. Mine spends most of its time on a music stand, but if I were to use it outdoors or in harsh environments, the back cover is an additional layer of protection.

Bottom line: if you want protection this is a great case. If you want slim and trendy you will probably not like it, though.

title: Almost five stars, but not quite - it's still a decent light and a bargain
review_text:
I received this is a free review sample. For the price this is a bargain, but there are two things that kept me from giving it five stars. First is this does not use a standard micro USB style cable for charging. That means that unless you can find an easy source of cables with USB A on one end and the barrel connector this one has on the other, you are stuck with a three foot limitation of cable length. I have USB micro cables that are double that, and would have made this light all the more useful. Also, since I am using this as a music stand light if I misplace it for a gig I am out of luck because I do not own a similar charging cable (although I always have spare USB micro cables in my gig bag.) If you intend to use this as a fixed table lamp the cable issue will not be the problem for you that it is for me.

Second, the gooseneck is sensitive. If I bump a music stand with this light clamped to the shelf it will move far out of place. It's not stiff enough to hold if you do plan to use it with a music stand. For tables, bed stands, etc. it should work fine, though.

Here are some of the strengths: the lowest setting of illumination is perfect for stage use or if you want to read in bed without waking your partner up. At the highest setting it is definitely bright when lose in (about 1.5 meters), and - as Goldilocks said - the medium setting is just right.

Another feature is untethered to the charger this will operate for three hours at the brightest setting and half more than double that at the lowest. That means that if you are camping, on stage (or in front of a lectern) without a power source nearby you can still use it.

Finally, the included wall wart has a 2 Amp port for phones and tablets, as well as a 500mA port for charging this light. That is handy and all the more reason why the cable style for this lamp is a frustration - it could have easily been a five star product, and especially at the going price.

title: High quality and versatile
review_text:
I purchased these based on the shorter [[ASIN:B00FC4Z842 Hosa HSS-010X2 Pro Dual Cable]] set that came bundled with a keyboard that I purchased.

If you do decide to keep them as are I highly recommend that you tape the places where the pairs split because they are very easy to peel back and separate.

Basically, if you want a high quality set of interconnect cables for stereo that take 1/4 inch connections these are well worth considering.

title: High grade optics and constuction - professional quality lens
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. It it intended to be used with the [[ASIN:B018JVE7PU 001 | bitplay SNAP! PRO iPhone Case for iPhone 6/6S]], and like that kit, this is a professional quality lens. However, this will work with any camera or adapter that has 13mm threads.

Before you purchase you need to know that this lens has a polarizer than can be rotated to reduce reflections and/or enhance color. The caveat it this lens will NOT work properly if you have your camera's flash active.

The lens itself is high grade optical glass with no distortions that I could detect. If you are accustomed to pro quality optical gear you will appreciate this lens. On the other hand, if you are a point-and-shoot type who is content with clip on lenses or the basic video capabilities of your iPhone this is probably overkill. I am not trying to discourage anyone from purchasing this, but I do want to point out that this is a lens for pros or serious hobbyists, and, moreover, will require either the aforementioned kit or an adapter for the 13mm threads for either an iPhone or a camera that has that lens mounting size.

Bottom line: this is constructed with the same quality as lenses used with my vintage Nikon SLR (although different form factor) and intended for high-end users. I did some test shots and it has zero distortion and can be adjusted to control some reflections and color saturation. If you are serious about photography this one merits serious consideration.

title: Well designed and pro-level construction and features for transforming an iPhone 6 into a camera
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. When I accepted this for testing and review I was a little skeptical. However, this has turned out to be a high-quality kit that will transform an iPhone 6 or 6s into a decent hand held camera, yet it will not interfere with other iPhone functions. With the case and attachments in place you can still make and receive calls, text, browse the web, etc.

This is actually the foundation for a more sophisticated set of lenses that will accept add-on lenses like the [[ASIN:B018TQUEYI 010 | bitplay Portable Add-on 3X Telephoto Glass Lens Compatible]]. As you can see from the product description this kit already comes with a basic wide angle/telephoto lens combination. It is not plastic junk, but a serious lens with a precision metal body that screws into this case. It has two parts - one lens screws into the other for combined or separate effects - and it is as good in quality and construction as the lenses that I used with a vintage Nikon SLR.

The case itself can be quickly removed to reconfigure your phone back into a ... phone. But while it is in camera configuration mode it feels just like a hand-held with a choice of grips, an integrated tripod adapter and even a leather strap. The case does not interfere with any phone function, and especially the iPhone's camera and flash. More importantly - for me - the case offers excellent protection. The lip that is slightly raised about the iPhone's screen is curved inward and adds protection for that critical area. The body of the case and two of the grips are textured so you can maintain a firm hold on the phone while shooting, even if your hands are wet.

Bottom line: this is not a gimmick or novelty - it is designed for folks who take photography seriously. I could not find a single flaw in the design from a photographer's perspective; nor could I find any faults from a build or design perspective. This is obviously not for casual users, but if photography is your passion and you own an iPhone 6 or 6s, this case merits serious consideration.

title: Works perfectly in my Note 4
review_text:
I purchased this because I had run out of space on my old [[ASIN:B00AK31M3G Samsung micro SDXC UHS-1 Card PRO 64GB Class 10 for Galaxy Note 2 II]]. That card had followed me from a Note II to a Note 3 to my current Note 4. I was a little concerned about compatibility and reliability because a few years ago tried to save a buck by getting a tier 2 brand card that literally melted down.

This time I took a chance with this non-Samsung card and cannot be more pleased. For one thing, the transfer from my old card to this one did not cause this to get hot. Considering that there was about 29GB involved that was my first indication that this is a well made card.

Another thing is after I transferred the contents to this card (via a card reader), as soon as I popped it into my Note 4, it immediately mounted and everything on the older card was there. I took the time to look for corrupted files, sampled a lot of random music, and checked a few videos. Zero issues and the Note 4 did not balk at this card or any of the files on it.

As for speed, I am not going to make claims one way or the other. I did not test it with benchmarking software, and since I use this mainly for streaming music the additional speed (if any) is not noticeable anyway. What is noticeable is the total compatibility with my Note 4 and the extra breathing room the capacity provides me.

Overall I am not only pleased, I feel as though this card is a better value than the Samsung brand cards that I had been purchasing. And every bit as reliable too.

title: Simple and effective, but documentation needs improving
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. Up front, the reason for only four stars is the documentation is too scant and that can be a problem.

When I received this I asked a friend to download the app to her iPad Air 2 (running iOS 8.3) and connect to the device. She claimed it would hang. I borrowed the iPad and was able to easily connect and set up a specific room for monitoring. Same app and same hardware, but because the documentation was so terse and the app itself a bit confusing I concluded that this can be frustrating to some folks.

You can set this up for different rooms and once you get the hang of the app's user interface that process is simple. Do note that you need to leave the sensor in a specific location for at least a week so that it can monitor and establish a trend.

For my home the main measurement and trend I am interested in is indoor air quality because of the pollens that manage to creep inside. I received this after our major pollen season in Central Florida, but the display shows at a glance some small spikes that I will investigate (checking weather stripping, and door and window seals.

Bottom line: this is easily a five star device if the documentation is rewritten to show even novice users step-by-step how to connect and get it running. In my personal opinion the installation and configuration screens should be redone too because it seems as though the software designers were more interested in a cool, modern look than whether or not less experienced users would catch the visual cues. If this were for geeks I'd give it a pass, but it's designed for a wider audience and can frustrate folks who just want to get it up and running, and monitor air quality, temperature and humidity.

title: Works nicely if properly applied
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. Mine has been affixed to the back of my vehicle for nearly a month, and has even weathered a storm and a few hot days.

If you properly prepare the surface of where you intend to affix this sticker it will stay put. The reason why I docked it a star is because there were no instructions other than a terse three step blurb on the package. Frankly, that did not go far enough.

A good rubdown with alcohol or even Windex, followed by a thorough drying with a lint free cloth works wonders. Also, do not affix it in the hot sun, and also let it sit in the shade or garage for at least eight hours before driving. I did mine in the early evening and by morning it was firmly in place.

One nice thing about this, aside from the decorative aspect, is it's highly reflective. Since there is not much continuous surface in the design, it is not going to reflect back to a driver behind you and blind him or her, but there more than enough reflection to be easily seen on a dark night.

title: Decent basic protection and a value in this price range
review_text:
I purchased this to compare to another case that I own - the [[ASIN:B00V6I7NBE TOUGH Cardioid Condenser Microphone Hard Case with Dense Foam for Audio-Technica AT2020 / AT2020USB / ATR2500-USB / AT2035 Studio and USB Microphones]]. I am using that case to house a [[ASIN:B00DYD77WY Samson Concert 88 Handheld 16-Channel True Diversity UHF Wireless System]], and it was a tight fit. This one will hold my second Concert 88 system, and it does so with a lot more room and flexibility.

This case is significantly better than the Tough case. For one thing the diced foam is easy to remove. I had to use a box cutter on the foam in the other case because it was not completely cut through. For another, the three bottom layers of foam (described in the product description) make it more convenient to work with, as well as the extra depth and overall inside dimensions of this case. Bear in mind that this and the case to which I am comparing it are the same price.

I do wish there were more dividers included, and also that the long dividers would go across the entire width. However, for my purposes what came with this case is more than sufficient.

One final point of comparison - I believe that in the long run the Tough box will outlast this one because of design and materials. That one is all plastic, while this one is a combination of materials that over time are going to break if roughly handled. That said, I prefer this case and will probably order a few more for some other microphones that I own.

title: A little complex, but excellent protection
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. I am not using it for drones, but to house a [[ASIN:B00378GEAM BEHRINGER EUROLIVE B205D]] along with some mics, DI boxes, a tablet and miscellaneous cables.

From a protection perspective I truly trust this backpack. It's well padded and the convex form factor combine to provide excellent protection for the electronics I carry. I do want to point out that if you use it as a carrying case instead of as a backpack the tablet compartment is not as protected. On the other hand, using it as a backpack will protect any tablet, even ones without their own covers and cases. Plus that particular compartment is more than large enough to accommodate my [[ASIN:B00HWMPTI2 Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2]].

The complexity comes in with the myriad of clasps, pockets and system of dividers. It actually takes a good hour to become thoroughly familiar with the pockets and other features. The dividers are versatile enough to be reconfigured to accommodate smaller (or larger) items. I am not using all of the dividers since I am storing a fairly large speaker, but the dividers from the set that I am using allow me to separate and organize the peripherals and cables that I mentioned above. One nice thing about the dividers is that they, too, are heavily padded and well constructed.

Overall construction is excellent. The zippers are smooth and come with convenient pull tabs. The material is water resistant and will take a lot of abuse. Also, the straps are nicely padded and are not going to fray or wear out even if you are rough with this backpack.

Bottom line: this is perfect protection for more than drones. For the equipment I am using it for this is a little on the expensive side. However, since I am using the gear in live performances I feel that the assurance that the equipment will be operational when I need it to be. That makes the value proposition more sane for the way I am using it.

title: Works with Samsung's 12.2 inch Note and Tab Pro tablets
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. I was not expecting it to accommodate my [[ASIN:B00HWMPTI2 Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2]], but it did. That earned it automatic high rating from me. You have to insert the Tab Pro into the supporting arm hooks in landscape mode, and if you attempt to adjust it to portrait there are no top and bottom supports.

More importantly, it also attached to the upper rod of a [[ASIN:B0018TAITA Musician's Gear Die-Cast Mic Stand]]. If you have any idea what a tablet mount for a microphone stand costs you will understand my enthusiasm. It will NOT work with the tripod mic stand that I tried, except for boom stands and attaching this to a boom was not only awkward, but unstable. Do note, though, that I had to remove the tightening handle on this unit and also remove the cup type washer to get it to fit to the die-cast mic stand's upper rod.

Assembly is easy to figure out so I cannot complain that the only instructions were printed on the box - and those were scant. It is super adjustable and in its current role as a tablet mount for a microphone stand it can be positioned exactly where I want it with my iPad Air 2 or smaller Samsung Tab 10.1 tablets. I am stuck in landscape mode with the Tab Pro as I mentioned above.

It's a shame this does not come with a clamp that will grab to tripod type mic stands because at the sub twenty buck price it would sell like hotcakes to musicians - especially those of us who have the larger Samsung tablets.

title: A vast improvement over fabric type pop filters
review_text:
I purchased mine on an impulse, not totally convinced that it was any better than the fabric type pop filters I use. How wrong I was. For evidence of that see Thomas G. Umstattd Jr.'s very helpful November 18, 2013 video review for a compelling demonstration of this pop guard.

Currently I am using this on both a MXL 550 and a MXL V67G mic (I am swapping the guard back and forth until I can purchase another one.) What I love is this fits directly over the two mics I cited. More importantly, there is no clumsy gooseneck and clamp, and even more importantly I can clean this one without destroying it.

As shown in the video I cited, this is as effective as the fabric pop guards. I will say that they will NOT make a good windscreen outdoors (I tested that and they pick up a lot of noise.) For indoors, though, they completely control pops and plosives.

One final reason why I love this: my fabric pop filters are prone to moving from their position if I accidentally bump into a mic stand. It seems that I am forever fine adjusting them, whereas this fits right over the mic and does not budge.

title: Packs a lot of sound into a small form factor
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. Volume is surprisingly loud for such a tiny speaker. I was able to clearly hear music I was streaming from nearly seven meters away. Most small, personal speakers are good for up to three meters, so it's ahead of most speakers in its class regarding sound volume.

Sound quality is equally impressive. I happened to have [[ASIN:B00ZJ5QXDO The Complete Concert By The Sea]] queued up on my phone when I went to test the speaker and the quality was superb. Every note in the high, medium and low frequency bands was crystal clean, even with the volume cranked to max. I tested a few other tracks from other albums to listen to the sound across all frequency bands with no problems.

The claimed play time is up to twelve hours. I got eight with the volume turned to maximum, and ten with it half way. If you keep the volume level at a quarter it will provide the full twelve hours. That is not an issue if you are listening to this close in like on a night stand or desk. At a quarter it's plenty loud. It does have an auto shut-off feature that turns it off if you are not playing music through it for fifteen minutes.

One final note: this comes up in bluetooth mode as soon as it's powered on. That means that even a novice can pair and connect to it by following the simple instruction sheet.

title: Excellent bargain and can be used as disposables or permanent
review_text:
I purchased these based strictly on price. They are not the heavy duty ties that are also offered by Velcro, but have a wider range of uses.

For one thing at five cents per tie I can use them for temporary cable management when setting up for performances, and not worry of I lose of miss one. Since they come in four rolls of twenty-five each I keep one roll in my gig bag, and the other rolls in a drawer at home. A single roll was all it took to get my morass of wires in my home studio under control, so the hundred-pack I purchased for less than a fast food meal will probably be six to nine months worth of cable management for gigs even if I treat them as disposable.

These are thinner than the heavy duty ties and are prone to stretching. However, they are every bit as strong when you are wrapping cable bundles. Do note that you need to separate them by tugging each tie from the roll. But you do need to be careful because the short head that contains the loop will also separate.

If you are a musician, computer tech or just want to get wires and cables under control a pack of these is a cost-effective want to do it.

title: Very heavy duty
review_text:
I purchased this to mount a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465smh 24-Inch SuperClear MVA LED Monitor]] to a speaker stand (a very light weight [[ASIN:B006H0DY3C Adam Hall SPS023S Speaker Stand]].

Frankly this mount is far sturdier than the stand on which I mounted it, and is so well constructed and heavy that it's overkill for the monitor. My monitor weighs less than eleven pounds and I am pretty sure this mount could easily support a monitor twice that weight.

Note that you can rotate your monitor 360 degrees, going from landscape to portrait, and every angle in between. However, you cannot tilt the viewing angle. I am not sure why not since the gimbal upon which the VESA mounting plate looks as though it should allow it, but it doesn't,

The clamp that mounts to the pole has a thick, anti-marring insert that will protect poles. It's also one of the reasons why this mount is so heavy - the construction is very heavy duty. All of the tools you need are provided to mount this to a pole and adjust it. The four bolts that come with it are a bit on the short side, although they worked with my monitor (and you need to provide a screwdriver for those.)

I am thoroughly pleased with this mount, especially since I almost purchased an [[ASIN:B001TMCVDW Audio2000'S AST420Y Portable Flat Panel TV/Monitor Stand with Foldable Tripod Legs]], but took a chance on this at the last minute. That decision saved me a lot of money and accomplished exactly what I wanted.

title: Great starter phones for sports
review_text:
I received these as a free review sample eight months ago. Since there are a lot of detailed reviews I will focus on my experience with these and also compare them to other sports phones.

First, these are good quality for twenty buck phones. But do be aware that sports phones are designed for comfort more than sound quality. Not that these are marginal - they have a typical bias towards the mid range, with compressed highs and adequate bass. They are not going to win acclaim from audiophiles, but do reproduce music that is clear and perfect for background listening.

Another thing I like is comfort. I can wear these for a few hours at a time without even noticing them. For sports phones that is a major plus. These allow in a little ambient noise for safety, but it does not appreciably affect the quality of music. Volume is somewhat limited. If you like music super loud these are not going to make you happy. On the other hand, high volume defeats the purpose of sports phones since you need to be aware of ambient noise and your surroundings. I cannot emphasize strongly enough that these are NOT general purpose phones.

Finally, the specs claim about four hours of music play time. That is true with the volume at about a third. If you crank the volume to max you can cut that time in half.

title: Very close to in-ear monitor quality sound
review_text:
I received these as a free review sample. I want to point out that these are hard-wired only. They use a 3.5mm connector and ARE NOT bluetooth. If you want phones for critical listening and transcribing music (or listening to a raw feed before mixdown) these are perfect. Bluetooth always entails some loss of sound quality, but these, and other direct connect phones, do not.

They are neutral enough to pass for high end in-ear monitors (IEMs), but there is a little bias on the low end. As long as you take that into account you can mentally compensate when listening to raw feeds.

One of the things that I found impressive is I could not detect any bias towards the mid range frequencies, nor do the high end frequencies sound compressed. For me this means that I can listen to acoustic jazz and hear the music as originally recorded. This is especially important for a lot of mid 1950s recordings before engineers started playing games with the mix. For these phones I sampled tracks from [[ASIN:B00CJYWUM6 At the Showboat / See What I Mean? / Settlin' In]] and [[ASIN:B000QQV5FM Dorothy Donegan Live]], and listened to the entire two hours and forty-eight minutes of Erroll Garner's [[ASIN:B00ZJ5QXDO The Complete Concert By The Sea]]. That test proved that these phones are absolutely superb for folks for love music.

While this is claimed to be for Android, I tested it on an iPad Air 2 and a ThinkPad T61 - it worked beautifully on both. In fact, on the ThinkPad I was playing from CD instead of an MP3 file and the sound quality was better than a direct connect from my Note 4 phone.

A few notes about the physical characteristics and features: I tested out the control block using my Note 4 phone and found it to be less than intuitive. I prefer controlling functions using those integrated in my Note 4 (including EQ.) I love the tangle free cord, and the comfort of the phones though. Everything about the construction and sound are of the highest quality.

Bottom line: if you are fanatical about sound quality these phones are ones that I highly recommend. I own other IEMs that cost twice as much that are close to these. Granted the expensive ones have completely neutral low frequency response, but if you are not mixing down these are as good in the overall scheme of things.

title: Works perfectly, but there are things you need to know
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample five and a half months ago and it's been invaluable. If your laptop has a fully functioning internal fan this array will augment that and keep your laptop cool even in unairconditioned spaces on a hot day. That will definitely prolong the life of the internal electronics and the hard drive.

This fan array moves a lot of air, promoting excellent heat transfer. However, it can interfere with other USB peripherals if you power it directly from your laptop, and especially if you add even more peripherals to the ports integrated into this unit. That is because the power draw form USB ports may exceed the capacity of the laptop, especially if you are running it off an unpowered USB hub. I had that problem when I tried running this, a mouse and a speaker from my laptop. I moved this one to a powered hub and the problem was immediately resolved.

If you are set in your ways regarding keyboard height know that this raises a laptop 1 3/8 inches higher at its lowest setting. For me it took a day to become accustomed to the raised typing height, but since it solved a genuine problem the tradeoff was worth it. Just know that you will need to adjust to that and it may slow down your productivity for a day or two.

One final note: if you live or work in a high dist environment take the time to shut this fan array down and blow it out with compressed air. It will greatly prolong the life of the array and will also ensure that it doesn't become noisy.

title: Excellent for electronics and other items
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample nearly a year ago and have been using it at least twenty times a month. I use it for carrying microphones, adapters and miscellaneous electronics I use when performing as a musician. For protection this is ideal, and the inside and outside zippered pouches make this even more versatile.

It does an excellent job of protecting the delicate microphones and adapters that I store in it. I am not using the dividers as vertical separators the way they were designed. Instead, I lay them on top of the mics, and then store the cables on top. That arrangement is perfect, and the bag and insert are relatively light and sturdy.

Close to a year of constant use is testimony to just how sturdy this bag is, especially considering the times it have been accidentally stepped upon. Since the canvas part is so sturdy I am guessing that the insert will probably last even longer. One of the reasons is the overall construction, though lightweight, is of the highest quality. I am betting that if this were used for its intended purpose of protecting a DLSR or other photo equipment it would do as great a job as it does protecting my mics and other items.

title: Inexpensive solution for two things
review_text:
I purchased this sight unseen, and solely to give my eyes a break from the much smaller laptop monitor I had been using. Since others have gone into the technical details (which are also amply described on this page), I'll stick to what I love about it and how I am now using it.

The main thing was price. At less than a hundred fifty bucks I took a chance. Hooking it up was super simple: a power cord, a VGA connection to my laptop (using the included cable), and screwing in the VESA adapter from my [[ASIN:B005C2914C Mount-It! MI-705, 3-Way Adjustable Tilting Desk Mount Bracket]] took literally ten minutes. This comes with a pedestal base that is more than adequate, but I wanted the mount I mentioned to free up desk real estate as well as to make this monitor a grab-and-go solution for a second use, which I'll get into below.

If there is one thing that I do not care for, it's the cramped area for connecting cables. The cable adapters for VGA, HDMI and power are inserted vertically, and the VGA and HDMI connections are closer together than necessary. Since I am connecting and disconnecting cables often this is a peeve, but if you plan to install it and leave it in one spot it's not even an issue.

The speakers are not the loudest when you are running sound via the HDMI port, but are more than adequate when you directly connect to the audio in port. This monitor comes with a 3.5mm cable for that purpose.

For my laptop (an aging ThinkPad) it is literally plug and play. I have finally migrated from XP to Windows 7 and this monitor's model was immediately recognized.

My second use is to press this into service as a large sheet music display. I am mirroring the screen using an [[ASIN:B00ZWOU5R2 EZcast 5GHz Wireless HDMI Streaming Media Player]] to display [[ASIN:B00WLIDHA4 MobileSheetsPro Music Reader]] mirrored from a tablet screen. Since this monitor weighs less than ten pounds it is fairly easy to set up at a gig. As a side note, if you do intend to use this on a gig or as a karaoke display this is an excellent mount: [[ASIN:B001TMCVDW Audio2000'S AST420Y Portable Flat Panel TV/Monitor Stand with Foldable Tripod Legs]].

Do note that the HDMI port will not power devices. For the EZcast dongle I have to use either a battery backup or a small wall wart (the same kind I charge my phone and tablet with), but that is not an issue either. I figured that for the price some corners had to be cut.

Although this is designed to be a desktop monitor I do wish there was a remote option for it. When I am using it to extend my laptop display it's perfect. For the screen mirroring use I mentioned a remote would be helpful.

The bottom line is I am thoroughly pleased with this monitor and may, in fact, purchase a second one so I am not swapping my laptop monitor out to take on gigs.

title: Rock solid for my ViewSonic 24-Inch monitor
review_text:
I purchased this specifically to mount a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465smh 24-Inch SuperClear MVA LED Monitor]]. It definitely holds the monitor - steady - in any position within this mount's range. Note that my monitor weighs in around 9.5 pounds, so factor that into your own needs.

Assembly is a snap. It comes with everything you need to mount the VESA adapter to your monitor, including washers and spacers. I had anticipated having to purchase bolts to fit, but that turned out to be unnecessary.

One of the things I love is the VESA bracket has slots that fit into horizontal posts. Those support the full weight of the monitor while you are installing the two adjustment bolts. In other words, assembling, mounting and adjusting this can be done by one person. My mount shipped with thumb style bolts and optional, heavier ones that you can use with the included hex wrench. Since my monitor was so light to begin with I used the thumb bolts, which hold the viewing angle in the narrow range of movement the VESA mount allows. Had my monitor been heavier I would have probably used the hex bolts, which are a lot beefier.

Bottom line: read some of the other reviews that discuss challenges that this mount has for heavier and larger monitors. However, if you have a 24" that is in the 10-12 pound range (or less) this is all the mount that you need. It's built like a tank, is a breeze to assemble, and holds lighter monitors absolutely rock steady.

title: Perfect for low draw USB devices
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. First, this is for low draw devices like mice, keyboards, thumb drives and the such. It will NOT support an external drive that gets its power from your machine's USB port.

For me this is perfect because it's USB 2.0 only (although it will also kick down to USB 1.1). I am using it on an old ThinkPad T61, which immediately recognized it as soon as I plugged it in. I did not test the Ethernet connection (which needs a separate driver on my XP machine), but the USB ports are problem free.

As a test I tried this hub on my Note 4 phone using a [[ASIN:B00LM4PDUU LinkS Micro-USB 3.0 OTG Adapter]] and the USB ports worked like they did on my T61. Again, I did not test the Ethernet port, but did populate two USB ports with a keyboard and mouse, and both were immediately recognized by the phone.

Bottom line: this is a nice way to expand USB ports for low power draw devices. The Ethernet port is a bonus and especially if you need to direct connect to a router, but you may need to download a driver to get it working.

I received this as a free review sample. This is NOT a bluetooth device. These phones are strictly for 3.5mm stereo connections. That means that this will work with a wider variety of devices.

The sound quality to my ears is why I awarded it five stars. There is definitely a crossover built into these phones because I could hear the separation of low and high frequencies, with a prominent bass in one ear. Also, there does not seem to be any compression at the high end of the frequency spectrum, which gives these phones a more natural sound. I listen to mainly acoustic jazz (piano jazz trios, vocalists, and similar), so I appreciate the realistic sound these phones provide.

There are a few areas that I would love to see improved: the cable is long and would be nicer if it were flat, tangle-proof. Also, the controls are a little too high up on the cable in my opinion. I can easily reach them, but when testing them I could not see the buttons. Of course, those are not show stoppers - just my own preferences. And regarding the controls, I already am familiar with their placement from use and memory, so that is really a non issue.

The phones are comfortable. They ship with small, medium and large tips and I used the ones that were already installed. The fit was perfect. These also ship with an extra set of premium, noise blocking tips. I have not tried them since the regular tips are more than adequate for me.

Other nice features are the zippered, hard case, velcro cable wrap and shirt clip. To be sure, they are value-added items, but the real value is the sound quality and these phones have that without a doubt.

Bottom line: if you want hard wired phones that allow you to listen critically to music (or transcribe it), this is a surprisingly inexpensive solution. I have used everything from high end studio in-ear monitors and premium phones, and these come close at a much more affordable price. I am not saying that these are as good as the expensive phones, but am saying that bang for your buck these are hard to beat and will surprise most audiophiles.

title: Very compact and with a micro B adapter does wonders for phones and tablets
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample (six months ago), and only sporadically used it with my laptop because that ancient thing only supported USB 2.0. It worked perfectly with the laptop, and was instantly recognized as soon as I plugged it in. The only reason I did not keep it plugged in is I was using an externally powered hub to power some thumb drives and external hard drive. An unpowered hub, no matter which brand would not cut it.

When I purchased a [[ASIN:B00LM4PDUU LinkS Micro-USB 3.0 OTG Adapter A male to Micro B adapter]] this small hub became my best friend. I Use the adapter to connect this hub to my Tab Pro 12.2 tablet (and on occasion my Note 4 phone), which allows me to use a real keyboard and mouse. I can also plug in a thumb drive, but the minute I do that the Tab Pro 12.2's battery starts getting consumed too quickly. However, when I need to transfer data (mainly movies and music) quickly, this hub truly supports USB 3.0 speeds.

What I have come to love about this is the small size easily fits in the padded bag in which I keep my tablet. Also, I always know when this hub is active because of the indicator light. As long as I keep my eye on remaining battery capacity on my Tab Pro when using a thumb drive I am OK. The key thing is this hub is appropriately sized for phones and tablets, and will support the transfer rates of which my phone and tablet are capable.

title: For non-bluetooth and very comfortable
review_text:
I received these as a free review sample six months ago and use them mainly on my laptop. I have also tested them on Samsung Note 3 and 4 phones, Tab 10.1 and Tab Pro 12.2 tablets, and an iPad Air 2. It works flawlessly with all of them, although some of the features like forwarding and skipping songs using the multi-function button only work with Apple IOS devices.

The main reason why I rated them so highly is sound quality. These phones are balanced across the high, mid and low frequency bands, although there seems to be some emphasis on the mid range, with slight compression on the high end. They are perfect for critical listening and even transcribing if you are a musician. Given the slight bias, though, these are not ideal for listening to monitor or raw tracks. Of course they were not designed for those tasks.

Another set of features I like are the flat, tangle-free cable and the comfort of the in-ear pieces. This ships with silicone ear adapters, but the default ones work well for me. Still, if you have smaller or larger ear canals the chances of this fitting well is good.

Ear adapters provide decent noise isolation, but not totally (not necessarily a bad thing if you are using this for walking and need to be aware of your surroundings.)

Overall, these are well constructed and have excellent sound quality - at least on the devices on which I tested them. Just know that all of the features are not available on anything but Apple IOS devices.

title: Excellent single-purpose monitor
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample five months ago and have been using it for around four months. This is a rear view monitor only - not a dashcam - and it works far better than one of the combination rear monitors/dashcams that I have also used.

Since there are a large number of reviews that cover this in detail I am going to keep mine brief. Here is the single thing I do not like about it: the terrible documentation. On the other hand you can have this professionally installed for not a lot of money, which is the route that I took. If you are a do-it-yourselfer installing it right is less than an hour job (according to the tech who installed mine).

What I love is the clear visual behind me. The camera works in dark and low light, and the display has sufficient clarity and resolution to easily see what is behind you and estimate distances. If you were to purchase this as an option on a vehicle I shudder to think of the cost, but for less than one hundred fifty bucks professionally installed this is a bargain. And if you do install it yourself you can knock a C-note off that cost.

If you parallel park frequently this is a perfect way to make that easier. For rural driving this may not be a needed accessory, but for city use it's a convenience (and a safety feature as well.) Do note the information in the product specs too because they are clear about what this will and will not work with.

title: Great gig bag
review_text:

title: Vast improvement over the iPad 2,  but ...
review_text:
Since there are nearly two thousand reviews at the time I am writing this one I'll stick with a few observations.

First - and this is important - do not make the same mistake I did and opt for the 16GB model. Go for the 64 or 128GB version because, frankly, the 16GB capacity is insufficient for the newer operating system. Coming from a 16GB iPad 2 that was not at capacity I thought saving a few bucks and getting the same capacity here would be prudent. It's not and I have already run out of space before completely transferring my existing apps and data.

Second, this looks to be the same size as the earlier iPad I own, but the screen is so vastly superior that there is no comparison. Plus the speed difference is amazing.

Other features, especially the camera and battery life, are giant improvements as well. If you are hanging onto an older iPad like the 2 model I had, this one is well worth the upgrade. Just be aware that the 16GB model is not going to cut it, even if you are nowhere near capacity on an older 16GB iPad. For more specifics on features and benefits read through the spotlighted reviews here.

title: This has come a long way since the Roku 2
review_text:
I'll keep my review brief because there are a number of excellent ones that go into the features and benefits. I am approaching this as someone who owned a Roku 2 and was on the fence about moving up.

Here are the features I personally like: integrated YouTube access. When I got the Roku 2 a few years ago that was only possible with a third party service and forced me to also purchase a Chromecast to conveniently access YouTube. So for me, this feature alone justified the upgrade because that particular channel is important to me.

Another improvement - for me - is you can now select Paypal in lieu of a credit card. I do not use credit cards, and had to purchase a prepaid one to install the earlier model. You cannot get through the install process without some payment method. There are no hidden charges, but the payment method is required to be on file in case you may want to pay for a premium service. If you have Paypal and do not want to (or cannot) give a credit card number, you can still proceed with the installation process.

Installation, like the earlier model, is a breeze. I had mine up and running in practically five minutes.

As for the voice feature - I honestly never bothered with it so cannot say one way or the other if it's good or bad. Check other reviews for that. I will say that the upgrade was worth it to me. If you are still on a Roku 2 and are happy with it in all respects this is not going to be a bargain. If you want expanded features and channels and faster response this is a good choice.

If you are new to Roku and are considering cutting the cable this is worthwhile - I am using Netflix at less than ten bucks per month and am getting all the entertainment I want from just that. It's certainly a bargain for me compared to local cable services, which I deem to be way overpriced. This may be the first step in 'cutting the cable' if Netflix, Prime Movies or other inexpensive services have offering that satisfy your needs.

title: Even works on my ancient Windows XP machine
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. I immediately plugged it into one of the USB 2.0 ports on my ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP and was up and running. No drivers, no fuss.

Since I do not have any laptops with USB 3.0 I could not test that speed, but a directory containing 19.4GB transferred via my USB 2.0 port in a little over twenty minutes. Blazing fast? Not by USB 3.0 standards, but darn quick form the ancient laptop (which may have actually slowed the process down.)

The real reason why I rated this so highly is the cost. I recall purchasing a 64GB SD card a year ago that was vastly more expensive (at the time) than this half terabyte drive. Of course the SD card was miniscule, but this drive will fit in a shirt pocket. For me this is a convenient way to not only back up my two laptops, but also my phone and two tablets. Those are backed up via a hard connection to my laptop because they require FAT32 while this drive out of the box is NTFS. I would have reformatted it, but it worked so well with my laptop that I left it as is.

If you are planning to use this with an Apple IOS or Android device only, you will need to reformat it via those operating systems.

This comes with a cable that is USB A on the end that connects to your laptop or OTG connector, and USB 3.0 for the end that attaches to the drive itself. The 3.0 end is a little tight in tolerance, but once it's perfectly aligned it slips in and holds firmly.

Bottom line: this is inexpensive mass storage that is great for backing up files and documents, storing large media such as movies and music, or transporting files to and from work.

The main reason why I own so many is I am a musician who owns amps, a PA and keyboard and the power in many venues is marginal at best. This is inexpensive protection and I have witnessed other musicians' gear getting fried in the same venues in which I play, so I know these surge suppressors work.

My combined experience with both of these models has resulted in zero problems. This is a professional-grade piece of gear and it designed to protect your equipment and to last if properly cared for and used properly. I do want to note that one rule of thumb I use is to not overload protected power strips. If you do you will be defeating the protection that this one affords. Please bear that in mind and read the specs while making a purchase decision. title: Excellent sound quality and small form factor
review_text:
I received these as a free review sample. Note that these are NOT bluetooth. They are strictly hardwired and require two connections: (1) 3.5mm into your device's audio out or earphone jack and USB A for power.

Sound quality is excellent. I was impressed with the bass in particular because it sounded natural. Many speakers I test have a bias towards bass, which is great for a lot of contemporary music that is bass-centric, but sounds artificial playing music that is more acoustic in nature. Since I listen to a lot of jazz piano trio albums these speakers are perfect for me.

The high end will not break up at the highest volume, but does sound a little compressed. Again, that is not necessarily bad because high frequency compression makes some music sound better. The mid range is very rich and one of the reasons why these speakers sound so good to my ears.

Volume is more than sufficient for a 20x30 foot room. There are no controls on the speakers, so you need to control the volume and EQ from whichever device you plug these into. My phone, tablet and laptop all have hardware/software to do this and chances are so will your devices.

My laptop's spare USB port was sufficient to power these speakers, and the big plus is you do not need to worry about batteries, wall warts and the such. I was able to also test these with my phone connecting the USB cable end to a charger. To be honest, that is a little inconvenient because the cables are hardwired into the speaker master unit. Despite the cable issue I mentioned above these are nice, compact speakers that sound great. More importantly (to me) there are no batteries to worry about, and they take up very little desk space.

title: Excellent portable light
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. Up front I want to explain why I subtracted a star: two reasons, foremost is the instructions are in Chinese. That is not a show stopper because no instructions are needed. The second reason is the USB charging cable uses a barrel style connector at the end that connects to the light itself. That means that if you lose the cable you will not be able to easily replace it. Standard micro USB cables are available from even grocery stores. This style is not. Normally I would not subtract a star for just one of the issues I cited, but I think both, combined, prevent it from being a five star product.

It has a lot going for it. It definitely illuminates, and I love the fact that I can go from dim, to medium that is sufficient for reading, to very bright that is suitable for hobby work. For example, I restore vintage fountain pens and at the brightest setting, plus a magnifier, I can see exterior details that I normally used an illuminated magnifier to discover.

The gooseneck stays put in any position I place it. That is mainly because the LED array is so light that it imposes little weight. I am on the fence about the base. I like it and it does stay put, but is easy to knock over, which can be a pain if you are using this for detail work. What I would love to see is a magnetic strip on the base, which would allow me to place it anywhere. In fact, I am probably going to glue a magnet to it.

Bottom line: this is a relatively inexpensive light that definitely does the job.

title: Excellent protection, but ...
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. As advertised the protection is excellent. The construction is as well, and you actually can turn it inside out to change the color scheme.

Here is the 'but': this case literally fits the Sound Blaster Roar 2 like a glove (and it is only for the Roar 2 model.) The stretching and pulling required is a bit onerous. I thought it would be a learning curve issue, but each time I use this bag it is as difficult as the last time. Difficult, but not impossible. On the other hand, had this been designed for an easier fit I am not sure the same level of protection would be there.

Also note that this is strictly for transporting the Roar 2. Once it is inserted in this case you cannot access controls. I kind of like that because I do carry my Roar 2 around and appreciate the fact that this will keep it from getting dinged.

One final thing: the top cover does not completely close. There is a gap and there is no zipper. That is why you can turn this inside out.

Bottom line: this provides excellent protection and is well made. On the other hand, there are challenges as I noted above and you will need to weight those into a purchase decision. I do use mine a lot and have a love/hate relationship with it.

title: Better for a night light than for music stands
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. As a music stand light it's functional, but not ideal. As a night light or even a clip on to a book for night time reading when your partner of sleeping this is truly useful.

Be aware that it's small and even at max illumination with all LEDs active it is not glaring. That is a good feature, but the tradeoff is as a music stand light you may have to keep adjusting the goosenecks to get optimum illumination.

The goosenecks are a little on the thin side, which is another reason I think this is best suited to clamping directly on a book or headboard (if you can find a spot that the clamp can grip). On a music stand turning pages too briskly can change the position of the LEDs; not a problem when reading a book, but not the distraction you want when playing an instrument.

Bottom line: if you are looking for a light for your music stand carefully comparison shop. If you are looking for a portable and effective reading light you will love this one.

title: Excellent sound quality and LOUD
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. I'll spare you a regurgitation of the product specs or paraphrasing the previous two reviews, but will focus on what sets this one apart from the pack.

The biggest surprise I had was volume. This is a relatively small speaker and most bluetooth speakers in this one's size and price range are designed as personal speakers that are meant to be nearby on a desk, night stand or counter top. I can clearly hear this one two rooms away indoors and even outdoors in areas with high ambient noise this can cut through and project sound.

Sound quality is neutral, and I mean that in a good way. While there is some bias towards the mid range frequencies it does not 'color' the sound of music being streamed to it. To be honest, this is not going to crank out heavy bass, so if you listen to bass-centric music you may be disappointed. On the other hand, the highs and lows are practically seamless, with a slight emphasis towards the mid range, so if you listen to jazz, blues or some forms of rock and Americana this speaker will probably please you.

One review discussed bluetooth range issues so I specifically tested that. Even two rooms away, which normally causes drops in quality, I was able to get crystal clear streaming with no drops in the music quality streamed from a Samsung Note 3. The distance is approximately twenty feet, but definitely not line of sight, so I am happy with that aspect.

While the product specs claim six hours of music, you can realistically expect somewhere between four and four and a half hours if you have the volume cranked. If you drop it to about a quarter - perfect for near listening up to two or three meters - you will get the claimed play time.

title: If you are in the Samsung camp this is great
review_text:
There are more than enough helpful reviews, product specs and Q&A, so I am going to focus on this tablet for folks who are upgrading from another Android tablet, and especially another Samsung. I'll say up front that the biggest reason [for me, anyway] is the extra screen real estate and resolution.

I had a small surprise in that mine did not come with Amazon apps pre-installed like they did on my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 (10.1-Inch, White) 2013 Model]] that it replaced. Locating the App Store application so I could install all of the applications that I have purchased was a bit of a hassle, but I finally got that resolved. Like my older Samsung tablet this one is a little less than spectacular when it comes to streaming music to a speaker via bluetooth. I do not know why Samsung cannot get it right on tablets because I have never experienced any issues streaming on my Note II and Note 3 phones.

Another issue of which you need to be aware is this tablet is thin and flexible. I knew that in advance and purchased a [[ASIN:B00KCDBD2E Samsung Galaxy Note Pro 12.2-inch Case Cover]], which in my opinion is one of the better cases for this tablet. The hard shell part of the case into which you insert the tablet provides a rigid casing that allows zero flex. No matter which case you ultimately select I strongly recommend that you get one.

You may have issues with some apps if you opt to install an SD card to expand your storage, or if you are moving an SD card from another tablet to this one. The KitKat version of the operating system will not write to SD cards under certain conditions. There is a free fix called SD KitKat Fixer by JRummy Apps that you can get from the Play Store. I highly recommend it. As a side note, I had no issues with this SD card: [[ASIN:B00N2ROG9O PNY Turbo Performance 64GB High Speed MicroSDXC Class 10 UHS-1]]. It is an inexpensive way to max out your memory. I have heard that this tablet will work with 128GB cards, but I have not tested any so cannot say for sure.

If you are accustomed to Samsung's user interface you will feel right at home. For me, after the little challenges I mentioned above I was fully up and operational on this tablet in a few hours. A lot of that time was reinstalling purchased apps from Amazon and the Play Store, tweaking my settings so that they mirrored those on my Tab 10.1 (which are identical to my Note 3 phone), and this feels as comfortable as an old shoe. A much larger old shoe to be sure, and it's incredible how much extra screen space you get going from 10.1 to 12.2.

title: Perfect for its stated purposes
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample. This is not a zoom type telescope. You can adjust focus for your objective (the 52mm end) as well as the eye lens (the 16mm end), but you will not be able to zoom in. Think of this as a mono scope that can bring a far object into sharp focus.

Another thing to note is the field of vision is less than the 18 degrees marked on the body. It's about half that, and the night and day marking does not imply that this is a night vision scope. You will still need an external light source in low level lighting conditions. For example, moonlight will work, but in total darkness you will not be able to see a thing.

For me this is very useful for a hobby of mine, which is reptile spotting. Where I live there is an abundance of species, especially turtles and snakes, but we also have alligators and many interesting lizards. I prefer observing gators from a distance, and when walking down trails in parks (and there are many in my area) it's nice to be able to sit in a stationary point and scan for gators on banks as well as swimming. Same for various snakes, both land and water.

What I love about this scope is it's rugged. There are no lens caps, but the nylon case that comes with it makes it ideal for outdoors activities in harsh environments. It's outer material appears to be rubber, and I have dropped mine a few times without damaging it.

When you do bring an object into focus it's sharp and crystal clear. The field of vision may seem narrow, but you can actually take in a lot of details by slow scanning. It may take a little time to get accustomed to viewing wide fields of vision with it, but once you do, it's easy to use.

title: Rock solid with some advanced features
review_text:
I purchased this to support a [[ASIN:B00ND1KHY2 Mackie Mix Series Mix12FX -Watt 12-Channel Mixer]], which it easily does. What impressed me the most is the construction. I had been using a music stand with the tray perpendicular to the ground and it worked, but was not nearly as stable as this stand. Moreover, I looked at a few other brands, but most were cheaply made.

Here are a few things that set this one apart: first, the clamping mechanisms are quick release type and not the cheesy knobs that every other stand I tried employs. Second, if you are considering this for a truly heavy device like a projector the pins for the support pole guarantee that it will be supported. Frankly, the pins are probably never going to be needed because the main release mechanisms hold firmly.

Dimensions are:
Tray: 15 9/16 x 10 7/8 inches with lips along the widths top and bottom.
Stand: adjusts from 23 to 53 inches - this is ideal if you are a keyboardist or drummer who wants to control your instrument and mics via a mixer because the height range is perfect for most scenarios.
Footprint: 25 inches between tripod feet points.

This also comes with a sticky silicone pad that measures 12 x 7 5/78 inches to hold a mixer or laptop firmly in place. My Mackie mixer did not budge when it was placed on the pad and the table tilted 30 degrees.

Finally, I purchased a [[ASIN:B000XZYXTG Hamilton Carrying Bag for KB50 & KB990 Series Stands]] that easily holds and protects this stand. I recommend it if you do opt for this model.

title: Allowed me to use a condser mic with my Samsung tablet
review_text:
I purchased this specifically to connect a condenser mic to my Samsung Tab 3 10.1. I needed two other devices to make it work - an XLR M to F cable and a phantom power source (for the latter I am using an [[ASIN:B00KAPGLQC InnoGear® 1- Channel 48V Phantom Power Supply]] and the combination works like a charm.

The cable itself is not especially heavy gauge, but the connectors and strain reliefs are high quality. Of course, the main point for me is this works with my tablet, and it not only does for it, but also for my Note 3 phone. I use my tablet as a video camera for recording musical performances and until I added a condenser mic (an MXL 551R) the sound quality was poor. Since using the mic - made possible in part by this cable - the sound quality has dramatically improved.

Basically, I carefully checked out a number of similar cables and this is the one that had the best reviews and specs. I paid more for it, but feel that I also received commensurate value because of the construction and overall solid performance.

title: Very effective. Does change the typing height of your laptop
review_text:
I received this as a free review sample and it was sorely needed because the internal fan in my ThinkPad T61 finally died. Note: if you are looking at this as a cure know that many laptops report a fan failure then shut down. In the case of mine, I found that I could press the On/Off button briefly when that happened and it would power back up and boot Windows.

This fan array moves a lot of air, promoting excellent heat transfer. So far it has worked well and I have had no premature shutdowns (although I still have to go through the On/Off button sequence every time I power the ThinkPad up.)

Do be aware that this fan array will interfere with other USB peripherals if you power it directly from your laptop, and especially if you add even more peripherals to the ports integrated into this unit. That is because the power draw form USB ports may exceed the capacity of the laptop, especially if you are running it off an unpowered USB hub. I had that problem when I tried running this, a mouse and a speaker from my laptop. I moved this one to a powered hub and the problem was immediately resolved.

Also, this raises a laptop 1 3/8 inches higher at its lowest setting. For me it took a day to become accustomed to the raised typing height, but since it solved a genuine problem the tradeoff was worth it. Just know that you will need to adjust to that and it may slow down your productivity for a day or two.

If your laptop has a fully functioning internal fan this array will augment that and keep your laptop cool even in unairconditioned spaces on a hot day. That will definitely prolong the life of the internal electronics and the hard drive.

title: As good as the OEM Samsung card
review_text:
When I purchased my Note 3 from Verizon I also purchased a 64GB Samsung card that has served me well for nearly eighteen months. I decided to purchase another 64GB card to back up the one in my phone and I took a chance with this one. It has yet to let me down.

Since my files are nearly static on my phone (the only major charges are new music and photos), after I synched my Samsung's card to this one I swapped this one into the Note 3 as my primary card. I figured that any issues with streaming music, shooting video clips and photos would show up fairly quickly with constant use. That is why I am pleased. I honestly cannot discern any difference in either performance or reliability with this card.

I am so pleased that I am going to purchase another to back up my laptop. At present the price of these cards have dropped dramatically since I paid Verizon nearly ninety bucks for my Samsung card. I am sure that brand has also dropped in price, but this one is so solid and reliable that I am going to stick with it - at least for the time being. The bottom line is if you own a phone or tablet that will recognize 64GB this is an inexpensive way to upgrade an older 16 or 32 GB card.

title: Almost plug and go
review_text:
I received this as a review sample and even though I am experienced with setting up and configuring networks, this was so easy that I honestly believe anyone can set it up with the scant instructions.

My initial set up was to connect it to my DSL modem just to check it out. Although the instructions are terse, you do need to read them regardless of level of experience. For one thing, it requires you to completely power off your broadband modem. For another, it takes a bit to boot up no matter how you intend to use it. Connecting to broadband was a snap.

What I really wanted was a range extender and this was as simple to configure for that as it was to configure for broadband. In that mode, when you first power it on and boot up it takes over a minute and you may be tempted to think it's broken. Don't. Once it is powered up, like the broadband set up (DSL or cable), the wizard makes it simple to discover your wireless router, connect to it and extend the range of your network. My wireless router turns in a weak -70dB from my master bedroom (measured with [[ASIN:B004EBZX6W Wi-Fi Analyzer]]) and once I installed this in the same room the signal dramatically improved to a strong -40dB. In the same room with my master wireless router this comes in at -47dB while the master router measures in at -56dB. That indicates that the signal of this router is exceptionally strong.

There are options for adding sensors for home control. I did not test that set of features because I did not receive sensors, but it is functionality that makes this router/extender a great choice if you do want to pursue home control too. There are IOS and Android apps that can be used in conjunction with the sensor features. Again, I did not explore those and probably will not since I am not interested in them. As a router alone I love this, and especially the overall signal strength and ease of setting up and configuring.

title: Not for hi-draw devices, but handy for common peripherals
review_text:
I received the four port model as a review sample. Note that this is a quick way to expand or multiply USB ports on a PC or laptop, but you cannot plug external hard drives into it along with other devices because you will quickly max out the USB power limit. I use mine for my mouse, a camera synching cable and a 32GB thumb drive. That leaves me a spare port for synching (but not charging) my phone or tablet.

For my purposes this hub is perfect. It gives me the expansion for the low power peripherals I use, and it is handier to plug those into this hub than to fumble around with ports on the back and sides of my laptop.

As for full speed, I cannot test this because my old laptop only supports USB 2.0. The speeds that I get from that, though, are on par with what I get if I were to directly connect my phone or tablet (or thumb drive) to the laptop's integrated USB ports. I will leave it to others to discuss USB 3.0 performance.

This is truly plug and play on my Win XP and Win 7 laptops, and I tested it on my Note 3 phone with an OTG adapter and it worked in that configuration too (I connected a keyboard and mouse for that test.)

Bottom line: if you are planning to plug in hard drives and other high power drawing devices you will need a hub with an external power supply. For mice, synching and other low power peripherals this is both convenient and well made, and is at the least the equal of every other USB hub I own or have tested.
