title: Works with Suddenlink perfectly. Increased signal stability and speeds
review_text:
We have Suddenlink cable, internet, and land line phone service and had been happy with our three year old router and their modem. Until we moved to a new house. The arris modem was dropping signal significantly every single day - we either had super slow or no connection for hours. I had the cable guys out here four times in 61 days to fix the problem. I was literally ready to just cancel Suddenlink and move to AT&T for internet, but decided to try this Nighthawk combo first.

It was spotted instantly by Suddenlink when I called to give them the new modem Mac address, so the connection was just a single phone call to start. No drama. I have 9 daily devices on WiFi and three TiVo receivers that connect via Ethernet or WiFi plus the land line phone. There's four Ethernet connections and two phone connections on the modem, plenty for our needs.

It's been almost three weeks and I've noticed an astonishing improvement in our initial connection and reliability. Rather than daily outages, we have had five total in three weeks and none lasted more than 15 to 20 minutes. Stability of the signal has improved and our speeds are double what they were with the arris modem - we're actually getting the high speed service we pay for. The router is also projecting the WiFi far enough that I no longer need to use a secondary extender to get WiFi by the pool and patio.

I like the Genie app with this. The ability to check channels, reboot the router if needed, and see which devices are online is very handy. I also like the clear, bright lights on the front. At a glance you know if there's a problem. Bottom line for me is that I haven't canceled our services from Suddenlink because this unit fixed 90% of our problem.

title: Only works with the remote! Nice, full, rich sound with 55" Vizio tv in very large room
review_text:
I bought my Bose Solo 15 at another online retailer during a one day sale for a price that made it irresistible and after a month, I am happy that I did it. We have two 55" televisions and the one in our master bedroom has the Denon sound base under it and that unit has simply been outstanding. I was actually looking to just buy a second Denon for the living room tv and chose this Bose unit due to the one time sale and the Bose reputation.

This unit sits directly under our 55" Vizio smart tv and connects with the digital audio optical cable - just like the Denon base. I turned off the tv's physical speakers and let the Bose take over. The sound is full and significantly improved over the thin tv speakers. The unit shines when watching movies that have lots of rich soundtrack music and when you use the Dialogue button to soften background sounds and highlight conversation type dialogue.

The Bluetooth connected with my LG V10 phone and my fourth generation Fiire tablet immediately, allowing me to play music and my audio book through the Bose. Very nice extra functionality - the Denon does this as well. The Bose includes a universal remote control that requires some effort to set up correctly and completely. However! Once the cursing and hair pulling was over, I got it done. The Bose remote now operates our television, the Bose base, and our TiVo/cable box exactly as the cable remote does.

My one star deduction is because the only way to use the Bose Solo is with their included remote control. There are no physical buttons on the machine and that strikes me as a real design flaw. If you break or lose this proprietary remote you cannot even turn the Bose on or off, much less actually use it for sound. At least the Denon sound base can be operated manually or trained to respond to other remote controls with three steps. For me this Bose Solo is worth the price I paid (under three hundred bucks) and it is equal to the Denon in sound quality. But for overall value and ease of use, the Denon is the five star product.

title: Never miss a soft flute or clarinet again! Comfortable, no cauliflower ear. Not noise canceling, great music
review_text:
Honestly, I have wanted a pair of good Sennheiser headphones for years, but I couldn't justify it to myself - I mean we have a Denon sound base that connects via Bluetooth and Alexa for music, so a personal pair of headphones seems like a selfish indulgence. OMG. Do it. Be selfish. I have been wearing these things for days now every chance that I get and falling in love with music all over again.

First thing, I must correct a misstatement in an earlier review - the HD 579 are NOT noise cancellation headphones. They do not have that technology and are not intended to, not marketed as such and I double checked with Sennheiser directly to be sure. It might be easy to mistake the beautiful sound quality and encapsulation of the sound for noise cancellation at first - simply because the headphones fit very well and at an upper volume, external noise doesn't readily intrude.

The fit is far more comfortable than I remember headphones being. The band is nicely padded and adjustable and the ear cups are very soft, thick and they fully cover your ear without any pinching. I have worn these for thirty minutes and up to three hours consecutively in vary increments, every day for five days now and never had cauliflower ear. Nor do my ears get hot. I'm using these with my Fire Tablet, my LG V10 phone and Sceptre 55" television playing music through our cable provider's music stations. The connection plug is tight and the cord has proven to be long enough for use in bed at night while reading, on the sofa reading & it rolls up to put in my pocket while wandering around cleaning house and doing barn chores.

As to the quality of the music.... simply outstanding. Far better than I really expected. One of my favorite soundtracks is from the movie Hannibal by Hans Zimmer. It has a mix of pure classical and opera. The HD 579 phones let me hear the French horns and the soft build of the clarinets as crisp and clearly as the big cellos and trumpets in other, louder movements. Simple acoustic vocal pieces from James Taylor, Tracy Chapman and Paul Simon are beautifully rendered and you can appreciate the realism of a live performance. These headphones are very nice and I wish I had bought something like them long ago, but now that I have these, I won't be far from them and I definitely will be grabbing them every time I want music, which is daily.

title: Beautiful picture, tiny eye for the remote control to aim at, works with Denon sound bar & wifi
review_text:
I bought this television (I double checked the exact model number to be positive that t I am reviewing the correct one) used at an estate sale in January and it's been used daily in our master bedroom every since. The color and clarity of the picture is simply wonderful. In comparison to our brand new Sceptre 55" 1080p tv in the living room and the 3 year old Samsung in the guest room, this Vizio has the prettiest picture and best refresh rate. The Samsung has the best native sound though without a sound bar enhancement.

This Vizio is our only Smart Television and I have a Firestick on the living room tv. As of today, June 16, 2016, the Amazon app and others are all working just fine through the television's remote control with the direct access buttons. Connecting this tv to our wifi network did take several attempts and I had to update the firmware twice before it would connect and hold the connection for more than 48 hours. (To be honest, I have no idea if the former owner every actually used the internet connection so it may not have been updated before I got it) Since January, I have had no trouble with the connection or streaming. We do have a super fast internet service and a dual band router with this tv as the only thing typically streaming on one band.

My one star deduction is the tiny receiver area for the remote control. If you are using the actual remote rather than a universal one for the cable box, you have to aim directly at the very tiny eye in the far left bottom corner and it can take a couple of tries to hit it just right from across a big room. This drives me nuts when I'm streaming from Amazon Prime and need to pause the show quickly or try to flick through the selections. However, I would totally buy another Vizio tv again in the future if the new ones are as good as this two year old used one has been - I've definitely gotten my hundred fifty dollars worth out of this one.

title: Excellent battery life, very fast boot up, almost no bloatware. Good basic laptop
review_text:
In comparison to my Toshiba Satellite 15" with similar specs, this ASUS is about equal - there are definitely some things I like better about the ASUS for everyday use and a couple of small quibbles that bother me. First off the computer itself is about the same weight as my Toshiba so carrying it around is exactly the same and it fits in my existing laptop sleeves and bags. It does have a DVD tray so you can play movies & music and burn discs as needed (as does my Toshiba), but a lot of laptops don't offer this anymore, so this is a definite plus.

I do really like that the ASUS comes a lot cleaner out of the box than my Toshiba - almost no bloatware pre-installed. The basic Windows 10 and you can don't have to spend 30 minutes messing around with a bunch of garbage you don't want and won't use anyway. Additionally, the ASUS boots up about 20 seconds faster from off than my Toshiba and again from the sign in screen, the ASUS is still faster. The screen is very pretty and clear with a variety of images and video - keep in mind that it's NOT a touchscreen. I've been averaging about 6 hours of use with the battery before it hits the 30% mark - that is net surfing, watching some random videos, and mostly word processing. Leaving it on in sleep mode with no use - it went almost 4 full days before needing a charge. The wifi connects immediately and I've had zero issues with it dropping out either inside or out on the back deck.

I really like the keyboard and the overall shape of the frame on this particular laptop. My Toshiba has the keyboard just open and exposed and what happens is that the heels of my hands tend to slip upwards as I type or bump the space bar. Or my thumbs slide into the mousepad area and now my cursor has bounced someplace new & I'm typing in the wrong spot. The ASUS keyboard is slightly lowered and has a border around it - for me anyway, this design is MUCH easier to type with. (See the photo.) The shape of the overall frame is better on the ASUS than the Toshiba as well. The rounded corners and edges on the ASUS don't poke into your wrists after an hour of writing or research.

My quibbles seem small on the surface, but after almost three weeks of use, they are aggravating me. First - the ASUS doesn't keep time as well as the Toshiba. It's off by 2 full minutes. (See the photos) I've checked both a couple of times and set them manually at the same moment and within 24 hours, the ASUS has lost 2 minutes - it never loses more than that though. Second - The charger is smaller than every other one I have for the other two laptops and the Chromebook in this house. The other three are standard size, but the one on the ASUS is a tiny bit smaller and thus you can't use another charger for this laptop in an emergency. Third - the speakers on the ASUS don't sound quite as full as the ones on my Toshiba. Of course... no built in speakers on a laptop are really meant for full music enjoyment.

My bottom line is that at this price point, this is a nice machine and will do almost anything you can want with regard to basic internet surfing, movie watching, office work and the like. This is not a gamer's computer and it's not meant to be. But as a regular, go to every day laptop, it's a pretty good one. I want to give it 4 1/2 stars.

I do really like that the ASUS comes a lot cleaner out of the box than my Toshiba - almost no bloatware pre-installed. The basic Windows 10 and you can don't have to spend 30 minutes messing around with a bunch of garbage you don't want and won't use anyway. Additionally, the ASUS boots up about 20 seconds faster from off than my Toshiba and again from the sign in screen, the ASUS is still faster. The screen is very pretty and clear with a variety of images and video - keep in mind that it's NOT a touchscreen. I've been averaging about 6 hours of use with the battery before it hits the 30% mark - that is net surfing, watching some random videos, and mostly word processing. Leaving it on in sleep mode with no use - it went almost 4 full days before needing a charge. The wifi connects immediately and I've had zero issues with it dropping out either inside or out on the back deck.

I really like the keyboard and the overall shape of the frame on this particular laptop. My Toshiba has the keyboard just open and exposed and what happens is that the heels of my hands tend to slip upwards as I type or bump the space bar. Or my thumbs slide into the mousepad area and now my cursor has bounced someplace new & I'm typing in the wrong spot. The ASUS keyboard is slightly lowered and has a border around it - for me anyway, this design is MUCH easier to type with. (See the photo.) The shape of the overall frame is better on the ASUS than the Toshiba as well. The rounded corners and edges on the ASUS don't poke into your wrists after an hour of writing or research.

My quibbles seem small on the surface, but after almost three weeks of use, they are aggravating me. First - the ASUS doesn't keep time as well as the Toshiba. It's off by 2 full minutes. (See the photos) I've checked both a couple of times and set them manually at the same moment and within 24 hours, the ASUS has lost 2 minutes - it never loses more than that though. Second - The charger is smaller than every other one I have for the other two laptops and the Chromebook in this house. The other three are standard size, but the one on the ASUS is a tiny bit smaller and thus you can't use another charger for this laptop in an emergency. Third - the speakers on the ASUS don't sound quite as full as the ones on my Toshiba. Of course... no built in speakers on a laptop are really meant for full music enjoyment.

My bottom line is that at this price point, this is a nice machine and will do almost anything you can want with regard to basic internet surfing, movie watching, office work and the like. This is not a gamer's computer and it's not meant to be. But as a regular, go to every day laptop, it's a pretty good one. I want to give it 4 1/2 stars.

title: Incredibly easy to install. Impressive sound improvement for a big tv in a big room
review_text:
I bought this at another website thanks to a Christmas gift card, but I researched the different types of sound bars and enhancement systems on Amazon & various places first. I wanted a very simple to use, unobtrusive setup, a digital connection and something that could work with our very open and large room without requiring setting up ugly components everywhere and still sound clean. This Denon base ticks every box for me.

I literally had this unit out of the box, installed under our 50" television, connected and working in less than 20 minutes - that includes reading the directions and unpacking. The box looked huge at first just sitting there alone, but once the tv was on top of it, it sort of vanished. Another 5 minutes and I had the Denon machine trained to respond to the volume buttons on my cable remote control. Mine came with a remote control, the digital optical cable and the red & white style connection. It connected to my phone and tablet via Bluetooth on the first try and played music through both using the Amazon Prime streaming and music saved to my devices - the sound is excellent by the way.

The included remote is handy for switching between daytime and night modes - the overall sound is lower in night mode. And you can choose between the surround sound mode or regular with the remote as well. One thing I have noticed, is that it can take three to five seconds for those changes to register and to hear them. The box turns on automatically when it senses a signal - no need to fiddle with it. Just turn the tv on & go about your business like always. The most impressive thing here is the improvement in the quality of the sound - every single bit is better! The guy reporting the news, music channels, background sound effects in movies, conversations in dramas... it's all crisp and clear and full. I am really pleased.

title: Exactly what I needed for music while riding horses - great for use in the arena,loud & clear
review_text:
I listen to music when I'm riding in the arena and I do some freestyle dressage to music which means my horses need to hear the music as well. I'm always hunting for a Bluetooth speaker that can be used inside and outside without breaking because of a little dust or sprinkle of water and that I can hear from 60 meters away. The actual quality of the music has sort of been pushed to the bottom of my wish list. This speaker has been a pleasure.

It has a carbiner snap and a loop on top so you can hang it up or hook it on a wall, but it's balanced perfectly and sits on a flat surface normally as well. For my purposes, suspended from a hook in the air is perfect. The speaker swings just a bit and the sound is projected outward rather than just up. Leaving my phone near it on a preset play list works very well when I ride - the speaker doesn't skip or stutter. When an email or text message comes in to my phone, the speaker just makes a pleasant boop noise and continues the song. No loud beep like some others.

The volume is sufficient for my outdoor needs while on horseback - I've used it with classical music, some country, some folk music and some 80s pop. I can't speak to the bass or thumping noise for hip hop or even heavy metal because that's not my listening preference. But the crispness of a violin, the breathiness of a fast flute and the deep resonance of a solo cello are well rendered and have no fuzziness or distortion. I have used this four times for an hour each time without recharging between uses, but I don't mess with it - I don't pause, skip etc. In all, this the best outdoor Bluetooth speaker I've used and indoors,it's pretty good too.

title: Steps lively for multi-tasking, responsive touchscreen, DVD RW drive, awesome battery ** APRIL 2016 UPDATE ***
review_text:
I've been using a 2009 17.9" Gateway Windows 7 laptop happily all these years until just recently when it began to cough and sputter and generally show signs of wanting to die. I nursed it for several months while shopping for a replacement and suddenly this Toshiba L55T-C/5388 appeared from Vine. Serendipity. I am writing my review from the Toshiba actually rather than my tablet which what I've had to resort to for the past few months - that's a nice change actually. My initial impressions after a week of daily use are pretty good overall with some niggling design complaints for the physical hardware.First - for the record ... I'm not a gamer - just a regular person using my laptop to write articles for the local newspaper now and then, do a lot of email, a lot of online shopping, some social media stuff, watch some videos now and then, sort and store serious quantities of photos and average net surfing. If I want to listen to music, I tend to use Alexa (the Echo) for that rather than my computer and we watch movies on the big television around here - though sometimes I'll use my laptop instead of my tablet for tv shows etc when I'm traveling.

This Toshiba has a very nice high definition screen and I haven't noticed any fuzziness or blurred screen edges etc. The HD video I downloaded from Amazon as a test sample looked as crisp and bright on the laptop as it did on our Samsung 1080p television. The sound clarity is very good for dialogue and background music - the full speaker running across the length of the front of the machine is really good and the volume is quite loud.

title: Easily portable, works from my car's USB outlet
review_text:
After using this little light for a week, I'm pretty impressed with it's overall handiness. It weighs next to nothing, but is still stable when standing on a table or stack of books, mine doesn't wobble or tip over if you lightly bump it. Mine does and I'll probably take this light along the next time we're on a road trip as part of the emergency kit. I received a free sample unit for testing and review.

title: Covers dead spots, multi devices have no slowdown, installation w/directions was trouble-free UPDATE APRIL 2016
review_text:
I am not super "techie" like some of the other folks reviewing this router, just your average housewife who likes gadgets and tries not to drown in the constant wave of weekly tech improvements. As such, I wanted a new router to replace our two year old dual band Belkin with similar speed output, but only a single antenna. The Belkin had a number of dead spots despite using one of those extender things and I had had enough. Enter this TP-Link router.

I was wary of the installation after seeing some other reviews and the difficulties folks have been reporting. However, after reading the box and the instructions fully FIRST and then following the directions exactly, I had no problems. One thing I did notice immediately, is this router is meant to be used with a cable modem and that modem must be powered off before you connect it to this router. I used the website installation method and was up and going in a total of 20 minutes - that is from opening the box to having all our wireless stuff connected to the internet again. The website management page is very detailed and allows for a lot of customization of your network, honestly, more than I need or understand. But changing the router's password and setting our network name was simple and worked on the first try.

After three days of use I like it. The speed is decent and the dual antenna set up has improved the coverage problem we were having with the old Belkin router. I haven't experienced any slowdown or degradation of connectivity with multiple devices going at once thus far. A Fire Phone surfing the net, Fire tablet streaming music, laptop doing email, and a smart tv streaming video all at once in different rooms. So...a good router for every day family use in a pretty typical home.

*********** UPDATE FEBRUARY 2015 ***********
After 90 days this router is trouble free and really working like a champ. Our cable company upgraded our modem and increased our internet speeds recently, requiring a full shutdown and reconnect of my entire network. It was a snap and the router has had no problem with faster connection and the new modem. I relocated everything to the center of our house when everything was being swapped out and the router is now sending a five bar signal out to the back deck, which means I can sit out there with the dogs in nice weather to do email etc.

*****************UPDATE APRIL 2016 *************

I'm still using this router every single day for literally every single WiFi device in our house and it just does its job with zero drama every day. We now have two tablets, two smartphones, three DVR boxes on WiFi, two laptops, a printer, a Fire Stick for streaming movies, a smart tv connected the web now and then, and the Echo that's connected all the time. (yeah, I know...we watch a LOT of television in this house!)

Right this minute I am streaming music on the Echo, recording tv shows on two different DVR boxes, using my laptop to update this review, and uploading 42 photos from my phone to the cloud and pushing email to my tablet. Oh - and I am sitting outside on the patio enjoying the lovely spring day. This router is powerful and I have no dead spots inside or out in the backyard.

title: Fits in your hand, works with Fire Phone, loud volume, can accept & make calls through phone
review_text:
I was very surprised at how powerful this little pod speaker actually is - it really does have a significant amount of volume and can be used in your car if you don't have a blue-tooth enabled system (for example my Mother's 10 year old Suburban out at the ranch) or at the barn when working horses in the round pen or dressage arena. It works via a standard blue-tooth connection or using the NFC option if your smart phone is equipped. There is also a microphone built in and the speaker does in fact, work very well with phone calls - we placed and received two calls using this as a speaker phone and the calls were a tad "tinny", but if you need to speak to someone hands free while cooking a meal or grooming a horse and you don't want a traditional headset, this is an excellent option.

I tested this speaker both inside and outside and it kept the signal from my Amazon Fire Phone almost 60 foot away outside in a direct line of sight with no degradation playing music. Inside the house, it managed to retain a strong signal through a closed door for about 30 feet before it lost the connection and that was far better performance than a no name blue tooth speaker we bought at Hastings in December. Sound quality is pretty good with both classical and country music. Pop can be a bit hollow at upper volume levels and hard rock has reasonable bass sound, but the vocals tend to become somewhat shrill to my ears. This is not a big deal in the least - just turn down the volume and know that at this price range you're buying the idea of portability rather than some super hi tech music snob gizmo.

Connecting this TechMatte Sound Pod to my Amazon Fire phone was super easy & took literally 10 seconds via NFC. It also connected just as easily to a Samsung Galaxy S2 and a Samsung Galaxy Note 1st Generation. My one complaint is that the on/off switch is directly over the charging outlet, so you have to disconnect the charging cable to turn it on or off and then reconnect the cord if you need it to charge or want to power it via the outlet while in use. A minor irritant that is at most worth a half star deduction. Overall, this is a very nice portable speaker that does exactly what it claims to do and fits in the palm of your hand. I did receive a sample speaker to test and review.

title: Adds some bulk, holds securely, easy to carry, buttons all work
review_text:
I got the gold case....think Gold Lame Barbie from 1985 to be more precise. Not ugly, but you definitely won't mistake this case for someone else's generic black folio Kindle HDX case. The case is actually a two piece set. The first part is a simple hard plastic pop out cover that goes over the back of the Fire and offers protection from scratches and bumps etc. It adds no bulk or weight at all. All the cut outs for the power & volume buttons and speakers are precisely placed and don't interfere with operations at all.

The second part is the zip around folio case. You snap the Fire with the first cover into the attachment on the folio. This is surprisingly secure and sturdy. Once it was snapped in, I jiggled and flapped the entire contraption every which way, trying to shake my Fire loose. It never budged or slipped. The folio case opens like a book would and can be folded back sort of like a paperback. There are pushable rubber buttons that reach inside the folio to actually touch your Fire's power & volume buttons, allowing the exterior of the case to remain solid with no holes except the speaker openings. This is a good thing since it's meant to be a travel case. The zipper is a bit stiff ~ something I don't mind, might keep it from coming open in a carry on bag dashing through the airport security etc. It does slide in and out of both my handbag and a carry on size suit case easily and packs well. There are pockets in the front cover for business cards and a loop to put a stylus as well. One thing I do like is the little handle/strap on the outside.

My reason for the one star deduction.... This case does add a bit of bulk to the normally svelte Fire HDX 7" and it doesn't allow for standing up to view videos and it can be hard to pop the Fire out of the folio part if you want to switch cases. Overall, it's not a bad choice and certainly a viable option when traveling ~ I'm writing this review on my Fire HDX sitting in this case at the end of a 4 day trip having used it.

title: Excellent value - good sound & long battery life
review_text:

I have only used these headphones with my Samsung Galaxy Note cell phone so I can't speak about how well they work with a laptop or other brands of phones. I have taken a couple of calls with the headphones and the sound is clear on both ends, so the microphone works fine. Overall....an excellent purchase!

title: Amazing for those with vision trouble!
review_text:
I had decided I did not "need" a Kindle, having tons of other gadgets for all sorts of things. Then I began to lose the vision in one eye and realized over a period of weeks that I could not read normally (or at all some days). Magazines, books, the newspaper.... heck even email was difficult to impossible some days. All my friends have Kindles, so I borrowed one for a day and fell in love. We immediately ordered the Special Offers Wi-Fi Keyboard version. I've had it about 45 days now and my quality of life has seriously improved! I can enlarge the font and change the style of the font depending on my needs at that moment and on really bad days, when my eyes are tired or refusing to focus, the voice function is amazing. The very idea that it reads aloud to me is tremendous and once you adjust to the sometimes robotic pronounciation of some words, it works like a charm. So far, all the books I've purchased have allowed the voice option.

I signed up for Audible.com about two weeks after getting the Kindle and the quality of the audio books on my Kindle is excellent. No robotic voice here - you get the narration exactly as read by the real person - it's an MP3 file I think. Additionally, getting the local newspaper every morning on my Kindle has returned to me my morning tradition of the local editorials & coffee. I do love the number of free books available as well - some are garbage, but most are pretty decent and some have been excellent books. (Loads of Sc-Fi for free too, what's not to love?) I have used the sample option for a ton of books and it's helped me decide to spend the money purchasing a novel, or not. In case you are worried about the Special Offers... they are the screensavers while the Kindle is in sleep mode and NEVER show up in your actual books. I've used a couple of them already now that I think about it.

One last thing - the Kindle in a case, fits into almost all of my handbags and has saved my sanity sitting in doctor's office waiting rooms and at the car repair shop, and I can now sit out under a tree on a pretty day with my horses again while I read a great book. This version of the Kindle will also play my own music while I'm reading. Bottom line is that the Kindle has helped me get a valuable part of my life back and this in turn has allowed me to be more rational while facing possible permanent loss of vision in one eye. Very worthwhile purchase!

title: Works with 6 connections & quite fast once it was connected
review_text:
I am soooo not a techie with regard to setting up fancy networks and having the latest greatest of every gadget out there - let's just get that out in the open. I don't know or even understand most of the jargon for computer stuff, what I do know is from an average person's point of view. My interest in gadgets is centered on fast, easy to use, and reliable so I don't have to do this stuff over and over. I want frustration free or as close to it as possible and I do NOT want to have to contact "support" just to connect, install or use new software or electronic toys. This router came at just the right time, my 3 year old little cheap Belkin router was trying to die. I had been debating on what to replace it with now that we have more than two peripherial gadgets to connect to our wireless network. Priorities were speed, strength of signal accross the entire house, reliable and something that would install easily with minimal cursing & throwing of things.

I had the old router uninstalled and the new Netgear N600 powered up and connected to our high speed internet cable modem and the wired desktop within minutes. I was on the net with the desktop computer with zero trouble at all. Next I connected my Blackberry via the wifi on the phone and it was up and going within seconds - no trouble here either. Third item was the wireless Canon printer.... drama. I tried my laptop and my mother's laptop next....DRAMA. None of them could access the network. I shut the router down and started from scratch. The second time everything connected and the router was seeing each computer, the printer and the Blackberry. However now I had no internet access. (mild cursing had begun)

Third time.... by now almost an hour had gone by. I started from scratch AGAIN. I followed the instructions in the booklet exactly and this time when the router checked in and registered itself, there was a message bar saying there was a "firmware" update available. By now I figured nothing I did was going to make the problem any worse, so I installed the update. Lo and behold! This time the router saw all three computers and the printer and my Blackberry & my mother's Blackberry AND they were all able to access the internet. Now the final test was to reconnect the Wii system to the new router so we can use the Netflix streaming again. Worked like a charm.

Overall impressions of this router after a half day of use (and 90 minutes install time) - It's currently connecting a desktop, one printer, 2 laptops, the Wii and one Blackberry smart phone and all are working smoothly. The speed for downloading Netflix movies seems exactly the same as before, the speed on the laptops is a little faster, and the speed (loading webpages) via the Blackberry is MUCH faster than with our old router. The signal strength is very good - this is a 2600sqft house on a very large lot and I was able to send email from the back deck outside. Our old router could never do that on it's best day!

Final thoughts - this router is worth your time. Just make sure the new firmware update is installed before you add your computers etc to the network and save yourself some time. The speed and signal are very good, so I am willing to forgive the install bugs.

title: Returned it - no sound & box was hot to the touch
review_text:
Ok... I KNOW better than to purchase any electronic gizmo with less than a four star overall rating. I took a chance this time - I was looking for a cheap way to stream video on my television via the computer without having to buy a Roku etc. This converter thing SHOULD have worked fine. I guess, technically it works, but not the way I needed it to and honestly, it's just a HUGE hassle to use on a regular basis.

Pros..... it's small. It does send the video to the television (you do have to tell your computer to send the data to another monitor). It was inexpensive.

Cons.... Our 3 year old tv has all the connections for stuff - USB, S-cable, that 3 prong thing, 3 HDMI outlets and it connects easily & streams Netflix via the Wii game box. It works with the DVD player and I've played DVDs through the laptop in the past with the USB connection, so I KNOW they all work. The ONLY way it would work with this converter box was to use the S-cable and the yellow prong cable AND the USB all at the same time. The picture qualtiy was fine. I tried for 20 minutes to get the sound to transfer through to the television - never happened. Which meant I had to leave the laptop speakers on in order to listen to dialog. Not conducive to sitting several feet away from the screen. Meanwhile there was a huge tangle of all these cables on the tv stand, the laptop, low sound and no ability to pause etc without getting up and going to the computer to do it manually. By the end of a single episode of Frasier (23 minutes) the little converter box was very hot to the touch and the wood underneath it was hot as well. I imagine if you watched a full length movie you might end up scortching the finish on the tv stand or table!

End result.... I'm returning this converter first thing in the morning. I'll just cough up the money and buy the ROKU I guess.

title: Blazing fast, shorter range than expected, works fine though
review_text:
Ok I will be clear - I am NOT a super techie like some of the other folks who are reviewing this router, so I can't explain some of it's fancy gizmos and tricks. What I can do is tell my impressions of this unit from the point of view of your average person who knows a little bit about the techie things and can set up my own wireless network at home. The things that make this router different from the lower priced options out there seem pretty straight forward to me - it's fast and it's secure and you can use it for multiple wi-fi connections in your house. What more can your average family ask for? Well I'll tell you... SIMPLICITY of set up would be on the wish list. Here's what happened the day the new Netgear N750 router arrived.

Out of the box we noticed there was no instruction book. Just a single sheet with basic instructions. Ok, so it's a simple process, simple enough not to need a big book of directions. At first this was true, then things got complicated. It did hook up easily enough and had no drama talking to our cable provider's internet service and the Windows 7 desktop computer saw the router and they communicated very easily.

The Good.....As a test of the range, we used a Blackberry and walked throughout the house and the front & back porches searching for the wi-fi signal. This is a 4000sqft house with two stories on a normal size lot, so when the Blackberry saw the Netgear network and was able to connect to the internet even out in the yard we were delighted! Upstairs, downstairs, in the kitchen, at the opposite end of the house and in the garage we had a solid, strong signal from the router. We then tested the connection with a Roku box, a Wii game system, a netbook computer, a different smartphone scattered all over the house. Every piece of equipment found the network and connected to the internet like they were supposed to. And using the Wii, netbook and Blackberry all at once to load a photo heavy website was amazing - twice as fast as the old, cheap Cisco router and smooth as silk.

The Obnoxious...The next step of course, was to the name the network and do the security block so strangers can't piggyback on it. Especially since it was broadcasting out into the yard and off the porches. And that's where it got complicated and obnoxious. It took two hours to sort out the security settings. The first time we did everything as directed by the software. The end result was a loss of signal from the router everywhere except the room it was physically located in. Multiple subsequent adjustments rendered it useful in three rooms, but no longer were we able to pick it up or access the internet upstairs or on the back porch or even in the far bedroom where the Wii console is located. Not good. The end result was to wipe all the information, reboot the entire computer and router and start over using the lowest security settings. (Can you say frustration?) Once this was done we had a signal and were able to maintain the connection with the Roku, netbook, and smartphones throughout 80% of the house and a weak signal on the porch. The Wii however, cannot hold the signal at the far end of the house which means the router will have to be moved to a more central area of the house.

End result.... The weakened signal issue might not be a big deal or even worth taking a star away from my rating, but I keep coming back to this one thought. The el cheapo, 2 year old, VERY basic "off the shelf at a big box store" router we had been using put out a stronger signal for a third of the price of this Netgear N750. However, the Netgear router IS faster than the old one and there isn't a noticable reduction of speed even when multiple things are connected at the same time. If that's more important to you than overall range, then this is a darn good router for the average home.

title: Love the colors
review_text:
Well, these are certainly interesting!
I often lose my little Roku remote, with it sliding off the bed, then being hard to find under the bed, under cat stuff, etc.

These are silicone covers. If you or your child has ever bought a game controller cover, these are like this.

These are not super easy to get on to the remotes. There are so many button cutouts, it gets caught every step of the way. As a chubby woman, it brought back flashbacks of trying to put on pantyhose too soon after a shower, or on a humid summer day...good luck! 😄

But, I persisted and slowly got it on correctly. It has a textured back to help keep your grip. It does kind of cause the volume button to feel recessed a bit, but that is not a deal breaker. It also includes a wrist strap, but there is no designated punchout for it, so it seems useless to me. The strap is also too small to go over your wrist, so just a pointless addition.

I love the colors though, and it will definitely help me find it on the floor, or amid blankets. The silicone might even help stop my cat from ceremoniously shoving it off his spot by my pillow, but we'll see about thay one.

Overall, I'm pretty happy with these. The only negative side is having to peel it off again if a battery change is needed, but that isn't oftem enough to be a concern.

title: Works just fine. Don't see any big difference from my 50-mile antenna
review_text:
I didn't want to review this until I'd had a chance to use it for a while.

We cut the cord on cable a few years ago, and went to antenna and a smart tv. The antenna I was using had a 50-mile radius. This one makes claims of 180 miles.

I placed it next to my other antenna. I have a very large tree fairly close to the bedroom window, so I do have some difficulty with reception here. We are near the STL broadcast area, so no mountains or forests in our way.

I first tried just switching the antenna connection without a new channel scan. Everything looked exactly the same as with my old antenna. No biggie. It has a nice, long cord, which helps for placement.

The next day, I ran a scan for new channels. I really expected to see some new channels pop up with the additional 130 mile radius. Nope. I have exactly the same channels.

Of course, your experience could vary greatly, depending on your location, topography, big buildings, etc. But I have to say that this 180-mike-radius antenna does nothing at all different from my 50-mile-radius antenna. So, not really better, and definitely not worse.

title: I LOVE this router!  Much stronger than my old Linksys.
review_text:
Okay, I realize that everyone's definition of "easy to set up" comes from a different place. For me, I've worked around computers for over 25 years now, so pretty comfortable, BUT - I am more comfortable with software than hardware. So although this should not have been intimidating, it was a little bit. I formerly was using a Linksys router on our home network. It did a fine job, and was very easy to maintain. However, it didn't give much of a boost to the downstairs connections. The computer was always slow, and would drop the connection from time to time, and require a reboot to get the connection back.

This router is truly great looking. It is white, sleek and has nice blue lights. It sits vertically, rather than horizontally like my old one. I wasn't sure I'd like it, but I do. It comes with three screw-on antennas that can be pointed in any direction to boost your signal in that direction. The metal frame is very sturdy and would take a LOT of pressure to bend. I currently have mine on a separate little shelf because my current desk is too small.

There is only a quick set-up sheet included with this item. Ironically, if you need help, it tells you to go to the company's WEBSITE! Ha! So, if you can't get it to work, go ahead and get online. Yeah, No. But, if you are willing to disconnect and reset up a single-user home network using your old router, it could work! The sheet does give you very plain graphic instructions that tells you which item to plug in where, which many will find very helpful It came with a very short ethernet cord, so you either need to keep the router close to you or buy a longer cord. (The one I had was just purchased last year and was six feet long, so I was in good shape.)

Now, I couldn't get it to connect right away. The short troubleshooter on the insert says to reboot your modem, then to reboot the router. I did. Several times. The computer refused to acknowledge the new router! I was ready to just reconnect my Linksys when I decided to go against all logic and swap the ethernet and modem cords. For many years, computers and peripherals have been fairly color-coded to make it easier for non-tekkies to hook things up. In this case for the TP Link, the ethernet ports (there are four) are yellow and the modem port is blue. I even had previously bought color-coded wires so I didn't accidentally pull the wrong one. After 45 minutes of not being able to connect, I take another look at the back. Everything is in the right spot. But, since I wasn't connecting anyway, I decided to swap out the modem cord and ethernet cord, plugging yellow into the blue slot and the blue cord into the yellow slot. Totally backwards. As you might guess, it took off immediately! So apparently, our unit was either labeled backwards or connected backwards on the inside. Seriously strange. But as long as it works, I don't much care.

The default setting of this router is PUBLIC, so be sure to change your settings to PRIVATE NETWORK, if you don't want everyone in the neighborhood to try and tap into your network. Yes, they would need your password, but there are a lot of smart hackers out there, so you just never know. Better safe than sorry. There are default settings for the account name, network name (your SSID) and passwords, so you will need to change those as soon as you can. (If you forget to write them down, there is a reset button on the back to rol it back to the default passwords.) I also had to change the other settings to WPA2 for our area for the home network. No big deal, just different from before.

The TP Link C9 runs two parallel bands - 2.4Ghz, which is what most home routers use for regular internet access and browsing, and a 5.0 Ghz band, which is for streaming videos and movies. The nice thing about this router, is that if you name BOTH the 2.4 and the 5.0 the same name, it will AUTOMATICALLY switches to the strongest network for your use. I love that! The on/off switch is on the back of the router, so it won't easily get bumped. While my photos show the antennas straight up (we haven't had to move any of them to get a better reception), they rotate and bend towards whatever area you might need a little boost.

Has our reception improved? Yes! The downstairs computer now cruises like it was directly connected to a wired access point. The kids can watch movies and I can browse the net without anyone slowing down. The reception range is fabulous - we live in a multi-unit building, and could probably provide internet connection to all four units. It offers connection speeds of 1.3Gbps over the clearer 5GHz bandwidth and 600Mbps on the 2.4GHz bandwidth. We have not yet found a dead spot in our place - even outside picks up the signal.

In addition to the fabulous signal and great connection speeds, this router can also handle your USB 2.0 and 3.0 devices. There are ports on the side of the router, so you can easily transfer files, photos or data from an external drive to your own computer, or even hook up your printer to print wirelessly. (I haven't tried that yet, but the possibilities are there.)

It also offers a "tether" function for your smartphones. I have not used that, and won't be using that, but it would be great for parents who want to monitor network access/usage from work for their older kids. It is nice to know that option is there.

I am so very pleased with this router! I probably would not have looked at this brand, since I tend to stick with the equipment companies I've had previous success with, but I cannot state enough that this would be an asset to anyone's home network setup.

title: Nice looking, but cheaply made
review_text:
This is my daughter's third MP3 player.
She wanted to try this one, since she loved the look of the design.
We figured how bad can a player be, right?
After seeing hers, my son ordered the same player.

Well, they do play music - for a while.
They also play videos nicely, albeit very small and hard to see.

As of today, with neither one a year old yet, one has had be to be sent back
to Sansa for work (totally locked up and could not even be rebooted). They took a
month to send back a refurb, rather than the one my son sent in with his music on it.

My daughter's lasted a little longer, but does freeze up often.
However, the latest trick is that it has part of the sound going out.
She had purchased four pairs of various headphones trying to get the sound to stop
cutting out, thinking it was the headphone's problem. Nope - turns out, it is the
player. Don't know what is wrong, but one of the stereo sides cuts in and out endlessly.

She'll be shopping for a new one, but it won't be this model anymore.
They are just too cheaply made to last. The technology has been around for a long time now,
and it shouldn't be that hard to make a decent, affordable player.
However, it seems like it might just be too hard for Sansa.

title: Fine for cheap laptops - looks good too.
review_text:
My daughter has used this cooler for almost three years. Yes, it takes a lot of special handling
for it to last that long - it gets tucked back into a laptop case every night.

It is an acrylic base, but not a thick one. It will definitely hold your laptop, but it really needs
to be on a flat surface to work properly. The blue lights look really great. It isn't too noisy,
unless you tip it - then it sounds like something grinding.

My daughter kind of killed hers off from repeatedly using her laptop on an uneven surface.
It caused the fans to stall out or grind, and burned them out. Right now, the cooler only has
one of the three fans working, and doesn't really keep the laptop cool enough.

Top points for looks - the acrylic and the blue lights are great. The price is good for what it is.
Got an expensive laptop? Get a different cooler - look for one that blows heat instead of tries to suck
heat (via the fans) away from the laptop. Try a Belkin. Forget Targus unless you don't mind going deaf while
cruising the internet.

Would I buy it again? Well, I think it would be a great low-cost alternative for a NETbook.
For a laptop, it would really be better to get something that has a stronger air movement capacity.

title: Great radio, but very high battery drain.
review_text:
This radio looks really good wherever you place it. Ours looked exactly as advertised.
The design is not obtrusive, doesn't require a huge footprint, and the buttons are easy to use.

The only DOWNSIDE I found is a major one - the battery consumption is apparently off the charts.
I didn't put cheapie batteries in it either - I got the blue lithium Energizer batteries.
That is the only one we use in our digital cameras due to their ability to last. I take an average of
500 photos a month between my home business and our family and pets, and get at least a month of camera
usage from a set. (I date them all with a Sharpie so I know how long they last.) Even when they are spent
for camera purposes, they still have enough power in them to get our haircutters going, so they are great batteries.

Anyway, I put in a brand new set of the blue lithiums 24 DAYS ago. I had the radio turned on to program it,
but other than that, turned it off until/unless severe storms were in the area. We hadn't had any, so it wasn't
sitting in the "on" position, listening to the regular radio, etc etc.

We had reason to use it this past Saturday, April 24th, when severe storms hit our area. (Part of that huge
system of tornados that hit so many states.) I hadn't thought about it much, even though there were bad
thunderstorms in the area, but there was no warning light on the radio. (It has three small lights on the
left side that light up if there is a watch or warning in your area, and you can turn it on to hear the NWS warning.)
However, suddenly, our town's tornado warning went off! We'd never heard it go off in the 3 yrs we've lived here,
so it was a big deal. We headed downstairs for safety, and I grabbed the radio to take along.
Guess what - dead as a doornail. THREE WEEKS without even being turned on, and the brand new
lithium batteries were DRAINED!!! O-M-G. There ended up being a tornado only a few miles from us that did quite a
bit of damage. I would hate to think what could have happened if I relied on this radio for our only information!!

Once the worst had passed us, I sent my son back upstairs for more batteries. We popped them in and
immediately had the weather warning lights and broadcasts. While that was good, it could have EASILY
been too little too late. I cannot even believe how this thing ate the batteries already that power my digital
camera for a month at a time with constant usage!

There is NO low battery warning light at all, nothing to tell me that it was not working. No beeps, no lights,
nothing but dead air when we needed it the most. If it had been nighttime and we were asleep, who knows what could
have happened! Note to Midland - you NEED a low battery light! Make it blue, so it does not get confused with
any weather warning lights! This is a potentially life-saving product - go the "extra mile" here and provide
a notice of some kind when the power is gone. I never expected the batteries to be drained after about 3 wks without
even using the radio.

If you get this radio, I highly advise keeping it plugged in somewhere. I do not know if the batteries will
continue to drain while it is also plugged in (without being turned on), so I'll revise my review when I
know. I am now on a hunt for the adapter that was supposed to come with it. I do not remember seeing
one in the package. I just got the original box back out this morning to get the adapter, and there's nothing in
there. So, it is possible that the box I got didn't get one put in there. I hadn't planned on plugging it in,
but now see that might be my only real way to get dependable notices. I'll check the radio to see what voltage
the adapter should be, and see if we have an extra one from some other electronic item.

This is the really bad weather season for us (Midwest), and it is very important this radio do its job!
Do NOT rely on the batteries, and keep a spare set of batteries on each floor of your home (if you have an upstairs
or basement, make sure you have some available for flashlights and radios on EACH FLOOR - I had not even thought
about that, but we keep our batteries upstairs, and did not want to go back up during the actual tornado warning!).
I have flashlights tucked every conceivable place in the home (including the bathroom, under the kitchen sink, etc etc), but never really gave a second thought to having extra batteries available per floor until last Saturday when we needed them.
Lesson learned!

S.A.M.E. technology is a must - don't consider any weather radio that doesn't have it, or you'll hear a
lot of stuff that doesn't even pertain to your location. This radio has it. Note though that on this model, you
have to choose the ALERT ON option to ON or you won't get the warning lights. (Odd that it is not a default to on, but it isn't.) You have the choice of a LOT of various types of warnings that will pertain to your area, which is great. You choose which warnings to turn on, except for tornado warnings. This is defaulted to the "on" position, although the manual does not tell you that. I wrote to Midland to ask about it. It took them two weeks to answer me, but they confirmed it was a default setting, which is why it was not included in the storm warning options lists.

In summary - great radio, great look, beyond-poor battery usage.
I've taken off one star for the poor battery life - I've never seen any electronic use them faster.
The lack of a low battery light or beep is a huge mistake for this type of product.
It takes four AA batteries, so be sure to keep a pack of them available on each floor of your home.

I really like the way this thing looks. this subwoofer also complements my sound bar very well.
I have; watched movies, TV and listened to music. all sound superb to me.I highly recommend if you buy any subwoofer you buy a quality subwoofer cable.
I highly recommend buying this subwoofer if you are looking for a good value or "best bang for the buck".

title: Very good tv for the size
review_text:
I would first like to state that i own a Sony and Toshiba LED backlit LCD televisions.
I have never seen the samsung LED DLP screens or the laservue DLP.
I will be making this comparison solely compared to my other LED LCD televisions.
I do not yet own any 3D movies or equipment.

Pros:
PICTURE:number one is the size of this screen, i love it! it is great for HDTV and HD movies. Image is very clear and crisp.it has 120hz witch is much better against motion blur. it has advanced video calibration options. i just went to [...] and used the settings there.
INTERNET TV:I also enjoy the wireless Internet. it has movies and it has news. my favorite feature is the ticker option. you can have a ticker at the bottom of your TV with facebook on it as well as other apps.
SOUND:The 16 speakers surround sound are very amazing! you can calibrate the sound with the microphone provided.
SIZE/WEIGHT: This TV is very light its almost as light as my 46" LED TV. I could easily lift it with another person. i don't think i would have needed another person but its better safe than sorry.

Cons:
POWER-ON/off: During power on it takes a few moments to come on during this time it displays a Mitsubishi start up screen kinda like a computer.it also does this for powering off(shutdown screen like a PC)
PICTURE: overall video is very good but not as good as my LED 120hz Toshiba. it is not as crisp and takes a few moments to fully brighten.Its not as good as my Toshiba for use as a computer monitor using the HDMI inputs.I would say the difference is very minimal.
INTERNET TV: the wireless tv requires you to buy an additional proprietary Mitsubishi AzureWave AW-NU231 Wireless Adapter. It also takes a minute for the internet TV to initially load.you also have to type with the remote control, not very fun.usb ports for the wifi adapter are in bad spots(one on back and one on rear side). they should be on top or directly on the sides. there is one on the side but it is being obstructed by the screen. causing it to loose signal strength. on top would be the ideal spot.
Sound: now that i have had a taste of the surround sound. I notice what it is lacking. A nice sub-woofer. now i gotta buy one because with one it would sound even better.
Heat: this TV makes some heat out of the rear by the lamp area. it might be good for the winter but not very helpful for the summer.

Conclusion: Overall this is a very good product i mainly bought it because they do not make a LED LCD screen in this size for this price.

title: Fits my iPad Pro 9.7 (A1674) perfectly ...
review_text:
An attractive case -- I tested the Rose Gold version -- nicely made with no obvious flaws. I've been trying various types of external keyboards as I like to use my iPad on trips and blog as I go. Having a full keyboard makes life a lot easier.

This is the first integrated case/keyboard I've tried, and so far, I like it. It's easy to set up -- charge it (a cable is provided), pop in the iPad, turn on, pair, and you're set to go.

The backlight is fully adjustable - brightness as well as color. That's a nice touch. Battery life seems to be excellent -- I've used it 2-3 hours every day for the past 10 days, and it's still going strong and it still hasn't indicated I need to recharge it. The keyboard size is a bit smaller than my MacBook Air laptop, but after a few minutes, I got used to the slightly tighter quarters and had no issues at all. Getting it into the case is easy; getting it out of the case takes a little more effort. When I take it along on my trips, I'll leave it in the case for the duration.

My only complaint is that it's quite heavy but given the battery capacity, that's probably not too surprising. So the trade-off is a slightly heavier case with LONG battery life, or a keyboard-only solution with much shorter battery life. I think in the end, I'll appreciate the longer battery life and fully integrated case/keyboard.

I'll continue to use this over the next few months, and plan to take it on my next couple of trips. If all goes well, it will come along on a 131-day world cruise early next year.

title: My first fine-point stylus:  I like it, despite a few issues ...
review_text:
I have mixed feelings about this stylus. Overall, I like it. There are some very good things about it, but it has a few issues.

I'm using this primarily with my iPad Pro, and to a lesser degree with my iPhone 6s. This is my first experience with a fine-point stylus, although I've considered purchasing one for awhile.

First, the pros:
-- I was able to get it charged with no problem
-- Using the included quick start guide, I found my way to the Wacom website to get more details on set-up and apps that I might want to use with my iPad Pro.
-- Found the apps in iTunes App Store and downloaded a few of them to my iPad, got them installed and ready to test.
-- Pairing went smoothly -- no hiccups or issues at all. This was a pleasant surprise, as I've had problems in the past pairing things with the iPad.
-- Was able to get it up and running with both Bamboo Paper as well as Sketches and ibispaint.
-- Nice look and feel -- since it's the size of a fairly standard pen (ball point, gel, retractable, etc.), it feels "natural" in use.
-- Surprisingly long battery life -- I used it almost constantly for 3 hrs, and still had a lot of battery charge left.

Cons:
-- it skips. My iPad doesn't have a screen protector, so the pen is operating on the bare glass. I thought maybe the problem was the glass, so I cleaned it -- twice. Didn't seem to help. It skips in all three apps, and in different parts of the screen each time. Still haven't figured out if it's operator error or problems with the apps or something with the stylus itself. I'll keep playing with it and see if I can find a common denominator cause. When it skips, it's only a short distance -- maybe 1/4" or so -- but it's enough to be annoying.

-- the tip has an annoying tendency to retract during use, especially if I'm using it for writing longhand. In 3 or 4 lines, it has already retracted over halfway. I'm not exerting much pressure on it -- only enough for it to "register" on the screen, so I think it might be the combination of the motion -- writing loops, "twisting" to make some of the letters, etc. -- plus the minimal pressure. What it means is that I have to stop periodically to twist the pen to move the tip "out" again. Otherwise, I end up trying to write with the hard plastic external edge of the tip, which doesn't work that well.

So why the 4-star rating? Despite the issues, I still like this stylus. I'm not a professional artist, but I do like to sketch, to annotate photos, etc. and it really does work nicely for that even with the skipping (I just move the image a bit and try again). If I were a student and I was looking to use this to take longhand notes in class or something, I'd probably drop the rating to 3 stars. But for my use, it's OK. I can work around the issues. So I DO like it.

title: Nearly indestructible, nice length ...
review_text:
I was actually looking for a longer sturdier lightning cable when this showed up. I've been using it for a couple of weeks now, and I'm definitely a fan.

First, it's very solid with reinforced plugs (both ends). I've worn out many lightning cables, and the place where they wear out first is where the cord connects to the plug (especially on the lightning end). That shouldn't be a problem here.

Finally, the length is great. A longer cable gives me more options and some reassurance that at least ONE of the outlets will be close enough with this longer cable to allow me to have the phone handy.

Charging speed is just fine, too - comparable to my Apple-original cables.

Basically, I have no complaints at all. With the quality and durability, this should last a long time. Solid 5 stars from me.

I'm not a heavy or careless user of this kind of stuff -- this was plugged into a connector on my nightstand that also handled a mini-USB cable for my bluetooth speaker, and wasn't moved around at all. I tested it initially with my iPad Pro and my iPhone, but after the initial testing, it was used ONLY for charging my iPhone 6s usually 3 times per week or so. The first 6 weeks, it worked perfectly, and I was thrilled with it. Unfortunately, it started malfunctioning after 6 weeks (lights flashing randomly); after 8 weeks of use, it no longer worked at all. CANNOT recommend. Sorry.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: I've been living with this for about 10 days and I've had a chance to use it with my new-ish iPad Pro 9.7" and iPhone 6S.

So far, no problems at all. Functions just like the original cable except this one is longer and has some extra features -- aluminum housing on both ends is much more "solid" than the plastic and everything is well secured with no manufacturing defects that I could find.

Probably the best part of this cable is the LED light that tells you where your device is in the charging process. Pulsing red means it's charging; flickering green means it's almost done; solid green means it's 100%. The solid green light stays on for awhile (haven't been able to time it precisely as it seems to vary a little from charge to charge -- I'm thinking maybe a couple of hours or so before it goes off; then it stays off unless something "wakes it up" (a notification, a phone call, etc.). I charge the phone on my nightstand and I've had no problem with brightness, but then I sleep like a rock once I get to sleep and it didn't keep me awake, either. Some folks might have a problem, though, because the light is rather bright.

It fits just fine with my Speck case on the iPhone and the MoKo ultra-light case on the iPad.

I actually like this enough that I'll be ordering another one before I make my annual trip back home for the holidays so I can charge both devices at once. It's a nice cable, well made, great length, and I can tell by looking at it whether my device is finished charging.

title: Excellent protection -- but maybe a little too much for light users ...
review_text:
Whether or not you'll like this case depends to a large extent on two things: 1) how much of a klutz you are, and 2) how you use your iPad.

Here's where I fit into that picture: I'm not generally klutzy -- I can count on one hand the number of times I've dropped any of my portable electronics in the past 10 years. I use my iPad mostly when I travel and don't want to bring my laptop, and it stays in my bag unless I'm using it. Otherwise, I bring it out now and again for games or to read (I have the Kindle app installed, and it works great for that). For me, this Otterbox case is probably a case of "overkill": perhaps a little more case than I really need.

The basics:
This is a multi-part case: the two-piece inner plastic "shell" with a clear window over the screen, the outer silicone "slipcover" that hugs the back and sides of the plastic shell, and another hard plastic snap-on outer "cover" that includes a pop-up stand, that snaps onto the back of the silicone cover.

The good:
This will definitely protect your iPad Pro 9.7. The thing is built like body armor -- solid, form-fitting, not too difficult to install. The colors "damson purple" and "hibiscus pink" aren't too garish, either, and match the photos on the page here.

The concern(s): The only screen protection is the thin plastic "screen protector" -- that's all. I'm a little concerned about how protective it would be in an accident. It would have been really nice if they had designed the outer cover/stand to snap onto the FRONT of the case. I've tried it a few times, and it doesn't work. The corner "clips" get caught in the silicone slipcover so that it can't snap securely. It only fits securely onto the BACK of the case. Pity.

Also, it's VERY heavy. I realize that you don't get this level of protection without adding weight, so that's a trade-off that you either choose to live with or not.

Soooo ... bottom line: if you have klutzy tendencies, if you're looking for 5-star protection for your iPad Pro and you're willing to live with added weight, this might be a super option. If you're more like me -- light user, not of the klutzy persuasion -- this might a little more protection than you really need. For me, it rates 3 stars: "It's OK."

title: IMPRESSIVE sound!
review_text:
Holy cow! I was NOT expecting the sound from this little speaker to be as good as it is. I own 3 other Bluetooth speakers, one lower price point, one "moderate"/medium, and another that is comparable in price to this unit. None comes close to the sound quality.

It's really unobtrusive looking, almost drab, slightly "retro" in a gunmetal gray with a darker gray screen. A single button surrounded by a ring on top of the unit controls everything that needs controlling (on/off, volume and skip). A thick rubber base keeps it from sliding around on polished tables (like a nightstand, where I'll be keeping this).

It took just over 3 hrs to fully charge using the included wall charger and cable. I paired it with my iPhone -- nothing tricky there -- and proceeded to play music. I'm a conductor/composer and write mostly music for choirs, so that's what I tend to listen to most of the time. First up: the [[ASIN:B0018NQ066 Britten: War Requiem (2 CDs)]] I'm intimately familiar with this work, having performed it three times and conducted rehearsals for it on one occasion. It's one of my "desert island" recordings. It has a huge variety of "sound" from soft/slim orchestration to full out full orchestra and chorus. The LG performed beautifully. NO distortion, every slight nuance was audible. The recording is a quality recording but I've listened to it on all my other wireless speakers as well as my Bose surround wired speaker set up, and the performance of this small LG speaker is impressive. Seriously exceptional performance.

OK, next up, something completely different: Fleetwood Mac [[ASIN:B00B1MHXY2 Rumours]] -- again, virtually flawless performance. All the "bits" of percussion come through crystal clear. It has a decent bass sound, too -- again something I wasn't expecting from a unit in this price point or of this size.

I've been playing this almost non-stop for over 5 hours and it's showing no signs of low battery. The description here says it runs 9 hrs on a single charge; I'm beginning to believe it. Also, it shuts off after 20 minutes if these is no input (Bluetooth mode). You can also turn it off from your smartphone using the app downloaded from the iOS app store (there's an Android version, too).

This has no built-in microphone, so you can't take phone calls on it. It's just a speaker but a VERY good one.

I really can't find anything wrong with this so far. It's really that good.

It fits beautifully -- lays flat, the key covers are precisely where they should be, there's no slippage or any feeling of insecurity about the cover shifting position. If you've never typed on a keyboard with a cover, it might take a little getting used to. It has a "softer" feel, but key action/etc. is not compromised at all.

Overall, I think this is a good product, a nice gift for someone with a new MacBook, with bult-in usefulness beyond protecting the keyboard from inadvertent spills and dust.

To that end, I've tried and used several different varieties of reusable K-cups, and had finally settled on the Ekobrew cups.

I was offered an opportunity to try this set, and decided to do a side-by-side comparison. The results were interesting. These Brewooze cups perform just as good as the more expensive Ekobrew cups.

I tried several different coffees and several different grinds. As with all reusable cups, you have to be careful how fine/coarse the grind is. Too coarse, and you get weaker coffee; too fine, and you get either overflow and/or sludge. I found that a medium-fine grind worked best for both cup brands. This way, I get the right strength and almost no powdery sludge in the bottom of the cup. One advantage of the Brewooze over the Ekobrew: I was able to use LESS coffee in the cup to get the right brew strength. With the Ekobrew, I needed to fill the cup; with the Brewooze, I filled it about 2/3 full to get the same flavor/strength.

As with all reusable K-cups, you need to take care when you seal them prior to use. These are no trouble to seal correctly -- you can easily see if there are gaps and do an extra "squeeze." Inserting them into the machine takes a bit of attention, too -- otherwise, you can pierce the cup. There are arrows on the lid that show which direction, so that shouldn't be a problem.

This set comes with 20 paper filters plus a replacement charcoal filter for the Keurig filter wand. I didn't see much advantage to the paper filters except possibly ease of cleaning. The coffee was weaker, and using a finer grind didn't seem to help. And it still resulted in some grinds getting "around" the paper filter and onto the mesh, so I still had to clean the cup. It's not a big deal, really -- the cups are easy to rinse clean after use. So I won't be using the paper filters, but you may find them useful.

I'm a little surprised at how nicely these performed, given the price. You get 3 cups (brown, medium tan, and light tan color -- the photo makes them look orange, but they're more of a tan/brown), so if you want to assign a color to different family members, there you go. Since I usually brew 2 cups into a large mug, I just fill 2 of them with the same coffee and run them one after the other in the morning.

kI have to say I was impressed. I didn't expect these to perform as well as they did. Definitely comparable to the Ek​​​​obrew so far -- the only question I have is durability, and only time will tell. I've been using these for about 4 days, and after the initial side-by-side test (when I brewed about 12 cups total), I've been brewing 2-3 cups every morning, rotating them, cleaning after each use, and so far, no signs of any wear problems. If I notice a serious issue, I'll update this review.

title: Super performance for a reasonable cost ...
review_text:
OK, let's get this straight at the beginning: I'm not an audio expert. I don't work in the industry, I haven't studied this stuff, etc. But I DO know what sounds good especially when it comes to classical music recordings. I've been involved in classical music my whole life, I've played and sung with orchestras, so I know how things should sound.

Bottom line: this unit produces very good quality sound over the range of dynamics and timbres that come with a variety of classical music. I have a few recordings that I use as "tests": Carmina Burana (the opening "O Fortuna" section); Bach "Magnificat"; Stravinsky "Firebird"; Mozart piano sonatas; Beethoven String Quartets; and various choral works (Eric Whitacre, Brahms, etc.). I got none of the tinny sound that sometimes happens with piano works; the softer sections of the Eric Whitacre choral works were clear and precise; the range of dynamics in the opening O Fortuna of "Carmina Burana" was crystal clear with no distortion. Really, this outperformed my expectations.

The unit is smaller than I expected, which is a good thing, since I intend to take it along when I travel. It's attractive (I got the orange color), and has a nice "feel" to it. The controls are easy to manipulate on the top of the unit, and I really like the ability to take phone calls via the unit (it has a built-in microphone).

Overall, I'm very pleased with this purchase. I paid less than forty dollars for mine, and at that price, I consider it a super deal. I've had it only for a couple of weeks, so if there are issues with durability, I'll update this review. For now, it's definitely worth 5 stars.

title: Great sound in a little package ....
review_text:
I did a LOT of research before purchasing this little speaker. My needs were pretty simple: I wanted a wireless speaker that could connect with either my iPhone or iPad to use on the nightstand. I like to play music before I go to sleep, so it needed to be small, but have great sound.

Based on the reviews here, I finally decided on this one, and I'm happy to say it's PERFECT!

It charged quickly connected to my MacBook Pro -- about 2 hrs, maybe a little less. Turned it on, turned on the iPhone, went to the "Settings" on the phone, found Bluetooth, and there was the JAM XT. Selected it, and voila! they paired. Entire set-up took about 10 seconds.

I listen to a lot of classical music, so my first "test" was the Brahms "A German Requiem" -- lots of highs, lows, soft, loud, etc. Strings, voices, woodwinds, brass -- it's all in there. I listened carefully for distortion -- everything was set on "medium" volume -- and I'm happy to say I heard NO distortion at all. Everything sounded great -- nearly as good as my Bose system, but without the bass resonance.

OK, so I haven't had this very long (about a week), so its durability remains to be seen. But I'm impressed with the quality and style of this. If I notice any issues, I'll update this review.

Meanwhile, I can now fall asleep to great sounding music from a small-footprint speaker. And that's exactly what I wanted.
