title: TERRIBLE instruction booklet ...
review_text:
I like the basic design of this -- the small sleek size, nice layout of buttons, large display. The radio reception seems to be decent, although mounting it on the wall is not possible in my area, since I have to turn it various directions to get a couple of local AM stations. Weather band reception is OK, as is FM reception.

That's about where my positive feelings for this little radio end.

It is way too difficult to set up, NOT with regard to the physical aspects of hitting the correct buttons in the correct sequence, but rather in terms of deciphering and understanding the instructions. The instruction leaflet, such as it is, is written in such small type that it's nearly impossible to read. I finally went to the Eton website and downloaded the instruction manual there, then "zoom"ed it so I could read how to set the time, store radio stations, etc.

Then there's the issue of the S.A.M.E. codes. I had never heard of this technology before I got this radio. NO WHERE in the included instructions is there any mention of NOAA, or even the "S.A.M.E." designation. On the Amazon product page, there is a mention of "S.A.M.E." in one of the product features bullets, and "NOAA" in another product feature bullet on the product page here on Amazon, but nothing that explains what "S.A.M.E. codes" actually ARE. The instruction manual tells you how to "Select the county" -- OK, so what does THAT mean? The instructions don't tell you that "Select the county" really means "enter the NOAA S.A.M.E. codes." You're not "selecting" anything; you need to know the S.A.M.E. code(s) for the desired area(s), and then ENTER those according to the instructions.

This was my first weather radio -- and I'm generally fairly good at figuring things out -- but this had me confused for a good 15-20 minutes while I searched via google for "county code," "weather county code," etc. Finally found the NOAA site and the codes, and entered the one for my county.

And I STILL don't know what "Setting Defeat" means. I mean, I know how to set it, and I can read what the manual says, but it doesn't really tell me WHY I might want to enable or disable "defeat," and what, precisely, it enables or disables ("ENABLE: Alert when receiving a message. DISABLE: Displays the message on the LCD when receiving a message" -- does that mean that when it's enabled, you DON'T get a message displayed on the LCD when receiving a message? What kind of Alert happens when it's enabled? the flashing light? the siren? what, precisely, am I "defeating" with this??)

I have no idea if the weather alert part of the radio works. We've had one National Weather Service-issued high wind warning here in the Pacific NW since I received and programmed the radio, and it didn't set off the alert -- no light flashing, no "message," nothing. I intend to take this along on an extended road trip this summer (reprogramming the S.A.M.E. codes along the route), and I figure I'll probably encounter some sort of "alert-able" weather event along the way. I'll update this review then if that part works.

Meanwhile, I'm giving this 2 stars -- it works pretty well as a compact "clock radio," doesn't take up a lot of space, and has decent reception. But Eton REALLY needs to do something about the instructions. The ones included with the product are useless, and the copy on the website isn't much better.

On the Amazon product page, there is a mention of "S.A.M.E." in one of the product features bullets, and "NOAA" in another product feature bullet on the product page here on Amazon, but nothing that explains what "S.A.M.E. codes" actually ARE. The instruction manual tells you how to "Select the county" -- OK, so what does THAT mean? The instructions don't tell you that "Select the county" really means "enter the NOAA S.A.M.E. codes." You're not "selecting" anything; you need to know the S.A.M.E. code(s) for the desired area(s), and then ENTER those according to the instructions.

This was my first weather radio -- and I'm generally fairly good at figuring things out -- but this had me confused for a good 15-20 minutes while I searched via google for "county code," "weather county code," etc. Finally found the NOAA site and the codes, and entered the one for my county.

And I STILL don't know what "Setting Defeat" means. I mean, I know how to set it, and I can read what the manual says, but it doesn't really tell me WHY I might want to enable or disable "defeat," and what, precisely, it enables or disables ("ENABLE: Alert when receiving a message. I have no idea if the weather alert part of the radio works. I intend to take this along on an extended road trip this summer (reprogramming the S.A.M.E. codes along the route), and I figure I'll probably encounter some sort of "alert-able" weather event along the way. I'll update this review then if that part works.

Meanwhile, I'm giving this 2 stars -- it works pretty well as a compact "clock radio," doesn't take up a lot of space, and has decent reception. But Eton REALLY needs to do something about the instructions. The ones included with the product are useless, and the copy on the website isn't much better.

title: I *LOVE* this camera!
review_text:
I'm just an amateur when it comes to photography. All I really want is an easy-to-use point-and-shoot camera that I can take on vacations to snap shots of places I find interesting, to use around the house to take photos of valuables for insurance purposes, etc. In other words, my expectations are pretty minimal.
That said, I'm extremely happy with the Kodak DC3400. This is my second Kodak digital (my first was a DC240), so obviously I'm pleased with the Kodak product line.
After unpacking the DC3400, I spent about 10 minutes getting it set up, and proceeded to take a few pictures. Another 10 minutes or so, and I had the photo software loaded on my laptop. Connect the USB cable, and I was able to load the photos onto the laptop immediately. The camera shows up as an icon, like a disk drive, which you can double-click to open and transfer the pictures to a folder on your hard drive -- piece of cake!
The quality of the pictures is amazing. I use the Ofoto service, and had some prints of some of my digital photos sent to my mother. According to her, you could not tell the difference between the digital images and those taken with a 35mm film camera. The colors were vivid, the images sharp -- just what you'd expect from the Kodak name.
I'll agree with most everyone else and say that batteries might be the only downside to this camera. It's definitely worth the investment to get the Kodak NiMh rechargables and the charger. The ONLY time I use NiCads is when I'm my NiMh set is in the recharger, and I need to snap a few pictures.
For the money, I don't think you can top this camera in terms of features, quality, and ease of use.

title: The Best 32-Inch TV Available
review_text:
If you want 4K in a 32-inch TV, this is the one to buy. Even if you don't want 4K capability in your 32-inch TV, this is still the one to buy. It's the best 32-inch I've ever had or seen, and it's also superior to Sony's other 32-inch TV, which is only offering 720p max.

I had to deduct a star because of the included remote control. This TV has Google TV with Google Voice Assistant, where you press the microphone button on a remote control and then Google will control the TV for you, including turning it off, and also answer all of your other Google inquiries. However, and astonishingly, Sony doesn't include the remote control that has the microphone built in. Without this, the Google Assistant is inaccessible and thus useless. So, if you want that convenience, and you do want it, you have to buy a separate Sony remote control for $65.

The picture quality is excellent once you remove the factory default picture settings. I highly recommend anyone wanting good brightness for this TV to turn off the light sensor. With the light sensor on, the TV won't get as bright as a lot of people like.

The Vivid setting is nice, and it doesn't oversaturate the picture the way some other TV's Vivid setting does.

The operating system in the TV is fast. Sound is okay, but of course, not as great as some of Sony's larger TVs that push the sound out from all over the screen, as opposed to small speakers at the bottom like this TV has. Of course, you can easily add an external speaker, if desired.

Viewing angles are not nearly as good as Sony's larger 4K 2022 models, but it doesn't bother me since I am almost always just watching the TV straight on.

The price is higher than a lot of inferior 32-inch TVs, but again, the Sony technology offered, along with it capable of 4K, justifies the higher price, in my opinion.

There is a lot to like about this monitor. It's easily height adjustable, it can pivot, the angle can be tilted up and down, it has built-in speakers (I am using a Bose Solo 5 soundbar instead of the built-in speakers), the side and top bezels are not too wide, and the picture quality is very good, with a lot of picture configuration options. I watch TV broadcast and cable channels, movies, and TV shows via my computer, so I wanted a larger high quality-picture monitor with a higher DPI capability. The monitor is very heavy...much heavier in weight than I expected. Attaching the stand is really easy. Detaching the stand is also very easy. Build quality of this monitor seems good. Assuming this just-released monitor stays working perfectly for a long time, LG did an excellent job and I am glad I bought it.

title: I Had High Hopes, But the Darbee Disappointed Me
review_text:
I expected so much better of a quality picture per the claims made and because of the very high price.

I have an excellent computer with HDMI output directly connected to an excellent 2017 model 1080p LED HDTV. The computer is used to stream live HDTV channels and either 720p or 1080p downloaded movies and TV show episodes, etc. (The computer puts out a resolution of 1920 x 1080 at 60 Hz, of course.)

The Darbee default setting out of the box is HiDef 100. The picture was not good at all at 100. (And I just found a video review online where the reviewer said he also could not tolerate 100 and had to turn it down to close to where I did.) I turned down the number to 75 and that helped. But the overall difference between Darbee on and off is very small at the 75 setting, and hard to like when I think about the fact it costs $200. And in fact, often the Darbee turned on was worse in the sense it accentuated flaws in the picture, especially in low light scenes.

Yes, I experimented with all 3 modes, and multiple number settings.

I am sure there are specific uses and set-ups of the Darbee where the difference in picture quality is high. But again, in my case the Darbee failed to impress me, and I cannot recommend this if your set up is like mine: computer to TV.

The Darbee is a great concept, and it is very easy to set up and use. But at $200, the value just isn't there compared with the end result I got.

title: Horrible Reception in the Same Location Where Other Antennas Can Pick Up the Signals
review_text:
My high hopes for this antenna were quickly dashed.

I am 43 miles away from the broadcast towers. I currently use the Marathon antenna (I use it indoors). The Marathon picks up all the major network channels perfectly except occasionally 1, and all the independent stations perfectly except occasionally 1. (It will pick up those 2 stations, but there is sometimes annoying pixelation and signal drops.)

So, after I read how this brand new Mohu Leaf Glide 65 Mile Range antenna was supposed to be so wonderful, I bought it, hoping I could get all the stations in perfectly.

It's awful! Placed exactly where the Marathon was placed the Leaf Glide cannot even come close to picking up as many stations. And yes, I made sure the amplifier was plugged in. And it is getting power. (It also could not pick up stations that cheaper/inferior antennas could.)

I moved the Leaf Glide to different spots, but no matter where I placed it it could not pick up stations that it should have been able to pick up. It picked up some stations, so I know the amp was working. I unplugged the amp and those stations were gone, so I know it is not a defective amp.

I know that when it comes to antennas people's results will vary. But for this $89 (current price) supposedly "new technology" antenna to fail so badly is a huge disappointment.

There is no doubt that this antenna will work perfectly for many people, if they are lucky when it comes to distance, terrain, height, interference, etc.

You would think in today's world of big technology there would be a way to broadcast signals that everyone can receive successfully.

My guess is that this antenna would only pull in 65 miles away if one had it outdoors, high up, and with clear line to the towers.

(I am in no way affiliated with the company that makes the Marathon. I am just a cord cutter trying to get all the stations received perfectly. If the Leaf Glide had worked I would have been so happy, and would have gladly done away with the Marathon since it is quite big and not the most attractive. The Leaf Glide is paper thin and not anything that would be something you would not wanna look at.)

The Leaf Glide is very easy to place. I appreciate that they included two easy ways to hang it: Either with white or black push pins or with velcro sticky dots.

If you get all the stations with this antenna you will love it.

title: Has The Potential To Be Great But Not Great Yet

A lot of things to love, and some things to dislike.

For the price they are charging for this pretty simple cheap-feeling box, their app for watching TV on Windows and Mac computers should be so much better. Also, once you click on the channel, you can only see a few hours of what's on later, instead of an entire day or more.

If you have an Apple TV 4, there is a $25 app for the Apple TV 4 called Channels which has a much better TV guide (and it allows one to pause live TV), but I can see where people might be unhappy they have to spend any money at all to use their HDHomeRun on an Apple TV. (In other words, perhaps Silicon Dust should offer their own free app for the Apple TV 4 for folks who do not want or need to pausing of live TV capability.)

So, if SiliconDust eventually truly improves the Windows and Mac software that lets you watch your OTA TV signals from the HDHomeRun box, this product would be 5 Stars, in my opinion.

The Windows and Mac computers I watch the TV on from the HDHomeRun are Ethernet connected and not Wireless, and thus the picture quality is excellent.

title: Another Love-Hate Relationship
review_text:
Amazon 1 Star Rating equals to "I Hate It" ... and I do have hatred for aspects of the Bolt, even though I also have love for it.

(Please keep in mind I have owned many different DVR's, such as the Moxi, ReplayTV, and Channel Master DVR+.)

I Hate:

TiVo wants a fee of $600 for a lifetime license, after you pay $300 or $400 for your Bolt. This is insanity! I could understand if they were asking for $600 for the lifetime of the person, no matter what TiVo boxes they swap out in the future.

The design of the box is terrible, in my opinion. I really hate it. (And please do not say they did it only to allow air to escape, because air can escape just fine on their Roamios and on other DVR's such as the Moxi.)

Final thing I hate is the difficulty prying the box apart to swap out the hard drive after the screws are removed. TiVo knows one's hard drive will fail eventually after the warranty, and/or that people will wanna upgrade to a larger capacity drive. They could have easily designed this box with a removable cover just under the drive, instead of making it where you have to take the whole cover off in parts.

Love:

Hands down, the TiVo interface and extra features of the Bolt are superior to any other DVR out there as of this writing. Once you have the opportunity to use Commercial Skip, you'll fall in love. Also, the Quick Mode feature is very nice, and it works well. The speed of the Bolt interface is excellent.

The TiVo software is really easy to use. The Bolt is easy to get set up. I like that if you have to swap out your hard drive, the TiVo software will automatically install itself on the bare new drive.

I like the online and mobile interfaces which allow you to set recordings remotely.

There are countless people online who feel that TiVo's $15 per month (or $150 per year) fee is too expensive ... and of course if you are paying it, you will wish the fee was a more reasonable $10 per month/$100 per year.

I am hoping TiVo has heard the endless complaints of folks who hate the Bolt's box design and who want a flat box. It will be interesting to see if they do a redesign of their next DVR model. And I'm hoping they come out with a TiVo Bolt OTA for cable cutters where the lifetime license fee will be far more reasonably priced than the Bolt's astronomical $600.

title: Positives & Negatives
review_text:
I bought my pair of Bluez 2S directly from AfterShokz company, and not via Amazon. Just like with so many things there are aspects to like and aspects to not like.

I will start with the negatives. If you are in a noisy environment, such as working out in an exercise room, the volume just is not loud enough or satisfactory at all. You need earplugs in the ears to get the satisfactory volume. Yes, earplugs. Of course, that defeats the whole purpose of buying headphones that do not go inside or cover your ears.

You can test this out by simply putting a finger in each ear and then you'll hear the remarkable level of volume change.

Because of the lack of loudness one can achieve in a noisy environment, I cannot recommend these (unless you want to buy earplugs and wear them at the same time).

The only other negative for me personally is the lack of a way to go back to a previous song, or repeat the currently playing song. (You can skip forward to the next song, but you cannot go back.)

The positives: These are comfortable to wear and very lightweight. The Bluez 2S offers the ability for decent call quality when using them to make calls. Microphones seem good (I have only tried this indoors, and not outdoors, so I cannot comment further on this particular subject.)

The Bluez 2S are very easy to operate.

In a quiet environment, volume is fine, and music quality is acceptable for this price point. (Of course you will not get the level of music quality or bass you'd get with a more expensive name brand headphones that go directly over the ear.)

So, for specific purposes such as cell phone calls where you want to keep both ears free, these are quite good indeed, offering good voice quality for both parties. (Pairing with my iPhone 5 and 6S went flawlessly.)

title: This Solved My Specific Problem
review_text:
I bought one of those very small ASUS VivoMini UN62-M037M computers. It has an HDMI out port to connect to either a monitor or your nice HD TV. (I have mine connected to my TV.) I am running Windows 8.1 on the computer.

Microsoft has acknowledged that there is a bug in Windows 8 and 8.1: When you turn off your TV but leave your computer on, the OS will always give you an Out of Memory error message. There is no software fix whatsoever. Many people are complaining of this issue on boards over at Intel and other places.

The only fix is to either never ever turn off your TV, or always turn off your computer when you turn off your TV, or fool the computer into thinking there is that HDMI monitor connected even when said monitor is powered off.

I bought this ConnectPRO for just this purpose...and it works.

Out of the box I did not get a green light, per the instructions. The light was orange, which implies it had a memorized EDID from the factory.

I reset the box and cloned the EDID from my TV.

I can now leave my computer on always if I desire and turn off my TV at any time, and no more problems.

Sad that Microsoft never offered their own software fix via an update, in spite of the fact they confirm the issue, which forced me to have to spend an extra $70.

title: Great Value For the Price. Great High Def Picture Via HDMI To Your HDTV.
review_text:
First I want to say that the first box I received did not work correctly immediately. The box kept failing to maintain recognition that my external drives were in fact present, no matter how many different types I used. There was surely something wrong with the ViewTV. (The ViewTV I received had software version installed from last month.)

I called the ViewTV company and they were really great. The nice tech support guy agreed I had to have something wrong with the unit...and he rushed me out a replacement. The replacement works much better...and interestingly its software version is dated 7 months ago.

I think the ViewTV at $50 is really a great value. (And I was impressed with the customer service the company provided.)

Running the antenna channel scan is relatively fast. The picture quality on my replacement box is stellar. Moving through all the settings menus is very easy and straightforward. Everything is easy to figure out.

When you think about the box's limitations, as pointed out by some very helpful reviews here, you must keep in mind the very reasonable price.

For $50 you get a good over the air box with a good tuner that sends a great picture via HDMI to your TV. You can time shift your viewing, if you plug in a drive to the USB port, and you can record programs to said drive.

For $50 you cannot expect multiple tuners or a great TV Guide. But at least you get to see the very basic guide info the broadcasters send down with their OTA signal. (My two HDTV's on their own do not show the OTA program info, which is very disappointing.)

For cable cutters out there on a budget, this box is definitely something you should consider. It delivers really well exactly what it promises.

title: Vizio Is Closer With This Model, But Still Far Away From Being Able To Satisfy Without The Need For A Separate Bass Speaker
review_text:
I got mine for $248 plus sales tax with the immediate $50 reduction in price if one has Amazon Prime. I think that is a fair price for this Soundbar.

There is a lot to like about this Soundbar. You will love its easy ability to program in your TV's remote control, or any IR remote, to control the volume and mute. Very convenient.

The volume on the Soundbar can get plenty loud. The sound is quite clear.

Vizio includes all possible cables you might need.

The Soundbar is heavy and appears solidly built.

Programming features via the Vizio remote are very nice and easy to understand and figure out.

The negative: I applaud Vizio for trying to include bass speakers into the Soundbar so you won't need a separate bass speaker, but sadly they have failed. I did lots of testing on various TV feeds, from Music Choice stations to movies to local newscasts to regular network TV shows. I did adjustments to the bass via the remote on all TV feeds. The bass level is not there yet to satisfy.

I plugged in an 8" Energy brand powered bass speaker (this is not a large bass speaker), and let me tell you the difference is remarkable with all the TV feeds.

I will strongly suggest that if you consider buying this Soundbar you accept that for the most satisfying sound you really need and should have an external bass speaker. You will not be sorry at all.

One day a company might be able to invent a Soundbar with built-in bass speakers that truly deliver. Vizio has not succeeded with this model. But again, excluding the bass aspect, the rest of the Soundbar does deliver the quality.

title: Warning About The Warranty
review_text:
First, a warning for you about the warranty. This Speaker Tower is very, very heavy. Should it break during the one-year warranty, as expected you will have to pay to ship it to Pyle. (I am OK with this.) But along with the item you must include a $50 money order to pay Pyle Audio to send the item back to you.

Most companies work by you pay to ship the broken item to them, they pay to ship the fixed item back to you under the warranty period.

OK, now to the product review:

Overall, I am disappointed with the quality of the audio and I do not recommend this item to people who want the best audio quality and I would not ever purchase it again.

If anyone out there paid even close to the full retail list price of $433.99, you have my sympathy.

This tower does have some positives. The ability to play either FM radio, an iOS device, or other music source (you will need a 3.5mm to dual RCA male cable if wanting to play directly from the headphone jack of an MP3 player, etc.). It would have been nice if they had included a 3.5mm input jack as well, especially at this price.

Some songs sound pretty good, but others sound muffled or muddy. Not crystal clear like you would expect at this weight and price, and from Pyle Audio. If you compare your songs through this tower and then through the $300+ Dr. Dre Original Model Beatbox as one wild example, you will hear the difference in clarity and quality from the speakers immediately.

But again, some songs do sound quite decent, and with that I can see why some give this tower a great review. But if you are like me and you want and recognize the best quality sound, you might be disappointed with this tower.

The instruction manual is very disappointing, as well. I, and most can figure things out eventually, but there will be some folks who might need to ask for help.

The FM antenna is a small hard wired wire. You cannot add your own antenna.

I got the black matte model, and it does look nice in the room.

I think this deserves 3 stars because I think there are some people who will enjoy this tower and its features and its small footprint and its look for the $171 price.

title: I could hear no discernible difference in sound quality
review_text:
I use a $100 external sound card when DJ'ing because I want better sound than what the built-in laptop sound card offers. I notice a big difference.

I then was doing more research and read how the makers of these way more expensive USB cables claim they offer superior sound. So, I took the plunge and spent $50 for this Pangea Audio solid silver USB cable.

I seriously could not hear any difference between this USB cable and the $10 short USB cable I was using. For $50, I expected a perceptible difference, even if it was just a small difference.

I had others also judge...and they agreed with me.

From looking at and holding the cable, it does indeed come across as a quality cable. But again, I heard no difference in the sound...and I tested it with different genres of songs.

I would not recommend this cable. If you indeed have a great (and expensive) external sound card or a great DAC, my guess is you do not need to buy one of these $50 (or even more expensive) USB cables.

I give the cable 5 stars for build quality and 1 star for its inability to cause the sound from your laptop to either an external sound card or DAC to be noticeably improved. (So, I averaged it out to 3 stars.)

(I have not tested the much more expensive than this one USB cables, so maybe those do produce a perceptible difference?)

title: At a total cost of $116, worth every dollar...and I wish I could get more

So, keep in mind that my review is for the $116 Touchpad and not the originally priced Touchpad.

My Touchpad is wonderful. The best part is the Web Browser that can access ALL of the Web. My biggest frustration with the iPad is that it cannot access ALL of the Web. And I visit lots of sites that use Flash programming in the site. I need Flash as long as those sites continue to utilize it.

Once the Touchpad arrived, I did the system updates and all is great.

The WiFi connects perfectly.

Touch response is nice.

I am very happy I got one at that price and will use it a lot. If anyone can get this Touchpad for that price, I feel it is a must-purchase for anyone who wants full-Web access.

title: It's All About The Price
review_text:
I own the Archos 70 Internet Tablet with Android 2.2 Froyo installed.

I am going to start by listing the three things I hate about this tablet.

1. It only has 256 megabytes of RAM. It really should have 512 megabytes of RAM. (And I would have paid a little more to get twice the RAM.)

2. It does not come with the Android Marketplace App or Google Apps pre-installed. (So, with each update, you have to rely on others to create the Google Apps .apk that you can hunt down and manually install. I did it, of course, but it is a little pain in the butt. And, not all the apps show up in the Marketplace.)

3. It is a fingerprint magnet like you wouldn't believe. The bezel around the screen absorbs oil from your skin like crazy. Keep a wiping cloth handy at all times.

OK, now to the good. I paid just over $250 for this tablet direct from Archos, and at that price, I am satisfied where I give the device 4 out of 5 stars. I like the size and weight (as I found the iPad to be too heavy when holding it for a long time). Battery life is good. The screen is excellent for Internet, email, and video.

Android 2.2 Froyo runs well on my tablet, and I am happy to have Adobe Flash (although not every single Flash Website works...and if you encounter a chat box that runs on Flash, like Chatango, the keyboard does not respond, you cannot chat).

Bottom line: If you want a very good and reasonably-priced 7" WiFi-only tablet right now, the Archos 70 is the one to get. (If you don't need one right now, it is expected there will be many more tablets offered in 2011...and they will have more RAM and a more powerful processor. And yes, I know, they will be more expensive.)

title: A Lot To Like With The Vizio
review_text:
First, let me say I own the 47" LG 47LE8500 for my living room with its stunning high def picture and extremely poor speakers. I was looking for a slightly smaller (and less expensive) TV for my bedroom and chose this 42" Vizio. Vizio has a similar 47" model under this newly released line. (So far, I am mostly happy with my purchase.)

Both the LG and Vizio have LED LCD with Local Dimming. I have to say that the high def picture on the Vizio is not as stunning as on the LG 47LE8500, but it is close, and still satisfying.

The black levels are better on the LG, but pretty close on the Vizio.

The Vizio arrived with one of the round rubber "feet" missing under the base. (Better quality control and inspection please?)

The WiFi on the Vizio is fabulous. The remote having a qwerty keyboard is fabulous.

First thing I had to do (for personal preference) is turn off the room light sensor. The picture was way too dark for me when the light sensor was on.

Also, the default screen brightness setting with the light sensor off is too bright, in my opinion. The brightness level is at 50 by default on the standard pic setting, and it looks brighter than the 50 setting on other sets. (But it is very easy to adjust, of course.)

The speakers on the Vizio are much better than on the LG.

I dislike that the Vizio does not have a swivel base.

Standard def is quite acceptable (and better than on the LG).

So, bottom line: If you want to save some money, this new Vizio line is a very good choice (and recommended). Once you customize the pic settings, I think you will be happy with the high def picture. If you have extra money to burn, the LG will give you a more stunning high def picture with better black levels, but you probably will dislike the LG's speakers, especially if you listen to a lot of music with the volume raised.

Adding to my review, August 28:

When the TV is off, the Vizio logo at the front is lit up in orange. I have found no way to turn this off. I hope that if enough people complain, perhaps Vizio will release a software update that will allow the turn off of this orange Vizio light.

I have encountered bad lip sync issues. But luckily, Vizio has included in the Audio settings a Lip Sync adjustment setting. I had to enable this setting, as the lip sync mismatch problem was really bad. The adjustment has helped.

review_text:
I love the Kindle.

I have noticed different comments that I would like to address. In the Amazon store, you can turn off the one click option. I never use one click as it is easy to make a mistake.. You can also delete pre installed apps by holding your finger on the app until a sign comes up with an option to remove from the device.

PdF files are a joy to read on the FIRE. Just get the EZ PRO PDF Reader app for $1.00. Get the free Gallery app to view pictures. It's fabulous. The Cloud works great so far as I can tell.

At first, the touch screen seems erratic, but if one persists, one will find how to get the system to do what one wants.

The only thing I can't find out is when one should shut it down and when put it to sleep.

I think the colors are fabulous, the browser is lightening fast and personally, I wouldn't want a bigger tablet as this is heavy enough. It is just the right size for me..

As with computers, there are frustrations from time to time, but there are solutions. I suggest. Just keep trying.

title: The form fitting is perfect and while I do feel my phone is highly ...
review_text:
The form fitting is perfect and while I do feel my phone is highly protected, the case doesn't make the phone too large to handle or carry around (as you are aware the iPhone 6 + is already pretty big). While I like the idea of being able to change the back plate to different colors, I always stick with the black one. It's not a feature that I care much about personally, although it is neat. The case looks pretty mean overall and I love showing it off (as with most NewTrent products).

As always the screen protector is great and feels very similar to the actual glass screen and does not distort color or text. The buttons for sound are perfect, they depress smoothly and function the changing of the volume 100% of the time.

The covers for the charger, headphones and volume are difficult to open though. While I do appreciate the fact they are great to offer resistance to water and dust, etc. I do feel they could be a bit easier to open. They feel quite stiff and can be difficult to open (perhaps the tabs can be 'improved'). Another and more serious gripe I have is the inability to reach the vibrate/silent switch when it's cover is open. I have a very hard time reaching in there to toggle the switch because the cutout is too small.

The sound quality is good and I have no complaints there.

My phone has survived two nasty drops without a scratch.

If you want a case that offers top notch protection and looks great too - look no further!

This seems to be a very bad PSU and I will be returning it. I took a gamble on this brand and I wish I wouldn't have.

title: AMAZING customer service
review_text:
UPDATE 22 August 2019:
The customer service team with GoScope contacted me soon after I left my original three star review (below) to explain to me that I had received a *newer* version of the customized case for Sony A6400 mirrorless camera. The newer version, they said, is engineered to not require the foam insert for the lid that I had been expecting. To demonstrate their concern and good faith, however, GoScope said they would send me a foam insert (with 3M adhesive) from the "old style" case, but ALSO a copy of the older case so I could use whichever one I prefer! Folks, you can't do customer service much better than that. In my original review I said that the case is well made and rugged. My problem with it has been fixed --in a friendly, helpful, and timely manner. So....Five Stars.
_____________________
When I first looked at this item I could have sworn that the photo illustrations showed a foam insert in the "lid" --the part that closes over the top of the camera. I looked at the Bergsma video on Youtube (see my screen capture from that video and another), and sure enough, there was a foam insert in those videos as well. The case that I received did not have one; I don't know if I got a used case or a dud from the factory. When I looked at the case on Amazon again just now, the photos look as if the foam insert has been blacked or blurred out. The case is well made, but no foam in the lid obviously reduces the drop or vibration security of my A6400. The $45 price tag seems steep if that's the new normal. The insides of the case are molded to cradle an A6400, of course, so the camera won't be rattling around, but now I think the Bergsma video might be misleading. As it is, I don't think I could drop my $900 camera body and $500 lens in this case and expect them to survive the fall. Anything to say about this, GoScope?

UPDATE August 24, 2018: The Seller of this mouse contacted me almost immediately upon seeing my August 17th update with an offer to replace the defective mouse with a battery-powered version (2 - AAA batteries). I received the mouse yesterday and it has been performing very well. The scrolling wheel and pointer are working fine, as one would expect. But I am most impressed with the Seller's eagerness to make things right. Thank you!

UPDATE August 17, 2018: This mouse died this morning. The pointer just wouldn't appear on my desktop. CANNOT recommend this mouse; I like the design, but the scrolling wheel never worked properly, re-charges never lasted more than a few days, and now this. Don't waste your money.

UPDATE June 13, 2018: The scrolling wheel on this mouse has been balky since almost the beginning. I've tried several mouse settings in Windows 10 and haven't been able to remedy the problem. If you've ever driven a vehicle in which there was a lot of "play" in the steering wheel --meaning you turn it quite a bit before it begins to catch and actually steer the car-- you can get an idea of how scrolling wheel feels on this mouse. Computers are never fast enough for me, and wheeling away to scroll down a few lines can get really annoying. Might just be a defective unit.

My (much) larger ANKER vertical mouse died, so I had to replace it. 7Lucky mouse is smaller and fits my hand much better! I've been using it all day and haven't had a bit of wrist pain. I LOVE THIS MOUSE.

title: Probably very nice --if you can get it working.
review_text:
I sure was excited to get this to replace my two year-old, suddenly intermittent Tenda router. The reviews were positively glowing on both Amazon and Best Buy. After a full day of trying to get it up and running --including a three-hour phone call to Linksys tech support, I got it working. Fifteen minutes later, it stopped working altogether. The system said I had wifi connected, but it would not load any content in any browser. Customer service was helpful and knowledgeable, but I don't have another 180 minutes to waste jumping through hoops and holding my mouth just right. It may just be that my PC and laptop are just too old (7 and 5 years, resp.); it was working fine with my Samsung tablet and smartphone. But I can't afford a new PC or laptop right now.

So, I took it all down, put it back in the packaging, and got my Tenda router up and running again in about three minutes. The Linksys AC2200 is going back for a refund.

title: Marketing promises KEPT!!
review_text:
I'm not a buyer of high-end ear buds. At my age my hearing isn't acute enough to hear much of the nuance of music through headphones, but I do like the sound to be much better than if I were holding a can and string up to my ears. That being said, these are the best earphones I've ever owned. When I first put them on, the bass response actually startled me and the middles and highs were present and clear --without any adjustment to my player. The "stays in your ears" feature actually works; you give them a twist in your ear and they stay put, as well as keeping out sweat. You can hear ambient noise just fine, but unless there's a high wind or other competing sound, you continue to hear the audio just fine.

I don't agree with other reviewers who report that the plastic earbuds fall off easily. I think those reviewers must be actually pulling the buds off to clean them and I don't believe that's the manufacturers' intentions. I clean mine with a mini-fiber cloth well moistened (but not soggy) with rubbing alcohol without removing them from the actual earpieces.

The reason I didn't give these earphone five stars is that there is no inline control --no mute off, or volume control. I like them VERY much, and would buy them again if I needed to replace.

title: After a pair of disappointments, I like it
review_text:
The specifications imply that this tablet is designed to accept a wireless sim card if the user decides to add an additional wireless telephone line. After spending half a day trying to register my purchase with Dell, I was told that, since Dell itself was not the seller, they are not bound to provide warranty coverage. So, Amazon Warehouse buyers might want to figure a Square Trade or other third-party warranty into the purchase price for this Dell. When I asked about the fact that a card slot for a wireless phone sim card is engineered into the Dell Venue, the Dell rep informed me that the Dell engineers originally designed a separate card slot for this purpose, but "in recent models it has been DISCONNECTED!" Which is just about the most nonsensical thing I've heard in a long time.

Several years ago, I worked as a technical telephone support person for Denon home theater systems, and realized at that time that audio and telecommunications engineers frequently make completely mystifying. unnecessarily complicated design decisions, so this was not news to me ....It WAS however, a disappointment that cost the Dell Venue 8 two stars on this review.

That said, the 2GHz processor and Jelly Bean OS are wicked fast for simple gaming, texting (with "My SMS" or other texting apps from Google Play, synched to your Android phone), etc. It can be synchronized via Wi-Fi, USB tether or Bluetooth. It's a nice size (although a little heavy), and makes a very good Kindle-type unit for reading news, books, online magazines, etc. I've decided I like the tablet very much, but would be a LOT happier with if I could get Dell updates and downloads or install a wireless phone card.

title: Outstanding sound and value
review_text:
Although I don't use/have any iOs products, I am glad that this compact shelf stereo unit has a COVER for the iPhone/iPod connector to keep out dust. This is certainly not a mini-unit, but it is small enough to fit a deep shelf. It was easy to set up and program, mostly with the remote that works quite well at about a 40-degree angle to either side. I loaded a USB thumb drive with around 390 music files, all of which are playing flawlessly (mp3 and/or WMA), with a way to shuffle or random play from one artist or from all files.

The different EQ settings could be more varied in tone and effect; however, I'm 67 years old with some mid-range hearing loss, so that might be my fault. The bass response is fine even without the bass boost feature, and vocals, especially high male and women's voices, can seem a little harsh. Volume is fine without distortion, even at enough cranking for me --not sure how it would satisfy a head banger!

My only "like to haves" for this unit include a way to mute the radio or CD playbacks; however, the volume control is very responsive so that's not really a problem for the radio, and one can pause the CD and USB file playback. And of course, I can't imagine what Sony was thinking not including a regular headphone jack.

It's not the most elegant-looking set I've ever owned, but I'm quite satisfied, especially for the cost to value ratio I got on this unit. Very pleased!

title: Electronics can become TOO small...
review_text:
After a career in advertising, during which I've been around video cameras of all sizes, weights and shapes, this is my first camcorder for personal use. After one day of monkeying around with it, I'm delighted --with a couple of reservations. It appears to be of very good quality, feels lightweight and yet sturdy (with the exception of the rather stringy hand-strap/lanyard) and the user interfacing seems straightforward and intuitive, once you figure out where things are. I'll be back in a few weeks or months to describe my experiences with the software, data downloading and manipulation, etc.

The main criticism I have --more of an observation, really-- is that, for my somewhat arthritic hands, operating the controls are challenging because of their placement on the camera and because the thing is so darned small. (As in the length of a soft drink can --at only 2/3 of the diameter!) This may be simply because I'm unaccustomed to using camcorders, or indeed holding any camera as one does with the JVC GZ-HM550. Many reviewers have complained that this 2010 model still has scrolling and MENU, OK, and INFO buttons rather than Mac-style rolling touch screens. This doesn't bother me, although it takes a very delicate touch to get to the right menu selection on this camera, because they zip by so rapidly under a man's stubby fingers.

Low light results seem more than adequate, especially for daytime indoor shooting, and the shake reduction seems to me to be working very well. title: Surprisingly good sound REVISED
review_text:
I just received this Sanjean RCR-10 and set it up. The good news is that the sound is wonderfully rich and balanced for a little radio. First bedside table clock radio I've ever had that sounds good enough to crank up loud to fill my whole apartment with music. I'm impressed, and I'm not easily impressed.

On the other hand, it seems that, the more sophisticated these digital electronics get, the more challenging and puzzling they are to set up. It could well be that these companies need to shell out a little more money for decent technical writers to produce more thorough step-by-step setup instructions. OR, they could simply design the units so they're easier to set up for those of us who are not geeks or electronics engineers. It's not all that terribly frustrating; just be ready for several minutes of trial and error ...and pray you don't have a power outage! (The unit also offers a back-up batteries feature, so I wouldn't forget to do that.)

The RCR-10 is solid, substantial (not flimsy or lightweight) and attractive. The display also includes basic metadata indicating station and artist. The only thing missing for me --since I use an Android phone as my personal music player-- would be a little close-able cover for the empty iPod docking slot. It's going to be a dust collector in my house.

UPDATE: I'm revising my five star review down to three stars, because after a couple of months' use, I've realized this thing is REALLY a pain in the butt to re-progam. Even turning the alarm pre-set volume down a notch requires that you go through a big long procedure, as if you were setting the alarm for the first time. The same thing is true if you think you'd like to awaken to some other type of music station. Hard to do anything on the fly; if you need to make a change, be prepared to sit down for twenty minutes with the OM open for reference to accomplish even the most simple adjustment. Sanjean needs to make these beautiful radios MORE USER FRIENDLY!

title: Spent more time buffering than actually streaming music
review_text:
Everywhere I looked online, there were nothing but the highest words of praise for this radio. It's an attractive, compact unit, with reasonably good sound and lots of options for add ons, additional speakers, usb ports, etc. However, I had such a difficult time getting it to find my home network, I had to completely reconfigure my router (and two computers as a consequence) in order to get the radio to "find" my home network and accept my password key. The enclosed setup instructions are so inadequate that most of the information and procedures required to sign up for services like Pandora, I Heart Radio, Rhapsody, NPR, etc., were completely missing from the manual. The only indications of how to start appeared in the radio's display window, instructing me to go online to do the setup. After some perseverance, I finally figured out how to use the Reciva Internet Radio site to connect the radio with the services I've been using with my computers for years.

Once I finally got the thing to start streaming (about 4 frustrating hours after I began the set up) I realized that, even less than three feet from my router, the unit stayed in buffering mode more than it actually played music, no matter what bps settings I tried. I don't really know much about the technical end of audio streaming, but my MediaLink router works fine with my two portable computers, and streams video and music from services like Pandora and Rhapsody with no glitches whatever. I didn't see much point in listening to 10 seconds of a song, then waiting through 15 or 20 while the unit's memory silently buffered so it could continue.

Even if you're not a digital audio newbie, if you're looking for straightforward setup and easy operation, this AIN'T IT. I may look further into wireless digital radio --but I doubt it, at least not in the near future.

title: Be patient while setting up...
review_text:
I purchased this router to create a small two-computer network in my apartment. My PC is a refurbished and souped up Gateway running Windows Vista, and I bought an older Toshiba laptop, also refurbished and running Windows XP Home Edition. I wanted to be able to sit in my living room or on the patio while working once in awhile, rather than being chained to my home office PC. No gaming consoles, DVRs, or other components to connect.

The setup literature and accompanying CD shipped with the router are invaluable, easy to understand, even for a non-techie like me. However, don't expect your setup to proceed with no glitches! You may have to reset your cable modem two or three times, or restart the various components two or three times. Take your time, follow directions, keep your wits about you, and think about possible causes and likely solutions and you should have no trouble setting up this router.

The day after my order, I also received a lengthy, substantive email from Mediabridge Products, thanking me for my order and supplying me with all kinds of background, links, and telephone technical support information, so I felt confident that I had resources handy during the setup if necessary. So far the router is working like a charm. I recommend it, especially if you're interested in a fairly simple LAN setup!

title: NOT FOR GAMING!!!
review_text:
Initially, I liked the ergonomic design. It put much less pressure on my wrist than the Logitech trackball I've been using for many years. Unfortunately, when I started up World of Warcraft, I noticed the Kensington trackball button mapping software disabled the ability to use more than one button at once. I found the same detriment in Overwatch where multiple buttons often need to be pressed simultaneously. When I contacted the company, they sent me an email. The following is a direct quote from their email:
"Thank you for contacting Kensington Technical Support.

We would like to inform you that these trackballs are designed for basic office use and will not work on gaming applications.

We appreciate your time and patience."

To me, this came across as rather rude. This, coupled with the fact that this very mouse shows up in searches for gaming trackball mouse made me extremely disappointed and, in fact, somewhat angry. I feel Kensington needs to do any or all of the following. 1. Fix the software to make their hardware gaming inclusive. 2. Stop advertising their non-gaming devices as gaming devices (I feel this is blatant false advertising.) 3. Ask customers how they could fix issues rather than giving them a short, curt email to inform us that we, apparently, are idiots for expecting their devices to work as advertised.

Bottom line: I do not recommend buying this product unless all you intend to use it for is emails and youtube.

review_text:
This product is almost perfect and probably could be if they fixed two issues. The first, and main, issue I faced was the microphone quality. I was extremely disappointed in the quality. They actually had worse quality than my iPhone’s built-in microphone and even the Lightning Connector Earpods that came with my phone. I’ve tried troubleshooting this multiple ways including, forgetting the device completely and pairing it again (exactly according to instructions in box) and turning my phone completely off and on again to no avail.
I also found that the volume level was somewhat lower than I expected. It isn’t extremely quiet, but to me it just seems a bit low.
Now, I don’t know if I am just unlucky and I’ve received a dud or if my expectations for this product are unreasonable, but I’d just like to see these problems resolved if not for my sake, then for the sake of others.
Other than those issues, I love the noise cancellation and the battery life is phenomenal.

title: One of the best cases for an iPad Air, particularly if you have apps that run in Portrait mode
review_text: The rooCASE Oragami Case seems to be currently at or near the top of the cases, the big advantage of this case being the number and variations of orientations, including both portrait and landscape, and at the price point, is hard to beat.  The oragami cover is ingenious, you can fold it up all sorts of ways, the iPad Air has a lot of applications that fairly beg for portrait orientation (reading a book, newspaper, etc.).  The conventional Apple case supports only landscape, as do a number of competitors (the CaseCrown Omni is one of the better conventional ones).  The Moshi and O!Case are also oragami cases, although the designs differ some.  The rooCASE has a more rubberized or grippy exterior, key because it's less likely to slip and get dropped.  Protection is generally pretty good, but the CaseCrown does a little better on edge protection, the openings on the rooCase tend to be U-shaped, the CaseCrown is more O-Shaped, but otherwise they are very similar.  The Moshi has one advantage, in that it has a back magnet, that lets it stay open better in book mode.  The rooCASE actually has magnets that keep it closed pretty well, but it lacks a back magnet.  The rooCase front cover of course folds up to support quite a number of variations or angles, which is a big advantage over conventional cases, and on a desk or table, is plenty stable.  The microfiber front interior is nice, it tends to help keep the screen clean, but it is worth noting that the orgami pattern tends to show up in the fingerprints and grease, so you do need to clean the screen from time to time.  rooCASE also shuts off the iPad Air screen when you close it, a very useful feature.  The end result is still pretty light and easy to carry, in keeping with the iPad Air design point.  Why not 5 stars?  rooCase is very close, but they could improve the edge coverage/protection, and add a back magnet (ala Moshi), and NuGuard KX probably has the better back protection (at the cost of some bulk), but at its price-point, front and back protection, oragami design that lets you pick multiple orientations and angles, the rooCASE is pretty much unbeatable, and worthy of consideration at any price.

title: They have software called Sentinel you install on your PC and this is your gateway to all updates and firmware and it can contro
review_text:
This review is for the Uniden BCD436HP I see reviews here for other radios, so not to be confused.
I used Amazon Prime Now to get the radio to me, in less than 1 hour (about 45 minutes) the delivery person was knocking on my door with my new receiver, wow, I was highly impressed and I will always check to see if Prime Now is available for all my deliveries from now on.....
So, the radio....
This receiver has a 4 gig SD card preloaded with every known frequency with text for the entire US and Canada. They have software called Sentinel you install on your PC and this is your gateway to all updates and firmware and it can control your radios SD card any way you like. Sentinel has an extensive database of all frequencies and let me say this again, all frequencies have text description included which is the most highly advanced scanner database system I have ever seen and I have owned scanner receivers most of my adult life, (long time)..
This is a digital receiver using the latest technology available. It can monitor any analog or digital TX (with some exceptions, like encrypted signals) and gives you extensive control over what you're listening to. There are FCC laws regarding what is legal and not legal to monitor and Uniden has got us right up to the maximum legally allowed to be monitored by civilians. If you are law enforcement persons you will have much more powerful receivers available to you capable of Cell phone conversation monitoring etc., things no civilian should even be interested in.
There is another version of this Uniden radio, the BCD536 which is a tabletop version. If you have large powerful outdoor weatherproof antennas the BCD536 is a good option and it is completely transferable to vehicle dash mount and back from your work desk to your vehicle.
I like this handheld BCD436 best personally for my purposes.
This is basically a plug and play receiver. It comes with 3 2300 milliamp rechargeable batteries, load those, charge them or just leave radio plugged in, enter your zip and you're in. Well theoretically that's how it works, in the real world? No.
When you first receive the radio I would suggest positioning yourself in front of your PC. Have the paper manual, the radio, you and your PC right there in front of you. Get ready to read and learn your radios keyboard layout and what these great, well thought out keys can do for you. You will learn, trust me, you will quickly come to love this radio.
Some cons:
No wall charger adopter included. You can charge from your PC's USB ports but you will need a wall charger with USB port. Most of us have several of these around the house from old cell phones etc. They work fine.
This unit should come with a nice wall charger adopter. That's really the only con, not to bad really.
Antennas:
Your ability to scan and receive signals on any scanner is proportionate to your antennas. The more robust and correct (correct meaning size, materials used etc).. You will need some nice antennas for this nice radio to increase your scanning powers. Amazon has some nice antennas, scannermaster.com has some also. Your local radio shop retailer will have some also. The included rubber ducky antenna is garbage, toss it from across the room to your garbage can, see if you can make a rim shot. Like I said, I have been playing with scanners for many years so I have many antennas to pick from.
Verdict:
This is without a doubt, the most powerful handheld scanning receiver available from any manufacturer. It is the luxury sedan of the scanning receiver world. It is easy and robust. It is backed up by Uniden's Sentinel software which will future proof your radio for many years to come.
I give Uniden 5 stars for this winner.
I give Amazon 5 stars for Prime Now 1 hour shipping, also a winner.

The Condor all band antenna is unsurpassed.
The desktop stand holds your handheld at the perfect viewing angle, you can listen and see all text clearly right beside your computer.

I give Uniden 5 stars for this winner.

title: I like this Blue- Black Ultra Metal drive's aesthetics, it is in short, gorgeous.
review_text:
I had a big clunky WD My Book Essential 1Tb USB 3.0 external drive and it was getting old and failing.
I received this Ultra Metal 2Tb model today.
I actually took the old My Book apart by prying the case off with a large screwdriver and removed the bare HDD from inside. There is a WD Green drive in there and I actually mounted it in my computer, wiped and formatted it and now it gives me 1Tb of extra storage, not bad.
So, the Ultra Metal external drive is so classy.
The only complaint I have is the included USB 3.0 cable, it is very short, maybe 12 inches long, not good, however, I had the other 3.0 cable from the old drive, it's about 1 meter long, and it of course works fine with the new drive, I have it plugged into a 1 meter USB 3.0 extension cable so now have about 6 feet of wiggle room from the computer to the external drive.
I like this Blue- Black Ultra Metal drive's aesthetics, it is, in short, gorgeous.
That big boxy My Book I had before was so clunky, big and ran hot all the time.
This device has no unnecessary power cable, just one USB port and nothing else.
I opened the file for this drive and saw about 5Mb of preinstalled apps installers including a PDF Users Manual and quite a few other apps in about 20 different languages.
WD has gone to a lot of effort to make this drive world class.
Except for that little 12 inch USB 3.0 cable. Get yourself an extension cable and this drive is the Cadillac of external drives. The included software is icing on the cake for you to choose how sweet you will make your drive.

title: Installation of the Corsair H80i V2 wasn't easy in this smallish case but the radiator sandwiched between ...
review_text:
I received this cooler today and installed it along with two new 140mm front panel case fans.
I have an AMD based system running stock cooling that came with the case and hardware components.
My system temps running stock cooling were way to high, idyling at temps around 45c to 50c and when running
demanding applications temps would shoot way up into the 80's and 90's sometimes causing shutdowns.
I kept remembering statements from AMD advising consumers to keep the down blowing fans installed but I decided
to try a liquid cooling solution out of desperation.

My case is a Corsair Spec 02.
My motherboard is a Asus Sabertooth 990FX R2.0.
The processor is a AMD FX-8320.
The graphics processor is a Sapphire Radeon R9 380.
That AMD FX 8320 runs hot, extremely hot also the NB and SB components on the Asus MB run very hot.
My system temps were way to high, I had to do something.

Installation of the Corsair H80i V2 wasn't easy in this smallish case but the radiator sandwiched between
the two 120mm fans does fit in this case. I followed the manufacturer recommendation and configured both
fans to push air inward into the case. This case has perforated holes in the roof for ventilation and this
allows used air to evacuate out of the case assuming the fans are configured to blow inward which will push
air out those top vents.
The two big 140mm red LED fans I installed in the front panel are configured to pull air inward and I set them
to run at 100% speed (1000 RPM), they are Cougar Red LED's, very high quality fans that move a lot of air
silently.

This Corsair H80i V2 has got to be the best liquid cooler available for smaller cases like mine, it has dropped
my system temps by 20 to 30 degrees C instantly. I am seeing system temps lower than I've ever seen them since
I built the system back in December 2015.

This fridge is rocking my system. Cool is good, the cooler the better when it comes to computer systems. I have
Core Temp 1.0 RC6 installed and it is showing my CPU temps idling at 13C - 15C... That is chill.

Chill is good.

Thanks Corsair, this liquid cooler system is awesome.
Thanks Amazon for the excellent service and thanks UPS for being the most dependable carrier on earth.
My system purrs away at 15C, OMG this is awesome.

title: Suprisingly substantial
review_text:
Just received these speakers today. Very easy to install on desktop PC. I like Classical Baroque playing lightly in the background while I'm online and these speakers are absolutely fabulous for this.
I put the sub on the floor below my desk off to the left, the two mains on either side of the monitor and checked my audio software settings then fired up some online Baroque live from Zurich and the sound quality was immediately impressive.
All power, volume and bass settings are built into a very nice control pod you can place nearby on your desk. I found using a light touch on the sub power gives nice bass accentuation without adding unrealistic and unpleasant booming.
The sub is rather heavy with a hefty solid feel to it and it's addition to the sound is substantial even at low volume levels.
All in all, I'm very happy and my ears are floating away with the delights of the Baroque era as I type this review.
Amazon has got me spoiled with so many fine products and the best customer service on earth.
And thanks to Cyber Acoustics for this great audio system priced so reasonably.
Edit:
Okay, now it's June 19th, I don't like these speakers any more at all. Threw them in the trash. Using my 6 year old Logitech Z320's which are still awesome. I'm looking for a serious pair of 2.0 speakers from Amazon next, maybe Creative GigaWorks T40 Series will be my next choice.

title: Astounding powers........
review_text:
Install this on your compatible motherboard and you will think you have installed the heart of Superman in your computer.
I am in awe of this prodigy of modern computer technology.
Edit:
I've had this processor running in my new build for about a month now. I was being annoyed by the stock cooler fan buzzing at very high rpm whenever the heat rose to moderate levels like 52C. The fan was really buzzing like a little aircraft prop at full throttle for takeoff. It would crank up to 6600 rpm at the slightest provocation like CPU temp hitting 50C.
I decided to take everything apart down to the motherboard coming out and all components attached to it.
When I pulled the cooler off the CPU and looked at the thermal paste situation, OMG what a mess. The stock thermal paste was not covering the whole area, it was reduced to a gummy, sticky glue. I had to pull very hard to get the cooler off the CPU.
I cleaned the cooler base and the CPU thoroughly and applied a pea sized spot of Arctic Silver 5 then reassembled everything.
Instant cure. Instant quieter fan. Instant low CPU temps andQUIET!AMD needs to stop using whatever they're putting on the coolers and just include a syringe of a high quality thermal paste for customers to apply themselves because whatever they're using is junk.
The stock cooler and fan they include with the fx 8320 are very high quality but the pre applied thermal paste is garbage.
Just apply new first quality thermal paste, you don't need to spend big dollars on third party hardware and I suspect those of you who have installed new coolers and seen great results is because of the new thermal paste used during installation.
The fx 8320 is a very powerful processor don't smoke it because of 10 cents worth of cheap thermal paste, use the best for your investment and this hot CPU will give many years of great performance.

title: Hot rod Blu Ray player...
review_text:
I bought this player from Sears, they were $20 dollars cheaper than Amazon and I picked it up from my local neighborhood store so no shipping charges and no waiting. This is one hot budget Blu Ray player people. If you have a Samsung HDTV of any type go ahead and buy this player you will be amazed. My little DLink N Router hooked my network to this player while it synched up to my TV and then it downloaded all the recent upgrades and then I hit the Netflix button on the remote and I was scanning through the Netflix library of movies before I could say WTF. Bam, HD movies streaming to my big screen in no time at all.. Swweeeet. Then I plugged in Avatar HD 2D (this player does not support 3D), bright big and blasting beautiful Avatar never looked or sounded better on my Samsung big screen. If you want to spend $600, go ahead or save your $$$ and grab this sweeeet Samsung BD D5700 it will make you happy. Check the specs, check your equipment, check your needs like the size of your space you plan to use this player in and check your expectations: maybe you need a more powerful device. For a modest user like myself, this is a very satisfying device. It rocks my equipment and my expectations.
Gus,
Portland, Oregon

title: Impressive
review_text:
I have put together many, many computers using cases of all shapes, sizes and costs. Dollar for dollar this case is hands down the best value I've ever seen. As others have noted the materials are a bit flimsy but this is a computer case, not the frame for a tank. As long as it isn't abused it should last and give good service for years. And I like that is fairly light weight, many cases that are "sturdy" are also on the heavy side. By the time you have them loaded with a good power supply and several hard drives they begin to feel like a tank when you need to move them.

The cutouts and gaps to make routing cables easy are nice, they not only improve the appearance but also help air flow freely through the case. I was a little worried about sharp edges but have not found any, which is good because knowing me if there was even one I would have cut myself on it.

I read several reviews which mention the hard drive rails being difficult and backwards so I wasn't sure what to expect. At first I was a little confused about how the hard drives are meant to be installed but once I understood it, it makes perfect sense and is no problem to work with. If you have right angled power and data cable ends you can mount the drives facing left or right which might make things easier if you have several drives installed.

Another thing that both surprised and pleased me was when I was installing the power supply I noticed there were two extra holes which makes it possible to mount the ps either right side up or upside down. I am not a huge fan of bottom mount for power supplies and as others have said, it can cause problems if the leads for motherboard power are not long enough. Mine just barely reached to the cpu power connector after running it up the rear of the case, resting as it is on the motherboard and running under the video card. I have extensions on order though I'm sure I could get by for the life of the ps as it is now.

I like the long, thin blue light on the front for power on though the green light for hard drive activity is a bit hard to see. Most of all though, I love the paint. No more of that ugly, dingy looking gray metal with thoughts of how I want to paint it black. I am not an expert on such things but I believe the paint is baked on giving it a very nice texture and appearance.

This is a case I would not have been disappointed by if I had paid 60 dollars. Getting it from amazon for 36 with free prime shipping is one of the best deals I've ever found.

Three cheers to NZXT !!!

I bought this to sit on top of my i5-2500K and I couldn't be happier. I love the way it looks through the case's side window and it is so quiet and smooth. I would recommend this fan to all except possibly severe gamers who need every bit of cooling they can get.

title: Great Hard Drive
review_text:
I have 9 or 10 Hitachi 1 tb drives and am very pleased with them. They may not be the fastest or quietest drives in the world, though I never hear them and they seem plenty fast to me, but in two years the only one I've had fail had been improperly packaged by amazon and was beat to death in shipping. I am currently using a pair of these in my main computer in a raid array. Using raid 0 on the first array partition, to boot from, and raid 1 on the 2nd for mirroring.

Before I started using hitachi drives I was losing a wd or seagate roughly every other month. It was all I could do to keep up with the rma's and I completely lost track of how much data I'd lost. I should note I have approximately 20 hard drives spread over 5 computers. With the size of modern hard drives an effective backup method is very hard to achieve. Few people can afford tape drive backups for home, I certainly can't and dvdrw disk simply do not hold enough to be cost or time effective. After so many wd and seagate crashes I have begun using many drives simply for mirroring and I am pleased that with the hitachi drives I have not lost a single byte.

As long as they keep making them at the current quality level, I will keep buying them.

title: Nice earbuds but I decided swapped them out for Bose QuietComfort earbuds
review_text:
I went on the search for a set of ear buds that would stay in my ears better than my Airpod Pros but with the same level of Noise cancellation. It seemed like the Sony WF-1000XM4 and Bose Quietcomfort earbuds were the top picks in this space. After a lot of research i went with the Sony earbuds. Besides their sound and level of ANC. i liked the fact the Sony earbuds still had a lot of playback control available from the earbuds and you can use either earbud individually. I also felt like the fact that they sit in your ear canal rather than on the outside would contribute to the noise cancellation.

The earbuds felt and sound good and the accompanying app was nice but the case had a cheap, almost cardboard feel. My main issues were, although the earbuds never actually fell out of my ear, I think their top-heavy design made them feel like they were always about to fall out. The bigger issue i had, which won't apply to everyone, is how much effort went into getting them to sit correctly in my ear. Even with twisting, and pushing, I could never get the right earbud to fit securely in my ear like the left one did.

After a day of wearing the Sonys i decided to pick up a pair of Bose Quietcomfort ear buds as i already had a pair of Quietcomfort 35 over the ears that i loved, i figured I'd give Bose another shot. As soon as i opened the Bose, I immediately fell in love. Besides the unboxing and charging case feeling more premium, the earbuds went into my ear effortlessly and securely. I wore them the first day and they stayed in place all day and sounded great.

Although the Sony WF-1000XM4 is a great set of earbuds, The Bose earbuds have the same functionality, sound and ANC but are designed in a way to comfortably fit a wider array of ear shapes and at a cheaper price. The Sonys are going back and the Bose are going to be my new day-to-day earbuds.

title: Acer gets 5 stars....Amazon gets a zillion.
review_text:
I did a little homework and this machine, especially at the price looked excellent. I noticed in reading Amazon reviews that a small percentage of buyers had received machines with faulty screens. So I went to BestBuy to see what they had, and found nothing appealing in any where near this price. So I ordered one. It arrived on Wednesday (days matter in this little story). Knowing there was a slight risk, I opened everything very carefully, saved everything in case I'd want to return it. Sure enough I got one with a faulty screen. However I'd also calculated the odds: very slim chance of getting two in a row. Thursday we started what I thought was likely to be a tricky, time consuming effort: filling forms, emails, getting to UPS, etc etc. It went like this: one click to get to the trade request on the Amazon order, five minutes to complete it ....Including a stunning question: did I want to drop the first one at UPS, or have them pick it up at my door? UPS would have the prepaid return label with them.
Then they shipped the replacement to me Thursday. SAME DAY! Monday the new one arrived, the man had the return label in his hand.He took one look at my shipping ready packaged box, slapped the label on, and left while I watched still in disbelief. This is way beyond 5 stars for Amazon.

And true to the odds, this machine I'm using for this is flawless. I love it. It's everything it is advertised to be, and more. The slowness some mentioned was easily remedied for my use by clearing the "Start Up", using Blackle as a homepage, and one click to change the "Next Window" screen. I don't play complex games, just puzzles, solitaire and the like so no need for speed there. Pictures, movies and TV are all beautiful, and quick to load.

The Windows 10 Home is surprisingly user friendly...and I'm 72. The machine runs cool, easy to upgrade, and most of all: affordable. So don't be afraid to take a chance if you're waffling. Thank you Amazon! Very much.

I recommend these HIGHLY. The ear loops and earbuds are fantastic! You won't be sorry.

I have not tried to jog in them so I cannot answer to that but for me, these are worth double or triple what I paid for them

title: High quality angled Lightening Cord
review_text:
I paired this cord with an Apple brand lightening charger after reading MANY horror stories of sparks, overheating, charging failures, etc. and I’m really pleased with it. (And the Apple charger, which is never warm, doesn’t spark, & has caused me no paranoia I’m going to catch on fire.)

The cord itself feels substantial. Ten feet is perfect for where I use it. It flexes, but is still quite stiff. The little adapter is nice, but so far is living in a drawer.

My only complaint, which is minor and will not apply to many users, is that the actual lightening tip end is longer than I need it to be. I’m sure this is to accommodate cases that don’t have any cut-out design where the port is. Mine does, so there is a lot of tip before the barrel it’s mounted in. This requires some extra care that I don’t jar it when setting my phone down. Not a problem when I’m holding it.
I’m a big fan of this angled design, and the company has good reviews here and elsewhere. I especially recommend it to those that have heavy cases with minimal port access.

title: ... for about 2 weeks now and I am very happy with the purchase
review_text:
I've been using this product for about 2 weeks now and I am very happy with the purchase! It provides a strong breeze of air to keep me dry despite the extreme Arizona temperatures. My only challenge is my daily driver is a 67 Mustang and this product will not mount on the dash too tall and too wide. I don't have the long center console in my car, so the only thing I can stick it to is the carpeted floor - and I would rather not do that. For the most part it stays put with nothing holding it, but if I hang a sharp right it goes sliding. Not the company's fault-but for anyone driving a 67 mustang, this won't sit on the dash. Other than the challenge with placement, i would definitely recommend this product. It's not a cure for the 110 degree heat but I have tinted windows to dim the sun and this to keep the air moving in the car. A huge help to get me through one more summer before I get an AC installed!
Edit: forgot to mention - it is not noisy! Obviously there is a little bit of a buzz but it's not annoying and nothing that can't be drowned out by your radio. Also, I like that the two fans can be adjusted up, down and side to side. So it can sit in the middle and one fan be pointed at the driver and the other at the passenger. It can tilt up or down depending if you have it sitting up high on the dash or low on the floor like I do. Anyway - great buy! Not sure why people have any issues with it dying on them but I will update if anything like that happens.
