title: It absolutely works, but you can do a lot better.
review_text:
This cord is an identical replacement for the one that comes with the monitor. This is a pro and a con. My husband and I have used it every night after our son moved into his own room, and we absolutely love it. It’s so much nicer than the one we had 10 years ago when our daughter was born.

The only issue we’ve ever had with it is the cord that connects with the screen. It started fraying at the end near the plug after 2-3 months. We were able to tape it and continue using it for several months after that. Eventually you could see the copper wiring coming through and it only worked when positioned perfectly. A couple weeks later, it was done. I desperately tried to salvage it, but it wasn’t happening.

My Mom ordered us a replacement cord and all was well again. That didn’t last long though, because history tends to repeat itself. I learned my lesson and didn’t wait until it became useless before replacing it. This time I bought a universal adapter. It was actually cheaper than this cord and can be used for just about anything requiring an ac adapter.

Use your money wisely. Why pay the same price for a cord that will just fall apart? There are a ton of options when you search for a universal adapter, but they seem fairly similar. I bought one for less money than this cord, it came with about 10 adapters, and is much sturdier.

title: Not bad, but ANNOYING pairing and audio interface
review_text:
I've had a number of Bluetooth headphones and the overwhelming majority of them have an "audio interface" that makes sense - some bare bones, some quite pleasant. This interface is in the form of sounds the relate to each of the functions - power on/off, paring, etc. These headphones have a TERRIBLE interface. When you power them on an annoyingly loud series of tones blares in your ear. The tones rise in pitch. When you continue to hold the power button, to access the paring mode, all you hear is an extremely brief, muffled tone. Apparently, the makers thought this was enough of a signal to indicate you're in paring mode. Believe me, it is NOT obvious at all. When you power off the headphones, you hear the same annoying loud series of tones. In this case, the tones do not decrease in pitch, which one might expect.

By comparison, the audio interface of my other Bluetooth headphones are a joy - unfortunately, they do not have volume controls or skip and rewind. When powering them on, a pleasant female voice says, "Hello", and when you enter pairing mode, the same voice says, "Ready to pair." When pairing is established, the voice says, You're connected", then tells me how much charge I have - either full, medium or low. These Cootree headphones do none of that. You'll be lucky if you're able to tell if they've been turned off properly.

In terms of sound quality, they're okay - nothing exceptional. In terms of fit, they're okay as well. Again, nothing exceptional. To my knowledge, they do not have an active noise cancelling function, other than what little noise they may happen to muffle by covering your ears. I mention this only because the rating form asks about it.

Anyway, they informed me that the problem I experienced was likely because the BT speakers (Upgraded, Anker Soundcore Boost) I used I paired with their device did not support the low latency aptx codec. This may have been the case, but I was unable to find specs for the speakers to confirm this.

I must say their customer support is extremely accommodating. In their email, they offered a number of options to make things right, including a gift card or a different BT transmitter. Unfortunately, I've already purchased wired speakers to replace the ones I had bought. Although I won't be taking advantage of their offers, I do give them high marks for service and have changed my rating from 2 stars to 4 stars.

title: Button functionality ruins this device. You get what you pay for.
review_text:
I wasn't expecting much given the price of this item, and I got pretty much what I expected.

The charging port is hard to reach and the LED charging indicator is difficult, if not impossible to see, without having to move the foam earpiece covering.

Setting up/pairing the device is pretty easy. Press the button for 4 seconds or so and you’ll hear a pleasant female voice say, “Hello”. This means the power is on. Continue holding the button and the device will enter pairing mode. You’ll hear the voice say, “Ready to pair.” When pairing is complete, you’ll hear the device say, “You’re connected” and tell you how much charge the battery has. So far, all I’ve heard is, “Battery full.” I have no idea what other battery indications the voice will give – perhaps only at 3/4, 1/2 and 1/4? Or maybe percentages?

The buttons are the biggest drawback with this device. Actually, it's really just one multi-function button on the right earpiece. The button functionality is not like any Bluetooth headset I've used before - very non-intuitive. The button has no label at all and the tactile feedback is nonexistent at times - I press the button sometimes and there's no "click" feeling. If a song is playing, it doesn't seem to matter where I press, the song stops if it is playing. When I press again, anywhere, it starts playing again.

There is no volume control on the headphones at all. You’ll have to adjust the volume from your phone/audio player. There is a bare bones EQ function. You control this by clicking the multi-function button 3 times in rapid succession. Each time you do this, the device advances to the next of 3 EQ setting – balanced, bass boost and JLab signature. The “balanced” setting seems to sound just like what it’s named – balanced or equal high, mid and low tones. The bass boos is decent – not overbearing. Not sure what the last one is, but if the pictograms in the manual are any indication, it boost the high and low ends. The EQ function does provide audible feedback – the voice announces each setting by name.

There's a next track function, but no function for going to the previous track. The next track function requires holding down the multi-function button for 2 seconds. There's no audible feedback for this function (other than a very short moment of silence). When you hear the silence, let go IMMEDIATELY. title: Inexpensive, but lousy UI
review_text:
For the price, this device is okay, but the user interface is pathetic. The touch interface is annoying because it only applies to half the screen. What's worse is when the device screen goes blank (to save battery life), you have to touch the screen - which performs one of the functions, like play or pause. It's quite annoying. The buttons of the touch screen are at the bottom and you can only navigate the interface by tapping up/down/left/right. So doing things on the device is a chore

I bought this for a friend and didn't spend much time with it - only to set it up. So I don't have an opinion of the sound quality or the build quality. However ... one comment on the latter. I've seen a number of reviews for this and similar products which reference the weight of the device and correlation it to the quality of the build. The 2 don't always to hand in hand. The Chinese have been known to add lead weights to devices to make them heavier so that people will believe it's better build quality or material than it really is. I don't know this to be the case with this device - just wanted to point out that weight may not be the telltale people think it is

BTW - the USB cable is SHORT. Probably only a foot at most. Also, it's micro USB, which is a pain in the butt.

The radio function required the use of headphones - as an antenna. Kind of a pain for Bluetooth headphone users. Also - if the headphones are plugged in, I presume you can't listen through the device's built in speaker (which is lackluster) or through an external Bluetooth speaker. I can't confirm this because, as I said, I only spent about an hour using the device.

FYI - the device has no internal storage. The 32GB is in the form of a micro SDXC card. This means if you opt to purchase a larger card to use with the device, you won't be adding to the 32GB, you'll be replacing it.

title: It's cheap and works with Windows, but that's about it.
review_text:
I bought this because my laptop keyboard began to fail.

Pros
- Inexpensive - I paid $19, including tax
- Both the keyboard and mouse work with Windows with no problems - so far.
- Batteries were included - 1 AA for the mouse and 2 AAA for the keyboard.
- Includes all standard/function keys plus dedicated media buttons. Shortcut keys for email, web home page, power and calculator.
- All of the shortcut keys work with no config - except the email key - see cons below.

On the con side:
- There is no LED to indicate that the keyboard is on. If there is supposed to be, the LED on my keyboard doesn't work.
- If you use Gmail or another online service, the email shortcut key may not be usable. I use Gmail and when I pressed the email key, Windows Mail launched. If this can be configured to work with online email services, Logitech provides no instructions in the box.
- Unifying receiver is incompatible with newer Logitech software and devices.
- The mouse is bare bones - left and right click buttons and a scroll wheel with middle click function. No next/back buttons, no tilt scroll wheel. This mouse is best for emergencies or for temporary use until you get a new mouse with better features, etc.

Bottom line - you get what you pay for.

title: Okay for $25.  Still a little disappointed.
review_text:
Let me start by saying I don't use the cell phone features of these headphones, so this review is not all encompassing.

That said, I was a little disappointed in these headphones. Although the sound quality is good, the build quality and attention to detail in design could be better. The control buttons on the right ear are difficult to use as you can't easily feel with your finger where one starts and another begins, You just have to press in the general area, which is not very reassuring. The buttons themselves have no raised symbols or any physical element you can touch to let you know you're on a button, let alone the correct one.

The build quality is not the best. The control buttons fit together less tightly than other Bluetooth headphones I've used. The main play/pause/on/off/pairing button, located in the center of the right earphone in particular seems loose and misaligned.

The functions of the buttons work well enough. However, with some functions, there is no audio feedback. Having used other headsets that provide a short beep each time a button is pressed, I was a little confused when I first tried these - I'd press pause and the audio would just stop, with no beep. I suppose some users would find this preferable though. Some of the button functions, such as play/pause, are not instantaneous. There's a slight delay (about a second) between the time you press it and the time the audio actually plays or pauses. I've experienced this with other Bluetooth headsets and it seems to be a common annoyance.

Because the fit is somewhat tight, getting the earphones on requires a little manipulation. I often find I have to guide the tip of my ear into the space between the neckband (the part that holds the earpieces and wraps around your neck) and the earpiece.This is mainly due to the padding on the earpieces. Once the headphones are on though, they've not uncomfortable. However, a little more space between the neckband and the top of the earpieces would be an improvement. Wearing the headphones lying down or with your head against the back of a seat is not uncomfortable for the most part.

The charging port is has a rubber cover. Although it serves a purpose and some might find this helpful, I find it just gets in the way and will likely fall off. The charging cable is VERY short - about 3 feet, and it comes with no AC adapter, so you'll need to plug it into a USB port for charging - or acquire an adapter so you can use an electrical outlet. Due to the shortness of the cord, it will likely be inconvenient for use with some outlets.

Attaching the charging cord is somewhat difficult. This is to be expected, I guess, due to the micro-USB size of the plug that goes into the ear piece. The end of the cord that plugs into the ear piece is tapered on one side, so there's some visual indication of which way it should go in, but it's always a pain trying to insert these kinds of plugs, no matter what the device. I haven't used the headphones for any great length of time, so I can't comment on the battery life at this time.

The fact that these headphones can fold up to a fairly small size is nice and may be helpful to some when traveling. Typically, I wear them while walking or taking public transportation, so no real advantage for me.

I purchased 2 pair of these - 1 for myself and one as a gift. The ones I bought for myself were to replace a pair of Motorola Bluetooth headphones I thought were malfunctioning. Whenever I wore them, if I turned my heard too far to the right, the sound would cut out or it would seem to skip slightly. The first time I tried the Kinivo BTH240 headphones, they did the exact same thing. Is this something common to Bluetooth devices?

All in all, I suppose the negatives I've noted are minor and are likely more personal, but they still prevent me from rating these higher than 3 stars.

title: Don't waste your money.
review_text:
OK, take 2. My original review of this product got hijacked somehow. After writing it, I checked back a couple hours later and my screen name and original title were there, but my review got replaced with what seemed like some guy's journal entry. It had absoluterly nothing to do with this or any other product. Strange.

Anyway - as mentioned in my original posting, this review is more a condemnation or earbud headphones in general than the Sennheiser CX300-B, which I decided to try after my "over ear" style Sony noise canceling headphones went on the fritz. My past experience with earbuds was not good, although I had only ever tried the type that come with the iPod and not the "ear plug" type that go in the ear canal, like the Sennheiser CX300-B. However, having owned a pair of Sennheiser over the ear headphones back in the 70's, my impression of the company and their products was good. So, I decided to take the plunge. What a mistake.

After opening the package (no easy feat - damn sound welded plastic clamshells!), I popped on the medium-sized bud covers (appropriate for my size ears) and inserted them into my ears. I turned on my mp3 player and listened for a few minutes. The sound was adequate - nothing spectacular. I did notice they had decent bass and did block some external noise. I kept listening as I stepped outside to go to the store. I couldn't believe what I heard. Every step I took was amplified in my head - like a booming bass drum. Even the gentle bumping of the cord against my chest was amplified - a constant thump, thump, thump that was impossible to ignore. As it turns out, the very feature that blocks a modicum of external noise, also amplifies any sound that travels through the body. Even breathing is amplified! As I walked, it sounded as though I was listening to someone breathe over a PA system! I had hoped to use these while running, but there's no way that's going to happen. In fact, the problem with amplified sound is so bad, I won't use them at all.

I am very disappointed in this product and will never buy any ear plug style headphones again. I don't understand why anyone would sell them, let alone use them. They may have great sound reproduction, but the listening experience is totally ruined by the sounds that get amplified through the body. It amazes me that people buy similar style products that sell for hundreds of dollars. The only way you can enjoy the sound they produce is to sit perfectly still. I'm glad I only paid about $16 for these things. I won't return them because it'll be too much of a hassle - probably cost more to ship them back than I paid.

BTW - The photo of the product is misleading. The cord looks thicker than it actually is and there's no way it can be coiled as is shown in the photo. It gives the impression the cord is more supple and flexible that it really is. Also, one end of the cord is longer than the other. Not sure why this is, but the thinness of the cord makes it prone to kinking and tangling. In fact, since one side of the cord is longer than the other, it makes it even more prone to tangling.

Bottom line - steer clear of the Sennheiser CX300-B and all ear plug style earbuds.

title: A Maintenance Nightmare
review_text:
What should have been on the front of the BOX:

Warning, Charge this Device up Immediately before install. During it's use, you will have to unscrew it from the wall and disconnect the doorbell wiring and throw it on a charger for 5-10 hours from time to time to keep it working properly. The engineers who developed this product weren't smart enough to make it run off of power supplied by your doorbell alone, or trickle charge the battery fast enough during usage. From the factory, there wasn't enough charge on it to install it and test it's features completely out of the box. The hard-wiring will trickle charge a battery but if there's a lot of motion it will run it down and you will have to de-install and re-install the Ring device. The engineers didn't provide any sort of quick electrical connection disconnect mechanism either for the hard wiring XD!! The should have had some sort of automotive style quick-disconnect plug. Or even better yet, an external USB charging port that you could run an extension cord and charge up the doorbell in place or some sort of external solar charger. If the doorbell is on the side adjacent to the door, you will most likely need a 45 degree mount (separate purchase) in order to get a better view of the visitor. Very Very displeased with this company not being forthright with key installation and usage information.

I didn't buy this device here, I installed one purchased by a customer from Amazon.

The fish eye lens and picture are great, works great, but the battery/power situation was a big disappointment.

title: When Power Goes Off, Firmware gets Corrupted, and Router will not work
review_text:
When the router is working ,it's awesome. Range, speed, and setup are very easy. However, just like a bad musical performance, when things don't perform well, that's what people remember.

Here is why I cannot' give the product 5 stars.

There have been two situations where the router lost power and the firmware got corrupted and I had to reflash the router to make it work. I have NEVER had a device EVER get corrupted firmware. What a JOKE! Probably corrupted data issue as nothing will bring a system down like bad data.

Google: Router Power LED Blinks Slowly and Router No Longer Works

So rather than issue a RECALL on the defective merchandise, they do the next worst thing possible and give you some funky software called TFTP to download and fool around with to get the router re-flashed. Well, I thought the re-flash would correct the corrupted firmware. I got news for them, IT DIDN'T. I was moving my Router yesterday while the cable guy was here and then when we tried to hook everything back up, I got the blinking light of death again. I knew it was going to be a hassle to get the firmware downloaded and reflashed, so I switched back to an older working router for the time being.

In my opinion, NETGEAR should have done a 2 things amongst other things...

1) As an interim solution, Made special re-flash software that made upgrades a breeze. A one click solution to read the router's make/model MAC address and current firmware, and auto-magically download the new one and install it while PRESERVING all existing settings. It should also remember the OLD mac address and use it when you were migrating the settings to a router with a new MAC address. If their software engineering department can't do that, they need to be replaced starting with the Manager.

2) Recalled and Replaced the defective equipment for FREE, send out a new unit, and a postage paid return box for your old unit. Then use the above software to migrate the settings and old MAC address to the new unit so it works seamless with your existing cable model and service provider.

What do you call a router that does not work? An expensive paperweight? Can you say Regression Testing? Can you say Error Trapping Netgear? Words for the day for your Engineering Department. who worked on this product line.

title: Very Very Disappointed
review_text:
I see a lot of people stoked about this product, and at first I was. Until I tried to use it. Perhaps I just got a defective unit. Too many CONS to keep:

The biggest problem I had with the unit was inserting the MicroSD card, it just did not function properly. It was spring loaded and sometimes would shoot the micro sd card a few feet into the air. That can't be good for the card, and if it happens to go down a storm drain or get lost in a gravel bed, that's not good either. I would try to press it in, it wouldn't 'stick', do it again, and again, 15 minutes later I realized something wasn't quite right with the unit. Endless fumbling.

The unit should have an LED that when the card is inserted properly should glow green or something. (When the case was shut, it could stop the LED to save batteries or something.) The unit has cryptic LED blinks for diagnostics, doesn't help a lot when you don't have the manual handy and are missing the action you are supposed to be recording. It was a non-stop fumble trying to get the device to recognize the card. I bought good quaility SanDisk 32 gig chips, it seemed to recognize them after much fumbling, but only recorded 2gb out of the 32gigs before I had to change them. That's terrible. When you are on a backpacking trip, you don't exactly have access to a computer to see what's going on with the memory, you have to wait until you get home to find out you recorded nothing. If I put a new Memory stick in, it should perform a format/check sum to make sure the card is good and then let the user know it's been tested /accepted and the media is ready to be used. Not wait until your action moment has arrived, then just blink off.

The unit is durable, waterproof, and works sometimes....but not when I really wanted it to. The video looks grainy, it lacks much detail. I know my miniDV tape recorder 10 years ago was better. Forget about sound quality...it's terrible, unit needs external microphone.

PROS: Unit recorded in .MOV and was accessible by my Mac and PC via USB.
Unit is tough.
Unit seems to be waterproof, had it down about 8' in a stream under a waterfall. Although the unit said it was recording, it recorded nothing. I'm sooooo livid about that part.

Units going back. There are some other helmet cameras that are about 2x the money that I will gladly buy. Expensive is when the product is not worth the money. Caveat Emptor!

So far I'm a happy camper with this little Philips unit.  The only con is the brightness of the backlit display which is rather bright.  I placed the unit in a different part of the room where the remote still works but the brightness of the display doesn't affect my sleep.  I like a dark room!

title: Pass on this one--you can get better in this price range
review_text:
I bought into the hype and some early favorable 'professional' reviews on this product (and am now convinced the website that posted it was probably paid by Whistler to hype up the release) and purchased it back in late June. I could have easily gotten a similar quality product for much less...or better yet, spent more and got a better, more reliable unit. Convinced that it wasn't working as advertised, I purchased a V1, the 'King' of radar detectors, and compared them in my car side by side. First off, the 78SE gives TONS of false alarms. Often it would go off when the v1 wasn't making a peep. Sometimes, it would go crazy when I was out in the middle of a road surrounded by corn fields! Is this because it is more sensitive? I think not. I had tested them on some speed signs set up in my area, and the V1 would go off a 1/4 mile or more before the Whistler made a detection. A 1/4 mile in the world of radar is an eternity--the difference between getting a ticket and not. By the time the 78SE starting making weak little burps warning you to start being on the lookout, the V1 was already going off at full blast. The v1 would also detect the speed radar when it was up and over a hill--presumably from the minute signature bouncing off different objects alongside the road. Again, not a peep was heard from the 78SE.

I am not saying I expect the 78SE to be as good as a $400 V1. I do, however, expect the performance to be enough to serve its purpose, which is warning you of radar before the cop has your speed. This detector simply won't do that, which makes owning it more or less pointless IMO. The numerous false alerts make you on guard when you don't need to be, and eventually you will simply ignore all the warnings--even the legitimate ones. When the real threats arise, it is doubtful you will know before the cop has your speed--MAYBE it will provide a small benefit in the most optimal conditions (a flat road going perfectly straight)...but how often is that the case? Save your hard earned $$ for a detector that will work...or if your dead set on spending less than $200, do more research and see if you can find something better or at least cheaper!

title: Very Disappointed!!
review_text:
Very Disappointed!!
I replaced my 3.5 year old Dell XPS-8300 after several hardware failures, expecting this system to be much, much better since it has 2 times the faster DDS memory, a hybrid solid state drive, an 8 core faster processor over my 4 core i5, but in fact it's actually slower when working with Adobe applications like PhotoShop and InDesign. After 3 weeks of daily use, I have not experienced anything that seems like an improvement. I develop websites using Adobe Dreamweaver and MS Expression Web with lots a graphic content and have managed fine (OK) on my previous system except that it wore out. Maybe that's a contributing factor to my totally unimpressive more expensive, less capable new computer. Bottom line, the fastest processor and faster DDS RAM and solid state drives don't seem to add any power or performance so save your money and look for a Windows 7, Intel i5 if you can find one. Sometimes, you don't get what you pay for.. I wish I could have a 'do-over' but I have work to do with my so, so OK new computer.

title: this is an amazing little device
review_text:
For its size and price, this is an amazing little device. This thing is tiny and pretty easy to conceal. I only wish it came with some type of bracket to help mount in a vehicle. It has a very strange shape and some grooves on the side which appear like they were designed for some type of bracket to slide into. Ultimately, I will probably make something.

Video quality on the highest quality is amazingly good. It even does pretty well in low light conditions. Better than some similar devices I've tried. It has some default modes that will work without the widget, but you pretty much need to download and use it to take advantage of all its features. The widget seems pretty well designed and is fairly intuitive. I've had no problems using it. Audio could be better and in some situations it works pretty well, while other time its almost unintelligible. I believe this is just the nature of the little pinhole mike pick up. Results will vary based on the situation. I have found that sometimes the audio appears out of sync, but I'm not sure that doesn't have something to do with playback software. On the best quality, the files are pretty big and it will keep a processor busy watching the video.

Overall, it's a great little package that includes cables, power pack and just about everything you'll need except the mini SD card. Some of the earlier mini DVRs were poor quality and lacked features as well as cost a lot for the size convenience. This device takes the mini DVR to a whole new level that is light years beyond some of the earlier stuff. Having tried many other little minis, I can say that this just blows them all away and clearly has been developed to a much more advanced level.

Once you have played with it for awhile, you'll find endless uses. With a bit of creativity, concealment is pretty easy and battery life is quite good.

title: Another non-standard use
review_text:
I decided to take a chance and use this a bit differently than designed.

I have a Foscam WiFi security camera in a steel pole barn. Even with a high gain antenna on the camera and a fiberglass door, my connection was pretty bad. Choppy video and lost connections were common. I needed to get the antenna outside.

Although this antenna isn't outdoor rated, it is pretty easy to make watertight. Some tape over the mounting screw holes on the back and a little self vulcanizing rubber electrical tape around the antenna joint and no water is going to get in. You could use something like RTV silicone too. Keep the moisture out and you now made it outdoor capable. It was pretty close the way it comes and I'm sure it would probably be fine for a long time, but sealing it completely is pretty easy. The magnet mount works great on the steel siding. The camera I have, like most, comes with a standard SMA connector vs.the SMA-RP (reversed pin), but you can get an adapter here on Amazon. [[ASIN:B005H488Y4 SMA Male to SMA-RP Female Adapter]]

Added a 20 foot cable with standard SMA male and female connectors and now I have a great outdoor antenna for an indoor camera in a steel building that is great for blocking radio signals. It works very well and the results exceeded my expectations.

I've bought another antenna for the same setup on another camera. Although it isn't exactly what they intended it for, it works extremely well.

title: A lot of camera for the price
review_text:
I am a bit of a digital camera nut, having evolved from a film camera nut. I have more than few digitals including some top of the line Canons.

This is a great camera for the price. (In fact it would be a very good camera at twice the price.) I was attracted to it because of a very good experience with a much earlier version of a similar designed Fuji. I bought it about 10 years ago. I beat the daylights out of that camera. Even had a set of batteries leak in it. Cleaned it up and it was fine. It looks horrible now. All banged up and I use tape to keep the battery door closed on it. I used it as a "work" camera. My work takes me into some pretty nasty environments. But that old Fuji still works today. I wanted something just as good but with higher resolution.

The S4500 fulfilled all my wishes and more. This thing is packed with features, many found only on top of the line cameras. Great 30X zoom and 14MP. One key feature I was looking for is the electronic viewfinder. I grew up with film cameras and I still struggle to compose shots with a screen on the back. This gives you the choice of using the bright, easy to see, real through the lens, viewfinder or the built in 3" display. The electronic viewfinder does a couple really good things for you. For one, using a viewfinder instead of holding the camera in front of you, provides an incredibly stable shooting position. You can take shots at pretty low shutter speeds without blur, much better than you can suspending the camera in mid air so you can look at the display. The second big advantage is hugely extended battery life. That LCD display on any camera, eats up a lot of power. With the display shut off and using the EVF, battery life is incredible. One of my Canons is a very nice Powershot. Great 3" display too, but no EVF. That thing eats batteries.

Now if you are looking for a pocket camera, this isn't it. It has the look, feel and basic size of a traditional SLR 35mm film camera with a motor drive. It's not huge, but it isn't small enough to stuff in your pocket. It does have the feel of a film SLR which is something I find very desirable. That design is not just an accident and it produced some of the best photographs ever taken by film photographers. It is a great natural feel to me, but then I grew up with film.

I have been nothing but pleased with this camera. It is very high quality at an amazingly reasonable price. You can easily pay a lot more and get a lot less. All of the features are very nice if you are into photography as I am, but you can just as easily use it as a point and shoot camera and produce excellent photos. It is a great camera for someone looking to advance a bit in their photographic skills. This camera can take you there if you want to, but you don't need a degree to use it either. Use it point and shoot out of the box and then try different features as you go.

I have a lot of cameras, and for the money, I'd give this one "six stars" if I could. My previous experience with Fuji's tells me they are "bulletproof".

Just one last note. I would suggest getting a case for this camera. It is big enough that a case makes it easier to carry and provides some protection. The standard Fuji case for this camera is on Amazon for a surprisingly good price. It's pretty well made and a good investment.

title: Great addition to a great tablet
review_text:
I bought this at the same time I bought an Infinity TF700. I'm glad I did. I find screen touchpad typing difficult and I have pretty big hands. The keys on this are quite nice. Very good positive feel and comparable to most laptop keyboards. Complete set of Android function keys that cover just about everything. No need to be touching the screen. I wish the mouse pad was just a bit better. It's more than functional I guess. It's not bad, but it isn't great either. But I'm not a big fan of mouse pads anyway so I might be a bit over critical in this regard. .

The unit connects and disconnects nicely and has a lock lever which latches automatically. You can open it to about a 140 degree angle which makes getting a comforatble viewing angle possible in virtually any situation. If feels quite solid with no free play. Nice snug fit.

It gives you another battery too that adds 4.5 hours of uptime. You also get a standard sized USB 2.0 port and SD card reader. The USB port can operate in "host mode" allowing you to connect a variety of devices that should couple automatically. Can't say that I've used the USB a lot yet.

It is a very nice addition to a great tablet that gives you a laptop PC feel. It is tapered a little in thickness being a bit thicker at the back, but overall not much thicker than the tablet itself. Folded closed with the TF700 attached it's about 3/4 inch thick at the most and makes a nice sleek package. Connected together the two weigh right at 2.5 lbs.

The current price seems a bit high compared to other tablet's docking ports, but the keyboard is superior and the other features are quite nice. It's a worthwhile addition. I'd give it 5 stars if it were about $50 cheaper.

title: Great piece of technology
review_text:
I debated for a long time about getting a tablet. A couple years ago I'd have sworn that I'd never have one. I've been a laptop guy for a long time and love the PC, but it gets cumbersome some times. You can't do everything with a tablet that you can with a PC, but for most people it can fill most of your needs. Smart phones are nice but they're just to small for my eyes and big fingers. Besides, my view of cell phones is something to make calls with and talk on.

That said as I read and looked at different tablets, I realized the potential for their use. I've got issues with Apple and didn't want to go the ipad route for a number of reasons. I did some research on the new Windows tablets and I like the idea, but they've got a way to go. I think they rushed it to get it to market. I like the ideas behind Android and although a lot of the apps are designed more for smart phones, apps optimized for tablets are increasing and all the other smart phone designed apps work. The open source design makes for all sorts of obscure market apps. Plenty of developers out there. You can find some weird stuff for Android that you won't find on other platforms. Lots of pretty good free apps and plenty of cheap stuff too that is impressive.

So next I had to decide on size. For 99% of my uses, the 10 inch seemed to be the better choice and with a number of these with docking key pads available, I went that way rather than the smaller versions. So then I had to decide which one. It didn't take long to realize that ASUS was probably the leader in the field and known for very high quality products. Likewise it only took a bit longer to see that the Infinity TF700 with 64GB, was the machine to have. I also opted for the docking keypad.

The tablet is very impressive. The screen resolution is right up there with the best ipad. The NVIDIA quad core CPU is a screamer. Can't get much better. Cameras are very good. Battery life is good and amazing with the dock which also has a battery in it. With all the features together, I think this is the best Android tablet out there today and most pro revues agree.

As a new user to this scene, I'm sure others may have different ideas that got me to this choice, but I can say that I am completely satisfied. That said, as a "newbie" I suppose you might think anything would seem that way, however, I did a lot of research and hands on comparisons and I'm comfortable I bought the best.

I am 99.9% thrilled with it. If it has a flaw, it's probably the speaker which faces the wrong way in my opinion and doesn't have quite the volume and sound quality I'd like. It is fine in a quiet environment, but if there's any background noise it leaves a bit to be desired. I have found that if you hold it with your hand somewhat loosely cupped behind the speaker, the sound level improves dramatically as your hand reflects if towrd you. It is fine with ear buds and I also recently picked up a great little bluetooth speaker, (Clalrity HD by Monster), that kicks butt.

Everything else about the Infinity TF700 seems perfect. The only other way to make it better would be built in 4G and phone capability. If I'm mobile I use mine with a Verizon Jet Pack, which is an awesome device itself. Even on 3G it works better than my built in mobile broadband in my laptop.

Do your own research and get some hands on time if you can to compare because all tablets are not equal. There is no doubt that as far as tablets go, a lot has to do with how you will use it and what for. But if you want the best Android tablet in the 10 inch size range, you can't beat the Infinity TF700. This thing is awesome!

title: Not Great, but cheap
review_text:
At $13 it's a decent buy. It isn't the greatest, the instructions are poorly written and the build quality is marginal, but it does work pretty well. I'm giving it 4 stars just because it's price is so good. This thing is sold elsewhere for as much as $90.

The user interface, (button) is a bit confusing but once you play with it for awhile and figure it out, it does seem to work as described. The alignment of the camera with the little hole on mine was a bit off, but it was pretty easy to "tweak" it into alignment. The video quality isn't too bad as long as you have adequate lighting. It is an ingenious design but could have been implemented just a bit better. Still it is convincing enough and unobtrusive, The way it is made, it completely comes apart quite easily and I can see opportunities to retrofit the electronics into any number of other objects.

Overall, if you're not a little bit tech savy, you may have probelms with this, but it's a great buy for the money if you don't mind having to play with it a bit to get it to work the way you want.

title: Not fantastic but OK
review_text:
If you expect things to look like daylight, you'll be disappointed. It is far better than an old Russian unit I have which was an early generation light amplification unit, (green glow type). What you have here is a lot like a B&W security camera with an IR illuminator built into a hand held portable unit.

As some of the other reviews indicate, in the beginning it will seem somewhat cumbersome and clunky getting used to the controls and finding the most pleasing contrast settings. Takes a while, but once you get used to it, it gets a lot easier to make it work like you want it too.

One problem is that if you are just moving around in very low light and want to take a better look at things, it takes time for your eyes to adjust from darkness to the brightness in the viewfinder and then going back. The best way to use it is looking through it for an extended time scanning the area of interest, keeping your eye on the eyepiece. Different types of scenes will take some adjustment to optimize the appearance. Some things reflect light better than others so the best scenario is watching a particular area for an extended period. Once your eyes adjust and you get the contrast dialed in, it works pretty well. The IR illuminators are surprisingly pretty powerful. At short distances the high powered one will "wash out" what you're looking at, but it does seem to reach out pretty good. The claimed 600 feet is a bit of a stretch except under the most ideal of conditions. If you have some ambient light, I think it is better without it. But in really dark country night where you can't see your hand in front of your face, it does a great job of lighting things up.

My feelings on it are mixed. The basic idea of a monocular fits that role of "occasional use" where you want a quick better look at something, but I think that is asking too much from such a device. Plan on spending some time to get a better look at things because your eyes need adjustment time. Once you get the unit dialed in for the scene your watching, it will work pretty well. It's not cheap by any means, but it does work and it's a nice compact package. If you want really high performance night optics, plan on spending a lot more. It will definitely allow you to see reasonable well in darkness, but you have to fiddle with it. A lot has to do with the application. The pros and cons have given me some ideas about building a special purpose device.

Overall, it's a big improvement on some of the early night vision technology. The more I use it, the more I like it and learn tricks about using it effectively. I am happy with it, but for the average person with little experience with night vision, your expectations may not be met and that's why I'm giving it 3 stars. You will need a little patience to go through the learning curve using it.

Build quality feels pretty decent for the price; comfortable; buttons are easy to find with the headset on, and I've been putting them on while taking public transit, without playing anything, just so I can concentrate on reading, and not the prattle.

So, thumbs up. If you've not been happy with Bluetooth cans in the past and don't want to spend too much to check them out again, the August EP650 is a very good option.

title: PROBLEMS getting it to work
review_text: I bought this to back up my LG phone because I was forced to buy a new phone since LG no longer supports their phones and I was already starting to have issues with mine.  In buying a new phone, I was particularly freaked out about the possibility of losing my photos and other important files since the newer phones no longer have MicroSD cards for backup.  This seemed like a great option--along with backing up to Google and Amazon cloud services, it added another layer of protection.  The problem is that the C port didn't even fit into the C port on my phone--even though I took the case off my phone.  After essentially having to cram it in the port, I kept getting a warning that my data would be corrupted if I kept "ejecting" it.  It also wanted to back everything up to a MicroSD card, since it did not recognize that the SanDisk was even inserted into the phone.  Since I'd spent a considerable amount of time moving everything from my SD card to the internal memory of my phone in anticipation of having to transfer it to a new phone without a card slot, I most definitely didn't want to back up everything back onto my card, so I took the card out.  Even so, it still took quite some time for the phone to recognize the SanDisk, and finally start the back up.  From there, the process was fairly easy, BUT it should have never been so difficult to get the phone to recognize the SanDisk in the first place.  After the backup, I of course plugged the SanDisk into my laptop (without issues) and everything was indeed backed up.  It should NOT have been that difficult to plug the device into my phone however!  I will also mention, not that it's a big deal, but the device is considerably smaller than it looks to be on the Amazon website (less than .75x1.5").  At least I have an additional backup, but not as easily as I would have liked.  Given the issues I had with it I don't think I would purchase this particular device again.

title: easy set up, easy to add pics, has a lot of neat options, overall quite pleased.
review_text:
Frame is a tad slow to respond to the remote; that could be better. It isnt always slow, just sometimes it doesnt pic up, other times it is fast & perfectly fine. I think it has to do with distance from frame. Dont be too close!

They have a large frame with touchscreen available, so I would personally go with that unless price dictates otherwise. I like the remote too, just wish it responded faster and more consistently. I wouldn't want just a touchscreen. Option for either/both in one would be cool. Anyway.. I like this. It is my first frame. I have been kind of using our Echo Show, and sometimes just a computer screen. But I have wanted a basic frame, so here I am.

Basically plug it in, get it on the network, get the app, make an account, pair with phone, then select pics off phone to be loaded. Can choose up to 50 at a time. Very easy. Surprisingly so. I am tech savvy but impatient. This was pretty easy to figure out. Takes a few minutes to get them loaded.

Picture quality is quite good, and occasionally looks off. Thought that might be original source rather than the frame. All considered, all pics are quite clear and detailed.

if you have it set to full screen, then some pics may be cut off. If you have it set to the other option (cant remember the term), then the pics come up as you took them. Glad I figured this out because at first I had some that were cut off and it made me sad. Got it fixed very easily and all is well. YAY

Can set up calendar, weather, location, an alarm, play music, load videos. Can set time and make it a clock, can choose clock face. Can choose 12 hr or 24 hr format. Can create slide shows, decide on length of time, random or sequential or based on when taken. Very cool. Oh, and even incorporate music. Can label/add words/text too. Easy on, easy off.

Can operate basic stuff directly from the frame. Including very quickly rotating a pic. No need to use remote for everything!

Has headphone jack on back

It really isnt bad as an entry level frame. Would be nice as a gift if preloaded for someone. Now that I have been using this, I know what to look for in an upgrade. But this will certainly make do as i get to know it more and more. Ive only been playing with it for a day or so. The more I write about it, the more I like it.

I think pics can be emailed to this like Skylight subscription frame. Can let other people add photos.

Can also add photos/music/video via a SD/MC/SDHC, USB, USB mini, or thumb drive.

Needs to be plugged into wall receptacle.

Says in one of the product pictures that it can be wall mounted . I dont see how. It is a landscape mode item with a back portion to help it sit upright. It would not ever be flush with wall. I wouldnt buy it for that anyway. I got it for use on a side table so I can see pics of my dogs and cats all day long.

title: compact, mighty 5 blade fan w/ attached USB cord,  3 speeds, easy to use, travel worthy
review_text:
Dont need to pay much for a basic fan. This is a little guy, really quite nice for use at desk, at bedside, or on table next to favorite spot on couch. Simple press to turn on to low speed, then press again for a step higher, then press again for high speed, then finally press again for off. The fan can be tilted any which way.

Fan has 5 blades.

**Attached** USB power cord. Good long length! But just know that the one end is permanent part of the body. No swapping out for even longer cord.

Very slim profile. Doesn't create room moving air flow, but I didnt expect it to. But I can feel the air when it is very close by. I have several small fans of this sort, and they tend to perform in similar fashion. Manage your expectations and use this for up close gentle air flow. Or even use as a sound machine. Nice natural white noise.

FYI it is a tad loud at high speed

We dont have AC, save for a couple of window units (one in bedroom, one in office) but other than that, we rely on dressing for the weather, keeping hydrated, and making use of fans. Sometimes all I need is a little air movement near me. I love the small fans for their small footprint. This is the smallest yet as the casing is just a band of plastic. No feet (just flat grip strips), no clips, no excess. And this will be able to be powered up by a power bank or generator if the power goes out. Just 3 watts. Can even use it in car! Although it doesnt have a clip or a real base, it might be useful near or on exercise equipment (home or at gym).

I am giving it 5 stars for the class of fan it is (OK, 4.5 but we cant do halfsies). Small, personal, low watt, easy to travel with/carry around. Works for personal close use. It has its purpose. While I dont rate on price, I know that there are listings for the exact same product (some call it "upgraded"-- know that this is the exact same item) for a few dollars more. This is a good price point at $10 or less. As they get pricier, so do my demands and expectations, haha

title: worth the try, gorgeous clear display, ease of use, fits my 7" wrist,
review_text:
It's pretty good, especially if you dont need a name brand. It has a beautifully clear display. Easy to install app and pairs well with no hassle. Has all the bells and whistles of name brand products. While I prefer fitbit due to familiarity.

I havent put it entirely through its paces. I noticed that it was registering nearly same heart rate as my fitbit sense. I havent it worn it long enough to determine blood oxygen. There is still a lot to learn. The learning curve feels a little clunky compared to my fitbit.

Has ability to connect to Alexa, take and make calls, music. Can make changes through app or scroll through the screen face.

The watch band fits my 7" wrist and feels comfortable enough. Typical silicone band. It is attached via pins, so I imagine it is possible to swap it out but not sure. I may try some old bands to see if it is doable. I'd also prefer for it to have a soft protective cover (bumper guard) to protect screen and edges.

I still prefer the ease of using a name brand, but this has a good looking interface. Main thing is to see how accurate it is. I think it has been fine for heart rate, steps, but will need more sleep time for seeing how well it tracks sleep and oxygen.

I dont rate on price, but I comment. This is pretty reasonable, but it looks like there are many similar products for less. So compared to a name brand of similar features this is a bargain. Compared to other no name generics, this is competitive. Some are easily $20 less. I noticed the price on this vacillates. I think I got it for $70, and have seen it as low as 35-40.

title: trusted brand, always holds up, lightweight hard cover, folds back, attractive, comfy in hand
review_text:
Great case. I have been buying Moko products since my first Kindle some 10 years ago. The cases last longer than the Kindle does, haha. I get the same style and same design-- I like what I like, and so when it came to choosing another case for my new Kindle Paperwhite Signature edition, I simply went with Moko again. Design and colors hold up too!

I noticed they [[ASIN:B09HCFFP63 have a listing for half the price]]. I wasn't immediately aware of the difference between that one and this one. It took a little poking around to determine that this is a hard cover (like all my others) and the other is more of a firm soft cover. I think either would be fine, but I really just wanted to go with what was familiar to me. I mention this in case you are also noticing the 2 products and are curious of the difference. I noticed one review over on the other page saying that the quality was different and they were disappointed. But what I concluded is that they were used to THIS product, and bought THAT product. It is two different products! Nothing changed! This is a hard cover and that is a soft cover. If all you do is keep your kindle at the bedside, then the other is just fine as a dust cover and added grip. If you tend to travel with your Kindle or are more likely to drop it or bump it, then the hard cover such as this is great.

It isnt heavy. The cover folds back. Adds just enough additional grip to feel much better than a plain/naked kindle.

Just pop the kindle into the cradle, and then that's it.

I do not have a wireless charger, but this is supposed to work with it without need to pop the kindle out. I trust Moko and will assume that is true if I ever get one.

title: ultra comfy, the most comfortable of any band I have ever used in 8 years of fitbit use
review_text:
Been wearing mine for a couple of weeks now, and I am very pleased. I only take it off to charge and to shower. Just a good fit and feel. I can customize how snug or loose I want it with ease. Very happy!

Two reasons that led me to ordering new Fitbit Sense bands:
1. I usually use the silicone bands, but the last set I bought weren't quite long enough leaving me fearful that I would lose my pricy smart watch. So I wanted a band that felt secure.

title: responsive touchscreen, sharp looking! wireless keyboard (no dongle needed), & wireless mouse
review_text:
This review is for the 12th Generation Intel Core i3-1215U w/ Intel UHD graphics

I like it so much that I would buy this again if I didn't already have a high performance gaming desktop, and a new lap top of similar specs to this Dell All in One. Know what you need your computer for. No fair in comparing it to a high end system required for gaming and huge programs when it is designed for home office use. This is excellent for typical web browsing, youtube watching, solitaire/mahjongg playing, video calling, office basics. It is plenty enough memory and processing power for shopping and watching cat videos. It's lovely. Would I try to run an MMO-RPG or a huge photo editing studio on it? Probably not.

I love it though, it is gorgeous, responsive, and I love the touch screen. It feels so intuitive. However, I got it with my mom in mind as she hasn't had an actual computer in several years (been living off tablet only). I set it up very quickly. Very easy.

Some observations off top of my head:

--The legs of the stand just snap on. Very sturdy, and attractive.

--The wireless keyboard just takes three AAA batteries (included) NO DONGLE REQUIRED. Just turn on, and it instantly pairs with the computer. As for the mouse, it takes one AA battery (Inlcuded) and uses a usb dongle. Also needs to be switched to on position.

--Windows 11, has many of the typical bells and whistles. Free Disney+ for 6 months (no idea of what is expected for that, I didnt check into it other than seeing the icon on the desktop)

--Very quiet. Is it on? is it off? very quiet.

--Love the white and silver appearance. Nice change from black. While I dont mind what color the computer is, my mom always preferred a lighter color for use on her large kitchen counter. This fits that need. Clean looking motif.

--Touch screen is just way too cool. I havent had experience yet with using a desktop with a touch screen. It just feels so intuitive. Just touch the screen to make things happen. LOVE!

--Web Camera is a "pop up" out from the topside of the monitor. So you will know if it is on or not. I like this for that reason, and it makes the overall appearance look nice and clean. But since it is an extra part of the sort, it brings to mind chance of breakdown. Just press down and it pops up. Takes picture and video as expected. Resolution of both is typical. Clear but nothing fancy.

--Sound is fine, visuals are fine.

--Built in card reader, 2 HDMI ports, 4 USB ports, 1 USB C port, Ethernet port, 1 audio port

--Good amount of weight-- it feels secure. At no point did I feel like it was going to move, or tip over.

--Screen tilts back or forward. I found this nice as it is sitting on a large kitchen counter, and sometimes it will be used while standing, and other times with butt parked on a bar stool.

--Keyboard tucks in between legs for cleaned up look.

--Information that comes with it is sparse. Very basic start instructions (I didnt need), warranty info (detailed), and a card that provides directions on downloading a Dell app for added assistance and information. I thought maybe a PDF would be available on this product page or on their website, but I didnt see one. I will have to try their app and see what sort of info is available. I really wont need it myself, but I want to make sure my mom has access to info.

Overall, it wasnt hard for me to conclude that this is a nice computer. It will take more time with it to truly see how it does. For that, I will come back to update if/as needed. My instant love of the touchscreen and how responsive everything is made me a little envious. At this time, I would recommend it. If you find you might want to spring for a little more hard disk size, then they also offer a 512 GB with 8 gig memory. This has 256 GB hard disk with 8 gig memory.

Going with 5 stars as it meets or exceeds my expectations. Again, know what you want this for and choose accordingly. I dont rate on price, but it is a reasonable price for what you get, how it looks. Ooh, and that sweet sweet touchscreen!

title: responsive, quick. Good machine for most needs, see data sheet link for details
review_text:
Not sure why anyone thought this is a touchscreen. Nowhere does it mention it. Take a look under "Product Guides and Documents", which you can find just above the review section. There you will see is a highlighted link to the "SPECIFICATION SHEET (PDF)". Click on that, and it will tell you even more detail about this machine than what is already outlined in the product description. And because of that, I wont rehash all what this has. But look for that link so you can decide if it has what you need!!!

For those saying that this does not have a finger print ID? YES IT DOES. Search for it in your settings. IT IS A SETTING that you must set up. Hit the magnifying glass icon, then type in "fingerprint sign-in". Follow instructions. Can also set for using a PIN, which I do.

Overall, it is a good basic laptop. Enough memory to load some photos and videos, plenty of processing power for a lot of basic uses: watching video, email, internet browsing, low end games. Likely good for most school needs, and some office needs. I haven't pushed it to the max because my needs are fairly low end. I have a separate high end desktop for true gaming needs, and for mega storage. Cant blame a machine for not doing what you want if you dont know anything about it to start. Learn what 8 gb ram is and what 512 gb ssd can do for you, and know what your needs are. Work up, or down from there. This seemed to be the sweet spot for my casual needs.

It runs smoothly, quietly, and cool. Battery lasts a long while, which is nice for on the go use. Your experience may vary. Depends on what you are doing, your settings, etc.

Very responsive, though like I said I havent put it through the paces.

Even Microsoft Edge is blazing quick and easy to use. I had it on my last laptop (half the memory and processing) and it was all I could run. I figured I would be switching to firefox, but I keep using Edge without issue.

Responsive touchpad, though since I prefer using a mouse I turned off the touchpad.

Optional backlit keyboard. Can turn on or off, or up at any time with press of button

Quickly boots up, good instant connectivity

Speakers are fine. Crisp. They are perfectly good, and offer some mild range. They dont make my ears bleed when I watch a music video.

ONLY thing I have experienced that has been bothersome is that sometimes my "m" key doesnt register. I will be typing along, and the letter m did not actually type. However, it is hit and miss, and it might be a matter of how I am sitting or something. I havent had the experience while writing this review. Unless you notice missing m's that I didnt.

I' pleased. So far so good. I am giving it 5 stars (4.5 if we could do half ratings), and am giving it that for the CLASS of laptop, and that it is what the product description says it is. Minor annoyances regarding anti virus, updates, microsoft stuff is typical across computers. All in all, it is what I expected, nothing negative that I can think of, and if I experience anything else worth sharing--good, bad, or otherwise-- I will do so. I keep up with my reviews. I am an avid reviewer and aim to be helpful as much as possible.

title: solar charge actually works, good assortment of features,
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:17a58332b933800fe99b76e58398768d]] We have a few of these emergency radios. I am the main prepper in the household, but even my husband bought one at random recently. He showed me his, then I showed him mine. Then I got this one to add to the collection. Different brands, all very similar. The one feature that STANDS OUT to me on this FORTECLEAR is that there is a light that indicates that it is being charged. I can see it glow brighter when using the hand crank, as well as when I have it sitting in a ray of sunshine. If in the sun with the light glowing, once I cover the solar panel with my hand, the indicator turns off. Really nice to see that working. Like others, there is also an indicator that shows about what percent of power is has (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) which will light up when it is being actively used. Really nice to be able to see this important info. For that I recommend this as an emergency item (or even casual use, why not?)

Has typical features such as flashlight (low beam, high beam, and flashing), has a flip up "reading" light, and radio bands such as alert, WB, FM, and AM. Nice long antennae, knob tuning, knob volume control. USB port, USB C port, comes with a cord & instructions, wrist strap, has SOS alarm- which requires pressing for a couple of seconds to activate, SO much better than another where I have accidentally triggered it by a simple short press. Scared myself. LOL. SO LOUD.

When looking for weather band, you may need to walk around to get a signal. I find this true of all emergency radios, or any radio with WB/NOLA option. As with most all other radios, FM comes in the best, the easiest.

I am a big fan of having multiple options for lighting- whether it be solar, battery operated, internal battery that can be charged, etc. This has the ability to be charged, to be hand cranked, and to be solar charged. Nice to have a few options in one device. I also keep regular flashlights, rechargeable flashlights, battery powered radios, etc on hand. Multiple options for when it is needed. But this will be one I will rely on. I would get it again, and I would get this for someone else. I tend to give functional gifts, stuff that most folks dont want to buy for themselves (preps, fire extinguishers, smoke alarms, car care kits, etc), and this would be a good one to give. Really pleased that it works so well because it happens to be a few bucks more than most options out there.

I will continue to play around with this. If I think of anything else, or experience anything else (good or bad) I will be sure to come back to update. So far so good!

title: good price for a must have prep item, keep one at home, at office, in car, on person, etc
review_text:
Another good one. Been restocking my radios, making sure I have a couple in the house, one in each car, and even one on my person. A basic radio is a must have for shelter space, emergency kits, keeping in car, having as part of Get Home or Bug out Bag. I have a thing for battery operated radios, and recently acquired a few more at the same time (2 is 1, 1 is none). I keep them everywhere because you never know when the need for info from the outside world will be needed, and right now that seems more relevant than ever *vaguely waves arm around*.

I have to say, other than price and a few details, the functions and overall performance are the same. This is a (refreshing) bargain at $9.99. For that, I recommend this.

I have found that radios of this style pretty much all work the same, sound the same. Just look for details that are of interest to you. When it comes to this Prunus radio, I like the small size. Not as small as another one I have, but close. It fits in palm of my hand, almost reminds me of my old portable cassette player. My thumb desperately wants to push a button, haha. Easily will slip into a pocket, hiking bag, purse, glove compartment, desk drawer, etc, . Roughly 5" x 2.75" x 1.25".

Has AM, FM, and WB. I can tune in to the weather band with some effort--so be patient. I tried it on a dark rainy day from inside my house, and with antennae fully extended I just moved it all around until I caught a signal. The sound was faint, but I got it. It will suffice in an emergency. As for FM, that is clearest (usually is), followed by AM. Works well and as expected. Sound overall is clear. I find that it could work as a portable sound machine. Just find a station or range of frequency that doesn't have a working channel. White noise!

Takes 2 AA batteries (not included), and has a standard ear phone jack port. Includes a wrist strap, and also has a belt clip (clip to whatever you want, nice addition for on the go use). I find the belt clip adds appeal as I keep a tactical back pack in my car, and this would slip no problem into a molle loop.

Another pro: Big numbers/letters--easy to see! Overall dimensions fit nicely in my hand. Adjustable volume is plenty loud. Very long antennae.

5 stars. No problems, works well, easy to use/manipulate, meets expectations, glad to have it. I'd buy it again, buy it for others.

title: so many features, easy to use face & app, responsive to touch, waterproof, check it out!
review_text:
This product description doesn't do this product justice. I am impressed. I am already a fan of Sanag products, so I expected this to be good. It is. I'll list everything I can think of below.

I have been looking for an easy to use fitness watch for my 70+ years old mom. She mentioned interest in one, but I am not sure how much she will enjoy it. While I like fitbit (been using that brand since 2015) I didnt want to get her one if she wouldnt like the technology. I looked through what I already own, but nothing seemed right. I have a garmin that I wouldnt have anyone new to fitness watches use (hate that thing). I have an Amazon Halo, which is great but its attached to my account so I cant have her try it. And I have a weird off brand tracker that I got a few years ago that it too complicated to use (clunky app, slow to respond swiping). I basically need a tracker to be easy to use (both the tracker and the app) and be something I feel comfortable having my tech adverse mom use. I chose this based on what I read in the description AND my positive experience so far with Sanag.

I figured I would try this watch for a couple of weeks before deciding if it would work for her. I have been wearing it day and night for a little over a week, and I may not give it to her.. because I love it. haha

I'm just going to bullet point the features I have noticed so far:

--waterproof. I wear it 24/7. Though I do take off for showering, I am just used to doing that. I also clean homes for living, and this can take a beating.

-- easy to find, install, and use App (da fit), many customizations, options to set up.

--pairs easily with bluetooth; no hassle.

--interesting color, nice feeling band. Very secure feeling. Though, I'd prefer the band to be a little longer.
I have a 7" wrist, and this just fits. Will be fine for my mom who has very petite bone structure.

--super long battery life. I charge my fitbit sense every other day. Other than initial charge, I have not yet had to charge this. I'd say they are accurate on their 7-14 day charge on normal use, or 30 days on standby. That being said..

-- blood O2 measurment is on demand. Not automatic. Just go into watch face or app to measure. It keeps track. Heart rate can be continuous measurement or on demand.

--Can choose from many many many watch faces. So many different styles, some are super cute. Different faces depending on what you want to see, ie just the time, time and date, time, date, steps, hr, cals burned, etc. If you have a few that you like, then you can scroll through what you have used in your watch itself to to select one, or you can go to the app to select one.

--steps are accurate as far as side by side with my Fit bit Sense. Same steps (within 20 steps) when worn side by side on same wrist.

--gorgeous display- very colorful and easy to read

--easy to navigate with swiping; very responsive. Easy to back out from selections.

--on watch can see time, date, steps, heart rate, 02, blood pressure (havent checked yet for accuracy but I will), weather, sleep data, exercise specific date (and tracking), alarms, timers, music control, camera shutter control, and settings notifications (can set up to see notifications from many sources such as email, phone calls, texts, FB, IG, Whatsapp, etc etc ect-- huge list that can be turned on for notifications to allow to come through if you want. Can pick and choose).

--on watch can select options such as "do not disturb", brightness settings, lock option,
--can connect to google fit
--can keep track of other health trends (menstrual, for example).
--can set a step goal, reminders to move, reminders to drink water

I am not sure if there is a spot to adjust how long the face stays lit when looking at something. As of now, it goes black after a few seconds. Much like other fitness watches.

--App has all this same info, with ability to look at more details

--VERY easy to navigate app.

REALLY an impressive gadget. I think some of it will come down to preference. I am still getting used to it, and sometimes I find the outer button is easily pressed by my bent wrist. I have accidentally changed my watch face that way, but I am seeing now that if I end up on that screen I have to make sure I am setting the face by swiping up (otherwise navigates to another face by swiping left/right). Litte annoyances that will vary.

For all that it offers, for the ease of use especially compared to some name brands, I am compelled to go 5 stars. If we could do half stars, maybe 4.5. But I like it more than 4 stars. Overall nothing glaring bad or super negative comes to mind. I'll update as I learn more or think of more, or experience something different (good or bad).

reasonable price at $79 (though I had a coupon which really helped make my decision), any higher and I would go with namebrand.

title: easy to set up, grab an SD card (up to 128 GB), then enjoy the added security & viewing
review_text:
Overall, I'm pleased with the features. Really no major cons, and the pros are solid. 4.5 stars (well, 5 stars since we cant so half rating and I like it better than 4 stars since I may buy another). I cant see why anyone would dislike it, and so far haven't seen any reviews saying anything that gives red flags.

We have several security cameras, but I have a couple of spots that I want to incorporate some redundancy, and a better angle/view. This being solar powered helps greatly to achieve that. Make sure to get the CloudEdge app, and from there just install and follow all directions. Makes for a nice entryway camera if you dont want to install a doorbell style.

We have been having some bad winter weather, so it took me awhile to get it set up, and the spot I put it has had so much snowfall that no one is walking near where it is installed, not even me. However imaging is good. Same or better than my current set up. Audio is good, if not better.

Main aspects I like.. EASY set up. No fancy skills or tools needed. No need for power source other than some sun. That can be tricky for stretches of darkness, but the big battery stores a lot of power. No issues thus far. The 4dbi dual antenna ensures that the solar security camera has stable network reception, and quickly connects to 2.4Ghz WiFi from a longer distance.

If you dont want to pay for cloud storage, then grab a 128 GB storage card.

I dont rate on price, but I do comment. For the price with $50 coupon, this is something I am considering buying another of for another area of house. Could be a trail cam if you have the wifi connectivity to reach. I might get one for my 70+ years old mom so she can have the added security of seeing who is coming to the door.

I also appreciate all the information on the product page. That always factors into my rating. I also appreciate that they seem to be open to contact if need be. That is reasurring in terms of customer service, and is what helped me decide to go with this Jeeber product over others.

So far so good, if I experience anything else I will be back to update

title: comfortable, good sound, sits securely over ears, plenty of options, very pleased
review_text:
LOVE these over the ear air conduction earphones. I have a pair of bone conduction earphones that I fell in love with, and I wanted another pair of different style to for use when working out (my others stay at bedside for evening podcast listening, music, meditation). These looked like they hook over the ear securely, and they do! If new to this style, be prepared to play around with them a bit, and take advantage of the ear plugs as they help deepen the sound. I personally find the sound to be good and clear. I have some auditory sensitivities, and these just feel right- no irritations, aggravations, or off sounds.

The reason why I dont use IN ear ear buds is because they always bother me- usually pain or some headache or nausea ensues. I can wear them for short periods of time as needed, but I do not enjoy them for longer duration- ie listening to music while working out. I can never find just regular headphones that hook over the ears without going in. So that is basically how I got to know bone conduction. Now that style is my go to. I also like that I can still sense/hear what is around me with these, again perfect for working out. Being waterproof puts me at ease when I sweat profusely.

Pair with a bluetooth MP3 player, or add to memory card for direct play through the headset.

Good price, good quality, so far really good experience. I recommend!
