title: so far so good, excellent clarity, accurate steps & heart rate, easy set up
review_text:
Probably want to select reviews based on "most recent" as that will provide you with most up to date and relevant information pertaining to this product. I acquired my Fitbit Sense in June 2021, it has not yet been a month, but so far so good with 24/7 use. I am slow to check out and use all the features, but what I have interacted with so far has been stellar.

I have been using Fitbit products since April 2015- kinda have a love/hate relationship with this brand. I use the activity tracker constantly, and I greatly enjoy the app. So I have stuck with it as I upgraded over the years (Charge x2, Blaze x2, Versa 2, and now Sense). As with many Fitbit users, there is a known frustration with the products. Despite some of my own qualms, and having the ability to spend whatever I want on any fitness tracker I want, I still end up (so far) with this brand. Mostly because I haven't found a tracker and app that I totally like better. I even have a Garmin, but I find that so far off base of accuracy (save for HR), that it is a glorified watch. Garmin seems to do best for actual intended activities (going for a run, going for a long walk, going cycling) where it seems to not be accurate in steps for any other part of the day (only counts about 1/3 of actual steps unless engaged in a longer duration activity, and even then it takes a few minutes for it to start). Also, the app seems to have a lot of info, but doent really tell me anything. That being said, when it was time for me to buy another fitness tracker--I went from Versa 2 to Garmin.. back to Fitbit. I went with the Sense because the price was right, and it was an upgrade over the Versa 2. After my underwhelming experience with the Garmin, I would have happily taken over a 2nd hand Charge from 2015. At least my steps would be accurate.

Ok, so back to the Sense. WOW, the visual on the screen is really clear and precise. Even way more so over the Versa 2, and I had no issues with that. Set up was EASY, and QUICK. Basically, just like in adding any other fitbit, just let it pair and it will very quickly be all set and ready to go. I didnt have any weird upselling offerings, or at least nothing that wasn't fantastically easy to opt out from. Nothing shady that I saw.

ONE POINT that I DO think is important to know is that if you happen to have a Versa 2 (Not sure if this also happens with regular Versa, Versa Lite, or Versa 3), but this could not be added alongside my Versa 2. I had to take the Versa 2 offline in order to add this Sense. I know this is the case with trying to add more than one of the same products, yet I have always been able to have several Fitbits paired no problem, as long as they were different models. SO, I guess the Fitbit app sees Sense and Versa 2 as the same. Not a big deal as my Versa 2 had essentially died after I wore it on a hot humid day and my sweat killed it (then I brought it back to life after putting it in a bag of rice for about a week, Then afterward the battery was never the same. It drained to nothing daily.. and I needed to not have to worry about daily charging.. hence my picking up a Garmin in the interim to see if I liked them enough to spring for a more fancy model--nope-- and ended up buying the Sense.)

Hope it lasts. I love the look. The band is way better than the old pin style. Swapping out bands is so much quicker, easier, less need for super fine motor skills. LOVE the charger. It just sort of magnetizes to the fitbit. No need to clip in.

SP02 wasn't the main feature I was drawn to, but in order to have accurate use it seems a special clock face is needed, and that clock face will drain battery quicker (from what I have read). That being said,

Battery life has been excellent for me.

Love being able to add other apps, and features. Scrolling is easy, turning face on/off is not complicated.

HEART RATE is accurate. I have tested it against my garmin, two blood pressure devices, and a doctors appointment. All saying the same.

Also, I the voice assistant is great. You can choose GOOGLE Assistant, OR Alexa. This is why selecting most recent reviews on this sort of stuff is important, as the early release of Sense did not have Google Assistant, but would soon with an update. True, and they followed through as I have it.

AT THIS TIME, I have ZERO issues, concerns with this Fitbit Sense. I will be back to update as I learn more, or if I have anything worth sharing that is bad. I keep up with my reviews as needed.

title: COMFORTABLE & CUTE! no fuss, super comfy, adjustable, stays in place, would buy more!
review_text:
If you want added comfort and easy of taking on and off, then try this elastic band!!

Finally, a nice elastic band that isn't a scrunchy. I actually keep a hair scrunchie on my wrist, but I dont want it to compete with my fit bit. So I'm pleased to have found a band for my Versa2 that is not only elastic, but is cute, AND adjustable. What is not to love?

This elastic band has lots of room to accommodate various sized wrists. My wrist is just at the 7" mark, and it is very comfortable. Can easily be made more loose or snug for a perfect unique fit. It is so comfortable, I barely feel like this is on my wrist. It just sits so naturally on my wrist, like it moves with it. Yet is so perfectly snug, that it doesn't move around (unless I intentionally loosen it up). Best feeling band I have ever used (and I have had fitbits since 2015!)

I bought the "Black Colorful Floral" band, and it is lovely. If you like printed bands, I want to point out one very important consideration that makes this stand out over other printed bands. I have tried wearing other colorful bands, but they are usually a design printed on a silicone band. What happens after awhile is that the print wears off the band, and what is left is a solid color band that looks junky. I have tried a few over the years (because I always hope that something changed, and I really want a print) and I am always disappointed after a short while. SO with this band being an actual cloth material (just elastic), the print wont be rubbing off. I'm so pleased with this band :)

Then lastly, I always have a "bumper" (protector) on Versa2, and I have lots of colors that I can switch to, so between this band and all my color options with the bumper, I have a different look whenever I want it! The bumpers, for reference :https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0859VXSPH/

I love this band and may add more to my collection. I definitely recommend!!

title: petite, light, digital display, front controls, remote w/ batteries, plug n play

title: top load, front display, comes w/ remote (INC batteries!), HDMI, USB power, inc Earbuds
review_text:
Compact, super lightweight, easy set up. There is an HDMI cord, and a USB power cord. Depending on how you plan to power up, you can use the USB side, or you will need to supply your own wall adapter, or your own USB-C adapter.
I wanted a DVD player for our spare room tv. I was looking at plain DVD players, and wanted something on the small side as well as something I could use with another tv or computer. This came up as an option, and I decided to take my chance on it (initially thought it pricey for a mini DVD player--but if it worked, then it would have been a good purchase).

It meets all my needs. I wanted it to have a display, and a remote. It has both. It is super easy to set up-- just plug in the two cords --HDMI from DVD player to TV/monitor and power cord (plug mini USB into DVD player, then plug USB into a USB port or wall adapter). DONE! There is a small front display to show track time. There is a power button, volume dial, pause/play, forward, reverse. So remote can be used or can make adjustments directly on unit. Headphone port. Comes with ear buds! Top load. Included a sturdy remote that comes with batteries!

Picture quality and response is spot on. No issues with sounds. No issues at all!

Everything works. I tried everything on it. I tried it on two tvs and a monitor (it is that easy to use). I kept a DVD going for a few hours (season 1 the office) and no issues.

I have tried both a store bought DVD and a rewritable. Both worked fine.

I noticed a slight pause when I was messing around with the cords (working on cord management when putting in the main spot I plan to keep it). So I am not sure how it would be for "active" use. I dont plan to move around with it.

So far, I am quite pleased with this unit. Meets all my needs. If I learn anything else, or experience anything else worth sharing, I will be back to do so.

My colorful band is dwindling down to a solid white band.

Buy it if you don't mind the design wearing off quickly. Buy it if you need/want a certain look for about a week before it disappears. But don't buy if you think it will last It just wont.

It recommends to keep on charger when not in use.

Possibly a good set of walkie-talkies for hunting with pals. Too early to tell. Outside of that, the main use is at the house- either within our two story house or when one of us is outside and one is inside. It is a convenience item for that reason. I think it will become a part of our camping or hiking items. Just a redundancy in ability to communicate as needed.

The units look and feel durable. They have the heft of a cordless phone and the buttons are responsive.

Can have more units added on.

4 stars because we haven't put it through its paces entirely. Will update as we learn, experience more.

title: impressive noise cacelling, easy set up, hurts my ears after awhile
review_text:
My primary use is simply to have a set of headphones for listening to music or watching videos. It has a built in microphone but I haven't used it for phone calls or giving commands. Not sure if I will.

The set up is easy. 1st, my pair came fully charged, and it has yet to need a charge, so I do not know how long it takes to charge from dead. It has a USB charging cord and it came with some other audio plugs. It paired easily with my phone. Just had to press and hold the center button for it to turn on the bluetooth function. The box did not come with instructions, but there is a link to their PDF manual on this product page under "product information" and then to the far right is, "Technical Specification". The link is under that.

The headphones can be used as a regular set- you will hear your music, as well as other environmental sounds, OR you can turn the Noise Cancelling feature to ON, and then you will notice a drastic reduction in other sounds. It says that it will reduce most sounds but human voices may still be heard. I had them on in our bedroom. My husband likes to watch tv, and I find it distracting, and loud. We also have the AC on, which adds to the noisy atmosphere. When I put these on, the sounds were mildly muffled. When I turned on the Noise Cancelling feature, the sound of the AC pretty much disappeared. So weird. The sounds from the tv were greatly reduced, though I could actually hear the person talking a little more clearly since the AC sound pretty much disappeared.

So yeh, it all functions as it should.

The controls on the side take some getting used to--figuring out which button does what without having to take the headphones off. I recommend practicing- long press to advance or back up a song, short press to turn up/down volume, etc.

The headphones are comfortable and accommodate my big head. They are adjustable. I like that they can be folded.

My only dislike, which can be a big one is that they hurt my ears after awhile. Not sure what it is, but my head feels like it is dragged down and my ears along with it. I really dont know what causes that, and if it as feature of these or something with my structure. Has a low level pain/discomfort associated with it. I can maybe use them for 45 minutes or so, then I need them off or simply take a break. You may not experience this.

To turn Bluetooth off (and save charge), you must remember to press that center button again. Turning the noise cancellation feature on/off does not do anything in that regard.

title: helped clean up my seriously gross keyboard, smells fresh & clean, scent doesn't linger
review_text:
EDIT: added pictures.

Not bad, about what I imagined having never used a gel glob like this before (but having wanted to for a long time!).

I have only used it on my keyboard. It is my main reason for acquiring it. I am always grossed out by how my keyboard looks. I sometimes use canned air (but ran out) and disinfectant wipes. I really just wanted to see if I could do better with a cleaning glob. I just wanted to know!

It did a great job with the surface of the keys. They look polished and shiny, and not at all greasy nor grimy. I would say it took more effort to get further down the sides, but I may have been too careful/light with my effort. I think next time I will really pressed into the keys and hopefully I can just work the stuff down the sides easier. Going forward, I would still use canned air to get anything out that is deeper down below the keys. And, still using a disinfectant wipe is a good idea these days. I think I will use this as maintenance rather than for going after a super gross keyboard. I like the scent- it smells fresh and clean. Doesn't linger, but while using it it is rather nice.

The look of it after using it to clean my keyboard really makes me want to hurl. I am not sure how often this can be reused, or if it would be better as a one time project use. I mean, it is meant to be used over and over, just not sure if I want to. Again, I think I like the idea of using it as a maintenance item if I plan to use it over and over. There is a little diagram on the container showing how to check if it needs replacing. It doesn't say much, but I surmise that if it goes from the bright color to a dark color, then it needs to be replaced.

Anyway, I think it is worth the try. It really does grab onto the nasty things and pulls it off/out. This wasn't too pricey, and I think stuff like this could be added on to a themed gift- like a car/truck lovers gift, an office supplies gift, and so on. Who knows.

There is some info on the container (a small clear plastic container with screw on lid, and labeling all around) that I will list here:

Directions say:
-- "Do not rub just press!" as well as, "Use with body hands" (lost in translation? maybe means both hands, or put your body into it?)

--Absorbs dirt and dust in cavities. Ideal for all devices and surfaces

--Keep away from direct sunlight and keep in a dry place. Keep away from children, don't eat it

--Ingredients:
Vegetable gum, Bactericide, Quaternium, fragrance, glycerin.

--Made in China

review_text:
Slick, small. The main aspect that I like about this is not having to change the batteries. It seems to hold a charge for quite some time (I have been using it nightly for a couple of weeks straight out from box; have yet to actually charge it). When not in use, the dongle is stored on bottom of mouse. It has a little magnetic port that it slides into.

Overall, it works perfectly fine. Smooth-- I use a colorful mouse pad most of the time, but sometimes solid black.

title: easy set up, adds boost to sound/dimesnion/volume compared to internal smart tv speakers,
review_text:

We would see.. er, hear. So I tasked my husband with replacing our other sound bar with this set. It took him very little time to get it set up (less than 10 minutes, and it only took that long because our cat was helping. "helping").

The sound is definitely better and clearer than just using the speakers the tv comes with (which is usually the case). The sound is on par with the sound bar we had been using, except with the added dimension that the subwoofer provides. Without the subwoofer, it sounds just louder. With the subwoofer, it adds some depth and a nicer overall sound. We really just needed our tv to be louder. Cable is typically loud, but some programs on the various streaming services we have all have different levels of audio, with many being much too quiet. So better speakers have helped a lot.

The subwoofer connects to the soundbar via bluetooth. Both plug in, so plan to have 2 open spots in your power bar or wall receptacle. We have this system set up so the volume can be adjusted using the smart tv remote, rather than having to use the remote it came with. No issues there at all. Easy!

While I have the soundbar directly under the tv, I have the subwoofer set up in a corner a few feet away

The soundbar has spots in the rear in case you want to mount it to a wall. Subwoofer, does not.

Both are basic and minimalist looking. Subwoofer is black on black, soundbar is black with dark gray. No obnoxious branding or colors.

The instruction booklet is thorough, including information about the remote, battery info, placement and mounting, general operation, bluetooth operation, AUX in operation, Line-in operation, Optical-in operation (which is what I am using for use with my tv).

Overall sound is decent. Not home theater experience, but it definitely provides a sound and volume boost to internal tv speakers. I haven't yet tried it as a speaker for music. I really only purchased my original soundbar for use with tv (and replaced it with this for same purpose). I may give it a try anyway sometime soon. If I do, I will report back on how it does.

I like the added dimension that the subwoofer provides. I like the overall aesthetic. And because the combination of the two allows me to hear shows better than just using the tv speakers (on low audio streaming, as cable is always loud), I am pleased to use this.

I don't know hat this product costs, so I can't compare it. But, in short, it is about the same as just about any other low to mid priced soundbar. This is better sounding with addition of subwoofer. Not amazing, but definitely adds to my listening experience. 4 stars so far.

When this item came up as an option for review I figured it would an interesting item to try out since it has the addition of a subwoofer. Maybe it would be louder? Maybe it would sound more dynamic? We would see.. er, hear. So I tasked my husband with replacing our other sound bar with this set. It took him very little time to get it set up (less than 10 minutes, and it only took that long because our cat was helping. "helping").

The sound is definitely better and clearer than just using the speakers the tv comes with (which is usually the case). The sound is on par with the sound bar we had been using, except with the added dimension that the subwoofer provides. Without the subwoofer, it sounds just louder. With the subwoofer, it adds some depth and a nicer overall sound. We really just needed our tv to be louder. Cable is typically loud, but some programs on the various streaming services we have all have different levels of audio, with many being much too quiet. So better speakers have helped a lot.

The subwoofer connects to the soundbar via bluetooth. Both plug in, so plan to have 2 open spots in your power bar or wall receptacle. We have this system set up so the volume can be adjusted using the smart tv remote, rather than having to use the remote it came with. No issues there at all. Easy!

While I have the soundbar directly under the tv, I have the subwoofer set up in a corner a few feet away

The soundbar has spots in the rear in case you want to mount it to a wall. Subwoofer, does not.

Both are basic and minimalist looking. Subwoofer is black on black, soundbar is black with dark gray. No obnoxious branding or colors.

The instruction booklet is thorough, including information about the remote, battery info, placement and mounting, general operation, bluetooth operation, AUX in operation, Line-in operation, Optical-in operation (which is what I am using for use with my tv).

I really only purchased my original soundbar for use with tv (and replaced it with this for same purpose). I may give it a try anyway sometime soon. If I do, I will report back on how it does.

I like the added dimension that the subwoofer provides. I like the overall aesthetic. And because the combination of the two allows me to hear shows better than just using the tv speakers (on low audio streaming, as cable is always loud), I am pleased to use this.

I don't know hat this product costs, so I can't compare it. But, in short, it is about the same as just about any other low to mid priced soundbar. This is better sounding with addition of subwoofer. Not amazing, but definitely adds to my listening experience. 4 stars so far.

title: works as intended, using w/ Pixel4xl, plug n' play, no need for separate power or charging
review_text:
Not to shabby of a gadget. It's just a wee little thing- fits in the palm of my hand- a little smaller than a deck of cards. Is powered through whatever device you are using. Does not need to be separately powered or charged.

What's in the (generic) box:
--Amplifier unit (roughly measured at 3.5" x 2.5" x .75")
--Type C to Type C Cable
--Type C to USB Cable
--3.5mm to 2rca Cable
--User Manual (a piece of paper with info)

I also received some other cable assembly in the box that I do not know what it is for. Appears to be used in Optical port. Bonus in terms of what is listed in product description, I guess.

What is on the Amplifier unit:
--One end of unit has: Headphone input, On/Off Switch for Bass, Volume knob
--Other end of unit has USB C port (in), Optical port (out), Gain (H/L) Switch, Line Out port.

Connection Diagram shows use between SPEAKERS OR HEADPHONES, and Mobile phone, Laptop, computer, or PS4. States that it does not work with tv. I haven't tried it yet, but I may attempt a work around- I'll let you know if I am successful.

In mean time, I have tried it between my smartphone (Pixel4XL) using AmazonMusic and two different types of speakers.

The first set of speakers is a nice plug in variety. They are circa 2004 CambridgeSoundWorks- where one cord is plugged into wall receptacle , and the other plug goes into a headphone port. They sound nice with use with my phone, so I didn't expect much difference when adding this amplifier. True enough, they have similar quality. My speakers without the amplifier are loud and I can hear some range. The addition of the amplifier allowed me to manipulate the bass, which can be nice depending on what I am listening to. I switched between High and Low on the gain switch. High boosts the overall sound, and low brings out a more mellow tone. Either are good.

Next, I tried it with a pair of novelty speakers circa 2002. Little SONYspeakers that are really just a headphone style output. So for purpose of review, using these is to mimic a set of basic headphones. They just happen to be in the shape of a speaker sitting on a desk rather than on the head. Cute little things, and when plugged into anything they really produce no further sound advantage over a basic set of headphones other than they aren't on the head. Thought these would be perfect to see how much this amplifier can help a bare bones basic sup par listening item. The sound went from a very low, just make out the music sound to truly being amplified. I could boost the volume and the sound opened up- not just got louder. So, while I will likely never use it with these, I thought hearing the difference on a terrible set of "speakers" (again, really just non head headphones) was absolutely worth mentioning. Tells me that this product IS working as intended.

Now, my Pixel4XL has fair sound already- not nuance, but not sounding like a tin can either. Using this with my nicer plug in speakers is great. Using my phone, with my nicer speakers AND this amplifier is a little nicer, but not hugely so. Perhaps in a larger room, or in other conditions where I may need a more dynamic sound to carry. This isn't a knock on the product, I think it is a nod toward the quality of my old speakers. I definitely can hear the improvement with ability to boost bass. High to high sounds similar. My speakers can't display a low end gain. So good for this product to offer that.

I do happen to have a speaker hooked up to my TV, and I am going to try to make that work if it doesn't complicate my wire management.

As for cord length.. if you are using it with your headphones, this is fine. You would otherwise be plugging it into the headphone port on your device, so really, with addition of the amplifier and the other cord to connect to device, you gain several extra inches of length. Beyond that, your mileage may vary in terms of what will work for you.

So far so good.

PS, I had low expectations of this unit, so I am impressed with my experience so far. As I continue to try it out with various devices in various environments, if I learn anything new-- good, bad, helpful, enlightening, I will surely be back to share.

I think it is worth trying out. I can't comment on price as I am not sure what these are really worth, and if there are true differences among the options out there. So my rating is based purely on effectiveness of product and accuracy of product description. If I had one wish on the options provided on this product, that would be to allow some additional range in the High/Low gain switch. I'd give this 4.5 stars, but since it is whole numbers only- 5 it is (unless I need to change it over time through learning something new about it).

title: handy gadet when wanting bluetooth capability on something that normally isnt
review_text:
Kinda neat gadget. Not new to most people, but new to me. My truck is too old for this to be useful (still has a cassette deck!), and my husbands car is too new to be useful (already has Bluetooth tech). but I have been borrowing my moms car (late model Hyundai something or other) this week, and hers has some new technology but not bluetooth connectivity. So this came in hand for me to play music from my phone. I use AmazonMusic on my Pixel4XL, so after plugging in one end to the AUX port and the other end into the USB port in the car, I just went into Bluetooth settings on my phone. This brand comes up in the list, and I just click connect. Then hit play on my music of choice. EASY!!

The USB side lights up when it is plugged in. It had me concerned that it may stay powered on once I turn car off, but so far the light on it goes out when I turn the car off. For the most part, I have been unplugging it when I am done driving for the day. --just in case it does draw on battery--

I only noticed one initial hiccup in the connection the very first time I used it, and it has been absolutely perfect ever since. This is multiple car trips, multiple unplugging/replugging in, etc. My music pics up right where it left off.

The car happened to have the AUX and USB ports side by side, so the cord was plenty long enough. This comes with an additional cord length if needed.

My experience so far has been perfect. It does exactly what it needs to, and easily.

title: good price, nice bundle size, works exactly as I need them too
review_text:
You know you are an adult when you get excited to add a big bag of zip ties to your home tool box. I have an assortment of zip ties in various sizes for various tasks. If you didn't know, it is better to go a little larger than what you think you need as the length indicated is entire length and not just working length. I just so happened to have had a need for the smaller size (6" or less) zip ties to secure some corners on a multi tier wire crate. I ratcheted them tight and trimmed off the excess. In all, I used about two dozen immediately. With a pack of 500 I should be set for awhile. Always better to have too many of these than not enough. I'll be using them for sure to secure snow netting. Not on the posts (need 10-12" ties for that), but to hold together the overlap going from one roll or piece to the next. Since a section of netting always gets blown apart at some point during the winter, I just head out with a handful of zip ties and put it back together again. So yeh, 500 seems like a lot, but when you have them you need a bunch of them.

The 6 inch size is also great for wire management in general, and just about any small sized securing needs.

No complaints. Happy to have them!

title: works mostly as intended, inc 4 aa batt, 2 cords (car and home), details in review
review_text:
This charger works. It comes down to preference in style, and perhaps the going price at the time you are shopping around.

Upon arrival, I immediately unpacked this ACDelco battery charger. It comes with 4 AA batteries, and since I didn't see anything on the package about them being precharged, I went ahead and plugged them into my truck adapter. I was curious how well it would do in my truck (with the included car adapter) and since I knew I was running an errand that would take no more than two hours, I figured it was a good time to try it out.

I plugged them in at 2:10 pm, and saw that the batteries were charging as indicated by the red light. When I got back into my truck (I remembered to look!), the time was 3:05, and the battery indicator light was green, telling me that the batteries were fully charged. So this 55 minute charge time (likely less, since I wasn't in the truck whole time) tells me that it charged faster than anticipated, or the batteries had a little bit of charge on them to begin with, which is more apt the case--which is nice when they can be used right out of the package. Either way, it clearly charges and works fine.

(edit to add..) I see in the lower product description that the batteries come charged. Mine weren't fully charged, but I assume half charge (or more), and my charge time just topped them off. So to test this product further, I grabbed a set of drained rechargeable batteries from another brand that I hadn't gotten around to re-charging yet. I mean, I used them but drained them. I hadn't charged them again yet because I don't care for the charger it came with, so I just keep putting it off. I LIKE THIS CHARGING UNIT, and I will explain after details..

DETAILS!
--This charger charges AA and AAA batteries. It comes with 4 AA batteries and two styles of cords 110-volt wall adapter and 12-volt car adapter

-- The cord measurement for each is as follows:
74" wall charger cord
41" car adapter cord

--Charging Time Per Battery Capacity:
AA 1400mAh - 1800mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours
AA 1800mAh - 2300mAh: 2-2.5 hours
AAA 600mAh - 750mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours
AAA 750mAh - 1000mAh: 2-2.5 hours

--So, on the face of the charger on the left hand side, there are two indicator lights: one that glows red as the batteries charge, and one that glows green when charged and ready for use. Easy peasy.

--On the right hand side, there is a switch. It is to be set to either 2 batteries, or 4 batteries (+2, +4). Among the rebels among us, I have no idea what happens if we tried charging three batteries! :O

--Within the battery placement area, the slots are numbered. 1 through 4. I wish there were more clarification on this on the product page because I can no longer find the directions it came with. I am thinking that if just two batteries are being used, and they were placed in #1, #2 slots (or #3,#4) AND the indicator switched was in place for 2 batteries, does the charging juice primarily go to those spot (so as to keep with the quick charge ability)?. I think if just two batteries are being charged, then they go in the center, in the #1 and #2 spots-- so that's my plan going forward. I imagine this information is in the little pamphlet that came with the package. I'll be back if I find it and learn anything.

--The charging batteries at no point has gotten too warm my Energizer one gets pretty warm).

MY THOUGHTS:
--I LOVE that it has the TWO charging cords, with LONG cords. First, I like that it even has a cord, period. I have the Energiizer one that is just plugged into the wall. It seems like it would take up less space, but it doesn't. I find it harder to use as I need perfect clearance to plug that thing in. With this, I just need to find an outlet, then I can have it placed further away, making it easier to see and access. With the addition of the car charger, it just adds another option. Nice for camping (flashlights, radio, etc), or if you still use non cellphone cameras that eat batteries like crazy (this is what originally got me into rechargeable batteries almost 20 years ago, the digital cameras- ugh, I'm old). I sometimes bring a speaker with me for use with smartphone. It takes AA batteries. If I think to actually carry this unit around with me, I can charge my speaker batteries on the go if need be. But I think I will use this primarily in my home. I go through batteries with use of a couple of lighted mirrors. I have one that takes 4AAA and one that takes 4AA. The lights are bright, and I tend to go through batteries- so I make sure to have rechargeables on hand. As mentioned before, I like this unit because it is easier for me to find a place to put it to plug in AND have resting nearby. I had been in need of recharging a set of batteries and just hadn't gotten around to it because I don't care for the inconvenient (to me) charging unit of the other one. It works great, but I just found I prefer to have a cord. This has a cord.

PICTURES include another brand of (depleted) rechargeable AA battery (2000mah) with start time of being placed in charging unit. I only use these to help in charging. I have no comment on data transfer speed.

No complaints, so far so good!

title: Light, basic, efficient thanks to Windows 10 S Mode (which is optional, read review for more info)
review_text:
Update!!: my review below was originally written 07/2019. I wanted to add an update THREE years later, 07/2022. This little laptop is still kicking. I use it every single day from comfort of my couch to write reviews, do basic doomscrolling (lol), write emails, etc. Camera still works. Speakers still good. No major issues. I never did do any adjustments to it. Just sort of kept using it as is. I;m maxed out for memory, so it isnt something I would rely on for loading pictures onto, but as mentioned.. if you just need something to get online with and do some shopping or searching, then this is fine. Has been worth it. I happen to be sniffing around for another laptop so I can go more photo work with it, but I havent been in a rush. I came back to this review so I could refresh my mind on the specs. It was then that I realized 3 whole years has gone by! OK.. back to orginal review:

It's a basic laptop. The price is right. You aren't paying a lot for a little. You are getting quite a bit of what you need for a couple hundred dollars. Cheaper than most tablets. If you just want something to get you online, to browse the internet, watch some videos, listen to some music, write some messages, play some basic games, do some video chatting, then this might be for you.I think most people want that. It doesn't have a lot of memory or speed, or a slew of storage- but it will get you far if you don't expect a lot from it.

I'm a gamer, so I won't be playing any MMOs on this (nor on most prefabs that are out there). But I will use it to play a variety of offline and online games such as those found on FB or POGO (ie; puzzles, word games, board games, hidden object, casino style, etc).

I use youtube to listen to music, watch videos, listen to podcasts etc.. the speakers are fine. I can hear what I need to, clearly and loudly, if I wish. Some of the sounds that come through are more dynamic than I expected, so that is a plus.

I do a little bit of office stuff, so I will continue to make use of Google docs but there is an option to activate a free 1 year trial of Office 365 which includes 1TB of storage (One Drive); after that there is a fee. The Microsoft website breaks down the pricing options, which include pay for the year, or by the month, if that is of interest to you.

This Windows 10 is in S mode, which is a special mode that essentially limits Windows 10 in a variety of ways to make it run faster, provide longer battery life, and be more secure and easier to manage. YOU DO NOT HAVE TO KEEP IT THIS WAY! The idea is that there is less security with non proprietary items (apps, browsers, internet security), and greater chance of phishing, slower processes, decreased PC health, etc. So "S Mode" isn't a different version, it is simply a different mode, with the usual Windows 10 home, underneath. From what I understand, you can take it out of S Mode, and you will have Windows 10 Home (and then you can use browsers of choice, apps of choice, security software of choice, etc) BUT you CAN NOT switch back to S Mode. It is a once and done deal. S Mode default browser is Microsoft Edge, the default search engine is Bing.

I'm used to using a different browser, and having more freedom of choice, but I am curious how this S Mode will do, as I have noticed in my time of using it that it never bogs down. It is likened to Chrome on Chromebook- it seeks to streamline all the while being as secure as possible. If at any point I just don't like it, at least I know I have the option of just using Windows 10 Home. But again, it is a ONE WAY DECISION.

The laptop itself is super light weight. It comes in at just 3.24 lbs according to description. Full keyboard, touch pad, USB 2.0, USB 3.1, headphone/microphone port, media card reader, web cam, 3 prong charge plug with long cord. Attractive black textured design. I've got some fingerprints on the lid/cover, but doesn't look bad.

No dvd/cd player. I bought a cheap external for those times I want to use it for storage, watching a video, or listening to a CD. Hey, I like options.

Set up is quick and easy. When Cortana (Microsoft virtual assistant) came on, I let her guide me through the start up process. I could answer a lot of her questions with speech. It did well with recognizing my words.

I still have quite a bit of learning to do about this laptop. One thing that I find interesting is that it has an option to use a phone app- where it will link your laptop and phone to each other, so you can (according to Microsoft website)
-Link your phone and PC to unlock a variety of cross-device experiences for Android and iPhone.
-See recent photos from your phone on your PC for Android only.
-View and send text messages from your PC for Android only.

Again, the price is right. This does come into play for me in terms of rating. For a couple hundred dollars, I am able to scroll through FB endlessly, add some comments without tapping them out on my phone or tablet, can access full webpages, can take pics, or video call with web cam, can play some lightweight games, etc..

At this point in time, I give it a full rating. I mean, I wouldn't go below a 4 for this anyway, and a 5 might be pushing it, but it is a nifty little machine, and I am happy so far. Once I realized that I am not stuck with S Mode, that boosted my opinion of it (not all PCs or laptops are given this S Mode option).

If I learn anything more that I think you will find useful, I will come back to update. I hope what I have provided thus far has been helpful to you. Take care :)

title: good volume, use friendly, comes with remote, works on charge or with power cord
review_text:
I bought it for use with my tv. We have a smart tc with terrible speakers. Well, more like the sound is terrible with some apps, like Netflix or Amazon Prime- where the volume is sometimes not able to go up enough to really hear it, and I have sound sensitive ears. So I bought this thinking that it could lend a boost to the sound. I was able to get it to work with the cable, and the DVD player (the two areas that really don't need help), but could not get it to function with the tv itself. I tried all options, and I am either missing something or it just doesn't work with the tv. So while that issue *may* be on my end alone, I will just rate it on the actual sound.

The sound it produces is definitely a boost over what I am used to with the tv speakers. It doesn't have a dynamic sound, but it isn't flat either. Not directional, more in the front sound. Clean though. I think it would be better for use with a phone, tablet, or even lap top- where you just need some clean volume. It is long, but it is sleek. It can be controlled from the unit, or with the remote. The remote is uncomplicated and makes sense it its layout.

So while it ultimately isn't working (right now) for MY purpose (I aim to figure it out), it is a nice speaker, at a decent price point (I wouldn't got higher), and the options it provides is nice. Normally I go into mega detail on items like this, but there are already plenty of reviews that go over the specs nicely. So in short,

-Long charge
-Easy blue tooth connectivity
-Comes with connectors
-comes with remote for volume, power, and switching between outputs
-easy to follow short instruction pamphlet
-TF card option
-USB
-AC adapter
-built in microphone (which I haven't used, and have no intention of using)
--slim, sleek design
--has great volume capacity, not super dynamic- but different ears will pick up different sounds. I am attuned to nuances, so I can tell that this speaker doesn't go there.. BUT I still recommend it, overall.

I figure out anything else, or if I get it working for my needs, I will be back to update. I hope my little bit helped, even if it was just reinforcing the more detailed reviews. Take care, and enjoy your day :)

EDIT!!! Perfection!! OK, so I took one more try at trying to get the sound to work with Netflix & Prime. I was watching Captain America last night, and could barely hear it despite the volume turned way up. I realized that the last time I had tried to use this speaker for that, I may have had the tv volume down and of course it wouldn't pick up on sound. For cable, you want volume on tv down as it is running through cable box and you the sound to only come through this speaker. For roku, etc, you would just plug it into the headphone slot, and hence want the volume up. The addition of the speaker totally amplifies the sound AND it did a great job with the sound nuances of the movie. It didn't just add volume, it enhanced the overall sound. SO this really impressed me and I knew I had to come back to update my review. I already liked the speaker at 4 stars, but now I am really happy to have this in my life. It makes ALL the difference in our program watching as we typically use Netflix and Prime daily and it is frustrating that the volume is greatly reduced. Now it is better than ever. The sound is large and fills the room, and I can hear various other tones and bass within the movie- so I guess it depends on the source not just the speaker..

title: awkward design, hard to get used to, finding it irritating to use
review_text:
So, I have this backpack, and it is kinda weird. You have to see my pictures as it is a different style than what is pictured in the description. I don't really care for it as it is awkward to handle.

--It is a basic looking back pack. I like the bright orange in contrast to the black. That is likely the only feature I really like.
--The bag is deep. It measures roughly 21" long, this includes the top portion being unfolded, as that is usable space if need be. @17" wide
--The access to the main compartment is a velcro closure with adjustable hook straps for added security (and to keep added length folded down). Unlike many backpacks, there is just one slit opening across the top with velcro to close. Most backpacks have a zipper closure, as well as going a bit down the sides, for ease of access. I'm not fond of how my bag is styled in that way.
--Inside the great nylon cavern of the main compartment, it splits into several more compartments and pockets, including a lightly padded pocket.
--exterior pockets included two open side pockets that would be great to stick a water bottle in or an umbrella.
--two good sized compartments on the front- one zippered, one velcro flap closure.
--one rear zip pocket, as well as what appears to be a pass through strap of material- perhaps for use on a luggage handle?
--padded shoulder straps are comfortable. Straps include d-rings for clipping keys, or whatever to.
--overall feel is good
-I cant for the life of me find the USB port that it claims to have. I don't see anywhere for headphones, etc.. so I don't know what is going on.

The part that makes me really not like it is the main opening. First, it is deep, which can be good or bad depending on your needs. But, the top folds over way to easily. So it takes some major rooting around to find stuff, and the flap wants to fold down, and if it manages to fold down, it is easily closed tight by the velcro. This is super annoying if you want to get into and out of the bag repeatedly. I'm just like STAY OPEN. If it zipped, it would be better, then at least if it folder over it would be easy enough to get it, but with the velcro closing it up, it is irritating.

The other aspect that I dont care for is the hooks on the front. Well, they are anchored on the front, but since they are used to help keep bag closed (in addition to the velcro), when they aren't hooked, they are dangling down the front. So you have those kicking around in the front, and the shoulder straps and all its extras kicking around in the back. It isn't as clean or stream lined as it could be. It feels frumpy, I am sorry to say. I was hoping to replace my every day carry bag- I like to have a little cross body purse, plus a back pack for all my additional daily needs. This might get old quick as I try to get used to the odd features.

title: Super Duper STURDY, never breaking down, useful from small phone to large tablet
review_text:
This stand is way strong. It will hold whatever you've got. You dont know it, but you need this is your life, haha. I am super impressed, and would be shocked to not see a full rating across the board. Ok, so here is a quick run down on this mighty little device stand:

--It has rubber pads on bottom to help give it added stability
--It has rubber pads where the device sits to give it stability and help keep it in place.
--The place where the device sits is slightly curved, promoting stability and keeping it in place. I approximate a fingers depth
--The stand adjusts in any which way. As you can see in pics that there are two pivot spots, so you can adjust height & angle to your hearts content.
--Not heavy, but it has this super solid, high quality, substantial feel to it.

I have tried it out with my Pixel phone, my Kindle, my 10" tablet- all with covers, both vertically and horizontally. Each device felt secure, and I was/am very happy with how well this stand is working out. NOTHING MOVED. The weight didn't make the stand move or falter.

I typically use my large tablet in the kitchen for looking up and following recipes, or for making lists...and although my tablet has a case that serves as a stand, I can't tap on it too much without it falling over (most stands are best for just using to watch, not interact). THIS has a new home in my kitchen for this purpose. I can set my big tablet on it and can put it at whatever angle suits me, and I can tap away at it, or scroll through a recipe without it falling flat.

Such a simple thing, but it is refreshing when something works as it should (and more). 5 stars

I included a bunch of pics. I usually say that I will come back it if learn anything new (good or bad), but I think I expressed all the good, and I doubt anything negative will come to light. I think this thing will last forever. Even so, I'll be back if need be. I hoped this information helped you today. Take care! :)

title: clear, loud, water resistant, high quality blue tooth speaker, 20 hour charge
review_text:
YES! A blue tooth speaker that has volume, bass, mids- all without distortion. Heading into summer, this is going to be a well used piece of equipment.

Out of box, first thing you notice is the heft. Also, it comes pre-charged, so with smartphone in hand I was immediately able to test this thing out. WHAT A BEAUT!

It beats every single other bluetooth speaker I have ever used. Basically everything I have tried just makes the noise come out but doesn't allow for the details of the song to come through. This isn't absolute perfection in that way, but it is super solid in terms of sound quality. I can't see anyone disliking the clean, clear sound it produces.

I love the analogue dials. I can make adjustments as I feel like. The battery/charge indicator is easy to check in on, and I love that it is shows a range- so you can see about how much charge is left. With a 20 hour expected use on charge, I imagine I won't need to plug it in too often. Speaking of which, you will need the wall plug to use the included USB cord. Or use it in a wall receptacle with built in USB port (which we have)

Multi directional sound is evident. I can clearly hear both in front of and in back of the box. Some changes in sound as I walk around it, but that is also a matter of acoustics. We used it inside as well as outside. It sounds good wherever it is placed. It will do just fine to accommodate large spaces, and the sound will travel for outdoor use.

I haven't let it get wet, but I appreciate that it is water resistant.

This is not a low end, low budget item, so I wont comment on price. I have spent half this for only a tenth as good (just a sound maker not a quality sound). I'm glad this at least lives up to its description (and if you have the budget, the price). I have noticed that the price fluctuates, so keep an eye on it.

I have some more playing around to do with it, if I learn anything new I will be back to add to this review.

title: Pleasantly cute pattern, could use longer band.
review_text:
This review is for the "Chrysanthemum Black" pattern. It is a cute pattern. A black or white frame over the silver would coordinate better, in my opinion, as the colors are white, black, and yellow. No impact on my rating as I can see what I am buying clearly.

Pros:
--So far (about one month of daily wear), the band and frame are holding up. I am pleasantly surprised that there is no wear. There are some bands out there where the pattern wears off within a week (I've reviewed them). I will edit if I find any major wear over the next couple of months as that seems a fair timeline.
--I can use the buttons without issue, and everything seems to work fine. Blaze seems securely in place in the frame.
--no smells, no skin reactions

Cons:
--While the band is long enough for my @7" wrist, it is not as long as the Blaze original Large band. The excess band after the prong is in place is rather short. The security loops certainly helps keep it in place, but that easily slides, leaving the excess just dangling when it pops out. While the prong seems almost too short, it has a bend to it that seems to help keep it in place. Overall, I would feel more comfortable with a slightly longer band and/or slightly tighter security loop just so there is more overlap between security band and it possibly falling off.

Despite that "con", I am considering purchasing second one as another option in color/pattern ..so long as price doesn't go up. I bought it for $9.99 May 2018.

* There is also one more button, it's the DPI sensitivity switch button.

* Battery compartment also has a magnetic compartment to house the 2.4 receiver.

THE BAD:
------------
* No bluetooth, then again, the L brand doesn't have bluetooth either and it cost twice as much.
* Now, I've gone through many L brand ones in my life. They all eventually go bad because the trackball collects debris, and no matter how often you clean the mouse, they eventually go bad. If you don't believe me, look at the picture I uploaded with the 5 blue marbles. That's 5 L brand versions that have gone bad, but I saved the marbles. So I'm anticipating the same sort of life span for this Micropack version, which is about 1 to 2 yrs.
* The L brand also beats the Micropack with it's unifying receiver system, as well as a dedicated software. This Micropack mouse simply uses your windows software for configuration.
* The L brand also has 2 more buttons next to the scroll wheel that you can customize.

Ultimately, I still rate this Micropack vesion 5-Stars! Because though it lacks some features compared to the L brand, it is half the cost. 5-Stars... for now.

title: Beautiful desktop power supply, but you'll need your own 3M adhesives...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
---------------
* Aesthetically, a very nice and clean design that you can proudly display on your desktop. Standard power strips are too ugly to be placed on a desktop, but this design is very sleek.
* You got two 3-prong outlets on each side, and a 2-prong outlet on the top.

* At the front end, you get one USB port, and two 20w usb-c PD ports, so 40w total.
* GaN technology.

THE BAD:
------------
* Similar products made for a desk would include adhesives so you can immobilize it. There was no such accessory in the box. Nevertheless, I'll still rate this charger 5-Stars!

DEC 14, 2022 UPDATE:
---------------------------
* This will be a non-issue for the majority of you out there. However, I found something that was an issue for me. You cannot automate this strip with a smart plug. I have devices that I want to turn on all at once by Alexa, Siri, etc. So I use a smart plug. When you cut off power at the smart switch, this power strip automatically goes to "OFF" state. So when you turn the smart switch back on, you still need to manually touch the on/off button on this strip. Most power strips will resume it's "ON" state when you turn on the smart plug. But not this one, it automatically goes to "OFF" state. I suppose this has something to do with having a "touch" button. Most strips have no buttons, or an actually switch that you flip from off to on. So when you cut power at the source, it doesn't automatically flip to off by itself. But I guess this is the behavior of a "touch" power strip. Just food for thought.

title: Bad instructions, but overall stand is very nice and sturdy...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
--------------
* The board pieces are nicely finished. All the pieces were perfect. No dents or cracks.
* I suspect this is some sort of MDF or particle board with a layer of wood veneer on top.
* If you use a notebook as a main computer, and outputs to a monitor, then the center shelf is perfect for that purpose.
* Approximately 42" W x 6" H x 10.5" D when fully assembled.
* Compartment closes via magnet, and is a nice "push to open" design.
* Non skid rubber feet are included. They are the adhesive kind.
* Nice convenient hex bit is included so you can use your power drill. If you don't have a drill, the standard "L" wrench is included as well.

THE BAD:
------------
* The instructions for this guy is pretty bad. If you follow their manual, you might get confused because they got some of the numbers labeled incorrectly. Some of the board pieces are missing number stickers too. They do have a picture of an exploded overall view of where all the pieces are supposed to go. I just look at that picture, as well as the product photos. You don't have to be Einstein, it's pretty easy to figure out even without the instructions.
* Because of it's unique design, there are exposed screws on the surface. They are drilled in and flushed with the table, so aesthetically, it's fine. But I wouldn't slide unprotected notebooks or smartphones across the top, you may scratch your devices. Normally with exposed screws, I've seen other furniture provide stickers that are camouflage with the veneer, but no such stickers were included.
* The "push to open" latch that sits inside the compartment is pretty big. The space is so small, so this thing taking up a lot of space seems like an inefficient design.

We still like this stand a lot. 4-Stars overall.

----------------------------------------
* The type of USB adapter you use will matter. If your phone has a USB-C port, then you'll need a female USB A to USB-C adapter. * Many USB Camera Viewer apps won't work. It's not an exact science because you're dealing with so many variables such as app version, phone brand, android version, not to mention your hardware. * If connecting a media device such as fire stick, roku, etc., you will need to bypass HDCP, and you'll have to trial and error with the different types of splitters on the market. The GOXMGO splitter in my video demo worked nicely.

------------

title: Good bang for your buck, and my PS5 can display 4k through this switcher...
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:a7a9d66e53e5179d8dcca6d8e9fe8d3b]] THE GOOD:
---------------
* Price. They have a 4x4 matrix that can cost close to $200. For a 4 in, 2 out, $46 seems like a bargain.
* Build quality is great as well. You're getting a nice brushed metal casing.
* This HDMI Matrix is the only device so far that solved my PS5 4k issue. My display is a 4K projector, but I use a Caavo universal remote/HDMI switcher. The Caavo is capable of 4k and has 4 hdmi inputs, but for some reason when my PS5 goes into this Caavo, then out to the projector, the PS5 4k doesn't work. But if I out my Caavo into this Matrix switcher, then out to the projector, the PS5 4k works. I'm essentially daisy chaining my Caavo switcher with this Matrix Switcher. Everything works, and I have a total of 8 inputs now. Before, I had to connect my PS5 directly to the projector to get 4k. I don't know how, but this switcher has solved my PS5 issue.
* Easy to operate. Very intuitive. You don't even need to read their manual. Each output can display a different source. I collect vintage tvs, and I have a nice little 1976 Toshiba 9" sitting right below my 120" projector screen. People always ask if it works, and this Matrix Switcher allows me to demonstrate it. In my video, that's two different Twilight Zone episodes playing at the same time. LOL! Of course my vintage tv doesn't have a HDMI input, so there are other adapters involved.

THE BAD:
------------
* Nothing at all. What a bargain! 5-Stars!

title: Make a second LCD screen for your DSLR camera, or turn old phones into mini TVs...
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:7c51c8affe21df7ad48095fb4eeeab3b]] THE GOOD:
---------------
* Plug and Play if you know what you're doing. LOL! If not, you have some software learning curves. If you're using this to capture on your computer, then a popular software people use is OBS.
* But there are better quality capture devices for your desktop. Most people use these little usb versions on their smartphone to create a second monitor for their DSLR cameras. Watch my video, I demo two use-case scenarios.
* Colorful! Not your usual boring usb capture stick. I love red!

USING YOUR SMARTPHONE TIPS:
----------------------------------------
* The type of USB adapter you use will matter. If your phone has a USB-C port, then you'll need a female USB A to USB-C adapter. If it has a micro usb port, you'll need a female USB-A to micro usb adapter. I found that the ones with a little cord are finicky. A solid one piece, cordless usb to usb-c adapter solved the issue for me. Watch my video to understand what I'm saying.
* Many USB Camera Viewer apps won't work. It's not an exact science because you're dealing with so many variables such as app version, phone brand, android version, not to mention your hardware. Some apps gave me video, but no audio, some slam you with so many ads, it's annoying unless you pay. The best paid app is USB CAMERA PRO by Shen Yao, their free version is good too, but has ads. The best free app that virtually has no ads is USB CAMERA VIEWER by Homesoft, LLC. This is the app you see in my video demo. I'm using a Pixel 6 Pro.
* If connecting a media device such as fire stick, roku, etc., you will need to bypass HDCP, and you'll have to trial and error with the different types of splitters on the market. The bi-directional ones DO NOT work, at least they didn't work for me. I have a splitter by VIEWHD I bought years ago that worked for me.

THE BAD:
------------
* Nothing at all. At first, I thought mine was defective, but as mentioned above, I realized the adapter was the culprit. This product is 5-Stars!

title: Very nice thin profile cooling pad, but it's loud, especially for a bedroom...
review_text:

title: I gave Ryzen 7 a chance, but this is my new daily driver...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
--------------
* This is a very nice midrange desktop replacement. Loaded with i5 10210U processor, 16GB ram, and 512GB SSD for storage.
* Loaded up my old photoshop CS6 program, as well as Cyberlink Power Director. PC handled it with no issues.
* Terrific as a Plex Server as well. Friends have tested from outside the home. Not a hitch. There are other variables here, I do have 500/500 service from Frontier.
* It's great that they gave us one 16GB stick, leaving the second slot open. So if you want to add a second stick, the term you'll want to search for when shopping is, "DDR4 SODIM."
* Aesthetically, the mini pc looks very nice as you can see by the pictures. It is a super space saver that packs a punch.
* Out the box, it is Windows 11 Pro, no installation required.
* This does everything I need it to do such as running photoshop, power director, plex server, etc. But at this price point, it can also be a very nice starter PC if you have a child in grade school.
* No lock-up or freezing, which I've been experiencing with my other mini pc that runs on Ryzen 7 AMD.

THE BAD:
------------
* Nothing so far. This is 5-Stars, but I'm a reasonable person. If you compare apples to apples, you will be very happy. If you compare this to a $2000 gamer rig, then of course, you won't be happy. Kids who play less intensive games like Roblox, Minecraft, etc. This is no problem!

title: Must have accessory for vintage tv collectors...
review_text:

This has a male end HDMI connector, so for something like a Fire Stick, Chromecast, etc., which also have male-end connectors, this won't work. For this version, it works with mainly set-top boxes that have female HDMI ports such as an Apple TV, Fire TV box, etc. In my video demo, I'm using a Fire TV box, and my connection is as such:

1. HDMI out from Fire TV box to Ablewe adapter.
2. RCA out from Ablewe adapter to RF modulator.
3. RF coaxial out from modulator to 75-300 ohm adapter on the back of the TV.

Works perfectly. 5-Stars!

title: The most fickle cable I've ever experienced...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
---------------
* Braid type shields are much more flexible than the traditional vinyl, or thick rubber cables.
* 48gbps, 8K ready, HDCP 2.2, etc.
* 15 ft, and gold contacts.
* Customer service top notch. I "thought" the cable a I got was defective, and they sent me another one no questions asked. More on this below.

THE BAD:
------------
* This is the most difficult cable I've ever experience. It is very fickle. I have reproduced this fickleness with many gadgets, not just one. So, I am fairly certain this isn't user error. Now the first cable I got wouldn't give me any signal between my HDMI switch and my PS5. I wanted to make sure the Switcher isn't the problem, so I tested it with my Nvidia Shied directly to my 4k projector. Still no signal. Took it upstairs to test between Fire TV cube and another Switcher upstairs, still no signal. So it is reasonable for me to think the HDMI cable is defective. I asked for a replacement, and the seller sent me one quickly. With this new cable, I tested it with the Fire TV cube and switcher upstairs, and I got a signal. Great! So I took this new cable, and went downstairs back to the original location I wanted to use it... Guess what, no signal! LOL! This confused me, perhaps I mixed up the old cable, so I tried that cable as well, and guess what... I got a signal! But now I'm dubious of these cables because I'm fairly certain I did not mix up the cables. In any case, I took this cable that I just recently received signal, took upstairs to confirm, and guess what... no signal! LOL! See, what I'm trying to do to eliminate all doubts is for the cable to get a signal both upstairs and downstairs. Ultimately, I realized the original cable that I asked for a replacement for, I guess, was never defective. It is just fickle, like the new replacement.

Good customer service is why I won't rate this any lower than 3-Stars. I'm pretty tech savvy, and I've never had this much trouble with a cable. This might be a case of YMMV (your mileage may vary.)

title: Very high quality tripod if you're willing to invest in the PD ecosystem of accessories...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
---------------
* Peak Design is a very nice brand. I'm familiar with this brand back when I was buying a lot of accessories for my DSLR camera. I knew they make high quality stuff, and this tripod is no exception. This is a nice slab of aluminum with good heft to it. Not cheap plastic stuff.
* Works with their "mobile universal adapter," or any case with a metal shim in the back, such as magsafe cases.
* Very functional, especially useful for taking shots using the timer. No more needing to ask a stranger to take the picture.
* If you don't want it to cling to the back of your phone, then it comes with a very nice drawstring pouch.

THE BAD:
------------
* If you have a magnetic mount in your car, and you're hoping this thing will cling to it along with your phone, I'm sorry to report it won't work. The magnet is on the side that will cling to the back of your phone. The back is neither magnetic, nor steel. Your magnetic mount may hold it loosely due to the vicinity of the magnets in the tripod, but it is a very weak hold. Overall, I'll go 4-Stars.

title: Neat little projector, but it's not a good value proposition...
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:121051b82f50880623cdf0499f74c575]] THE GOOD:
--------------
* 1080P native and extremely small, so it's very portable. The size is the whole reason I got this. It's for traveling and being able to project bigger screens in hotel walls.
* 300 ansi lumens, ALPD laser tech.
* 25000 hrs lamp life.
* Airplay, Miracast thru wi-fi.
* Aesthetically, very nice minimalist design.
* Picture quality is good, but I'm not a videophile. I do have a more serious Vava UST 4k projector in my living room, so all these portable projectors will never compare. They serve as a traveling device for me, and will not be the go-to video source at home.
* Very nice case is included to hold everything.

THE BAD:
------------
* Onboard 1W speakers are very weak to say the least. You will definitely want to hook up a portable speaker. It has a headphone jack, which is basically the same as an aux out jack. I hooked it up to a cheap little speaker and the sound improved drastically. Watch my video.
* No remote.
* No smart OS, so I have a chromecast connected in my video demo, and I just cast from my phone.
* No Bluetooth, so you must use aux if connecting a speaker.
* No mounting solution or tripod included. Depending on your situation, you might not even need it. Just set it on a coffee table and you're good.
* No built in battery.
* Lastly, the price. There are so many features lacking, so I do not understand the price point. If you're willing to spend $600, then check out the Nebula Capsule Max that's less than $500. It is also compact, the size of a coke can. It has a built in battery, 8w speakers, smart interface, bluetooth, and remote. The only thing it doesn't have is native 1080p, it is native 720p. But it's hard to even tell the difference with these little projectors anyway. So I am not sure that paying more money, and having less features is worth that 1080p. And if you have to also lug around an external speaker, a chromecast or fire TV, then it really defeats the purpose of being completely portable. With the Nebula, everything you need is inside a device the size of a coke can.

In conclusion, this is a neat little barebones projector, but the onboard speakers are so bad, you'll need to carry around a portable speaker as well, so it's no longer as portable as I anticipated. At its price point, I assume they're saying it's a premium to have a projector at this size that is 1080p.. But again, that size feature is almost negated by the need to bring along external speakers, and smart devices like a Fire TV stick. And if the Nebula Capsule products doesn't exist, then I guess this price point is justified, but the Nebula does exist, and it's a much better buy. I'm going 3-Stars.

title: A lot of bells and whistles at this price range, but build quality could be better...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
--------------
* I won't go through the specs because you already know from the product listing.
* Beautiful picture quality, but I'm not a videophile. This is for my bedroom, and I'm coming from a TCL 65R613, which is a great budget tv.
* TV has a layer of film covering the entire screen, allowing you to get your finger prints on it while you set-up. Then when you're finished, peel it off.
* Comes with accessories for placing the Samsung on a table. The base is extremely heavy duty and weighted.
* You can wall mount using your own brackets, which is what I did.
* The remote is very unique. It has a solar back. I've never seen this before. So it will charge by light, or by usb-c. The fact that you don't need alkaline batteries is a first for me.
* Smart Home interface has a lot going on. There will be a little learning curve, but this could potentially replace my Fire TV Cube.
* Voice recognition allows you to choose between Bixby, Alexa, or Google Assistant. That's very nice of them to not force Bixby on you.
* No dark corners, which were present in my TCL. If there are, they are imperceptible. Dark corners are a hallmark of budget tvs. I'm definitely stepping up in picture quality.

THE BAD:
------------
* This is just something superficial, but I'm not in love with Samsung's build. This may be subjective, but I really love TCL's design. I have a picture comparing the side profile between the two tvs. The Samsung has a 3/4" side profile, but it's misleading, it's not really 3/4" thin, it has a hump back, which is all plastic btw, so the entire width is really 2". Whereas my TCL has a side profile of 1-1/8" all around. It's amazing that they can make a TV that thin all around, and the brush metal on the TCL looks better too. What I'm saying is that, aesthetically, this isn't the best TV out there when my budget TCL can beat it in looks. Then again, like I said, this is subjective.
* Picture Presets are: Dynamic, Standard, Movie, and Film Maker Mode. They are all underwhelming besides for Dynamic which is the brightest and has the most pop. I can tweak them all except for Standard. Something is wrong with the Standard preset right now. It is less bright than Dynamic, but once you choose it and exit the menu, it becomes even dimmer, much more dimmer than what was previewed to you. If you go back to the setting to see if you can up the brightness, you'll see that it's already at 50, which is the brightest. There is something wrong with this Standard preset, hopefully a firmware can fix this. I just use Dynamic.
* Smart Home navigation lag. Not sure if this can be fixed with firmware, I hope it can. The remote is pretty sweet, but lag can make or break whether or not you stick with an O.S. Right now, I still prefer to go to my Fire TV Cube. Hopefully, with firmware updates, they can improve the OS navigation and convert me.
* The storage in this TV I'm guessing is 8GB. Because after downloading a few apps, as well as the apps they force you to have, it says I've used about 3.5GB, and I have less than 2GB of space left. Why do TV makers continue to go cheap on this? They plaster you with all these apps in their home, all these ads, they want you to download games, this and that... yet they give you a measly 8GB, half of which is already used up for the OS and their forced bloatware, which you cannot delete. And I'm wondering if this has anything to do with the lag. It's truly comical sometimes, the decision making process of a multi-billion corp.

HOW TO GET RID OF THE SOAP OPERA EFFECT:
--------------------------------------------------------
* Wow, I spent a long time trying to figure this out. YT tutorials say turn off "Picture Clarity Settings" would turn this off, but it had no effect. I had this issue with the TCL too, when you make these adjustments, sometimes the TV just doesn't respond. The trick for the TCL was to unplug the tv, then replug and the motion clarity would be eliminated. I tried that trick with this Samsung, and it still didn't work. Ultimately, I found out turning off PICTURE CLARITY doesn't work, so you need to set it to CUSTOM, then turn off everything one by one, especially the BLUR and JUDDER reduction.

1. From your Home, go to MENU on the left side bar.
2. Then go to Settings, then ALL SETTINGS.
3. Go to PICTURE.
4. Choose your picture mode, I like DYNAMIC.
5. Then go to EXPERT SETTINGS.
6. Scroll down to PICTURE CLARITY SETTINGS.
7. Change it from Auto to CUSTOM.
8. Then reduce the Blur Reduction to 0.
9. Then reduce the Judder Reduction to 0.
10. You can also set the "Noise Reduction" to OFF, instead of AUTO. I can't tell the difference with noise reduction off. It's not like all of a sudden, your tv looks grainy. The difference is imperceptible, so I leave it off. Because a little noise makes the movies look more like theatre quality.

* Another tip I have is to NOT use "intelligent mode." If you enable this, it over-rides your custom settings above, and it will turn on the soap opera effect as it pleases.

Overall, I'll give this tv 4-Stars! Knocking a star for the navigation lag issue. I'm just using my Fire TV Cube for the moment. Hope this review has been helpful.

I can tweak them all except for Standard. Something is wrong with the Standard preset right now. It is less bright than Dynamic, but once you choose it and exit the menu, it becomes even dimmer, much more dimmer than what was previewed to you. If you go back to the setting to see if you can up the brightness, you'll see that it's already at 50, which is the brightest. There is something wrong with this Standard preset, hopefully a firmware can fix this. I just use Dynamic.
* Smart Home navigation lag. Not sure if this can be fixed with firmware, I hope it can. The remote is pretty sweet, but lag can make or break whether or not you stick with an O.S. Right now, I still prefer to go to my Fire TV Cube. Hopefully, with firmware updates, they can improve the OS navigation and convert me.
* The storage in this TV I'm guessing is 8GB. Because after downloading a few apps, as well as the apps they force you to have, it says I've used about 3.5GB, and I have less than 2GB of space left. Why do TV makers continue to go cheap on this? They plaster you with all these apps in their home, all these ads, they want you to download games, this and that... yet they give you a measly 8GB, half of which is already used up for the OS and their forced bloatware, which you cannot delete. --------------------------------------------------------
* Wow, I spent a long time trying to figure this out. YT tutorials say turn off "Picture Clarity Settings" would turn this off, but it had no effect. The trick for the TCL was to unplug the tv, then replug and the motion clarity would be eliminated. I tried that trick with this Samsung, and it still didn't work. Ultimately, I found out turning off PICTURE CLARITY doesn't work, so you need to set it to CUSTOM, then turn off everything one by one, especially the BLUR and JUDDER reduction.

1. From your Home, go to MENU on the left side bar.
2. Then go to Settings, then ALL SETTINGS.
3. Go to PICTURE.
4. Choose your picture mode, I like DYNAMIC.
5. Then go to EXPERT SETTINGS.
6. Scroll down to PICTURE CLARITY SETTINGS.
7. Change it from Auto to CUSTOM.
8. Then reduce the Blur Reduction to 0.
9. Then reduce the Judder Reduction to 0.
10. You can also set the "Noise Reduction" to OFF, instead of AUTO. I can't tell the difference with noise reduction off. It's not like all of a sudden, your tv looks grainy. The difference is imperceptible, so I leave it off. Because a little noise makes the movies look more like theatre quality.

* Another tip I have is to NOT use "intelligent mode." If you enable this, it over-rides your custom settings above, and it will turn on the soap opera effect as it pleases.
