title: High quality NVR, but requires some trial and errors if you're not fluent in networking...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
--------------
* Terrific build quality. I've seen cheap ones that come to you with dented cases, and the internal circuitry looks like a half baked job with messy wires and bad soldering jobs. This is a real professional NVR.
* 4TB Hard Drive is included, but you can install a 10TB drive if you wish. That's the max capacity.
* Records 4k video, and 8MP images.
* Instant feed, no delay like wireless cams.
* App works well provided you have everything set-up properly.
* If you're not sure of what you're doing, like I was, it's easy to restore the HD back to factory default again. I had to trial and error many times, and the good thing was that he factory reset was very quick each time. It's basically like restarting the device.

THE BAD:
------------
* No cameras provided, but you knew that when you bought it.
* Manual font is for little ants to read. But it's readable. It's just my pet peeve when manufactures make it uncomfortably small.
* Just like any other network product, the manual doesn't spend anytime with what to do if your service provider goes by 192.168.254.XXX versus providers that use 192.168.1.XXX. A lot of network products go by 192.168.1, and so I get a lot of headaches being a Frontier customer. Granted I'm not fluent in networking. A networking expert reading this might say, "easy, all you have to do is this, this and this..." Well, you see, that's what I was hoping the manual would do. LOL!

Having said that... I actually got everything to work properly. I don't know how, but I did it. As mentioned above, I'm with Frontier and they use 192.168.254.xxx, so depending on how I hook up the NVR to my network, the DHCP will generate a proper working address, or it may not. Here are some noteworthy things I discovered. This pertains to my personal network/situation, but if you find yourself in the same boat, maybe this info could be useful:

1.) Connecting the NVR directly to my frontier router causes the NVR to use it's default IP address 192.168.1.XXX. This is fine if I'm viewing the cams on my ethernet connected PC. But the app over wi-fi will not work. It will say my NVR is offline.
2.) For some reason, using a POE SWITCH between my NVR and my Router makes all the features work properly. I can view on my PC, and I can view on my APP via wi-fi. So if any of these issues sounds familiar to you, then this is what worked for me... Connect the UPLINK port of the POE SWITCH to a port on the home router. Then, connect an ethernet cable from the Network port of the NVR to any of the POE ports on the POE Switch. Once I hooked it this way, the NVR's DHCP created an IP address that is in line with my Frontier network 192.168.254.xxx. Now I can view the cams on my ethernet PC, as well as my wi-fi app.
3.) Ideally, you want to connect all POE cameras directly to the NVR which has 8 ports, but if for whatever reason, you need to connect a camera to the POE SWITCH, then understand that it'll require 2 ports of the POE Switch, one for the camera and one going back to any 1 of the 8 ports on the NVR. And remember in step #2, one of the POE port is already connected to the network port of the NVR. So 3 ports total have been taken up in this scenario.

Love the quality of the hardware, as well as the streams. I also attached a screenshot of the App's live view page. You'll see I tested 2 cameras. You simply tap a camera to get the full screen view of it. I'll rate this NVR 4-Stars overall.

title: If you're a beginner like us, this set is more than enough to get you started...
review_text:
THE FACTS:
--------------
* Complete set to get you stargazing right away.
* Is this a refractor, reflector, or catadioptric telescope? This is a refractor telescope!
* 700mm focal length. This length is equivalent to the length of your actual refractor telescope.
* Aperture: 90mm aperture.
* Maximum magnification of this telescope is 180x. You derive at this number by multiplying the aperture (90mm) by 2.
* Eyepieces included: 25mm, 9mm. To calculate magnification of your telescope. Take 700mm divide it by the eyepiece you're using. So if you're using the 25mm eyepiece, your magnification is 28x. So you shouldn't buy eyepieces less than 4mm focal length since 700/4= 175x. So a 4mm eyepiece gets you to the max essentially.
* 3x barlow lens included. Used to increase the magnification of your telescope 3x. How do you use this? Eyepiece goes inside the barlow lens, then everything goes inside the telescope. Using a 25mm eyepiece in the example above, we get 28x magnification. So if you combine the 25mm eyepiece with the barlow, you get 84x magnification.
* 1 Finder scope and 1 finder scope bracket included: Some googling, I found this.... "A finderscope uses low power with a wide field of view and assists you in locating objects to observe through the main telescope. Crosshairs aid in centering the object you seek."
* Smartphone adapter included.
* 1 tripod tray included.

There are lots of YT tutorials. I'm just sharing with you info I've learned. From a newbie's perspective this set is very impressive, and more than enough to get going. Once you get more experienced, then I believe you can compare and contrast telescope qualities as you try out others. For now, I have no experience to compare this to anything else. Just getting my feet wet. This is 5-Stars for a beginner!

title: A very nifty piece of tech, which will surely be a conversation piece...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
--------------
* High quality, and very professionally manufactured.
* At it's most basic function, it is simply an animated picture frame, and the images are stylized to look pixelated.
* Downloading the app, Divoom, and setting things up was pretty self explanatory and intuitive.
* USB-C power port, which means no worries about which way the cable plugs in like the hassle of micro usb cables.
* Hang or use the included kick-stand.
* Overall, just something really fun to play with. A conversation piece for sure.

THE BAD:
------------
* Social media and game linking are very limited. My son would go bonkers if we can somehow link Roblox. There is Fortnite though. He doesn't play that as much, but we were able to link Fortnite, and it showed his stats.
* The screen doesn't really pop as much as I'd like. It's decent, but it would be nicer if it was brighter.
* It's covered by two film protections, full of bubbles. There should have been some easy lifting tabs. There are no lifting tabs, and the films run right up against the bezel. Making it extremely difficult to lift an edge. You feel like you're scratching the screen just trying to lift this film. I got the top film off. The second film was too difficult, so instead of lifting the second film, I just took a credit card and straighten out all the bubbles, and kept it as a screen protector.

Overall, I'll go 4-Stars for this nifty piece of tech.

--------------
* Pretty unique. I've never seen a Hologram fan at work up close.

I kept fiddling with it, I just didn't understand it. I eventually gave up, and thought mine was defective. But I turned it on again, just to see the animations. Then after awhile, all of a sudden, I hear music. So I finally understood there is a 5-8 second delay for the music to kick in. Watch my video.

Overall, I'll rate this 4-Stars. I'm knocking 1 star for it's music and video limitations.

title: Complete DIY alarm kit from a known brand name...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
--------------
* Very easy to set-up, app is intuitive to use and follow.
* This is a very complete kit with a hub, 6 entry sensors, 2 motion sensors, and a keypad. You don't need to use everything, or install everything in one day. I started off just my garage door and the front door. Same thing with the extra keypad. There is already a control panel on top of the hub. The idea of they keypad is for quicker access to the control panel. So ideally, the keypad will be next to your bed on a nightstand or something.
* Hub is not obtrusive at all. I have it next to a soda can for size reference.
* Sensors work really well. I was concerned about the garage door sensor because usually I get bad wi-fi in the garage. I put the hub near my living room. The garage sensor worked flawlessly. Anytime you open the door where you've installed a sensor, there is a chime that goes off on the hub. You can disable this chime if you wish.
* No need to subscribe to a service, which is perfect for us. We live in a fairly safe neighborhood, knock on wood. But there are times when everyone is gone, and no cars are parked in the driveway. So these are the times, I'll arm the system.

THE BAD:
------------
* The sensor and the magnet has to be half an inch or less apart. Installation will be tricky for some of you. My front entry door has a raised decorative trim that makes this impossible. I made it work by having the sensor at a weird angle, and half the 3M backing isn't even attached to the trim. I will need to think of a solution for this. Or better yet, ADT should have thought about this ahead of time and given us adapters, spacers, etc.
* If you choose not to subscribe, like in our case, you should understand the system is nothing more than a deterrent. You hope the loud sound will be enough to deter would be criminals. If it's not, then no authorities are coming unless you called them yourselves.
* The instructions assumes we all know the industry lingo For example, "Entry or exit delays." It would have been nice if the manual explained what this means. I had to search online for more info. It's basically the time the system allows for you to properly turn off the alarm before it goes off. That's my understand from YT videos of other brands. I couldn't find an exact "Blue by ADT" video on this matter.
* Whenever you arm the system, it takes forever, like 60 to 90 seconds, and during this time, there is a CHIME that's counting down with the seconds. Once the system is armed, then it shuts up. There doesn't seem to be a way to mute this. You see, I'm a night owl, so I don't need to arm the system until very late like 1 or 2 am. People are asleep at this time, the chimes will wake them up. I have contacted customer service, we'll see what they say.
* The 2 yard signs and stakes are great, but the 4 stickers they give for your windows are tiny. My Brinks windows stickers were bigger.

Overall, I'll rate this 4-Stars. And base on the customer service response, this might go up to 5-Stars, or get bumped down to 3-Stars. There has got to be a way to mute the chimes when arming the system. If there isn't a way, then I will bump the rating down because that would be ridiculous. So, 4-Stars for now.

title: This is a complete bundle with 5 hdmi and 5 usb link cables, but it is not a high end switch...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
--------------
* 4 HDMI port in, 4 USB link ports, 1 HDMI port out.
* You can share up to 4 usb accessories
* 1 usb calculator included.
* 4 hdmi cables included.
* 4 usb link cables included.

THE BAD:
------------
* Case seems to be metal, but it's a little light. Doesn't feel has sturdy and robust as the Avstar.
* You're getting a lot in this bundle, but there is a reason for that... this is a very basic kvm switch.
* No usb 3.0 or 3.1. The usb ports on this switch are 1.1 and 2.0. If you don't need 3.0, then you should be happy with this switch.
* No mic port.
* No audio ports.
* Included calculator is a gimmick to create value, but it's pointless and lightweight plastic, very cheap.

Depending on what your needs are, you might want to check out the Avstar kvm switch that I recently reviewed. That one is $10 less, but it is more future proof, and more of a premium product. That one has 3 usb ports to share but they are 3.0 and 3.1. The Avstar also has an optical audio port, a stereo audio port and a mic port. The Avstar also has a remote control to switch inputs. So it is a better kvm switch overall, but it does not include any hdmi or usb link cables. Here is an Amazon link to that switch: https://www.amazon.com/review/RR34E657C5MOF/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B09D6Y2CFL

USE CASE SCENARIO:
--------------------------
* Why would you need a KVM switch? You can share a single set of keyboard, mouse, speakers for multiple pcs. You can use your same PC monitor to view the Fire Stick, play PS5, Xbox, etc. There is no need to hook up different speakers, as long as you hook up your main speaker to the optical or stereo ports.

I was ready to give this switch 5 stars because of all the cables provided, but now that I've used both switches, I understand why the Avstar didn't include any cables. The Avstar is a higher end product, so they're keeping the cost down by not providing any cables. I use the Avstar with my higher end pc, and I'm using this Basicolor switch for master bedroom pc that has lower needs. I'll rate this switch 4-Stars as well.

title: Mid Century style retro radio with a 5 yr warranty...
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:3f4b028ed4887ded77fba90586e9150]] THE GOOD:
--------------
* Beautiful retro design. Don't quote me on this, but I believe this is called Mid-Century style.
* These retro radios are first and foremost, display props. Don't expect the world in terms of sound quality for something that's less than $100. The sound is decent and par for the course.
* ClearClick is a name I've come across before when I reviewed their capture card products. They are base in the US, and have been in business since 2010. The reason I'm mentioning this is because this product has a 5 year warranty. Normally, I would say warranties from fly by night overseas companies are worth as much as the paper they're written on. But the warranty here, provided by a company based in the US, should have real value.

THE BAD:
------------
* No built in battery. This is corded.
* About that warranty I discussed above. Keep all your records, you may need it down the road. I got two vintage radios from ClearClick and they both had QC issues. I had to do a replacement for one radio because the distortion was unbearable. Now for this version, I can hear some humming, but since these are novelty items, and I won't be seriously listening to them, I didn't bother to do a replacement for this one. Plus, with some volume, the humming is drowned out. Nevertheless, to have issues on both radios was a bit concerning. Maybe the experience is just unique to me, unlucky perhaps.

I'll still rate this radio 4-Stars due to the warranty. If the humming should get worse over time, I'll put their 5 year warranty to the test.

title: Premium drawing tablet with very convenient shortcut keys and roller wheel...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
--------------
* High quality premium build.
* Direct usb-c connection, or Bluetooth connection.
* There is no delay with Bluetooth connection. My drawings are instantaneous. If there are any delays, it is imperceptible to my eyes.
* 8 shortcut keys, and roller wheel. Once you use this tablet, you'll never use another writing tablet without these shortcuts. They are so convenient.
* Roller wheel can be assigned as a zoom in/out function, a scroller, change brush size, or rotate images. I have mine set to change brush size. This is so much more convenient than going to the upper left menu in photoshop to change brush size. Plus, at default from the factory, the 8th shortcut key is programmed for you to access and change the roller functions quickly. So even though I have my roller set to change brush size, if I hit the 8th key, I get a pop-up menu of my choices again.
* Top of the roller wheel is a touch pad, so you can assign it as a mouse.
* Pen is housed in a cylinder with storage on both ends. On one end is the actual pen, and on the other end is storage for the Bluetooth usb dongle, and 10 replacement pen nibs/tips.
* As is, the idea is you write with your right hand, and your left hand controls the wheel and shortcut keys. What if you're left handed? In the XP-Pen software, you can flip the layout 180, this will allow you to flip the tablet so the roller and shortcut keys are on the right. You must set this in the program. If you don't, and you flip the tablet, everything will just move in reverse.

THE BAD:
-----------
* We will all have a different experience because we all use different apps and programs. I use Photoshop CS6 and the roller was quirky. None of the roller functions worked. So I switched programs and used Windows Paint, and everything worked fine. When I went back to CS6, the roller started working. As if it learned something from the Paint program. LOL! I uploaded a bunch of screenshots of the software so you can see what setting and features are available.

I will rate this 4-Stars for now. I'm pretty sure it's the tablet that's quirky with CS6, and not user error. But I'll be using this a lot in the next few weeks, and I'll bump this to 5-Stars should I learn that it was user error. But so far, I don't think I'm doing anything wrong, the roller is just really quirky in CS6.

title: High quality poe NVR system with 4tb pre-installed, plug and play if connecting directly to NVR...
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:1190b451faf9653857f6725f71e2a33c]] THE GOOD:
--------------
* This is the real deal! Every component is high quality, and the NVR unit is externally and internally immaculate. Why do I have to even say this? Because I've tried other NVR systems. I have encountered NVRs with flimsy dented cases, and messy soldering jobs on the motherboard.
* 4TB is pre-installed.
* You get 8 POE cameras! A mistake I made as a newbie was thinking all I have to do is get POE switches, then I would be able to get rid of power adapters for any camera. That is incorrect! A camera has to be designated as a POE camera in order to use POE switches and POE NVRs.
* You get eight 65 ft ethernet cable. If you can run those cables back to the NVR, which has 8 ports in the back, then you won't need to hook up any intermediary POE switches. I plan to use at most four cameras, so If I need to hook up a POE switch, the four extra cables will come in handy. However, more on this issue later.
* Included are also outdoor plugs to protect your wire connections.
* PLUG & PLAY... As long as you run the ethernet cable back to the Ethernet ports of the NVR, it is plug and play. If for any reason, you need to find the IP in your service provider's router admin, look for HEROSPEED DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY. That's the name it shows up under.
* Unlike most security cameras, the live feed of this NVR system has no delay, it's real time, or pretty close to it.
* If you're using a KVM switch at your computer, so you can switch back and forth between different sources... I said in my video that once I get a USB cable to link up the KVM switch with the NVR, then I should be able to use my PC's mouse and keyboard, which are connected to the KVM switch. Well, since then I've learned that what I said is half true. I'll be able to use the mouse, but not the keyboard. The NVR doesn't respond to any keyboards no matter if it's through the KVM switch, or directly connected to the NVR. It only uses the onscreen pop-up. You will need to use the mouse to select the letters and numbers from the virtual keyboard.

THE BAD:
-----------
* Like I said above, it's plug and play as long as you connect each camera directly back to the NVR ports. It goes without saying, but the NVR also needs to be connected to your router or nearby switch to be online. I'm running into issues testing POE switches. If the camera is not directly connected to the back of the NVR, the system cannot find it. There are 16 channels available in the NVR, and only 8 ports in the back, so obviously, this should be compatible with POE switches. But so far, I can't get it to work. I've asked for help from OSI, so we'll see...
* No guidance or instructions on how to install the actual cameras. For a moment, I was SMH. I was looking for the bases. I thought my package was missing them. But I realized the bases were already threaded onto the cameras. For each camera, you need to unthread the base, drill the base onto the ceiling of your choice location, then thread the main camera body back on it.
* Another nitpick is that installing under a ceiling will not always be ideal, or possible. It would have been great if they had included some adapters so that we can install them onto walls like bullet cameras.

Despite the little nitpicks, I still rate this 4-Stars right now. Might bump it up to 5-Stars if we can get the POE switches sorted out. I'm a newbie, so I know this might be easy for experienced networkers. The manual is a bit lacking. There were no discussions on how to install the cameras, and it assumes you'll be directly connecting all cameras back to the NVR, so it doesn't discuss the use of POE switches at all.

Now when I move all my oldies mp3 to the MP3 player, and I go to the ALBUMS category, there will be an album called Oldies. I just hit shuffle an enjoy.

I'll rate this player 4-Stars.

title: Magnificent Bang & Olufsen Portable Speaker with a unique design...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
--------------
* Beautifully crafted high end speaker.
* Built like a tank, it weighs about 7 and a half pounds.
* Three ways to position the speaker: Flat, on it's end, or mount it on a wall (bracket sold separately).
* From what I can tell, it produces beautiful sounds. However, I'm not an audiophile.
* 105 watts, 79dB bass, and 96dB mid-range.
* Awesome charging design. The round object you see in the pictures is the charger. The usb-c goes into this object, it then docks magnetically to a round slot in the back of the speaker. Contrary to other reviews that said you're in trouble if you lose this charging device, the back of the speaker has another usb-c port for charging. So if you lose the round object, you're not in trouble. I think it's there for tactile purpose. Without it, you have to constantly turn the speaker around to look for the charging port. With this magnetic charger, mounting and dismounting is a breeze. BTW, Ethernet and Line In is hidden under the rubber cover of this round charging slot.
* Works with Airplay, Chromecast built in. If you have a google smart home, you'll like this. My wife is an Apple person, I'm Android. She's been taking over the speaker with Airplay.
* 16 hours of play time after fully charged.

THE BAD:
------------
* Not necessarily a bad, but more like a reality nowadays. You have to hunt for the user manual at their website. No user manual is included.
* Bluetooth connection was easy with some of my devices, and was very difficult with others. My MP3 player took forever to find the Level. Not sure if the issue is with the Level or with the player.
* Tested it with my Fire TV Cube. Does not work well. I have to connect/disconnect several times to get audio to the Level. But when I change apps, I lose audio again. To be fair, this wasn't made for TV. But cheap $50 Bluetooth speakers can work flawlessly with media players, why not a $1300 speaker?
* On the speaker, there are 4 touch buttons that are for favorites that you can customize. Such as spotify, pandora, etc. You can also long press to save a Google Voice command for each button like Play some music, what is the weather, etc.. Initially, I thought this meant Google Assistant was built in, but it is not unfortunately. It's only good for four phrases. Upon further research, I realize that they do offer this same speaker on their website with Google Assistant built in. They have an option that you can choose with or without Google Assistant, and it's for the same price. I guess this option is available because some people don't like smart devices listening in their homes. This Amazon listing is WITHOUT GOOGLE ASSISTANT.

Even with some of these "BAD" things I've listed and discussed, I still rate this speaker 5 stars because it's the most magnificent speaker I've ever owned.

title: A terrific photo box, but you'll need to clear your living room to put this thing together...
review_text:
SEPTEMBER 23, 2021 UPDATE:
------------------------------------
* Loving this thing more and more every day. But I wanted to discuss a little more about the floor space that you'll need to assemble at home. I listed this as a "bad" in my initial review. Recently, I was able to dismantle it and reassemble it in my garage. You have to dismantle because a 40 inch square isn't going to fit through any of your doors. I absolutely did not have 13.3 ft by10 ft worth of empty space in my garage to lay down the material that covers the frame. But because I am now familiar with the material, the orientation of it, where it zips up, etc... I was able to just let the material sit all bunched up. I then rebuilt the frame inside the material. It was a bit funny cause I'm working inside out, a 40 inch square is huge, I found myself inside the frame zipping the material up from the inside. It's a weird scene if you were to walk in on me. LOL! So it is possible for you to do the same, you don't need to clear a 13.3 ft by 10 ft floor space. However, do follow my advice in setting up the backdrop last. Please read the original review below.

ORIGINAL REVIEW BELOW:
-------------------------------

THE GOOD:
--------------
* Led lights provided are very bright. That's also due to the fact that you're trapping light in a box with reflector material on all sides.
* Assembly isn't difficult to understand at all, it is easy. But more on this in the BAD section.
* You get a carrying bag as well as 5 pvc color backgrounds.
* 40" square shooting space is huge!!!
* 3 types of shooting angles, depending on how much light you want to trap.

THE BAD:
------------
* A little QC issue... My led light came with a broken clip, and instead of bothering the seller since the light still worked, I just used sugru to mold a new clip.
* Think long and hard if you need this 40 inch version. There are smaller versions. It can be unwieldy to handle this 40 inch version. Like I said above, it's not difficult to understand how to put it together. It's just you need a lot of space. It doesn't come to you in a square form. You first build the 40 inch square pvc frame. Then you lay the main material that makes the box on your floor, you put the frame on it, then you fold it up, wrapping it around the pvc frame and zip everything up. It isn't difficult at all, the problem is the floor space you'll need! 13.3 x 10 ft worth of empty floor space to lay the material down. For some people, especially people with kids, it is not easy to find this much open floor space. LOL! I included a picture from the manual to show you what I'm trying to articulate.

MOST IMPORTANT TIP:
---------------------------
* Don't follow the instructions in laying the background on the floor, and then putting the frame on it. If you do it this way, you'll never change backgrounds again because it is a hassle. Secondly, the background will then be under the frame, so the back bottom frame will be exposed in the pictures. What you should do is follow the instructions, except for the background part, just leave it out. Then when everything is done. Choose the background you want. It has velcro on both upper left and right corners. Inside your box will have the velcro counterpart on both the upper left and right corners as well. So you simply stick your background on it. It is pvc and doesn't crease easily, you can bend and curve it at the bottom to achieve a seamless look with the frame hidden underneath. Not only will your pictures be nicer without the exposed frame, but if you change your mind about the color, swapping the background will be much easier too. Here is an example of product pictures I took for another Amazon review using this light box. https://www.amazon.com/review/R3FM8X6Z2ZFY7E/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8

I'll rate this 4-Stars! It would be 5-Stars if not for the QC issue.

title: Important to understand this is a mouse cursor mover, not clicker...
review_text:
I actually needed a mouse clicker, and for some reason I just thought all these "jiggler" products would have that option, but they don't. All they do is jiggle or move your mouse. It is completely plug and play, no software. Your PC should set-up device automatically, when it's done, this is how you operate:

1. Long press the only button on the device. It will turn on to A3 mode. This is the slowest mode. The mouse will move imperceptibly.
2. Short press button again to toggle to get to A1 mode. This is the fastest mode. Your cursor is flying around fast.
3. Short press button again to toggle to A2 mode. This is the medium speed mode.
4. If you want to leave this thing connected, but don't want to use it all the time, then simply long press again to turn jiggler off when not in use.

In every mode, there is a timer that shows you how long it's been moving. If you're looking for a cursor mover, this guy gets the job done. But don't make the assumption that I made. These things do not have an option for clicking. That's not the product's fault, it never claimed that, it was my assumption. So I'll still rate this product 5-Stars for doing exactly what it advertises to do... move your cursor.

title: High quality 4k Multiviewer, so many uses, this is too awesome...
review_text: Wow! This thing is awesome, especially during the Olympics. Please do not mistake this as just a HDMI switch, this is a 4k Multiviewer! A HDMI switch only allows you to switch HDMI sources and watch one source at a time. With a Multiviewer, you can split your screen into 4 sections and view 4 different sources at the same time. We use an UST projector in our home with a 120 inch screen. So with this Multiviewer, I can view four 60 inch screens at the same time. In my photo example, I only inputed 2 sources (Nvidia Shield and Chromecast) because connecting all 4 sources requires reorganizing my wires and cables, which I'm not ready to do yet. But in playing around with just 2 sources, I can already tell how awesome this is and how useful it will be. Especially gaming during games! For example, you can play your Nintendo Switch, while the Olympics is on quietly. Which source gets the audio is your choice. Perhaps on the 3rd screen will be my front door surveillance because I'm waiting for a package and the house is noisy. The 4th screen is a connected PC to browse the net! What you'll be using it for is only limited by your imagination. I already know one cool thing we will certainly be doing... You see we have multiple Nintendo Switches in our home, and we love Splatoon. However, Splatoon does not have split screen for multiplayer. Everyone is playing together, but everyone has to stare at their own little screen. Well, with this Mutiviewer, we can play side by side on the big screen! Lastly, the build quality of this device is very nice. It has good heft to it, not cheap lightweight stuff. Can't wait to set everything up. This is an enthusiastic 5-Stars!

review_text:
THINGS YOU'LL NEED THAT ARE NOT INCLUDED:
----------------------------------------------------------
1. Your own micro SD card, up to 2tb.
2. A power adapter that has a usb-c port. The Qubii will be plugged into this adapter.
3. A usb-c to usb-c cable. To connect from the Qubii to the usb-c port of your Android phone.
4. A usb-c to Apple lightning if you'll be using an iPhone.

SOME NOTEWORTHY INFO:
---------------------------------
* This is a good idea, now that Google Photos is no longer unlimited.
* It basically backs-up every folder that has an image. There doesn't seem to be a way to choose which folders you want it to back-up. I only need my main camera folder to get backed-up, but oh well, backing up too much is better than too little.
* Once you disconnect from power adapter, you can use the Qubii as OTG storage. You'll need to turn on OTG storage in your system settings. If you have a case on your phone, you'll probably never bother to use it as OTG because you'll need to remove the case.

* After you transfer everything safely to your pc, if you delete the files on the micro SD card to clear space, the Qubii still maintains its count. So even if these files are still on your phone, it will not re-download them again.

In conclusion, how accurate and precise this system is remains to be seen. So far, it has backed up everything I need it to. I know people complain of missing files, not everything getting backed-up, etc. Most of these complaints revolves around people using iPhones. But we'll see, time will tell. As of now, this is 5-Stars!

title: A bit inconvenient if you're buying this for kids under 10...
review_text:
This is pretty nifty, but it's not as convenient as they make it sound. Here are some things to consider...

1. You can't be handsfree like a microscope, unless you set up your phone with a mini tripod and stuff.
2. It's advertised for kids, but I don't think so, not if they're under 10. My children were very interested, but I had to do all the holding and focusing.
3. Most likely you'll need to take off your phone case for the lens to stick to your camera lens, especially if the case rises above the phone lens. With the case I'm using, there is a very slight rise, almost imperceptible, yet the microscope lens won't stick to my phone because it's sitting on top of part of the case.
4. The lens stick to your phone via some sort of suction/sticky pad. After awhile, it will no longer stick. However, the manual has a solution that did work. You simply use clear tape to clean the dirt off the lens as well as the lens on your phone. It's like when you're putting on a screen protector for you phone, and they provide you with stickers to pick up the dust. Same thing here.. you're using tape to pick up the dust. It actually works. My lens was able to stick again to my phone.

All in all, it's nifty, it's something you're curious about, but after going through with it. I'm 100% sure we won't be using it much. We have a dedicated microscope at home for the kids, and to me, that's still much more convenient. I don't want to take off my phone case, focus the camera for the kids, etc. If you're buying this for yourself.. go for it! If you're buying this, thinking you'll be using it a lot to keep your kids busy, think again. Because it'll end up keeping you busy. LOL!

I'll rate this 4-Stars.

title: If you're a Frontier customer, or any other service for that matter, my review should help...
review_text:
I've been trying to get good coverage in my garage so the security cams and smart devices don't get dropped connections, or long wait times when I try to connect from my app. This is finally the one! Frontier uses and all in one gateway, Arris NVG468MQ. In order to use the Netgear as the main router, I would need Frontier's help to put the Arris in bridge mode. I'm not sure if they can even do this, and since I purchased my own Arris to save rental fees, I wasn't sure how much they'd be willing to help either. So I didn't bother to try, instead, I set up the Netgear router in AP mode. To do this...

1. Go to Frontier's admin to turn off all wi-fi modes. Turn off both 2.4 and 5.0 modes.
2. Connect ethernet cable from the WAN port of the Netgear Router, to any available lan port of your Frontier gateway. Turn it on.
3. Using your smartphone or PC, connect to the Netgear wifi using the credentials labeled on the Netgear Router.
4. That's it. You should be online with the new wi-fi, but you'll want to change some things such as the orbi's admin password, your SSID's, etc. When you launch a browser under this new wi-fi, Netgear's admin should pop up allowing you to login to change your credentials, if it doesn't, then use routerlogin.net or orbilogin.net.
5. Since you've disabled Frontier's wifi, all your connected devices at home no longer works. But if you change your orbi's SSID to the same SSID that you were using, all your devices will work again. Keep in the mind, the Orbi system allows 4 different SSIDs. So you can still create other networks with different security levels.
6. Place the Orbi Satellite where you need better coverage. Power it on. Go back to Orbi Router and hit the sync button, within 30 seconds, you need to go back to the satellite and hit the sync button as well. Once they sync, which is indicated by solid blue for a few minutes, all lights will then be turned off. So keep that in mind, when it's up and running, there are no lights on the orbi router, or orbi satellite. I'm used to seeing some sort of lights on router equipment, so when there wasn't any lights, I was wondering if it was working properly. As it turns out, all lights are turned off when everything is up and running properly.

Even if you're not Frontier, the process I laid out above, to connect the Orbi in AP mode, should be similar. Hope this has been helpful! This is 5-Stars all the way!

title: Nifty tech with a lot of quirks that you have to get used to...
review_text:
THE GOOD:
--------------
* It will do as it says.. capture videos from your sources.
* Video quality seems fine to me. I'm not that picky, the stuff I record isn't important.
* You can install a micro SD card, or connect a hard drive via usb.

THE BAD:
-----------
* Consistent with their products, they cut corners when it comes to the remote control. It's just a terrible clunky experience. I can't even put into words what's wrong with it. I guess there is a delay. So if you're impatient, you'll be pressing too many buttons, and you'll be in the wrong menu, navigate to the wrong places, enable the wrong features, etc. So my advice is to be patient. Press the button you want to press, then wait a week for it to respond. I don't know what inner components make a great remote control. Whatever they are, they are not inside ClearClick remotes. I've reviewed some of their other Clearclick products that are $150 and less, and so I was more forgiving. But at $250, really? You're going to still skimp out on the remote at this price range?

* If you toggle into PLAYBACK mode... good luck getting out of it. Back button doesn't work, and it's always thinking you want to delete files. Everytime I escape playback mode, I'm relieved, but also have no clue how I got out.

* Power on/off is weird. There are scenarios that will make your heart stop because you'll think the device shorted out. Just like their terrible remotes, I've noticed this power issue with their other models too. The quirk is this... sometimes when you power off and on too quickly, it just goes dead. It will not respond for a long time. Don't panic. Stop pushing the power button. Just unplug everything. The hard drive, the HDMI, the power, unplug everything. Go walk your dog, and when you come back, and connect everything again, it will power up. This happens to other Clearclick devices I have, so when it happened with this device, I didn't panic. I knew what was up.

* Power port is micro usb. Again, at $250, I'd like to see USB-C. Micro usb is antiquated, and their cords are prone to get damaged.

* You will need a HDMI splitter to bypass HDCP, as well as be able to turn off your Clearclick when you're not recording, and still watch TV. In my scenario... my source goes into my splitter, and my splitter has TWO outs. One goes into the Clearclick, and the other goes to my projector. This way, I can turn off my Clearclick if I'm not recording, and still watch my projector. If I connect the source directly to the Clearclick, and then go OUT from the Clearclick to my projector, then I would get their ugly icons on my projector. In my pictures, the source is my Nvidia Shield, you'll notice a row of white icons at the top. There is no option to hide these icons in passthrough mode. So if you use the Clearclick as a passthrough, you will get those ugly icons on your big screen. So even if you're recording sources that do not need a HDMI splitter. I'd still get one anyway because using the hdmi passthrough is not pretty. However, the good thing is that the files you record, will not have those icons.

In conclusion, if this weren't a Vine item, I would send it back. Having said all that, it's possible that my expectations may be unreasonable for a very niche product. If a big company like Sony or Samsung create a polished standalone capture device like this, maybe it'd be $500-$600. In which case, you'd be pretty happy with the ClearClick. If you learn to live with the quirks, it's a nifty piece of tech. Hopefully, they can improve on the user experience through firmware updates. I'll go 3-Stars this time.

Other than that, I don't think I'll be putting any effort into this. I'll go 3-Stars!

title: Frontier customers, this is plug and play...
review_text:
I did not get mine on Amazon, so this is not a verified review. I got mine on a famous auction site, but I'm hear to assure you this is plug and play. I was confused by the product photo saying you need a MEB1100. Basically, if you're a current Frontier customer, and you don't have and don't know anything about the MEB1100, and everything has been working fine in your house with just the Arris, then don't worry about the MEB1100. However, if Frontier set you up with both the Arris and the MEB1100, then I recommend buying both. You want the set-up to stay the same.

I do use moca adapters to bring internet to rooms with coax cable. These are the ones I use: https://www.amazon.com/Motorola-Adapter-Ethernet-2-Pack-MM1002/dp/B078HMDDVS/ref=sr_1_2?dchild=1&keywords=Motorola+moca&qid=1617140900&sr=8-2 With the Arris router, you do not need to put an adapter next to it. My connection is like this:

* Ethernet from ONT in my garage goes to WAN port of the Arris router in living room.
* Coaxial from ONT goes to a 4 way splitter, one line goes to the living room, I connect this line to the coaxial on the Arris.
* Coaxial line in my bedroom goes to the network coaxial port of my moca adapter. I then hook up an ethernet hub to the ethernet port of the moca adapter. Voila! That's how I bring ethernet to my bedroom.
* I do the same to the other coaxial lines in my home to bring ethernet hubs to those rooms as well.

This has been how my home has functioned. All connections were left untouched. I simply swapped out the Frontier Arris for this identical Arris. I then made sure to go into the new Arris admin and create the same wifi SSID with the same password as before. All your wifi and network devices will function as normal, no need to re-enter any passwords. I contacted Frontier, and they are sending me a box with pre-paid envelope to ship back their router, and I was assured I will no longer be charged with rental fees. I'm happy to report every customer rep I've talked to have been very nice and accommodating. The FCC ruling to allow consumers to use their own routers have been in effect since December, so I think they've been given a memo that they need to accommodate us, instead of selling us on why we should use their router, or say they cannot remove the rental fee. The process has been painless.

5-Stars!

title: If you're a NVR newbie like me, I think my review has good info...
review_text:
Prior to getting this NVR system, I had already started researching on POE switches. For some reason, I assumed all NVR cameras are POE. I knew this Dragon Touch NVR had no POE ports in the back, but it didn't matter because I had planned to use POE switches. If you're a newbie like me, here are some noteworthy things before you make your decision:

1. The four cameras in this set comes with four power adapters. I thought how nice of them to include this option. But as it turns out, this is NOT an option. You need to use the power adapters for each camera. I learned that getting POE switches is only half the battle, the other half is making sure the cameras are POE compatible. I didn't know that. I thought POE switches would allow me to get rid of power adapters to any camera, any brand. Sadly, this is not the case. So this Dragon Touch system is designed for wi-fi. You only need to hook up the power adapter to each camera. But the whole point of me going to NVR is to use ethernet for more dependable connections. You can still do that with this system, but you'll still need to connect the power adapters, so you're running two cables for each camera. Had I known that, I would not have gotten this system.

2. You can use other brand cameras with this NVR if the cameras are ONVIF. However, I'm betting they still need to be the non-POE kind. I'm trying to connect a H.View POE camera, but I'm getting a black screen. Dragon Touch said that model is not compatible. End of email. I had to follow up with "What POE cameras are compatible?" I'll update when they respond.

3. It goes without saying, but in case you don't know, you need to connect NVR to a monitor for viewing. The back of the NVR has options for VGA or HDMI out. Alternatively, you can view via their Homeviz app.

4. No hard drive is included, but a hard drive is not necessary for you to start learning, testing, and setting things up. You can live view without a hard drive, but to record you'll need to install a hard drive.

5. Lastly, I'll talk about the build quality of this system. The Dragon Touch is very professionally packaged, the NVR is small and light, but that's without a hard drive currently. The cameras feel real nice, has good heft to them. I am not going to subtract any stars because of my newbie assumptions. As a matter of fact, I'm learning that if you want NVR systems with POE cameras, they would be much more expensive than what you're paying here. If I can figure a way to run both ethernet and power adapters, I may end up using this system. However, I will subtract a star for the lack of info in their listing, and emails. A product like this should clearly state whether or not their cameras are POE, and whether or not the NVR can handle POE cameras. 4-Stars.

title: Awesome camera! My review includes tips should you have issues accessing the ADMIN page...
review_text:
Feels like a very solid camera in terms of build quality. Nice and hefty. Everybody's networking ability is different. Some may find this very difficult to set up, some may find it a breeze. I hit a snag, and was SMH for awhile, but I figured it out, and I'll share with you my issue, and how I solved it. So if you happen to run into the same issue, these notes may help.

So H.View provides you with an ADMIN IP address which should work once your camera is connected to your home network. In this case, it's 192.168.1.120. You punch this into you browser, and you should be able to get to the ADMIN page to change your password and view your camera. But what happens when this IP address doesn't work for you? You will need to change it accordingly to your IPV4 gateway. I found out the easiest way is to simply let the IPC Manager modify it automatically by DHCP. I posted 3 screenshots to hopefully guide you. Here are some worthy notes...

1. Google "IPC Manager H.View" to find your way to their site to download the software. Top result with the headline DOWNLOAD CENTER should be the correct one. Be sure to download the version for your device, Linux, Mac, or Windows. BTW, they keep this in a Google Drive folder, so don't worry, you're in the right place.

2. Connect your camera to your network via POE switch. This set DOES NOT come with a power adapter, it is meant for POE switch users.

3. Install and launch the software and login in the lower left corner. Default is ADMIN and 12345. You can change this later. The login is strange because it doesn't give any feedback. Usually after logging in to a software, something changes or refreshes, such as a "log out" option, this lets you know you're logged in. But there seems to be no reaction in this software. After you hit enter, nothing changes. So don't fret, you're really logged in.

4. If you don't see any cameras, right click and hit refresh. Once you see your camera, check the box to SELECT your camera. Now, if you right click on your camera, there is a menu with a "OPEN HOME" option. If you click this, it "should" launch you to the admin page at 192.168.1.120, where you can change your password and view the camera. You can also manually punch the ip address in your browser.

5. This is where I ran into a snag. The default IP did not work for me. The browser would load an error page, "This site could not be reached." Proceed to #6 if you encounter this issue...

6. Go back into the IPC software. Make sure the default login credentials are still present, make sure your Camera is still Selected. Now, SELECT the DHCP box, and hit MODIFICATION. There should be a pop-up indicating the modification was successful. The IP address should now have changed from 192.168.1.120 to whatever new address that your router assigned. If it's still the same, try hitting refresh.

7. So now, you right click on your camera and hit OPEN HOME again, and you should be able to get to the admin page now. Or as mentioned before, just manually punch in the new IP address into your browser. When you successfully reach the admin page for the first time, you will be prompted to change your password. Now you can view your camera. Next time you go back tin the IPC software, make sure to use your new password.

I included 3 screenshots to supplement these notes. Hope that helps! This is a 5-Star product!

title: Not like any other digital picture frames out there. This is next level!
review_text:
In terms of hardware, this is the best as well as biggest picture frame we've ever owned, and believe it or not, it's not even their biggest offering. This is next level stuff, not comparable to the plethora of unknown 10 inch digital frames in the market. It is also by Netgear, a well known brand. However, the app is not intuitive at all. It's not impossible to get used. Someone who is used to tech, like me, will fiddle around with it and eventually get it. But if you're giving this as a gift to your parents or aunties? You better be there to set it up for them, and walk them through.

So they decided to make this gesture base instead of touchscreen, I guess to keep your screen free of fingerprints. But gestures require a knack, so it will be hit or miss with friends and family trying to do the gesturing. But for the owner, it's a knack that you an easily master. There are basically 2 gesture sensor locations. If it's in landscape position like ours, then they'll be in the middle of the top frame, and in the middle of the left frame. I have a picture illustrating this. The palm of your hands should be facing yourself, and the back of the hand toward the frame, gesture up and down at a pretty good speed, and be as close to the frame as possible without touching it. That's why I say this is a knack only owners will master. Friends who try it will be less aggressive because they don't want to knock over your frame, so their hands won't come as close to the frame. So it'll be hit or miss for them. For owners who are used to it, response rate can be 100%.

The Meural app is not intuitive. For example, you have an UPLOAD button that will have access to your phone's default CAMERA folder. Once you make your selections, you hit SEND. In the Meural app, your uploaded photos will be found under YOUR LIBRARY, and at the top under RECENTS. If you browse your YOUR LIBRARY and view the pictures you just SENT, it will prompt you to SEND again. Which is confusing. Because I've already uploaded the pictures, why do I need to hit SEND again? It should be PLAY. So for whatever reason, it likes to use the word SEND. You'll be doing a lot of sending. LOL! It's just like Amazon's photo app, Google or iPhone, there is a learning curve that is not impossible to understand.

Lastly, it seems to be a ploy to make money off of premium art pictures via membership or one time purchase prices. Like in-app purchase in games, you have in-app purchases in Meural for premium photos. They have free pictures labeled SAMPLES. Here is a big tip, DO NOT hit send. I realize once you stop viewing the SAMPLES, and switch to your own family photos, those SAMPLES are gone. They are not in YOUR LIBRARY. You have to go look for them again in their picture store. What what you should do is hit FAVORITE. This way it will stay in YOUR LIBRARY under Favorites, and you don't have to go searching for it again.

At the end of the day, if you would like something less expensive, but more intuitive, and is 100% geared towards your own photos, and has nothing to do with selling you photos, then look for frames made for the FRAMEO app. Feel Care is a popular brand that uses the Frameo app. As a gift for non-tech relatives, those will be a much better option: https://www.amazon.com/review/R2VC33MUEW4RFN/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B08DFW6R9F

As for the Meural Frame, I'll give it 4-Stars! I like it a lot, it's next level stuff in digital photo frames, but the decision to go with gesture is interesting. Maybe Gesturing is more higher end than Touching? LOL? It's like they're trying to drive that point home that they are in another league. Why not give us the option of touchscreen too with gesturing? People are giving bad reviews, but I think those are impatient people. Like I said this is no different than Google photos, Amazon, or iPhone, there is a learning curve. I will take 1 star off for the app being counter intuitive, which could make non-tech people frustrated.

title: Great dashcam, but read my review for alternative installation method.
review_text:
This is a terrific kit, complete with everything to get you started... Some important notes...

1.) If you already have a camera in place that uses mini usb, then half the battle is already won. Most of these cameras use mini usbs.

2.) The Viofo has a capacitor battery, which is what you want, especially if you live in the hot areas. They are not prone to ballooning like lithium batteries.

3.) Instructions say to slide the camera onto a mounting plate, which has an adhesive backing, you then remove the adhesive cover and stick entire unit on the glass. But it comes to you preinstalled, at least mind was. All you have to do is peel the adhesive cover and stick the unit onto your glass. Out of curiosity, I tried to remove the plate, but I couldn't, it is very tight. So if you stick the unit to your window, taking it down for whatever reason will be a pain. I don't see how you can dismount the camera and leave the plate on the window. You would have to take the plate with you, which means ripping the adhesive from the glass.

So here's my tip... I'd like to be able to remove the camera, fiddle with it, change settings, etc. without hassle. Or perhaps, even dismount and hide my camera in the glove compartment when I need to. If you install it the way they tell you to, you will never take this camera down. My solution for this is using strong round earth magnets. I installed a round earth magnet on the back of the unit. This is easy, since it already has an adhesive back, just remove the cover and stick a magnet on it. Then I install another one directly onto the glass. These neodymium magnets are very strong and the hold is absolutely solid. This is how I install dashcams for myself and family. I have not installed the rearview, but I'll be using the same method. This is a 5-Star kit!

title: Sleek design, nifty tech, and terrific sound quality...
review_text:
Replacing my altec lansing speakers from the early 2000's. Honestly, I'm not an audiophile. My altec speakers were pretty good speakers too, and I can't tell the difference. My upgrade is simply cosmetics. This logitech set is black and sleek, looks more modern. My altec speakers were grayish, very early 2000's design.

I like the nifty wireless controller that looks like a little echo dot, but it's smaller. So coming from speakers in the early 2000's, my first question was.. Can this function like old school speakers if I don't care for all the tech? So I simply used the 3.5mm connection method from my dell to the logitech, but there was NO SOUND. So you have to at least power up the wireless controller for the first time. Because under the controller is a button to switch from bluetooth to wired. Press the WIRE option, and you will then get audio. After this, if you remove the batteries and take away the wireless controller, the speakers will continue to work as 3.5mm connected speaker. You just have to turn on the wireless controller on the initial set-up. So this is good. My concern was what if the wireless controller is lost or damaged? If that happens, then you would like the speakers to go on like old school speakers connected simply by 3.5mm. So I'm happy to report, this will function without the wireless controller module. I'm not even sure turning on the wireless controller in the initial set-up is absolutely required. Your PC my pick-up sound the moment you plug in the 3.5mm jack. For me, I had to turn on the wireless controller during the initial set-up.

Another thing I wondered is if I connect a bluetooth device, say my smartphone, to these speakers, then disconnect, will the speakers automatically revert back to wired? The answer is no. To connect to a bluetooth device, you have to press the bluetooth pairing button under the wireless controller, and it will stay in this mode even after you disconnect. You have to press the "wire" button to get back to 3.5mm.

One more thing, the left and right speakers have 2 slots in the back to insert the stand. So you can configure it to stand vertically or horizontally. Conclusion... I love the sound, the sleek design and the technology. 5-Stars.

review_text:

But the best thing about this device is that you DO NOT need a hdmi splitter to bypass hdcp. If you've tried other capture devices, you might have ran into this issue. You will get a black screen. I was pleasantly surprised no splitter was necessary. There are so many use cases for this device, mostly people will use it to capture game play. My use case is recording Laker games. Frontier no longer carries my Lakers in Southern California, so I'm using my relatives Spectrum credentials. LOL! But doing that, I don't have any DVR functionality. title: Premium product, lackluster app and instructions...
review_text:
Very nice high quality item, but you're sort of left in the wind to figure things out yourself. Here are some things to note, so you don't encounter the same issues as I did.

-The app to download is called PRINT MASTER. You'll naturally want to download Phomemo app, but you'll soon realize it won't connect with your printer. Then you'll notice there is a specific Phomemo 110 app, so you download that as well. But after installing this app, a pop up says "we are discontinuing this app, please download PRINT MASTER." There, I saved you from the run-around I encountered. LOL!

-You are given a starter roll of labels, but to use the templates in the Print Master app, you'll need to choose the proper dimension. It would be nice if this info was given in the manual, but the manual doesn't even mention the free roll. Everything is in mm, but I happened to have a mm ruler and measured the labels to be 40x30mm.

-Lastly, the most important advice you need to know is you need to turn on AUTOMATIC. You might ask AUTOMATIC what? My reply is.. EXACTLY. LOL! You see, once you go to print your label. There is a setting called AUTOMATIC. There is no explanation as to what this means. The default is WHITE, which is OFF. What it means is where it will stop after it prints your label. If it's OFF, it will NOT stop. It will continue spitting out blank labels. I saw a YT reviewer who had this issue, and I didn't think anything of it, until it happened to me. LOL! You need to turn this to GRAY, which is ON. It will then automatically stop after it prints your label. Why in the world is the default set to continuously print blanks? We all tend to use default settings because we trust the manufacture knows what's best for us. I mean why would you turn something on if you don't know what it does? So I can see why many make this mistake. But now you know. Turn it on! Even if you need multiple copies, for example 5 copies. You still need to turn it on, so that it will stop after 5 labels. I would love for someone experience with these things, or the seller, to comment below what that setting is for, and why is the default off?

The hardware is 5 star. The app is okay, it's a little slow. There is some lag after you make your selections. So I'll subtract a star for that. Then I'm subtracting another star for the lack of useful instructions. 3-Stars.

title: Read my review to avoid my mistake...
review_text:
IMPORTANT ADVICE... do not thread the mini ball head onto anything too tightly. This stand is actually fine, it's the cheap ball head that has given me headaches. The ball head has a... I'm not sure what the technical term is for this kind of bolt, but lets call it a "dual bolt." 1/4 bolt is threaded inside a bigger bolt, I presume 1/2. I threaded a mini projector onto this thing, I guess a little too tight. When I unthreaded the projector, the 1/4 bolt was stuck, meaning it was unthreading WITH the projector. So the 1/4 bolt came off the 1/2 bolt. You would think that all it takes are some pliers, but surprisingly, pliers even with teeth, have a hard time gripping this bolt. I had to use my drill press vise to get it off.

To properly use that ball head, you want to thread it onto whatever device you're using, but don't thread it on too tight like me. Then tighten with the lower knob. You might think, this reviewer isn't using common sense. I don't think so at all. Anybody would like his/her electronics threaded securely. The amount of strength I used was reasonable. The issue lies in that inner 1/4 bolt not being secured enough inside that bigger bolt. But I fixed that. Once I was able to unthread the projector from the vise... with the 1/4 bolt now free, but secured by the vise, I then took the ball head body to the vise and threaded the bigger bolt onto the 1/4 bolt a "wee bit" tighter than the manufacturer did.

If you don't have drill press vise like I do, then you better be extra careful using this. 3-Stars.

title: Relatively easy to set-up. If you can't access the user interface, read my review...
review_text:
I had my concerns because I've researched Powerline Adapters before, and there is talk about how your home's electrical wiring may cause your adapters to work or not work depending on where you plug in your adapters. For me, the process was pretty painless. I plugged the main adapter (GPL-2000PT) to a wall outlet next to my Frontier Gateway. Then an ethernet cable connects my Gateway to this adapter. BTW, the GPL-2000PT is the smaller of the two adapters. For some reason, my brain correlates MAIN as being BIGGER. So without looking at the model numbers on the device, I connected the bigger adapter next to my router initially and got it wrong, and had to start over. Anyway, so remember the smaller one is the one that gets tethered to your router. Next you plug the bigger adapter (GPL-2000WAC) to wherever you want to have the new wi-fi network. Press the Security button on the main adapter, then press the Security button on the other adapter.. wait for them to pair, and voila, you have a new wi-fi network. In my case, I was pleasantly surprised that everything worked because I needed better wi-fi in the garage, and there weren't any wall outlets available. Manual specifically recommends using wall outlets. I have these outlet boxes that the previous homeowner had installed along exposed 2x4 beams. I plugged the adapter into one of these and crossed my fingers, and amazingly, everything linked up. Speeds are super fast and snappy too.

The hiccup I run into, which is the same hiccup I run into every time I play around with gadgets of this kind whether it be powerline, meshes, or wi-fi extenders.... is the part where I would like to change the SSID and password. The default they give you is always something that's hard to remember, so you always want to change this. I can never get to their user interface with their provided IP's. The idea is that once you're on the adapter's network, you should be able to go to the provided address to access the user interface. It never works for me, no matter the brand. Either there is something about my network that I'm not understanding, or there are many consumers in the same boat as as I am. In any case, I will tell you what does work for me every time.. I simply go to my own router ADMIN. So if you're Spectrum, go to your Spectrum admin, if you're Frontier, Verizon, etc., go to their router admin. Then look for your new Nexuslink adapter. Your router would have assigned it an IP address. Type that ip address into the browser, and it will take you to the Nexuslink user interface. So whenever you can't get to a user interface provided the manufacturer of a powerline adapter, wifi extender, etc., just go to your own router admin and get the IP address that it was assigned. BTW, when you're browsing your router admin for the IP address of the adapter, you might not know what you're looking for since it may not be labeled by your router properly. So you'll need to find it through a process of elimination. All the IP addresses listed will show whether the device is connected by wi-fi, moca, or ethernet. So you can ignore all the wi-fi and mocas. Look for the ethernet connection that is unfamiliar to you. Mine showed up as "UNKNOWN." I have several devices connected to my network as UNKNOWN. I simply tried them all out, and one of the addresses eventually took me to the Nexuslink user interface.

If any network expert is reading this, I'd love for you to chime in below in the comment section and explain when it comes to this part regarding accessing the user interface of an adapter whether it be powerline, wifi extenders, etc., why the default given address in the manual never works for some of us. This hiccup doesn't deserve a star subtraction since I've experienced this with every other brand I've tried. Anyway, I can now access my garage camera blazingly fast, versus the 50/50 hit or miss connections before. This is 5 stars!

title: This is a 480p projector with an awesome on/off design...
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:a1ea9dee5ef92897a45e22f1f1942100]] When it comes to mini projectors, the Nebula Capsule 2 is still the best in my book, but you'll be spending more than twice the cost of this Walnutt DLP. If money is not an obstacle, then go check that one out. Who is Walnutt? I don't know, but I think even the big boys like Anker (who makes the Nebula) would be impressed by their design. This isn't quite small as a soda can, but it's still a nifty beautiful design. You twist the top to form a shape that looks like those right angle PVC elbows, and your projector turns on. Twist it back to form a cannister, and it turns off. That is a very neat design. It doesn't seem like it's a white label product either since I can't find any similar projectors under different brands. Walnutt is the only one selling this. So kudos to them for their unique product.

Because of the built in 3200mah battery as well as a USB port, you can be completely wireless watching the fire stick, the chromecast, etc. You simply use the USB port to power the fire stick. For how long, maybe just one movie, before you need to plug in the projector power adapter, but you'll never need to find a power source for your fire stick as long as you use the USB port. However, the native resolution is 854x480. I was completely fooled by the 1080p in their product headline, when it actually said "1080p supported." That's my fault for skimming, not reading. But this means you can play 1080p, it will just be scaled down. This is a 480p projector. The speakers are 2.5 watts x 2. There are no controls, other than the focus wheel, on the projector unit. So you better make sure you never lose your remote.

At this price point, you can't ask for the world. If you want to pay double and get the Nebula Capsule 2, that thing is 720p, has a 9700mah battery, android, and has 8w speaker.. all in a soda can size body. But for all that, you're paying over double. So at the end of the day, this is a good 480p projector, at a proper price with a nifty design. I'll give this 5 stars.

My video demo is in a garage with no white screen, just the garage door material, you can see the garage door hardware. LOL! It was about 4 pm, sun was still out. I simply turned off the lights.

title: Of all the surveillance cameras I've used, this one has the best software...
review_text:
I've used cheap Wyze cameras as well as more expensive cameras like Arlo in my garage, but wi-fi is pretty iffy there. I wanted to see if the wi-fi receiver in this HomeHawk beats the Wyze or Arlo, but unfortunately, that's not the case. The HomeHawk struggled in my garage as much as the others did. As a matter of fact, I couldn't connect to it at all. So right off the bat, that is something to note... that paying more for a camera doesn't necessarily mean better wi-fi receivers are inside the camera. This isn't something I'm going to subtract a star for since no cameras on the market can help with my wi-fi situation, that's something that will have to be remedied by wi-fi extenders.

Now once I move this camera indoor, with better wi-fi reception, to monitor the backyard, it does the job wonderfully! The app is great and full of features. Be sure you select the proper MODE. By default, it was on BASIC and it did not do any recordings. I realize I had to change it to PROTECTION mode or 24/7 mode. Or, better yet, you can create your own mode! You can determine if it will record 24/7, or only when it detects motion. You can determine the duration of the clip. Now that is pretty cool! The default is 10 seconds, and for several weeks I thought I had to live with the default, until I discovered that I can actually change this by creating my own Mode. You can determine if it will notify you for every motion detected, or only for human detections. Lastly, you can name the mode anything you want, then select it and you're set! I've only used Wyze, Arlo and Homehawk cameras, and without a doubt, this Panasonic software is the best of the bunch. 5-stars!

title: High quality camera, but it runs very hot currently...
review_text:
Okay, you know the saying about first impressions? Presentation matters in a "premium" product. Anything north of $200, I expect good packaging. This Panacast is priced over $500 and has a retail of nearly a $1000. This is iPhone territory, yet the thin cardboard box with creases looks like packaging you'd find on any other white label gadget coming outta China. It was smushed a little cause it was shipped in an Amazon white padded envelope. If it weren't for the fact that this is a Vine item for me, I'd be so upset.

As for the camera itself, it is pretty nifty and the quality is what you'd expect for something over $500. It is small, but when you hold it in your hands, you feel the heft of the metal. It is definitely not one of those cheap lightweight plastic cameras. However, they got to do something about the heat. After a few minutes, you can fry eggs with it. It runs hot! I hope future firmware can do something about this.

There is nothing obvious in terms of picture or video quality that would separate this from the $100 stuff on the market. They all look the same to me. The 180 degree is the reason you're getting this. If you download their JabraDirect software, you'll have more control over the camera. For instance, you can lock in at a certain degree. I like to play around with the 180 degree, so initially I was annoyed that it kept automatically zooming in and out on me due to movement. The desktop software will allow you to lock in on any degree you want. I'm sure this will make a fine camera for business settings, but for us, it's simply for video calls with relatives overseas. Grandparents will often say, "what's my little boy doing over there?" Well, now they get to have a wider view.

The price, the underwhelming packaging, and the heat issue... I'm knocking 2 stars.

title: All plastic, no 1080P recording, and read my advice regarding micro sd card insertion...
review_text:
I used to have a cheaper one where you connect it to your smartphone, so when I saw this I grabbed it. I read two reviews where one said you cannot record 1080p, but the other said that you could. You know there are cheap cameras everywhere recording 1080p. For $90, I'm disappointed to confirm the reviewer who said this only records videos in VGA and snap pictures at 720p. 1080p is only for onscreen viewing. This won't be a big deal for me since I'm not in a profession that uses this daily. I figure it's nifty to have in the toolbox, and perhaps know my way around my walls. For example, last month I drilled a hole into my wall, thinking I can drop some cables down, but the cables hit a horizontal beam. I think in construction this is called a fire stop. Hopefully this will help me learn the paths I could take in my walls.

For a professional who will use this daily, who perhaps would like to bring back a picture or a video and blow it up on his monitor for a more detailed view, 1980's VGA quality is a big thumbs down! The build quality is also not substantial either. Everything is plastic. The whole unit is about 13.5 ounces.

I do like all the provided accessories, especially the hook. I can see how that will come in handy. To view something in the wall or pipe and to pry it out with the hook. The cable is stiff and bendable allowing you to position your lens just the way you want it.

IMPORTANT ADVICE REGARDING MICRO SD CARD!!!
------------------------------------------------------------
Be very careful when removing and inserting the sd card. You have to be sure to look at the slot, and be sure you slide the card in completely horizontal. ORIGINAL REVIEW:
--------------------------
I tried and tried, but it just didn't work for me. Perhaps you truly need newer tech? I contacted Anker to get some info. They told me I absolutely have to use a USB-C to USB-C cable. Which basically means, only newer pcs and laptops. I was connecting the dock to my windows laptop with a USB-C to USB-A cable. Anker says this is not sufficient power, but my laptop has it's own power source and the Anker has its own power source, and the HDMI goes from the Anker to the monitor. Why can't this work?

So in any case, the only USB-C powered "laptop" I have is my Google Pixel Slate. Again, the Anker is connected with its own power source, and since my slate has two usb-c ports, I gave power to the Slate independently instead of having the Anker dock be the sole source. Then the other USB-C port is then connected from the Slate to the Dock. From here, HDMI out from Dock to monitor.... drum roll.... still no dice. I tried two dell monitors, so I figure lets try a normal tv, and unfortunately, no picture there either.

Perhaps I just don't have the proper USB-C laptop or tablet that's compatible with this dock. Perhaps it's not compatible with the Pixel Slate since it's running on Chrome. I dunno... Perhaps there is a firmware update that can fix this? I went to Anker's site. Went to SUPPORT. Clicked on UPDATE FIRMWARE. I was given three choices... Cables, Audio or Hubs and Docks! This is getting exciting! Perhaps there is a firmware update! So I clicked on Hubs and Docks and downloaded the software for Windows. But when I ran the software, it turns out to be an updater for their Speakers. :( Anker told me perhaps it's defective, so we did a replacement to no avail, it still doesn't display for me. All the other ports work fine, just no display.

My computer gear is top of the line from about 5 yrs ago. One of which is a Vaio Canvas Z, but neither have USB-C. My only USB-C laptop is the Pixel Slate, but it's a chromebook. Maybe you need a recent windows laptop with USB-C? I would appreciate any info in the comments section. Anybody who got theirs to work with a PC that doesn't have USB-C, please comment below. If you got it to work with a Chromebook, please comment below. Please let me know what you did. For me, it's not displaying anything, but all the usb ports, card reader, ethernet work fine. I will update and revise my rating if I can get it to display. Otherwise, it's a nice looking dock, sleek and compact.
