title: Complicated, but it got rid of HDCP for me...
review_text:
08/13/2020 UPDATE:
-------------------------
All right, so a quirk that some of you may encounter is that when you connect the splitter, your TV may turn on Action Smoothing automatically. I have a TCL and that's the term they use. Other TVs may go by a different term. But essentially, it is the "soap opera" effect. It is great for sports, but weird for movies. But when I turned it back to off, the "soap opera" effect was still there. So I thought the splitter overrides the TCL settings, which would make it unusable for me. But on a hunch, I decided to unplug the TCL tv, and when I replugged, the "soap opera" effect was gone. So if you're experiencing this, try unplugging your TV and replugging it. I was able to reproduce this quirk with a different HDMI splitter, so this is not an issue with the HDMI splitter, it is an issue with the TV being stuck on Action Smoothing... In my case, it's a TCL.

Original Review
------------------
I needed to disable HDCP for a PC-less capture card. This splitter is more advanced than any splitter I have ever used. I'm used to the splitters that just splits and has no settings. This splitter makes you use your brain, and sometimes I don't want to use my brain. After a lot of tinkering with the various combinations of the switches, I ended up leaving the EDID at COPY1 and the Scaler switches to OFF... which was actually the default settings they ship to you. LOL!

Also understand that for every setting you play around with, if you don't get a picture, it might not mean it doesn't work. Along with your settings, you need to try switching your tv inputs back and forth, turning off/on your sources, turning off/on your capture card, etc., to truly see if it works. This will be the most confusing and frustrating part of setting this up. Not to mention, do you have the proper HDMI cables? Manual says use HDMI 2.0 cables. A lot of my cables are 1.3 or 1.4, but it still worked. So maybe if I had some HDMI 2.0 cables, it would have saved me some headache?

Ultimately, I stumbled upon the fact that if I leave it at COPY1 and Scalers off, turn off my capture card, then turn it back on, as well as switch tv input, then switch it back. It works! And it's not something you always need to do every time you turn on your tv. It's a one time thing. Once the splitter and your devices are in sync, you're good to go. There is one more step you can take if this doesn't work. There is a pinhole on the splitter labeled "UPDATE." Right on the splitter itself, there are printed notes on what this pinhole is for. Basically after resetting switches, changing inputs, etc., and you still have video or audio issues such as garbled noises, you need to use a tiny pin key, like the ones supplied by your smartphones to remove your sim trays. Poke it inside and feel for a button. Press it until it flashes 3 times. I guess this does some sort of "update" telling the splitter.. "Hey, these are the new settings, get with the program!" It worked for me in fixing garbled audio.

I will acknowledge that user experience and expertise level in AV tech plays a role in how much "tinkering" is necessary. The less you know, the more you're going to tinker. Still, I think the manual could be better and more in depth, maybe provide a pin key for the pinhole? Regarding this pinhole, the instructions says to push the "button." There is no button, and I had to look around for my sim key. For most consumers, this won't be "plug and play" as the listing suggest. But it works, and I will go 4 stars for this.

title: You will need a HDMI splitter....
review_text:
THINGS YOU WILL NEED:
----------------------------
-HDMI Splitter that can bypass HDCP (For digital caputuring. What device isn't digital nowadays?)
-Flash drive or Hard Drive: Maximum flash drive space is 256gb. Maximum hard drive is 8tb.

As a kid, I used to love recording tv or cable to VHS. Then in the late 90's and early 2000's, I was into those Hard Drive recorders with built in dvd-r burners by Pioneer and Philips, remember those? But then Tivo and Cable DVR really took off and made recording to actual dvds a thing of the past. So what we have here with the ClearClick is simply a device that brings the "old way" of archiving to 2020, but instead of VHS and DVR-Rs, it will record as MP4 files into your flash drive. I also think the reason these devices are still relevant is due to the phenomenon of gamers who love to record all their game-play. Anyway, I'm happy to report it does exactly what it advertises brilliantly. However, unless you're only capturing analog signals (VHS transers), you will need a HDMI splitter that can bypass HDCP. In my use case scenario... I have a Caavo Universal Remote/HDMI Switcher. The Caavo has four HDMI inputs. I have my Tivo, a Fire TV, a Android TV box, and the Nintendo Switch hooked to it. Then it has one HDMI output. This output normally goes to the TV. So that's my set-up...

Now to hook up this ClearClick, I remove the HDMI that connects to the TV from the Caavo, and instead, I connect it to the Input of the special HDMI Splitter. Then HDMI OUT from this splitter to the input of the ClearClick. Finally, HDMI OUT from the ClearClick to an input on my TV. This way, I can capture from any device I want that's connected to my Caavo. Of course, you can just connect one source at a time too if you don't have a hub like I do. title: Not just for displaying photos, I have some outside the box ideas...
review_text:
I've always thought photo frames are gimmicky, but FeelCare has changed my mind. The difference in using these versus turning a tablet into a photo frame is that it SIMPLY WORKS as it should. Getting a tablet to be a photo frame is quite involved and requires more maintenance. Also, this item actually looks like a picture frame! When you fire it up, it's actually running Android, a stripped down version that focuses just on being a photo player. The Frameo app allows you to beam photos to it easily. You can designate sleep hours for the frame so that it's not always on 24/7. I have mine asleep from 1 am to 8 am. Techies will turn old tablets into photo frames, but I think the main market here is for older people who are not techies. Great for parents and grandparents, but we'll be using it too and we're not quite grandparents yet.

Here are some outside the box ideas...

A joke on your friends:
--------------------------
Imagine your buddy come over to your house and looking at all the frames on your mantle. Smack dab in the center is a picture of his grandparents, or perhaps, his mom? LOL! He'll be like, "What the... why do you have a picture of my mom?" LOL! To do this joke, you need the frame to have only a few photos that's because it doesn't know how to display just 1 photo all day. It has to be in Slideshow mode 24/7. But you can select photos to hide. So if you have 5 photos, you can easily hide 4 of it, then it will only show 1 photo all day. If you have 200 photos, you would have to select 199 to hide. The joke is probably not worth that hassle. LOL! To pull it off, you also need to lower the brightness so that it matches the brightness of the regular surrounding pictures. And of course, hide the wires as best you can.

Card Magic Trick:
-------------------
I do card magic, and immediately I thought of a use for this frame. Have your spectator choose a card, then read his mind, then point him to the photo frame and say, "is that your card?" If you do Magic, you'll figure out plenty of ways to pull off this trick. This frame is pretty neat! 5 Stars!

title: Easy peasy back up!
review_text:
I read some of the reviews and concerns. Many are saying you need the original power adapter. My testing says that is NOT true. I plugged this cube into two separate charging hubs, not apple brand, and both scenarios worked.

You need a micro SD card (not included). Some of the questions in the Q&A shows that shoppers don't realize this. There is no built in hard drive in this cube, you provide the storage.

Turning off auto-sleep/auto-lock may get you through thousands of pictures in one shot. This is what I mean... I'm no stranger to trying out different back-up programs. The current program we use is from Plex. When the iphone is backing up to my plex server, the iphone doesn't know that plex is working, so it goes to sleep after about 50 pictures. When it goes to sleep, plex stops backing up. So I always turn off auto-sleep prior to backing up. With the Qubii, the iphone KNEW that it was working, so it "almost" never went to sleep. I said almost because after 4000 files, for some reason, the phone went to sleep. Still, this is much, much, better than the plex app. When I started Qubii again, it picked up where it left off and backed the remaining 1000+ files. But I did the test one more time to make sure! I cleared the micro sd card, and I reset the Qubii count. This time I turned off auto-sleep/auto-sleep on the iphone, and it backed-up the entire camera roll of over 5000 photos and videos in one shot! More trials need to be done to conclusively say this thing can't get through 5000 files without the auto-sleep disabled.

After backing up everything, you should remove your SD card from the Qubii and transfer them to a larger permanent hard drive where you store your collection. The next time you charge your phone, the Qubii will remember the photos it already backed-up even if those photos are no longer on the SD card. So you can always clear your SD card. For whatever reason, if you need the Qubii to back-up the same photos again, like I did when I was testing things out, all you have to do is RESET the Qubii count, which you can do in the Back Up Settings in the app.

Below are the two pictures showing you the scenarios in which I tested this Qubii. Both scenarios used third party charging hubs, but I believe I had the original apple cable. As with all products dependent on apps.. one Apple update can ruin everything. LOL! So these types of app products depend on the company to stick around, so that if Apple breaks anything, they can fix it with a new firmware update. Qubii was on Kickstarter, but only time will tell. As is, this is an amazing product.

title: Subtle Wavy Diagonal Lines....
review_text: You know I see a lot of positive reviews, and if you're happy that's all that matters. But I'm wondering if all the positive is because people are not comparing one adapter to another, so they don't know any better. This adapter is a generic design, most likely a white label product, meaning many people are selling the same thing, and they are just slapping their own logo on it. I bought this version and the MayFlash version, and after comparing them, I returned this generic version. I got wavy diagonal lines with this generic version. The picture is still okay, but I could see the lines. With the MayFlash, it  was gone. The picture was much smoother. I don't know if using a projector makes a difference, but that is what I'm using, an ultra short throw projector with a 120" screen.  With such a big image, maybe I'm seeing the diagonal lines much easier. So I'm not sure if this is the case for people using smaller LCD tvs. In any case, all else being equal, if the mayflash could eliminate the lines for me on a 120" image, it would surely do a spectacular job for smaller screens. If you see subtle wavy diagonal lines, then give the mayflash a try. If you don't see any lines with this version, then stick with it, no need to tinker. This was just my experience.

review_text:
Right off the bat, you need to understand I did not purchase this case for a Surface Pro, I purchased it for the Pixel Slate. It is very difficult to find any accessories for the Slate, but luckily the Slate and the Surface Pro are very similar in size.

I first bought a similar case by Infiland for $24. When I realized this Finite version is basically the same case for less money, I bought it to see which charcoal color I like better. title: One word.... UNCOMFORTABLE.
review_text:
At $160, I said Nah. At $120, I said let me check this out, and my instincts were right, this is a no-go. Brydge seems to be a legit aspiring company, but I hope they go back to the drawing board and add upper cases to their keyboard design. So that you can put your tablet in a case, then the case connects to the keyboard, a perfect example of this design is an iPad keyboard made by Yoozon, I just reviewed it, it is awesome. There is absolutely no fear of damaging the screen with that type of design. But as for this Brydge keyboard, one word sums up my experience.. uncomfortable.

So there are 3 issues with this design:

1. There is no case, your tablet is exposed. This is not a deal-breaker, I knew it going in. But understand nobody makes any cases for pixel slate. Even Brydge makes a bunch of cases for various ipads complete with slots cut-out so that they can be slide right into their hinge keyboards. But there are no such products for the Slate, so you'll expose it to scatches.

2. Light bleeding in the corner caused by the hinges. I knew this going in as well, but I was thinking maybe it's paranoia. At $120, I wanted to check it out. And honestly, playing with it did not ease my concerns. You don't see any light bleeding at all, but you do see it when you close it like a laptop and the hinge is applying its pressure. I tried to reproduce this light bleed by applying pressure with my thumb, and I could not get it to bleed. So this tells me the hinge is applying a tremendous amount of pressure. Right now, the bleeding goes away the moment it's opened, but by opening and closing constantly and daily, I fear one day the bleeding will stay lit because I've seen this issue on normal laptops.

3. The hinge is a very thin sharp metal. The padding is what prevents it from scratching your tablet. But the padding for one hinge was no longer sticking flush with the metal. It would get caught at times when I'm sliding in the tablet. Good thing I was careful because if you carelessly trust the product, it can scratch your tablet if the rubber gets caught and pulled. Hard to articulate what I'm saying, so I've attached a photo to show you the separation of the rubber from the thin metal hinge. After a couple of uses, it was a chore for me to carefully slide the tablet in because that rubber kept getting caught. A little disappointed that just one day into this testing, I already have to resort to glue?

Like I said... uncomfortable. Brydge, please continue to focus on rigid hinge keyboards. You're on the right path. This is what we want. We want rigidness and lappability, but please design a detachable case so that the case takes the brunt of the hinge pressure, as well as protect the tablet from scratches exactly like the Yoozon design I mentioned above.

title: So much more than Harmony
review_text:
I was using the Harmony companion for the longest time, and before that, the Harmony 900. This Caavo is by far the best universal remote because it's so much more than that. Harmony is just a remote, it does not give you one unified user interface. If you've played around with a Smart TV's user interface, then you'll get the idea what this Caavo is all about. Except with Smart TV's, you still have to reach for your other devices' remotes, and if any device has voice search, it's only good for that specific device. The Caavo controls and searches all your devices! If I have a movie that's in my Tivo, that's in my plex, that is also available on Netflix.. all the choices are presented to me, so I can launch it from whichever device I choose. I have PLEX as my search priority, and it works beautifully. I was also a little nervous when hooking everything up because my TV is a Samsung from 2009, my Audio system is Sony from 2010. The Caavo has ZERO issues controlling everything.

My set-up.

Input 1: Tivo
Input 2. Fire TV
Input 3: Chromecast
Input 4: Currently Nothing
Optical OUT to my SONY AV system

My TIVO is set as the default. So when I push the power button on the remote. The Sony AV system comes on, tv comes on, and Tivo is what I'm watching! I was pleasantly surprised that it has all my Tivo controls because each button does double duty by short or long press. Let's say I want to watch a movie, I use the voice search to say BACK TO THE FUTURE, and since Plex is my priority, CAAVO gives me a list of choices with Plex highlighted. If it's in my tivo, netflix, prime, etc. it will give me all the options, but Plex will be highlighted since I set it as my priority. If I hit play, the Caavo switches input to my fire tv, launches Plex and auto-starts Back to the Future. And it happens fairly quickly. It's buttery smooth. If your preferred device to play Plex is on something else, say a Roku, you can set Roku as the default to launch Plex. If I fling something from my phone to the Chromecast, Caavo switches to my Chromecast input automatically. The voice search is perfect for youtube too because If you search something that doesn't sound like a movie, for example, How to Shop For a Miter Saw, the search results will show that there is no such movie, but included in the search results are youtube WEB searches, so you can easily play a youtube video on how to shop for a miter saw. LOL! Youtube is something I mainly do on my phone or pc because of the typing involved. But because of Caavo's voice search, we're watching it more on the big screen.

BTW, the voice recognition is terrific. It's pretty much on par with anything else out there. I've seen videos where some guy is complaining that he says Open Plex and it keeps giving him search results for DUPLEX. I don't know if Caavo has improved since his reviews, or if it just didn't like his voice, but I've never had an issue with Caavo not understanding what I said. Alexa, Google Assistant, etc. can also be integrated, but I don't see them as an efficient way to use Caavo, unless you lost the Caavo remote, then you can ask Alexa to turn on your tv I guess.

There is a slight learning curve, but it will be time well spent. And it will be easy to teach to your household members because it simply works. Lets face it, non-techies in the home will never touch your Harmony, right? I've used Harmony for 10 yrs, and nobody in my family touches it. They know how to use this Caavo!! This is a game changer!

July 17, 2019 UPDATE:
--------------------------
If you have Plex as your search default, I have a tip for you. The voice search will not understand funky spelling. For example the documentary "Comix: Beyond the Pages." The voice search will spell Comix correctly as COMICS, and so you will get zero results. But if you simply say "Beyond the Pages," the search engine will be able to find "Comix: Beyond the Pages" for you. Another quirk I ran into was "Mr. and Mrs. Smith." Even though the search engine spelled it exactly as my Plex has it, for some reason it didn't find this title. But if I just say, "Smith," it then pulls up the movie for me. So basically when you hit a snag, just use fewer words instead of saying the whole title. That's it! I really love this feature of the Caavo.

title: Big Thumbs Up!  Lots of power, itty bitty little space
review_text:
I wasn't too sure how well this speaker would work when I first requested it since every portable speaker we've ever gotten has had a sort of tingy sound to it, but this portable speaker rocks! The sound quality is even better than what we get on our home speakers and I love that you can feel the 'thumps' and hear some of the background sounds in the music that really weren't noticable before.

My husband's been wanting some way of listening to music out at the barn so we charged this little unit up and then headed out for the afternoon milking. We were easily able to hear the music over all the normal machinery racket - the whole time the hubby's giving me the thumbs up. He especially loves that once it's set up it will automatically connect to his bluetooth (though I could happily live without having to listen to his conversations!). It played the entire 4 hours we were out there and still had more battery life left!

UPDATE: This SOLEMATE finally died - and I mean it won't charge, won't pay, nothing... so we've bought another one to replace it and the new one did not come with a standard plug in charger for an outlet. It has to be charged with a computer (not real happy with that). It's still a great speaker but miss the freedom of being able to plug it into the wall and know it's charging without having to leave a computer running.

At first I couldn't figure out how to hook up the SOLEMATE to the computer, iPad or the iPod then the hubby pointed out that there's a cord underneath it that attaches to them so I'm good to go. The Bluetooth range is great as well. 33 feet I believe I read but I know my husband was able to walk the entire length of the milking parlor without having any disruption... oh and there's a convenient bag to put the SOLEMATE in so it's safe from sand and water (though I wouldn't recommend getting it wet or sandy on purpose). We had it in the bag and coveredd with paper towels.

My only complaint is that the instruction manuals really aren't very thick.. just basic information - and while I don't mind learning by doing it would be much simpler and less frustrating if there was someplace I could find answers - besides reading through other reviews.

The SOLEMATE works much better than I ever expected it to and I'm extremely impressed. Will definitely be using it instead of our home stereo system. It certainly sounds better!

title: 4.5 blue ribbon Romance Junkies review
review_text:
At the tender age of fourteen, Davie Adams's life is ripped apart. His mother's loose ways leads to a series of events that leave him homeless after his she dies in his arms. Grief-stricken, Davie makes the decision to leave Blackburn and go in search of his father.

Davie could have returned to his grandfather's house but he can't imagine remaining in Blackburn and having to endure the pitying looks and talk about his mother. After his mother's collapse, Davie runs for help and finds Tom Makepeace. They get his mother situated in the back of his wagon and are getting ready to head to the infirmary but she passes away moments later. Immediately afterward Davie jumps from the wagon and runs into the woods. Everyone assumes he'll return. Tom even yells into the woods for Davie to come to his home when he's ready that he's welcome there. Davie has other plans though.

He does go to the Makepeace's home but it's only to spend the night in their barn. He hadn't expected anyone to see him but Judy, Tom's daughter and Davie's longtime friend spots him from her window. She goes out to see him and reassures him that his mother's body is taken care of and his grandfather will be just fine. Judy realizes that Davie has to do what he feels is right for him but she also knows that her feelings for him have gone beyond friendship.

Davie leaves the following morning with nothing more than the desire to leave his memories behind him. Life on his own isn't everything he thought it would be and his search for his father proves fruitless. For years Davie travels and holds many different jobs but through it all Judy and his life in Blackburn remain firmly at the forefront of his mind.

THE LONER is sure to pull at readers' heartstring. Spanning over an eight year time period, you get a lot of insight into the characters' personalities and backgrounds. I love that Josephine Cox doesn't focus solely on Davie and Judy's story, there are many other characters who possess stories of their own which add a feeling of realism to this storyline. Davie's journey of self discovery is the main theme and it's a story you won't want to miss. Josephine Cox is a gifted storyteller who knows how to keep readers engrossed page after page so that the doldrums of winter just disappear.

Chrissy Dionne (courtesy of Romance Junkies)

title: Synch your Phone With your Car Audio System
review_text:
This is a very nice product. I spend a lot of my time listening to podcasts while I do a 1.5 hr drive to work. In the past, I used to just sit my telephone in a cradle and turn the volume up, but at freeway speeds the ambient noise was enough to make it hard to hear the sound coming from the phone's speaker.

This product charges in your cigarette lighter and allows you to connect your phone to the car radio via bluetooth. You then have to pick a radio station that is not carrying a broadcast and set the control on the bluetooth FM to the same station. All of this sounds like a lot while I'm typing it out, but it goes quickly. However, I do highly recommend that you make sure the radio is set up correctly before you start driving. There are enough accidents caused by texting, and this does represent another potential driving distraction. If you set this item up while parked, it is very useful, but if you try to do it on the roll, then it could be dangerous...fair warning.

Once you have your phone connected to your car speaker system you can listen to your own music, podcasts, etc. It is a little bit of a problem when somebody calls you, however, because the device doesn't automatically un-pair when there is a call. I found I usually had to call people back if I got a phone call. Not a huge issue really.

There is also a mini flash card slot on this device so you could play your music directly from that.

Really a good product. I received a complimentary sample in exchange for an honest review.

title: Truly impressed with this and at that price point, will be buying more!!
review_text:
I installed this over a week ago and have been using it daily... I looked up the price today so I can comment on it's "value" and I am genuinely surprised at how cheap it is! I've had cameras over $100 that didn't perform half as good as this!

To set it up, all you have to do is download their app, make a login, and have the camera scan the QR code in the app and it's setup! Super quick and painless! And putting the camera up on the porch consisted of drilling 4 screws in so that was super easy! Comes with a template to help you mount it perfectly straight or whatever but I didn't use that and it still looks good.

Functionality- this thing spins all the way left and right (wont spin in circles but it does reach all the way to each side.) Then it's range of looking up and down is really good too. I posted this on a porch post out front and I can turn the camera to the left and look down to see when Amazon delivers my packages now! Truly impressive the coverage this one camera has!

Night vision has like 3 different modes- one of them I think it keeps the spotlight on (which is BRIGHT) and I can see my car in full color/crystal clear from a few feet away! Another mode is just black and white with the IR lights on. And the other mode is black and white but it switches the spot light on and goes to full color when it sense motion.

I need to see if it has a sensitivity setting because the on bit of annoyances is that as is- it catches motion of bugs and everything under the sun so I look at my phone and have 30 alerts at any given time from the camera! Hopefully I can fix that but even if not, I am happy with the camera for the price point!

Picture- it auto starts off in standard def but you click that icon and it switches it to HD which is MUCH clearer!!

Overall I'm truly amazed by this and will be buying a few more to cover my current house and the house we're remodeling. I normally go with another company's cams but this one is far more impressive and I'm a convert for sure!

title: Great for the shower but not a great all around speaker outside the shower...
review_text:
So for the shower- this things great! But outside the shower I'm just not impressed with this. I've reviewed several $20 ish price range bluetooth speakers and each of them has a little more bass and oomph than this one. It's pretty weak for what it is, even my Echo dot puts out more sound. That being said, this does get decently loud and is just fine for the shower! I used the attached suction and put it in my shower and it was great not having to reach outside the shower and touch my phone with wet hands to skip songs or commercials on youtoube.

Some things I've noticed on youtube though- I'll click the next button when it has a ad up and I can skip it. It'll then just send me to the next song as well and I'll have to hit the back button if I want to return to my original song. The ad will still be out of the way at this point so it WORKS for this, just kinda adds one more step. Just a minor annoyance but still so much better than having youtube take advantage of me being in the shower and cramming 2 to 3 ads at me at once since I often don't wanna reach outta the shower to hit skip every couople of minutes.

Battery lifes decent. For the price, it's not bad at all. Again, I'd really just use this for the shower. Maybe outside around a pool even... But if you're not using it for the waterproof feature, I'd skip it- the sound quality isn't impressive at all.

title: Plug n play, very easy to use for a first timer!
review_text:
The price of these seems bloated and seems like these should be a bit less but other than that, I love these! If one was on a budget then I suppose VR goggles you just slide your phone into would give you the same effect as these. These don't take up much space though and would be great for something like an airplane instead of having to have a giant laptop out the whole time and your neighbor judging you for watching a horror movie on the plane. I get bored easily and even a 2 or 3 hour flight could be made so much better by watching a movie so these little glasses are my best friend! You can plug the usb c into your phone and into these and you get instant mirroring without any apps even! I went to some VR videos and you can look up and down and turn around in a room and see all around it- it's really neat!

Honestly I don't know the full potential to use these for gaming or whatever but for streaming video, they work great and have a great picture! I've even used them in bed and they light up the room a little less than my phone screen so don't disturb my boyfriend as much.

If you're worried about someone seeing what you're watching from the front (they used see thru lenses for some reason)- I suppose you could put some sort of darkening tent or something on the outside and it'd keep people from seeing what you are watching.

I was truly blown away at how quickly I got these up and going without having read any instructions or having ever had anything like this previously. I do absolutely love them but again- the price point for what they are seems a bit insane.

title: Nice system, comes with everything you need but a monitor!
review_text:
This is a decently put-together system and comes with all the cords, dvr (with hard drive), 4 cameras (you can add 4 more cameras on, can even be another brand- just has to have the same connections), and it has a mouse. All you need is a monitor and it gives you the option to connect an old school vga monitor or an hdmi one. You can often find flat panel monitors at thrift shops or the marketplace super cheap if you're trying to stick with a budget.

Setup was super easy, each camera comes with a sticker template to put onto the surface so you can line it up how you want and drill any necessary holes for the cables and such. The system is pretty plug n play, easy to setup. The cameras have like a very sturdy steel metal housing which is very nice. One complaint is that like many- they put it together on the end and the end piece (that's black) is a separate/ joined together piece. So that has the ability to open the camera up to moisture/ water leaking in. Sadly most cameras have this in some form or fashion. Ways to make your camera last longer would be to install them under a awning if you have one or if you are installing near a garage, install it in the recessed part of your garage door so it acts as a mini awning for the camera. Beware of leaky gutters outside that drip or pour a lot of water- that'll ruin about any of these cameras quick. You COULD put a small bead of silicone or even some clear outdoor rated tape along the seam on the cameras to help keep moisture out but it's something you'd have to keep up with and replace as necessary- sadly no tape or silicone will provide a permanent seal and nothing will in the elements outside. Don't be deterred by this and go with a different brand, sadly this is a flaw of all outdoor cameras I've ever tested. Just beware and plan accordingly to keep them lasting as long as possible. That being said, I love the sturdy steel housing on these cameras. The picture they provide is crisp and clear- sooo much better than any of those surveillance pictures you see that people post online asking if you've seen this person (and you can't really see them because it's terrible quality.) This system gives you a pretty clear picture and for the price point, I'm very impressed! Even it's night vision is very usable and nice. I'll be looking for some pan/tilt cameras to try and hook into this system so I can utilize all 8 slots on it. A lot of people are fine with 4 cameras of course, I just like to be extra. I also love to be able to follow someone on camera and these cameras are fixed so you can't really turn them to look at people so I'd recommend adding pan/tilt cameras to this system.

The dvr drive is very lightweight and it records your video directly to it and you can access it from the drive directly with a monitor or you can use their app and access it thru your phone from anywhere. You can also view live streams from anywhere to check on your house, pets, kids, etc. The one thing I've got to say is just like with any system- if you're a cheapskate and don't pay for the subscription service, just beware that you really need to hide your dvr somewhere and at the same time allow for ventilation so it won't overheat. (don't stuff it in a small enclosed space) You could put it in a sturdy safe and mount that to a wall or floor but heat is still an issue, you'd need to drill or cut out some ventilation holes in the top (since heat rises) and that will allow heat to escape from the safe so it doesn't overheat your dvr.

Overall for less than a $200 price point, I am very happy and impressed with what you get and the quality of the picture it provides. Highly recommend this system.

Then just be careful that no one trips over the cord. (use brightly colored rope/ cord)

This is the best projector screen I've come across! For the price, it's completely worth it! I think because of the tripod legs that a lot of people wouldn't wanna keep this up full time in their house, for that you could just attach one to the wall possibly. That being said- the tripod legs don't actually stick out too far so they don't pose a huge tripping hazard.

title: Nearly flawless! Types very well! Holds a flawless connection to the computer, no cutting out!
review_text:
I'm a very fast typist so get angry when a keyboard can't keep up and quite often- a cordless keyboard can't keep up with fast-paced typing! This one can! I was very impressed by that and the fact that typing on it feels pretty natural!

The bad is that everything on the right is kind of jumbled together and there's no space around the arrows or enter key. Those keys also double as the page up and page down keys and they do work but the page scrolling that it gives is kind of jerky if you will. It jerks as it scrolls and it scrolls SLOWLY. I work from my pc and often I need to search thru hundreds of pages in a short amount of time. The included mouse works well but it's not great to scroll thru a lot of documents and my hand gets tired having to drag and drop the bar on the right... SO because of this sadly, I've gone back to my old keyboard which has the typical page up and down and it flawlessly scrolls up and down on a page VERY fast and without it jerking around while doing it. To some this might not matter and in that case- if you don't use the page up and down key then this keyboard is PERFECT. As I said the typing is natural. Very silent typing too which I LOVE.

The mouse works fairly well. I do a lot of work in bed so I use my sheet as a mousepad, the mouse has an issue with that sometimes and it's hard to get it to do what I want. I have noticed if I grab literally anything from a magazine to a pillow- it'll work as a mousepad though. Aside from that the mouse is great and works as it should!

Battery life- I've had the same set of cheap batteries in the keyboard and mouse for a week, they automatically shut off when not in use- no need to flip a switch! They seem very easy going on batteries because I use my computer for hours each day and after a month on some cheap batteries- that's impressive!

Wireless connectivity: I'm actually IMPRESSED. I have a pile of terrible wireless keyboards and as far as name brands go- Logitech has cornered the market on budget wireless keyboards it seems. That being said- I've yet to find a logitech keyboard that will keep a connection! They cut out non stop and miss key presses, it just makes the keyboards unusable! So I have a pile of their junk I need to donate... I've tried many other off brands and such and they all have the same issue, they cut out on and off and irritate me. This one triumphs over the others because the keyboard doesn't mess key presses even at a fast speed and that's certainly something!

At this price point, this set is 100% worth it! I think you'll be very impressed unless you need to use the page up and down buttons a lot!

title: Beautiful tv at a good price!
review_text:
I love this tv, it is definitely a masterpiece! Very well made and fantastic quality. Deep blacks, vivid colors, natural skin tones...

Not the thinnest tv on the market but a great tv still! Easy to set up and get going. Slim feet that slide into place with no tools- only have ONE configuration. 2 USBs, 4 HDMIs, Ethernet, optical & headphone outputs, & a mini a/v input. Operating system is Google Tv which works smoothly and has lots of apps built in. Works with Google Home and Alexa.

Has some intrusive ads on the homepage. You can go into the settings/privacy/ ads to opt out of personalized ads though. You can use your remote microphone to do voice commands on the tv. It also has the nice shortcut buttons for Youtube, Netflix, Disney+, and Prime Video.

Sound has tweeters on the side. It upscales the audio to give you a surround sound effect. Acoustic auto calibration which when you go to your sitting area with the remote and start this- it sends these crazy alien laser blaster sounds out of the speakers for a couple seconds and your remote reads them so the tv can process the information and adjust your speakers accordingly. It will then adjust the speakers so it sends sound to where you're sitting to give you the best experience possible!

The cognitive processor in this puts more emphasis into the areas of the picture that you'll be focused on- definitely makes a noticeable difference!

XR TRILUMINOS PRO technology gives you better color accuracy and depth.

XR Contrast booster gives you better contrast.

Very deep blacks with very little light blooming (meaning it has very even brightness across the screen.) The screen has PLENTY of brightness, that is definitely not an issue with this tv!

Ambient optimization option which changes your screen based on the ambient lighting in the room. Controls brightness and color tones. There are settings to optimize the screen for Netflix, Imax, Cinema, Etc that are amazing!

Motion is great, it has 120 hertz which keeps up with the action very well! You can adjust the Motionflow settings to your custom settings or just set it to auto and let it do it's thing.

Comparing it to the other top Sony models:
If you're on a budget and this is on the higher end of that, you might look into the Sony X80J- it's also a 2021 model and is 4k Ultra HD. It's not quite as nice of a picture as this Full Array but it's still a great tv! Otherwise if you can swing it- this X90J Full Array is definitely a fantastic choice! If your budget can STILL swing more though, you might even look into the X90J OLED tv, it's picture pops even more than this Full Array. Whatever your choice, you'll love any of them! I have all 3 models and we absolutely love each and every one of them- the X80 and X90 line are just fantastic tvs at a really fair price point.

title: Definitely the biggest bang for your buck if you're looking for an OLED tv!
review_text:
Beautiful true blacks and insanely lifelike vivid colors make the picture pop almost like it's 3D/ real life! Very impressive features jam packed into this! Sound is amazing- you won't need a soundbar at all. Super thin screen, the thickness of a folder. Screen has a nice metal edge which helps protect it. Setup was quick and easy. Very slim lightweight remote with nice shortcut buttons to all of your favorite streaming services. Apps load quickly and run smoothly in this tv.

Feet are easy to install, no tools or screws which is amazing. They can be attached to make your tv flat on the surface or raised so you can put a soundbar down. You can also put the feet closer together and further apart. Lots of options which is nice!

Some of the features I love on this are:
*The auto light sensor- it adjusts the screen brightness based on the lighting of the room. (this feature can be turned off of course)
*Acoustic auto calibration- you sit wherever (like on your couch) and it sends these loud sound blasts that sound like alien gun blasters. The blasts reach the mic in your remote where you are sitting and then the tv records the information and auto calibrates the sound so it reaches you better based on your room and where you're sitting.
*The speakers use vibration to turn the whole display into a loudspeaker- sending sound everywhere. Small subwoofers in the back to give it an extra bump of bass. You absolutely notice this technology working- the sound is amazing and PLENTY loud. You can always add surround sound if you have to have a deep boom of bass like in the movie theater though.
*XR Motion processing- means blur-free scenes. You can really notice this on things like watching sports from football to surfing.
*Upscaling is great. HDR is fantastic too- I really notice the differences in skin tones, they look a lot more natural on this tv. The XR processor really puts noticeable light into the highlights of the picture which really helps the image pop.

The bravia core seems more like a advertising gimmick, wasn't impressed with that at all.
That aside- this tv does definitely tout a lot of tech packed into one nice looking slim package! It has a TON of settings and customizations you can play with and set it up exactly like you want it! I've never seen so many different settings in a tv! No worries, if you don't want to customize, you certainly can just choose one of the standard programmed modes and the tv still produces a gorgeous picture!

CONS:
*The only ones I have noticed that might be a deal breaker are there is no functioning VRR and it only has two hdmi 2.1 ports which might mean that you won't want this if you're a gamer.
*Has a matte anti reflective coating which really doesn't do an amazing job at keeping reflections out of the tv like the coating they put on the 90J- that one does a better job. It doesn't make it unwatchable, it's just that sometimes you might notice a reflection in the tv in settings with windows nearby or a light fixture that shines near it.

Comparing this to the 90J I notice some other things:
The 80J doesn't have the heatsink in the back that the 90J does. This might become noticeable for gamers and is a letdown. The speakers are a little less powerful in this tv than the 90J, they sound good but don't have as much power. The 80J doesn't have the backlit Sony remote that the 80J has which is crazy and a replacement remote in case you're wondering costs a whopping $80!!

At $1300 less than the 90J, the decision for me is clear! I definitely say go with this 80J because the small improvements aren't worth paying the $1300 more. BUT if price isn't an issue- go for the 90J. I can tell you for sure, you'll be happy with either that you choose, they're both fantastic devices that are well built and jam packed with the latest tech and features.

title: Well made workstation, top of it's class! Thinnest smallest workstation on the market.
review_text:
Very sleek looking amazing machine! Powers on very quickly and runs flawlessly smooth no matter what demanding tasks I'm doing.

Looking at the outer case you'll see a metal shell on the top and bottom with a diamond cut polished edge that results in a stunning sturdy feeling shell! On the inside you see a very classy looking carbon fiber palm rest. You'll also notice they took out the 10 key pad to make room for big speaker panels on each side of the keyboard. The panel is so large because it has a speaker on top and a subwoofer on the bottom which makes for very impressive sound! You definitely won't need to tote around external speakers with this! You can however get a 10 key pad that hooks into one of the 4 usb- c ports. Those ports are all thunderbolt 3 ports which support full native 8k resolution (this is the smallest workstation on the market that has this feature.)

The screen is a gorgeous 17" touch screen UHD+ display that has hardware enabled blue light filtering that doesn't cause that ugly dimming or yellowing that others do. This keeps your graphics looking good while reducing the strain on your eyes and you will absolutely notice the difference! It drastically helps your eyes when you have to work many hours at a time without a break.

Supports Windows Hello so you can use a pin number, fingerprint, or your face to login. The power button in the upper right is unmarked due to it doubling as the fingerprint reader. The facial recognition works thru the IR camera and it can be set to lock your computer the second you walk away from it and unlock it when you come back. Amazing for shared work spaces where you're constantly having to get up and leave your computer- never have to worry about whether you locked it or not! The camera and microphone built in are impressive- I've done Skype video calls and Zoom meetings and gotten flawless results without even needing an external microphone! The camera produces a very smooth video feed that isn't ever choppy as long as you have a good reliable internet that's high speed.

If you're wondering about the price tag, it's because this isn't a laptop- it's workstation. This is more made for things like high end video work, medical imaging, architectural work, 3D CAD, graphic design, animation, AI, and VR (this is also the smallest workstation on the market that is VR capable.) As for video editing- I'm VERY impressed. You get very smooth playback while editing 4k videos and can do it in much less time than other workstations- extremely impressive!

If you're worried about it overheating while you're running more demanding tasks and multitasking- it has metal and copper channels inside of it that help the dual output fans cool it and push hot air thru the system and out the back which keeps this thing running cool! I've yet to see mine begin to overheat while I'm running demanding programs and really pushing it.

Working from home and on the go- this is absolutely your perfect solution and the best workstation on the market in my opinion! I'm just blown away by this impressive powerhouse of a workstation! Dell really took my breath away with how well built this is and how jam packed with tech it is. I could tell you about the tech in it all day long but I'll leave the rest for you to research on your own. It suffices to say- this is a workstation that can handle quite the work load and not begin to get weighed down in the process, total game changer!! This is definitely the one you've been looking for!

Picture is very clear, color is decent. Overall I say yes this is a great starter projector! If you're just getting it for kids, there are ones in the $70 range that might also work for your needs but if you want to use it for movie night or whatever, this works great too! Just don't get it expecting the same results of a more expensive projector. If you need high definition in video, you always have to pay the price!

title: Good Overall
review_text:
I use these for work, 8 hours a day in a work from home call center. I have a large head and am a big guy. The sound is fantastic for voice communication, I would never use these for gaming, music or multimedia. The audio range is not good enough for those applications, it is great for voice. The microphone works beautifully and others can hear me clearly and crisply.

To say that these are "passive" noise cancelling is laughable. There is really no such thing as passive noise cancelling, it's just how much noise is blocked out by wearing the headphone. Do not take that into consideration when buying headphones, unless they totally cover the ear. You can hear everything going on around you.

The ear pads are pretty comfortable, much more than a foam ear pad on standard headphones. I do need to pull these away from my ears every now and then to restore circulation and reduce soreness. Durability of the pad itself is in question, but I have not had these long enough to figure that out. First impression is the pad might last 6-12 months using 5 days a week for work. To me the pads seem to be a weak spot durability speaking.

Overall a great headphone for work. If these had active noise cancelling and a more comfortable/durable ear pad, they would be perfect. I have no experience with microphone filtering yet.

title: Fantastic Radio
review_text:
To mention right off the bat, I am not even an amateur radio operator, just someone who enjoys radio. I find radio to be far more romantic and compelling than modern methods of broadcasting. Staying up late in the night and turning the dial with the soft glow of the tuner, the sound of static and mystery that can sometimes accompany radio broadcasts offers something truly genuine that you can't get anywhere else today. That feeling is priceless and not duplicable (If that was even a word).

Anyway, this radio is good quality and contains the capability needed to reach further than most others. If you enjoy radio as I do, a clock radio, ghetto blaster or home stereo won't cut it. If you know what I am talking about, then this radio is for you. I've stayed up many nights listening to Coast to Coast AM on the internet, but it lacked the feeling something like this radio will bring you. I was unable to pick up a station on my home stereo to listen to CTC and was forced to use the internet. The internet provided a clear, stereo sounding broadcast and was very clear.

The CC Radio has been spoken about on the program for many years. I finally picked one up and am very pleased with it's performance. I can now pick up the radio broadcast of Coast to Coast AM and with all the nuances I expect of a a late night radio broadcast. When interesting speakers talk about compelling topics, a crystal clear internet broadcast does not move you inside. However, using the CC Radio, the slight static, the slight fading in and out and all other fantastic experiences you can only receive using a real radio, it has the ability to make you feel and even send chills up your spine. There is just something a good solid radio can do for you that nothing else can and the CC Radio delivers on that 100%.

You will not be disappointed and I really need to get my license.

title: Fantastic deal for the price
review_text:
I have some very good cameras that take video, but they are large and heavy and getting them to do time-lapse is tricky. I wanted something to film the development paintings in my studio, and later in the season, in the field. So far, I am impressed. This kit comes with an external microphone, a remote control (uses aaa batteries--not included), two rechargable batteries, a charger and cable, a bracket, and a compact case with a belt loop. It does not include a memory card, so you will need to order one if you don't have one on hand. It accepts a variety of sizes (larger is better.) It will prompt you to format the card the first time you use it.

The camera is so small and light it fits in the pocket of my winter jacket. Its shape snuggles into the palm of my hand. It has a lot of features that take a while to explore. You can adjust the resolution and the asa, which is amazing for a camera at this price point. It also has a hot shoe, but you probably won't need a video light in most situations because there is one built in.

The viewing screen is bright enough to view in full sun and tilts for convenience. It shows you how much battery life you have and whether or not it is recording. So far, I haven't been able to tell what mode I am using by looking at the screen. I also need to figure out how to keep the date and time from recording, but that's on me. I'm sure there's an easy setting. I just need to find it.

If you want to film things closer than 2 meters, this isn't the camera for you. There's no automatic focusing. It's set at infinity. You can zoom a little. Of course, the wide angle setting has the greatest depth of field. I think the video quality is just fine for the Internet, which is why I ordered it and the built-in mic worked fine in my test videos.

The only thing I had trouble with was the single photo feature. It worked once, but when I tried it again, the camera locked up. I don't really need that anyway. I look forward to making time-lapse artist-at-work videos for my site with this nice little camera! For the price, it's amazing, and it's lots of fun.

review_text: I am torn when it comes to this smartwatch. First, you track everything through an app on your phone, which I like a lot better than just the watch itself. You are supposed to be able to swipe through the different things on the watch but you literally can't most of the time. You have to press down so hard and hope that it swipes but usually, it doesn't and you have to keep trying and trying. It's so freaking annoying and complete trash. It's just a high tech watch that you can't use for anything else that it says you can use it for. Such as taking pictures, using it as a remote, and even control your music from the watch. I have managed to get to the program on the watch but unable to use it because of not being able to swipe or use the watch at all. Oh, and there is only one button on the watch itself, which controls the power and turning the light on and off. That's it, doesn't control anything else. title: Really Great Photography Kit!
review_text:
I am very, very happy with my order of the GLOSHOOTING Photography Lighting Kit. This kit arrived in great condition and was very well packaged. Each piece had it's own box, so this was great protection for the shipping process. This includes everything I need to use with my own camera to make my own quality portraits. I work nights and often struggled with lighting to take photos at home. I really like to pose dolls from my collection to make photo stories to share with other hobbyists. This can sometimes be a long process that takes several sessions to complete. This kit does not take up too much room for me to use it over the course of several days to complete a project. It does not take much time to setup after the initial opening. Between uses, it is easy to store in it's own nylon case underneath my bed. I especially appreciate the thoughtfulness of all the inclusions of this set. The backdrops are light-weight and easy to store. When I set up a backdrop after storage, I find that a little bit of wrinkle spray works right away! I do use the green screen often too, and that is included as well as 2 others. This is a great set for me and my uses.

This is an ideal set for anyone that wishes to shoot photos as a hobby. It is sturdy enough to stay setup for days on end, but not so sturdy that it could take much abuse. I would not recommend this for professional portraits of children that may be prone to knocking over equipment, as the components of this set is not designed for abuse. I find that for all of the inclusions, and the ease of storage, this set makes a really great value. I would happily recommend this to anyone that wishes to have a good lighting and backdrop set for hobby use. I hope that my experience is helpful as you kindly click the button below.

title: Versatile Use, Easy to Store
review_text:
I ordered the 43 Inch/110 Centimeter Light Reflector. It comes in it's own little zippered bag. The fabric appears to mostly be nylon, so it should wash easily with a damp cloth. The stitching is solid. I didn't know what to expect, but the Light Reflectors are exactly as pictured. My only little gripe is I had to refer to the listing to remember how to fold it to fit back into the pouch. Once you remove it, you have a large disk, silver on one side, black on the other. This has another zipper on the side. Inside the reflector's zipper is a diffuser which you will need to remove from the larger pouch to use. This is where the mounting tab is located. You will need the mounted clip that is available as part of the kit, or you may purchase it separately. That's not all. The large, outer pouch is reversible, so you then reverse the large pouch and you have a gold reflector one one side or a solid white on the opposite side. This is how you have black, white, gold, silver and a diffuser all in one. The diffuser has it's own tap to clip on your tripod, which pokes through from a button hole to mount the entire piece. You will need to make sure it's pulled through if you remove the outer layer of the reflector.

This is a good purchase for the value. I'm a hobbyist, and sometimes take photos of my projects. My problem comes from being a night-shift worker. I live and work at night. I must make my own lighting setup if I want to photograph anything at night, even in my home. It's light weight, and folds to a small circle, so this is also portable. It weighs less than a pair of jeans.

Here's a free tip: Only use the gold if your subject is brown. I don't find the gold reflector so useful. I'm glad it's available, but I doubt it will get much use for me. Also, place the reflector in a way that would mimic the sun's light, and your subject will look more natural. This is where the clips and extension arms from your tripod can come in handy if you are working solo. Of course, you can always enlist the assistance of another for outdoor shoots. Sometimes this is a best option if it's available. In the movies, they tend to show someone holding a reflector with it facing up towards the subject, but that's only because it does look silly holding a big disc over your head. If you hold it, you will need to hold it up over your head, and it will look silly but your photos will not.

It's a good tool to have on hand for any level of photography. I mostly photograph my doll collection. Once or twice a year, our doll collectors group will gather outdoors for shoots. We've not had a reflector available to us before, so this will help us immensely finding good spots to make photographs, even if the clouds are moving or we want to setup under trees.

I also ordered the 2-pack clips. These are nice because they come with an adapter on them. If you remove the threaded black female cylinder and threaded ring, you are left with a standard sized male mount that will fit a tripod base. You do not need to make a separate purchase for an adapter, it's already there. The ball joint swivels all the way around and there is a groove in the base to tilt the clip in towards the base, so you can use these clips for holding the reflectors, diffuser or even a backdrop on a side or top mount adapter of your backdrop frame.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.

title: Great Microphone for Hobbyists, Gamers and Bloggers
review_text:
A warning to first time users, you may experience the microphone picking up background noise. It's very sensitive. Be prepared to set-up an area for recording if you are wanting to get clean audio. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came in a fairly plain box with a large hard foam protective insert. This microphone seems to be a great starting point for anyone interested in a higher quality microphone. I can whole heartedly recommend it.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone is a USB interface microphone that is a large step-up in quality to those used to the basic microphones that come with many web cameras. It provides a higher sensitivity to sounds; enabling both a greater ability to pick up lower volume noises and the ability to comprehend higher volume ones.

The lower volumes it was able to obtain included whispering, including the mouth noises associated with ASMR videos, and keystrokes from a non-mechanical keyboard roughly 6 feet away [With it's recording volume turned down to 50%]. On the higher end of volume it is able to accommodate singing, yelling, and screaming; by not topping out what it able to accommodate this allowed for wide arrays of vocals and would assist with those wanting to record instruments. I did many different experiments to test the range at home on different days.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came with a short stand and pop filter that is attached to the stand by goose neck. The stand and metallic goose neck are both adjustable to assist with angling, but it is not vertically adjustable. The microphone, when pointing directly up, is about 26 cm / 10 in in height to the top of the microphone. It has a rubber ball footed desktop tripod for stability. The microphone can also detach from the included stand and be mounted to a standard size tripod or any other compatible stand, making the pop filter necessary depending on setup.

I had a great experience using VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone to audition for a voice acting role organized by fellow fans of an animated series. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone certainly made me sound much better than my webcam microphone is able to do. I have been using this for cooperative game-play online as well. This is a great value, especially at the price point.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you have found it informative and helpful.

title: I Wish I Had These Sooner!
review_text:
For my uses, these are great. They were very well packaged and secure for shipping. The box is very nice and sturdy, lined with foam. I need to hear the environment around me. This has been an issue with previous earbuds. Commercials between videos or songs can get so loud! That is the deal-breaker for me, as it's a safety issue. These do not get too loud, even on the loudest setting, so I am able to remain safe. I don't have an issue hearing the sounds coming from the buds, but I'm not in high-traffic outdoor areas regularly either. My ear canals are unusually small for an adult. I was afraid these may be too-big, but they are snug. Any bigger and it may have been an issue. I used the smaller of the plastic tips. Over the ear designs are the only ones that have ever worked for me. I did look at some other models in the past, but I found them a bit more expensive than I felt justified to spend unknowing how well they may work for me. However, knowing how well these work, I find them to be a really great value and would have purchased them before if I had known how well they worked. It was only by chance they were up for review and I had been seeking a replacement on my old pair that I've been using for the past few years.

The Bluetooth is nice. I have a simple cell phone. It only took asking my phone to connect to work. It was the easiest that I have ever had with connecting anything Bluetooth to my phone. I liked this as I'm not the most savvy at using Bluetooth electronics. If I can do it, anyone can.

I'm not great at using the buttons as they are really sensors on the flat-side of the body on the earbuds. I'm getting used to it but they are touch sensitive and there is a correct spot and amount of pressure that works best. I'm still getting a feel for it and there is a slight delay, so it's very easy to double-tap. The included booklet has been helpful to learn to use these straight out of the package.

Sometimes I get down on the floor at the gym to use the foam rollers and stretches, other times I'm using them in the car to take calls. I've tried them at work as well. Every scenario has worked well for me. I really do wish I've had these before. Sometimes while getting my breaks at work, I would want to listen to things from my phone, but didn't want to risk disturbing my co-workers with some of the news and hobby related videos I enjoy. I asked a few co-workers if they could hear my earbud noise, they could not.

The case is very easy to use as well and fits easily into my pockets. I'm a lady, so my pockets are not always very generously sized. It charges very quickly, and I've not found myself running out of charge. I cannot speak on the long-term durability for this as they are new. If/when I experience any issues with the charge, I will be sure to post an update.

In summary, these would be better for users that need to hear their surroundings for safety. For those that want extreme high volume, they may not be as happy. They stay on my ears securely and the case works very well. I'm pleasantly surprised how well I like these and hope that they are durable since they are working so well for me.

Thanks for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.

title: Takes great pictures!
review_text:
This is a great little camera. It takes surprisingly good pictures. I guess I wasn't expecting much for a kids camera. It is pretty easy to operate. All the pictures in my review were taken on my recent visit to Colorado. As you can see, it handled a variety of shots with aplomb. The wildflowers was a closeup, the two landscapes were long shots with varying light conditions. The stained glass shot is the ceiling on the Broadmore Hotel in Colorado Springs. Everything came out clear and beautiful. I am not very steady when I hold a camera, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that most of my shots aren't fuzzy or blurred from my wobbly camera holding.

The only reason I didn't give this camera a top rating is because of the viewfinder. There isn't one, and the view screen is stationary. There is no way to rotate it or adjust it so that you can see what you are trying to shoot from any angle that you might hold it at. That made getting a good shot very challenging. The wildflower shot, for instance, was taken completely blind. I could not see the view screen at all. That would have meant crawling on the ground to see the screen. I can't get on the ground (mobility issues). I had to just gold the camera in front of the flowers and snap the picture, hoping for the best. The other issue is that, because you can't adjust the view screen, lighting conditions often make the screen unseeable, even if you are looking straight at it. The second landscape photo (the one on the right) was impossible to see what I was shooting at, even though I was looking directly at the screen. The lighting prevented me from being able to see the screen. Luckily, I got a good shot anyway, but I really don't like shooting blind.

So, overall, I recommend this camera. It is a good beginning camera. Very basic, takes good photos. It's just hard to use in some circumstances.

title: Nice little notebook
review_text:
I admit, I haven't been a fan of Chromebooks in the past, but I decided to give this one a try. I have been pleasantly surprised. I like this little notebook/pixelbook is really nice. I like how light it is. It is very portable and will fit in a backpack, large purse or tote.

One of the reasons I didn't like these before, was simply because I didn't like Chrome as a browser. Now though, you can load a different browser on it, so I put Firefox...my preferred browser. It doesn't work 100% the way I'm used to, but it is close enough, and I have all my bookmarks from my other devices that use Firefox.

Another thing that has been improved is the size. The last one I had was really small. The keyboard felt cramped and I couldn't type on it properly. I kept hitting the wrong keys, because the spacial arrangement of the keys was too small. This one is great...very functional. My hands rest comfortably on the keyboard, everything is spaced logically for maximum ease of use. My only issue is a small one. I am a touch typist and don't like to look at the keyboard, even when first placing my hands on the keyboard. Most keyboards have a tiny dot, or something on the letters "f" and "j" so that you can find your "home row" without looking. There is a tiny raised bar at the leading edge of those letters, but they are almost imperceptible. I keep having to look down to make sure my hands are placed correctly. It annoys me to no end. I think I will find a way to modify those keys just for my own sanity's sake.

This Chromebook comes with no instructions...at all. Granted, it is easy to set up, you just open it and go, but then you have to figure things out by asking Google play (oh yeah, you need to have a Google account to use this) or Googling it. An example is, how the screen is displayed when browsing. Every website I went to was reading my device as if it was a cell phone. I was getting a slender column of content that was too tiny to read and only filled one third of the page, down the middle. I couldn't enlarge it, and couldn't read it. I had to Google the solution. It was a setting that I had to change to "view as desktop". Now, everything is oriented correctly...except for Facebook. It is still showing up weird and I don't know how to change it. All that is to say that you may encounter issues, and if you do, you will have to know how to do Google searches to find the answers.

At any rate, I like this Chromebook and will continue to use it. I recommend it for people needing access to the internet in a portable manner, but who want a larger screen to view than a cell phone. It is very portable, the battery seems to last a long time, and it is easy to use.

title: A Great Linux Laptop
review_text:
So my only complaint about Microsoft devices as a whole is their lack of compatibility with Linux. This one is better than the other 4 I have owned. It still isn't working well with CentOS, but Kubuntu works awesomely, and I also have Kali running. I've got a tripple boot (with Windows as well) set up, and the whole thing took about 5 hours to set up. If you're looking for a laptop to run Linux on, that is light and has a great battery, the choice is this one or the XPS. The XPS (my friend has one) doesn't run touchscreen, but it is lighter than this one and gets even better battery...

Overall, this laptop has a great battery, a great screen, and runs Linux with very little effort. The only downsides are the requirement to have power connected in order to detach the screen (yes, the button does work in Linux), the fact that all ports (USB, SD and charging included) are on the base (so in tablet mode it can't charge, can't read an SD card, and can't use a USB device), and the fact that it is so sealed that you can't upgrade or repair it yourself. Those are the reasons I dropped one star (personally, I'd drop 4 stars for all that, but I know most people wouldn't).

Although the risk of SIDS is small, it is still a risk, and this device can help prevent it by alerting you before it is too late.  I felt like I could sleep at night knowing that something was checking to see on it.  Yes, we've had false alarms and that will happen with any, but it is so worthwhile to know.  This one is particularly great because it is portable, so you can take it when you are out somewhere or if your baby sleeps somewhere else and not just in the crib.  Of course it's not a substitute for proper supervision but I would never not have a motion alarm on a newborn.  I have heard many cases where babies' lives were literally saved.

title: Could Be Better And Breaks Easily
review_text:

I'm going to strip it for parts and feel that Dell cheated me. This will be the last Dell product I ever buy!

title: What Happens When Things Go Wrong...
review_text:
When I first purchased my 3 TB MBL some time ago I was quite pleased. Network access, remote access, even an android app. In short, everything my DLink had plus the app and a nicer look on the shelf. I used it extensively for pulling up photos on my cell phone when I was bored as well as to store my most important files. I didn't back them up, a back-up drive is something I kept saying I would add later...

14 months later (note the 12 month warranty had just expired) the drive stopped being accessible over the network. I spent a week and at least 40 hours of my time going back and forth with tech support by e-mail and trying every option they could offer, and the result was that they deemed the unit broken. They said that the unit can not be opened because that would break the drive inside, and they said that they can't fix it. They "kindly" offered me a referral to one of several companies that give them a kick back for data recovery services. Incidentally, I asked two for pricing by e-mail and they didn't respond.

So I took the unit apart and bought a new unit and took that one apart and swapped the drives. Neither one worked. After talking to support again it turns out that WD didn't want these to be upgradable because if they were upgradable you could buy a cheap drive instead of a new unit so they code each board to the drive that will be in it. TO make matters worse, they encoded the drive in a Linux format that no known version of Linux can translate. Attaching it to my Linux system I couldn't mount it using any utility. Several Linux recovery programs couldn't do anything either.

Okay, having told you why I will never buy a WD NAS again, I should now tell you how to fix this if you have the same problem that I do: DiskInternals makes a program called Linux Reader. That's right, Linux can't read the drive but a program designed to read Linux drives from within Windows can! Recovering the data to a drive is time consuming though. I tried it all at once but that froze after a few days. Then I tried one major directory at a time and that worked better. But recovering nearly 3 TB of data has taken a very long time! I'm about 3 MONTHS into the recovery effort and I have about 400 GB remaining. After starting on my wife's computer because mine is a laptop and causing a few crashes and a lot of delays I finally had to pull out an older computer and set it up just to run this program.

If anyone has the same problem and can't get this solution to work, I'll do my best to help if you simply reply to this review and give me all the details. If anyone is considering buying a WD NAS, I want to encourage you to buy a DLink model 323 (I think the 325 is the current version but it is missing some features so I'd get an older one) instead. I've had that thing running for 5 years without a glitch!

title: Not A Stellar Case
review_text:
Okay, before I mention what is wrong with this case, I will mention two things that are right:

1. The leather feels so soft. For a mass produced case, they did a good job at this aspect.

2. The strap, which I am going to call a negative down below, does look cool if you are thinking of your KFHD as an ebook reader because it resembles the straps that are sometimes found in books.

Okay, done with the good. Now for the critique:

1. The spine likes to stay open. By that I mean when you open the device and then close it you have to use the strap to hold it shut because it will not do so naturally. Since the device turns on and off when you open and close it, this means that the device will waste power staying on because it thinks that the case is open. There are many ways to avoid this, but they manufacturer did not try to.

2. There are no pockets to put note cards or business cards.

3. There is no loop to hold a stylus or pen.

4. The case is open around all sides. This isn't a design flaw, but if I were the company I would offer a zippered version to protect the device from rain.

5. The strap SUCKS!!! I mean really, it takes effort to properly close this case! Why not design it not to need one like my Toshiba Thrive case, or design it with a magnetic clasp like my Kindle Touch case?

6. The rotating mechanism is pretty cool, I have seen similar for other devices, but it is pretty tight. Perhaps this will loosen up, but after 3 days I still report this to be difficult to turn.

7. The hand strap is useless. If you hold it open like that, the device is secured only to one side and can flap about. If you are going to put in a hand strap, this should provide secure and stable device placement.

8. And now for the most annoying factor: they get a point for designing a case that can sit at several angles, but then loose several million for designing it so that NONE of those angles are comfortable. They range from pointing slightly down to pointing slightly up, and all of them are best if the device is at or within 6" below eye level. If you sit it on your desk and not a long way off, it is not angled enough for a good view! Seriously? Didn't they test this before going into production?

My advice to the user is to find another case.

My advice to the manufacturer is to redesign. And while you're at it, please send me a free one of the new cases after the redesign so that I don't have to buy a new case!

One more word about the price. I know that this is a high end case with the rotating feature and all, but anything over $30 is just ridiculous! I got mine free in exchange for this review (sorry about that, but I am always fair and I have never been bribed in my reviews), but I wouldn't have paid for it if I had to do so!
