title: Two Low Priced ANC Earbuds Compared
review_text:
This is a combined review of two of the lowest cost “Active Noise Cancelling” earbuds on Amazon:
[[ASIN:B004K09H32 Audio-Technica ATH-ANC23 QuietPoint Active Noise-Cancelling In-Ear Headphones]]
[[ASIN:B00SA5JCWO Egghead 1010 - Active Noise Cancelling Earbuds with Travel Pouch]]

PRICE
The price difference as of May, 2015 was $14 with Audio-Technica being the more expensive unit.

IN THE BOX
Both products contain:
--Earbuds
--Multiple silicone earbud cups
--Airline headset adapter
--Carrying Pouch

Audio-Technica contains in addition:
--Battery
--Pair of foam earbud cups. Not memory foam, just normal foam. I have not tried these.

Egghead:
--Mute button: In addition to the ANC on/off switch, Egghead has a nice mute button that turns off Noise Cancellation while it is pressed down.

SOUND QUALITY
I am not an audiophile so the sound from both headsets were good to me but the difference comes when you factor in the fit of the earbuds.

FIT
Both sets sit deeply in your ear and from pictures of both products, you will see that beyond the earbud, they have a circular piece before the actual connection to the wires.
--Egghead: The earbuds are attached straight to the circular piece so the fit is actually straight out away from your ears.
--Audio-Technica: The earbuds are angled forward so the circular piece actually serves as an anchor that sits nicely in your ear lobe and further cuts out outside noise. The additional foam earbud cup may make the difference for some people when it comes to a comfortable fit.
--Kids: I purchased these for a trip that the family will take. The kids usually have a hard time with normal earbuds not fitting in very well but they were able to keep the Audio-Technica earbuds in using the smallest earbud cups. The kids are 6 and 9.

NOISE REDUCTION
Here is the main event. I want to make a few points about Active Noise Cancelling: --Noise cancellation filters are designed to cancel out lower pitched, repeating noises like airplane engine rotors and car tires on a road, but it will not cancel out high or mid-range sounds like human voice. The same engine rotor and road noise also contain components of higher pitched sounds so NC filters will not cut out the noise completely.
--Using Noise Cancellation often feels like being underwater with your ears popping. It is a discomfort that you would have to get used to. The greater the cancellation effect, the greater the discomfort. Be prepared for this if you haven’t used NC before.
--ANC only works IF the inverted noise wave can overpower the noise coming in. If you are using a lawn mower and the noise it makes overpowers the “anti noise” because you’re standing right in back of the motor, you will not hear a big difference in the Noise Reduction effects.

Ok, so on with it. The Audio-Technica claims to reduce 90% of noise. I don’t have anything to confirm the claim but if we assume the Audio-Technica(AT) to be at 90%, my own assessment of the Egghead’s (Egg) noise reduction effects would be around 50-60%.

--Computer Fan Noise: Egg reduces the noise to slightly audible but you’d need to use toggle the mute button on it to really tell. AT completely removes the noise.
--Clothes Dryer: Egg takes the “edge” off the noise produced. You can still hear most of the noise standing about 3 feet away from the dryer. AT takes the bass tones completely out of the noise while leaving the higher pitched metal friction and buttons hitting the tumbler noise. In effect, with the AT, standing only 3 feet away, it sounds like you are actually 20 feet away.

So in conclusion, you have probably guessed that I think the additional cost of the Audio-Technicas are worth it. In addition to the benefits mentioned above, I have recently been able to get a great deal on a pair of [[ASIN:B00UETOW4C Harmon/Kardon SOHO II NC]] on ebay. The noise reduction effects of the Audio-Technicas equal or maybe even exceeds those of the Harmon/Kardons.

title: Love this enclosure
review_text:
I love how compact this case is. The rounded edges make the case seem even smaller.
I'm not going to section off the Good, Bad, Ugly features because I really haven't found any real problems with this enclosure.

Features I like:
- Fits 2.5" notebook HDD at the standard height (not necessary to buy a low profile SSD)
- Plug and Play. Some enclosures take almost a minute for the PC to recognize. The drive shows up instantly in My Computer once plugged in.
- Fast USB 3.0. I'll go into this in more detail.
- Aluminum case. Good for keeping the drive cool.
- Opens without a tool. A button (a little hard to press) releases the top and bottom covers allowing easy access to the drive inside.
- Led is not too bright. The LED is hidden behind black translucent plastic so it doesn't get too bright. Just enough for you to see that it is on and the drive is reading.

Speed:
I boot Windows 8.1 To Go from a standard 5400rpm drive plugged in to this enclosure. Windows To Go contains the entire windows OS and boots it from USB which allows a computer to dual boot to Windows 8.1 by simply plugging the drive in. From this drive, I've also installed and played games like Assassin's Creed Unity and Shadows of Mordor. While loading speed may be slower than an SSD plugged in to SATA, I still felt that the loading speed for the games were acceptable.

In conclusion, this is a nice looking case that feels good to hold, easy to slip in to a pocket and easily accessible (I switch out the drives sometimes). It is fully supported by Windows 8 and is sold at a great price.

title: Affordable and adds very little bulk.
review_text:
This SmartShell case is not just a magnetic cover for the iPad Air. It has a hard shell that protects the back of the tablet. To me, this is preferable to the magnetic cover because of the extra protection. The disadvantage is that you will not be able to take the cover off easily like the magnetic cover. It adds about 1/8" to each dimension of the iPad which is a minimal as you can get and still have protection.

My kids dropped the tablet on its corner near the volume buttons from about 2 1/2 feet off the ground. The plastic around the volume buttons cracked (it's the weakest part of the entire case) but the tablet was fine. No dents or scratches. A little super-glue to seal the crack and the case was as good as new. Had it been the magnetic cover, the tablet would have had a pretty bad dent.

This case gives you the "tablet" stand capability of the magnetic cover while providing more protection.

title: It charges alkaline...  but mostly, it's an excellent Ni-MH charger.
review_text:
More than anyone, I really wanted alkaline charging to work like other rechargeable batteries but the sad reality is that they're just not made for it.

The reality of alkaline charging:
- Duracells seem to leak more than cheapo "Kirkland" brand from Costco.
- Energizers do not hold charge very well.
- All brands leak eventually.
- Takes a long time to charge.
- Unreliable even if successfully recharged -- usually, batteries are connected in series, which means that if one fails, the device will not work.
- Battery leak can happen while charging or while being used in the device, resulting in a very messy charger and messy device.

title: Clock that doesn't quite do what you need it to.
review_text:
I thought I wouldn’t be picky when it comes to buying a new alarm clock; I mean, I owned a Sony Dream Machine (yeah, you too?) for over 30 years and that had minimal features! At least, that’s what I thought until I actually started looking for a new one.

When you look at the possibilities out there you start to think that perhaps I need:
- Bluetooth? It would be nice to wake up to a playlist I set up in my phone.
- Good sound quality? If I’m gonna have bluetooth, the sound quality needs to be good.
- Projection? It would be nice to see the time on the ceiling with the press of a button.
- Atomic? It would be nice to NOT have to manually set the time for Daylight Savings.
- Temperature/Weather? It would be great to know the weather when I look at the time -- especially if it is projected on the ceiling!

The Soundbot tries to provide many of these features but fail to put them together into one cohesive unit. It tries to be an alarm clock and bluetooth speakers but fails at both.

The Good:
- Great looking design. The wood look and the size, color and placement of time and temperature all add to a great look for the Soundbot.
- Impressive sound. As I’m currently searching for a bluetooth portable speaker (and have already reviewed a few), I pay special attention to sound quality. It’s comparable to the Jambox Mini.
- Touch controls. No buttons to detract from the wood look of the clock. The snooze, volume, and phone buttons are all touch sensitive.
- Time is remembered even when unplugged.

The Bad:
- The clock does NOT play a bluetooth when the alarm goes off. The workaround is to use your phone as the alarm, but what’s the point?
- No Next/Prev track buttons. The +/- buttons only control volume.
- Only one level of dimming. You can choose full or half brightness with the snooze button but it is still a little bright for me. I have to turn the clock away while I sleep.
- Alarm only has one sound: an annoying beep.

Tip:
The alarm clock can be set to go off every day (the alarm LED is solid, not flashing). When the alarm goes off, PRESS and HOLD any touch-sensitive button to disable the alarm for today. It will then go off again tomorrow.

Conclusion:
With the inability to use the bluetooth as an alarm tone, and without an FM Radio as an alternative, the Soundbot serves as a pretty poor alarm clock. You’re stuck with a simple beep. Without a next/prev track button, the Soundbot serves as a pretty poor wireless speaker. The good sound quality is the only thing it has going for it.

title: Good HDMI-CEC support; unimportant to most, important to me.
review_text:
I purchased this Panasonic Soundbar in June of 2013. At the time, my requirements were:
- Good sound (can't afford GREAT sound)
- Wireless Subwoofer
- HDMI input and good HDMI-CEC support
- Bluetooth support

In my search, I tested the [[ASIN:B00811NMMI Toshiba SBX4250]] and the [[ASIN:B00BLX9510 Samsung HW-F450]] from my local Costco. My final choice was the Panasonic.

Sound:
- Acceptable sound -- The front speakers are not a big improvement over the built-ins. With the subwoofer turned off, it is easy to mistake the Panasonic sound bar with the speakers from the Television.
- Good subwoofer -- The sub sounds good even at high volumes and fills out the overall sound from the sound bar.
- The Samsung has clearer mid and high ranges so the Panasonic seems slightly muffled in comparison.
- Overall sound better than the Toshiba.
- Wireless range for the subwoofer is short -- especially if placed behind the sofa (interference from people sitting in front of it). Range is about 15 feet with clear line of sight.

Decoders and Passthrough:
- AC3 and DTS Decoder (Toshiba lacks DTS)
- ARC (Audio Return Channel) -- If you use the Netflix app built in to your TV, audio is generated by your TV. Normally, an "optical out" cable from the TV back to the sound bar is necessary. ARC removes that need.

HDMI-CEC (also Aquos Link, Anynet+, Bravia LinkSync, Regza Link, etc):
This is where the Panasonic beats the Samsung. HDMI-CEC allows Televisions to control a connected device -- no matter the brand; The TV remote should be able to turn on a bluray player and send navigation (up/down/etc) and standard playback buttons without the need for a second remote control.

In the case of a sound bar, through HDMI-CEC:
1. The sound bar should turn on when the TV turns on -- Panasonic does this, Samsung does not.
2. The TV should play all sound through the sound bar and volume buttons on the TV remote should control volume on the sound bar -- Panasonic does this.
3. Turning on a bluray player, the sound bar should turn on and switch to the correct input automatically. The TV should also turn on and switch to the correct input -- Panasonic does this. It's then up to your TV do its part.

In conclusion, I chose the Panasonic because it gave me the ability to eliminate a remote control through HDMI-CEC (which Samsung didn't) and it had both AC3 and DTS decoders (which Toshiba didn't). With the added ability to play music from my phone through bluetooth, I'm still happy with my purchase one year later.

Tip: Unlike the Samsung and Toshiba, the Panasonic has a small "receiver" unit that adds another machine to your entertainment center. For me, I use some velcro strips and attach the "receiver" to the back of my TV. It is only 1 ¾" thick which was thinner than my wall mount.

title: Music that moves with you.
review_text:
Almost weightless with a great fit, and good battery life, the Avantree AS8Q Earbuds are great exercise headsets. The only factors keeping it from being perfect is the sound quality and clunky button controls.

For contrast, I also have the “Chicklets” style earbuds that have been rebranded by many companies (e.g. ECSEM Mini Lightweight...). If these “Chiclets” earbuds worked well for you, the Avantree will be a nice upgrade.

You should get the Avantree AS8Q if you are looking for:
-- lightweight and moves with you (after tightening the headband, there is nothing on these earbuds that flap, swing, tangle, or stick to your neck).
-- in ear, not over-the-ear (earbuds are angled slightly forward so they will fit deep into the ear).
-- separate earbuds (buds are not held together by a rigid band like the Motorola S10).
-- sweat proof.
-- good battery life (5 hours, while the “Chiclets” style earbuds have 2 hours).
-- no controls that dangle from the wires (like the Plantronics Backbeat)
-- great noise isolation (Deeply seated earbuds means you block out most of the noise. I’m able to hear the music and audiobook over the sound of a basketball bouncing off hardwood floors in an enclosed court without having to turn the volume up high).
-- good bluetooth range (I keep my phone on a chair near center of the basketball court, on the sidelines, and I’m able to go to both sides of the court without any drop outs. “Chiclet” style buds did not have this range).

And you don’t mind:
-- Fair sound quality. Compared to even the “Chicklets” style earbuds, upper and middle frequencies sound a little muddy, and the bass sounds blown out. Ever stand next to speakers on the dance floor? They sound horrible, but step away and they sound fine. The earbuds seat so deeply in your ear that you feel like the speakers are right next to your ear drums. Yes, the design advantage is also the design flaw. For all the other qualities that these earbuds have, I can overlook the sound quality issues (because let’s face it, you get used to it).
-- Clunky controls. The rubber that covers the control buttons are designed to keep sweat out, but they also make it hard to push the buttons. I often press the power button thinking I’ve got it pushed down, but after 10 seconds, I realize the earbuds aren’t turning on (or off). Same with trying to skip tracks. By contrast, controls on the “Chiclets” earbuds are easy to press while still being sweat proof.
-- Controls that seem backwards. Volume up is toward the back of your head and volume down is toward the front. Skip FORWARD is a long press of the volume DOWN button and the volume Up for skip back.

Wishlist for next revision:
-- Reduce the size of the housing.
-- Hard plastic buttons
-- Active noise cancellation. Noise isolation is nice, but you really can't hear anything when someone is talking to you.

In conclusion, I thoroughly enjoy my workouts with these earbuds.

title: Solid tablet mount for a good price.
review_text:
The Arkon Tablet arm everything that you see in the pictures:
- Two clamps that secure tightly to the metal posts on a car's headrest.
- The arm is extendable and can be locked in to position.
- There are two sets of L brackets to allow for multiple configurations depending on the size of your tablet.
- The L brackets have rubber footing that securely hold the tablet.

My concerns:
- The screws that tighten the clamps to the headrest posts are very very thin. I can see them breaking if someone tightens them too much.
- The tablet mount is held to the extendable arm using a ball joint. While a ball joint works well for a cell phone, my concern is that tablets are much heavier and that the ball joint would slip -- especially with car vibrations. It is necessary to tighten the ball joint a lot in order for it to stay put.

I do not deduct any stars for these concerns because they have not happened to me, but potential design flaws should be pointed out.

For my iPad, I use two long and two short L brackets (exactly as you see in the sample picture). This is the perfect size for the ipad. The position that of the iPad at the center of the car means both kids are able to see the videos comfortably on long car trips.

title: Good enclosure with added benefits
review_text:
Video files are big and add up quickly to fill up your tablet. With a WIFI enabled hard drive, you can free up space but still have access to your movies and shows. With a USB 3.0 and Ethernet connection, the Macally enclosure not only solves these storage issues, it provides some side benefits as well. Unfortunately, with limited WIFI range and unstable firmware, there is plenty of room for improvement.

Macally has the following advantage over similar devices:
- Ethernet port AND USB 3.0: Other enclosures on the market either do not include ethernet or is not USB 3.0. This enclosure has both. With Ethernet, the enclosure functions as a portable router and NAS.

Good:
- Transfer speed: USB 3.0 means transferring large files is FAST. I get 60Mb/sec.
- Files On-The-Go: Files are shared via HTTP if you use the WifiStor app or SAMBA if you use a computer.
- Battery life: I get about 3 hours because I have a SATA drive, not SSD. Life can be extended using any cell phone charger pack.
- Functions while charging: Plug in to car charger and no worries about batteries during a long road trip.
- Portable router/Wifi Repeater: In a hotel room, share the ethernet connection with the rest of your devices or use the WIFI repeater function and log in to the hotel’s gateway page only once for all devices.
- Acts as a NAS: Plug this into your router using an Ethernet cable and you have a nice Network storage device.

Bad:
- WIFI range is short. Because of additional interference you’d get in a hotel room (other wifi hotspots), WIFI wouldn’t even work across the room.

- Desperate need of a firmware upgrade:
-- Need automatic switching between Ethernet or Wifi. If Ethernet is plugged in, use that as the Internet connection otherwise, use the last WIFI AP.
-- Need stability. When using WIFI as Internet connection, the unit crashes and requires a few reboots before becoming useable.
-- Need FTP Server.
-- Need UPNP/DLNA. While playing videos off SAMBA is possible, UPNP/DLNA is more widely supported on the IOS and TV’s.

Tips for iOS:
Don’t rely on the WifiStor app. Players like PlayerXtreme HD will stream videos directly from SAMBA shares. Share is \\10.10.10.254\WiFiDisk1_Volume1

Tips for Android:
Video is already supported because WifiStor will launch the correct player for each video, but my top choice is to use XBMC and connect directly via SAMBA.

Macally has the following advantage over similar devices:
- Ethernet port AND USB 3.0: Other enclosures on the market either do not include ethernet or is not USB 3.0. This enclosure has both. With Ethernet, the enclosure functions as a portable router and NAS.

- Transfer speed: USB 3.0 means transferring large files is FAST. I get 60Mb/sec.

title: It's a mouse, it works.
review_text:
When purchasing a bluetooth mouse, or any bluetooth device, an important factor is how well it connects and how well it STAYS connected. After all this time, the industry still can’t make up its mind about how bluetooth works:
- Microsoft with their mouse and Sony with their controller that pair without the need of a code (which Android’s bluetooth stack doesn’t support).
- Mice and keyboards that will not reconnect after it wakes from sleep mode.
- To this day, bluetooth devices still can’t wake a computer from suspend state.
So when I get a simple bluetooth mouse for a good price, and it actually works as expected, I was happy.

For my review, I’m comparing the Bornd mouse to the [[ASIN:B006428K7I Motorola 89519N Bluetooth Mouse]] which I got in a set that included the [[ASIN:B004L9MBH6 Motorola Wireless Keyboard for Motorola ATRIX and XOOM (Motorola Retail Packaging)]].

With the Motorola mouse, its frequency somehow conflicts with the Motorola keyboard, resulting in sticky keys, as in “I’m having a good daaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaay”. Conversely, the keyboard interferes with the mouse where the computer would actually lose connection with the mouse for a few seconds after typing, or lose connection completely.

What I liked about the Bornd:
- Pairing was simple using the button at the bottom of the mouse.
- Operating distance is about 5 feet, but this may be because of my computer’s bluetooth antenna
- Takes a single AA battery which lasts over a month of moderate use (2 hours per day)
- Mouse movement is good. No need to adjust mouse speed in the control panel.
- Accuracy is good. Editing images using Pixlr.com, I’m able to select precisely the parts of the image I need.

What gave me trouble with the Bornd:
- When you first put your hand on this mouse, you will not feel that it is very well built. The plastic is completely smooth and the mouse wheel seems to rattle when you shake it. I got used to it after a few minutes, though.
- The mouse reconnects with the computer most of the time, but sometimes it was necessary to turn the mouse off and on again after the computer reboots or if the computer was out of range for an extended period of time.
- Lately, I’ve been experiencing double-clicks when I click on the left mouse button once. I’m usually able to fix this by getting angry and slamming the mouse down a couple of times. This may indicate a build quality issue with this mouse.

In my specific case, the Bournd did not interfere with my Motorola keyboard at all and it seems the sticky key occurs only when the batteries on the keyboard runs low.

title: Cheap, and it shows: not cheap enough!
review_text:
Nice idea, and my son was looking forward to using them, but these broke on his first outing (one prism set dislodged, rendering one eye’s view very dim and odd). Nothing abusive, just a gentle knock while it was hanging around his neck.

Junk.

I've added a star because Amazon's exchange process has been completely painless, and I'm taking the second pair into consideration. The replacement binoculars arrived, and haven't broken yet. They are, however, still pretty crappy. Maybe one step above something you might find in a Happy Meal. The optics are headache inducing just like less pretentious toy binoculars and the diopter adjustment is unstable and out of adjustment (my 20/20 vision has it maxed to the positive side to work). I wasn't expecting Swarovski quality here for $20, but the favorable reviews these got here on Amazon are frankly surprising given the optical mediocrity and poor quality control.

Do yourself a favor and save up for a real brand (refurbished?) for your kid's binoculars, even if it costs more (I've been pleased with the $80 Nikon Trailblazers for my older son). It's worth the extra $60 to avoid the headaches and feeling nthat you've purchased something that should have come for free in a Cracker Jack box.

title: Great Portability, Okay Pictures, Poor Durability
review_text:
I bought this camera for my wife last summer when she was in China. She was looking for something with less shutter lag than our last generation of Nikon and Canon digital point-and-shoots, and something cute and portable. The Panasonic DMC-FX30 is both of these things.

Out of the box it overexposed and undercolored things, but this was easily fixable after fiddling with the settings menu. Even set up right, photos using the flash still look too shiny whit, and photos taken at high ISOs are pretty noisy. The lack of a real viewfinder also makes capturing action clunky, but this is obviously in part an artifact of my preferences. This camera takes fine outdoor pictures, and the wide angle zoom allows for some cool shots and works well in confined (well-lit) spaces.

The camera is a small, precision-made jewel of a camera, with controls and buttons designed for smaller hands than mine; they fit my wife fine. We both missed the lack of a real viewfinder; pocket cameras seem to making an unfortunate departure from this useful standard (bright sunlight washes the display out, and it's easier to take a picture from your eye, as that's what you're composing with in the first place). The camera performed fine in its role as a city camera in Beijing, and for snapping quick shots back home when lugging the SLR around was inconvenient.

Now, however, we are in rural China for a year doing field work, and I was using the Panasonic as a backup to my Nikon DSLR. It was nice having a wide-angle lens in a pouch in my pocket when I had my normal or telephoto primes on the SLR. The Panasonic worked great in this role for 3-weeks, and then the automatic lens cap froze shut and wouldn't open, despite my coaxing, cleaning, etc. I finally just pried it off so I can still use the camera (I keep a business card over the lens in the soft pocket pouch), but let's say that I am not impressed with the camera's durability, compared to any other camera I've had, film or digital. It never got wet, dusty, dropped, or sat on; it looks brand new, but the lens cap won't work, and failed in a way that renders the camera useless to someone unwilling to take pliers to a Leica lens (failing and staying open would be preferable).

Anyway, if you're looking for a field or reliable travel camera, pass this one up.

title: Flawless Set Up
review_text:
I took this laptop to use for running a Cameo cutting machine. The Silhouette folks suggest a gaming type platform for the machine so that there is enough memory and processing power.

This is my first time to have an HP computer. Set up was pretty straightforward once I found the power button. A little guidance on that would be nice from the manufacturer. It's on the top of the keyboard on the left. The unit runs quietly and does not get hot like some of the others I have. The keyboard is OK. The characters are backlit with a bright green light which doesn't do much for me and the alphabet is some sort of modern thing where the "A" doesn't look like an A. I'll adjust.
What I'm not impressed with is the construction of this. The top is very flimsy when you open and close it. Kind of bendy and thin. Not framed well like others I have had. It will be fine for me in my studio, but I don't think it would hold up to being carried around and banged about.
I also don't much care for the touchpad at all. It seems hypersensitive even set on medium touch and requires multiple fingers to scroll and capture. I never could figure out how to get it to grab something to copy and paste. I'm off to get a mouse as soon as I'm finished.
Processing time seems fast. The display is very clear and the colors are true. As an artist this is important for the work I do. Peripherals all connected and installed easily. All in all I am pleased to have this.

title: Nothing Special
review_text:
Let me preface this review with saying that I love the Spectrum Noir markers. Have had both generations and recommend them to everyone. They are easy to use and a good value. On the other hand, I am not so "gobsmacked" about the new line of pencils. I bought the complete set because I am an illustrator and I like to have full sets of the tools I use. First off I was put off by the fact that there are 5 tins to sort through to find a color. I'm sure they did this, so folks could buy a tin at a time, but it easy to keep flipping open lids and looking around for just the right color you want. The pencils also fit very snuggly in the boxes and it is difficult to get them out sometimes.
As for the "creaminess" of said pencils, I would say there are some inconsistencies in that as well. Some of the Floral colors are really soft and creamy, some of the browns and grays are hard and scratchy and then there are some that are just so waxy you can't lay down two colors on top of each other.
If you are a rubber stamper or crafter that plans to use them, you will probably be fine with these. They seem to be geared more to that kind of audience. The price is right for what you get. I had no trouble sharpening the few I used. No breakage like I have encountered with the Prismacolor set I've had for 10 years. The blending solution I suspect is just Gamsol which most stampers already have if they've been using pencils before. I was able to achieve the same results using the Prismacolor pencils I had over the markers.
I will say their customer service rocks because they are going to allow me to send these back. This is a great company to deal with, I just think they kind of missed the mark with these.

title: Cool Concept - Poor Quality, Short Battery Life and Connection Issues
review_text:
I have had the opportunity to review many headsets and headphones over the years and without question the recent technological advancements have aided this area by leaps and bounds.

I can not recommend buying Bluetooth 5.0 enough over previous technologies if your devices support it. Nearly all devices that are Bluetooth 5.0 capable, including this one, will be backwards compatible with earlier technologies as well.

While the listing boasts of incredible battery life my testing has proven that simply is not the case. Battery life is lacking with these headsets lasting on average under 3 hours each in my tests. It is easily charged using the included charging case which will allow the earbuds to be recharged a many times from its one full charge. Since the earbuds can be used together for stereo sound or individually you can potentially double play time by using one at a time. Even with this, 3 hours of playtime from wireless earbuds is way below average. Even having the case which allows charging on the go, this doesn’t mitigate the frustration of having to charge after a few hours of listening.

The charging case is cool. It allows for Qi charging of devices and will act as a portable power supply. The downside to this is the size and weight. Sometimes I want to travel light and this set does not allow for that.

After receiving, I made sure the case was fully charged then confirmed each earbud had a full charge. After verifying full power within each earbud I followed the simple pairing instructions and had no problems whatsoever. Once the earbuds are removed from the case they first pair with each other then you simply pair with your Bluetooth device.

These earbuds will require testing which of the 4 sizes of ear bud caps work best for the individual user. I typically use the medium size which with this set the medium small ones worked better for me. I purchase sets of replacement memory foam ear bud pads which I ended up replacing them with as they are more comfortable and simply work better. Even with having better pads these buds tend to fall out.

The sound from these headphones is mediocre - from the bass notes to the midtones to the treble - not terrible but also not great. I tested these headphones with a wide range of audio - from audiobooks to jazz, heavy metal, country, classical and blues - everything just sounded ok.

I have listened to both music and audiobooks through these as I moved throughout my home and interestingly while these claim to be Bluetooth 5.0 they do not have near the range of other Bluetooth 5.0 sets I’ve tested. I estimate the effective range at around 20 feet.

While these are ok for listening to music, how are they for calling? The sound through these headphones is again mediocre- on both ends.

Controls are overly complicated and the buds do not always respond to the commands given which is especially frustrating when listening to an audiobook as I often skip ahead or back not intending too.

After fully reviewing these headphones over the last couple of months I have to recommend passing on this set. They are simply overpriced for the quality.

Thanks for reading my review. I enjoy writing them as I value reading other’s reviews when I’m making a buying decision. I regularly update my reviews to reflect any changes I may discover and to include helpful tips you may need if you purchase the product. I will always make every effort to answer any questions I can as it is my pleasure to help.

title: Decent Quality Clone at the Price - Budget Friendly Blue Iris Camera
review_text:
I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential.

As with all security systems my advice is never use cloud based recording - this opens your entire network to not only the company who you are giving blanket access too but also to hackers. The same is true for WiFi. Obviously WiFi is more convenient but if your privacy is a concern this really needs to be taken into account. Hackers have become quite adept at hacking into WiFi cameras and being able to not only watch your feed but control your cameras and access your entire network. If you choose to utilize WiFi cameras take the time to understand your router and employ proper VPN protocols.

Due to my security concerns with WiFi cameras my current security system is completely run through a dedicated computer utilizing the Blue Iris software. While this may seem intimidating to some, it is well worth learning and utilizing for the huge advantages in privacy and security.

I’ve noticed many people have asked if this camera works with a Blue Iris and it does without any issue. Just update to the latest firmware. The remainder of setup within Blue Iris is straightforward. This HITOSINO / VALUCAM 8MP IR IP CAMERA supports PoE 802.3af and will work with 48V active adapters which are more expensive, but you can also rely on a PoE switch, which in my opinion is a much easier, straightforward option.

The fixed lens size of 2.8mm provides decent field of view and the digital zoom is acceptable. The 1/2.7" CMOS image sensor is decent in low light, certainly not as good as 1/1.8” but I’ve found the low light capabilities average in comparison to other similar cameras. While low light capabilities will not blow you away they are reasonable. The LEDs must be illuminating objects to provide what is considered “colored night vision” which is misleading.

The camera has a built in microphone that allows for sound recording, though no speaker so two way communication will not be possible with this unit.

In terms of storage, the HITOSINO / VALUCAM 8MP IR IP CAMERA utilizes H.265 which is currently the best option for video compression. I have had this set up utilizing Blue Iris software which I definitely recommend. By fine tuning BI settings I have been able to find a balance between file size and image quality that works for my situation.

When all things are taken into account this is a solidly built camera, reasonably suited to outdoor environments - if at all exposed to elements rake the time to seal as an added layer of protection, decent daytime / nighttime resolution, easily mounted, and setup in Blue Iris was reasonably easy and straightforward.

While I would prefer to have pan and tilt capabilities at this price point that is unrealistic.

Overall I have been moderately impressed with this budget camera and would recommend it for many security situations.

That being said there are key components I look for in wireless doorbell cameras: clear picture that provides a wide viewing angle, it either be hard wired or have excellent battery life, when chime button is pressed alert is sent and app can be opened and responsive in a quick time, 2 way audio communication is clear on both ends, motion sensitivity is adjustable and accurate.

I have thoroughly tested this product over the last 4 months and in comparison to the others on the market around this price point this product has proven to be clearly the best.

The vast majority of wireless doorbells use proprietary batteries which forces users to purchase secondary batteries typically costing $30-$50. This factor is a huge bonus.

The camera is quite good. Images are clear and the wide angle provides a full view of the area in front of the doorbell. The AI Smart Human detection is without question the best I have found. This is a huge feature that helps prevent constant false alerts.

The base station holds up to a 128GB SD card for video storage. This is awesome for multiple reasons. If the camera was stolen the evidence will be saved on the base station within your home and all of your recordings are stored locally. This is an outstanding system.

Unfortunately, as with many similar products, while the hardware is good the software needs some work. As is typical, I can not find any way to force this doorbell to work with better software. I would much rather use the Tuya app where I have the bulk of my automation set but this will not migrate.

The 2 way audio is spotty. It sounds like ordering through a drive through where every 3rd word is audible. Since I don’t use these to have in depth conversations it isn’t a huge deal but should be noted.

This is definitely among the best wireless doorbells I have tested for a while. It is not perfect, the sound leaves room for improvement as does response times but overall this is a quality unit.

While the vast majority of the doorbells I tested I advised to avoid all together this one is one worth using.

title: OK Cable Management Box - but Not for Bulky Power Adapters
review_text:
I have reviewed several similar products and while this could work for some I found the design of this cable management box needs a bit of redesigning.

The point of cable management is to keep your cables looking neat and tidy - this can help achieve that - as long as your plugs are relatively small. While there are four rotating outlets on the ends they are close together and depending on the size of you power adapter plug many will block the plug next to it. I found this was also the case with the outlets located on the top.

This is nearly always an issue with power strips of any sort but when you try to add a cover this becomes even more challenging.

This brings me to the cover design. The side wings expand and must be spread to the maximum width in order to unlock and lift the lid - and even then it’s not easy. This inner cover is thin and not very substantial. Once the other wings cover it that is protected but access is difficult.

Typically I am a big fan of Legrand products and find their designs innovative, helpful and user centric. I cannot say that about this product after testing it for a while.

In real world use I simply have too may power adapter plugs and USB powered devices for this to be a viable solution at my desk. I found it works ok for my entertainment center though I already had my plugs organized there.

In the end, I would recommend one of the more simple box style cord management systems. These allow the greatest flexibility and are definitely far less frustrating to use.

title: DECENT WIRELESS HEADPHONE SET AT A GREAT PRICE!
review_text:
I have had the opportunity to review many headsets and headphones over the years and without question the recent technological advancements have aided this area by leaps and bounds.

I can not recommend buying Bluetooth 5.2 enough over previous technologies if your devices support it. Nearly all devices that are Bluetooth 5.2 capable, including this one, will be backwards compatible with earlier technologies as well.

Battery life is outstanding with these headsets lasting a solid 5 hours each in all of my tests. It is easily charged using the included charging case which will allow the earbuds to be recharged several times from its one full charge. Since the earbuds can be used together for stereo sound or individually you can potentially double play time by using one at a time.

This unique charging case is powered via an included super fast standard USB to USB Type C cable. This case will allow the headsets to be recharged even when you don’t have access to electricity.

After receiving, I made sure the case was fully charged then confirmed each earbud had a full charge. After verifying full power within each earbud I followed the simple pairing instructions and had no problems whatsoever. Once the earbuds are removed from the case they first pair with each other then you simply pair with your Bluetooth device.

The design of these headset makes it so it fits securely in your ear and is relatively comfortable. As someone who has used many of these units, this design is not the most comfortable as the weight is all on the ear canal. I’ve found headsets that are worn only supported by the ear canal can end up being painful when used for extended periods.

The sound from these headphones is decent - from the rich bass notes to the vibrant midtones to the bright treble. I tested these headphones with a wide range of audio - from audiobooks to jazz, heavy metal, country, classical and blues - everything sounded reasonable.

I have listened to both music and audiobooks through these as I moved throughout my home and it will easily pick up the signal through walls up to 25’ away, and even more without obstacles. This is a decent set Bluetooth headphones.

While these are great for listening to music, how are they for calling? The sound through these headphones is absolutely outstanding - on both ends. That is not always the case. Many of the other headphones I have tested, while they sound good to the person using it - those who they are speaking to can’t hear them clearly. It is no fun having a conversation where the other person keeps saying, “huh, what did you say?” You won’t have to worry about that with this set.

If you are looking for a decent headphone set, especially one at a reasonable price, with decent sound and reception and has the power to last this is a great choice.

title: Awesome Concept - Poor Execution
review_text:
Being both an audiophile and a lover of all new tech when I first read about this technology coming out a few years ago I started looking forward to testing it.

So what are the potential advantages of bone conduction earphones? I’m glad you asked. When properly adjusted they allow the user to enjoy listening to whatever they choose while not blocking external noises, thus allowing the user to react to ambient noises. This should make them safe to use while driving or doing other activities that require hearing ambient noise in order to conduct safely.

As with other bone conduction headphones, these 9 Digital headphones allow for little fine adjustment. In order for this type of headphones to work properly and provide the highest sound quality they should rest flat, or almost flat against the skin between the front of the ear and the rear part of the cheek bone. When adjusting the speaker it will be clear when the speaker is properly adjusted. This set of headphones is designed to fall lower on the back of the head which for me pulled the speakers out of the ideal placement. While I have worked on adjusting this, it really is not possible. Due to this, sound quality is decent yet not optimal and surrounding people are able to hear what the listener is playing.

Just so it is understood, these headphones are rated IP53, meaning that they’re protected against dust, in so much as their inner workings won’t be compromised if dust were to get inside. They’re also protected against spraying water, with no pressure when tilted up to a 60-degree angle. This is a lower rating as compared to other headphones in this price range.

In terms of operation these headphones struggle to maintain a solid connection for anywhere close to the full 33 feet they are rated - typically Bluetooth 5.0 holds a connection with no problem though I have found that isn’t the case with these headphones. The batteries lasted approximately the amount of time listed. Sound quality is middle of the road especially due to not allowing for fine adjusting of the speakers.

This is a great technology with a lot of potential. I have tested and reviewed bone conduction headphones since they first were released a few years ago, due to how these fit and the connectivity issues this is not a set I would recommend.

title: ABSOLUTELY AWESOME BLUETOOTH SPEAKER
review_text:
I have tested and reviewed literally hundreds of Bluetooth speakers and while I am not a fan of music that is particularly bass heavy I found this speaker produces rich, vibrant sounds from all wave lengths. It produces more than ample volume for most any setting and has several connection methods.

While I have tested and reviewed Bluetooth speakers costing far more than what this does, the sound quality from this speaker rivals them. In relation to the sound quality this speaker is simply incredible.

In regards to charging time and battery life, both are outstanding. In my tests charging takes about approximately 3 hours to charge the built in 5,000 mAh battery and the speaker lasts a solid 4.5 hours at max volume - 12 hour with volume midway (of course this will vary a bit due to exact settings).

There are multiple ways to connect to this speaker including Bluetooth 5.0, which can reach much further than previous versions, through an AUX cable, a 3.5mm jack, SD card and you can even connect via NFC (Near Field Communication).

I have taken this speaker with me to the pool for the last couple of months and have been thoroughly impressed with its performance. The battery, being 5,000 mAh, it’s much longer lasting than most allowing for all day listening and the sound quality has been outstanding.

This speaker is rated IPX4 meaning it is tested and proven safe for splashes - technically, a device with a level 4 water resistance rating can survive small water jets projected by a 6.3mm nozzle at any angle.

If you have 2 of these speakers they pair for true surround sound producing a full, rich, encompassing sound environment that is hard to believe can come from a pair of small Bluetooth speakers. I have the larger version of this speaker and pair the two together outside by our pool for a really amazing sound quality.

This battery and speaker comes with a bit of weight - 2.31 pounds to be exact, far less than the larger version but still heavier than most Bluetooth speakers.

This is an all around great Bluetooth speaker that I certainly recommend.

title: ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE BLUETOOTH SPEAKER!
review_text:
I have tested and reviewed literally hundreds of Bluetooth speakers and while I am not a fan of music that is particularly bass heavy I found this speaker produces rich, vibrant sounds from all wave lengths. It produces more than ample volume for most any setting and can connect to another for awesome stereo sound..

While I have tested and reviewed Bluetooth speakers costing far more than what this does, the sound quality from this speaker rivals them. In relation to the sound quality this speaker is simply incredible.

In regards to charging time and battery life, both are outstanding. In my tests charging takes about approximately 3 hours to charge the built in whopping 14 hour battery (of course this will vary a bit due to exact settings). By utilizing the latest in USB technology USB-C this speaker charges far faster than many others.

Connecting to this speaker via Bluetooth 5.0 is a breeze. What is really a standout feature of this speaker is its ability to pair with another for stereo sound. By double clicking the left most button the speaker will pair with a second Sudio Femtio Wireless Speaker and you will experience a far more rich listening experience. My iPhone allows me to connect to both speakers independently which I have found provides a far truer surround sound by utilizing left and right channels.

I have taken this speaker with me to the pool for the last several months and have been thoroughly impressed with its performance. The battery is much longer lasting than most allowing for all day listening and the sound quality has been outstanding.

This speaker is rated IPX6 meaning it is tested and proven An IPX6 device will stay fully functional when sprayed with strong water jets (15psi) at any angle, from a 3m distance for 1min. In practice, this means that a device can survive light, moderate, or even heavy rain for a certain period. It can also survive heavy sweating. Accidentally spilling a glass of water over it should not be a problem.

As mentioned before, if you have 2 of these speakers they pair for true surround sound producing a full, rich, encompassing sound environment that is hard to believe can come from a pair of small Bluetooth speakers. I got 2 of these speakers and have loved the sound quality they produce working in tandem.

What is amazing is all of this battery and speaker comes with so little weight - under 1.5 pounds to be exact (675 grams). That is incredible as other speakers with similar sound quality and features I have tested and reviewed typically weigh 3 times this much.

This is an all around great Bluetooth speaker that I certainly recommend.

title: An AMAZING Shower Speaker
review_text:
This shower speaker has far exceeded my expectations, after a very thorough evaluation I can completely say this is an outstanding product - in fact, the best shower speaker I have reviewed.

First of all, this item arrived quickly and is exactly as described.

After following the instructions and fully charging using the USB cable, I paired it with my iPhone with no issue.

All of the control buttons are on the front of the speaker while the charging port is on the lower side. Every opening is sealed very well and withstands the moisture of the shower without an issue.

The sound is rich and clear. It is clear in the full range of sound from the deep bass notes to the clear high pitches.

Calls are clear and can be received without any issue. Microphone volume is a bit low when speaking - the person calling may have some trouble hearing the person speaking in the shower. Part of that is the ambient noise generated by the shower, which is to be expected. Most people won't make a habit of talking on the phone while showering, so I really don't see this as an issue.

The super powerful 1800mAh internal battery will last and last. After the initial charge, I was able to use the speaker daily while in the shower and then getting ready for well over a month before recharging and probably could have gone longer. I used the speaker not only while showering but also while getting ready.

In conclusion, as far as listening to music or audiobooks while in the shower and getting ready this speaker is excellent. The speaker produces a rich sound quality with more than enough volume. The battery is excellent, providing plenty of power requiring less time charging and delivering more time enjoying the music.

If you are looking for a great speaker for in your shower or other moist environments - look no further. This is definitely a Bluetooth speaker I highly recommend.

title: Decent TV Ceiling Mount - Could be Better
review_text:
We recently moved in to a new house and needed this mount to install a TV on our patio. I measured the VESA holes on our TV and knew this would work prior to ordering so that was not an issue.

This will hold a 55” Visio TV from a vaulted ceiling.

Installation is not as straightforward as I have experienced with other mounts though not terribly difficult either. The issues with installation really come from limited space to work to attach the parts together and there not being great instructions.

A few tips we found as we installed that will help you - first locate your ceiling joist stud to mount into. Then find the distance from the wall where your TV can swivel both left and right to the farthest point you desire - then mark your spot.

As with all mounting brackets you want to mount into a stud with as many bolts as possible.

In terms of use this works but there are features that just should be more user friendly. For instance if the height is in the highest position the cables will be pinched in place and can not be moved at all - the cable pass through should have a notch so this is not an issue as it is never good to have cables being pinched.

In addition if you want to either swivel or tilt the TV a hex key is required instead of being able to do this with a finger tightening knob like most mounts - this is definitely the worst design flaw in my opinion. This issue has left us unable to rotate our TVs mount that is “able to swivel” when we’ve had guests at our house due to not being able to locate the correct sized hex key. Ugh.

This mount works, but I would really only recommend it for locations where the user does not intend to alter the tilt or direction of the TVs screen very often.

title: Persistent Connecting When Charging
review_text:
I have had the opportunity to review many headsets and headphones over the years and without question the recent technological advancements have aided this area by leaps and bounds.

I can not recommend buying Bluetooth 5.0 enough over previous technologies if your devices support it. Nearly all devices that are Bluetooth 5.0 capable, including this one, will be backwards compatible with earlier technologies as well.

Battery life is outstanding with these headsets, lasting a solid 6+ hours each in all of my tests. It is easily charged using the included charging case which will allow the earbuds to be recharged 4 times from its one full charge. While many similar sets come with a charging case this one is tiny - having a built in 500 mAh battery, it will charge the headphones 4 times. The case has a dot display that shows the percentage of battery remaining so there is no surprise when it runs out of power.

Since the earbuds can be used together for stereo sound or individually you can potentially double play time by using one at a time.

This unique charging case is powered via an included super fast USB Type C cable.

After receiving, I made sure the case was fully charged then confirmed each earbud had a full charge. After verifying full power within each earbud I followed the simple pairing instructions and had no problems whatsoever. Once the earbuds are removed from the case they first pair with each other then you simply pair with your Bluetooth device.

These earbuds will require testing which of the 3 sizes of ear bud caps work best for the individual user. I typically use the medium size stereo caps but found the buds fell out of my ears with those. I switched to the small sized caps and, while better, I still had one fall out. I ended up using small cylindrical caps I had Can youand they fit perfectly.

Having no buttons on this set means controlling them requires touching either the right or left ear bud - this can be a bit finicky in terms of control.

The sound from these headphones is decent - while not amazing they are far better than others I have tested. I tested these headphones with a wide range of audio - from audiobooks to jazz, heavy metal, country, classical and blues - everything sounded decent but will not blow you away.

I have listened to both music and audiobooks through these as I moved throughout my home and it will easily pick up the signal through walls up to 35’ away, and even more without obstacles. This is really an outstanding set of Bluetooth headphones in terms of reception.

While these are great for listening to music, how are they for calling? The sound through these headphones is absolutely outstanding - on both ends. That is not always the case. Many of the other headphones I have tested, while they sound good to the person using it - those who they are speaking to can’t hear them clearly. It is no fun having a conversation where the other person keeps saying, “huh, what did you say?” You won’t have to worry about that with this set.

One critical area that I’ve had issues with concerning these headphones is they will randomly pair with my phone while charging in the case - I only realize it after I have missed calls and texts due to the sound being diverted to the headphones. I have no idea why these headphones do this but it has definitely proven a drawback to this set.

If you are looking for a small headphone set, that is comfortable to wear, provides decent sound and reception and has the power to last all day this is an ok choice. My primary concern is the persistent connecting when not intended causing calls and notifications to be missed. This issue has made this set one that I would pass on.

title: Quality Budget Friendly Blue Iris Camera
review_text:
I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential.

As with all security systems my advice is never use cloud based recording - this opens your entire network to not only the company who you are giving blanket access too but also to hackers. The same is true for WiFi. Obviously WiFi is more convenient but if your privacy is a concern this really needs to be taken into account. Hackers have become quite adept at hacking into WiFi cameras and being able to not only watch your feed but control your cameras and access your entire network. If you choose to utilize WiFi cameras take the time to understand your router and employ proper VPN protocols.

Due to my security concerns with WiFi cameras my current security system is completely run through a dedicated computer utilizing the Blue Iris software. While this may seem intimidating to some, it is well worth learning and utilizing for the huge advantages in privacy and security.

I’ve noticed many people have asked if this camera works with a Blue Iris and it does without any issue. Just update to the latest firmware. The remainder of setup within Blue Iris is straightforward. This IPC2387C supports PoE 802.3af and will work with 48V active adapters which are more expensive, but you can also rely on a PoE switch, which in my opinion is a much easier, straightforward option. Something to note, if you plan on powering via a DC cable this is not included.

The fixed lens size of 2.8mm provides decent field of view and the digital zoom is acceptable. The 1/2.8” CMOS 8MP image sensor is decent in low light, certainly not as good as 1/1.8” but I’ve found the low light capabilities average in comparison to other similar cameras. The LEDs must be illuminating objects to provide what is considered “colored night vision” which is misleading.

The camera has a built in microphone that allows for sound recording, though no speaker so two way communication will not be possible with this unit.

In terms of storage, the IPC2387C utilizes H.265 which is currently the best option for video compression. I have had this set up utilizing Blue Iris software which I definitely recommend.

When all things are taken into account this is a solidly build camera, suited to outdoor environments, decent daytime / nighttime resolution, fairly easily mounted, and setup in Blue Iris was reasonably easy and straightforward.

While I would prefer to have pan and tilt capabilities at this price point that is unrealistic. Overall I have been moderately impressed with this budget camera and would recommend it for many security situations.

When I initially saw this camera it checked most of the boxes I look for when looking for security cameras. It is PoE, has H.265, ONVIF support allowing use with Blue Iris, Sony IMX274 Starvis Sensor. Once I received this camera and began digging into it I quickly realized certain important facts.

Most importantly, this is a rebranded Hikvision camera. This is among the companies that has been discovered spying on the US using their cameras - the firmware this camera comes with is long outdated and, in fact, can not be updated to anywhere close to what is current. This is far too risky for me to install on my system.

Any camera you install on your system should have the latest firmware installed and you need to have a good understanding of network security protocols. Cameras such as this one, that are older versions of cameras made by manufacturers that are blacklisted - while still being sold, people who understand the industry avoid them - are an invitation for hackers to invade your system.

While the specs on and price of this camera seem decent - this is not a camera I recommend. This poses far more risks than it is worth.

title: ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE BLUETOOTH SPEAKER
review_text:
I have tested and reviewed literally hundreds of Bluetooth speakers and while I am not a fan of music that is particularly bass heavy I found this speaker produces rich, vibrant sounds from all wave lengths. It produces more than ample volume for most any setting and has several connection methods.

While I have tested and reviewed Bluetooth speakers costing far more than what this does, the sound quality from this speaker rivals them. In relation to the sound quality this speaker is simply incredible.

In regards to charging time and battery life, both are outstanding. In my tests charging takes about approximately 2 hours to charge the built in whopping 10,400 mAh battery and the speaker lasts a solid 6.5 hours at max volume - 10 hour with volume midway (of course this will vary a bit due to exact settings).

There are multiple ways to connect to this speaker including Bluetooth 5.0, which can reach much further than previous versions, through an AUX cable, a 3.5mm jack, TF/SD card and you can even connect via NFC (Near Field Communication).

I have taken this speaker with me to the pool for the last couple of months and have been thoroughly impressed with its performance. The battery, being 10,400 mAh, it’s much longer lasting than most allowing for all day listening and the sound quality has been outstanding. The battery is so awesome this can even be used as a power bank to charge your phone - most speakers can’t make that claim.

This speaker is rated IPX5 meaning it is tested and proven safe for splashes - technically, a device with a level 5 water resistance rating can survive small water jets projected by a 6.3mm nozzle at any angle. The testing lasts for 15 min and the volume of water is 12.5 l/min.

If you have 2 of these speakers they pair for true surround sound producing a full, rich, encompassing sound environment that is hard to believe can come from a pair of small Bluetooth speakers.

All of this battery and speaker comes with weight - 5.28 pounds to be exact. That is definitely the downside to this speaker.

This is an all around great Bluetooth speaker that I certainly recommend.

title: Decent Wall Mount for Large TVs
review_text:
Large flat screen TVs require special mounting brackets in order to safely hang them on the wall.

We used this bracket to hang our new 75 inch Sony TV. The bracket itself has worked well. We did end up utilizing the extension bracket which gave us added mobility in locating the TV in the center of the wall. Due to our hanging the TV on an interior wall that had a narrow gap between the drywall and cinder block I had to get special wall anchors to support the weight of the TV.

Due to how this bracket is designed it can be difficult to access ports, such as HDMI and USB, once the TV is hung upon the wall. It can be done but someone must unlock it by pulling the straps and hold the bottom of the TV away from the wall as someone else navigates wires below. It is definitely not easily accomplished.

This is definitely a stable TV mount - even for large TVs, it’s just not the easiest to connect accessories once the TV is hung.

There is limited tilt mobility but enough to adjust for viewing angle.

This is a decent TV mount for large TVs but could be better.

title: OUTSTANDING NEW OUTDOOR CAMERA BY VIMTAG
review_text:
I have been using Vimtag cameras for over four years and absolutely LOVE them.

This new outdoor camera by Vimtag is absolutely outstanding.

Installation was as easy as all their other cameras have been. Simply follow the instructions and you won’t have any problems whatsoever. You’ll download the Vimtag app, plug the camera into your router via the included Ethernet cable, log in to your network and establish the connection. Once added into the Vimtag app it’s just a matter of mounting the camera.

This new B5 Outdoor Camera by Vimtag has several advanced features the previous Vimtag Outdoor cameras did not have - it has both a speaker and a microphone, allowing for two way communication, a super bright motion activated LED light and superior lenses allowing for crystal clear viewing and recording.

There are so many things I love about the Vimtag camera system. Firstly, each camera holds its own micro SD card so you don’t have to pay for monitoring or video storage, unless you want too. By utilizing the latest in video compression technology, this can hold far more video footage on the SD card than previous versions. The only downside to this is if the camera was stolen you’ll lose the footage. Another option you have is to utilize Vimtag’s S1 Storage Box which will store the data from up to 6 cameras. In addition you can subscribe to cloud storage.

While other reviewers have commented on their cameras being hacked, I have never had this be an issue but I understand internet security and utilize firewalls that prevent access. While the first versions of the Vimtag cameras had vulnerabilities I have found those to be secured now.

This camera has worked flawlessly. Motion sets it to record whatever is going on or send an alert to my phone. If the motion takes place at night the bright LED Light comes on and I receive crystal clear images. The two way communication is incredibly clear on both ends.

This is another outstanding product by Vimtag that I don’t hesitate to recommend.

title: Simple Security Device - Batteries Drain - Too Much Hassle
review_text:
For many years I have researched, written about and reviewed all types of security equipment - from the most advanced to the most simple. This set falls into the later category.

I have tested and reviewed several similar sets. Each of these sensors work based on a simple magnetic principle which is why it is critical they be mounted on the same plains, directly next to to each other when the door or window is closed. When open the magnet is released and the switch triggers causing the alarm to sound. This technology has been used with great success for many years.

The alarms are very loud and work the way they should. If the batteries lasted as long as the listing claimed this would be a reasonable set though they do not. These sets will require battery changes every 2.5-3 months, each sensor requires 3 AG13 or LR44 button style batteries. If all 6 sensors are utilized you will need 18 batteries every 3 months or 72 batteries a year. Not only does this get expensive but it is a hassle staying on top of the batteries always dying.

For those interested in utilizing these sensors, I recommend the following batteries: Eunicell SR44W 303 357 Silver Oxide Button Cell 1.55V Battery Long Shelf Life 0% Mercury (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07MMTG4ZF/ref=cm_sw_em_r_mt_dp_7RB98F39642K4BXJ2Q2C) - while these are the same size and voltage they are made with better components and tend to last a bit longer and are far more consistent upon arrival.

After using these for 8 months I can say while these work and consistently sound when the sensors are separated there are far better options that use much more sophisticated, long lasting batteries. This is the type of product where you want a quality lithium ion battery that you can count on for many months or a year at a time - and ideally recharge it at that point.

After thoroughly testing this set I suggest looking into more sophisticated, sets that will cost slightly mor upfront but cost far less in the long run.

review_text:
This review is for the Anpviz 5MP vari-focal 2.8~12mm PoE Dome Camera (IPC-D250G-4X).

I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential.

If you are new to home security camera systems, I recommend going with wired (non-WiFi), NVR or computer based recorders run with systems such as Blue Iris. This type of system is infinitely more secure and stable. While initial setup costs are a bit more the security it affords is worth every penny. It always pays to research the products, discuss them with those in the field, understand vulnerabilities and PLAN YOUR SYSTEM PRIOR TO PURCHASING ANYTHING. If you are at all tech savvy at all you can do it. While there is a bit of a learning curve it is not awful and in the end you will be thankful for the time you spent in the beginning as it will save you time, money and endless frustration.

I have set up, tested and reviewed more security systems and individual products than I can possibly remember. Without question my go to solution for home security solutions is a computer based, Blue Iris system with POE cameras run off of quality POE switches. This type of system is not only easy to operate but is highly secure.

As with any component there are a host of factors to consider. In terms of cameras more megapixels is not always better. For instance 2MP cameras often perform better in low light while 5MP will allow for more detail when lighting is good. One disadvantage of higher megapixel cameras is the recordings will take up more hard drive space. Depending on the number of cameras, this can become a larger concern.

When I saw this camera at this price point I knew it was something I needed to check out.

While the vast majority of cameras I test at this price point are disappointing I am pleased to say that was absolutely not the case with this gem of a camera.

First of all, let me point out this camera WILL NOT PAN NOR TILT. Where you position the lens is where it will remain. This means planning your installation location is very important. The ideal location for this camera is 8-12’ above ground. This will allow full use of the vari-focal lens (2.8~12mm vari-focal lens)
so you can capture both the wide angle and closeup images (4X zoom). When installing this type of camera I test different locations with it hooked up prior to install in order to decide on the optimal location.

I set this camera up on my Blue Iris system with no issues whatsoever and have had it in constant use for four months. I ran it via PoE router and everything has worked exactly as it should.

I use this as a secondary camera so after fully testing the capabilities I reduced the resolution to save on disc space and have found minimal image degradation. By using the H.265 high-efficiency coding you will save a lot of hard drive space while maintaining quality.

As with all dome style cameras night IR enhanced viewing can result in glare from the dome. I over come this by placing exterior light sources and not depending on the built in IR lighting which I have found produces far better image captures.

After four months of putting this camera through full testing, I can safely say this is an excellent camera at an amazing price. Without question I recommend buying it. This is dependable, easy to set up and use, made to last and an outstanding bargain.

While I was a bit intimidated at the idea of making my own Ethernet cables, once I got this set and did a bit of research I found it really isn’t near as difficult as I thought it may be.

It is important to look for “SOLID BARE COPPER CONDUCTORS” as this will make an enormous difference in the performance of your cable. The above cable listed works incredibly well and will not let you down.

I chose to create my own Ethernet cables as I was running cables to PoE security cameras and I wanted them the exact length so I could run them as far as I needed and not have excess that caused transmission delays.

Adding the pass through connectors and crimping them is quite easy once you get the hang of it. Watch a video and take your time as you begin. This tool is well made and will hold up to years of use.

While I was using it I had a bit of issue when stripping the wires as it can be a bit tricky to get a clean strip. After creating several wires I found I got better at this and was able to strip more efficiently.

I have been very pleased with this set and would recommend it.

title: Outstanding Extender for the Price
review_text:
I have tested and reviewed several WiFi extenders and this one works nearly as well as one that cost over six times as much and was far easier to set up.

I set this up simply using the WPS pairing method with the extender being plugged in next to my primary router. It paired perfectly in just over a minute and I was able to unplug it and move it to an outlet farther away where it would then repeat my signal for greater range into my shop in my back yard. This worked perfectly.

Here are a few tips for getting the most out of this or any similar device.

1. Understand this will only extend the coverage you already have. If you are not satisfied with your current speed when located close to your current router this type of device will not help. In this instance you will need to improve your internet service, modem or router.
2. An extender / repeater must be placed close enough to receive an optimal signal that it then repeats - if it is too far away, it can only transmit what it picks up - if this signal is weakened due to distance from your primary router the end result will be a reduced signal. It can only work with the signal it is receiving.
3. When placing any extender / repeater pay attention to what is between it and your primary router - keep in mind interior walls tend to not have insulation and are thus easier to penetrate than exterior walls, metal objects deflect signals more than other materials as do especially dense materials.
4. Optimally a primary router should be placed in a centralized location within a home and where the bulk of the time is spent. Extenders / repeaters can then be utilized between that and where you have found weak signal points.
5. In some instances, such as within Mesh WiFi networks extenders / repeaters can slow down the entire network and are thus not advised. A lot of this depends on advanced settings.

In all of my testing over the last 4 months I have found this to be an outstanding unit at frankly an unbeatable price.

This is definitely a product I recommend.
