title: WOW!  That was a HUGE disappointment.
review_text:
I had been anxiously waiting to try out the NETGEAR Nighthawk. I’d read over the impressive specs long before it was released, I’ve read glowing reviews touting it as the fastest, most powerful router Netgear had yet to produce... Specially made for the high demands of Smart Homes. All the hype made it sound like it was going to be AMAZING.

Now that I’ve set it up and run a full battery of tests - honestly the best thing I can say about it is it looks cool. 😕

I have been working with NETGEAR products for 25+ years so setup was not a big deal. As with most of NETGEAR’s new products don’t expect much printed material - that’s OK with me... I downloaded the Nighthawk app and followed the directions - they are fairly straightforward.

Restart your modem, plug in your Nighthawk Router, plug Ethernet Cable from modem to router, connect cell to router’s network using the ID and password provided on the sticker on top of the routers plastic cover, return to app. Here is where things began making less sense.

When I return to the Nighthawk app it goes through the process of connecting to my router and I receive an error message: ROUTER NOT SUPPORTED. Odd, but I’ve learned when installing a new router anything can happen. I exit the app and return, same message. I exit the app, restart the router, wait and restart the app and it recognizes. Great - I’m in... no big deal.

I update the Firmware, change the network name and password and start checking through the settings. I notice right away there are very few settings within the app - no security settings tab, no parental controls tab - odd, but I’ve learned NETGEAR tends to move these types of things around when they redesign their apps, so I put that concern to the side.

I plug my Ethernet cables into the 1G ports (there are 4 of them) in the back and watch the lights on front illuminate.

One of these runs to my computer and once it initialized the internet connection I ran a speed test - I’d tested with my previous router just prior to switch and was consistently benching at 210Mb/s download and 15Mb/s upload. With the Nighthawk I speed tested at 130Mb/s and 9Mb/s - definitely not what I’d hoped to see but I knew all my smart devices were working on rejoining the network so that could be slowing it down.

I decided to give it some time to let everything register on the network. In the Nighthawk app I had 42 devices and about half were still listed as unknown.

I let it work for about an hour and it recognized the majority of them... I ran another speed test - again through my laptop connected via Ethernet through the Nighthawk and this time received 154Mb/s and 11Mb/s. Still not great.

Then I went into my Nighthawk app as it has a speed test feature in there - I try that and receive an error that I must be on the network to run a speed test. I was on the network. I exit the app and go back in and receive the message ROUTER NOT SUPPORTED again. Ugh - really???

I reboot the router again and then the app recognizes it. While I’m able to control the router the speed test function does not want to work. Not a huge issue. I went through the browser on my phone and ran a speed test. The results were absolutely pathetic. This is the NIGHTHAWK - the router that is supposed to provide blazing fast speeds to WiFi devices and I received results of 5.4Mb/s download and 2.1Mb/s upload - and similar on 3 consecutive tests. At this point I’m starting to be less than impressed.

I decided to log in to the more advanced router settings via my computer. I had no problem getting in there but to my surprise there are ABSOLUTELY NO PARENTAL CONTROLS. This is the same company that has sold itself as allowing you to have complete control over every aspect of your home internet. NETGEAR Genie is no longer available and the NETGEAR Nighthawk panel doesn’t even have a section for parental controls - let alone work with Disney Circle.

While there are some advanced security features available within the NETGEAR Nighthawk Router controls on the computer they are anything but user friendly - they are hard to find, hard to set, and less than optimal.

As I was discovering all of this and researching these issues in the NETGEAR Community Forums I started receiving notifications from my smart devices that they were losing WiFi signal and then after a minute or two they would reconnect. This happened with my security cameras, LIFX lights, Wemo switches, and August door locks. After this went on for about an hour I decided my experiment with the NETGEAR NIGHTHAWK had reached its conclusion.

Unfortunately I can’t recommend this router at this time. While the hardware inside should have this out performing most any other router on the market I found it to be slow and glitchy.

title: Limited Connectivity Docking Station
review_text:
I had high hopes for this docking station from StarTech but, thus far, I’ve been pretty disappointed.

Like many people I like the portability of working from a laptop but when I am at my workstation I want more screen space to work on - I thought this Docking Station would be a perfect solution. Well, in theory, it would.

Inside the box you’ll find the docking station, a 3.0 USB cable, a power adapter with snap on plugs to fit various world power sources, a DVI to VGA adapter, and a CD-ROM.

Unlike many docking stations or hubs this is not Plug and Play. I’m running the most updated Windows 10 64bit and the CD-ROM is completely useless. After inserting it in my computer I received a message reading that it was not compatible with my machine. No problem, I went to the manufacturer’s website, found the product, clicked on support, downloaded the zip file containing the setup and updated drivers for my OS and continued.

I went through the installation process and it appeared to install fine. After accepting the user agreement it checked my system for compatibility - finding no issues it continued and completed installation. I went to device manager and noticed an error in USB connected devices but figured with a restart it would correct.

I restarted but the error remains. Configuration Descriptor Request Failed - Windows has stopped device. I have uninstalled and reinstalled, searched help, used Windows Update to search for a better driver - so far nothing has worked.

In regards to functionality - the USB ports (two 3.0 and four 2.0) all function without issue and the Ethernet Port works great providing me over 200Mb/s. Due to not having the correct drivers I’ve been unable to test the multiple monitor capabilities.

I have contacted tech support and as of writing I have not heard back. If they are able to help me solve these issues I will update my review to reflect my further findings.

It appears this Docking Station is outdated being developed for older operating systems and while it may work for some users, others will find it needlessly difficult.

I would look at more recently manufactured docking stations that have been developed with the current operating systems - especially if you are using Windows 10.

title: Very sturdy legs but lack the ability to do fine height adjustments
review_text:
I got these legs because when we used the Sony Sound Bar in front of our Sony 65” TV on its factory legs where it partially blocked the IR input and the remote was not as responsive as it should have been.

I mounted this set of PERLESMITH Legs on my Sony XBR-65X850E 65” TV and while the instructions are straightforward it was a challenge and definitely a two person job to attach and adjust.

At first I mounted the brackets that attach to the TV completely flush with the TV where they would be the strongest but then realized in order for the legs to match up with holes for them to bolt through the TV would be far too high or not high enough.

So I moved the brackets that attach to the TV down to another setting that works but requires a bit of overlap of the contour of the back of the TV. That definitely allowed me to get the TV much closer to my desired height but not perfect.

I have our Sony Sound Bar sitting on top of the legs and would really like the TV directly above that so I wouldn’t see any wires but I still have a 1” gap between the bottom of the TV and the top of the sound bar. Unfortunately that’s as good as I can get it - I’ve tested every alternative mounting position and none work out better.

In order for the legs to be strong enough to support the weight of a TV safely over time fine tune height adjustment can be tricky. These legs are very sturdy and hold my 65” TV securely. They are a much better alternative to the factory legs as now our remote picks up perfectly. The only thing you should know is you can only adjust the TV height in increments.

I would recommend these legs for anyone, like us, needing to raise their TV a bit but still maintain stability.

I am very pleased with this extender and would recommend it to anyone who needed to extend their WiFi range or provide an Ethernet Port to a device that is too far from their current hub.

title: Incredible sound quality, super easy set up - GREAT BUY!
review_text:
I paired this sound bar with our Sony XBR-65X850E 65” TV and it could not have been easier.

While my TV would allow me to connect to the sound bar via Bluetooth I opted to connect via the HDMI ARC connection to avoid any sound lag. In addition to these 2 connection options you can connect via the included optical cable.

I followed the instructions - plugged the HDMI cable (not included) into the ARC HDMI port, plugged the sound bar and subwoofer into the surge protector and turned everything on. The TV automatically recognized the soundbar and changed my output.

All I had to do was press the “secure link” button on the remote and the sound bar wirelessly linked to the subwoofer without issue.

I decided to move the subwoofer to another area of the room - I unplugged it, moved it, plugged it back in and it reconnected without any problem.

I was able to pair the system with my iPhone without any issue and the sound is stunning. From the rich bass of the subwoofer, the vibrant midtones, to the crisp highs - every note is clear and distinct.

While I have a true 5.1 surround system most of the TV broadcasts are not going to utilize that type of system and the sound is actually richer through a sound bar with a subwoofer.

This soundbar can be easily wall mounted using the included template.

The entire system is intuitive and user friendly. While many sound systems require hours to hook up and figure out how to use correctly this one is so straightforward. The remote doesn’t have a bunch of excess buttons that you’ll never need or use.

In my instance my TV remote was able to control it immediately with no issues.

I highly recommend this soundbar for anyone looking for an easy way to improve the quality of the sound from your TV - and you’ll be pleasantly surprised by the rich sound it will deliver regardless of what you play through it.

title: Excellent updates on an already awesome light!
review_text:
I stumbled upon the IVISII brand a while ago and decided to give their products a try and I’m so happy that I did.

This upgraded IR-45 Ring Light Set by IVISII is exceptional. I purchased and have used their original IR-45 regularly for several months and was excited when I saw that they were releasing an updated model.

While many times the only option is to purchase high quality items a la cart or buy a lesser quality as a set I was so pleased with this set. Every piece in this set is constructed from high quality components and performs beautifully.

It comes with a light filter, a white softening filter, which snaps snuggly around the ring light and can be attached and detached with ease.

The set is complete with a standard 1/4” camera mounting bracket, a 1/4” mini ball head mounting bracket and a universal cell phone bracket. I’ve had no problems attaching and detaching all of my equipment repeatedly.

The light performs incredibly well. Due to the 19” size, it casts an immense amount of light. The new multi control knob is AWESOME- making adjusting the light output effortless - I can easily adjust the brightness of the bulbs from 1-100% just by spinning the dial and with a simple press of the knob’s center button, I have complete control over the temperature (or color of the light) from 3,000 Kelvin (soft white) - 5,800 Kelvin (Daylight).

Below the digital readout screen and the adjustment knob there are buttons with allow for the light to be synced with other lights so when this light is adjusted all of the others on that channel will automatically change as well. In addition there is a button that will step up the brightness in increments for quick adjustments when testing different shots.

This light can be synced with an optional remote control that IVISII offers. I purchased it a while ago with another set and would highly recommend it.

Due to the bulbs being LED the light weighs very little, produces no radiant heat and will last a very long time.

Unlike many photography sets that include a cheap, poorly made tripod, this set is complete with an excellent, sturdy tripod that will hold up for years.

The light and all of its accessories, except the tripod, fit within a great padded, easy to carry, case. The case has padding built into both outer sides and a middle divider. It is complete with heavy duty zippers, handles and an adjustable shoulder strap.

If you are looking for a light that will take your photography to another level, look no further. This is a set you are guaranteed to love.

Once again, IVISII hit it out of the park with this new and improved ring light.

title: An excellent external hard drive - fast, dependable & at a good price!
review_text:
As with anyone reading this review, I store and backup many large files - in addition I need quick access to them and this drive delivers. The primary quality I look for in this type of product is dependability and this drive has yet to let me down.

While this external drive is not as small or portable as a laptop unit - it does require its own power supply (provided) it is perfect for everyday use plugged in to my laptop. I have yet to see a USB powered 5 TB drive that I would trust.

I use it primarily to store large photo and video files once I'm finished working on them but have never had any issue pulling a file straight from there into PhotoShop, Lightroom or Illustrator working on it and resaving.

Transfer speed is really impressive for a drive of this size. That being said, I'd definitely recommend having a filing system that makes sense to you as searching through 5 TB (actually just under due to system files) for the file you need would be daunting.

I've had my current drive for quite a while, in use everyday without a single issue, so when I realized I was down to only having 340 GB available yesterday I ordered another without hesitation.

In my experience this is an awesome external hard drive that will deliver all you need it to do.

title: It's okay...
review_text:
I have a Garmin e-trex GPS as a backup for my sailboat navigation system so my use of handheld systems has been limited to marine use only. At first I thought this Magellan Trinton 400 system would be a good handheld for marine use. Then I changed my mind.

1. Yes, this 400 is in color... but the battery life is half that of my e-trex and I would much prefer longer battery life than a color screen. This is personal bias of course and may not be of importance to you.

2. I noted the 400 was much larger than my old e-trex and seemed "clunkier".

3. However, the biggest frustration was attemping to link the 400 with my boat's navigation program on my laptop. I simply wasn't able to link and their website help page was close to worthless. Never was able to link. My e-trex links right away.

4. I should have been able to download marine charts to the 400 but after several hours on their website, I was also unable to do this.

5. Finally, it was discouraging to google "Triton 400" and find so many negative comments about the unit and Magellan's support.

For land use, other than the short battery life, it might present a decent option. But for marine use, I'll stick with my Garmin e-trex.

title: Great GPS!
review_text:
I have a Magellan RoadMate 1412 which I have used for the past few years, both as a stand-alone and in comparison with other units including a "built-in" in a Lexus. Both the 1412 and this 1440 model work exceedingly well and always do better than comparison units.
1. Both units have fast initiation times, that is from turn on to seeking and then de-coding information from satellites. This may seem of minor consequence but gets old after a while with a unit that's initiation time is of several minutes.
2. Both units are very intuitive and thus easy to learn and use. It just "makes sense" as one needs to go thru the menus to set up or change a function.
3. The screen displays are bright, easy to follow, and easy to use. I don't see how they could make this any better.
4. The newer 1440 has some added bells and wistles, such as being able to "go-to" a favorite place more easily, and being able to access some functions directly on screen that are menu driven on the 1412.

Summary: This 1440 model is accurate, easy to use, and has enough added features to make it slighly better than my old 1412.

title: Bulky but functional backpack for your camera equipment
review_text:
There is room for my 13" laptop, my 12.9" ipad pro, all my camera lenses and the body for my sony A7ii, snacks, water bottle, and you can attach a tripod to it.

The failure of this camera backpack (along with all others I've tried is that it looks really bulky on my short petite frame ( 5'4" woman). I think it makes me look fatter because of how wide the bag is, I tried it on my guy friend (also a photographer) who I was hanging out with and it looks much better! He really appreciated the hip and chest straps that go across the front for when he's on his motorcycle.

I would definitely use this for travel. Your expensive camera gear can only be retrieved by taking off the backpack since the zipper is next to your back which makes me feel safer. Would be great for carrying everything through the airport and sending your photography equipment through the security scanners.

The hip and shoulder straps really help to distribute the weight of the bag so it's also great for long hikes to get that perfect landscape shot in the mountains. I'm looking forward to trying it out more this summer in the rockies.

TLDR:
Pros:
- color/texture of the bag is really attractive
- has plenty of room for your favorite lenses and mirrorless camera (I don't have a DSLR so couldn't test that)
- can also fit laptop + tablet, charging cables, snacks
- comfortable shoulder straps
- comes with a waterproof bag that fits around the backpack in case you're stuck in bad weather
- camera section is modular which allows you to fit a variety of lenses, I was also able to fit my flash in here.
- GREAT bag for the price. You can't beat $44 for this.
- there are thoughtful interior flaps by your lenses that prevent water from touching them in case if rain gets in by the zipper.

Cons:
- Bulky looking
- could have more pockets instead of two laptop sections.
- If you open bag when its sitting up instead of laying down your camera will fall out
- the interior finishings arent as nice as the outside fabric
- mine was missing the black strap you see in the product photography that holds the camera in vs. having it just sit at the top of the bag.

Overall it's a great bag if you're starting out in photography for traveling and just to store all your gear in one place safely. I think you can't beat the price for this bag and the fabric on the exterior is very attractive. It does get heavy with all your gear in it so I really appreciate the hip straps to distribute the weight.

review_text:

I was a bit uncertain when I first got it, because the hinge seemed really tight and I was afraid I was going to break it, but after a few uses, it loosened up enough that it no longer worries me. The case feels relatively well built and the set up is so easy that you don't need any technical know how to do it. The instructions that came with it were simple and easy to follow and I have had no issues with is so far.

The battery life is easy to check, since there is a button just for that, and the colour of the case itself is an exact match for the rose gold of the ipad I bought.

My only real complaint, is that it is somewhat difficult to get the ipad out of the case once you have put it in, without feeling like you are either going to damage the device or the case itself. perhaps there is an easier method to do it and I just haven't discovered it yet. Otherwise, this is a great product and if it endures m abuse for a year or so, I will consider it to have been well worth the money spect on it. title: Innovative design and works flawlessly with ipad 6th gen
review_text:
I'm relatively happy with this pencil. It is certainly better than many of the off-brands claiming to do the same thing. There are a few things I don't love, so I will get those out of the way first. The pencil in perfectly rounded and very slick, so it is a danger that it will roll away or fall from the desk or other surface you are using it at, unlike the Logitech Crayon. As a comparison, this pencil is much more comfortable to hold than the Crayon, but it feels more breakable.

I also don't love that the extra charging piece (converter) that you get is so tiny, as is the cap, since that makes me feel like I am always in danger of losing these small parts off of the counter where they charge. (If you have kids, then you know what I mean about things sprouting legs and disappearing.)

Otherwise, I love it. This pencil is highly responsive to the touchscreen of the ipad (I'm using the 6th gen) and it works great with note taking apps, beautifully with procreate, and also as a general scrolling tool or selection pointer. The battery lasts for a decent while and I am happy that there is now a way to charge it, without having to have the pencil sticking out the bottom of the ipad, as that just seemed like a recipe for disaster.

The pencil feels like it is made of good quality materials. it is heavy, but not obtrusively so, and the points are nice. The pencil feels sturdy to the grip ad like it isn't cheaply manufactured as some of the other pencils do. This is more than just your average stylus.

Although, I admit, when I first saw the price I thought it was a bit ridiculous, after owning this product for a while, I now see the difference between it and the competitors and I do believe it was worth the investment. Plus, you can order tips for it directly from amazon for a reasonable price, which, in my opinion makes it even more worth the money. I have had a hard time finding tips for the crayon without going to the logitech site or other outside sources. I prefer to do all my shopping at once, so this works for me.

I would definitely recommend this product to other ipad users, as it has changed the way I work for the positive and sped up my productivity. It was easy to connect, the packaging is beautiful as always, and the instructions were clear and helpful. I find myself becoming more and more attached to Apple products as time goes on.

As far as protection goes, it does make the device seem safer to hand with respect to the idea of dropping it. The edge around the front of the screen sticks out, which makes it less likely that the screen will fracture if you drop the device. There is a good amount of rubber around the plastic encasement and that is obviously shock absorbing, so that is comforting as well. Overall, this isn’t terribly poorly designed, the camera holes fit where they should and everything looks pretty good once the case is in place, it’s just getting it in place without destroying the device or the case that I took issue with.

title: some good some bad
review_text:
I bought this laptop because I wanted something that wasn't too heavy and could perform basic word processing and web functions. I had read product reviews for it before purchasing it and it seemed like it would suit me for what I required of it. After receiving the laptop computer I noticed two things immediately. The keyboard is made cheaply and to me, resembles something you might find on a first learning computer for a child. The keys have a cheap plastic-feel. After using the computer for two weeks, I already had to send it back to the manufacturer to have it repaired because two of the keys on the keyboard would get stuck and not produce the desired reaction when you push them.

Once I got the laptop back again, the keys were fixed but a few days later, the screen began to go black randomly and without warning. When it would come back, it would be in rainbow colors. After the second fix, it has been okay in those departments, but tends to overheat if you use it for any type of media, such as movies or music. The computer freezes a lot and has to be shut down manually at least once or twice a week.

I still think it is a bit heavier than I would like and since I have already had so many issues with it, I am actually afraid to carry it anywhere for fear that jostling it around in a carrying case might screw it all up again. The speakers on this computer are not nearly loud enough in my opinion.

What I do like about it is that it has pretty decent battery life (about 4-5 hours) depending on what you are doing at the time. I also like the colors the screen is capable of displaying when it is working correctly. I like that there are multiple USB ports for various endeavors. Overall I would say that this is a decent computer as long as you are prepared for the potential issues.

title: Great battery life...little bit of a learning curve!
review_text:
I bought the Samsung Chromebook with the idea in mind that it was even smaller than my laptop and would work great to read books on the go without having to drag along my kindle as well as my phone as well as...blah blah blah. Sometimes I honestly feel like all of my various devices turn me into a walking satellite receiver. The first thing I took note of when using the chromebook for the first time was how easy it was to set it up and make it personal. There is a handy one screen guide to walk you through the process. It is all pretty straight forward and if you are a user of google chrome, you pretty much have it in the bag already.

I set up the chromebook and downloaded the apps I would need to use offline and found the process simple and satisfying. Typing on the chromebook is pretty much the same as on any other keyboard with the noted exception that the keys have somewhat large spaces between them which can cause my typing to be a little awkward since I am used to my laptop where the keys are all close together.

The screen has beautiful even illumination and the apps download very quickly. It was a bit of a change to go from windows to the google operating system and took me a few days to organize things to where I could easily access them and remember where I put them.

As for battery life, this thing rocks! I have used this thing for seven hours before and still had it estimate that I had over an hour left. Mostly I use the chromebook for business applications and perusing the web for my job so I have not had to much experience playing movies on it or listening to music. I don't do much with multimedia.

So far it was a great purchase and I have been thrilled with it after a month of use. If you are looking for a lightweight, portable device to fill your basic needs, this is an excellent choice.
